 Program, Texts and Objectives Professional title conferred. Early Childhood and Primary School Teacher The Master's Degree in Single Cycle in Sciences of Primary Education is qualifying for teaching in both Early Childhood School and Primary School. The number of places is set at the national level based on estimated needs, which facilitates rapid integration into the job market. For the academic year 2023-2024, the total number of available places for aspiring teachers in Early Childhood and Primary Schools is nearly 10,500, but this quota (calculated on a national basis) still does not meet the need for trained teachers in schools, due to the high turnover rate expected in the coming years (Ministerial Decree No. 1027 of August 4, 2023, https://www.mur.gov.it/it/atti-e-normativa/decreto-ministeriale-n-1027-del-04-08-2023). Graduates in Primary Education Sciences obtain a degree with qualifying value for teaching in Early Childhood and Primary Schools. This degree is required for participation in regular competitions for the recruitment of teaching staff. To access the employment opportunities of this degree, registration with any professional register or order is not required.
 Final Exam Characteristics The final exam for the Single Cycle Master's Degree in Sciences of Primary Education consists of writing a written paper on a theoretical or applied topic, prepared by the student in an original manner under the guidance of a supervisor, and the preparation of the final internship report. The final exam consists of the discussion of the thesis and the final internship report. This discussion constitutes – pursuant to Ministerial Decree 249/2010 – an exam with qualifying value for teaching in Early Childhood and Primary Schools. For this purpose, the Commission, appointed by the competent academic authority, is composed of two tutor professors and a representative designated by the Regional School Office. The grade is expressed on a scale of 110, with the possibility of an honor (cum laude).
 Required Knowledge for Admission For admission to the Master's Degree course, it is required, by derogating from Article 6, paragraph 2, of the Ministerial Decree of October 22, 2004, No. 270, to hold a secondary school diploma or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent. A solid basic linguistic and cultural preparation is required, as well as good analytical and synthetic skills in texts. The Master's Degree course is number-controlled. The number of places, date, content, and mode of the selection test are determined annually by a specific Ministerial Decree. Initial preparation verification is mandatory and conducted according to the methods specified in the course's academic regulations and described in section A3.b. A negative outcome of the verification results in additional mandatory educational obligations as specified in the course's academic regulations and described in section A3.b.

Autonomy of Judgment.
The master's graduate in Primary Education Sciences will have acquired:
- the ability to construct intervention hypotheses based on data emerging from the context, with empirically grounded decision-making competence in the interest of the development of students;
- the ability to adopt inclusive perspectives, capable of valuing talents and recognizing the perspectives of culturally and ethnically minority groups (post-colonial teacher);
- the ability to produce simple data sets and read them to understand as much as possible the transformations affecting family systems and informal learning contexts (research teacher);
- the ability to develop autonomous professional thinking on social issues impacting or potentially impacting school organization (social teacher).
- the ability to self-assess one's work and modify it appropriately.
Autonomy of Judgment and critical analytical spirit are promoted and stimulated through discussions in courses and workshops, reflections during and after internships, and the guided design of educational segment simulations.
Autonomy of Judgment is evaluated and valued in written and oral exams, in the assessment of the internship and thesis work, which must take into account the candidate's reflective, critical analysis, and autonomous processing capabilities.

Learning Ability.
The master's graduate in Primary Education Sciences possesses:
- awareness of the importance of engaging with educational research and continuous professional development for the teaching profession;
- competencies related to: study strategies, source retrieval, critical approach to update proposals, to successfully and satisfactorily pursue continuous professional development;
- competencies for group learning and for the realization of shared educational projects.
Students must:
- map and analyze existing organizational and didactic innovation practices;
- construct documentation suitable for disseminating knowledge produced within a single school organization;
- activate networking paths with other schools and research communities;
- rethink the school's educational curriculum in relation to current socio-cultural changes and scientific research.
Learning abilities are stimulated and achieved through lectures, in deepening workshops, and in the realization of direct and indirect internships. The verification of learning abilities will occur through written and oral tests connected to exams, other training activities, and through the in-process and final discussion of the internship and thesis work.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Pedagogical-Didactic Area. Below are the macro-goals for applying knowledge and competencies, as detailed in the Course Design Document and the Tuning matrix available in the SUA Quality D5 framework.

Macro-goal 3. Construct didactic paths capable of responding to personalization and individualization needs, taking into account regulatory references and specific pedagogical, psychological, social, cultural, and regulatory knowledge.
Macro-goal 4. Activate paths conducive to developing a new vision on evaluation, whether formative or certificative, and a constructive and coherent integration between design, teaching, and evaluation processes.
Part of this educational macro-goal involves facilitating formative experiences aimed at fully involving students in their own learning processes.
Macro-goal 4.1.: Develop docimological knowledge and new perspectives on evaluation (new assessment) necessary to construct paths for evaluating competencies;
Macro-goal 4.2.: Design tools for evaluation and self-evaluation to be used with students and within institutional evaluation processes.
Macro-goal 6.1.: Be able to design strategies to reduce, and in perspective contain, any form of discrimination, considering cultural, gender, social, ethnic, and ability diversity among students.
Macro-goal 7: Promote research and innovation in schools, in collaboration with school networks and the world of work.
Macro-goal 7.1.: Ability to map and analyze existing organizational and didactic innovation practices;
Macro-goal 7.2.: Ability to construct documentation suitable for disseminating knowledge produced within a single school organization.
Pedagogical-Didactic Area courses share the adoption of active development methodologies and highly collaborative methods. To encourage student participation and engagement in their learning processes, teaching activities are strongly oriented toward a project-based and inquiry-based logic. Knowledge and competencies developed in this area are assessed through multimethod assessment systems, including project work, individual and group exercises, case studies, oral interviews, written tests, and the construction of reflective e-portfolios.

Scientific-Mathematical Area. Below are the macro-goals for applying knowledge and competencies, as detailed in the Course Design Document and the Tuning matrix available in the SUA Quality D5 framework.

Macro-goal 3: Construct didactic paths capable of responding to personalization and individualization needs, taking into account regulatory references and specific pedagogical, psychological, social, cultural, and regulatory knowledge.
Students will be able to design educational and didactic experiences for exploring and studying natural phenomena and environmental ecosystems, using observation and data collection strategies aligned with the scientific method.
Assessment methods for knowledge and competencies developed in this area include oral and written tests, application-oriented tests, multiple-choice quizzes, project work, and small group design exercises.

Historical-Social Area. Below are the macro-goals for applying knowledge and competencies, as detailed in the Course Design Document and the Tuning matrix available in the SUA Quality D5 framework.

Macro-goal 2: Design didactic situations according to various models (concept-based, goal-based, project-based, and integrative background models, as well as problem situations, case studies, authentic and meaningful tasks) after conducting a context analysis;
Macro-goal 3: Construct didactic paths capable of responding to personalization and individualization needs, taking into account regulatory references and specific historical and geographical knowledge, enabling students to appropriate the tools necessary to understand society and the geographical contexts they inhabit;
Macro-goal 3.1.: Know the main references of ancient and modern history and use them for analyzing historical-cultural phenomena.
Assessment methods for knowledge and competencies developed in this area include oral and written assessments, production of reports or documents in individual or collaborative form, and case analysis.

Language Area. Below are the macro-goals for applying knowledge and competencies, as detailed in the Course Design Document and the Tuning matrix available in the SUA Quality D5 framework.

Macro-goal 4: Be able to activate learning experiences aimed at involving students in their learning processes, also considering their linguistic development and communication skills.
Macro-goal 4.2.: Be able to design and implement didactic paths that encourage students to consciously adopt different linguistic codes and communication modes (linguistic, pictorial, musical).
Macro-goal 4.3.: Be able to design educational and didactic experiences for approaching English language and multilingualism, drawing on multimedia devices and resources.
Courses in the Language Area contribute to acquiring communication skills and discursive and written production skills. In these courses, active and collaborative teaching approaches are particularly promising, involving students in classroom exercises and requiring public presentation of group work. Therefore, assessment methods favoring text production, reports, case analyses, reports, documents, and individual or group designs are preferred.

Psychological and Sociological Area. Below are the macro-goals for applying knowledge and competencies, as detailed in the Course Design Document and the Tuning matrix available in the SUA Quality D5 framework.

Macro-goal 3: Construct didactic paths capable of responding to personalization and individualization needs, taking into account regulatory references and specific pedagogical, psychological, social, cultural, and regulatory knowledge.

Macro-goal 6.2.: Cultivate shared values that enable students to develop a sense of belonging to the community, a sense of responsibility, and autonomy in respecting democratic citizenship principles.
Assessment methods for knowledge and competencies developed in this area include oral or written exams with quantitative or qualitative structure; preparation of reports or documents in individual or small group form; case studies or conducting small-scale empirical micro-research under supervision.

Communication Skills.
The Master's graduate in Primary Education Sciences:
- is able to master the various specific registers of individual disciplines, also having meta-linguistic control;
- possesses various communication codes to present specific content;
- is able to lead group discussions, stimulating contributions, moderating discussions, and summarizing the situation clearly and comprehensively;
- is able to manage communication processes with students, their families, and colleagues most effectively;
- is able to argue and share their educational choices.
Communication skills are promoted in all training activities. In particular, they are achieved through interaction with others, and argumentative skills play a central role in laboratory activities and in the internship.
The verification of communication skills as a whole occurs through written and oral exams, active participation in laboratories, intermediate and final internship reports, and the presentation and discussion of the thesis work.
Expected occupational and professional outcomes for graduates.
Early Childhood School and Primary School Teacher The Single Cycle Master's Degree in Primary Education Sciences qualifies for teaching in both Early Childhood School and Primary School. The number of places is set at the national level based on estimated needs, which facilitates rapid integration into the workplace. For the 2023-2024 academic year, the total number of available positions for aspiring Early Childhood and Primary School teachers is nearly 10,500, but this national quota still does not meet the demand for trained teachers in schools, due to the high turnover rate expected in the coming years (Ministerial Decree No. 1027 of 04-08-2023,
https://www.mur.gov.it/it/atti-e-normativa/decreto-ministeriale-n-1027-del-04-08-2023).
Graduates in Primary Education Sciences obtain a qualification enabling teaching in Early Childhood School and Primary School.
This qualification is required for participation in regular competitions for the recruitment of teaching staff. No registration with any professional register or order is required to access the occupational opportunities of this degree course. Official language of teaching and assessment.
ITALIAN. Competencies associated with the role.
Early Childhood School and Primary School Teacher The competencies associated with the main role of Early Childhood and Primary School teacher relate to:
1) being able to design teaching paths that enable students to become active subjects, progressively more aware of their life and learning journey;
2) being able to manage observation practices for evaluating teaching paths and to construct and manage different documentation processes integrated into the formal and informal school curriculum;
3) ability to program flexible curricula that allow developing alternative strategies based on the user, the school institution's culture, and emerging needs from family systems;
4) being able to adapt activities within multicultural learning settings through understanding educational phenomena and recognizing the identity (and thus specificity) of the student;
5) organizational skills capable of fostering and developing dialogue with others (colleagues, school directors, families) aimed at educational planning, sharing choices, innovating service culture, and building educational ecosystems between school, families, and university.
Professional role in the workplace context.
Early Childhood School and Primary School Teacher The main functions of the Early Childhood and Primary School teacher relate to designing and implementing effective learning paths and educational practices that translate the guidelines in the National Guidelines for Early Childhood School and Primary School Curriculum (2012; 2018). Among the functions of Early Childhood and Primary School teachers are cultivating students' competencies, valuing talents, providing targeted and effective support to students with specific educational needs, promoting formal and informal learning, and constructively engaging with colleagues and families.
These functions are carried out within reference frameworks (National Guidelines 2012 and subsequent) that identify for Early Childhood School broad experience areas (Self and Others, Images, Sounds, Colors; Discourses and Words; Knowledge of the World) and for Primary School in competence areas and objectives (valuing students' experience and knowledge; implementing appropriate interventions regarding diversity; fostering exploration and discovery; encouraging collaborative learning; promoting awareness of one's learning style; carrying out didactic activities in laboratory form). These guidelines are now enriched by renewal requests for curricula derived from changes in increasingly heterogeneous family and social systems, driven by advanced multiculturalization phenomena and growing sensitivity regarding multiculturalism, inclusion, critical use of technologies, citizenship education, and sustainability.
The functions are thus also distinguished by levels of intervention, ranging from the student group, to relationships with families, to work with colleagues, up to building multi-institutional educational communities capable of integrating non-formal and formal learning processes.
For Early Childhood School, the function of the section coordinator teacher is noted, who presides over relations with parents, with any external professionals involved in caring for the children in the section, and monitors children's attendance, reporting critical situations.
For Primary School, teachers are assigned cross-functional coordination roles that can be exercised in relation to the class teaching team. For Primary School, the following are noted: the class coordinator teacher function, representing the point of contact for communications between the class teaching team, parents, the School Director, and students; the inclusion reference teacher function; the school visits reference teacher function; and the physical activities reference teacher function.
Description of specific learning objectives.
The Single Cycle Master's Degree in Primary Education Sciences (LM-85 bis) has a duration of 5 years and qualifies for teaching in Early Childhood School and Primary School. The Course is aimed at the cultural and professional training of Early Childhood School and Primary School teachers.
The Primary Education Sciences degree aims to train graduates with solid disciplinary knowledge across all fields of knowledge taught, with psychopedagogical and methodological-didactic competencies useful for designing teaching practices characterized by transversal attention to welcoming and supporting the educational needs of children with disabilities, neurodevelopmental disorders, and neurodivergence.
The course aims to develop competencies in managing and valuing diversity among students with varied learning needs, multicultural and multiethnic backgrounds, and differentiated physical, assistive, material, or compensatory support requirements.
Teaching in these areas is structured in courses and laboratories. The latter are aimed at practical application and reflection on knowledge acquired in courses, through individual and group work production, critical analysis, and evaluation of educational projects and interventions.
In addition to the three previous macro-areas, there are also: the five-year language laboratory for acquiring English language competencies, the didactic technologies laboratory, and direct and indirect internship activities, which constitute an indispensable part of the Course's training project.
Internship activities, totaling 600 hours (24 university credits), must develop progressively from the second year to the fifth year and conclude with the presentation and discussion of a report. The internship includes observation, planning, and direct experimentation activities. Internship activities offer a unique training opportunity regarding the specific professional profile, both for the possibility of entering the classroom and applying the learned teaching methods, and for the opportunity to engage in dialogue and reflection with various experts (tutor teachers, course instructors, coordinator tutors).
The internship is aimed at particularly developing the ability to design and develop didactic experiences (in this context, the ability to use didactic technologies functionally and strategically in relation to predefined educational goals, and the ability to observe, interpret, and address emerging difficulties will also be developed) and the ability to critically analyze and evaluate educational experiences from multiple perspectives (pedagogical, didactic, disciplinary).
The Master's degree in Primary Education Sciences, structured as a single teaching path, is organized around three axes that concretize the initial training objectives for teachers (DM 249/2010, art. 2).
A. Design and implementation of a curriculum that revisits disciplinary content and learning goals contextualized and related to variables presented by Primary School and Early Childhood School students, by the local school context, and cultural context. Expected exit competencies must integrate a pedagogical vision with solid disciplinary, methodological-didactic, and evaluative knowledge. The curriculum, understood in its formative reading as the integration of regulatory devices with practices supporting formal and informal learning, requires careful articulation of cognitive, emotional-affective management of students, and organizational management of the class, as well as specific knowledge regarding technologies for teaching (Specific Objectives 1-2-3-4-8; Pedagogical-Didactic, Scientific-Mathematical, Language, Psychological and Sociological, Historical-Social Areas) (M-PED, MAT, L-FIL-LET, BIO, CHIM, M-PSI, SPS, M-STO).
B. Design and articulation of interventions aimed at promoting the full development of students in their diversity and difference. It emphasizes the need to place the student in a position to acquire specific knowledge for special education and to interact in situations aimed at integrating students with disabilities, enhancing students with special educational needs, and preventing potential learning difficulties. The diversity of the school population also requires developing intercultural competencies and strong attention to the dimension of citizenship, transversal dimensions addressed in multiple training opportunities provided by the degree course (Specific Objectives 1-2-3-4-8; Pedagogical-Didactic, Language, Psychological and Sociological, Historical-Social, Hygienic-Health Areas) (M-PED, L-FIL-LET, L-ANT, MGGR, MED, M-PSI, SPS, M-STO).
C. Documentation, school quality evaluation, research, and innovation. These three processes must be reviewed in their integration and the mutual contributions they can provide. Acquiring competencies in collecting information and documenting processes supports both identifying problems and identifying possible solutions based on real and specific data, as well as the corpus on which to build analyses and produce evaluations. The design and participation of students in such processes, simulated or real, is an unavoidable condition to foster the initiation of professional self-design within meanings and objectives contextually or shared at a higher level of generality (Specific Objectives 4-5-6-7-8; Pedagogical-Didactic, Psychological and Sociological, Historical-Social Areas) (M-PED, M-PSI, SPS, M-STO, M-DEA).
The specific objectives of the study path can be summarized around eight competency areas:
1. Acquire appropriate knowledge in disciplinary fields, also with reference to historical and epistemological aspects, to relate them to the process of didactic transposition of disciplines. Students will be able to:
- design the transposition and mediation of teaching in relation to the specific context and as prescribed at the ministerial level;
- select basic constructs of logical-mathematical, physical, and biological disciplines, appropriate for analyzing the cultural and social landscape, to foster the development of students in all cognitive, affective, motor, and relational dimensions.
2. Deepen knowledge of new perspectives on teaching, using the most recent technologies for teaching, and design, in the research perspective, teaching paths aimed at supporting students' learning processes. Students must be able to:
- implement various teaching strategies and rethink, in light of collected data, possible influences on students' classroom behavior;
- design teaching situations according to different models (concept-based, goal-based, project-based, and integrative background, as well as problem situations, case studies, authentic and meaningful tasks) after conducting a contextual analysis;
- actively participate in situations of comparison on experiments and collected data analysis.
3. Build teaching paths capable of responding to personalization and individualization needs, taking into account regulatory references and specific pedagogical, psychological, social, cultural, and regulatory knowledge. Students must be able to:
- design curricula that support situated learning processes for students, considering the specificity of learning in relation to different ages;
- manage the class group by valuing existing diversities;
- collaborate with territorial teams and sector experts to build educational and didactic paths that understand and support the potential of all students.
4. Activate processes aimed at developing a new vision of assessment, whether formative or certificative, and a constructive and coherent integration between planning, teaching, and assessment processes. Part of this major training objective is to facilitate formative experiences that fully involve students at the center of their learning processes. Students must:
- acquire docimological knowledge and knowledge of new perspectives on assessment (new assessment) necessary to build paths for assessing competencies;
- design tools functional for assessment and self-assessment to be used with students and within an institutional assessment process.
5. Exercise functions connected to teaching professionalism, in collaboration with colleagues, families, school authorities, training agencies, and territorial representative institutions, having knowledge of the functioning of the school system and its historical evolution. Students must develop competencies to:
- design devices for evaluating the quality of school and teaching functioning;
- elaborate pedagogical-educational proposals in synergy with other educational agencies and situated within the context;
- value and manage resources present in the school and territory;
- understand and evaluate organizational and institutional transformations.
6. Build collectively an ethical vision of the teacher's professional identity and mission in society. Students must:
- be able to design strategies that allow reducing, and in perspective containing, any type of discrimination, taking into account cultural, gender, social, ethnic, and ability diversity of students;
- cultivate shared values that enable students to develop a sense of belonging to the community, sense of responsibility, and autonomy in respect for the principles of democratic citizenship.
7. Promote research and innovation in school, in collaboration with school networks and the world of work. Students must:
- map and analyze existing organizational and didactic innovation practices;
- construct appropriate documentation for disseminating knowledge produced within a single school organization;
- activate networking paths with other schools and research communities;
- rethink the school's educational curriculum in relation to changes present in the socio-cultural context and in scientific research.
8. Manage one's own professional development, using personal and collective resources, operating within practice communities with methodological competencies specific to educational research. Students must:
- build a professional competency balance sheet and identify improvement goals;
- select, among locally and network-available resources, those that best respond to their professional goals and explore different dimensions (situated, national, international, global) that provide a broader and scientifically grounded vision of educational processes.
The training devices The degree course offers a renewed proposal to align with current perspectives of scientific, cultural, and professional scenarios. Through frontal teaching and experiential activities, the training project promotes the construction of a conscious cultural and professional path, where a progressive path leads to the development of methodological, multidisciplinary, reflective, and organizational competencies required to work in current school contexts.
The methodological and didactic framework of the degree course intercepts and manages the current challenge of connecting research-education-profession in preparing future teachers.
The training devices of the degree course are based on differentiated types of learning settings:
- frontal lectures, dialogued lectures necessary to build the necessary knowledge frameworks in the areas specified by the learning objectives;
- analysis of real teaching experiences that will provide significant elements to activate analysis of didactic action and the scientific or implicit theories underlying it;
- production of writings and representations useful to collect and synthesize the most representative stages in the change of the training path (teacher portfolio) and related reflections;
- collective research practices among peers, with the support of professionals from the workplace or connecting to school and academic research communities, to build scientifically validated interpretive frameworks and methodological repertoires.
.
Internship objectives The direct and indirect internship, transversal to all learning areas, constitutes a particularly important experience for the development of professional practice and reflective competence necessary to build knowledge from practice, both on the job and on one's own positioning regarding work and continuous training. The objectives to be achieved in the internship will therefore be:
- to be able to recover and analyze one's own conceptions of teaching and school (mission, potential, issues) to compare them with the training project to be undertaken and pursued;
- to be able to construct, also in light of regulations and theories developed in the sciences of education, a possible profile of professional competencies that serves as orientation for the degree course's training path;
- to be able to use theoretical tools to analyze teaching projects and experiences (through videos, sector readings, case studies). The purpose is to identify the elements characterizing a teaching situation to make them the object of understanding and deepening;
- to be able to problematize, starting from complex contexts, in order to design teaching interventions;
- to be able to relate the knowledge acquired during activities carried out in courses and laboratories with the experiences lived in the direct internship, in order to find how the school reality interprets and re-elaborates theories or presents a particular knowledge about teaching;
- to be able to design teaching interventions with particular attention to the necessary coherence between purposes, objectives, mediators, teaching strategies, activities, and evaluation;
- to be able to argue one's teaching choices in light of pedagogical, psychological, didactic, and sociological knowledge;
- to be able to interpret one's role within an organization, such as a school, in relation to assigned functions, expected results, and negotiated outcomes.
Devices to be activated in the internship The different devices to be activated will have the fundamental purpose of enabling the student to construct their own learning history in the context of a progressive construction of a conscious professional identity.
It is therefore about fostering the achievement of this goal through devices that:
- promote narrative and reflective writings both on one's own paths of knowledge acquisition and on specific experiences (logbooks, teacher portfolio, documentation, summaries, concept maps);
- allow the student to virtually and actually enter situations to understand and analyze their complexity (simulations, role playing, case studies, video analysis, analysis of writings by pedagogists and didacticians or even teachers, classroom lessons, planning);
- involve the student in using specific tools to observe, collect, and categorize data to understand a situation and build their own explicit, arguable thought;
- place the student in a cognitive apprenticeship path where they construct and reconstruct action schemes based on families of situations (e.g., planning, addressing group management problems, evaluating learning) and operate in the direction of their continuous enrichment;
- activate the student to critically analyze materials present in the professional sector (journals, teaching guides) and make them capable of articulating always contextualized teaching paths with awareness of the choices made in relation to the specific learning objectives of the degree course.

, FABIO FERRETTI Chair/FABIO FERRETTI Chair Program, textbooks and objectives Admission requirements The Master's Degree in Medicine and Surgery is a program with limited places (Law 2 August 1999 n.264) and access requires a Five-year Upper Secondary School Diploma or an equivalent foreign qualification. Professional title conferred by the degree.
Medical Surgeon Master's graduates in Medicine and Surgery carry out the activity of medical surgeon in various clinical, health and biomedical professional roles and contexts. The Master's Degree in Medicine and Surgery is also a requirement for access to Medical Specialization Schools and the General Medicine Doctor Training Course.
Final exam characteristics To be admitted to take the Master's Degree exam, the student must have attended all courses and passed the related exams.
The Master's Degree exam is taken after completing a practical test for each internship area at the end of the TPVES (Practical Assessment Internship for State Exam), aimed at verifying the level of technical preparation for professional qualification. Additionally, to be admitted to take the Master's Degree exam, the student must have demonstrated the acquisition of specific skills related to writing a scientific paper in English.
The Master's Degree exam focuses on the discussion of a thesis developed originally by the student under the guidance of a supervisor, in accordance with the course's teaching regulations; the role of a co-supervisor may be provided.
The thesis can also be written and discussed in English.
The final grade is determined by the average of the marks obtained in the curricular exams, the evaluation of the thesis during the discussion, and the evaluation of other activities according to the methods established in the Master's Degree course teaching regulations.
The Master's Degree grade is expressed on a scale of 110 with possible honors.
Required knowledge for access Students possessing a secondary school diploma or another foreign qualification recognized as suitable are admitted to the Single Cycle Master's Degree in Medicine and Surgery.
The study course has national limited access.
The modalities for access to the Master's Degree in Medicine and Surgery and the content of the admission test are established by Law 2 August 1999 n. 264 "Provisions on access to university courses" and subsequent amendments, as well as by annual ministerial decrees concerning both the modalities and content of the admission tests for nationally limited access courses and the definition of available places for admission to the Master's Degree in Medicine and Surgery.
The test covers scientific disciplines such as biology, chemistry, physics and mathematics, as provided by current regulations on access to nationally limited access courses.
Students who pass the admission test must possess a level of English language knowledge at least equivalent to A2/2.
Adequate initial preparation in biology, chemistry and physics is also required.
Verification of the possession of such knowledge is mandatory. It will be carried out in cases where admitted students have obtained a score below the annual threshold set by the Teaching Committee, resulting in specific mandatory educational obligations (OFA) to be fulfilled in the first year of the course through additional lessons.
Degree awarded.
MEDICINE AND SURGERY DEGREE Teaching delivery method Conventional Knowledge and understanding.
Generic Area Master's graduates must have demonstrated knowledge and understanding capabilities sufficient to develop and/or apply original ideas within the context of biomedical and translational research. The following learning objectives must be achieved:
Scientific Foundations of Medicine
1) Know the normal structure and functionality of the organism as a complex of biological systems in continuous adaptation.
2) Be able to interpret morpho-functional anomalies of the organism observed in various diseases.
3) Be able to identify normal and abnormal human behavior.
4) Know the determinants and main risk factors for health and disease and the interaction between humans and their physical-social environment.
5) Know the molecular, cellular, biochemical and physiological mechanisms maintaining organism homeostasis.
6) Know the human life cycle and the effects of growth, development and aging on the individual, family and community.
7) Know the etiology and natural history of acute and chronic diseases.
8) Know epidemiology, health economics and the foundations of health management.
9) Know the principles of drug action and their uses, and the effectiveness of various pharmacological therapies.
10) Know and be able to implement the main biochemical, pharmacological, surgical, psychological, social and other interventions in acute and chronic disease, rehabilitation and terminal care.

Judgment Autonomy.
Master's graduates must have the ability to integrate knowledge and manage complexity, formulate judgments based on limited or incomplete information, including reflection on the social and ethical responsibilities related to the application of their knowledge and judgments. The following learning objectives must be achieved:
Critical Thinking and Scientific Research
1) Demonstrate a critical approach, constructive skepticism, creativity, and a research-oriented attitude in carrying out professional activities.
2) Understand the importance and limitations of scientific thinking based on information obtained from diverse resources, to establish the cause, treatment, and prevention of disease.
3) Be able to formulate personal judgments to solve analytical and critical problems ('problem solving') and independently seek scientific information without waiting for it to be provided.
4) Identify, formulate, and solve patient problems using the foundations of scientific thinking and research, based on information obtained and correlated from various sources.
5) Be aware of the role of complexity, uncertainty, and probability in decisions made during medical practice.
6) Be able to formulate hypotheses, collect, and critically evaluate data to solve problems.
Professional Values, Skills, Behavior, and Ethics
1) Be able to identify the essential elements of the medical profession, including moral and ethical principles and legal responsibilities underlying the profession.
2) Acquire professional values including excellence, altruism, responsibility, compassion, empathy, reliability, honesty, integrity, and commitment to following scientific methods.
3) Know that every physician has the obligation to promote, protect, and improve these elements for the benefit of patients, the profession, and society.
4) Recognize that good medical practice depends closely on interaction and good relationships between doctor, patient, and family, safeguarding well-being, cultural diversity, and patient autonomy.
5) Possess the ability to correctly apply moral reasoning principles and make appropriate decisions regarding possible conflicts in ethical, legal, and professional values, including those arising from economic distress, commercialization of healthcare, and new scientific discoveries.
6) Be conscious of the need for continuous professional improvement with awareness of personal limitations, including those of medical knowledge.
7) Show respect for colleagues and other health professionals, demonstrating excellent ability to establish collaborative relationships with them.
8) Be aware of moral obligations regarding end-of-life medical care, including palliative symptom and pain management.
9) Be aware of ethical and medical issues in handling patient data, plagiarism, confidentiality, and intellectual property.
10) Acquire the ability to effectively plan and efficiently manage time and activities to address uncertain conditions, and the ability to rapidly adapt to changes.
11) Acquire a sense of personal responsibility in caring for individual patients.
Learning objectives are achieved through ex-cathedra, seminar, interactive teaching tools, and attendance at scientific structures of the Department. Verification of achievement is conducted through profit assessments (ongoing and final).
Learning Skills.
Descriptor 5: Learning Skills
Master's graduates must have developed learning skills enabling them to continue studying mostly in an autonomous or self-directed manner. The following learning objectives must be achieved:
Information Management
1) Be able to correctly collect, organize, and interpret health and biomedical information from various available resources and databases.
2) Be able to collect specific patient information from clinical data management systems.
3) Be able to use information and communication technology as appropriate support for diagnostic, therapeutic, and preventive practices, and for health level surveillance and monitoring.
4) Be able to understand the application and also the limitations of information technology.
5) Be able to manage a good archive of one's medical practice for subsequent analysis and improvement.
For this purpose, familiarity with Informatics and multimedia methodologies that facilitate critical reading of scientific articles and prepare the graduate for future continuous updating is important.
Learning objectives are achieved through ex-cathedra, seminar, interactive teaching tools, and attendance at scientific structures of the Department. Verification of achievement is conducted through profit assessments (ongoing and final).
Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area Master's graduates must be able to apply their knowledge, have understanding capabilities, and skills in solving problems on new or unfamiliar topics within broad and interdisciplinary contexts related to achieving excellent clinical skills for the complexity of care and population health, with attention to gender specificity. The following learning objectives must be achieved:
Clinical Skills
1) Be able to correctly perform an adequate clinical history, including social aspects such as occupational health.
2) Be able to conduct a physical and mental status examination.
3) Be able to perform basic diagnostic procedures and techniques, analyze and interpret their results to correctly define the nature of a problem.
4) Be able to correctly perform appropriate diagnostic and therapeutic strategies to safeguard life and apply evidence-based medicine principles.
5) Be able to exercise correct clinical judgment to establish diagnoses and therapies for individual patients.
6) Recognize any condition that poses an imminent threat to the patient's life.
7) Be able to correctly and autonomously manage common medical emergencies.
8) Be able to effectively, efficiently, and ethically manage patients, promoting health and preventing disease in relation to gender/sex and population differences.
9) Be able to correctly assess health issues and advise patients considering physical, psychological, social, and cultural factors, with attention also to existing gender/sex differences.
10) Know the appropriate use of human resources, diagnostic interventions, therapeutic modalities, and technologies dedicated to healthcare.
Population Health and Health Systems
1) Know the main determinants of health and disease, such as lifestyle, genetic, demographic, environmental, socio-economic, psychological, and cultural factors in the population as a whole.
2) Be aware of the important role of health and disease determinants and capable of taking appropriate preventive and protective actions against diseases, injuries, and accidents, maintaining and promoting the health of the individual, family, and community.
3) Know the international health status, global trends in morbidity and mortality of socially relevant chronic diseases, the impact of migration, trade, and environmental factors on health, and the role of international health organizations and existing gender/sex differences.
4) Be aware of the roles and responsibilities of other health personnel in providing healthcare to individuals, populations, and communities.
5) Acquire understanding of the need for collective responsibility in health promotion interventions requiring close collaboration with the population, and a multidisciplinary approach including health professionals and intersectoral collaboration.
6) Know the basic organization of health systems, including policies, organization, financing, cost containment measures, and principles of efficient management for correct healthcare delivery.
7) Demonstrate good understanding of the mechanisms underlying equitable access to healthcare, effectiveness, and quality of care.
8) Be able to correctly use local, regional, and national surveillance data, demographics, and epidemiology in health decisions.
9) Know the basis for making correct decisions when necessary in healthcare issues.
Learning objectives are achieved through ex-cathedra, seminar, interactive teaching tools, and attendance at scientific structures of the Department. Verification of achievement is conducted through profit assessments (ongoing and final).

Communication Skills.
Master's graduates must be able to communicate their knowledge, conclusions, and the rationale behind them clearly and unambiguously to both specialist and non-specialist audiences. The following learning objectives must be achieved:
Communication Skills Descriptor 4: Communication Skills
1) Listen attentively to understand and synthesize relevant information on all issues, comprehending their content.
2) Apply communication skills to facilitate patient and family understanding, enabling them to make decisions as equal partners.
3) Communicate effectively with colleagues, departments, the community, other sectors, and the media.
4) Interact with other healthcare professionals involved in patient care through efficient teamwork.
5) Demonstrate basic teaching abilities and appropriate attitudes towards others.
6) Demonstrate good sensitivity towards cultural and personal factors that improve interactions with patients and the community.
7) Communicate effectively both orally and in writing.
8) Be able to create and maintain good medical documentation.
9) Be able to summarize and present information appropriately to meet audience needs, and discuss achievable and acceptable action plans representing priorities for the individual and the community.
Special attention is given to communication skills in the courses of Clinical Methodology - Human Sciences. Students can thus grow scientifically and develop greater sensitivity to ethical and socio-economic issues, enabling interaction with the patient as a whole person, according to the concept of whole person medicine.
In this context, narrative medicine, reflection grids, and role-playing techniques are used as important tools for students to acquire genuine emotional and professional competence (used by Psychologists and Psychiatrists in the Clinical Methodology course and Psychiatry course).
Learning objectives are achieved through ex-cathedra, seminar, interactive teaching methods, and attendance at scientific departments. Assessment of acquired results is conducted through progress and final examinations.
Expected occupational and professional outcomes for graduates.
Medical Surgeon Master's graduates in Medicine and Surgery perform the activity of medical surgeon in various clinical, health, and biomedical professional roles. The Master's Degree in Medicine and Surgery is also required for entry into Medical Specialization Schools and the training course for General Practitioners.
Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIAN Associated competencies.
Medical Surgeon Master's graduates must be able to apply their knowledge, have understanding capabilities, and possess skills to solve problems on new or unfamiliar topics within broad and interdisciplinary contexts related to achieving excellent clinical skills for the complexity of care and population health.
Description of admission tests.
The admission test for the Master's Degree in Medicine and Surgery is prepared by a decree of the Ministry of Education, carried out simultaneously and with identical content throughout the national territory. The admission test consists of solving eighty multiple-choice questions with five options each, only one of which is correct, on topics including general culture and logical reasoning; biology; chemistry; physics and mathematics. Based on the programs determined by ministerial decree for each subject, forty questions on general culture and logical reasoning; eighteen on biology, eleven on chemistry, and eleven on physics and mathematics are prepared. Students are admitted based on merit ranking and the number of available places, with those ranked within the programmed number for the specific Academic Year.
Professional role in work context.
Medical Surgeon The professional role intended to be formed in this Master's Degree course is that of a general medical practitioner operating in both clinical environments and the territory.
Additional information.
http://www.unisi.it Specific educational objectives description.
To achieve the educational objectives, the single-cycle Master's Degree course provides a total of 360 CFU over six years, with at least 60 CFU to be acquired in training activities aimed at developing specific professional skills.
In the study plan, training activities in the first two years of the course are distributed across Integrated Courses in: General and Molecular Biology; Chemistry and Biochemical Prerequisites; Scientific Methodology; Biochemistry; Histology and Embryology; Human Anatomy and Clinical; Human Physiology; Medical Microbiology, General Pathology; Medical Genetics; Clinical Scientific Methodology, English, Human Sciences and Health Promotion; courses included in the fields of General Disciplines for Medical Training, covering structure, function, and metabolism of biologically relevant molecules, human morphology, integrated biological functions of organs and systems, physio and immunopathology, and clinical methodology, medical microbiology, medical pedagogy, computer and communication skills.
In the third and fourth years, Integrated Courses are provided in the fields of pathophysiology, medical and surgical methodologies, laboratory and diagnostic medicine, pharmacology, behavioral disciplines, anatomopathological disciplines, interdisciplinary clinical training, human sciences, community medicine, and specialized medical and surgical disciplines: General Pathology; Methodology and First Aid; Semeiology and Medical Pathology; Semeiology and Surgical Pathology; Pharmacology; Laboratory Medicine; Pathological Anatomy; Integrated Courses on Cardiovascular, Infectious, Genetic, Oncological, and Blood Diseases; Specialized Medical and Surgical Disciplines.
In the fifth and sixth years, the training offer includes Integrated Courses in Neurology; Specialized Medical and Surgical Disciplines; Gynecology-Obstetrics-Urology; Imaging Diagnostics; Pediatric Medicine and Surgery; Legal and Occupational Medicine; Public Health; Medical Emergencies; Medical and Surgical Clinical Practice within the fields of neurological disciplines, obstetric-gynecological and sexual medicine, radiological and pediatric disciplines, Medicine and Public Health, Human Sciences and Health Management, Medical Emergencies, and General Medical and Surgical Clinical Practice.
Curricular internships are distributed across different specialties in different years, with qualifying internships in Internal Medicine, Surgery, and General Medicine scheduled for the sixth year.
Specific mission of the Single-Cycle Master's Degree Course The mission of the Single-Cycle Master's Degree Course is to train a professional-level doctor with a biomedical-psychosocial culture, possessing a multidisciplinary and integrated vision of health and disease problems, with education oriented towards the community, territory, and fundamentally towards disease prevention and health promotion, and with a humanistic culture in its medical aspects; this specific mission more adequately responds to new care and health needs, as it focuses not only on disease but especially on the sick person considered in their entirety of body and mind within the social context.
This medical education is also viewed as the first segment of an education that must last over time, and in this perspective, the knowledge the student must acquire in this phase has been calibrated, giving due importance to self-learning, experiences not only in hospitals but also in the territory, epidemiology, for the development of clinical reasoning and preventive culture.
The qualifying characteristics of the doctor to be trained include:
1) Good ability in human contact and attitude towards respecting the patient (communication skills);
2) Ability for self-learning and self-assessment, and ability to integrate into subsequent stages of medical training (continuing education);
3) Ability to analyze and solve problems related to medical practice independently, along with good evidence-based clinical practice (evidence-based medicine);
4) Habit of continuously updating knowledge and skills, and possession of methodological and cultural foundations for autonomous acquisition and critical evaluation of new knowledge and skills (continuing professional development);
5) Good practice of interdisciplinary and interprofessional work (interprofessional education);
6) Attention to equity and sustainability of care;
7) Awareness of the importance of social determinants of health, gender differences, and global health;
8) In-depth knowledge of the methodological foundations necessary for a correct approach to medical scientific research, along with autonomous use of information technology.
The specific teaching project provides horizontal and vertical integration of knowledge, a teaching method based on a solid cultural and methodological foundation acquired through the study of pre-clinical disciplines, and subsequently primarily focused on the ability to address problems, early contact with patients, acquisition of good clinical skills alongside human contact skills.
A solid foundation of clinical knowledge is also ensured for students through the organization of certified internships based on tutorial teaching, together with a strong understanding of the medical-scientific method and human sciences.
In the teaching project of our Master's Degree course, the right balance of integration is proposed between:
1) Basic sciences, which must be broad and include knowledge of evolutionary biology and biological complexity aimed at understanding the structure and function of the human organism under normal conditions, for maintaining health conditions;
2) Clinical and methodological medical practice, which must be particularly solid, through extensive use of tutorial teaching capable of transforming theoretical knowledge into personal experience and building one's own value scale and interests;
3) Human sciences, which must constitute a useful background to achieve awareness of being a doctor.
Many essential contents of our Teaching Project integrate the European specifications for global standards in medical education of the World Federation for Medical Education regarding basic international standards and quality development in biomedical education (WFME Office, University of Copenhagen, 2007).
The distinctive characteristics of the Master's Degree in Medicine and Surgery aimed at achieving specific objectives are summarized as follows:
1) The teaching method implemented is interactive and multidisciplinary, integrating basic sciences and clinical disciplines with early clinical involvement of students. Problems of basic sciences and clinical areas are addressed with a unified and integrated vision.
2) Specific objectives of basic courses are chosen primarily based on the relevance of each objective within human biology, and on their propaedeutic value for current or foreseeable clinical topics, with particular attention to the scientific methodology component.
3) Specific objectives of characteristic courses are chosen primarily based on epidemiological prevalence, urgency of intervention, possibility of intervention, severity, and didactic exemplarity. Attendance in hospital wards and outpatient clinics of territorial structures is also valued, as well as the relationship with the patient, including the psychological aspect.
4) The teaching process relies on tutor teachers who collaborate in the student's training process with teaching and support functions, and when possible, modern teaching tools, consisting of the tutorial system, clinical trigger, problem-oriented learning, experiential learning, problem solving, decision making, and the use of seminars.
5) Attention is paid to acquiring practical skills through: a) learning the basic semeiology of clinical sciences at the bedside and in laboratories during the intermediate period (professionalizing internship organized as guided tutorial with certification of skill level, in the third year of the course), b) attendance of wards and outpatient clinics (clinical internship - clinical clerkship - with certification by the tutor of achieved skills) for completing clinical internship in the final years of the course and the internship period for preparing the Master's thesis. An innovation has been introduced regarding the professionalizing internship following Ministerial Decree No. 58 of May 9, 2018, on the procedures for the State Exam. The decree moves the evaluative practical internship (TPVES) from post-graduation to within the curricular internship provided by the course's teaching regulations. The TPVES to be carried out within the last two years of the course consists of 15 CFU with dual value, divided into three periods of 100 hours/5 CFU each, with 5 CFU in Medical Area; 5 CFU in Surgical Area; and 5 CFU in General Medicine context with attendance at a General Practitioner's outpatient clinic.
6) Attention is given to learning English and information and multimedia methodologies.
7) Special attention is given to aspects related to Clinical Methodology-Human Sciences (Methodologies). The importance of the method in medicine is well known, both for understanding medical methodology and its rules according to evidence-based medicine principles, and for clinical methodology applied to individual patients. This will be achieved through the application of 'evidence-based medicine', 'evidence-based teaching' through the use of 'guidelines', 'concept maps', and 'algorithms'. Topics related to interdisciplinarity and interprofessionalism, health economics, medical professionalism, social responsibility of the doctor, social and gender perspective, relationships with so-called complementary and alternative medicines, prevention, chronic patient education, dependency-related pathologies, and palliative care for terminal patients will also be addressed.

Legal professions (notary, lawyer); judiciary; State Attorney; positions in various fields of social, socio-economic and political activity characterized by high responsibility, in institutions, public administrations, independent authorities, private companies, trade unions, in the field of information technology law, comparative, international and European law (European lawyer), as well as in international organizations.
Final exam characteristics The final exam consists of a written dissertation on a topic assigned related to one of the training activities carried out by the student. The thesis, of a monographic nature, must be defended before a committee of at least 5 teachers. The evaluation is expressed in 110 points with possible honors.
The increase in CFU for the thesis (in line with other Law Faculties) derives from the decision to require a higher level of in-depth study for the final work. The thesis must therefore result from a broad and reasoned review of sources and show a motivated critical analysis of the assigned topic, according to the model of a monographic treatment. This increased work responds to the need to further refine in young lawyers the techniques of orderly and systematic written exposition of legal aspects characterizing any social fact.
Required knowledge for access Students must possess a high school diploma or another equivalent qualification obtained abroad, recognized as suitable.
Initial knowledge verification tests are provided, focusing on general culture, with particular attention to principles of the Italian legal system, current politics, modern and contemporary history, legal reasoning ability, vocabulary, and basic discourse operations. Participation in these tests is mandatory. For students who do not achieve a positive outcome, specific recovery courses are organized.
Awarded degree.
Master's Degree in Jurisprudence Teaching delivery method Conventional Knowledge and understanding.
General description The five-year training path and the significant effort required for the final thesis will enable the Master's graduate in Jurisprudence to acquire in-depth knowledge and high levels of professional qualification, in line with the challenges constantly imposed by the complexity of contemporary legal reality.
Such knowledge will mostly be acquired through frontal lectures, during which the teacher will encourage discussion and exchange among students. Frontal lectures - an essential component of traditional teaching - will frequently be integrated with exercises aimed at maximizing direct involvement and critical learning for each participant.
Preparation will be verified through optional intermediate tests and a mandatory final oral examination.
PRIVATE LAW In the private law learning area, the Master's graduate:
- possesses in-depth knowledge of private law institutions
- knows civil law institutions in light of doctrinal and jurisprudential contributions
- has in-depth knowledge of relevant legal issues concerning agricultural, commercial, industrial, and labor law
- knows the European and international aspects related to the private law area.
PUBLIC LAW The Master's graduate
- possesses in-depth knowledge of the system of sources of national law, with particular reference to constitutional norms, characteristics of the state legal system, structure and powers, as well as a high level of knowledge and understanding of administrative organization in the central and local government structures and administrative justice institutions
- also knows tax law in both substantive and procedural dimensions.
ECONOMIC The Master's graduate
- acquires in-depth knowledge and high comprehension abilities regarding institutional elements of political economy (microeconomics and macroeconomics) and introduces the main topics of legal economic analysis.
HISTORICAL-PHILOSOPHICAL-METHODOLOGICAL The Master's graduate
- possesses the necessary historical, philosophical, and methodological knowledge for the historical-cultural analysis of contemporary law, with particular reference to interpretation theory and argumentation theory.
- knows the origin and evolution of legal, anthropological, and normative constant research experiences
- acquires the knowledge necessary to understand in a diachronic perspective the unitary nature of legal experience in relation to the systematic framework and disciplinary segmentation.
INTERNATIONALIST The Master's graduate
- acquires in-depth knowledge of the institutional aspects of European Union law, also with reference to relations between European law and national legal order
- knows the norms of public and private international law
- knows the instruments for resolving disputes, both diplomatic and judicial/arbitral, provided for by international law.

Judgment autonomy.
The teaching and training activities will enable graduates to independently research relevant data to correctly frame legal problems, even complex ones, and formulate plausible solutions.
Learning ability.
Upon completion of the single-cycle Master's degree course, graduates will have acquired methods and techniques that can be applied, should they continue their studies by participating in post-graduate training activities.
Ability to apply knowledge and understanding.
General description The training activities provided in the single-cycle Master's degree in jurisprudence will equip students with the necessary tools to apply their knowledge and understanding in various professional contexts requiring the contribution of a qualified jurist. Graduates must be able to independently choose the best strategies to address and solve the various issues that may arise in the professional field in which they will operate. To facilitate the coordination between theoretical preparation and practical activities, seminars and exercises will be organized where judgments, practical cases, and procedural, contractual, and administrative acts will be examined and discussed.
PRIVATE LAW The Master's graduate
- is able to move comfortably within the plurality of legal sources and apply acquired knowledge for the resolution of concrete cases.
- acquires the ability to understand the interactions and connections between national, European, and international law.
PUBLIC LAW The Master's graduate
- has in-depth knowledge of the fundamental concepts of criminal law, the categories of the general part, and the criminal offenses of the special part
- acquires the ability to interpret and apply national substantive and procedural legal norms, also considering potential links with European norms.
ECONOMIC The Master's graduate
- is able to understand and apply the main concepts underlying the economic analysis of law, particularly those related to individual rationality.
- acquires the ability to use the acquired concepts to address issues related to criminal behavior, property, civil liability, contracts, business theories, and judicial disputes.
HISTORICAL-PHILOSOPHICAL-METHODOLOGICAL The Master's graduate
- is able to apply legal interpretation techniques through mastery of legal reasoning and knowledge of the historical and philosophical evolution of positive law.
INTERNATIONALIST The Master's graduate
- is able to interpret and apply European and international law norms, moving with mastery within the interactions between the plurality of legal sources
- possesses a level of understanding enabling the application of international norms, particularly those protecting human rights, with critical capacity regarding the influence of specific cultural contexts.

http://www.unisi.it http://www.dgiur.unisi.it/it Specific training objectives description.
In accordance with the provisions of Ministerial Decree of November 25, 2005, the Single-cycle Master's Degree in Jurisprudence aims to provide legal training that includes:
- Achieving in-depth knowledge of the fundamental national and European legal culture, in relation to themes useful for understanding and evaluating principles or institutions of positive law;
- Acquiring in-depth historical, comparative and methodological knowledge to evaluate institutions of positive law;
- Acquiring knowledge of the institutional and organizational aspects of judicial systems, as well as the tools for their evaluation;
- Acquiring the ability to produce clear, relevant and effective legal texts in relation to employment contexts;
- Acquiring the ability to draft normative, contractual and procedural legal texts;
- Acquiring full capacity for analysis and combination of legal norms, as well as the ability to present in written and oral form—aware of their technical-legal, cultural, practical and value implications—the reasoning and arguments appropriate for correctly addressing general and specific legal issues, cases and factual situations;
- Acquiring in-depth interpretative, case analysis, legal qualification, understanding, representation, evaluation and awareness capacities to address interpretative and application problems of law;
- Acquiring broad mastery of basic tools for updating one's own knowledge;
- Acquiring the ability to fluently use, in written and oral form, besides Italian, at least the English language at B2 level, also with reference to disciplinary lexicons.
- The qualifying training objectives are reflected, as indicated by ministerial decrees, in the disciplines provided for basic and characterizing training, while for related and integrative fields, students may choose courses, with the possibility of drawing from scientific-disciplinary sectors not included in the ministerial table. In particular, to achieve the stated objectives, the training path is structured as follows:
- In the first year, the study of basic subjects is provided. The curriculum begins with the study of Roman law history (IUS/18), and medieval and modern law (IUS/19), continuing with legal philosophy (IUS/20), constitutional law (IUS/08) and institutions of private law (IUS/01). The path is completed by acquiring English language proficiency at B2 level.
- In the second year, the completion of historical-legal (IUS/18-19) and constitutional (IUS/11) training is accompanied by the study of characterizing subjects in the economic and public law (SECS-P/01), community (IUS/14) and comparative (IUS/02-21) fields, where students may choose between comparative public law or comparative private law.
- In the third year, courses in the penal (IUS/17), labor (IUS/07) and international (IUS/13) law fields are taught. For specific territorial productive vocation, it was deemed appropriate to include Agricultural Law (IUS/03) as an optional course.
- The fourth year is dedicated to the study of Administrative Law (IUS/10), Commercial Law (IUS/04), Civil Procedural Law (IUS/15), as well as the completion of philosophical-legal training, aimed at specific training objectives in the IUS/20 sector. In the fourth year, students are also required to begin the study and bibliographic research necessary for the preparation of the thesis, carrying out research activity subject to certification by the Teaching Committee.
- The final year is reserved for the in-depth study of Administrative Law (IUS/10), Private Law (Civil Law IUS/01) and Criminal Procedural Law (IUS/16). Tax Law is also provided to complete training in the economic and public law field (IUS/12).
Master's graduates in jurisprudence, in addition to directing towards legal professions and the judiciary, may carry out activities and be employed in positions involving high responsibility in various fields of social, socio-economic and political activity, or in institutions, public administrations, private companies, trade unions, in the field of information technology law, in the field of comparative, international and community law (European lawyer), as well as in international organizations where the jurist's analytical, evaluative and decision-making capacities prove fruitful even beyond sectoral content knowledge.

Pharmacist The completion of the Master's Degree in Pharmacy enables the exercise of the profession of Pharmacist as:
Owner, director, or collaborator of public or private Pharmacies Owner, director, or collaborator of Parapharmacies Director in the National Health Service, particularly in Hospital Pharmacy and Territorial Pharmaceutical Service, following the acquisition of the Specialist in Hospital Pharmacy title according to current regulations Scientific information provider for the pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and dietetic-food sector Collaborator and manager in the pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and dietetic-food industry for the dissemination of scientific information on drugs and health products.

Final exam characteristics The final exam consists of preparing and publicly discussing a thesis, which can be compilative or experimental, developed originally by the student under the supervision of a faculty member of a discipline present in the study program, and related to a topic relevant to the curricular disciplines. The compilative thesis consists of a bibliographic in-depth study on a topic agreed upon between the faculty member and the student, and the writing of an original written document. The experimental thesis consists of conducting original research or collecting and processing original information from clinical-scientific databases. The experimental thesis can be carried out at a university laboratory, a company, or a research institution, in Italy or abroad, with which the University has signed a convention or international agreements.
The final exam includes the performance of a practical assessment of professional skills acquired through the practical internship assessment preceding the thesis discussion, aimed at verifying the candidate's technical preparation level for professional qualification. The final dissertation is conducted in the presence of a graduation committee composed of experts in the field and members designated by the professional order; the student must demonstrate mastery of the thesis topic, critical ability, and good communication skills. The final grade is expressed on a scale of 110 with possible honors.
Required knowledge for access To access the study program, it is necessary to hold a secondary school diploma or another title obtained abroad and recognized as suitable. Additionally, knowledge of English at a level of at least A2/2, as defined by the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages, is required.
Students enrolled in the Master's Degree in Pharmacy must possess adequate initial preparation in chemistry, biology, and mathematics, which is verified through the TOLC-F test. This test is mandatory but not binding for the enrollment procedure.
For the evaluation of the test, minimum scores are established. For students who do not achieve these scores, faculty members verify the recovery of the required educational obligations that students must complete within the first year of study.
Knowledge and understanding.
Basic physical-mathematical and chemical area The Master's graduate acquires knowledge of the basic scientific aspects of mathematics, computer science, and physics; general and inorganic chemistry and stoichiometry; analytical chemistry and organic chemistry; laboratory behavioral and safety norms Basic biological area The Master's graduate acquires knowledge of animal and plant biology, biochemistry, applied biochemistry, clinical biochemistry, nutritional biochemistry, molecular biology, microbiology, and epidemiology.
Basic biomedical area The Master's graduate acquires knowledge regarding human anatomy, general physiology, and human disease pathology, and becomes familiar with medical terminology Pharmaceutical and toxicological area The Master's graduate knows medicinal plants and their pharmacologically active principles and acquires knowledge of phytotherapy; knows pharmacology, pharmacotherapy, and toxicology to fully understand the action of drugs, diagnostic products, and other health products; additionally acquires knowledge of clinical pharmacology and pharmacovigilance Chemical-pharmaceutical area The Master's graduate knows the chemistry of the main classes of drugs; knows the different synthetic processes and methodologies used for quality control of the main classes of drugs; knows the qualitative and quantitative analysis methods for medicinal products, even in complex matrices, and the chemical-physical characteristics of raw materials used in therapeutic preparations, including polymer materials of pharmaceutical interest; knows the chemistry and analysis methods for herbal, nutraceutical, dietary supplements, biotechnological drugs, and cosmetic products.
Technological-legislative and professional area The Master's graduate acquires knowledge of pharmaceutical technology and knows the procedures for formulating galenic and magistral products and cosmetic products; acquires knowledge of innovative pharmaceutical forms and medical devices; knows the legislative and ethical norms regulating the Pharmacist profession; acquires basic knowledge of computer use in business and useful knowledge for the economic management of pharmacies and relationships with the public; acquires linguistic competence in specific content related to pharmaceutical disciplines, scientific literature, and the Pharmacist profession.
