Judgment Autonomy.
Master's graduates in Pharmacy are able to: - correctly dispense medications; - correctly advise on over-the-counter medications and health products (dietary supplements, cosmetics, medical devices); - provide consultation to healthy individuals for disease prevention and personalized support for chronic patients to adhere to therapies; - identify drug interactions and report adverse reactions; - monitor pharmaceutical expenditure; - manage the economic/organizational management of pharmacies and other organizations responsible for preparing and distributing pharmaceutical and parapharmaceutical products; - retrieve and use data to formulate responses to practical or theoretical problems; - perform additional services such as technological controls and analyses required for different types and formulations of health products. The didactic tools used to achieve these levels of autonomy are frontal lectures by instructors, laboratory activities, and reports developed in these training activities, as well as a practical-evaluative internship in pharmacy under the guidance of a pharmacist (company tutor), who will provide feedback on this activity in a dedicated internship diary. The verification of acquired judgment autonomy occurs through evaluations of student reports, particularly related to laboratory tests and the execution and presentation of the final exam.

Learning Capacity.
Master's graduates in Pharmacy must have developed learning capacity: a) for continuous updating of their knowledge; b) for deepening specific themes related to drugs; c) for using computer tools for consulting databases and specialized literature; d) for addressing Specialization Schools of the Pharmaceutical Area (DM 1 August 2005), Biomedical, Pharmaceutical and Pharmacological Research Doctorates, and second-level master's programs related to the training path. Achieving these goals, besides attending lectures (which constitutes a central didactic aid), is significantly contributed to by autonomous activities in the training path, such as presenting independently prepared reports, conducting in-course tests, executing and presenting the thesis, as well as all professionalizing activities like seminars on advanced topics and training internships. Verification will be entrusted to individual exam tests (written and/or oral) and especially to the final exam.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Basic Physical-Mathematical and Chemical Area
Master's graduates are able to apply knowledge acquired in physical, chemical, and mathematical fields for understanding subsequent disciplines in the training path; they are able to respect behavioral and safety norms required for working in an experimental laboratory; they are also able to apply acquired knowledge to solve specific problems related to the profession.

Biological Area
Master's graduates are able to apply biological knowledge as an indispensable prerequisite for correctly understanding drug interactions with living organisms;
they are able to apply microbiology and epidemiology knowledge for understanding the action of antimicrobial drugs;
they are able to apply biochemical, applied biochemical, clinical biochemical, nutritional biochemical, and molecular biology knowledge for understanding and studying the molecular mechanisms underlying drug and nutraceutical product actions, and to perform biochemical-clinical analyses.

Basic Biomedical Area
Master's graduates are able to apply anatomical, physiological, and pathophysiological knowledge as an indispensable prerequisite for correctly understanding drug interactions with living organisms.

Pharmacological and Toxicological Area
Master's graduates apply knowledge acquired through the study of pharmacology and pharmacognosy for the correct dispensing of drugs, herbal products, dietary products, and other health products, and for educating the population on the correct use of drugs;
they apply pharmacovigilance concepts for reporting adverse effects caused by medications, herbal products, and other products dispensed in pharmacies;
they apply knowledge acquired on drug efficacy, safety, and toxicity to ensure their correct use.

Chemical-Pharmaceutical Area
Master's graduates apply pharmaceutical chemistry knowledge for the correct storage and dispensing of drugs, herbal products, and nutraceuticals; they apply pharmaceutical analysis knowledge to control drugs; they apply cosmetic chemistry knowledge for preparing and analyzing products for cosmetics.

Technological-Legislative and Professionalizing Area
Master's graduates are able to apply technological knowledge for preparing pharmaceutical forms and cosmetic preparations; they are able to perform technological controls on pharmaceutical forms; they are able to manage and dispense medical devices; they are able to apply legislative, computer, and economic-business knowledge for performing the profession; they acquire the ability to communicate, understand, read, write, and interact in English within the pharmaceutical sector and the pharmacist profession; they are able to manage a pharmacy and establish a correct relationship with the public.

For all the above learning areas, the main didactic tool is represented by frontal lectures, integrated where required with single-seat laboratory exercises.
The assessment of knowledge and understanding abilities occurs through oral interviews and/or written tests prerequisite for the oral exam.

Communication Skills.

The didactic tools used to achieve these levels of autonomy are professional seminars, computer simulations of pharmacy management, and practical assessment internships. The acquisition of written and oral communication skills will be assessed through written and/or oral examinations and highlighted at the end of studies through the presentation of the thesis work.

Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIAN Associated competencies for the role.
Pharmacist The fundamental competencies for the exercise of the pharmacist profession concern knowledge of pharmaceutical chemistry, pathophysiology, pharmacology, toxicology, pharmaceutical technology, and legislation for preparation, quality control, management, dispensing, surveillance, and information on drugs, medicines, medical devices, foods, health products, and cosmetics in public pharmacies, hospital pharmacies, and Territorial Pharmaceutical Service.
Scientific Information Officer for the pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and dietary sectors For the professional role of Scientific Information Officer, knowledge of pharmaceutical chemistry, pathophysiology, pharmacology, pharmaceutical technology, drug epidemiology, pharmacoeconomics, pharmacovigilance, and marketing is required.
Expert for the pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and dietary industries The competencies associated with the profession in pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and dietary companies include knowledge of pharmaceutical chemistry, chemical-pharmaceutical analysis, pharmacology, toxicology, and pharmaceutical technology for the development of drugs, medicines, foods, health products, and cosmetics.
Role in work context.
Pharmacist The Master's Degree in Pharmacy provides adequate preparation to operate in the various fields where the professional role of Pharmacist, a healthcare operator performing a primary role in the National Health Service to protect citizen health, is required.
The pharmacist's competencies concern the preparation of medicines based on medical prescription and other general-use products codified by the national and European Pharmacopoeia, for which they have full responsibility; quality control of preparations; storage, custody, and distribution of medicines.
In public pharmacies, they distribute medicines, medical devices, personal and environmental hygiene products, infant foods, and special diet products, elderly and/or weakened person dietary supplements, and cosmetics. In this context, they also perform information and therapeutic advisory functions (dosage, contraindications, side effects). The pharmacist also exercises functions prescribed by law regarding pharmacovigilance, communicating suspected adverse drug reactions to competent authorities.
The pharmacist may also perform integrated home care services, first-level analysis, second-level service provision based on current regulations, healthcare services, correct drug use, guarantee and continuity of drug dispensing, and health educator role.
After obtaining the Specialist title in Hospital Pharmacy, the pharmacist can exercise their profession in Hospitals within: a) Hospital Pharmacy (procurement and management of medicine stocks, dressing materials, sterile materials, medical devices, and diagnostic equipment; preparation and management of enteral and parenteral nutrition; pharmacovigilance and consumption monitoring within the hospital and protected facilities; drug information for healthcare staff; monitoring and management of experimental drugs); b) Territorial Pharmaceutical Service (supervision of public pharmacies, pharmacovigilance on the territory, supervision of pharmaceutical care provision, monitoring of general practitioner prescription activity, monitoring pharmaceutical expenditure, drug information for healthcare staff).
Scientific Information Officer for the pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and dietary sectors The Pharmacy graduate possesses the necessary competencies for the professional role of Scientific Information Officer, whose main functions are to inform medical, healthcare, cosmetic, and dietary sector operators about the characteristics and properties of medicinal specialties, medical-surgical devices, and cosmetic and dietary products, to ensure their correct use as provided by the National Health Service.
The Scientific Information Officer may also perform pharmacovigilance, pharmaceutical expenditure monitoring, and clinical trials activities at companies holding development, registration, and production of medicinal specialties, medical-surgical devices, dietary products, and diagnostic tools.
Expert for the pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and dietary industries The Pharmacy graduate can exercise the profession at pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and dietary companies as an expert in formulation, analysis, and control of medicines, cosmetics, and health products. They can therefore operate as research and development staff in the pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and dietary industries, conducting applied scientific research for new product development; or operate within quality control, regulatory affairs, production, quality assurance, and marketing.
Specific training objectives description.
The Master's Degree in Pharmacy aims to provide a set of theoretical and practical knowledge in chemical, biological, physiological, pharmaceutical, technological, pharmacological, and toxicological fields, enabling Master's graduates to address the multidisciplinary nature of drug sciences, including drug structure design, quality control systems according to European Pharmacopoeia codes, production, and utilization. The Master's Degree is structured over five years and is organized to allow students to progress from basic disciplines toward characteristic disciplines, preparing them for a professional profile aligned with current labor market needs.
- During the first two years, students address basic disciplines starting from chemistry, physics-mathematics, biology, computer science, and medicine (e.g., CHIM/03, CHIM/01, CHIM/06, MAT/01-MAT/09, FIS/01-FIS/08, BIO/13, BIO/15, MED/07, BIO/16), must achieve English proficiency (B2 level), and acquire basic knowledge of behavioral and safety norms necessary for attending subsequent laboratory courses. During the same academic period, the characteristic discipline BIO/15 is taught to complete the first-year basic training for this SSD, along with characteristic biological disciplines (BIO/11, BIO/10);
- In the third and fourth years, characteristic disciplines in pharmaceutical-food (CHIM/08), biological and pharmacological disciplines (BIO/14), and technological, regulatory, and economic-business professional disciplines (CHIM/09, SECS-P/07) are offered. These disciplines are necessary to acquire: a) adequate knowledge of the chemical and structural characteristics of active ingredients and raw materials used in medicine formulations; b) adequate knowledge of pharmacological bases in terms of pharmacodynamics and pharmacokinetics, necessary for understanding drug mechanisms of action, including toxicological aspects; c) adequate knowledge of legislative and ethical norms, useful for exercising various aspects of professional activity, including economic-business aspects; d) adequate theoretical and practical training for analytical-quantitative aspects of medicines, including biological medicines; e) adequate technological knowledge for preparing various pharmaceutical forms and their quality control; f) adequate knowledge of medical devices and performing first-level analytical services. At the end of the fourth year, students may complete part of the practical assessment internship (TPV);
- The fifth year is primarily reserved for the practical assessment internship (TPV) and final exam preparation. Additionally, in the fifth year, students may complete their training with related or complementary activities to acquire useful soft skills for the profession and deepen interests in cosmetics, phytotherapy, nutraceuticals, food and dietary supplements, biotechnological drugs, clinical pharmacology, and pharmacovigilance.
In addition to the mentioned training activities and practical-professional preparation acquired through TPV, further knowledge is also acquired through the autonomous selection of training activities from those provided by the study courses affiliated with the DBCF or offered by the University.

Scientific expert or consultant in the pharmaceutical, cosmetic and food sectors, Pharmacist, Chemist The completion of the LM in CTF offers the following career opportunities: pharmaceutical industry; chemical, toxicological, chemical-clinical and biochemistry-clinical analysis laboratories; public and private quality control laboratories; National Health Service structures; School (graduates with sufficient credits in appropriate subject groups may, as provided by current legislation, participate in the admission tests for secondary teaching training paths), Universities and other public and private entities; drug distribution and marketing.

Final Exam Characteristics The final exam consists of preparing and publicly discussing an original experimental thesis, developed by the student under the supervision of a faculty member of a discipline present in the study program, related to topics relevant to the curricular disciplines. The experimental thesis may be carried out at a university laboratory, a company or research institution, in Italy or abroad, with which the University has signed a convention or international agreements.

The final exam includes the completion of a practical assessment of professional skills acquired through the preceding practical internship, aimed at verifying the candidate's technical preparation level for the qualification to practice as a Pharmacist. The final dissertation is conducted in the presence of a graduation committee composed of subject experts and members designated by the professional order; the student must demonstrate mastery of the thesis topic, critical ability and good communication skills.

The final assessment methods and criteria take into account the student's entire academic career within the Study Program, the timing and methods of CFU acquisition, previous training activities, and the final exam. The final grade is expressed on a scale of 110 with possible honors.

Required Knowledge for Admission To access the study program, it is necessary to hold a secondary school diploma or another foreign qualification recognized as equivalent. Additionally, knowledge of English at a level of at least A2/2, as defined by the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages, is required.

Students enrolled in the LM in CTF must possess adequate initial preparation in chemistry, biology and mathematics, which is verified through the TOLC-F test. This test is mandatory but not binding for the enrollment procedure.

Minimum scores are established for the evaluation of the test. For students who do not achieve these scores, faculty members verify the recovery of required training obligations that students must complete within the first year of study.

Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area The entire study program progresses from basic and prerequisite disciplines towards characteristic and related disciplines. Master's graduates acquire knowledge and understanding capabilities in the chemical, biological, pharmaceutical and pharmacological fields. In particular, they gain knowledge of the scientific approach to solving problems related to the structural design of biologically active molecules, synthesis, development, evaluation of biological and/or pharmacological activity, pharmaceutical formulation, quality control in production, patenting procedures and drug registration, as well as knowledge of the legislative contexts in which pharmaceutical industries and pharmacies operate. By consulting scientific literature, the master's graduate must be able to promptly receive scientific and technological innovations occurring rapidly in these fields and be able to develop and apply original ideas at the forefront of current knowledge. Assessment of learning involves traditional exams where the candidate demonstrates to a committee of subject experts their ability to assimilate and integrate acquired knowledge and communicate it clearly and unambiguously. In addition to exams, written reports and intermediate discussions on specific topics may be required, depending on the assessment and judgment of course instructors. These knowledge assessment types aim to verify whether the student is able to integrate and form judgments on acquired knowledge and their ability to continue studies and autonomously acquire specific knowledge.

Area of Basic Disciplines Basic courses prepare the student to address subsequent characteristic topics by acquiring a strictly scientific approach. The student must know the principles underlying chemistry and biology at the molecular level and apply basic mathematical operators of thermodynamics. They must understand the correlation between the molecular context and the complexity of organization typical of cells, tissues, organs, systems and organisms.

The student must acquire in-depth knowledge of general and inorganic chemistry and analytical chemistry, especially focused on the analysis of complex systems, including biological systems. Particular importance is given to organic chemistry as a central discipline for the subsequent study of biochemistry, pharmacology and pharmaceutical chemistry. The student must know the physical and chemical processes regulating a living organism and its relationship with the external environment, including physiological processes occurring within it. They must know the eukaryotic cell, the organization and development of animal tissues, and human anatomy of organs and systems. They must know plant and animal biology, the basic principles of the immune system organization and pathogenic mechanisms of viruses, bacteria and parasites.

Area of Characteristic Disciplines - Chemical-Pharmaceutical-Technological Field The courses in the Chemical-Pharmaceutical-Technological area include disciplines contributing to defining the following thematic areas of learning:
1) Synthesis and molecular aspects of active pharmaceutical ingredients
2) Formulation and "delivery" techniques of a drug and legislation

Thematic Area 1: Starting from basic knowledge of organic chemistry, the student must know the issues related to molecular structures associated with various drug classes, deepening aspects related to structure/activity relationships and synthesis and production processes of active ingredients. The student must understand the main models for studying the pharmaceutical activity of an organic molecule, its pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics, always at the molecular level. The student must understand the main mechanisms of action of an active ingredient, correlating molecular structures to the biological properties of molecules, including their toxicology.

Through practical exercises consisting of 4 single-seat laboratories for a total of 160 hours of activity, the student will have the opportunity to apply the theoretical knowledge acquired in various courses, being able to perform analyses and preparations of pharmaceutical active ingredients. The student must also learn to use the main laboratory tools, demonstrating the ability to process experimental data obtained. The student will also be trained in bibliographic research and report writing.

Thematic Area 2: This thematic area aims to provide the student with knowledge and skills to evaluate different drug administration methods and related formulation techniques. The student must know the methodologies for preparing and controlling various pharmaceutical forms within the context of evaluating criticalities related to incorrect application in different stages of the supply chain, following good practices. They must know the functioning of production techniques applied to various pharmaceutical types, in order to be able to assess suitability and quality in compliance with hygiene and safety criteria. Additionally, the student must know the legislation related to drug production, registration and distribution. In this area, a single-seat laboratory activity (40 hours) is also provided where the student will personally prepare a pharmaceutical/galenic formulation and must be able to draft a "master format". Finally, the student will acquire competencies in the food sector through the study of molecular processes associated with food preparation and metabolism, integrated with nutraceutical aspects.

Area of Characteristic Disciplines - Biological and Pharmacological Disciplines The student must know the issues of biochemical mechanisms underlying the correct functioning of the cell and related problems linked to pathology, deepening aspects related to the identification of a biological process, its analysis and interpretation of results, prioritizing, when possible, the holistic aspect of analysis. The student must acquire and understand the main models for studying cellular and molecular biology, being able to describe with appropriate scientific language the notions related to the functioning of biological processes and their interpretation.

The student must know the principles of drug functioning, drug/receptor interactions and types of drug administration and intake routes, pharmacokinetics (absorption, distribution, biotransformation, excretion, pharmacokinetic models), pharmacodynamics (drug/receptor interaction and mechanisms of action), factors modifying drug response, drug interactions and side effects, residue formation and withdrawal times. They must know the concepts of pharmacovigilance and pharmacosurveillance and the relevant current regulations. They must also understand the fundamental concepts of statistics and their main applications in medicine, especially regarding clinical "trials". Through practical exercises, the student will have the opportunity to apply the theoretical knowledge acquired, being able to perform biochemical analyses associated with the pharmaceutical activity of some active ingredients. The student must also learn to use the main laboratory tools in the biological field, acquiring the basic knowledge to work with animal tissues and to follow the metabolism of a drug in an organism.

Critical Judgment.
The student's critical judgment develops progressively throughout their studies, is verified by themselves and the instructor at the end of each course, and reaches its completion during the preparation of the experimental master's thesis. This involves collecting and critically analyzing international scientific literature, designing, applying, and developing research protocols, collecting and interpreting data, deriving original insights and solutions. Conducting an original research work in the laboratory, including analysis and evaluation of the obtained results, under the supervision of the advisor, is the candidate's responsibility, and the degree to which this autonomy is achieved will contribute to the final master's degree grade along with an overall assessment of their academic curriculum.
Learning Ability.
The master's graduate has developed:
the learning abilities necessary to continuously and autonomously update their knowledge;
the learning abilities necessary to develop their professional skills in a national and international work environment;
the learning abilities necessary to pursue further studies in doctoral schools with a high degree of autonomy.
Achieving these objectives is supported by the experiences gained during the professional internship and the preparation of the experimental thesis, as well as participation in professionalizing activities such as seminars on advanced topics.
The main tools for instructors to verify the achievement of this objective are the passing exams, in-course assessments, intermediate and final laboratory tests, with the presentation of reports prepared individually and autonomously by the student.
Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area The ability to apply acquired knowledge is developed by the student during attendance at practical exercises and theoretical-practical laboratory courses that involve solving experimental problems, including interdisciplinary ones, and, like theoretical course exams, passing a final exam. Specifically, the master's graduate is able to perform qualitative analyses (drug identification and purity tests), quantitative analyses (drug dosage), synthesis of new active ingredients, evaluation of their biological activity, and preparation of pharmaceutical formulations. The master's graduate also possesses the necessary competencies for the production and technological control of pharmaceutical forms as described in the Pharmacopoeias. Finally, the ability to apply acquired knowledge is completed through the master's thesis, which is mandatory and experimental. In particular, a good knowledge of English, mastery of laboratory techniques, and chemical, pharmaceutical, biological, pharmacological, and statistical methodologies must be acquired and demonstrated. The application of acquired knowledge is also required during the internship, where the master's student performs, as per regulations, a period of activity at a public pharmacy. In this case, the learning is certified by the Pharmacist Tutor in an internship log, endorsed by the President of the Provincial Order of Pharmacists where the pharmacy is located.
Basic Disciplines Area The student must be able to describe various topics with precise language and correct scientific terminology, and demonstrate the ability to logically and sequentially analyze cause-effect sequences of chemical and biological processes, clearly understanding the interdisciplinary nature of different subjects.
The student must also be able to understand why different topics are addressed in relation to their importance, particularly for understanding chemistry, including chemical analysis, biology, and physiology.
The student must also develop an independent judgment on the cultural and professional importance of the topics covered, referring to the centrality of basic disciplines in relation to future professional practice. The study of a foreign language should provide the student with the potential for internationalization and understanding of international scientific productivity.
Learning is supported by self-assessment tests (in-course tests) and knowledge of examination methods. Additionally, to support students in exam preparation, teaching materials are provided in the form of PowerPoint presentations of lectures and handouts with practical deepening on topics covered during lectures.
Characterizing Disciplines Area - Chemical-Pharmaceutical-Technological Field The student must be able to describe with precise language and correct scientific terminology the processes of the drug synthesis chain, including the molecular principles underlying therapies. They must also demonstrate the ability to sequentially analyze cause-effect sequences of processes underlying drug function, clearly understanding the interdisciplinary nature of different subjects. They must also apply acquired knowledge to identify the causes of problems in given cases and suggest appropriate intervention measures.
All training activities in the relevant thematic areas are integrated with individual practical activities aimed at consolidating the understanding of operational skills and, where relevant, the ability to interpret data. Students are therefore strongly motivated and stimulated to engage in discussion and debate. For some disciplines, self-assessment tests are regularly organized. Reference teaching materials are provided to students in the form of PowerPoint presentations, handouts prepared by instructors, links to relevant websites, and software with practical deepening on topics covered during lectures.
Characterizing Disciplines Area - Biological and Pharmacological Disciplines Field The student must be able to describe with precise language and correct scientific terminology all aspects of pharmacology and biochemistry, including aspects related to clinical trials, diagnostics, and ethical/professional issues.
All training activities are integrated with individual practical activities aimed at consolidating the understanding of operational skills and, where relevant, the ability to interpret data. Students are therefore strongly motivated and stimulated to engage in discussion and debate. For some disciplines, self-assessment tests are regularly organized. Reference teaching materials are provided to students in the form of PowerPoint presentations, handouts prepared by instructors, links to relevant websites, and software with practical deepening on topics covered during lectures.
The theoretical knowledge and practical skills acquired during courses are consolidated by students during the mandatory internship activities at contracted pharmacies or hospital pharmacies. The internship aims to provide students with the necessary knowledge for proper professional practice.
The internship is regulated by a specific regulation:
Internship Regulation
Communication Skills.
Master's graduates acquire the necessary knowledge, characteristic of a drug expert, to communicate clearly and unambiguously, using appropriate terminology, with both specialists and non-specialists in the field, as well as within research groups. This result, in accordance with European regulations, also requires a good knowledge of English, both spoken and written. These characteristics are gradually acquired (also through student mobility programs promoted by the Faculty) and progressively verified throughout the studies by instructors. Communication skills are evaluated at the conclusion of studies during the oral presentation of the experimental thesis with the aid of multimedia tools.
Expected Occupational and Professional Outcomes for Graduates.
Scientific Expert or Information Specialist in the pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and dietary food sector, Pharmacist, Chemist The completion of the Master's in CTF offers the following occupational opportunities: pharmaceutical industry; chemical, toxicological, chemical-clinical, and biochemical-clinical analysis laboratories; public and private quality control laboratories; National Health Service structures; School (graduates with sufficient credits in appropriate subject groups may, as per current legislation, participate in admission tests for secondary teaching training paths), Universities, and other public and private entities; drug distribution and marketing.
Official Teaching and Assessment Languages.
ITALIAN
Competencies Associated with the Role.
Scientific Expert or Information Specialist in the pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and dietary food sector, Pharmacist, Chemist The Master's provides professional competencies related to: preparation of pharmaceutical forms in industry; drug control in public or private drug control laboratories; storage, preservation, and distribution of drugs in wholesale trade; preparation, control, storage, and distribution of drugs in public pharmacies; preparation, control, storage, and distribution of drugs in hospitals (public and private hospital pharmacies); dissemination of information and advice in the drug, cosmetic, dietary, nutritional, and herbal sectors for maintaining and safeguarding health; production of phytomedicines, antiparasitic agents, and medical devices; analysis and control of physical-chemical and hygienic characteristics of mineral waters; analysis and quality control of food products, including those for special diets and dietetic products; production and control of medical devices and medical-surgical devices; transformation, mixing, concentration, and fractionation of plant parts and their derivatives for therapeutic or herbal use; formulation, production, packaging, quality control, stability, and toxicological evaluation of cosmetic products; pharmacovigilance and monitoring of adverse effects of drugs in the population; regulatory affairs expert in the pharmaceutical industry.
Role in the Work Context.
Scientific Expert or Information Specialist in the pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and dietary food sector, Pharmacist, Chemist The Master's program in CTF primarily aims to train a professional who operates: as an expert in drug research and development and health products (herbal, diagnostic, chemical-clinical, cosmetic, dietetic, nutritional, medical-surgical devices, medical devices, health articles, etc.) at industrial, public, and private centers, and universities; in production at the pharmaceutical, chemical, cosmetic, and dietetic-food industry level; as an expert in quality control, stability, and toxicological evaluation of drugs and other health products; as a scientific information specialist on drugs and health products.
Description of Specific Educational Objectives.
The Master's degree in Pharmaceutical Chemistry and Technology (CTF) aims to provide adequate basic scientific preparation, linguistic and computer support, and a set of knowledge necessary to address the entire sequence of the complex multidisciplinary process, starting from structural design, synthesis, development, evaluation of biological and/or pharmacological activity, and preparation of the pharmaceutical form, leading to quality control in drug production (according to the standards codified in the Pharmacopoeias), health products (medical-surgical devices, health articles, cosmetics, dietetic products, herbal products, medical devices, diagnostic and chemical-clinical products), and patenting and registration procedures. The training path aims to form a professional capable of operating in complex environments with appropriate critical analysis tools, specific design capabilities, and analytical skills.
The main design choices underlying the study program have led to a credit organization that provides the main knowledge in basic disciplines during the first two years of the course. In particular, basic disciplines in the chemical, physical-mathematical, biological, and medical fields (CHIM/01, CHIM/02, CHIM/03, CHIM/06, MAT/04, FIS/01, BIO/09, BIO/13, BIO/15, BIO/16, MED/04, and MED/07) are complemented by language skills (B2 English level), workplace safety regulations, and computer knowledge that integrate the basic cultural background.
Regarding the characterizing training activities, scheduled in the third and fourth years, the CFUs in chemical-pharmaceutical, technological, and biological-pharmacological disciplines (CHIM/08, CHIM/09, CHIM/10, BIO/10, BIO/11, BIO/14, and SECS-P/07) are distributed to achieve a proper balance between different disciplinary fields.
Starting from the fourth year, students can complete the Evaluative Practical Internship (EPI). The fifth year of the course is primarily reserved for concluding the internship and preparing the final exam.
Free-choice CFUs allow students to independently complete their personal preparation.
The entire training path has been designed to form a master's graduate who operates in all departments of the pharmaceutical industrial production, in chemical, toxicological, chemical-clinical, and biochemical-clinical analysis laboratories, in public and private quality control laboratories, in National Health Service structures, in universities, and in other public and private entities, as well as in drug distribution and marketing.
Upon completion of the Master's degree and the corresponding professional qualification, the CTF Master's graduate can also practice the profession of pharmacist at both territorial and hospital levels, as well as engage in related professional activities and the profession of chemist.

Final exam characteristics To be admitted to take the graduation exam, the student must have attended all courses and passed the respective exams.
Pursuant to Articles 1 and 3 of Law 8 November 2021, n. 163, the final exam for the Single Cycle Master's Degree in Dentistry and Dental Prosthodontics - class LM-46 enables the exercise of the Dentist profession. For this purpose, the final exam includes the performance of a Practical Assessment Test (PAT) of professional skills acquired through a Practical Assessment Internship (PAI) within the study courses, aimed at verifying the candidate's practical preparation level for professional qualification, which precedes the thesis discussion. The PAT is organized through the student's discussion of 3 multidisciplinary clinical cases treated as the primary operator during the PAI, involving multidisciplinary treatment plans with services related to the majority of disciplines covered by the PAI, according to the procedures outlined in the protocol drawn up by the Permanent Conference of Presidents of Dentistry and Dental Prosthetics Degree Courses, in agreement with the National Dentist Register Commission.
For the successful completion of the PAT, students receive a suitability assessment, after which they proceed to the thesis discussion.
Therefore, for the attainment of the Master's Degree, an original thesis elaborated by the student under the guidance of a supervisor is required. The thesis, written in English, must meet the requirements of a research work on clinical or basic themes, or may take the form of a compilation.
The final graduation exam grade will be expressed in hundredths, with possible honors.
Required knowledge for admission To access the Single Cycle Master's Degree Course in Dentistry and Dental Prosthodontics LM-46, a secondary school diploma or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent is required.
An adequate initial preparation, acquired through previous studies, in mathematics, physics, chemistry and biology is necessary.
Access to the course is granted upon passing an English-language admission test, prepared by the Ministry.
The access modalities to the Single Cycle Master's Degree Course in Dentistry and Dental Prosthodontics LM-46 and the content of the admission test are established by Law 2 August 1999 n. 264 "Provisions on access to university courses" (GU n. 183 of 6-8-1999), as well as by annual ministerial decrees concerning both the modalities and content of admission tests for nationally programmed courses, and the definition of available places for admission to the Single Cycle Master's Degree Course in Dentistry and Dental Prosthodontics LM-46.
Students admitted to the course with a score below a predetermined minimum threshold will be assigned additional educational obligations to be fulfilled within the first year of the course.
The adequacy of the student's preparation will be verified according to the modalities indicated in the Study Course Didactic Regulations.
Additionally, certification of English language knowledge at B2 level of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages of the Council of Europe is required.
Knowledge and understanding.
General area The Master's graduate possesses advanced knowledge regarding the anatomy and physiology of the organs of the stomatognathic apparatus.
The Master's graduate knows the etiological factors and understands the pathogenic mechanisms of the main diseases of the oral-facial district. Furthermore, they know the rational bases of various preventive measures for odontostomatological pathologies currently recognized as effective.
The Master's graduate knows the active principles and mechanisms of action of drugs indicated for the therapy of odontostomatological diseases, as well as for the techniques of anesthesia practiced in the oral cavity.
The Master's graduate possesses competence regarding the healing mechanisms of tissues and surgical wounds, as well as regarding the osteointegration mechanisms of endosseous implants and the biomechanics of orthodontic tooth movements.
The Master's graduate knows the etiopathogenesis and prognostic evolution of neoplasms of the hard and soft tissues of the oral-facial district.
The Master's graduate is trained to establish a relationship with the patient based on their correct information, indispensable prerequisite for obtaining consent to therapy, as well as respecting their psychological dimension.
Basic disciplines The study of basic disciplines aims to help the student understand the structural organization and vital functions of the human body, pathogenic mechanisms, biological defense mechanisms, and pathological mechanisms of the immune system.
The student acquires basic knowledge of chemistry and biochemistry, biology, anatomy, histology, physiology, general pathology.
Scientific methodology and behavioral sciences The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthodontics LM-46 must possess adequate knowledge of Biostatistics and Epidemiology, as tools of the scientific method and evidence-based dentistry practice. They must also acquire the general principles of bioethics and general psychology, as indispensable references in the relationship with the patient.
General medical disciplines The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthodontics LM-46 must know the etiopathogenesis, diagnosis, therapy, and prognosis of the most frequent medical and surgical pathologies, with particular reference to those manifesting in the oral cavity. The dentist must also have received the fundamental notions of law relevant to medical-biological matters and the ethical norms of the medical profession.
Professional dental disciplines The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthodontics LM-46 must achieve solid theoretical and practical preparation in various dental-stomatological disciplines, with particular attention to the most common diagnostic pathways and therapeutic measures of reconstructive dentistry, pediatric dentistry, orthodontics and gnathology, periodontology, and oral surgery.
They must also be able to perform accurate differential diagnosis in the presence of lesions and neoplasms of the soft tissues of the oral cavity or maxillary bones.
The Dentist must also possess adequate knowledge of general and dental radiology, as well as the clinically relevant properties of dental materials.
The Dentist must additionally receive the fundamental concepts of economics for efficient management of professional activity.

Judgment autonomy.
In the Single-cycle Master's Degree in Dentistry and Dental Prosthodontics LM-46, various teaching tools are used to promote judgment autonomy. Among these, organizing teaching in small groups aims to encourage interactivity in the student-teacher relationship, while also discussing clinical cases or scientific articles aims to value the individual contribution of the student. Similarly, students may be required to prepare a monograph on a specific topic of their interest, or to work on the development of an experimental research project.
Master's graduates in Dentistry and Dental Prosthodontics LM-46 must therefore be able to:
- formulate hypotheses, collect and critically evaluate data to solve problems;
- develop personal solutions to analytical and complex problems based on information obtained through scientific methodology;
- be aware of the importance of decisions made during dental practice for patient health;
- respect colleagues and other health professionals, demonstrating the ability to work in a team and establish collaborative relationships;
- identify the essential elements of the dental profession, including moral and ethical principles and legal responsibilities related to the profession;
- be able to recognize their own limitations in patient care, seeking other competencies for specific medical therapies when necessary.
Judgment autonomy is acquired by students through frontal, seminar, clinical internship, and TPV activities. It is verified through interactive frontal teaching, examination tests, and by assessing students' decision-making capacity in the discussion of clinical cases and the development of treatment plans.

Learning ability.
The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthodontics LM-46 is able to consult scientific databases and critically read scientific literature, applying the principles of Evidence-Based Dentistry and consciously choosing among the various opportunities for continuous updating.
The graduate knows the legislation governing the practice of the dental profession in European Union countries and is aware of the ethical principles recognized in the country where they practice.
Learning ability is acquired by students through frontal, seminar activities, and clinical internship and TPV, and is assessed through verification methods during training activities, integrating knowledge acquired during specific activities with those gained through personal study, evaluating the critical contribution demonstrated during exercises, seminars, and clinical internship, during TPV, as well as through the assessment of self-learning ability developed during the activities related to the final exam. For this purpose, the final exam includes the completion of a Practical Assessment Test (PPV) of professional skills acquired through internal TPV within the study courses, aimed at verifying the candidate's practical preparation level for professional qualification, which precedes the thesis discussion.

In this way, the Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthodontics LM-46 is able to proceed with further studies, accessing the extensive post-graduate training offer in the Dental field, which includes Specialization Schools, Master's courses, and Research Doctorates.

Application of knowledge and understanding.
General area The Master's graduate possesses specialized skills related to the clinical and instrumental diagnosis of odontostomatology diseases.
They are able to recommend effective measures for the prevention of odontostomatology diseases to patients.
They are capable of implementing medical protocols and surgical procedures for the treatment of odontostomatology diseases, also in collaboration with other healthcare professionals in a multidisciplinary approach.
They are able to correctly inform patients about the possible prognostic evolution of treated pathologies.
In particular, the Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthodontics LM-46, drawing on their familiarity with the English language, can easily access high-quality scientific evidence published internationally through specialized journals and electronic databases, as well as training events featuring internationally renowned speakers.

Basic disciplines The Master's graduates are able to apply their basic biomedical knowledge in the diagnostic assessment of the dental patient, in the choice of therapies, in the execution of surgical procedures, and in post-surgical monitoring.

Scientific methodology and behavioral sciences Master's graduates are able to use their knowledge of scientific methodology to understand the most recent scientific articles published in international literature, as well as 'classic' studies that have represented milestones in the evolution of Dentistry. Moreover, Master's graduates use scientific methodology knowledge to design original research projects and scientific reports on topics of interest to the dental profession. In particular, in-depth knowledge of the English language enables the Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthodontics LM-46 to directly consult authoritative textbooks on biostatistics, epidemiology, and research methods, which are written in English. Exposure to the principles of behavioral sciences aids the Dentist in establishing a correct relationship with the patient.

General medical disciplines
Application of knowledge and understanding The Master's graduate applies their knowledge of general medical disciplines in evaluating the general health status of the dental patient, in differential diagnosis of oral pathologies, in choosing pharmacological therapies and anesthesia techniques, in preventing surgical complications, in post-operative patient management, and in prognostic prediction.

Professional dental disciplines
The knowledge acquired by the student in learning dental science is applied in clinical activities with patients. Theoretical preparation and practical experience contribute to building the professional profile of the Dentist, as a specialist capable of diagnosing various clinical issues that may arise in the orofacial district and performing appropriate medical and surgical therapies, independently or with the contribution of other specialists, while being aware of and respecting the biological and psychological uniqueness of each patient.

Communication Skills.
The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthodontics LM-46 has been trained from the beginning of the course to establish effective communication with the patient. The development of this skill is essential to fully explain to the patient their clinical condition, the indicated therapy, the expected prognosis, as well as to instruct them on oral hygiene techniques and motivate them to adopt correct lifestyles.
It is also appropriate for the Dentist to demonstrate relational and collaborative abilities with other professional figures they interact with: fellow Dentists and Doctors, as well as the Chair Assistant and Dental Technician.
Students acquire communication skills through frontal teaching activities, the TPV, and are tested during the degree course through interactive frontal teaching, oral examination tests, verifying the ability to relate with patients during clinical internship and during the TPV where they constitute evaluation criteria, and finally, by assessing the presentation of the experimental thesis, which the graduate presents before the Degree Committee with the aid of multimedia tools.
It is relevant to emphasize that English language training facilitates the graduate's integration into the global network of professionals and the international scientific community, as well as participation in international congresses.
Planned occupational and professional opportunities for graduates.
Dentist Master's graduates in Dentistry and Dental Prosthodontics LM-46 have professional opportunities in the private practice of Dentist, after registration with the Professional Register. They may also carry out managerial activities of I° and II° level within the National Health Service, as provided by current legislation.
Specialists in reconstruction of hard dental tissues Private practice and managerial activities of I° and II° level within the National Health Service, after registration with the Professional Register, as provided by current legislation.

Specialists in Oral and Implant Surgery Private practice and managerial activities of I° and II° level within the National Health Service, after registration with the Professional Register, as provided by current legislation.
Specialists in Orthognathic Dentistry Private practice and managerial activities of I° and II° level within the National Health Service, after registration with the Professional Register, as provided by current legislation.
Official teaching and assessment language(s).
ENGLISH Associated competencies for the role.
Dentist To perform the above functions, the Dentist must have acquired basic knowledge of Anatomy, Physiology, Pathology, Pharmacology, Imaging Diagnostics, as well as specific competencies in Odontostomatology. Additionally, the Dentist must develop communication and relational skills, acquire management and planning capabilities, and mature the aptitude for continuous updating.
Specialists in reconstruction of hard dental tissues The Dentist must have theoretical and practical knowledge of the techniques and materials used in Conservative Dentistry, Endodontics and Prosthetics.
Specialists in prevention, diagnosis and therapy of pathologies of the supporting tissues of the tooth The Dentist must have theoretical and practical knowledge of techniques and materials used in Periodontology.
Specialists in Oral and Implant Surgery The Dentist must have competence and experience regarding the techniques and biomaterials used in Oral Surgery and Implantology. They must also possess solid knowledge of the anatomy of the stomatognathic apparatus.
Specialists in Orthognathic Dentistry The Dentist must have theoretical and practical knowledge of diagnostic and therapeutic procedures in orthodontics. They must also have solid knowledge of Gnathology.
Role in work context.
Dentist The Master's graduate in Dentistry and Dental Prosthodontics LM-46 performs activities related to prevention, diagnosis and therapy of diseases and congenital or acquired anomalies of teeth, mouth, jaw bones, temporomandibular joints and related tissues. The Dentist is responsible for dental rehabilitation, prescribing all necessary medications and devices for the exercise of the profession. The Dentist designs, verifies and inserts dental prosthetic devices, controlling their suitability.
The Dentist can collaborate with Maxillofacial Surgeons in the treatment of patients requiring complex rehabilitation of masticatory function and facial aesthetics.
The Dentist can collaborate with Doctors and Surgeons in the prevention, diagnosis and therapy of all pathologies that may present oral manifestations.
Specialists in reconstruction of hard dental tissues The Dentist is able to restore the function and aesthetic role of severely damaged teeth due to carious lesions, trauma, abrasion and erosion processes.
Specialists in prevention, diagnosis and therapy of pathologies of the supporting tissues of the tooth As a private practitioner or subordinate worker, the Dentist treats pathologies of the supporting tissues of the tooth, motivates the patient to adopt correct oral hygiene habits to prevent recurrence of periodontal disease, and performs surgical interventions to restore the anatomy and integrity of the supporting apparatus of the tooth.
Specialists in Oral and Implant Surgery The Dentist performs surgical interventions for the extraction of teeth even completely included in the jaw bones. Additionally, they insert in the jaw bones implants made of biocompatible material capable of osteointegration, for the rehabilitation of edentulous sites in the dental arches.
Specialists in Orthognathic Dentistry The Dentist corrects dentoalveolar and, within certain limits, skeletal malocclusions, creating more favorable occlusal conditions for the correct function of the temporomandibular joints and masticatory muscles.
Description of specific training objectives.
The Single Cycle Master's Degree course in Dentistry and Dental Prosthodontics LM-46 aims to develop the knowledge and skills necessary for the exercise of the Dentist profession, in both private and public contexts.
Among the objectives of the Single Cycle Master's Degree course in Dentistry and Dental Prosthodontics LM-46 is to equip students with basic knowledge in biomedical disciplines, aimed at understanding etiopathogenetic mechanisms, therapeutic processes and prognostic perspectives of pathologies.
Specific competencies related to prevention, diagnosis and therapy of diseases and anomalies of the stomatognathic apparatus are strengthened from the third to the fifth year.
Throughout the training path of the Single Cycle Master's Degree course in Dentistry and Dental Prosthodontics LM-46, theoretical teachings find application and verification in practical internship activities, which are fundamental for preparation to exercise the Dentist profession.
In particular, in the sixth year, clinical practice becomes the primary commitment of the student, with the aim of developing decision-making ability, operational autonomy, management skills, and relational skills with patients. Students are also involved in seminar teaching activities, aimed in particular at promoting the ability to develop interdisciplinary treatment plans.
Pursuant to Articles 1 and 3 of Law No. 163 of November 8, 2021, the final exam for the acquisition of the Single Cycle Master's Degree in Dentistry and Dental Prosthodontics - Class LM-46 authorizes the exercise of the Dentist profession. For this purpose, the final exam includes the performance of a Practical Evaluation Test (PPV) of professional skills acquired through a Practical-Valuation Internship (TPV) within the study courses, aimed at verifying the candidate's practical preparation level for authorization to exercise the profession, preceding the thesis discussion. The PPV is organized through the student's discussion of 3 multidisciplinary clinical cases treated as the primary operator during the TPV, involving multidisciplinary treatment plans with performances related to the majority of disciplines covered by the TPV, according to the modalities set by the protocol drawn up by the Permanent Conference of Presidents of Dentistry and Dental Prosthodontics Degree Courses, in agreement with the National Dentist Register Committee. For the PPV to be passed, students receive an aptitude assessment, after which they proceed to the thesis discussion. Graduates of the class must achieve the competencies specified in the specific professional profile.
Specific emphasis, as an integral and qualifying part of professional training, is placed on the professional training activity of the pre-academic title TPV. Within the 90 CFU to be acquired throughout the training path and destined for professional training activities, 30 CFU are allocated to the performance of the TPV within the study course, which involves performing, as the primary operator, practical activities in preventive, diagnostic and therapeutic fields of odontostomatology, related to disciplines of oral surgery, restorative dentistry, endodontics, implantology, pathology and oral medicine, pediatric dentistry, special dentistry, orthognathic dentistry, periodontology and prosthetics, as regulated in the modalities by the specific protocol drawn up by the Permanent Conference of Presidents of Dentistry and Dental Prosthodontics Degree Courses, in agreement with the National Dentist Register Committee. For every CFU equivalent to 25 hours reserved for the TPV, at least 20 hours of professional training activities as the primary operator are required; the remaining 5 hours may be dedicated to individual study or other professional training activities.
Pursuant to Article 2, paragraph 9 of Ministerial Decree No. 653 of July 5, 2022, TPV credits are acquired in the sixth year of the course and a quota not exceeding 30 percent of the total may be acquired in the fifth year of the course.
Finally, the thesis elaboration assesses students' ability to conduct bibliographic research and experimental, laboratory and clinical activities.
Within the seminar activities and practical internships, teachers aim to contribute to developing in students the so-called 'soft skills', which can help the Master's graduate integrate into the workplace. With this intent, students are also evaluated on their aptitude for 'team development', 'time management', 'critical thinking', 'problem solving'.
Distinctly, the use of English as the official language of the study course prepares the Master's graduate for easy consultation of international scientific databases, for the practice of Evidence-Based Dentistry, as well as for regular participation in international scientific congresses, for continuous updating.

Sustainable Industrial Pharmaceutical Biotechnologist The original combination of biotechnology linked to an industrial sector fundamental for the country in an international context with innovative and now indispensable aspects of sustainability should ensure that graduates in Sustainable Industrial Pharmaceutical Biotechnology have a growing job market. Below is a list of main career opportunities:
- Researchers in public and private sectors, conducting research, research and development, and research and management in bio-industrial production and related transformation processes; for human health needs and overall sustainable development; for managing and designing production facilities in biotechnology, pharmaceutical, diagnostic, chemical, environmental, agri-food, and renewable energy industries.
- Heads of research and development laboratories and production and quality control departments in biotechnology companies and other companies interested in sustainable biotechnology innovation, such as pharmaceutical, diagnostic, cosmetic, agri-food, chemical (fine chemistry, bioenergy, innovative materials), renewable energy, and bioeconomy sectors, or companies interested in planning industrial activities oriented toward sustainable development.
- Managers of biotechnology plants.
- Entrepreneurs of sustainable biotechnology companies, transferring innovative ideas from green, eco-sustainable, bioeconomic, and circular economy research to commercial application.
- Professionals in the evaluation of the economic, commercial, and financial impact of a biological or biotechnological technology, and the protection of industrial property and patents.
- Professionals in public and private institutions active in environmental impact analysis and environmental certification services.
- Heads of public and private laboratories for biotechnology, environmental, agri-food, cosmetic, chemical, clinical, control, and research services.
- Commercial managers for developing and managing presentations of sustainable biotechnological products or processes to specialized or non-specialized audiences.
- Managers in bodies responsible for drafting patent regulations regarding the exploitation of products and/or processes of the bioindustry; commercial organizations and documentation.
- Employees in communication of science, integrating their knowledge with communication science, to disseminate biotechnology in specialized environments and to the general public through traditional and innovative media or through scientific dissemination agencies and specialized press.
- Employees in companies and institutions for quality certification.
- Trainers, integrating scientific knowledge with communication, sociology, and educational sciences for transferring knowledge and technical-scientific training and updating.
- Self-employed professionals, for example, registration in the Biologists' Register, the Chemists' Order, or the National Association of Italian Biotechnologists, after passing the state exam.
- Roles and profiles that may increasingly occupy positions in emerging production processes, where the spread of intelligent technologies induces demand for profiles dedicated to monitoring, storage, and analysis of information generated.
- Technical and professional profiles linked to the key of the future in the digital factory: big data analysis, artificial intelligence, and biotechnology.
Graduates will also be well prepared to pursue further education in Doctoral Programs, Specialization Schools, and Second-Level Master's Programs at national and international universities and research centers.
Collaboration with the Department of Educational Sciences, Humanities, and Intercultural Communication at our university will also allow the Master's graduate in Sustainable Industrial Pharmaceutical Biotechnology to effectively perform teaching functions in the following teaching categories: Code A060 - Natural Sciences, Chemistry and Geography, Microbiology and Code A057 - Food Sciences, thereby hopefully filling a gap in the educational and learning of Italian students in the field of Sciences compared to the European average, as recently described in the OECD-PISA 2018 report.
Final Exam Characteristics To be admitted to the final exam, all credits in the training activities specified in the study plan must be earned.
The training activities related to the preparation of the final exam for the degree and the corresponding verification in the preparation of a final thesis, conducted under the guidance of one or more supervisors and consisting of two individual works, the first based on in-depth analysis of topics covered in seminar activities, through meta-analysis and data mining in teamworking with final individual processing, the second derived from an original individual experimental activity (related to a project or carried out within an internship) in Italian or foreign university laboratories, or in research and development laboratories of external industries and accredited bodies, according to the procedures established in the Regulations.
The dissertation must demonstrate mastery of the topics, critical ability, the ability to work independently, and a good level of communication skills. In addition to the experimental content and its scientific value, clarity of exposition, synthesis ability, and the degree of experience gained in using multimedia communication tools are evaluated.
Required Knowledge for Admission To access the Master's Degree Course in "Sustainable Industrial Pharmaceutical Biotechnology" (LM-8), it is necessary to hold a university degree or a three-year diploma or another foreign-acquired title recognized as suitable.
To be admitted to the Master's Degree Course, certain curricular requirements and an adequate personal preparation must be possessed.
Curricular Requirements:
Curricular requirements are met by holding a degree in one of the following classes of D.M. 270/2004 (or corresponding in the former D.M. 509/99):
-Biotechnology ─ L-2
-Biological Sciences ─ L-13
-Agricultural and Forestry Sciences and Technologies ─ L-25
-Food and Agricultural Sciences and Technologies ─ L-26
-Chemical Sciences and Technologies ─ L-27
-Pharmaceutical Sciences and Technologies ─ L-29
-Physical Sciences and Technologies ─ L-30
Graduates from different degree classes may also be admitted provided they have earned at least 75 ECTS credits in the specified disciplinary sectors:
BIO/10 Biochemistry BIO/11 Molecular Biology BIO/18 Genetics BIO/19 General Microbiology CHIM/01-CHIM/12
MAT/01-MAT/09
FIS/01-FIS/08
Additionally, a B2 level English language certification according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR) is required.
Foreign students must demonstrate adequate knowledge of the Italian language. Students lacking such linguistic skills must attend specific courses to reach the required level within additional training activities (Article 10, Paragraph 5, Letter d).
Verification of Personal Preparation:
Verification consists of an interview or a test. The verification methods will be detailed in the course's didactic regulations.
Knowledge and Understanding.
Biotechnology and Biomolecular Area To effectively combine knowledge and skills, the new Master's Degree in Sustainable Industrial Pharmaceutical Biotechnology was co-designed with scientific, humanistic, economic, legal departments, and especially with companies. The training path leaves ample space for co-teaching and industrial and extra-academic seminar activities on topics not covered by conventional courses, thus benefiting from experiential training from the workplace. Students will be trained using innovative and immersive teaching methods, with laboratories spread across the territory, prioritizing the development of passion, interest, curiosity, emotional intelligence, teamwork ability versus a traditionally very individualistic academic path in Italy.
The Master's graduate in Sustainable Industrial Pharmaceutical Biotechnology:
- Knows sustainable methods for the design, production, purification, and development of bioactive molecules of pharmaceutical or diagnostic interest
- Knows biocatalytic methods necessary for the requalification of industrial processes
- Understands and applies spectroscopic and computational techniques used for determining the structure of biological macromolecules
- Understands a production process scheme for a biotechnological product, and selects the most appropriate process based on the type of product to isolate and the required purity, knowing how to perform material and energy balances for multi-component systems in single equipment and complex systems
- Knows specific technological platforms ('omics', post-genomic platforms, high-throughput screening systems, molecular graphics programs, big data analysis)
- Is able to analyze and discuss with mastery issues in organic chemistry, bio-organic chemistry, biochemistry, molecular biology, life cycle thinking, and understand the methodologies used for such studies
- Knowledge of technology transfer and intellectual property
- Can propose experimental strategies, design, plan, and manage processes through the selection and application of appropriate analytical methods
- Can apply the 10 top skills indicated by the third World Economic Forum
Bioinformatics and Industrial Area The Master's Degree in Sustainable Industrial Pharmaceutical Biotechnology aims to train new professionals who, in addition to a deep knowledge of biomolecular and bioinformatics sciences, also possess specific knowledge of sustainability applied to the biotechnology-pharmaceutical industrial field, in its scientific, economic, environmental, and international regulatory aspects. To achieve this goal, integrated and consequentially coordinated scientific-disciplinary teachings will be used, grouped into five thematic training areas (Pharmaceutical Products, Biobased Products, Sustainability, Bioinformatics & Big Data, International Management & Regulatory Affairs) to arrive at a completely original specialist and professional knowledge structure, representing the most innovative aspect of biological sciences related to drugs and industrial biotechnology applications, allowing students to understand and manage the main technologies applicable to development and resource management issues.
The Master's graduate:
- Possesses solid chemical, biochemical, and bioinformatics knowledge of the structure-function relationships of biological macromolecules and connected cellular processes
- Possesses solid knowledge of instrumental and methodological approaches for the sustainable and green design, preparation, and production of synthetic and biotechnological drugs
- Possesses solid knowledge of instrumental and methodological approaches for studying and characterizing bioactive molecules and biological macromolecules
- Knows the fundamental procedures in various fields of industrial biotechnology, with particular attention to multidisciplinary approaches
- Acquires in-depth knowledge of methodologies applied to the design, production, and characterization of bioactive products and biomaterials in a biorefinery, bioeconomy, and circular economy perspective
- Knows the latest developments in the production of biofuels, bioplastics, and biomaterials from waste, understanding the evolution of a bioprocess from laboratory scale to pilot scale and then to industrial scale
- Acquires in-depth knowledge of environmental impact assessment analyses of industrial biotechnology processes and products in an integrated sustainability perspective
- Possesses solid methodological knowledge for performing big data analysis in computational biochemistry, also considering their applications in industrial biotechnology and Industry 4.0
- Knows in detail the scientific elements for international business development, strategies and policies for internationalization, and related legislative, regulatory, and patent aspects of biotechnology compared to national and international trends.
The aforementioned knowledge is acquired through activities involving participation in frontal lectures, integrated for each teaching with experimental didactic laboratories, single-seat activities, and interactive teaching. Knowledge will be verified at the final exam for each teaching course through written and/or oral tests designed to evaluate the use of logical rigor, understanding of sustainable biotechnological processes, and, where possible, the ability to work in teams.
The language used will be English, allowing students to gain fluency in the sector's reference language, refine their presentation and communication skills in scientific terminology, and facilitate direct interaction with international industry experts or those providing seminar activities.
A significant part of the knowledge will be acquired through the acquisition and experimentation of Soft Skills (the 10 top skills indicated by the third World Economic Forum) and seminar activities, also delivered as webinars by prominent figures from the industrial, international academic, or extra-academic sectors, internship activities, interviews, and visits to biotech-pharma and sustainability sector companies and institutions, allowing students to deepen additional professional and multidisciplinary knowledge, enabling a meaningful understanding of real-time evolution in the production world, fostering the development of problem-solving abilities in broader contexts than conventional ones.
These additional professional and multidisciplinary knowledge will include topics such as: Socioeconomics, Bioeconomy, Circular Economy, Ethics, Industry 4.0, Green Chemistry, New Drugs, Precision Medicine, -omics, Eco-innovation, Globalization, EU Law, Bioprocess Technology, Sustainable Biochemicals, Systems & Synthetic Biology, Cell as a Factory, From Discovery to Product, Biotechnology & Health, Sustainable Health, Rare Diseases, Advanced Therapeutics, Digital Transformation, Innovative Services, EU Project Design, as well as regulations related to patent legislation, product authorization procedures, and economic dynamics of the biotechnology sector, characteristics of sector companies, investments, and funding sources, with particular attention to international funding sources.
These seminar and internship activities will be an integral and foundational part of the training plan and will constitute highly qualifying moments in the training process. Master's students will be required to deepen one or more topics covered in seminar activities through meta-analysis and data mining in teams to produce an original individual work to be included in the final thesis.
