Judgment Autonomy.
The specialized and professional knowledge structure, entirely original for the Master's Degree in Sustainable Industrial Pharmaceutical Biotechnology, has been completely designed to maximize the student's judgment autonomy, both through the highly multidisciplinary nature of the content of the courses and industrial and extra-academic seminar activities, as well as through the international structure the course aims to have, and also through innovative teaching methodologies (single-seat laboratories, specialized seminars and internships, cross-cutting training and soft skills, direct interaction with prominent figures in the biopharmaceutical sector and sustainability, Problem-based learning, Design & System thinking, interactive and immersive teaching with augmented reality, Virtual Lab - Virtual Interaction for Training and Analysis Lab, immersive education; i.e. Simulation of a pharmaceutical production process; Fab Lab, Santa Chiara Lab, COIL – Collaborative Online International Learning) with which such content is delivered. The acquisition of judgment autonomy will also be achieved through the acquisition of the 10 top skills outlined by the World Economic Forum: 1) Complex Problem Solving; 2) Critical Thinking; 3) Creativity; 4) People Management; 5) Coordinating with others; 6) Emotional Intelligence; 7) Judgment and Decision Making; 8) Service Orientation; 9) Negotiation; and 10) Cognitive Flexibility (https://www.ideatovalue.com/inno/nickskillicorn/2016/09/leaders-agree-creativity-will-3rd-important-work-skill-2020/). The Master's Degree in Sustainable Industrial Pharmaceutical Biotechnology aims to train a new professional with high-level managerial responsibilities in the biopharmaceutical sector; a hybrid, versatile, multi-competent, and cross-disciplinary figure capable of occupying responsible roles in an industrial sector crucial for the country, for which the acquisition of adequate judgment autonomy becomes indispensable for the required managerial position.

The exclusive use of English will continuously prompt the student to engage in comparisons with international environments and information, further stimulating the exercise of comparative evaluation and thus the further development of judgment autonomy.

This is complemented by the final thesis, which will further encourage the student to make autonomous choices and will consist of two individual works: the first based on in-depth analysis through meta-analysis and data mining in teamwork with a final individual report, the second derived from an original individual experimental activity in Italian or foreign university laboratories, or in research and development laboratories of accredited external companies and institutions.

The Master's graduate acquires through the above tools the ability to integrate knowledge learned in highly multidisciplinary fields and apply them – through their judgment autonomy – to new and interdisciplinary situations and problems, to formulate autonomous judgments in relation to the ideation, planning, conduct, coordination, and the selection of the most appropriate procedures, protocols, methodologies, and technological platforms, to the ability to interact appropriately with technical staff, as well as critical evaluation of the outcomes of industrial production, research and development, intellectual property valorization, business management, promotion, and development of scientific and technological innovation, especially in relation to themes, including ethical, environmental, economic, bioeconomic, and social aspects, and sustainability related to the biotechnology sector.

The versatile knowledge acquired and the applied teaching methodologies lead the student to the ability to solve problems in broader (multidisciplinary) contexts than those in which they were acquired and to critically evaluate limitations and opportunities, as well as discuss scientific, practical, and ethical aspects.

Based on these experiences, the knowledge acquired in the teaching courses, the internship, and the final thesis, the Master's graduate in Sustainable Industrial Pharmaceutical Biotechnology will acquire transferable action and judgment autonomy in different research, research and development, production contexts, based on:
- the ability to optimally choose in the design, planning, and management of sustainable biotechnological processes for the production and isolation of bioactive and bio-beneficial products of industrial and commercial interest
- the ability to select the most appropriate experimental procedures and instrumental and computational techniques for the structural and functional characterization of different types of biomolecules and biosystems
- the ability to critically evaluate the results obtained and the final outcomes of projects
- the ability to evaluate the life cycle of processes and products, adopting a circular, bioeconomic, environmental, ethical, and social sustainability perspective
- synergistic integration between analytical and synthetic aspects aimed at defining general methods for the study, modification, and sustainable industrial management of biosystems and biomolecules
- the ability to express autonomous judgments on the applicability and commercial potential of theoretical knowledge
- the ability to retrieve and critically evaluate data and information from international scientific literature
- the ability to interact effectively in diverse work environments and on different topics, demonstrating flexibility.

Judgment autonomy is acquired through laboratories, focus groups, and the final project, and is verified through passing exams, practical activities, and the final exam.

Learning Ability.
Regarding autonomous learning abilities, the Master's graduate in Sustainable Industrial Pharmaceutical Biotechnology is capable of deepening complex themes in their field of expertise, developing innovative techniques in the field of pharmaceutical biotechnology, proposing solutions, working independently, and continuing advanced studies in biotechnology, knowing how to combine knowledge in bio-molecular and chemical fields with management competencies and indispensable elements of socio-economic and environmental sustainability and themes related to the profound digital transformation of the Health and Industry 4.0 world.

The Master's graduate in Sustainable Industrial Pharmaceutical Biotechnology must enhance their aptitude for study and scientific and professional updating, so that these characteristics can be exercised even after obtaining the Master's degree, for example, by consulting specialized databases, learning innovative technologies, and acquiring advanced knowledge tools for continuous knowledge updating. Given the dynamism of the biotechnology sector, especially in the context of sustainability, which is the focus of the study program, and the high competitiveness of the field, the Master's graduate must also acquire the habit of updating in the context of new biotechnological technologies for the sustainable production of drugs and bioactive substances, national and international regulatory provisions, sustainable development, international management, bioeconomy, circular economy, renewable resources, and ethical, social, and communication-related topics.

The Master's graduate in Sustainable Industrial Pharmaceutical Biotechnology must be able to evaluate cost-benefit ratios and environmental impact in the design and planning for the production of new biotechnological products and processes, analyze problems, and choose the most effective methodological approaches for optimal resolution within a production and research context.

The Master's graduate in Sustainable Industrial Pharmaceutical Biotechnology is therefore capable of:
- independently deepening complex themes in their field of expertise
- independently developing innovative techniques in their field of expertise
- working independently and continuing advanced studies in biotechnology

The learning ability of Master's graduates should also be interpreted in light of the prospects, not necessarily exclusive, of accessing further levels of education (master's, PhD, specialized schools) and developing and organizing self-learning paths that enable continuous professional training towards very diverse product sectors but requiring biotechnological approaches, or towards biotechnological sectors requiring sustainable approaches, in order to implement the ability to solve problems in further multidisciplinary contexts.

The learning ability, acquired through passing exams, seminars, laboratories, and internships, will be assessed during the exams through the elaboration of reports that, starting from the experimental activities carried out and the knowledge acquired, are personalized and updated based on bibliographic research, database consultations, and group discussions between students and/or experts from various biotechnology sectors and/or other product sectors. At the end of the training path, therefore, it will be possible to evaluate the learning ability, which will consist in the analysis and evaluation of the ability to process, present, and discuss the project developed as the thesis.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Biotechnological and Biomolecular Area. Within the courses, through a continuous exchange between theory and practice, between knowledge acquisition and their application, on a multidisciplinary and highly innovative basis, the ability to:
- conduct research for collecting and comparing metadata on databases, even through big data, with the ability to understand, discuss, and present scientific data and information. In all teaching courses, single-seat laboratory activities, tests, and in-course exercises are provided to create a continuous exchange between theory and practice, between knowledge acquisition and application, thus developing the ability to apply what has been learned.
- apply knowledge in the context of research project management, in the design of entrepreneurial initiatives for research valorization (spin-offs, start-ups), and in compiling authorization procedures and ensuring compliance with international regulations (compliance, regulatory affairs, etc.).
- correctly read sector-specific regulatory norms.
- apply acquired competencies to correct writing, oral communication, and the presentation of results and projects.

Bioinformatics and Industrial Area. The final thesis, as the concluding element of the entire knowledge acquisition process, will serve as an additional tool to develop independence and critical awareness on the student's part regarding their training in the context of sustainable pharmaceutical biotechnology. Indeed, after completing an internship in a research laboratory or in a research and development department of a company operating in the pharmaceutical biotechnology sector or in the sustainability sector, under the guidance of a supervisor, the student must demonstrate having acquired autonomous choice-making ability and project planning skills in the most innovative technological fields, using the most advanced tools.

Based on their autonomy in managing knowledge, acquired also in relation to the knowledge provided by the professionalizing Master's program, the Master's graduate will be able to work with broad autonomy, having developed full awareness to evaluate the main sustainability discriminants for the production of biotechnological products and processes in terms of cost-benefit ratios and environmental impact, and will be able to assume managerial roles that require full responsibility for projects, development programs, coordination of structures and personnel, even at the management and administrative level.

The Master's graduate will also be highly qualified to carry out basic and applied research, promote and develop scientific and technological innovation, and perform professional and project activities in areas related to biotechnological disciplines.

Communication skills.
The specialized and professional knowledge building of the Master's Degree in Sustainable Industrial Pharmaceutical Biotechnology has been entirely designed to maximize students' communication skills, both written and oral, within international contexts, thanks to the exclusive use of English, innovative and interactive teaching methodologies, and transversal and integrated competencies focused on acquiring the 10 top skills specified by the third World Economic Forum.
The Master's graduate in Sustainable Industrial Pharmaceutical Biotechnology:
- is capable of working in teams within the design and application of experimental protocols
- possesses relational and communication skills enabling work in both national and international contexts
- possesses written and oral communication skills using both Italian and English
- is able to communicate information, ideas, problems, and solutions to both specialist and non-specialist audiences using both Italian and English
- is able to disseminate experimental data and prepare technical-scientific reports, both in Italian and English
- is able to communicate using multimedia tools. Communication skills will be continuously stimulated by the applied teaching methodologies and will therefore be subject to constant and distributed assessment throughout the entire educational path through observation of the student's ability to interact effectively with teachers and colleagues in individual meetings, practical experiences, teamworking activities, text and hypertext elaboration, as well as the ability to clearly, precisely, rigorously, synthetically, and with appropriate iconography express collected data and obtained results, especially but not only for the presentation of the final thesis. Students will also be encouraged to engage in communication during the course through the preparation of reports during profit verification or in-course assessments, presentations of scientific articles (Journal Club), and 'progress reports' aimed at illustrating, discussing, and transferring developments in their meta-analysis and data mining work, in-depth study of seminar topics, and research activities for the preparation of the Master's thesis.
Study trips, internships, interactive seminars, and meetings with experts and sector associations allow students to confront diverse languages and issues throughout the educational path. In-course orientation activities, such as participation in conferences on industrial biotechnology, bioeconomy, and sustainability, will provide concrete opportunities for students to interact with the scientific, productive, regulatory, and economic worlds in various biotechnology pharmaceutical and sustainable development sectors. The necessary laboratory activity for preparing the final report, to be carried out in an academic or non-academic, national or international environment, also allows acquiring the ability to interact with collaborators and technical staff, with different professional backgrounds.
The comprehensive sustainability themes addressed in the Master's Degree in Sustainable Industrial Pharmaceutical Biotechnology are indeed disseminated to both specialist and non-specialist audiences, aiming to foster external awareness and transfer judgment autonomy in a global perspective of indispensable socio-economic-environmental sustainability elements, knowing how to combine correct information in the biomolecular field with those related to management and sustainable development and issues linked to the profound digital transformation of the Health and Industry 4.0 world.
Communication skills are acquired through seminars, focus groups, and the final exam, and are verified through profit exams, practical activities, and the final exam.

ENGLISH Associated competencies.
Pharmaceutical Industry Biotechnologist Master's graduates will apply the acquired knowledge (through all comprehensive activities provided in the study plan) to cognitive and practical activities related to the following competencies:
- Knowledge and use of innovative and sustainable methods for producing organic molecules for use in the pharmaceutical, diagnostic, cosmetic, agri-food, and renewable energy sectors.
- Design and production of sustainable next-generation vaccines.
- Knowledge and use of innovative and sustainable methods for utilizing biological waste to obtain high-value-added secondary and tertiary products, such as bioactive products for use in biocosmetics, functional cosmetics, nutraceuticals, and bio-nutraceuticals, preventive supplements for diseases, and new drugs and bio-stimulants for applications in organic and eco-sustainable agriculture.
- Knowledge and use of technological platforms for functional genomics, post-genomics, high-throughput screening, and molecular modeling.
- Application of Life Cycle Assessment for evaluating environmental, social, and economic impacts of production processes of goods and services in the pharmaceutical, diagnostic, cosmetic, agri-food, renewable energy, and innovative technology sectors; ability to optimize resources, reduce raw material use, and consequently lower pollution emissions associated with production and transformation processes, contributing to the concept of circular economy and particularly bioeconomy.
- Understanding of strategic management and control tools to implement the 2030 Agenda in organizations and companies for sustainable development to address environmental challenges.
- Use of Big Data in chemical and biological fields and related applications of artificial intelligence.
- Understanding of variables and decision-making processes relevant to the international development of a company from a strategic and operational perspective in a globalization context.
- Understanding of all international regulatory and legislative aspects for the production of goods and services in the pharmaceutical, diagnostic, cosmetic, and agri-food sectors, as well as regarding intellectual and industrial property and economic and financial impact assessment in the commercialization of a biological or biotechnological technology.
- Ability to work autonomously, in groups, solve problems, optimize processes, make decisions, and take responsibility for one's actions.
- Ability to detect data (Big Data) pervasively, communicate them, and analyze them (artificial intelligence) to derive useful information for making the system more efficient.
Function in work context.
Pharmaceutical Industry Biotechnologist With the Master's Degree in Sustainable Industrial Pharmaceutical Biotechnology, a new professional in the pharmaceutical biotechnology sector with advanced scientific and professional skills, with a strong interdisciplinary connotation, is intended to be formed in the various areas of interest of industrial biotechnology. A new hybrid, versatile, multi-competent, and transversal professional figure that can hold responsible roles in research, development, and management in a crucial industrial sector for the country. The target of the new Master's Degree in Sustainable Industrial Pharmaceutical Biotechnology is therefore a student who must acquire highly multidisciplinary knowledge, with an advanced bio-molecular scientific-technical basis on the most innovative experimental aspects and sustainability in the bio-industrial field. A Master's student who can also acquire international management skills as well as regulatory aspects of new European directives to align biotechnology pharmaceutical companies with sustainable development. A graduate who possesses at the end of their Master's path the 10 top skills indicated by the third World Economic Forum. The management of Big Data, the 4.0 theme, and Artificial Intelligence for applications in Personalized and Precision Medicine are destined to play a strategic role in technological innovation for Biotech-pharma, Agrifood, Bioeconomy, and Bio-based Industry, revolutionizing public and private systems, redesigning new boundaries and horizons for both companies and research. The target of the new Master's Degree will have the opportunity to approach technologies and applications based on Artificial Intelligence for processing, integrating, and analyzing data from the biotech and pharmaceutical field, providing predictions or recommendations for diagnosis, therapy, health status, lifestyle, and nutrition, defining new models and improving therapeutic outcomes, in the perspective of sustainable growth of the biotech-pharma process. From here, through digital technologies, passes the renewal of industrial capitalism, allowing the creation of goods and services in an innovative way that we can still only imagine today. It will also be possible to develop innovative immersive educational systems with Virtual and Augmented Reality in the Biotech-farma, Agrifood, and bio-based industries.
The Master's graduate in Sustainable Industrial Pharmaceutical Biotechnology represents a professional figure at the top of a work context where research activity and the application of research, both at the laboratory and industrial level, form the basis for producing innovative and sustainable goods and services. Such a figure combines competencies in programming and development of scientific and technical-analytical biotechnology applications in industry and management of related business processes, with particular regard to Life Cycle Thinking, eco-sustainability, and sustainable development aspects. Knowledge of international regulations, exclusive use of English, practice of soft skills, adoption of innovative teaching methodologies, cultural contamination, and contribution of companies through co-design of the study course will allow this type of Master's graduate to position themselves within both national and international contexts, with a strong propensity towards a global vision and not a reductionist one.
The acquired knowledge will allow this new Industrial Biotechnologist to enter the most innovative application areas of bio-chemical-biotechnology research, with high-responsibility functions for the design, coordination, and scientific and technical-productive development of goods and services, and transfer of products and processes from the research phase to actual industrial application in sectors such as:
• basic research in public and private research centers
• research & development in biotechnology, pharmaceutical, cosmetic, nutraceutical, and agri-food industries
• basic research and research & development in the field of bioeconomy, environmental and socio-economic sustainability, and innovative technology sectors for renewable energy use. Professionals in Sustainable Industrial Pharmaceutical Biotechnology can also carry out activities in the following areas:
• customer management for product use and connection between customer needs and laboratory, production, and marketing activities
• promotion and development of scientific and technological innovation in various application and industrial contexts;
• design and application of scientific and technological methodologies for solving concrete problems in the biotechnology field;
• design and development of biological systems for the production and transformation of molecules, biomass, and interventions in industrial production activities aimed at improving quality of life and the environment.
• manage production process automation, Big Data management, Artificial Intelligence for applications in Personalized and Precision Medicine, and sustainable development of Biotech-farma, Agrifood, and bio-based industry.
Additionally, professionals in this field also play a key role in conducting research on fundamental concepts and theories in the field of bio-chemistry-biotechnology, increasing scientific knowledge in the field and applying it in research and experimental activities (production, processing, interpretation, validation of obtained data), making such knowledge available in the production of innovative goods and services or through the role of teachers in various training levels.
The Master's degree in Sustainable Industrial Pharmaceutical Biotechnology is also particularly suitable for starting a research career through access to a Research Doctorate.
Master's graduates in Industrial Biotechnology, based on the current DPR n. 328/01, can access the professions of Senior Biologist, Section A of the register, by passing the state exam.
Description of specific training objectives.
Training objectives In accordance with the qualifying training objectives of class LM-08, the Master's Degree in Sustainable Industrial Pharmaceutical Biotechnology aims to train Master's graduates with adequate mastery in professional activities of research and production of goods and services in the various sectors of industrial biotechnology in contexts related to chemistry, biochemistry, sustainability, and management disciplines, applying the experimental scientific method as the basic approach to biotechnology disciplines.
The Master's Degree in Sustainable Industrial Pharmaceutical Biotechnology aims to train a Master's graduate who constitutes a new trans-disciplinary professional figure in the thematic areas of Biotech-pharma, Biobased Industry (and Bioeconomy), Big Data and Industry 4.0, who can present themselves on the job market with a completely original curriculum at both national and international levels, oriented towards the job market in terms of professional capabilities.
To facilitate scientific communication and to more effectively enable entry into the job market, courses are delivered in English and English level B2 is required upon entry.
The Master's graduate must therefore acquire:
-a deep knowledge of the scientific method, laboratory methodologies, analytical tools, analysis techniques, and result management in order to acquire skills in processing and developing analytical investigation methods;
-a deep knowledge of the molecular bases, both chemical and biochemical and cellular, of biological systems and the structure and functionality of biological macromolecules and technological platforms for post-genomic analysis through courses in SSD BIO/09, BIO/10, BIO/11, BIO/13, BIO/14, CHIM/02, CHIM/06, and CHIM/08;
-mastering technological platforms for molecular target identification, molecular modeling, diagnostic kit design and development, fermentation and bioconversion techniques for producing biomolecules (enzymes, recombinant proteins, metabolites, vaccines, fine chemicals, etc.), biomolecule purification and analysis techniques, biocompatibility validation, and bioactivity assessment using high-throughput screening systems;
They must also have:
-an adequate knowledge of scientific, ethical, and legal issues related to the use of biotechnology, in order to effectively operate in the field of technological innovation through courses in SSD BIO/10, BIO/11, M-FIL/01, IUS/13, IUS/14, CHIM06, CHIM/09, SECS-P/08, SPS/09;
-an adequate knowledge of scientific issues related to sustainability, circular economy, bioeconomy, and sustainable development through courses in SSD CHIM/02, CHIM/06, BIO/10, CHIM/06, SECS-P/01, SPS/09, and SECS-P/07;
-a good ability to promote and develop scientific and technological innovation (CHIM/09, M-STO/04, L-ANT/01);
-any scientific aspect related to the topics of interest of the class, as well as familiarity in condensing such aspects into written reports or oral presentations (transversal competencies) L-ANT/01, L-FIL-LET/12.
The Study Plan includes practical activities and also the acquisition of Soft Skills.
The study course represents fertile ground for new didactic experiments that provide a new way of teaching and a teaching approach where the student has a central and active role.
Educational path In the first year of the course, teachings in biological, chemical, and economic fields are provided, mostly activated in characteristic activities (BIO/10, BIO/11, CHIM/01, CHIM/02, CHIM/06, CHIM/09, SECS-P/07) and some in related and integrated activities, through which the student can integrate and deepen knowledge (CHIM/09, SECS-P/01). Attendance at lectures and laboratories in the first year prepares the student for approaching industry and research laboratories, which will culminate in the second year. An obligatory internship activity is therefore provided at companies, public or private research bodies, study stays at other Italian and European universities, also within international agreements.
In the second year of the course, the student's commitment is mainly dedicated to seminar activities and internship in preparation for the final exam, which is assigned a considerable number of CFU.
Students will be called to carry out group work in the perspective of developing their teamworking skills, seeking creative solutions to real problems.
Some of the themes covered by internship and seminar activities offered by companies and the extra-academic work world will be: Socioeconomics, Bioeconomy, Circular economy, Ethics, Industry 4.0, Green Chemistry, New Drugs, Precision medicine, -omics, Eco-innovation, Globalization, EU Law, Bioprocess technology, Sustainable biochemicals, System & synthetic biology, Cell as a factory, From discovery to product, Biotechnology & health, Sustainable health, Rare diseases, Advanced therapeutics, Digital transformation, Innovative services, EU project design, and others.
The preparatory activity for the final exam allows the student to contextualize, in an operational reality, the knowledge, methodologies, and skills acquired during classroom teaching and practical activities and laboratories.

Program, texts, and objectives Professional title conferred by the degree. Expert in persuasive and advertising communication. The expert in persuasive and advertising communication finds professional opportunities in public and private institutions, as well as specifically political ones, where they can serve as a critical analyst of communication campaigns and positioning of various subjects, manage the image of political figures, contribute to the elaboration of programmatic documents and their dissemination strategies. In the private sector (communication agencies), they can serve as communication manager, image curator for public figures (entertainment), conduct consultancy for institutional, social, and political communication campaigns, as well as advertising campaigns.
Expert in socio-political communication and socio-political analyst. The employment opportunities for the expert in socio-political communication and socio-political analyst are found in various sectors. This expert can define communication strategies in the public administration sector, particularly in analysis and planning offices, public relations offices, and needs research and analysis offices; they can also define communication strategies in the third sector and international organizations, with specific attention to the European area.
Expert in interaction and experience design. The employment opportunities for experts in Interaction and Experience Design, as IU/UX Designers, span all fields related to the innovation of ICT products in both public and private sectors.
Final exam characteristics The final exam consists of a discussion, before the graduation committee, of an original thesis prepared under the guidance of a faculty member of the course, who serves as the thesis advisor. The thesis and discussion must demonstrate that the master's graduate has acquired a critical and in-depth knowledge of communication strategies, in accordance with the disciplinary principles typical of each curriculum under which the thesis work is conducted. Candidates must produce a written thesis with originality, involving adequate research effort commensurate with the required ECTS credits. The thesis will focus on one of the scientific-disciplinary fields of the training activities, within which the candidate has attended at least one course.
Students may write the thesis in English; in such cases, a motivated request must be submitted to the Course Director, duly countersigned by the thesis advisor, stating the student's commitment to present an Italian summary of the foreign language thesis of at least 10 pages. The thesis advisor and co-advisor are typically members of the graduation committee.
The final exam is worth 15 ECTS, evaluated based on the following criteria: completeness, methodological rigor, and originality of the work; presentation and argumentation skills in presenting the thesis.
The final exam will be graded on a scale of 110, with possible honors.
Required knowledge for admission To enroll in the Master's Degree in Strategies and Techniques of Communication, a degree, a four-year old-style degree, a three-year university diploma, or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent, or an AFAM First Cycle Academic Diploma is required.
Pursuant to Article 6, paragraph 3, of Law No. 268/2002, holders of diplomas issued by Academies and Conservatories, including certificates issued at the end of coreutic preparatory courses, are admitted to the Master's Degree program upon recognition of the acquired ECTS credits and provided they hold a secondary school diploma.
For admission to the Master's Degree, certain curricular requirements and adequate personal preparation are necessary. Knowledge of English at B1 level is also required.

Degree awarded. Master's Degree in Strategies and Techniques of Communication.
Knowledge and understanding. General area: Graduates of the Master's Degree will develop knowledge and understanding in the field of communication sciences, reaching the point of elaborating original ideas, especially in the areas of persuasive languages (politics, advertising, institutional and social communication), communication produced by companies (advertising and marketing strategies), and user experience design of technologies (Experience Design), without neglecting their possible application in a research context. Master's graduates will also acquire the ability to solve problems related to the use and design of new media in an eminently interdisciplinary key (communication technologies, marketing, rhetoric applied to the analysis of advertising, political discourse, institutions, content design, interaction design).
Persuasive and advertising communication: Graduates following the Persuasive and Advertising Communication area will develop knowledge and understanding regarding both the methods and tools of persuasive communication, articulated into its two fundamental components: (i) public communication (further divisible into institutional, social, and political communication); (ii) communication produced by companies (advertising and marketing strategies). These competencies will be based on a broad and comprehensive reflection on: (i) communication models (from pioneering communication research to semiotic models, to international and inferential models proposed by pragmatics); (ii) theories and techniques of semiotic text analysis (advertising and media); (iii) rhetorical argumentation techniques (including the theory of argumentative fallacies); (iv) sociological and psychological theories of communication; (v) theories and techniques of digital communication.
Public and social communication and journalism: Graduates following the Public and Social Communication and Journalism area will acquire knowledge enabling them to analyze and understand the institutional context in which political, economic, and social communication occurs, the tools for detecting questions from the social, economic, and political environment, and the most suitable methods for communicating relevant messages to different publics. They will also acquire interdisciplinary competencies aimed at ideating, analyzing, using, and evaluating new media, in relation to potential implications for investigating both social and cognitive components, and those of political, economic, and social communication. They will develop the ability to analyze and communicate social transformations and social risk. These abilities will be based on knowledge of the most recent psychological theories, individual and collective decision-making, and the functioning of the media system.
Technologies and methods for Experience Design: Graduates following the Technologies and Methods for Experience Design area will develop knowledge and understanding regarding the methods, tools, and theoretical foundations of User Experience design. They will appropriate the ideation and design process specific to User-Centered Design, understanding the differences and similarities with other design processes (e.g., Industrial, Software, Architectural, etc.). They will master the methods and software/hardware resources necessary to support the various phases of the user-centered design process, knowing how to adapt methods and resources to different operational situations where the design process may take place. They will build knowledge of these methods and tools based on the most accredited and heuristically positive theories of human action and cultural evolution.

Autonomy of judgment.
Given the interdisciplinary nature of the Master's Degree in Strategies and Techniques of Communication, Master's graduates will acquire the ability to integrate knowledge and manage the complexity of the communication world mediated by technology. Students will develop decision-making skills in selecting sources, defining operational objectives, adopting research/development methods and tools, within both individual and collective production processes.
These abilities will be assessed through critical discussion of topics related to the didactic programs of each course and associated practical projects.
Learning ability.
The acquisition of the ability to use and design new media and produce persuasive messages is embedded within a framework offering opportunities for continuous, autonomous, and self-directed learning. Students will first acquire the ability to learn how to learn (learning by invention) and secondly to know the tools for continuous updating. In this direction, fundamental resources offered by MOOCs will be integrated into the didactic paths of the courses. The methods and teaching tools used to assess learning abilities consist of periodic project development tests, both technological and related to persuasive communication.
Ability to apply knowledge and understanding.
General area Master's graduates will be able to apply acquired knowledge, understanding, and problem-solving skills related to the analysis and management of communication, cultural, political, and institutional processes, also utilizing the use and design of old and new media, in an eminently interdisciplinary key (communication technologies, marketing, rhetoric applied to the analysis of advertising, political discourse, institutions, content design, interaction design). They will finally be able to analyze and produce texts, also multimedia, evaluating and designing their communicative effectiveness and impact on recipients, in both institutional and social sectors.
The methods and teaching tools through which the expected outcomes are achieved consist of classroom activities (including project development and field investigations) and laboratory activities, which may include presentation of research results, collective discussion of alternative approaches and methods, problem solving, analysis and discussion of case studies, team activities, design briefs, etc.
The methods and teaching tools through which the ability to apply knowledge, demonstrate understanding of problems, and problem-solving skills are assessed consist of final examination tests, possibly preceded by interim tests related to various disciplinary areas.
Persuasive and Advertising Communication Master's graduates in the area of Persuasive and Advertising Communication will be able to apply acquired knowledge: (i) to the analysis and production of media and advertising texts; (ii) to the analysis of discourses produced by political, social, and institutional communication, recognizing their argumentation modules, including fallacious argumentation; (iii) to understanding and analyzing the communication needs of institutions and client companies, identifying the target public profiles to which to direct communication, structuring content appropriately; (iv) to elaborating communication plans, linking them to both the economic impact dimension and the persuasive forms suitable for different targets.
These abilities will be achieved through classroom and/or laboratory activities, with frontal lessons and/or group work and presentations of individually or group-conducted research, depending on the courses.
These abilities will be verified and assessed through various activities ranging from discussion, also collective, of specific case studies, to guided presentations of research and projects, to diversified forms of exercises. They will also be verified through final tests in individual courses, possibly preceded by intermediate tests.
Public and Social Communication and Journalism Master's graduates in the area of Social and Political Communication and Journalism will be able to use the most appropriate theoretical approaches and quantitative and qualitative methods to address the analysis of questions and identify channels of political, economic, and social communication in the current context characterized by multi-level policy-making. They will also be able to analyze message content, identify framing aspects, and adopt the most suitable methodological choices (experimental and observational) to communicate them.
They will acquire critical analytical ability and problem identification in public contexts within economic, social, and political spheres, to understand limitations in communication and definition of such issues. These competencies will be acquired and verified using both frontal teaching and laboratory assessments, with theoretical and empirical content, exercises, internships, and experimentation with concrete cases in the numerous laboratories active within the Department.
These abilities will be achieved through classroom and/or laboratory activities, with frontal lessons and/or group work and presentations of individually or group-conducted research, depending on the courses.
These abilities will be verified and assessed through various activities ranging from discussion, also collective, of specific case studies, to guided presentations of research and projects, to diversified forms of exercises. They will also be verified through final tests in individual courses, possibly preceded by intermediate tests.
Technologies and Methods for Experience Design Master's graduates in the area Technologies and Methods for Experience Design will be able to apply acquired knowledge to solve design challenges related to improving and evolving existing tools and services, both by evaluating usability or socio-organizational fragility issues, and by ideating (also through prototyping design) new technological solutions and new services. To this end, they will be able to capitalize on opportunities offered by enabling new technologies made available through technological innovation and on perceived opportunities and knowledge produced by human capital involved in the activities for which they design. The methods and teaching tools through which the expected outcomes are achieved and measured consist of guided project activities and responses to original design briefs.
The methods and teaching tools through which the expected outcomes are achieved consist of classroom activities (including project development and field investigations) and laboratory activities, which may include presentation of research results, collective discussion of alternative approaches and methods, problem solving, analysis and discussion of case studies, team activities, design briefs, etc.
The methods and teaching tools through which the ability to apply knowledge, demonstrate understanding of problems, and problem-solving skills are assessed consist of final examination tests, possibly preceded by interim tests related to various disciplinary areas.

Communication Skills.
As a Master's Degree in Communication, graduates will develop the ability to communicate clearly and unambiguously using multichannel and multimodal tools, ensuring comprehensibility and effectiveness for both specialist and non-specialist interlocutors (in other words, for both mass audiences and professional or academic specialists). They will cultivate the capacity to share, elaborate, synthesize, and argue knowledge and results in both cooperative and competitive contexts. These skills will be assessed through the verification of the development and use of communication tools related to content (e.g., public speaking, social media content production) and/or containers (e.g., interaction design). Verification will occur periodically through classroom presentations of both content and communication tools.
Planned career and professional opportunities for graduates.
Expert in Persuasive and Advertising Communication.
The expert in persuasive and advertising communication finds professional opportunities in public and private institutions, as well as specifically political ones, where they can perform the role of critical analyst of communication campaigns and positioning of various subjects, manage the image of political figures, contribute to the elaboration of programmatic documents and their dissemination strategies. In the private sector (communication agencies), they can serve as communication manager, image curator for public figures (entertainment), or consultant for institutional, social, and political communication campaigns, as well as advertising campaigns.
Expert in Socio-Political Communication and Socio-Political Analyst.
The career opportunities for the expert in socio-political communication and socio-political analyst are found across various sectors. This expert figure can define communication strategies in the public administration sector, with particular reference to analysis and planning offices, public relations offices, and needs research and analysis offices; additionally, they can define communication strategies in the third sector and international organizations, with specific attention to the European area.
Expert in Interaction and Experience Design.
The career opportunities for experts in Interaction and Experience Design, as IU/UX Designers, span all fields related to innovation in ICT products, both in public and private contexts.
Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIAN Associated competencies.
Expert in Persuasive and Advertising Communication.
The expert in persuasive and advertising communication develops various competencies across numerous work areas, both public and private, where they can perform tasks at various levels, from leadership in a communication and social relations agency to the role of expert analyst or copywriter.
Expert in Socio-Political Communication and Socio-Political Analyst.
The expert in socio-political communication and political and institutional communication develops competencies aimed at setting up strategies for data collection and analysis of social and political markets, market segmentation, and needs and demands research, with particular reference to market research (political and social), social data analysis, construction and communication of social and political scenarios (foresight), and political communication.
Expert in Interaction and Experience Design.
The expert in interaction and experience design develops various competencies in both public and private sectors: planning, coordinating, and conducting user and human activity needs analysis for interaction design, and organizing usability tests. In particular, they can design and specify user interfaces and information architecture using participatory design techniques, including field surveys, customer interviews, usability tests, and other requirement definition methods; specify user requirements for existing or hypothetical products; produce storyboards, scenarios, flow diagrams, design prototypes, and project specifications in the form of Role and Look&Feel Mock Ups.
Function in work context.
Expert in Persuasive and Advertising Communication.
The expert in persuasive and advertising communication in public institutions can perform the role of URP manager, manage media relations, plan communication campaigns, design cultural and promotional events. They may also be employed as communication staff training manager. Finally, they can serve as consultant for communication plans of private companies of various sizes.
Expert in Socio-Political Communication and Socio-Political Analyst.
The expert in socio-political communication can perform the function of needs and communication analysis research, particularly in the socio-political area and scenario-building, foresight, and proactive strategy for complex institutions.
Expert in Interaction and Experience Design.
The expert in interaction and experience design, as an IU/UX Designer, can perform the function of discovering, understanding, and communicating to clients business needs, emotional desires of their customers, and the context in which these intersect, and design appropriate technological solutions.
Additional information.
www.unisi.it www.dispoc.unisi.it Specific educational objectives description.
The course aims to provide Master's graduates with interdisciplinary skills in areas where the teaching and research resources of the department of origin, DISPOC, are recognized as excellence. For this set of skills, no analogous study programs exist at universities in the same region or neighboring regions.
The Study Program aims to orient training in three different areas: (a) persuasive and advertising communication; (b) public and social communication and journalism; (c) communication technologies for Experience Design.
By combining characteristic and common elective courses for all students in the first year (belonging to the following SSD: M-FIL/05, SPS/08, ING-INF/05, SPS/04, M-STO/04, SECS-P/01, L-LIN/12) and more specialized courses in the second year, specific to each area (for the area of persuasive and advertising communication: M-FIL/05, SPS/08, SPS/07; for the area of public and social communication and journalism: SPS/04, SPS/08, M-GGR/01; for the area of communication technologies for Experience Design: M-PSI/01 and ING-INF/05), the course aims to provide in-depth knowledge of current theoretical models related to communication; adequate critical capacity to compare current communication models with those found in the semiotic, philosophical, and rhetorical tradition of the past, which form the basis of the most recent; a thorough capacity for analysis and production of texts, also multimedia, evaluating and designing their communicative effectiveness and impact on recipients; adequate capacity to design models and theories useful for the realization of communication prototypes at various levels and with different technologies; methodological skills combined with technological competencies aimed at mastering both traditional and new communication media.
Master's graduates will also develop interdisciplinary skills aimed at ideating, analyzing, producing, and evaluating new media, defining their relationships and potential implications aimed at analyzing social and cognitive components, as well as those oriented towards political communication, social communication, and advertising communication.
For this reason, the program has been defined with direct reference to the content and objects of the courses, rather than emphasizing specific approaches and disciplines. In other words, the focus has been placed on didactic content functional to the central idea of the course rather than the distinct inclinations of the teachers.
Consequently, the principle is shared that within this study program, syllabi and course content must be discussed collegially and continuously monitored by the organizing committee/for teaching.
The core elements of this study program are three: 1) an authentic interdisciplinary perspective, modeling different scientific approaches to practical student preparation through dedicated courses; 2) a robust specialist preparation focused on the fundamentals of a series of concepts underlying communication professions (public communication, corporate communication, service communication, persuasive communication, communication for cultural design); 3) a broad overview of new professions in the information world, new media, cultural enterprises, and public and private organizations.

Final exam characteristics To be admitted to the final exam, all credits specified in the student's study plan must be earned. The final exam, which holds particular importance as a concluding assessment of the Master's study path, consists of the discussion of a written dissertation (thesis) on an original and significant topic, agreed upon with a supervising professor who guides the student during the research and writing process. The dissertation text may be supplemented with multimedia supports. In the written work and discussion, the candidate must demonstrate mastery of methodology, full ability to use selected sources, and in-depth knowledge of the bibliography and debate related to the topic. The thesis discussion before the Committee (with active participation of at least one co-supervisor) must verify that the Master's graduate has acquired advanced knowledge in their field of study; is able to develop original research ideas and perspectives through critically aware application of research tools; is capable of identifying innovative perspectives in their field of investigation; and demonstrates the ability to present and argue effectively in both written and oral form.
The Teaching Committee may authorize, at the candidate's request, that the final exam and discussion be conducted in a European Community language other than Italian.
A fundamental evaluation element will be the quality of the work performed, the correctness of the methods used, the maturity of the analysis, and the pertinence and originality of the results obtained. The final exam grade will conform to the criteria for calculating the merit score defined in the Final Exam Regulation for Master's Degree courses adopted by the Department. This grade will be assigned considering the weighted average of the grades obtained in the course exams, the quality and novelty of the thesis work, and will be expressed on a scale of 110 with possible honors.
Required knowledge for admission To be admitted to the Master's Degree in History and Philosophy, one must hold a three-year university degree or equivalent foreign degree deemed suitable.
Additionally, students must possess specific curricular requirements and adequate personal preparation, including sufficient knowledge of English to read texts used in various courses.
Curricular requirements are satisfied by holding a degree in one of the following classes (ex D.M. 270/2004 or ex D.M. 509/1999 or equivalent foreign degree):
Cultural Heritage (L‐1), Philosophy (L‐5), Literature (L‐10), Language mediation (L‐12), Educational Sciences and Training (L‐19), Communication Sciences (L‐20), History (L‐42).
Graduates in the listed classes must have earned at least 40 CFU in the following scientific-disciplinary sectors:
L‐ANT/02, L‐ANT/03; M‐GGR/01; M‐DEA/01; M‐FIL/01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 06, 07, 08; M‐PED/01, 03; M‐PSI/01; MSTO/01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 06, 07, 08, 09; SECS‐P/12; SPS/02, 07, 08.
For those holding a degree outside the qualifying classes, at least 75 CFU must be earned in the following SSDs, in addition to obtaining the degree with a grade of at least 100/110:
M‐FIL/01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 06, 07, 08; M‐STO/01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 06, 07, 08, 09; IUS/18, 19, 20; M‐DEA/01; M‐GGR/01, 02; SECS‐P/01, 02, 04, 08, 12; SECS‐S/01, 03, 04, 05; SPS/01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 06, 07, 08, 09, 10, 11, 13, 14; MPED/01, 02, 03; M‐PSI/01, 05; L‐ANT/02, 03; L‐ART/04.
Personal preparation is verified through a mandatory interview, accessible also to students meeting curricular requirements but with a grade below the specified threshold. The methods for verifying personal preparation are defined in the Teaching Regulation of the Master's Degree Course.
Awarded degree.
Master's Degree in History and Philosophy
Knowledge and understanding.
Generic area Master's graduates must have acquired the ability to understand at a post-secondary level, developed through the study and critical analysis of classic and specialized texts, also in foreign language; they must also embrace the specific dialectical relationship between the historical dimension and the philosophical perspective, while remaining open to further disciplinary contributions. The selection of textbooks must ensure high scientific level, updated research status, content transparency, and methodological effectiveness. Students must be able to critically use such texts based on knowledge and skills acquired through the three-year degree and further developed through the Master's courses. These courses will alternate lectures and seminar activities, including the presentation and discussion of written works, individual study, and group discussion; methods aimed not only to transmit knowledge but also to foster familiarity with communication and critical debate practices in both historical and philosophical contexts.
Knowledge and understanding levels will be assessed by instructors through active student involvement during lectures and seminars, to constantly verify progress in individual study. These progressions, along with the ability to understand and personally rework disciplinary content, will ultimately be verified for each course during the final exam, which may be oral or written.
The acquired knowledge and skills will ultimately enable graduates to address novel or infrequently addressed themes with sufficient confidence, clear methodological approach, and rapid ability to navigate extensive bibliographies. The acquisition of such knowledge and skills will be comprehensively verified through the completion of the final dissertation, the culmination of an in-depth and structured study path.
Historical area The Master's graduate in History must possess in-depth knowledge in the disciplinary fields characterizing the degree course, a solid ability to analyze sources, and synthesize historical literature texts. They must therefore be able to critically understand original documents and sources, thanks to secure knowledge of the methods and languages characteristic of historical interpretation and reconstruction. Such knowledge and skills must emerge in both ancient and medieval history and modern and contemporary history, also in relation to the use and valorization of archival and documentary sources.
Philosophical area The Master's graduate in Philosophy must possess in-depth knowledge in the disciplinary fields characterizing the degree course, a solid ability to analyze philosophical works, and synthesize critical studies in philosophical and historical-philosophical contexts. They must therefore be able to critically understand original texts and works of individual authors, through mastery of vocabulary, specific languages, and argumentative forms characteristic of philosophical research. The preferred study fields will be historical-philosophical, theoretical, and moral, with specific reference to intercultural, anthropological, and religious dimensions.

Judgment Autonomy.
The Master's graduate in History and Philosophy must be able to formulate clear syntheses based on a correct understanding of the scientific bibliography texts, recognizing various approaches and interpretative hypotheses, and demonstrating judgment capacity and willingness for open and constructive discussion.
The objectives are pursued within seminar and group activities, through constant dialogue with teachers via discussion and jointly with the preparation of individual papers by students. Particular attention will be devoted to constructing study paths and research projects in the specific fields of reference.
Judgment autonomy will be acquired through the teaching activities provided by the Study Course, particularly through seminars and exercises. The acquisition of this ability will be verified throughout the entire educational path. Classroom and field training (through didactic laboratories) will allow the acquisition of these skills, which must also be applied in the preparation of the final thesis.

Learning Ability.
Master's graduates in History and Philosophy will acquire: - Competence in nourishing and self-directing their personal and professional growth even after the completion of the educational path. - Ability to search for and use sources, documents, and texts not encountered during the study path, functional to deepening and acquiring specific professional skills useful for entering the job market and for continuous updating in situations of flexibility and rapid transformation of society and the role of individuals in such changed contexts.
This learning ability will be achieved through attendance at both frontal and especially seminar teaching activities, preparation of individual exams, and particularly in the work of preparing the final exam, adequately guided and supported by the supervisor.

The acquisition of this ability will be verified throughout the entire educational path through intermediate tests and exams. The final paper and its discussion will constitute the crucial moment for verifying the acquired intellectual maturity.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area Master's graduates must have acquired the ability to apply knowledge and understanding in the relevant occupational sectors, demonstrating the ability to turn "knowledge" into "know-how" even in multidisciplinary and international contexts. To this end, the educational path implemented during the Master's degree must not be separated from concrete examples and exercises in applying theoretical knowledge. Common activities for both degree classes may include, for example, constructing bibliographies related to specific research topics, preparing bibliographic reviews, designing and organizing seminars and study days, planning and implementing modules and didactic units. The interactive nature of such activities will allow for ongoing verification of the ability to apply acquired knowledge.

On the other hand, students' interaction with representatives of the working world represents a useful and effective element to increase awareness of the multifaceted possibilities of applying historical and philosophical knowledge, for example in relation to the valorization of collective memory or new ethical sensitivities related to the environmental, health, and information fields, etc. Particularly significant in this regard will be the integrated activities proposed from time to time within or outside the university campus in collaboration with public and private bodies, libraries, museums, superintendencies, cultural centers, and associations, etc.

Historical Area High ability to apply knowledge and understanding regarding the reconstruction of the economic, social, and political dimensions of historical events. Completeness of bibliographic research. Use and critical analysis of historical sources and documents.

Philosophical Area High ability to apply knowledge and understanding to the analysis of philosophical texts and their historical-critical context. Completeness of bibliographic research. Ability to identify, use, and evaluate the main forms of philosophical language and research. Ability to apply main philosophical methodologies to the analysis of historical or current issues.

Communication Skills.
Master's graduates in History and Philosophy will acquire high ability to communicate, both orally and in writing, the contents of the disciplines with clarity and scientific rigor, revealing argumentative skills and logical progression, in order to transfer the information and outcomes of their analyses appropriately to different target audiences, specialist or not, both through traditional presentations of results achieved in their studies or research projects, and by using computer tools.

Acquisition of specific terminology will occur during frontal lessons. The acquisition of such communication skills will be verified throughout the entire educational path. Communication skills will be stimulated and verified during seminar meetings where students will be called to present, within predetermined times and modes, reports on specific topics deepened in individual study or project lines for subsequent research.

Description of specific educational objectives.
The Interdisciplinary Master's Degree Course in History and Philosophy is based on a deep integration and interaction of different research perspectives related to historical and philosophical sciences, forming a broad and articulated constellation of knowledge born in a distant past but characterized by full and pressing actuality. As living and updated knowledge, history and philosophy are considered in their internal dynamics and evolutions and in their relations with the sciences of culture and society. The Study Course aims to offer Master's graduates an interdisciplinary education capable of acquiring theoretical attitudes and historical investigation skills, professional competencies, and argumentative abilities referring to diversified but flexible and interactive disciplinary areas.

Through this Study Course, the graduate will acquire full mastery of the tools and languages of historical research and philosophical studies, based on knowledge of texts, sources, theories, and discursive practices, analyzed in their content and formal characteristics, in order to be used for studying and deepening topics and problems of history and philosophy, from the most ancient past to the present in a methodological, historical-philosophical, and ethical key, and for reconstructing historical, cultural, and social events from Antiquity to the Contemporary Age.

The historical sciences - of ancient, medieval, modern, and contemporary scope - as well as those related to documentation - of archival and paleographic scope - and the philosophical sciences of theoretical, moral, and general history of philosophy scope constitute the fundamental axis around which the Study Course is organized, which is also characterized by interactions with other knowledge contributing to the formation of graduates. The Study Course is structured in two curricula, one at the administrative headquarters in Siena at DSSBC and the other at DSFUCI in Arezzo. In fact, these are two specific curricula aiming to achieve the common educational objectives of the Study Course following partly different paths.

The Siena curriculum features a significant presence of anthropological, geographical, ancient (Greek), and contemporary history teachings as compulsory and common to both classes LM-78 and LM-84; the activation of teachings in the area of medieval, modern, and contemporary history and civilization, codicology, and Latin paleography, and in the philosophical field, the history of ancient philosophy, the history of medieval philosophy, and aesthetics, which complement general philosophical disciplines. In this way, the educational path in both historical and philosophical fields unfolds chronologically and thematically from Antiquity to the Contemporary Age.

The Arezzo curriculum prioritizes the contemporary aspect, considers the public use of history, and emphasizes the cultural and social practical character of historical and philosophical training. Through this path, graduates will thus access theoretical knowledge and competencies that also dialogue with the sector - rapidly growing - of public transmission and narration of historical and philosophical knowledge. In this curriculum, Greek history is reserved for Philosophy students (LM-78) only, modern and contemporary science history has a larger space, historical teachings, while maintaining the mandatory presence of medieval and modern history for LM-84, provide more credits for contemporary history and Risorgimento history. Philosophical disciplines are also more oriented towards contemporaneity both for M-FIL/06 and for M-FIL/01 and M-FIL/03. The Arezzo curriculum includes a sociology subject, assigns a more limited space to cultural geography, and does not provide anthropological area teachings.

In both teaching locations, the above educational objectives will be achieved through the delivery of suitable teachings to address relevant themes and issues for individuals' lives in their relationship with the natural and social environment through the method of interdisciplinarity, i.e., by interacting a deep knowledge of past events and the history of philosophical, scientific, and idea thinking, and knowledge as shared practices through the appropriate use of investigation tools also of anthropological and sociological character and analytical techniques useful for investigating relationships between different areas and contexts of human intellectual, practical, and material activities.

In this didactic dimension, specific educational objectives of the Study Course merit being highlighted as the acquisition of specialized competencies related to:
1) The use of methodological and theoretical models in the fields of both historical and philosophical studies;
2) Knowledge of sources, investigated in their technical-formal and content characteristics, as well as the ability to use them for reconstructing, analyzing, and studying historical events;
3) The ability to intervene in the field of analysis and editing of literary and documentary testimonies both with traditional methodologies and with the aid of information technologies and the application of new media;
4) Reading and critical analysis of philosophical texts, historical sources, and their bibliographies;
5) Preparation of critical studies on topics and problems central to the formation in the Study Course.
6) Attention reserved to the languages and places of public transmission of historical and philosophical knowledge.

- Access post-graduate training represented by Doctoral Programs Characteristics of final exam The Master's thesis represents a crucial formative moment in the student's career, allowing them to apply the knowledge and skills acquired in their field of study, as well as critical and methodological abilities developed. The thesis topic, to be identified and developed under the guidance of the supervisor, should preferably be partially or fully unpublished, offer research opportunities both bibliographic and archival, be capable of contributing innovatively to the field of study, and, if applicable, present operational implications within the discipline. In writing the thesis, the candidate must demonstrate confidence in bibliographic orientation (also in foreign language) and ability in archival research, where this is necessary; secure and precise use of scientific terminology in the relevant field; capacity for independent critical elaboration; ability to manage interdisciplinary connections. Naturally, the candidate must be able to argue and present the results of their research clearly and coherently, both in written and oral form. The Master's thesis cannot be written in a foreign language. The final exam is awarded 27 CFU; and the final merit score (degree grade) will take into account, based on the student's curriculum, the quality and novelty of the thesis work in its various methodological, historical, and critical implications. The final merit score will be expressed on a scale of 110, with possible honors. See Final Exam Regulation for Master's Degree Courses approved by the Department.
