Master's Degree in Art History Teaching method Conventional Knowledge and understanding.
Generic Area Master's graduates must have acquired the ability to understand at a post-secondary level, developed through the study and critical comparison of specialized texts, even in foreign language, and to internalize the inseparable dialectical relationship between the history of art (and other humanities disciplines) and general cultural history. In particular, textbooks will be selected based on high scientific level, research updates, content transparency, and methodological effectiveness, while also considering an increasing degree of complexity that students must be able to address with precise awareness and understanding based on knowledge acquired through the Bachelor's degree and specialized courses in the Master's program. Such knowledge and abilities will enable them to confidently address novel or infrequently encountered themes, with a clear methodological approach and rapid ability to navigate extensive bibliographies. Acquisition of such knowledge and abilities will be verified throughout the training path through seminars, written and oral exams, and reports. Historical-Artistic Area High level of knowledge and understanding for the fields of:
History of Art History of Architecture History and methodologies of conservation Art literature History of art criticism Historical Area Good level of knowledge and understanding for the fields of:
History Archival Studies Theatrical, musical, cinematic areas Good level of knowledge and understanding for the fields of:
Theater Music Cinema Judgment autonomy.
At the end of the Master's program, graduates must be able to formulate, based on acquired knowledge, study of existing bibliography (updated and international), and a solid and correct methodological approach, an independent judgment regarding the themes, authors, or works that will be the subject of their research. To encourage and stimulate personal reflection, the training path aims to provide as broad and diversified a panorama as possible of different critical positions around the themes treated in the courses, highlighting strengths and weaknesses for each; similarly, the seminar nature of many segments of the training path, and the intervention of external teachers who can usefully contribute to in-depth comparison of different evaluations, will allow students to develop their ability to articulate independent judgments anchored to an objectively verifiable context. The inclusion, in the training path, of artistic and architectural production within the broader historical and cultural context (with references to literature, music, theater, cinema) also stimulates students to establish connections, influences, and dependencies between different creative expressions. Achievement of judgment autonomy occurs through the teaching activities provided by the Course, study seminars, and exercises. Acquisition of this ability will be verified throughout the training path through exercises, seminars, written and oral exams, reports, and will be fully expressed in the Master's thesis. Learning ability.
Master's graduates must be able to confidently and, above all, consciously approach further studies. The training path is structured with a gradual and progressive increase in the complexity of themes addressed, with a parallel increase in the demand and verification of learning ability and critical capacity, culminating in the Master's thesis, a fundamental opportunity to effectively and autonomously apply acquired abilities and knowledge. Knowledge of foreign languages, ability to navigate extensive and complex bibliographies or databases, full mastery of methodological tools, enrichment from the internship period, and solid judgment autonomy are all essential aspects for pursuing further studies after the Master's degree, and as such represent a constant reference point, like a backbone, of the entire training path of the Course. Learning ability is acquired through teaching activities provided by the Course, study seminars, and exercises, internship activities, and is continuously verified throughout the study path through oral exams, written reports, seminars, reports from host organizations regarding the internship; and finds a fundamental moment of comprehensive verification in the elaboration, writing, and discussion of the Master's thesis. Application of knowledge and understanding.
Generic Area Master's graduates must have acquired the ability to apply knowledge and understanding in relevant occupational sectors, demonstrating the ability to transform "knowing" into "knowing how," even in multidisciplinary and international contexts. To this end, the training path implemented during the Master's degree is never disconnected from concrete examples and exercises in applying theoretical knowledge, which in the specific field of art history may relate to the conception and organization of an exhibition (with issues concerning exhibition spaces, loan and movement of works, insurance values, press office), structuring the scientific catalog, drafting work sheets; or to the conception, organization, and management of a study day; or to cataloging methods for works and related documents. The interactive nature of such activities will allow for ongoing verification of the ability to apply acquired knowledge. On the other hand, students' interaction with professionals from the working world represents a useful and effective element to sharpen awareness of the inseparable link that exists in various fields of historical-artistic heritage between history, theory, and practice, and between individual knowledge and interaction with the environment. Particularly significant in this regard are laboratory activities and internship activities, which always take place at institutions (public or private) whose activities are closely related to the field of study of the Course (museums, superintendencies, cultural centers and associations, private galleries, cultural foundations, etc.). Historical-Artistic Area High ability to apply knowledge and understanding regarding:
Reconstruction of historical events of artistic and architectural artifacts Reconstruction of critical events of artistic and architectural artifacts Completeness of bibliographic research Critical analysis based on original research Historical Area High ability to apply knowledge and understanding regarding:
Placement of artistic events within historical contexts Conducting archival research Theatrical, musical, cinematic areas Good ability to apply knowledge and understanding regarding:
Placement of artistic events within contexts related to theater, music, and cinema Communication skills.
The Master's graduate must be able to effectively communicate the knowledge acquired during their studies, as well as make their acquired skills easily shareable, both in written and oral form. They must also be able to balance and differentiate their communication level: depending on whether the interlocutor is a specialist in the field of art history or a general audience, similar to what they will likely face in the workplace (from a presentation at a scientific conference to a guided school visit, from a scientific essay to a catalog sheet to a popular text). To stimulate and verify communication skills, many courses include seminar-style exercises, as well as an oral exam, in which students are required to use sector-specific scientific terminology consciously. To accustom students to relating to an audience and defending their positions, each academic year, students organize, with the supervision and coordination of teachers, open study seminars lasting a day, consisting of brief student presentations on agreed topics related to specific moments in art history, followed by discussion. This is a very useful exercise not only for refining communication skills but also for learning to effectively use the available time (equal for all) to clearly and concisely present the chosen topic. Moreover, both in the preparatory work and during the seminar day, these seminars are of great importance for stimulating students to engage in discussion and group work, aiming for optimal collective results. Verification of communication skills occurs throughout the training path: oral exams, written reports, seminars, discussion of the final exam. - Associations and cooperatives offering services in research and documentation, training, and cultural tourism Additionally, Master's graduates in History of Art can:
- Participate in admission tests for teaching training paths in History of Art in secondary schools, as provided by current legislation
- Participate, if holding sufficient CFU in appropriate subject groups, in admission tests for secondary school teaching training paths in other subjects besides History of Art, as provided by current legislation
- Access post-graduate training at the appropriate Specialization Schools in Historical-Artistic Heritage for managerial careers in the Ministry for Cultural Heritage and Activities
- Access post-graduate training represented by Doctoral Programs Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIAN Associated competencies for the role.
Art Historian The Master's graduate in History of Art must possess:
- Advanced historical-methodological competencies applied to research and critical analysis of artistic and architectural heritage from the medieval period to the present
- High competencies in conducting and managing bibliographic, archival, and iconographic research
- Knowledge of museological and museographic aspects, both historically and in contemporary developments
- Theoretical and applied knowledge regarding the history and methodologies of conservation of artistic artifacts
- Knowledge of disciplinary terminology within the historical-artistic, architectural, museological, protection, and conservation fields
- High ability to express oneself in written and oral form, both at a scientific and popular level
- Ability to work in teams and interact with diverse professional profiles
- Ability to plan and direct an exhibition event of historical-artistic nature
- Good knowledge of English language, and possibly other European Union languages Description of admission tests.
Personal preparation verification test
1. The personal preparation verification test is conducted orally, through an interview with three teachers of the Master's Degree Course (assigned to SSD L-ART/01, L-ART/02, and L-ART/03 and designated annually by the Teaching Committee), focusing on the candidate's knowledge of artistic and architectural manifestations from the medieval, modern, and contemporary periods.
2. The test will be considered passed if the candidate demonstrates good chronological-stylistic orientation ability and sufficient critical reading ability of works.
3. The test may be held in one or more sessions. If multiple sessions are scheduled, those not admitted in the first session may reappear in the next.
4. The test is open to graduates meeting the curricular requirements specified in Article 7, paragraphs 1, 2, and 5, and to students enrolled in courses belonging to the classes specified in Article 7, paragraph 1, who have earned at least 120 CFU in total by the test date, including all CFU specified in Article 7, paragraph 1, letters b), c), d).
5. Students who pass the verification test will be admitted conditionally and may enroll provided they obtain their degree within the deadlines for closing enrollment.
Article 10 – Direct admission
1. Exempt from the verification test, as they are deemed already possessing the required personal preparation, are graduates meeting the curricular requirements of Article 7, paragraph 1, who obtained their degree with a grade not lower than 100/110, or who, despite having a lower degree grade, have earned the required CFU in their study plan with a weighted average grade of not less than 27/30 for the following SSD: L-ART/01, L-ART/02, L-ART/03, L-ART/04, ICAR/15, ICAR/16, ICAR/18.
2. Additionally exempt from the admission test are Master's graduates under Article 7, paragraph 4, meeting the curricular requirements.
3. Students who, despite being eligible to participate under Article 9, paragraph 3, have already achieved a weighted average grade of not less than 27/30 for all courses in their study plan in the SSD: L-ART/01, L-ART/02, L-ART/03, L-ART/04, ICAR/15, ICAR/16, ICAR/18 by the test date, will also be exempt from the test, as they are deemed to possess the required personal preparation. In the absence of this requirement, students planning to graduate by the enrollment deadline may choose to take the test, with the understanding that, regardless of the outcome, they will be admitted by right if their final degree grade meets or exceeds 100/110.
Workplace role.
Art Historian The Master's Degree in History of Art trains highly competent professionals able to access roles as art historians in public and private institutions dealing with cultural heritage, both regarding their study, conservation, and protection, and regarding their management and valorization. In particular, they can:
- Perform functions as a staff member or curator/conservator at state or local public bodies such as superintendencies, museums, and picture galleries, archives; or at private entities such as foundations, museums, collections
- Perform editorial activities, iconographic research, and cultural promotion at specialized art publishing houses
- Perform cataloging, archiving, and documentation activities in the historical-artistic sector at public or private entities
- Perform activities of conceiving and realizing exhibitions, events, and cultural manifestations, museum paths, and related educational activities
- Perform research and promotion activities in the art market and auction houses
- Perform autonomous activities within associations and cooperatives offering services in research and documentation, training, and cultural tourism
- Offer historical-artistic consultancy and conduct appraisals and expert opinions. Finally, for Master's graduates wishing to acquire further competencies and reach higher levels of responsibility, the training path can continue in Specialization Schools, Second-Level Master's Programs, and Doctoral Programs. Additional information.
http://www.unisi.it/dipartimenti/dipartimento-scienze-storiche-e-dei-beni-culturali Specific educational objectives description.
The specific educational objectives of the Master's Degree in History of Art are based on two main lines, taking into account the high professional standards required by institutions, both public and private, currently operating in the cultural sector. Primarily, the Course aims to provide a solid preparation in the historical-artistic field through progressive deepening of direction: indeed, the Course is characterized and distinguishes itself from similar Courses at the national level by offering students the possibility to choose one of three directions in which the discipline is structured, namely Medieval Art, Modern Art, and Contemporary Art. Secondly, the Course also encompasses more operational aspects related to the historical-critical ones, concerning contemporary museums and the protection and conservation of artistic heritage, according to an approach that places students in direct contact with specific work contexts. In the first year, educational objectives focus on a solid preparation regarding artistic and architectural manifestations from the early Middle Ages to the present and their critical analysis (historical-artistic learning area, 24 CFU), which, based on knowledge acquired during the three-year program, can be further deepened in terms of treated themes. Throughout the first year, and based on the chosen direction (Medieval Art, Modern Art, or Contemporary Art), these deepening will be accompanied by an indispensable knowledge of contemporary historical events, without which a full understanding of the motivations, genesis, and outcomes of artistic and architectural production would be impossible (historical learning area, 12 CFU). Among the core courses, archiving and paleography are also included, which for students directed towards medieval and modern art represent a fundamental aid (historical learning area, 6 CFU); while among optional courses, there are courses related to theater, music, and cinema, which can effectively help establish connections and parallels with contemporary artistic production (theatrical, musical, cinematic learning areas, 12 CFU). A course focused on contemporary museography is also placed in the first year, representing the first approach to one of the possible employment opportunities for Master's graduates in History of Art, namely museums: knowledge of the methods, both historical and contemporary, of "presenting" cultural heritage in its museographic and museological components aims specifically to develop in students a critical awareness of the fundamental operation of display choices and to provide them with the basic tools to address the complex work in the museum field. The chosen direction in the first year finds full application in the second year of the course, as it is dedicated exclusively to specialized historical-artistic courses differentiated according to the three directions characterizing the Course (18 CFU). The possibility of deepening knowledge and historical-methodological issues, together with increasing critical awareness and greater ability for independent judgment, characterizes all courses of the second year. In this perspective, the 6 CFU reserved for internship activities or other knowledge useful for entering the job market, such as operational contact with the professional reality in the field of knowledge, management, protection, and valorization of cultural heritage, should also be considered. Site visits and visits to exhibitions, museums, urban-architectural complexes, restoration sites, and environmental art installations in both urban and natural contexts are an integral part of the training path and represent, for all courses, a fundamental moment to place students in direct contact with artistic and architectural artifacts and the issues related to their knowledge, protection, and management, and to develop their critical reading abilities. Within the Department's structures, students have access during the entire study period to the "Giovanni Previtali" Photographic Archive (rich in over 50,000 photographs of artworks) and the Laboratory for Computer Applications in Iconography and Iconology, which can effectively complement the training path both in exam preparation and in research for written assignments or the Master's thesis. The Master's thesis, which plays a fundamental role in the entire training path, is assigned 27 CFU. Thanks to its structure and content, the Course allows access, upon admission test, to post-graduate training courses, such as the Doctoral Program in History of Art or the Specialization School in Historical-Artistic Heritage (both active at the University). Program, Texts, and Objectives
Professional status conferred by the degree.
Specialist Social Worker Master's graduates in Social Sustainability and Welfare Management can take the state exam for professional qualification and register with Register A of Specialist Social Workers.
The Specialist Social Worker can work, also in managerial and directorial roles, at public bodies (ASL, Prefectures, Ministries - Justice, Labor, Health, etc. - Local authorities, etc.). Additionally, Master's graduates in Social Sustainability and Welfare Management can work in managerial roles at Third Sector organizations (Social cooperatives, volunteer associations, NGOs, Foundations, Mutual Aid Societies, etc.) and private companies (residential facilities for the elderly, minors, asylum seekers, etc.).
This professional can also engage in autonomous professional activities in the fields of consulting, research, and social planning.
Final Exam Characteristics The final exam consists of discussing a thesis chosen by the candidate from a course in their individual study plan on a topic agreed upon with the responsible instructor (supervisor). A co-supervisor is required. The thesis is a written paper and is discussed before the Graduation Committee. The student may use paper, computer, audiovisual, multimedia, or other supports. The thesis should be a monographic work of appropriate length, with the following characteristics: a) be the result of thorough research; b) demonstrate the candidate's ability to organize and structure work; c) include adequate bibliographic references and precise citations; d) address the study's issues using a scientifically correct method, also demonstrating the candidate's critical abilities. At the student's discretion, and subject to the supervisor's favorable opinion, the thesis may be presented in a foreign language.
The final grade is expressed on a scale of 110, with possible honors.
Required Knowledge for Access To access the Master's degree in Social Sustainability and Welfare Management, one must hold a three-year university degree or a foreign degree recognized as equivalent. To enroll in the program, specific curricular requirements and adequate personal preparation are necessary.
Curricular requirements are met by holding a degree or a Master's degree in one of the following classes of D.M. 270/2004 (or corresponding in former D.M. 509/99):
L-12 (Linguistic Mediation)
L-14 (Juridical Services Sciences)
L-16 (Administration and Organization Sciences)

L-24 (Psychological Sciences and Techniques)
L-36 (Political Sciences and International Relations)
L-37 (Social Sciences for Cooperation, Development, and Peace)
L-39 (Social Services)
L-40 (Sociology)
L-41 (Statistics)
LMG/01 (Jurisprudence)
L/SNT1 (Nursing and Midwifery Health Professions)
L/STN/2 (Health Professions and Rehabilitation)
Admission is also permitted with a suitable degree in a different degree class, provided at least 75 ECTS are obtained in at least two of the following scientific-disciplinary sectors:
- Sociological/History/Political (SPS/03, SPS/04, SPS/05, SPS/07, SPS/08, SPS/09, SPS/10, M-STO/04, M-FIL/01, M-FIL/06);
- Legal (IUS/01, IUS/02; IUS/04, IUS/05, IUS/06, IUS/07, IUS/08, IUS/09, IUS/10, IUS/12, IUS/13, IUS/14; IUS/19);
- Economic (SECS-P/01, SECS-P/02, SECS-P/03, SECS-P/05, SECS-P/06, SECS-P/07, SECS-P/08, SECS-P/09, SECS-P/10, SECS-P/11, SECS-P/12, SECS-S/01, SECS-S/03, SECS-S/04, M-GGR/01, M-GGR/02);
- Anthropological/Psychological/Pedagogical (M-DEA/01; M-PSI/05; M-PSI/06; M-PED/01; M-PED/02)
The student's preparation adequacy is verified through an interview, the modalities of which will be described in the course's academic regulations and adequately advertised in time to ensure enrollment.
Only students meeting the curricular requirements can access the personal preparation verification.
Knowledge and Understanding.
Area Theoretical Paradigms and Analysis of Social Change At the end of the Master's program, graduates must possess multidisciplinary knowledge aimed at critically analyzing specific social issues and reflecting on the dynamics in which social services are embedded. These knowledge areas are pursued through a mix of disciplinary deepening with lectures, seminars, exercises, and simulations. This area aims to organize teaching and training activities to provide students with knowledge and understanding of the main dynamics of social change from sociological, historical, anthropological, pedagogical, and economic perspectives. These are knowledge and skills that connect and develop those typically associated with the first cycle, enabling the elaboration and application of original ideas based on the relationship between social sustainability and the design, planning, organization, management, and evaluation of social interventions in the welfare sector.
These educational objectives will be pursued through: lectures, case analysis, individual and group study, and verification activities to complete theoretical-practical experiences.
Area Support Tools In this area, advanced knowledge is included to equip students with the appropriate tools to transfer theories and reference paradigms into professional practice. Based on the teaching activities in this area, students are able to demonstrate knowledge and understanding: a. of the legal and institutional systems underlying social change and regulating intervention possibilities; b. of public communication systems, with particular attention to the interaction between citizens and services.
These educational objectives will be pursued through: lectures, case analysis, individual and group study, and verification activities to complete theoretical-practical experiences.
Area Professionalizing and Management of Social Services In this area, advanced knowledge is included to develop and support the most typical elements of the Specialist Social Worker profession. Based on the teaching activities in this area, students are able to demonstrate knowledge and understanding of the dynamics related to the design, planning, and organization of innovative welfare interventions; students will develop specific managerial skills in human resource coordination and management of complex structures.
These educational objectives will be pursued through: lectures, case analysis, individual and group study, and verification activities to complete theoretical-practical experiences.

Autonomy of judgment.
The Master's graduate in Social Sustainability and Welfare Management is able to:
- analyze and interpret social issues with full autonomy of judgment through the use of methods from social sciences and research;
- analyze and evaluate work contexts and select the most sustainable methods to ensure the efficiency and effectiveness of welfare interventions;
- design and coordinate local social and welfare interventions on the territory, and is able to coordinate social diagnosis projects with reference to the main areas of disadvantage;
- design information, awareness, and prevention programs with reference to different forms of social vulnerability.
Autonomy of judgment is achieved in particular through participation in seminar activities, preparation of assignments, internship activities, and tasks assigned by the supervisor for the preparation of the final exam.
The acquisition of autonomy of judgment is verified through the evaluation of the individual study plan courses and the evaluation of the degree of autonomy and ability to work, also in groups, during seminar activities, the internship, and the preparation of the final exam.
Learning ability.
Learning abilities are acquired throughout the study path, with particular regard to individual and group study, preparation of individual projects, internship experience, and activities carried out for the preparation of the final exam. The constant interaction between theoretical teaching moments and field experience provides students with learning abilities that are updated and verified throughout the entire educational path.
The Master's graduate is able to independently and responsibly pursue in-depth paths related to both continuing studies and entry into the labor market.
Learning ability is assessed through continuous verification forms during training activities, requiring the presentation of individual or group elaborations and research on data to be constructed, through tutoring activities in the execution of individual projects and internships, and through the evaluation of the ability to self-learn developed during the process.
Ability to apply knowledge and understanding.
Theoretical paradigms and analysis of social change: Students acquire knowledge to develop an adequate capacity for critical reading of scenarios related to social needs and institutional changes; in particular, students mature the ability to apply such knowledge to new or unusual problems, taking into account broader and interdisciplinary contexts connected to the specialized approach of social services and welfare services, allowing the application of multidisciplinary theoretical competencies in the operational and concrete practice of social professions.
These abilities can be assessed through written and oral exams and classroom presentations that verify students' ability to autonomously select the most appropriate theoretical and methodological premises and analytical tools for the issues addressed. These knowledge can also be verified through the preparation and presentation of the final exam.
Support tools: Students are able to apply the aforementioned knowledge, understanding abilities, and skills to the concrete situations of welfare systems; students will be able to understand the complex legal and institutional aspects of social issues and will have acquired the methodological tools of public communication in order to apply them in solving problems involving the need to protect the most vulnerable subjects.
These abilities can be assessed through written and oral exams and classroom presentations that verify students' ability to autonomously select the most appropriate theoretical and methodological premises and analytical tools for the issues addressed. These knowledge can also be verified through the preparation and presentation of the final exam.
Professional and welfare services management: Students are able to apply the aforementioned knowledge, understanding abilities, and skills to the concrete situations of welfare systems; they know how to design and coordinate interventions in specific spatial-temporal coordinates and apply their knowledge in the sustainable management of resources necessary for the effective conduct of those interventions, for example through the coordination of social service structures on the territory and the construction of inter-institutional networks. Furthermore, these knowledge develop into practical abilities through the practice carried out during the professional internship.
These abilities can be assessed through written and oral exams and classroom presentations that verify students' ability to autonomously select the most appropriate theoretical and methodological premises and analytical tools for the issues addressed. These knowledge can also be verified through the preparation and presentation of the final exam. Moreover, these knowledge are verified through the internship activity.

Communication Skills.
The Master's graduate possesses advanced communication and interaction skills towards the multiple interlocutors of the reference professional and institutional community; knows and knows how to use tools and techniques of interpersonal and mediated communication and information management; coordinates team work and has advanced relational skills in contexts characterized by listening relationships; contributes to strengthening networks also through participatory methodologies supporting decision-making processes.
Written and oral communication skills are acquired during training activities that require active student participation, through the preparation of written reports and documents and the oral presentation of the same and/or texts or documents proposed by the teacher. The acquisition of communication skills also occurs through internship activities, as well as through the preparation and discussion of the final exam.
The verification of the acquisition of communication skills is carried out through the evaluation of the student's expressive and argumentative ability during oral and written exams, internships, and the final exam, as well as through the evaluation of the written reports and documents prepared by the student within the individual activities that require them.
Planned occupational and professional outcomes for graduates.
Specialist Social Worker Graduates in Social Sustainability and Welfare Management can take the state exam for professional qualification and register with the A register of Specialist Social Workers.
The Specialist Social Worker can work, also with managerial and leadership functions, in public bodies (ASL, Prefectures, Ministries - Justice, Labor, Health, etc. - Local Authorities, etc.). Furthermore, the Master's graduate in Social Sustainability and Welfare Management can work with managerial functions in Third Sector Organizations (Social Cooperatives, Volunteer Associations, NGOs, Foundations, Mutual Aid Societies, etc.) and private companies (Residential facilities for elderly, minors, asylum seekers, etc.).
This professional figure can also exercise autonomous professional activities in the areas of consulting, research, and social planning.
Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIAN Associated competencies for the role.
Specialist Social Worker At the end of the study path, the Master's graduate will have acquired a plurality of competencies enabling the performance of the required functions; in particular, they will have gained:
- Advanced knowledge of social sustainability, with particular attention to social policies and welfare systems;
- Advanced knowledge of societal transformation phenomena, theories and methods of social work, and relevant legal disciplines;
- Ability to organize and manage social and socio-health services, public and social private, with attention to relational dynamics, participatory approaches, and management of human resources, organization of resources and structures, and economic management of entities, services, and organizations;
- Competencies for communication and information management;
- Social research competencies, related to the collection and processing of data useful for understanding the functioning of complex societies and the functioning of policies and services;
- Competencies to design integrated local well-being systems and activate and manage social protection policies for individuals, groups, and communities, social rights protection, and participatory local development.
Role in the work context.
Specialist Social Worker Within the work context, this professional is characterized by the ability to design, organize, and manage sustainable socio-assistential and socio-health services in various intervention areas; to coordinate projects related to the main areas of action of the welfare system; to evaluate and monitor interventions carried out by the structures and services to which they belong; to manage information and raise awareness on welfare issues within the context of various social problems. This is a professional who, besides the ability to work with people using the services, must be able to exercise management functions in terms of programming, organization, and management of social policies and services, lead work groups, and coordinate the services provided as well as the personnel employed in such services. This professional can also carry out social research activities and training activities related to the programming and management of social service policies.
Description of specific learning objectives.
The Master's degree course in Social Sustainability and Welfare Management LM-87 aims to train a specialist capable of exercising functions of design, organization, and management of interventions aimed at promoting social well-being through sustainable and responsible welfare services; the Master's graduate will also be able to offer consultancy to individuals, organizations, and institutions engaged in the field of social inclusion policies. Such functions may also concern relational dynamics, participatory processes, management and organization of resources and structures, economic management of entities, services, and organizations, as well as social policy design.
The Master's graduate in Social Sustainability and Welfare Management stands out not only for their ability to critically and reflectively interpret social phenomena, but also for their ability to experiment with intervention programs to protect the most vulnerable social groups through tools aimed at social innovation, valuing the relationship with service users, as well as with the network of local public institutions and social private entities.
Furthermore, the Master's graduate has the ability to integrate into the complex design and management of current welfare, understood as comprehensive well-being of the population, ranging from community welfare to corporate welfare.
Finally, the educational objective of this Master's degree course is also to provide students with training appropriate to the professional profile of Specialist Social Worker. Specifically, Master's graduates in Social Sustainability and Welfare Management have the knowledge and competencies to contribute to the production of development models respectful of the environment and sustainability.
The training path specifically includes, in the first year, the acquisition of intermediate/advanced knowledge in sociology (social inequalities, vulnerability SSD SPS/07, SPS/09), history (history of social security and welfare M-STO/04), economics (happiness and well-being economics, development economics SECS-P/01, SECS-P/02), administrative law (tenders, public contracts, public calls IUS/10); in the second year, advanced knowledge in labor law and social security (anti-discrimination, social law IUS/07), or private law with welfare legal structures (IUS/01); social planning (co-design, social innovation, design thinking SPS/04, SPS/07, SPS/09). The training path also includes a professional internship carried out in public or private entities with supervision by a Specialist Social Worker registered with the professional register. Finally, the training path includes the acquisition of B2 level English language proficiency and the completion of a final thesis.

Access to the course requires theoretical and practical knowledge related to the training objectives of the Bachelor's Degree courses in health professions of class L/SNT2.
The course is subject to numerical limitation, defined annually by the Ministry of University and Scientific Research.
Required knowledge for access: theory and practice related to exercising health and rehabilitation professions, general culture and logical reasoning; specific regulation of professional practice and health legislation, culture, science and mathematics, statistics, computer science and English, human and social sciences.
Professional status conferred by the title.
Manager/coordinator/responsible for advanced processes in the rehabilitation field The Master's graduate in Rehabilitative Sciences of Health Professions finds placement within the National and Regional Health Service, in private accredited and contracted structures with the SSN (Clinics, rehabilitation centers, Residential Health Care Facilities, thermal resorts and wellness centers, medical offices and/or multi-specialty clinics) where managerial, applied research and training skills are required.
The possession of the Master's Degree is legally and contractually required for leadership and teaching positions in the SSN (L. 43/2006).
Manager - Responsible for professional activities in the rehabilitation field, both in organizational and teaching contexts The Master's graduate in Rehabilitative Sciences of Health Professions primarily finds placement within the National and Regional Health Service, in private accredited and contracted structures with the SSN (Clinics, rehabilitation centers, Residential Health Care Facilities, thermal resorts and wellness centers, medical offices and/or multi-specialty clinics) where managerial, applied research and training skills are required. Additionally, the possession of the Master's Degree is legally and contractually required to hold the role of Director of Professional Teaching for Bachelor's and/or Master's Degree courses in the specific area.
Final exam characteristics To be admitted to the final Master's exam, the student must have passed all exams, obtained the required qualifications, and received a positive evaluation for all internships. The final exam for the degree, equivalent to 6 credits, consists of two parts:
a) an English language test consisting of reading and translating a scientific article in the rehabilitation field;
b) the discussion of a written thesis (dissertation) with originality and/or experimental or theoretical-applicative character regarding the in-depth study of managerial, research, training, and advanced professional methodology aspects specific to their professional field.
If a total score of 110/110 is achieved, the chair of the final exam committee will put the award of honors to a vote, which can only be granted unanimously by those present.
Required knowledge for access to the Master's Degree course in Rehabilitative Sciences of Health Professions is subject to numerical limitation. To access the selection, the possession of a three-year university degree or diploma in class L-SNT/2, or another title obtained abroad recognized as suitable, or another equivalent title is required.
The number of students admitted will be decided annually by Ministerial Decree.
Curricular requirements are met by holding a degree in one of the health professions of class L-SNT/2 (Rehabilitation Professions: professional health educator, physiotherapist, speech therapist, orthoptist - ophthalmic assistant, podiatrist, neuro and psychomotor therapist for childhood, psychiatric rehabilitation technician, occupational therapist) and/or a title equivalent according to current regulations or a title obtained abroad, recognized as suitable by the competent authorities, as specified in the Didactic Regulations of the Master's Degree.
Theoretical and practical knowledge related to the training objectives of the Bachelor's Degree courses in health professions of class L/SNT2 is required for access to the course.
The student's initial preparation is assessed through the results of the entrance exam, which covers the knowledge required for access: theory and practice related to exercising rehabilitation health professions; general culture and logical reasoning; regulation of specific professional practice and health legislation; scientific-mathematical culture, statistics, computer science and English; human and social sciences.
Verification of personal preparation is mandatory in all cases, and can only be accessed by students who meet the curricular requirements; in particular, this possession cannot be considered as verification of personal preparation.
Degree awarded.
MASTER'S DEGREE IN REHABILITATIVE SCIENCES Delivery method Conventional Knowledge and understanding.
1) ADVANCED REHABILITATION SCIENCES AND RESEARCH METHODOLOGY AREA Master's graduates in Rehabilitative Sciences of Health Professions, upon completion of their studies, must have acquired the following knowledge and understanding:
a) Knowledge of guidelines and advanced clinical progress in the disciplines foundational to the rehabilitation field;
b) Knowledge of advanced clinical progress and current research in rehabilitation, neurology, pediatrics, cardio-respiratory, musculoskeletal, otorhinolaryngological, orthoptic, and psychiatric sciences;
c) In-depth knowledge of clinical components susceptible to rehabilitation, referring to the profiles included in the class;
d) In-depth knowledge of statistical sciences applied to biomedical research and sources of scientific updates, aimed at developing original research studies and projects.
2) MANAGEMENT AND BUSINESS SCIENCES AREA Master's graduates in Rehabilitative Sciences of Health Professions, upon completion of their studies, must have acquired the following knowledge and understanding:
a) Knowledge of principles of public law and administrative law applicable to relationships between administrations and users involved in health services;
b) Knowledge of main theories and techniques of business organization and processes for optimizing the use of human, computer, and technological resources;
c) Knowledge of essential elements of business organization and human resource management, with particular reference to issues in the health sector;
d) Knowledge of epidemiological methodology related to the health and rehabilitation field.
3) EDUCATION AND TRAINING SCIENCES AREA Master's graduates in Rehabilitative Sciences of Health Professions, upon completion of their studies, must have acquired the following knowledge and understanding:
a) Knowledge of pedagogical models, learning theories, and tutorial methodologies;
b) Knowledge of "core" principles foundational to training at basic, post-basic, and continuous levels, with specific reference to the health professions sector;
c) Knowledge of principles foundational to the historical and educational evolution of health professions;
d) Knowledge of the method for independent study and continuous training.
4) PROFESSIONAL COMMUNICATION AREA Master's graduates in Rehabilitative Sciences of Health Professions, upon completion of their studies, must have acquired the following knowledge and understanding:
a) Knowledge of communication theories and relational development at the level of the individual, groups, and organizations;
b) Knowledge of verbal, non-verbal, and written communication techniques for managing interpersonal relationships with individuals, groups, patients, and their families;
c) Knowledge of the evolution and history of health professions;
d) Knowledge of multicultural and intercultural phenomena in contemporary society.

Judgment autonomy.
The master's graduate in Rehabilitation Sciences must be able to predict and evaluate the effects of their own decisions and activities in management, teaching/learning, and applied clinical research fields, assuming the corresponding responsibility. They must demonstrate the ability to make decisions, express diagnostic/evaluation judgments in the rehabilitation field and in the specific professional area, and be able to participate in research activities to understand or contribute to advancements in rehabilitation.
They must also formulate autonomous reflections through multidisciplinary scientific, legal, ethical, and deontological discussion.
The master's graduate's judgment autonomy will be fully realized through the habitual and judicious use of communication, knowledge, professional skills, clinical reasoning (diagnostic and evaluation process), emotions, values, and reflection in daily practice for the benefit of the individual or the community.
This ability will be achieved through frontal lessons and specific teaching/learning activities (internship and teaching laboratories).
Verification methods will be: written and oral reports on technical/professional aspects, in-course tests, briefings with tutors and coordinators, and capacity demonstrated during internship activities.

Learning abilities.
The master's graduate at the end of the study path must be able to:
- Evaluate their performance based on professional practice standards and organizational criteria, continuously identifying their educational needs in relation to the nature and complexity of problems to address and the project and operational strategies to manage, in order to realize their professional improvement plan;
- Independently adopt effective strategies to continue learning, formally and informally, throughout their professional life, also through further training paths;
- Use complete information systems, software, and databases to collect, organize, and catalog information; identify a problem, conduct a literature review on the topic, critically analyze the problem and current knowledge, develop a strategy to apply research in practice, and facilitate the dissemination of research results;
- Attend further higher education training paths oriented towards research, health management, and educational methodology.
Learning abilities are acquired during the two-year program through frontal activities, internships, seminars with in-depth projects, and individual study work within research methodology and rehabilitation evidence activities, as well as activities preparing for the thesis. Verification of these abilities occurs through the formulation of the research problem, data collection based on the analyzed context, evaluation of collected evidence, integration between data collection and the formulated problem/question, and evaluation of the entire process by querying databases and critically analyzing international scientific publications.

Ability to apply knowledge and understanding.
1) ADVANCED REHABILITATION SCIENCES AND RESEARCH METHODOLOGY AREA Master's graduates in Rehabilitation Sciences for Health Professions must be able to:
a) Apply guidelines, procedures, and therapeutic programs related to the clinical context under study;
b) Apply research activity results to continuously improve the quality of care;
c) Ensure the impact on the work team of the most recent methods and tools provided by continuous scientific and technological development in the field, particularly regarding opportunities offered by bioengineering, bioelectronics, and bioinformatics applications in rehabilitation;
d) Promote and manage the development of interdisciplinary and interprofessional recovery and rehabilitation projects, relevant to both individual users and user categories;
e) Conduct systematic bibliographic research and periodic updates;
f) Read, translate, and critically analyze specific scientific articles in the area, discussing their outcomes;
g) Design and implement a research plan and/or a thesis.
These knowledge and understanding abilities will be acquired and verified primarily through curricular teachings and respective exams in different areas, including internship.

Communication skills.

Possession of the Master's Degree is legally and contractually required for leadership and teaching positions in the National Health Service (L. 43/2006).

Description of admission tests.
The course is quota-limited, defined annually by the Ministry of University and Scientific Research. Admission requires passing an entrance test. The admission test consists of solving eighty questions as follows: 32 questions on theory/practice relevant to exercising the healthcare professions included in the Master's degree class of interest; 18 on general culture and logical reasoning; 10 questions each on the following topics: regulation of healthcare professions included in the Master's degree class of interest and health legislation, Scientific-mathematical culture, statistics, informatics, and English, Human and Social Sciences. Each question has multiple-choice answers with five options, only one of which is correct.

Required knowledge for admission: theory and practice of healthcare and rehabilitation professions, general culture and logical reasoning; specific regulation of professional practice and health legislation, culture, science and mathematics, statistics, informatics and English, human and social sciences.

Work context function.
Advanced process leader/coordinator/responsible in rehabilitation field. Leadership and/or coordination functions in rehabilitation management and organization of rehabilitation activities, development, construction, and implementation of teaching and pedagogical pathways applied to rehabilitation.
Leader - Responsible for professional activities in the rehabilitation area, both in organizational and teaching fields. Personnel management and rehabilitation area organization functions, rehabilitation processes and procedures at management level; design and implementation functions of rehabilitation procedures and pathways; development and design functions of healthcare training, at access to profession and/or ECM level.

Description of specific educational objectives.
Specific educational objectives of the Course.
Graduates in this class, in accordance with Article 6, paragraph 3, of Legislative Decree 30 December 1992, No. 502 and subsequent amendments, in accordance with Law 26 February 1999, No. 42, and in accordance with Law 10 August 2000, No. 251, are healthcare professionals whose specific field of activity and responsibility is determined by the contents of the ministerial decrees establishing professional profiles and didactic orders of the respective university courses and post-basic training, as well as specific deontological codes.
Master's graduates included in this class (podiatrist, physiotherapist, speech therapist, orthoptist - ophthalmology assistant, neuro and psychomotor therapist for developmental age, psychiatric and psychosocial rehabilitation education and rehabilitation technician, occupational therapist, professional educator) propose protocols, methods, and procedures related to recovery sciences, manage both organizationally and teaching/learning the rehabilitation, care, and prevention areas for pathologies and disorders of motor skills, motor disabilities, psychomotor and language disorders, motor and sensory vision disorders, neuropsychiatric pathologies of developmental age, psychiatric pathologies, and educational therapy aimed at psychosocial reintegration of individuals in difficulty.
The Master's Degree in Rehabilitation Sciences for Health Professions aims to:
• provide an advanced professional methodology to intervene with high competence in assistance, management, teaching, and clinical research processes in one of the fields relevant to the various healthcare professions included in the class;
• deepen the basic knowledge of sciences relevant to each professional figure in the class, necessary for making decisions in rehabilitation;
• develop an integrated approach to techniques, procedures, and health management within healthcare facilities of low, medium, or high complexity for managing human, technological, informational, and financial resources available in healthcare facilities;
• provide methodological knowledge in pedagogical/teaching fields to intervene in healthcare training processes, in teaching the discipline relevant to the specific professional figure, in basic, complementary, and permanent training, in tutorial and internship coordination activities;
• enhance research methods and tools in the areas relevant to the professional figures of the class, in clinical-care areas, in organization, and in training.
The specific educational objectives of this Course are aimed at advanced training for graduates already qualified to exercise one of the eight professions of the class, and their achievement is realized through theoretical and practical learning focused on the class specificity.

The main learning areas of the Master's Degree Course are:
1) ADVANCED REHABILITATION SCIENCES AREA, which includes, on one hand, teachings aimed at implementing clinical (MED/10 - MED/11 - MED/25 – MED/26- MED/31 – MED /33 - MED/38) and integrated rehabilitation (MED/26 - MED/48 – MED/50) processes and procedures, and on the other hand, consolidation of the scientific method applied to research and critical interpretation of available international scientific evidence (MED/ 42 – SECS-S/02 – MED/48) for structuring a research design and writing a specific thesis.
2) EDUCATION AND TRAINING SCIENCES AREA, addressing the learning of teaching and tutorial methodologies, both in the university and professional sectors, and the historical/temporal evolution of rehabilitation healthcare professions (MED/02 - MED/48), based on teachings related to pedagogy applied to adults in the specific field of action (MED/45 - M – PSI/04).
3) MANAGEMENT AND HEALTH MANAGEMENT SCIENCES AREA, which includes teachings relevant to understanding the regulations governing healthcare organizations and the workplace (IUS/01 – IUS/07- IUS/09), knowledge of the dimensions of business planning in healthcare (MED/42), as well as personnel management and procedures in rehabilitation (M –PSI/06 - MED/48).
4) PROFESSIONAL COMMUNICATION AREA, which includes teachings for developing relational and communication abilities (M- DEA/01 - M-PSI/01 - M-PSI/08 - L-ART/05), ethical and deontological abilities (MED/43) necessary for performing the professional and corporate roles that the master's graduate may hold (professional teaching, personnel and management/learning structure coordination, teaching responsibilities in healthcare professions degree courses, rehabilitation area leadership, health leadership).

Starting from the 2019-20 academic year, in compliance with Legislative Decree 31 January 2018, the Course modifies the didactic organization and programming by including the SSD L-LIN/01 Glottology and Linguistics, M-FIL/05 Philosophy and Theory of Languages, theoretical and applied language sciences area, considering that these disciplines constitute the fundamental theoretical basis for future specialists working in language pathology areas.

Students must attend an ENGLISH language course necessary for reading, understanding, and interpreting reference scientific literature, to achieve a high level of written and spoken knowledge of at least one European Union language.

Admission Requirements The indispensable curricular requirements for admission to the Master's Degree Course are identified through: a) graduates from Bachelor's Degree Courses that demonstrate a specific and proven cultural and didactic affinity, particularly the class (L-19, Sciences of Education and Training); b) graduates from Bachelor's Degree Courses in the fields of human, psycho-social, and literary sciences who have acquired a sufficient number of credits (approximately 60-80 in total) in areas and scientific-disciplinary sectors consistent with the orientation of the Master's Degree Course, particularly those related to pedagogical, psychological, sociological, philosophical, and historical disciplines. Professional status conferred by the title. Expert consultant in the design and management of training processes in organizations The graduate in "Sciences for Training and Pedagogical Consulting in Organizations" will be able to access two professional fields: a) consulting for individuals, families, and communities on education, inclusion, disability, and personal and professional development; b) consulting for organizations on human resource management, workplace well-being, coordination, corporate training, and the design of training activities for young people and adults.
Final Exam Characteristics The final exam consists of the preparation and discussion before a Commission of a written dissertation, whose content and development occur with the assistance and under the direction of a faculty member. To be admitted to the exam, the student must have passed all exams and training activities specified in the Study Plan. The exam aims to demonstrate the acquisition of specific knowledge, skills, and competencies and the ability to critically reflect on them, and will be graded out of 110 with possible distinction.
Required Knowledge for Admission To be admitted to the Master's Degree Course in Sciences for Training and Pedagogical Consulting in Organizations, one must hold a three-year university degree or another foreign degree recognized as suitable.
Curricular requirements are satisfied by holding a degree in one of the following degree classes (ex D.M. 270/2004 or ex D.M. 509/1999 or another equivalent foreign degree): Sciences of Education and Training (L-19), Philosophy (L-5), Literature (L-10), Modern Languages and Cultures (L-11), Linguistic Mediation (L-12), Sciences of Administration and Organization (L-16), Sciences of Economics and Business Management (L-18), Communication Sciences (L-20), Sports and Motor Activities Sciences (L-22), Psychological Sciences and Techniques (L-24), Economic Sciences (L-33), Political Sciences and International Relations (L-36), Social Sciences for Cooperation, Development, and Peace (L-37), Social Service (L-39), Sociology (L-40), History (L-42), Rehabilitation Health Professions Degrees, Professional Educator (L/SNT02), Nursing Degree (L-SNT01).
Graduates in the listed classes must also have earned at least 40 CFU in the following scientific-disciplinary sectors: SPS/01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 06, 07, 08, 09, 10, 11, 13, 14; M-PED/01, 02, 03, 04; M-PSI/01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 06; SECS-P/01, 07, 08, 10; M-FIL/01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 06; M-STO/01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 06, 07, 08, 09; L-ART/06; L-FIL-LET/08, 09, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14; M-DEA/01; MED/25, 42, 44, 45, 48; IUS/01, 07, 09, 14; M-EDF/01, 02, and must have obtained the degree with a grade not lower than 95/110. (If the graduate obtained a degree grade lower than 95/110, they must have passed, with a weighted average not lower than 26/30, the courses in their study plan for at least 40 CFU in the following scientific-disciplinary sectors: SPS/01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 06, 07, 08, 09, 10, 11, 13, 14; M-PED/01, 02, 03, 04; M-PSI/01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 06; SECS-P/01, 07, 08, 10; M-FIL/01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 06; M-DEA/01; L-ART/06; L-FIL-LET/08, 09, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14; M-GGR/01; MED/25, 42, 44, 45, 48; IUS/01, 07, 09, 14; M-EDF/01, 02).
Students not meeting the above requirements may also be admitted to the course of study, provided they satisfy the requirements specified in the Didactic Regulations of the course. For admission to the course, students possessing the required curricular qualifications must take a test to verify their personal preparation. The test involves an interview on topics of pedagogy and didactics, general sociology, work psychology, and social psychology. The methods for verifying personal preparation are detailed in the Didactic Regulations of the course.

Judgment Autonomy.
The training path offered by the Master's Degree course enables students to acquire:
- Ability to integrate pedagogical, psychological, and sociological knowledge to manage complex theoretical and practical problems using interdisciplinary analysis approaches and perspectives.
- Competence in formulating critical judgments regarding different study areas even in the presence of partial or incomplete information.
- Ability to retrieve data and sources useful for defining evaluations on theoretical and methodological issues.
- Ability to use critical thinking capable of engaging with interpretations different from one's own.
- Ability to search for and use sources, documents, and texts not encountered during the study path, functional to deepening and acquiring specific professional competencies useful for entering the workforce.
- Ability to personally utilize research tools to produce situated knowledge necessary for resolving specific problems.
- Ability to systematize and validate knowledge derived from work practices.
- Ability to identify the criticalities and potentials of the adopted theoretical or methodological perspective.
In particular, it is considered that courses delivered in pedagogical and philosophical fields (M-PED/01, M-PED/03, M-PSI/06, M-FIL/01, M-FIL/06) contribute to acquiring a personal autonomous perspective of judgment on educational issues. Furthermore, to strengthen this area, annually in the second semester the Master's Degree course proposes project work activities that students must then discuss in peer groups and in the presence of at least one course instructor. It is during this feedback session that judgment autonomy is assessed through a 'pass' grade, which, if achieved, allows the student to be awarded the corresponding CFU for 'Other knowledge useful for entering the workforce'.

Learning Ability.
The Master's Degree course dedicates particular attention to developing the skills necessary for continuous updating, adaptation, and growth of one's knowledge, stimulating and developing in particular: competence in nourishing and self-directing one's personal and professional growth process even after the completion of the training path; ability to search for and use sources, documents, texts, and online resources not encountered during the study path, functional to deepening and acquiring specific professional competencies useful for entering the workforce; ability to process situated knowledge and functional to the context in which one is called to work; ability to leverage technological methodologies and tools for the collaborative representation and management of online knowledge.
One of the ways this ability is supported is through the use of versatile spaces during lessons. In these adjacent spaces to classrooms, students are invited to independently carry out projects and research by consulting bibliographic materials. All delivered courses are required to use these spaces at least once (see Committee of April 9, 2015). This skill is primarily assessed through intermediate exams of the courses and the final exam.

Application of Knowledge and Understanding.
Consulting Area
- Ability to design a situated training intervention;
- Ability to interpret a training need;
- Ability to manage the relationship between client and users of the training intervention.
Training Design Area
- Ability to design a micro-consulting intervention;
- Ability to identify which strategy to adopt to manage a training process;
- Ability to adopt different relational registers according to the training issue addressed and the client.

Communication Skills.
The specific competencies and methodologies characterizing the Master's Degree Course are developed through experiences, laboratories, and internships where it will be possible to acquire:
- Ability to provide information, data, and solutions to different types of interlocutors, from sector experts to non-specialists, from representatives of the working world to specialists in psychological, pedagogical, and sociological fields.
- Ability to formulate plausible conclusions consistently with the premises and methodologies specific to a particular disciplinary field.
- Ability to professionally use advanced computer and telecommunication systems, as well as an EU second language (English).
- Ability to use the specialized language of pedagogical, psychological, and sociological disciplines in non-academic contexts such as professional and informal settings.
- Ability to reconstruct and communicate data, ideas, and information in situations of ambiguity and complexity.
- Ability to develop communication and training projects using the methodologies and tools characteristic of information and communication technologies.
In particular, it is considered that the teachings delivered in the psychological and sociological sectors (M-PSI and SPS) contribute to the acquisition of communication skills. Furthermore, to strengthen this area, all teachers are invited by the Teaching Committee (see Teaching Committee of April 9, 2015) to adopt teaching approaches where students are involved in public classroom presentations of work done in class. This skill is mainly assessed through the presentation of the final thesis.

https://consulenza-pedagogica-organizzazioni.unisi.it/it www.unisi.it Specific educational objectives description.
Specific educational objectives of the Course The Master's Degree prepares professionals with pedagogical, psychological, and sociological knowledge, transversal competencies, and linguistic and managerial skills, capable of responding to the increasingly widespread demand for employment at a managerial level in the areas of personal services and human resource management in public-private structures operating in the sectors of goods and services production, education and corporate training, and consulting for individuals, communities, and organizations.
The Master's Degree allows the acquisition of skills, competencies, and abilities related to:
a) the use of theoretical models in the fields of pedagogical, psychological, and social studies;
b) the use of methodologies derived from different paradigms of theoretical and empirical research;
c) the analysis and design of training paths applied to organizational transformation processes and human resource management;
d) the design of educational, training, and consulting services for individuals and organizations;
e) the design and implementation of research to support the management of consulting interventions in public-private, profit, and non-profit structures.
Description of the educational path The Master's Degree course is structured over two years. The teachings belonging to pedagogical, psychological, and sociological areas, delivered in the first year, provide interpretative theories, methodologies, and teaching methods, aimed at developing theoretical competencies and acquiring the tools useful in the fields of education, consulting, and training in various social and organizational contexts.
In the second year, teachings related to specialized disciplinary fields are provided to offer the necessary competencies to understand social and organizational phenomena, conduct empirical investigations, address issues related to social, school, and professional inclusion, and manage projects as a project manager.
During the course, students can choose from a limited selection of teachings to orient their path towards the area of consulting and intervention methodologies for individuals/families or for communities/organizations. Within the teachings, research-based, action learning, practice-based learning, and problem-based learning approaches are used, models that involve learning settings where students can investigate practical problems in groups, using the acquired theoretical and methodological frameworks to find possible solutions.
The Master's Degree requires an English language proficiency test (B2 level) to be taken in agreement with and with the support of the University Language Center, as well as a training internship. At the end of the second year, a thesis discussion is also required, with topics agreed upon with the supervisor.
The rules for writing and organizing the thesis are reported on the website https://www.dsfuci.unisi.it/it Transversal competencies Beyond acquiring disciplinary knowledge and skills, the Course aims to foster the acquisition of certain transversal competencies required by the professional world through specific training activities offered in both the first and second year (these activities, delivered in TAF F CFUs entitled 'Other useful knowledge for entering the workplace'). The main transversal competencies developed are: critical thinking (advanced knowledge in a work or study area, requiring a critical understanding of theories and principles); problem solving (advanced skills demonstrating mastery and innovation necessary to solve complex and unpredictable problems in a specialized work or study area); decision making (managing complex technical/professional activities or projects by taking responsibility for decisions in unpredictable work or study contexts).

Final exam characteristics The final exam consists of the discussion of a thesis chosen by the candidate in a course among those present in the individual study plan and on a topic agreed with the teacher responsible for that course (supervisor). A co-supervisor is required.
The thesis must be original work developed by the student under the guidance of the supervisor and must have the following characteristics: a) be the result of thorough research; b) demonstrate the candidate's ability to organize and structure work; c) provide adequate bibliographic references and precise citations of sources; d) verify the issues related to the subject of study using a scientifically correct method, also showing the candidate's critical abilities. At the student's discretion, and subject to the favorable opinion of the supervisor, the student may submit the thesis in a foreign language.
The final grade is expressed on a scale of 110 with possible honors.

Degree awarded.
Master's degree in International Sciences Teaching method Conventional Knowledge and understanding.
Generic Area Master's graduates in International Sciences possess specialist-level knowledge of international issues in legal, economic, historical, political and social contexts, supported by adequate linguistic competence in at least two foreign languages. The typical competencies of International Sciences are delivered through varying disciplinary doses and different focuses to achieve diverse knowledge paths: in particular, they study the typical processes of formation and transformation of the international community, the areas of action of cooperation with developing regions, the challenges of globalization and the transformation processes that have affected European countries in institutional, legal, economic, political and social terms over the last half-century, and the evolution of the political and administrative organization of the European Union. The understanding of different disciplines, distributed semester by semester, is facilitated by the use of appropriate teaching aids. In particular, courses include active participation in seminars, conferences and meetings with high-profile specialists. In consideration of the training objectives, Master's graduates have been offered stimuli for critical discussion of the topics covered. Acquisition of knowledge and understanding is assessed during both final exams and in-course assessments. The thesis work constitutes a fundamental part of the training, during which future Master's graduates engage in developing original topics directly related to the world of work or suitable for further scientific research.
Historical Area Specialist knowledge of the processes of development of contemporary history in a comparative perspective, with attention to the European and extra-European context, the evolution of international relations, the organization and functioning of diplomatic services, and the evolution of legal and political systems within the European framework.
Economic Area Specialist knowledge of issues related to international economics, monetary economics, environmental economics and development economics.
Legal Area Specialist knowledge regarding the discipline and functioning of international organizations, human rights protection, international economic law, and European Union legislation, in its internal and external relevance.
Political Area Specialist knowledge in the field of comparative analysis of political systems within the European and extra-European context and understanding of the factors determining the current dynamics of international relations.
Linguistic Area Knowledge and understanding of two foreign languages.
Acquisition of knowledge of English at least at level B2 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages of the Council of Europe.
