Judgment autonomy.
The Master's degree program in International Studies aims to provide its graduates with the ability to profitably and confidently apply the knowledge and concepts acquired during their university studies. The teaching methodology, which goes beyond traditional lectures to include seminar activities, research, exercises, and group work, is designed to develop the ability to critically analyze sources and their organization and evaluation. The Master's graduate has deepened the acquired knowledge through the identification of relevant materials (historical documents, international documents, court rulings, doctrine, specialized bibliography, and press). In this context, an extensive seminar program and a teaching organization that rewards proactive student participation will serve to develop judgment autonomy regarding available data. Assessment will therefore rely on a set of evaluations based on both the fundamental concepts of various courses and moments of original synthesis and analysis by students, including in-course assessments, simulations, and tests. This will also enable the integration of knowledge acquired across different courses. The multidisciplinary perspective of the Master's degree program in International Studies thus enables the graduate to independently reflect on the surrounding reality, whether represented by social changes or historical or international events. In this context, the opportunity to complete internships or traineeships at institutions and companies during the study period constitutes a significant moment for verifying the ability to apply learned knowledge models and evaluate them in terms of appropriateness and, if necessary, legitimacy.

Learning ability.
Master's graduates in International Studies possess a foundational methodology applicable in a general context for acquiring a wide range of knowledge related to characteristic and related disciplines. The teaching, based on a diverse range of educational activities, offers the primary set of tools for achieving learning ability. Nevertheless, the specificity of the studies undertaken enables them to master the main aspects of international legal, economic, historical-political, institutional, and social disciplines. The flexibility and heterogeneity of the educational program are not indicators of reduced specific competence but rather of the completion of knowledge that appears distinct but is strongly interconnected. Therefore, upon completion of the Master's degree, it is possible to view the professional world as an opportunity for further specialization, allowing seamless participation in full-immersion courses, internships, master's programs, and doctoral studies. The inclusion of study paths strongly characterized by distinct educational and professional profiles (international and diplomatic careers, development and cooperation, professions related to European integration processes) multiplies opportunities for socialization and learning through numerous complementary educational activities.

The opportunity to complete internships and traineeships at national and international institutions and companies, particularly within the community system, constitutes an important verification moment, enabling the acquisition of additional knowledge appropriately valued within individual educational paths. In summary, the Master's graduate possesses a high level of autonomy applicable both in the professional field and for further study. The final thesis and the internships scheduled in the second year constitute the logical completion of this educational path.

Ability to apply knowledge and understanding.
Generic Area Master's graduates possess the necessary competencies to critically address international issues in legal, economic, historical, political, and social contexts. These competencies enable them to design and monitor high-complexity projects and strategies in the fields of international relations, cooperation, and European studies. The teaching tools for acquiring necessary knowledge include seminar exercises in written and oral form, preparation of essays, and organization of study groups on original topics, primarily focused on current affairs. This teaching organization promotes genuinely multidisciplinary approaches. An important verification moment for the ability to apply knowledge and understanding is participation in internships at public and private institutions operating in professional sectors aligned with the educational objectives of the Master's degree program. Such internships are an essential step, aimed at developing the final thesis, a synthesis moment where knowledge and skills acquired throughout the educational path are applied.

Historical Area Master's graduates acquire the ability to analyze scenarios and develop projects and strategies while considering the historical evolution of phenomena under their attention.

Economic Area Master's graduates acquire the ability to analyze scenarios and develop projects and strategies while considering the global economic context and the main factors determining its evolution.

Legal Area Master's graduates acquire the ability to analyze the legal framework and the necessary competencies to address and manage complex issues in the field of international law and jurisdiction.

Political Area Master's graduates acquire the ability to analyze scenarios and develop projects and strategies while considering the political-institutional context specific to case studies.

Linguistic Area Ability to fluently use two foreign languages in written and oral form, including reference to disciplinary terminology.

Communication skills.
The teaching organization also aims to adequately develop the communication skills of master's graduates, verified through numerous teaching tools (in particular oral and written exams, as well as the writing and discussion of the final thesis). First, they refine their ability to logically and coherently organize the knowledge acquired during the courses. To this end, individual and group presentations and the use of computer tools are encouraged. Master's graduates have mastered the technical languages related to the various disciplines studied, particularly regarding the correct use of terms and concepts in the legal/economic and historical/political fields. The activities related to the study of foreign languages contribute to acquiring these competencies. Second, the acquired communication skills concern written communication and the drafting of scientific texts. To this end, in addition to the written works presented for seminars and in-course assessments, the work done for the writing of the thesis (final exam) is fundamental, during which the master's graduate, closely guided by the supervisor, learns the technique of scientific dissemination of ideas, the importance of justifying and adequately supporting their statements, dividing their arguments appropriately, and finally, preparing conclusions to highlight the originality of their thought and the suggested solutions.
Expected career and professional opportunities for graduates.
International relations specialists in public and private sectors. Typical career opportunities for graduates of the Study Course are:
- Diplomatic career;
- European institutions;
- International governmental and non-governmental organizations;
- Development cooperation bodies;
- Companies and other private organizations operating in the international field (multinationals, banks, insurance companies, sector associations and volunteer organizations);
- Ministry offices, embassies and consulates, cultural institutes abroad;
- Research and study centers.
Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIAN, ENGLISH Associated competencies.
International relations specialists in public and private sectors The master's graduate possesses competencies in international law, economic and financial analysis, global political scenario analysis, and reconstruction and interpretation of the historical roots of international events. They master the comparative method and the analytical and cognitive tools specific to the fields where the international dimension of economic, political, and social phenomena unfolds. They have written and oral proficiency in at least two foreign languages. Based on these competencies, they are able to develop and apply management and organizational strategies in their professional fields.
Description of admission tests.
No admission tests are required for the course. Function in work context.
International relations specialists in public and private sectors The Study Course aims to train master's graduates capable of performing leadership functions at national and international organizations as experts in implementing public policies and experts in internationalization processes; consulting, planning, drafting, and managing projects in the field of international cooperation, assuming responsible roles within national and supranational, governmental and non-governmental organizations; policy-making expertise within public institutions and community institutions; responsible functions supporting the operation of representative institutions at the national level, within international, governmental and non-governmental organizations, European institutions, international relations offices of public administrations and private companies.

Description of specific educational objectives.
The specific educational objectives of the Study Course are:
a) To provide analytical tools and comparative institutional knowledge aimed at understanding, evaluating, and managing issues concerning contemporary societies, complex relations between states, democratization processes, and human rights protection. The cognitive data and competencies acquired aim to enable the master's graduate to develop the necessary abilities to enter the job market, plan, and implement high-complexity operational strategies with awareness. Master's graduates will thus be able to access, in high-level roles, employment and consultancy activities at diplomatic structures, international and supranational bodies, public administration offices dealing with international relations, human rights, cooperation, and peace; non-governmental organizations, public and private enterprises developing internationally significant activities; European Union institutions.
b) To provide, prioritizing methodological and comparative analysis tools, knowledge regarding the dynamics of structural change processes occurring in the international arena, as well as basic knowledge of the methodologies used by multilateral cooperation organizations for developing cooperation programs. The Study Course aims to train competent professionals to plan, manage, and coordinate activities in this sector. Master's graduates will therefore be able to perform high-responsibility functions within public administration and international organizations in the field of cooperation and aid to developing countries; in the third sector, particularly in transnational NGOs and organizations protecting citizens' rights.
To achieve these objectives, the training path includes a common base in the following disciplinary sectors: M-STO/04 Contemporary History, SPS/06 History of International Relations, SECS-P/01 Political Economy, IUS/13 International Law, SPS/04 Political Science, L-LIN/04 French Language, L-LIN/12 English Language, L-LIN/07 Spanish Language. Additional credits are acquired in the following scientific-disciplinary sectors: IUS/19 History of Medieval and Modern Law, M-GGR/01 Geography, SPS/07 General Sociology, SPS/13 History and Institutions of Africa, SPS/05 History and Institutions of the Americas, SPS/02 History of Political Doctrines. Training activities also include internships, traineeships, and other knowledge useful for entering the job market, computer proficiency, English language proficiency (B2 or C1 level of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages of the Council of Europe), as well as preparation for the final exam.
The Master's Degree Course in International Sciences aims to provide methodological and cultural, scientific, and professional knowledge in the following learning areas:
historical area - with particular reference to acquiring competencies related to the dynamics of development and underdevelopment processes, contemporary history from a comparative perspective, regional histories (Asia, Africa, and Latin America), evolution of international relations, modes of organization and functioning of diplomatic services, evolution of legal and political systems within the European context;
economic area - with particular reference to deepening themes related to international economics, monetary economics, environmental economics, and development economics;
legal area - with particular reference to the regulation and functioning of international organizations, human rights protection, international economic law, and European Union legislation, in its internal and external relevance;
political area - with particular reference to comparative analysis of political systems within the European and extra-European context and understanding the factors determining the current dynamics of international relations;
linguistic area - with particular reference to acquiring the ability to fluently use two foreign languages, both in written and oral form, including discipline-specific terminology.
These competencies aim to develop in the student the ability to understand and analyze issues concerning the international dimension of political, economic, and social phenomena.

Regional School Diploma Fees and Contributions For information on tuition and contribution amounts, visit the University website www.unisi.it/tasse Dates and Deadlines For information on dates and deadlines, visit the University website "Study Plan" www.unisi.it/didattica/immatricolazioni-e-iscrizioni/immatricolazioni Roles Responsibilities for Student Mobility ANTONELLA NALDINI Student Mobility Coordinator/Chair of Teaching Committee FILIBERTO MARIA SEVERI Program, Texts, and Objectives Admission Requirements Admission to the Master's Degree Course is nationally regulated. The number of students admitted, within the limits defined by the class, is decided annually in accordance with laws 264/1999 and 1/2002 by the Minister of University and Scientific and Technological Research. Students who have graduated in health professions in Nursing and Midwifery may be admitted to the Master's Degree Course in Nursing and Midwifery Sciences without academic debts. Additionally, students holding diplomas or equivalent certificates obtained in Italy (pursuant to law 42/1999) or abroad may be admitted, provided they have completed at least 20 university credits in the professional scientific disciplinary sector, as well as at least 50 clinical internship credits; in such cases, the Curriculum Regulations specify the required curricular integrations. Required knowledge for admission: theory and practice relevant to the exercise of nursing and midwifery health professions; general culture and logical reasoning; regulation of specific professional practice and health legislation; scientific-mathematical culture, statistics, computer science, and English; human and social sciences Professional status conferred by the degree.
Master of Science in Nursing and Midwifery Hospitals, Local Health Authorities, IRCS, Private and Non-Profit Organizations, Nursing Homes, Home Care Service Cooperatives, etc., in dependent or self-employed status.
Final Exam Characteristics The final exam for the Master's Degree Course, worth 6 CFU, consists of writing an original research paper and its presentation, demonstrating the candidate's advanced cultural and professional training to intervene with high-level competencies in management, training, and research processes within nursing and midwifery health professions. The final paper is defended before a judging committee that assigns a grade out of 110, with possible honors.
Required Knowledge for Admission Students who have graduated in health professions of class L/SNT1 may be admitted to the Master's Degree Course in Nursing and Midwifery Sciences. Additionally, students holding diplomas or equivalent certificates obtained in Italy (pursuant to law 42/1999) or abroad may be admitted, provided they have completed at least 20 CFU in SSD MED/45 for Nurses and MED/47 for Midwives, as well as at least 50 CFU of clinical internship; in such cases, the Curriculum Regulations specify the required curricular integrations. The suitability of personal preparation will be verified using methods indicated in the Curriculum Regulations of the Master's Degree Course. Degree Awarded.
MASTER'S DEGREE IN NURSING AND MIDWIFERY SCIENCES Teaching Delivery Method Conventional Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area The Master's graduate knows the fundamental theoretical and applied principles of management, training, and research processes in their professional fields, as well as general bioethical, deontological, legal, and medical-legal principles. Specifically, they possess managerial knowledge to lead nursing and midwifery services in simple and complex healthcare structures; they possess advanced professional knowledge to intervene in healthcare processes of nursing and midwifery disciplines; they possess epidemiological and statistical knowledge to analyze community health needs and socio-cultural factors influencing them, as well as the evolution and changes in healthcare systems; they possess computer science and research methodology knowledge to design and conduct clinical-assistive, organizational, and educational studies, as well as participate in health research and promote the dissemination of evidence; they also possess computer science knowledge useful for managing service information systems and self-education; they possess didactic/pedagogical skills to conduct educational planning and teach in any type of university course or professional update program. They know an EU language, in addition to Italian, at a level enabling comprehension of international literature and updates. Learning objectives will be achieved through ex-cathedra, seminar, interactive teaching tools, and clinical internship at Faculty and cooperating Healthcare Organizations. Learning assessment will be conducted through in-course tests, suitability evaluations, and final exams.
Management Area The Master's graduate knows the fundamental theoretical and applied principles of management processes in their professional fields, as well as general bioethical, deontological, legal, and medical-legal principles. Specifically, they possess managerial knowledge to lead nursing and midwifery services in simple and complex healthcare structures; they possess advanced professional knowledge to intervene in healthcare processes of nursing and midwifery disciplines; they possess epidemiological and statistical knowledge to analyze community health needs and socio-cultural factors influencing them, as well as the evolution and changes in healthcare systems. Learning objectives will be achieved through ex-cathedra, seminar, interactive teaching tools, and clinical internship at cooperating Healthcare Organizations. Learning assessment will be conducted through in-course tests, suitability evaluations, and final exams.
Research Area The Master's graduate knows the fundamental theoretical and applied principles of research processes in their professional fields. Specifically, they possess epidemiological and statistical knowledge to analyze community health needs and socio-cultural factors influencing them, as well as the evolution and changes in healthcare systems; they possess computer science and research methodology knowledge to design and conduct clinical-assistive, organizational, and educational studies, as well as participate in health research and promote the dissemination of evidence; they also possess computer science knowledge useful for managing service information systems and self-education. They know an EU language, in addition to Italian, at a level enabling comprehension of international literature and updates. Learning objectives will be achieved through ex-cathedra, seminar, interactive teaching tools, and clinical internship at Faculty and cooperating Healthcare Organizations. Learning assessment will be conducted through in-course tests, suitability evaluations, and final exams.
Teaching Area The Master's graduate knows the fundamental theoretical and applied principles of training processes in their professional fields, possesses didactic/pedagogical skills to conduct educational planning and teach in any type of university course or professional update program. Learning objectives will be achieved through ex-cathedra, seminar, interactive teaching tools, and clinical internship at Departmental and cooperating Healthcare Organizations. Learning assessment will be conducted through in-course tests, suitability evaluations, and final exams.

Judgment Autonomy.
The Master's graduate possesses critical analysis skills enabling autonomous action in relevant professional contexts, in various management, training, and research situations. Specifically:
-is able to identify problematic elements in the organizational setting of nursing and midwifery services in healthcare facilities, simple and complex, to select and implement appropriate quality improvement processes;
-is able to evaluate human and community behaviors in healthcare work contexts, also in relation to users, with particular reference to attitudes towards change and professional and organizational development;
-is able to identify the training needs of individuals and communities to design and deliver suitable training programs, also evaluating their outcomes;
-is able to conduct bibliographic research on major biomedical databases and critically read scientific articles to select the best available evidence and identify research problems.
Learning objectives will be achieved through seminar and interactive teaching tools, as well as clinical internship at the facilities of the Departments and Convened Healthcare Companies. Assessment of learning will be conducted through ongoing assessments, suitability evaluations, and final exams.

Communication skills.
The Master's graduate is able to establish and maintain professional relationships aimed at informing, persuading, and motivating healthcare staff under their coordination or supervision, applying the fundamentals of relational dynamics to promote empowerment and organizational well-being; applies necessary communication strategies for team work with various professionals operating in the socio-health sector; designs and implements institutional health communication interventions for individuals and groups using autonomous, appropriate tools, including information technology, for information dissemination.
Learning objectives will be achieved through seminar, interactive teaching tools, and clinical internship at the facilities of the Departments and Convened Healthcare Companies. Learning assessment will be conducted through in-course tests, suitability evaluations, and final exams.
Planned occupational and professional opportunities for graduates.
Master's degree holders in Nursing and Midwifery Hospitals, Local Healthcare Companies, IRCS, Private and Non-Profit Organizations, Residential Care Facilities (RSA), Service Cooperatives for home care, etc., in dependent or freelance roles.
Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIAN Associated competencies for the role.
Master's degree holders in Nursing and Midwifery Advanced managerial skills to hold senior roles in management-organizational, educational, research, and advanced clinical fields, as well as cross-cutting communication-relational skills to address health needs of individuals and communities, elevate operational standards, and contribute to innovation and progress in nursing and midwifery professions.
Description of admission tests.
Access to the Master's degree course is nationally regulated. The number of eligible students, within limits defined by the class, is decided annually in accordance with laws 264/1999 and 1/2002 by the Minister of University and Scientific and Technological Research, after consulting other relevant Ministers, based on the potential offer of the university system, also considering the need for professional skills in the social and productive system. The entrance test focuses on knowledge required for access: theory and practice relevant to the exercise of nursing and midwifery professions; general culture and logical reasoning; regulation of specific professional practice and health legislation; scientific-mathematical culture, statistics, computer science, and English; human and social sciences.
Role in work context.
Master's degree holders in Nursing and Midwifery The study program provides the legal requirement to compete for senior/directorial roles in services related to healthcare professions.
- Organization and management of hospital nursing services (high and medium intensity wards and health management);
- Organization and management of district/home-based nursing, midwifery, and neonatal services;
- Organization and management of outpatient nursing services;
- Organization and management of delivery areas, midwifery-neonatal services, and territory-based midwifery services;
- Organization and management of nursing services in low-intensity care, rehabilitative, and socio-health facilities;
- Organization and management of nursing services in residential facilities;
- Organization and coordination of multidisciplinary and multi-professional work groups in health and socio-health contexts;
- Participation in health research, promoting its culture and dissemination of evidence-based practices;
- Organization and implementation of teaching activities in all university study programs and professional update courses activated by health or professional organizations.
Additional information.
http://www.unisi.it/dipartimenti/dipartimento-medicina-molecolare-e-dello-sviluppo Specific educational objectives description.
The educational objectives of the Study Program aim to provide advanced cultural and professional training to intervene with high-level competencies in assistance, management, training, and research processes within areas relevant to nursing, pediatric nursing, and midwifery professions.
In particular, at the end of the study program, Master's graduates in the class will be able to:
1. Analyze, through epidemiological methods, the health needs of the community and the factors influencing them, as well as the evolution of health systems;
2. Intervene in assistance processes with advanced competencies, respecting ethical-deontological values, pursuing innovation in nursing and midwifery disciplines;
3. Coordinate and direct nursing and midwifery services in healthcare facilities, simple and complex, where they program, organize, manage, and evaluate resources and clinical assistance activities, as well as design, apply, and evaluate quality improvement models for assistance;
4. Conduct clinical-assistive, organizational, and educational research, as well as participate in health research and promote the dissemination of evidence-based practices;
5. Carry out educational design activities and conduct teaching in all types of university study programs, as well as professional update courses activated by health or professional organizations.
Based on the described educational objectives, the training path is structured over 2 years.
The achievement of educational objectives is realized through theoretical and theoretical/practical learning (laboratories). Training activities include legal and economic disciplines and disciplines in management, organizational, and quality development fields, supported by a clinical risk management laboratory and integrated with core disciplines (Nursing and Midwifery Management) and in-depth studies of core disciplines oriented towards managing clinical and assistance pathways.
A significant space is reserved for statistical-computer preparation of students through basic modules in statistics and applied computer science, which, through laboratory activities in research techniques and computer science, as well as the basics of scientific research, provide theoretical/practical means for adequate and autonomous technical-scientific updating, and for the design and implementation of clinical and organizational models based on research results, as well as for the design and implementation of research protocols in relevant fields. Special attention is given to human resource management and adult training in the workplace, as well as ethics and bioethics. The internship, which is a fundamental part of the Master's degree course, receives particular attention regarding site selection and timing relative to the advancement of the study program.
Each discipline corresponds to at least one module, delivered through frontal lessons, classroom exercises, or laboratory sessions, covering relevant topics, collected into courses, to facilitate the acquisition of essential knowledge for the profession and support internships in corresponding sectors.
Learning outcomes are assessed through in-course tests and a final oral or written exam, providing an opportunity to verify the achievement of proposed objectives.

Official in Public and Private Administrations Master's graduates acquire transversal skills: they can perform professional activities in companies and businesses, particularly in the areas of administration, management control, and corporate finance, as well as throughout the public administration sector, from administrative departments of state bodies, to state administrations, to territorial public bodies with particular reference to the tax agency, as well as within associations, institutions, and private foundations with public purpose.
Career opportunities and professional activities expected from the Master's program are therefore to be found in national and international institutions, in private companies operating also in the international market, in public and private organizations with high responsibility functions. Graduates may also perform professional activities in the governance structures of national, European, and international bodies, developing and implementing public intervention policies, also aimed at territorial management and within the tourism sector.
In this last sector, the Master's graduate has among the professional opportunities the possibility of becoming a "tourist consultant", an emerging professional figure that falls within the broader sphere of corporate consultants.
Professional opportunities are also expected in the field of publishing companies, newspapers, public and private press offices, press agencies, and in any other sector of information and communication.
Professional opportunities are completed by activities at research institutes, public and private schools, associative, recreational, cultural, and sports organizations.
Final exam characteristics The final exam consists of writing and discussing a written thesis – paper-based – within one of the courses included in the candidate's individual study plan, on a topic agreed with the course instructor (Supervisor). A Co-Supervisor is required.
The thesis consists of a monographic work, the result of research on documentary and doctrinal sources related to the topic, accompanied by clear bibliographic indications and/or the results of experimental investigations.
This work aims to verify the ability to analyze and synthesize knowledge collected and selected in view of developing a personal perspective on that topic, carried out with scientifically correct methodology.
The student, after obtaining a favorable opinion from the Supervisor, may write the thesis in a foreign language.
The final exam is awarded 18 CFU.
The final grade is expressed in hundredths with possible honors.

Role in work context.
Official in Public and Private Administrations Master's graduates can perform functions in various work contexts, corresponding to the different curricula in which the study course is structured:
functions within public administration: general public administration activities; public administration activities aimed at regulating social activities; public administration activities aimed at regulating economic activities, with particular reference to the tax sector; centralized support services for the institutional activities of public administrations; Foreign Affairs; National Defense; Mandatory Social Insurance;
functions within tourism and territorial marketing; education; activities of associative organizations; recreational, cultural, and sports activities; press agencies; organizations and bodies outside the territory.
functions of financial intermediation and other types of monetary intermediation; credit activities; insurance activities; auxiliary insurance and pension funds activities and supervision over insurance and pension funds;
functions of research and experimental development in the field of social and human sciences; services to companies; management and administration of personnel on behalf of third parties; market research and opinion polls; administrative-organizational consultancy,; company management; advertising and research, selection, and provision of personnel.
Specific educational objectives description.
The educational objectives of the Master's degree consist in providing in-depth knowledge in legal, political-social, institutional, economic, management, historical, communication, and information disciplines. The specificity compared to other Master's programs in the same class lies in the multidisciplinary nature that allows intertwining diverse and complementary knowledge and competencies for the effective management of public administration and private companies, for evaluating the policies of public and private bodies, for managing communication flows in the public, private, and large cultural, sports, and associative organizations. The course aims to prepare for high responsibility functions in companies, institutions, and organizations and associations at national and international levels.
The training path is structured on a common base of CFU distributed in the characteristic scientific-disciplinary sectors (statistical-quantitative, economic-organizational, legal, decision-making and organizational processes), to which are added the CFU acquired in related or integrative scientific-disciplinary sectors, for elective training activities, for internship and traineeship activities, and for other knowledge useful for entering the job market, as well as, finally, for the final exam. Master's graduates must also consolidate their linguistic training through the acquisition of English language proficiency at B2 level (Common European Framework). However, it is considered advisable to deepen English language knowledge and mastery in order to form more competitive professional figures both at national and especially international levels.
These structures allow the formation of modern state bureaucracy and public bodies leadership at national, European, and international levels, as well as the creation of professional figures able to confront normative, organizational, and technological innovations, to design initiatives for improving services.
The various courses in which the course is structured are mainly related to five disciplinary areas:
1) Statistical-Quantitative, referring to knowledge and consequent mastery of the main statistical concepts used in management disciplines.
2) Economic, referring to the acquisition of those tools of economic theory relevant to the problems of international and European economy; tools are also provided for analyzing the financial behavior of economic subjects, the functioning of markets and financial intermediaries, the effects of money and finance on the real economy; the topics of public action are also deepened, also in territorial context, and those relevant to the organizational characteristics of companies.
3) Legal, referring to the deepening of the foundations and legal institutions of administrative law, also in matters of territorial governance and tourism, civil and commercial law, as well as material law of the EU and international environmental law; acquisition of knowledge of regional public law, national tax legislation, and how it results from community sources, dynamics of European social law, and the penal law in general; finally, learning of the normative and jurisprudential aspects of information law, as an autonomous disciplinary area and with reference to communication processes in the political sector.
4) Political Science, referring to the acquisition of analytical tools necessary for understanding political and social systems, public policy dynamics, research methodology in political science, and tools, also historical, useful for understanding political language.
5) Historical, referring to knowledge of historical events that contributed to the construction of the nation-state and the related identities, learning of the history of main institutional bodies present on the territory, history of information and Italian journalism between the 19th and 20th centuries, in a national and international perspective, and for the same period, also the history of communication networks analyzed in relation to modernization and social change.

Roles Student Mobility Responsibilities LEONARDO DISPERATI President/Chair of Teaching Committee ENRICO TAVARNELLI Program, Texts and Objectives Professional title conferred. Geologist
In line with factors related to the labor market trends and economic and environmental development policies, it is expected that graduates in Resources and Geological Hazards of the Territory, thanks to their broad multidisciplinary knowledge base and specific methodological and applied skills, can flexibly shape their career opportunities across a wide range of professional directions.
Professional opportunities are found in the following sectors:
• industry (hydrocarbons, minerals, and raw materials);
• environment and green development (sustainable development management, parks, urban areas, environmental protection, etc.);
• consulting (private agencies, freelance, engineering companies);
• public offices (Geological Services, Regional and National Environmental Protection Agencies, etc.);
• private companies (management of water plants, landfills, material reuse, infrastructure);
• dissemination and scientific journalism.
More specifically, professional fields will focus on the following areas:
• geological and thematic mapping;
• preparation of urban planning, territorial, environmental, and georesource plans, using geological tools, with appropriate safeguard measures;
• analysis, prevention, and mitigation of geological, hydrogeological, and environmental risks;
• analysis, recovery, and management of degraded sites and abandoned extraction sites;
• management of Territorial Information Systems, with particular reference to geological-environmental issues;
• studies for environmental impact assessment (VIA) and strategic environmental assessment (VAS);
• geognostic and geophysical investigations for subsurface exploration and geological studies applied to civil engineering works, defining the appropriate geological-technical model and environmental hazard;
• modeling of geological processes (slope stability, water circulation, underground excavations, 2D and 3D reconstructions, etc.);
• aquifer characterization and modeling of subsurface flow and contaminant propagation problems;
• retrieval, economic evaluation, and management of georesources, including water resources and industrial and commercial geomaterials;
• management of extraction activities;
• analysis and management of geological, hydrogeological, and geochemical aspects of pollution phenomena and resulting risks;
• definition of preventive and risk mitigation measures, also aimed at drafting safety plans for workplaces;
• coordination of safety in temporary and mobile construction sites;
• evaluation and prevention of geological aspects of environmental cultural heritage degradation, and activities related to study, design, work management, and inspection for conservation;
• certification of geological materials and analysis of both physical-mechanical and mineralogical-petrographic characteristics;
• analysis of degradation of stone monuments and their conservation;
• management of geotechnical laboratories;
• environmental protection of the territory and sustainable development;
• protection and valorization of cultural heritage;
• characterization and studies for mitigating global climate changes.
Professional opportunities are related to the Economic Activities Classification Ateco 2007:
B: extraction of minerals from quarries and mines C: manufacturing activities D: supply of electricity, gas, steam, and air conditioning E: supply of water; sewerage networks, waste management, and remediation F: construction J: information and communication services K: financial and insurance activities L: real estate activities M: professional, scientific, and technical activities O: public administration and defense; mandatory social security P: education S: other service activities Regarding access to professions (DPR 328/01), the Master's Degree in Geological Sciences and Technologies (LM-74) allows, after passing the State Exam, registration in Section A (Geologists) of the Geologists' Register.
Final Exam Characteristics The final exam consists of preparing a document with original data and content; the preparation of the document takes at least six months, and the results are discussed in a public session before a committee that, through the appointment of a counter-reviewer, verifies the consistency of the candidate's objectives, methods, and results. The Master's thesis is generally characterized by original scientific and/or applied content in the fields of geological sciences and/or applications, although it is common for works to respect originality and experimental criteria while focusing on specialized content in the basic disciplines of geological sciences (stratigraphy, sedimentology, structural geology). The final grade will be expressed on a scale of 110, with possible honors. The merit score will primarily consider the quality of the work performed.
Required Knowledge for Admission For admission to the Master's Degree Course in Resources and Geological Hazards of the Territory, it is necessary to hold a three-year university degree or equivalent foreign degree recognized as suitable. Admission to the Master's Degree Course is permitted for graduates in Classes L-32 (Sciences and Technologies for Environment and Nature) and L-34 (Geological Sciences). Admission is also permitted for graduates in other Classes, provided they possess adequate foundational knowledge in mathematical, physical, chemical, and Earth Sciences disciplines, and have earned at least:
- 24 ECTS in SSD from GEO/01 to GEO/12
- 6 ECTS in SSD from MAT/01 to MAT/09
- 6 ECTS in SSD from FIS/01 to FIS/08
- 6 ECTS in SSD from CHIM/01 to CHIM/12.
Additionally, it is required to hold an English language certificate at the B1 level of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages.
The student's initial preparation is verified through an interview with a committee of professors specifically appointed. Only those who meet the curricular requirements may attend the interview. The verification methods or indications for direct admission without an interview are detailed in the course's teaching regulations.
Knowledge and Understanding.
Learning Area: Geological The Master's graduate in Resources and Geological Hazards of the Territory will acquire knowledge and understanding related to:
methods for studying sedimentary geological bodies and the deformed evolution of complex structures;
geological models of hydrocarbon deposits and geothermal systems;
advanced integrated stratigraphic analysis tools for studying depositional environment sequences and archaeological contexts.
Learning Area: Geomorphological and Applied Geological The Master's graduate in Resources and Geological Hazards of the Territory will acquire knowledge and understanding related to:
physical and mechanical characteristics of soils;
research and capture of groundwater;
hydrogeological tests;
geological contributions at various levels of territorial planning;
geographic and geo-thematic databases and modern cartographic representation techniques;
techniques for identifying geomorphological hazards;
methods for assessing slope stability;
techniques for identifying and protecting groundwater resources;
remote sensing and close-range sensing techniques;
geognostic surveys of hydrocarbon deposits.
Learning Area: Mineralogical, Petrographic, and Geochemical The Master's graduate in Resources and Geological Hazards of the Territory will acquire knowledge and understanding related to:
chemical processes in mineral and rock alteration in surface environments;
soil, atmospheric deposition, and surface and groundwater geochemistry;
petrographic characterization of geomaterials;
characteristics of mineral resources;
archaeometric investigation techniques;
alteration and degradation processes of stone monument materials.
Learning Area: Geophysical The Master's graduate in Resources and Geological Hazards of the Territory will acquire knowledge and understanding related to:
surface geophysical survey techniques;
methods for defining seismic hazard maps and expected damage at local scale;
physical models of geothermal systems.
Learning Area: Geological, Environmental, and Sustainable Development The Master's graduate in Resources and Geological Hazards of the Territory will acquire knowledge and understanding regarding the relationship between the use of planetary/territorial resources and environmental conservation within both substantive and administrative frameworks, also evaluating the sustainability of actions using quantitative systems in the context of geological resource utilization.

Autonomy of Judgment.
Upon completion of their studies, the master's graduate in Geological Resources and Territorial Hazards will have acquired the ability to:
• Critically analyze data and information obtained through their own investigative activities, both experimental and compilation-based, in accordance with the most up-to-date standards, disciplines, analysis methodologies, and best practices applicable in the professional context in which they operate.
• Draft technical reports based on the data and knowledge at their disposal, in which opinions, judgments, and parameters related to the analyzed geological issues are explicitly stated, clearly indicating any potential criticalities of the information provided to third parties in cases of high complexity and uncertainty due to fragmented or incomplete foundational knowledge or specific operational difficulties.
• Define general approaches and specific analysis methods aimed at resolving proposed questions, while evaluating scenarios connected to their observations and, if deemed necessary, proposing mitigation actions for potential criticalities linked to uncertainties that sometimes characterize geological and environmental phenomena.
• Critically analyze, through their scientific and technical expertise, the ecological, environmental, and socioeconomic consequences and implications of natural resource utilization activities, in light of the need to adopt sustainable methods and technologies.
• Evaluate the quality and efficiency of results produced by their own professional activities and those of others, especially when working within an interdisciplinary team.
The educational path, through the initial delivery of common and related courses, allows the student to follow a cultural growth process that enables them to progressively develop sensitivity and autonomy of judgment regarding the methods to be employed in different operational scenarios and based on the questions posed. In this sense, the completion of the educational path occurs during study and experimental research activities related to the preparation of the final thesis, supplemented by experiences gained during the required curricular internships and the soft skills acquired through extracurricular activities (seminars, supplementary courses, excursions, workshops, conferences, etc.). Throughout the educational path, particularly during the final thesis and internship phases, the student is guided on the analytical challenges often characterizing geological issues they must address, and is encouraged to improve their soft skills through participation in seminars and discussions with professionals and academic representatives from the working world and the academic community, not necessarily belonging to the fields typically included in the educational path. The acquisition of these competencies occurs through frontal lectures, laboratories (on-site and open-air), and internships. The assessment of preparation is carried out through the evaluation methods of the courses followed by the student, within the disciplinary sectors characterizing and related, aimed at verifying the acquisition of specific knowledge and critical abilities. The collegial assessment of the final thesis relates not only to the merit of the topics addressed but also to the student's organizational autonomy (e.g., for the purpose of off-site data collection for the final thesis or internship) and their ability to work in a team.

Learning Ability.
The master's educational path in Geological Resources and Territorial Hazards involves a progressive maturation of the student's analytical abilities and identification of work methods related to the themes they address. In this sense, upon completion of the study path, the graduate will have acquired the ability to:
• Identify a work path and determine the most appropriate investigation tools and technologies.
• Acquire a self-assessment method and personal motivation to deepen and continuously update their cultural and technical background, especially regarding specializations that align with their inclinations.
• Adapt to the changing needs of new work contexts, managing personal resources to address new scenarios even under stress and critical conditions, including workplace safety considerations (e.g., open-air and underground construction site scenarios).
The learning ability and critical sensitivity, including self-assessment capability, is stimulated throughout the educational path through both individual study and group activities. Off-site activities (open-air laboratories), primarily conducted for internships and final thesis preparation, which require students to develop organizational skills, represent a key element of the educational path. Another educational vehicle is provided by scientific bibliographic deepening, achieved using advanced international publications made available by the university library systems in both print and electronic formats. Learning ability is thus acquired through frontal lectures, laboratories, and seminars (especially group-based), as well as thesis preparation work. This ability is verified continuously throughout the educational path via exams and discussions, assessing the ability to present autonomously collected data and the capacity for self-learning developed during the final thesis.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Learning Area: Geological
The master's graduate in Geological Resources and Territorial Hazards will be able to:
• Apply stratigraphic and sedimentological methods for the geometric reconstruction of the subsurface;
• Analyze complex structures for the reconstruction of deformational evolution;
• Characterize hydrocarbon deposits and geothermal systems;
• Apply physical, sequence, and seismic stratigraphy for the interpretation and reconstruction of depositional environment sequences and archaeological areas.

Learning Area: Geomorphological and Applied Geological
The master's graduate in Geological Resources and Territorial Hazards will be able to:
• Perform geotechnical characterization of soils;
• Plan the research and exploitation of groundwater;
• Carry out hydrodynamic and hydrodispersive characterization of geological media;
• Apply geological knowledge to territorial planning;
• Apply remote sensing and close-range sensing techniques;
• Perform geomorphological applications to seismic micro-zonation and fluvial and coastal environments;
• Analyze slope stability;
• Analyze aquifer vulnerability and delineate safeguard areas for extraction works;
• Plan investigations for hydrocarbon exploration.

Learning Area: Mineralogical, Petrographic, and Geochemical
The master's graduate in Geological Resources and Territorial Hazards will be able to:
• Define the chemical characteristics of soils, atmospheric deposits, and surface and groundwater;
• Assess surface environmental contamination;
• Define the petrographic characteristics of geomaterials;
• Characterize mineral resources and assess risks associated with their use;
• Characterize archaeological finds composed of geological-derived materials;
• Characterize natural and artificial lithic materials used in historical architecture and sculpture.

Learning Area: Geophysics
The master's graduate in Geological Resources and Territorial Hazards will be able to:
• Apply surface geophysical exploration techniques;
• Characterize shaking and its effects on structures;
• Perform seismic risk assessments;
• Interpret geothermal processes.

Learning Area: Geology, Environment, and Sustainability
The master's graduate in Geological Resources and Territorial Hazards will be able to evaluate, from both qualitative and quantitative perspectives, the effects of geological resource use on the environment as a whole and on the landscape. They will acquire competence in evaluating the sustainability levels of typical geological activities, particularly those concerning resource use.

Communication Skills.
At the end of the training path and based on the topics covered in the disciplines addressed in classroom, laboratory, and off-site activities (e.g., open-air laboratories) and other described training activities, the Master's graduate in Geological Resources and Territorial Hazards will have acquired the ability to:
• Draft a report on study activities specifying objectives, methods, data, results, discussion, conclusions, and present the obtained results with linguistic precision to both specialist and non-specialist audiences, and optionally in English.
• Transmit knowledge to different stakeholders by describing the study methods used, achieved results, and expected requirements, especially within interdisciplinary team activities characterized by scientific skill heterogeneity, task diversity, and varying preparation levels.
• Respect the roles and responsibilities of team members (including consulting organizational charts and service orders), value the skills, perspectives, and data from other team members and the professional community to which they belong.
• Evaluate the different needs and interests of stakeholders, especially when they come from different professional backgrounds, such as public administration employees, technicians, and administrators, various types of qualified and non-qualified technicians, pursuing a collaborative spirit while maintaining clarity and punctuality.
These skills are acquired throughout the training process using all communication tools of the scientific and technical field, namely report compilation, short papers, thematic slide presentations, websites, social media activities, distance learning platforms (GoogleMeet, Microsoft Teams, Webex, etc.), and are verified through pass/fail exams and the final assessment. The ability to work both independently and in a group constitutes a teaching objective and consequently a criterion for evaluating the achieved preparation.

Description of specific educational objectives.
The Master's Degree Course in Geological Resources and Territorial Hazards aims to expand the basic scientific training obtained through the three-year degree in chemical, physical, mathematical, computer science, and various Earth Sciences disciplines. The main objective is to provide the ability to analyze physical phenomena of the Earth system for interpreting geological processes and their spatiotemporal relationships on the territory. An additional objective of the Master's Degree Course is to provide in-depth technical and professional preparation in the field of sustainable resource management and mitigation of geological hazards (https://rischi.protezionecivile.gov.it), whose territorial impact is emphasized by climate change.

These objectives are achieved through lectures, laboratory exercises, and fieldwork (ground surveys), where students acquire:
• Programming and design capabilities for collecting geological surface and subsurface data through cartography and geological section processing techniques, as well as processing data acquired via remote and proximal sensing and spatial and geostatistical analysis using GIS and WEB GIS platforms.
• Ability to develop surface and subsurface geological models aimed at researching and retrieving water resources, minerals, stone, and energy resources;
• Collaboration capability in designing works for managing underground water resources and mineral and thermal waters.
• Advanced analysis capability of geological resources, referring to mineral deposits and industrial geomaterials through field and laboratory techniques for their innovative and sustainable use.
• Ability to plan and manage activities aimed at understanding and protecting architectural-monumental heritage and archaeological and natural sites using advanced technologies.
• Ability to develop geological models for mitigating seismic risk (seismic microzonation), slope instability, hydraulic risk, and for protecting and utilizing natural heritage.
• Programming and implementation capability of geological-technical investigations, planning of geophysical survey campaigns, realization of geological sections and 3D models using specialized software platforms.
• Technical scientific skills to operate in geotechnical, geochemical, physical, and geological site laboratories for assisting drilling, surveys, and excavations.
• Capability to design renaturalization interventions for beaches and slopes, defense, and reconstruction of hydrogeological equilibria.
• Collaboration capability for engineering design of slope consolidation works in unstable areas prone to landslides.
• Capability to design and implement spatial databases of cartographic data, analysis of digital terrain models, photogrammetric analysis, and surveys using topographic-cartographic instruments and equipped drones.
• Scientific, professional, and regulatory skills for territorial management related to environmental issues and analysis of geo-environmental risks.

The above-described educational objectives are achieved through the delivery of characteristic courses aimed at expanding scientific and methodological knowledge, which are mostly delivered in the first year of the Master's Degree Course.
In the second year, courses are delivered that complete the student's preparation, focusing on their areas of greatest interest, acquiring scientific and technical knowledge for preparing the thesis with an emphasized experimental character. These courses allow for deeper knowledge in slope instability, engineering geology, structural and stratigraphic geology, and applied geology for territorial planning.

In addition to geological disciplinary content, preparation is completed with courses related to ecology, anthropology, physical chemistry, environmental chemistry and cultural heritage, coastal environment protection and management, hydrocarbons, and subsurface fluids. To complete the cultural training path, cross-disciplinary courses are also provided in economic management engineering, information processing systems, international law, statistics for experimental and technological research, and economic policy. These courses provide graduates with adequate preparation to work in interdisciplinary teams where technical issues must be discussed with specialists from different backgrounds and training.

To finalize the study path for acquiring high preparation for the world of work and professions, the Master's Degree Course curriculum includes a significant acquisition of CFUs dedicated to curricular internships, which students can complete (after signing a convention between the University and the host entity) at public bodies managing the territory, research institutions, professional offices, companies, and even university laboratories, both in Italy and abroad. Through participation in the University's internationalization programs, the Master's Degree Course in Geological Resources and Territorial Hazards promotes international student mobility through study and internship periods abroad within Erasmus programs and other international mobility calls. Faculty members also organize study and research stays abroad through their professional and scientific relationships for thesis preparation and professional activities.

As highlighted by the high number of credits allocated to it, the final exam represents a crucial phase of deepening and verifying the preparation acquired by the student, both for its purely experimental nature and for the analytical and synthetic skills the candidate must demonstrate. In this sense, students are advised to select the topics to deepen within the final thesis by the end of the first year, reserving at least six months for the final documentation. It is possible to combine the experimental material processing of the final exam with the experience gained during the internship, with the aim of achieving a concrete professional experience or scientific deepening through the thesis. Language skills are reserved for the training and assessment activities defined by the University in collaboration with the University Language Center, and students are advised to address these educational aspects well in advance of the scheduled conclusion of their studies.

International representations Characteristics of final exam For the completion of the Master's Degree in Public and Cultural Diplomacy, a thesis must be written by the student in an original manner, under the guidance of a supervisor. Degree awarded.
Master's Degree in Public and Cultural Diplomacy Knowledge and Understanding.
General Aspects The Master's graduate possesses advanced knowledge within a multicultural context where fluent English is essential and knowledge of at least one second language and its associated cultures is required, present in the areas central to the program. Socio-Political Studies Area Master's graduates have advanced skills in the comparative analysis of political systems, with particular reference to extra-European areas; knowledge of theories and interpretations of the dynamics of international relations and models of intervention in a range of public policies, with particular reference to the area of development cooperation.
Historical-Legal Analysis of Contemporary International Dimension Master's graduates possess specialized knowledge regarding the political-institutional development and functioning of international organizations in various parts of the globe, with particular reference to human rights, constitutionalism in transition areas, the history of globalization, and international relations.
Cultural History and Heritage Area Master's graduates have in-depth knowledge of long-term transformation dynamics and cultural sedimentation in the areas of interest. They also possess specific skills in designing public policies from a supranational perspective in the field of cultural heritage.
Territorial Socio-Economic Models Studies Master's graduates possess specialized skills in the field of geographical and economic analysis and socio-cultural sustainability models of systems in developing countries and generally in extra-European areas.

Judgment Autonomy.
Master's graduates in Public and Cultural Diplomacy are able to analyze the dynamics of an intercultural system, a fundamental premise for becoming familiar in environments distant from one's socio-cultural origin, and to emerge professionally in contexts characterized by conflicts and tensions.
The main teaching tools that enable graduates to operate autonomously in professional fields requiring relationship and negotiation skills are training in an international classroom, research experiences on current issues, and project activities carried out at institutional and non-institutional organizations of international cooperation.
The primary verification tool regarding judgment autonomy consists of passing exams, whose evaluation is based not only on substantive preparation expressed in written and oral form but also on the adequacy of initiatives undertaken by students (drafting and management of projects, conducting interviews and discussion panels, ability to discuss others' work, etc.).
Learning Ability.
Master's graduates develop learning abilities through core knowledge in public diplomacy, a necessary key to achieving more specific competencies in typical international relations and cooperation professions. The specialized methodologies acquired in the course areas (cooperation, conflict resolution, international cultural policy design and management) consolidate advanced learning abilities in research, project design, and knowledge dissemination in these areas. Teaching tools such as specific curricular internships, the use of numerous Erasmus bilateral reports, and the COiL (Collaborative Online Learning) project for enhancing communication skills, as well as activities for entering the professional world, foster learning ability for the "transition" from the academic to the professional dimension.
Verification tools, participation in working groups, decision-making process simulations, and role-playing activities allow for a clear evaluation of learning abilities among students with diverse socio-cultural backgrounds.
In particular, the advanced learning abilities developed in public diplomacy activities are applied in institutional, diplomatic, supranational organizations (including the European Union), associative organizations, and NGOs. Activities related to cultural project design determine marked learning abilities in areas relevant to the work of foundations, museum networks, research institutions, training agencies, and companies engaged in tourism and cultural heritage protection.

Application of Knowledge and Understanding.
General Aspects The master's graduate possesses specialized linguistic skills, having applied throughout the program knowledge and practice of the English language, which is the course language. Such knowledge is assessed not only through evaluation in individual exams but also through writing scientific and technical texts, participating in seminars, workshops, and international internships. Additional linguistic skills are applied through attendance at language lectures, activities in a mandatory language and cultures course, and using the language in seminar contexts, monographic research, and the final thesis writing.
Socio-Political Studies Area Master's graduates are able to apply their substantive and methodological knowledge of the socio-political framework and public policies in the studied areas through discussion of models, application of qualitative and quantitative comparative research methodologies, presentations developed in monographic seminars, and participation in simulations and experiments, conducted individually and in groups.
Contemporary International Dimension: Historical-Legal Analysis Master's graduates are able to utilize their analytical skills regarding the historical and legal framework through participation in research and seminars, preparation of reports, commentaries, and presentations.
Cultural History and Heritage Area Master's graduates are able to apply their competencies in developing cultural enterprises and policies through preparing essays on comparative cultural evolution and elaborating practical projects for development, partnership, and transnational cultural policies in various fields (art history, paleography, archaeology, etc.).
Territorial Socio-Economic Models Studies Master's graduates are able to apply their knowledge to address issues related to development models and social and cultural sustainability in crisis areas, as well as mapping socio-political phenomena in various global regions. The tools to be used include preparation of monographic research on economic, anthropological, and geographical themes, ethnographic reconstruction, use of inferential models, practice of experiments, and use of information geography.

Communication Skills.
Master's graduates possess communication and organizational skills, acquired through interactive methods that form the basis of their training (term papers, posters, reviews, etc.) and scientific dissemination tools (websites, blogs, case studies), which master's graduates are required to use during their studies. The use of social media and digital platforms is considered fundamental for developing these skills.
The acquisition of communication skills is verified through the preparation of scientific and popular texts, reviews, reports, presentations, and graphic syntheses. In addition to the material produced in each course, all in English, and interactive work during internships, a tool for verifying communication skills is the final exam: an English dissertation resulting from original research that also highlights the chosen methodological techniques. The subject of the exam varies depending on the chosen discipline, ranging from core social sciences for public diplomacy to humanities disciplines inherent to the cultural diplomacy approach, but the common thread linking the works is the emphasis on dissemination ability, the originality of the explored issues, and the relevance of the achieved implications.

Specific training objectives description.
The Master's degree course in Public and Cultural Diplomacy aims to develop knowledge and professional skills in international cooperation, typical of the Master's degree class LM-81, deepening the field of new public and cultural diplomacy.
This is a rapidly expanding field, involving an increasing number of professionals, not only within political institutions and public administrations, but increasingly among global governance actors: non-governmental organizations, new media, interest groups, associative bodies, and the third sector.
In light of this context, the Master's degree course in Public and Cultural Diplomacy develops two specific dimensions: public and cultural diplomacy practices in international relations, and the international approach in designing policies and institutions aimed at preserving, enhancing, and promoting cultural assets.
The Master's degree in Public and Cultural Diplomacy aims to provide:
- In the first year, advanced knowledge in socio-political studies, with specific reference to extra-European comparative politics and international relations. In this regard, among the core disciplines of the course, teachings related to SSD SPS/04 (political science) are included to ensure the presentation of key themes and approaches for studying public and cultural diplomacy in extra-European political systems. Other teachings focus on socio-economic sustainability and human rights studies in diverse global areas, with courses offered in the SSD sectors IUS/13 (international law), M-GGR/01 (geography), L-ANT/08 (Christian and medieval archaeology), M-DEA/01 (demo-ethno-anthropological disciplines), SPS/03 (history of political institutions), and SECS-P/02 (economic policy). Additionally, to develop significantly diverse knowledge within the course, students may choose a teaching related to a language and cultures relevant to the areas where master's graduates will operate (L-OR/12 Arabic Language and Literature; L-OR/21 Languages and Literatures of China and Southeast Asia).
- In the second year, adequate and applied knowledge for interpreting the contemporary world through the lenses of historical, social, socio-linguistic, and legal disciplines, with specific reference to understanding interactions between the West and other global regions, the role of international organizations, and media. To this end, the course includes teachings in SSD M-STO/04 (contemporary history); humanities and classical disciplines that develop the competencies of cultural diplomacy operators in SSD M-STO/09 (Paleography), L-ANT/01 (Prehistory and Protohistory), L-ANT/09 (Ancient Topography), IUS/11 (ecclesiastical and canon law). Additionally, training activities specific to a profile tailored to public diplomacy figures include advanced courses in social sciences and communication fields: SPS/08 (sociology of cultural and communicative processes); SPS/06 (history of international relations), linguistics (L-FIL-LET/12).
All teachings emphasize the interdisciplinary and intercultural dimensions of the course. The execution of all activities in English promotes immediate intercultural comparison practice and eliminates linguistic barriers for master's graduates destined to operate in international contexts or closely interact with institutions and actors from diverse cultures.
The robust toolset in various fields of social, historical, legal, and humanities sciences is united by the common denominator of deepening institutional and cultural contexts characterizing evolving political and social realities: the Mediterranean and Middle East, but also China, East Asia, Africa, and Latin America. Methodological competencies converge on study objects and phenomena relevant to each student's preparation (globalization, multicultural contexts, international politics, human rights, crisis areas, cultural pluralism, use of soft power in dialogue between governments and other international governance actors).
The acquired competencies align with the goals (of governments and organizations) of sustainable socio-cultural development, through the dissemination of good administrative practices, conflict resolution practice, and reorganization of civil society in crisis areas.

Final exam characteristics The final exam consists of a discussion, before a designated Degree Committee, of an original thesis prepared under the guidance of a supervisor. It must verify that the Master's graduate has acquired advanced knowledge in methodological and applied statistics within the field of data science and has the ability to clearly present and argue in written and oral form. The thesis may be written and presented in Italian or English.
For each Master's thesis, a co-supervisor is appointed, proposed by the supervisor, and a counter-supervisor is appointed, proposed by the competent teaching body.
The merit score awarded for the final exam will take into account, in particular, the level of theoretical depth, the ability demonstrated by the candidate in using appropriate quantitative methodologies for the research objective, the effectiveness of the empirical analyses conducted, the originality of the arguments proposed, and the effectiveness of the discussion. The merit score awarded for the final exam contributes to the formation of the final Master's degree grade together with the average of the course exams, according to criteria defined by a specific Regulation. The Master's degree grade is expressed in hundredths. If the sum of the merit score awarded for the final exam and the average grade of the course exams exceeds 110/110, the Master's Degree Committee, unanimously on the proposal of the supervisor, may award the highest distinction.
Required knowledge for admission Students intending to enroll in the Master's program in Statistical Methods and Data Analytics must hold a three-year university degree or equivalent foreign degree recognized as suitable. They must possess adequate preparation in mathematical and statistical fields, in addition to the following curricular requirements.
For graduates from classes L-8, L-9, L-18, L-33, L-35 and L-41, the curricular requirements for admission are considered automatically satisfied provided they have acquired:
- at least 16 CFU in the SSD SECS-S/01- S/02-S/03-S/04-S/05-MAT/06-SECS-P/05;
- at least 3 CFU specific in computer skills.
Students from other degree classes may enroll provided they have acquired:
- SECS-S/01-S/02-S/03-S/04-S/05-S/06 (16 CFU)
- MAT/01-02-03-04-05-06-07-08-09 (8 CFU)
- SECS-P/01-02-03-04-05-06 (16 CFU)
- INF/01 and ING-INF/05 (8 CFU)
- SPS/03-04-07 (24 CFU)
- L-LIN/12 (3 CFU).
For admission to the Master's program in Statistical Methods and Data Analytics, the following are required:
- specific knowledge in mathematical and statistical fields.
- basic computer skills;
- knowledge of English at least at B1 level.
The verification of personal preparation is conducted orally. The subjects, composition of the examination committee, and evaluation criteria for the exam will be defined by the course's teaching regulation. Personal preparation is considered verified for graduates from classes L-8, L-9, L-18, L-33, L-35 and L-41 who obtained their degree with a grade above a minimum threshold defined by the course's teaching regulation.

Finally, the Master's graduate is able to understand the sector literature, both advanced texts and scientific articles published in specialized journals, even in English, and to reprocess the content for specific theoretical and applied objectives.
This knowledge and understanding will be acquired and verified primarily through the curricular courses and their respective exams in different fields.
