Autonomy of judgment.
The Master's graduate possesses an autonomous and critical judgment capacity, acquired and developed through the in-depth study of case studies and the processing of data sets presented during courses. The Master's graduate, based on data analysis, is able to formulate interpretative hypotheses regarding the phenomenon under study, derive strategic indications, and suggest solutions, using statistical information appropriately.
These competencies will be acquired through seminars and study groups dedicated to the analysis and interpretation of data from various sources: for such training activities, collaboration with particularly qualified experts from the business world and various research institutions is also provided. These competencies will be verified through passing exams; particular importance will also be given to their verification during the final project assessment.

Learning ability.
The commitment required during the training path to deepen the topics covered and to critically process the concepts and methodologies learned allows the Master's graduate to develop autonomous study, learning, and reflection abilities, enabling them to both excel in higher-level study courses and acquire the necessary technical-operational skills to successfully integrate into various professional contexts.
These abilities will be primarily acquired within the context of specialized courses, as well as in the training activities for preparing the final project, and will be verified through both passing exams and the final project.

Ability to apply knowledge and understanding.
Generic Area The Master's graduate in MSDA is capable of translating a knowledge need arising in economic-financial, social, and environmental applied contexts into statistical and data analytics terms, correctly formulating the problem, objectives, and selecting the most appropriate data science solutions. In particular, the Master's graduate is able to design and manage all phases of a sample survey: identifying an appropriate sampling design, implementing it, choosing the most suitable data collection method and tools, selecting and training personnel for data collection, collecting, organizing, and processing data using the most innovative data science and analytics techniques, and finally interpreting the results.
These competencies will be acquired and verified using theoretical and empirical articles as study material, as well as proposing in-class and exam exercises on current and concrete cases and problems. Particular importance will also be given to verifying these competencies during the final project assessment.

Mathematical-Statistical Programming and implementation of complex sampling.
Application of statistical tools to data analysis in environmental, economic, and social areas through the most recent and innovative data science and analytics techniques.

Economic Environmental data economic analysis.
Application of methods for environmental decision-making.

These skills will be acquired through the course's teachings, where particular attention will be given to acquiring specialized vocabulary; furthermore, through the language teaching, where special emphasis will be placed on written communication skills.

Statistical Workplace Function.

Designs and supervises sampling surveys for data collection, acquires and manages data from both traditional official sources and new sources (big data, open data), and applies appropriate methodologies for analyzing various data types, also using programming languages specific to data scientists. Interprets, contextualizes, and communicates the results of analyses effectively, interacting with experts in various application areas and decision-makers in both public and private sectors.
- By appropriately utilizing the flexibility provided in defining the training path, the graduate can perform further more specific functions.

Supports decision-making in public administration and, more generally, in public and private sector companies.
- The graduate who has focused on environmental topics is able to conduct empirical analyses for sustainability and assess the impact of environmental decisions related to public or private projects and programs.
Description of specific educational objectives.
The Master's Degree Course in Statistical Methods and Data Analytics, consistently with the educational objectives of the class, allows for the acquisition of solid knowledge of statistical methodology, its application aspects, and the tools for designing sampling surveys. The course also aims not only to provide graduates with a solid preparation in mathematics, probability, and statistics, but also, following the indications from stakeholder consultations, to provide knowledge of methodologies and mastery of the computer skills characteristic of the data scientist profile. The course thus enables graduates to successfully enter the job market as a reference figure in managing and interpreting information flows of diverse nature and origin.
The course's training path is characterized by:
- The presence, in the first year, of advanced-level mandatory courses in mathematical-probabilistic and statistical fields (MAT/06, SECS-S06, SECS-S01, and SECS-S/03), ensuring students a solid foundation in core disciplines;
- The presence, in the second year, of mandatory courses providing in-depth knowledge of sampling survey techniques in economic, social, and ecological-environmental contexts, as well as specific methodologies for integrating information from diverse sources (SECS-S/01 and SECS-S/05);
- The presence, in both the first and second years, of mandatory computer science courses aimed at acquiring the necessary competencies for managing various data types and implementing appropriate statistical analysis techniques (INF/01);
- The presence of a mandatory English language course ensuring the acquisition of the ability to fluently use the language in both oral and written forms, with particular attention to disciplinary vocabulary;
- The flexibility of the training path, allowing students to tailor their study plan according to their inclinations and interests, strengthening their formation in data science (ING-INF/05), socio-economic disciplines, or ecological-environmental disciplines (SECS-P/01 and SECS-P/02);
- A final exam consisting of a written thesis (dissertation) prepared under the guidance of a faculty member (supervisor) on a mutually agreed topic, aimed at verifying mastery of methodological and applied statistics knowledge and communication skills;
- The possibility of completing a training internship at various institutions and companies, both during the training path and during thesis work, offering students the opportunity to acquire advanced specific and transversal professional skills, facilitating their entry into the workforce.

- that it has the ability to apply acquired knowledge and solve problems on innovative topics, also within an interdisciplinary context;
- that it has the ability to clearly present and argue in written and oral form.
For each Master's thesis, a co-supervisor is appointed, proposed by the supervisor, and a counter-supervisor, proposed by the competent teaching body.
The merit score attributed to the final exam will take into account, in particular, the level of theoretical depth, the candidate's demonstrated ability to use appropriate quantitative methodologies for the research objective, the effectiveness of the empirical analyses conducted, the originality of the arguments proposed, and the effectiveness of the discussion.
The merit score attributed to the final exam contributes to the final degree grade together with the average of the course exams, according to the criteria defined in the relevant Regulation.
The final exam evaluation will be expressed on a scale of 110 with possible honors.
The thesis may be written and presented in Italian or English.
Required knowledge for admission To be admitted to the Master's Degree in MaGo, one must hold a three-year university degree, or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent, or a specialist or Master's degree, or a degree from the previous four-year curriculum.
Additionally, the ability to use main computer tools (text processing and spreadsheet use) and knowledge of English corresponding to at least the B1 level of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages are required.
Specifically, for admission to MaGo, certain curricular requirements and adequate personal preparation are required as specified below and verified.
Curricular requirements To be admitted to the Master's Degree in MaGo, one must hold a suitable degree in business or economic fields (First Level Degree classes under D.M. 270/2004: L-18 - Economics and Business Management Sciences, L-33 - Economic Sciences or similar classes under D.M. 509/1999).
Admission is also permitted with a suitable degree in a different class of degrees, provided it includes sufficient university credits in specific scientific-disciplinary sectors of the business, economic, mathematical-statistical, and legal areas (minimum 60 CFU, of which at least 24 CFU in the business area). Specifically:
• Business area: SECS-P/07 - Business Economics, SECS-P/08 - Economics and Management of Enterprises, SECS-P/09 - Corporate Finance, SECS-P/10 - Business Organization, SECS-P/11 - Economics of Financial Intermediaries;
• Economic area: SECS-P/01 - Political Economy, SECS-P/02 - Economic Policy, SECS-P/03 - Public Finance, SECS-P/04 - History of Economic Thought, SECS-P/05 - Econometrics, SECS-P/06 - Applied Economics, SECS-P/12 - Economic History;
• Mathematical-statistical area: SECS-S/01 - Statistics, SECS-S/03 - Economic Statistics, SECS-S/06 - Mathematical Methods for Economics and Actuarial and Financial Sciences, MAT/02 - Algebra, MAT/03 - Geometry, MAT/05 - Mathematical Analysis, MAT/06 - Probability and Mathematical Statistics, MAT/08 - Numerical Analysis, MAT/09 - Operations Research;
• Legal area: IUS/01 - Private Law, IUS/04 - Commercial Law, IUS/05 - Economics Law, IUS/07 - Labour Law, IUS/09 - Institutions of Public Law, IUS/10 - Administrative Law, IUS/12 - Tax Law, IUS/13 - International Law, IUS/14 - European Union Law.
Credits in the specific scientific-disciplinary sectors required as curricular requirements must be held before enrollment.
For graduates with foreign degrees, the required access knowledge is defined by the study course teaching regulation based on the minimum content deemed necessary for the different disciplinary areas, including linguistic ones.
Verification of personal preparation For admission to the study course, students holding the required curricular qualifications must pass a test to verify personal preparation, the modalities of which are defined by the study course teaching regulation.
Exemption from the admission test is granted to graduates holding the required curricular qualifications who obtained the degree with a grade above a minimum threshold defined by the study course teaching regulation, where the following are also specified:
• subjects, composition of the examining committee, and evaluation criteria for the test;
• specific modalities for evaluating the initial preparation of foreign university graduates, including necessary linguistic knowledge.

Autonomy of Judgment.
The autonomy of judgment demonstrated in the conduct of teaching activities constitutes one of the evaluation parameters for the student's overall academic performance. It is the responsibility of the course instructor to appropriately verify and evaluate - reflecting it in the final grade - the quality level expressed by the student.
Master's graduates who have successfully completed the course of study must be able to:
a) correctly interpret analyses to adopt the most suitable management approach;
b) find and effectively utilize professional contributions related to management issues;
c) possess abstract thinking to identify the essence of a problem and apply general principles to specific cases.
These competencies will be acquired and verified through seminars and study groups dedicated to the analysis and interpretation of empirical data relevant to business decisions; for such training activities, collaboration with particularly qualified experts from the economic-business context is also provided.
Particular importance will also be given to verifying these competencies during the final assessment.

Throughout the duration of the Course, students are encouraged to engage with diverse texts including books, scientific articles, manuals, databases, reports, and texts in foreign languages, etc.
It is expected that, by operating in this way, at the end of their educational path, students will be able to implement different learning strategies according to the context and available materials. In particular:
a) they will be able to tackle subsequent and advanced study programs (Master's, PhD, etc.);
b) they will be able to independently manage their professional life through continuous education, which the modern workplace requires.
These competencies are primarily acquired and verified within specialized courses, as well as in the training activities for preparing the final examination.

Communication Skills.
Active teaching methods in economic and managerial disciplines consistently involve frontal presentations and the preparation of reports. Students must possess adequate drafting skills for various business documents.

- teamwork, ability to work in a group;
- public speaking, ability to speak in public.
These skills will be acquired and assessed both through language courses specialized in technical vocabulary, with particular emphasis on written communication skills, and through the final exam.
Planned occupational and professional outcomes for graduates.
Economic and Business Expertise Graduates are capable of working in private and public enterprises, holding managerial and operational responsibility roles, as well as conducting consulting activities both in Italy and abroad. They are also able to manage their own business or implement its growth, carry out an international development path, and initiate new entrepreneurial ventures.
Chartered Accountant and Statutory Auditor The Master's Degree in Management and Governance provides access to the examination for the profession of Chartered Accountant under Legislative Decree 28 June 2005, No. 139, as well as the performance of statutory audit activities under Legislative Decree 27 January 2010, No. 39 (subject to obtaining the professional qualification according to current regulations).

In all these cases, the individual can perform decision-making, leadership, coordination, management, and data and information analysis functions.
Chartered Accountant and Statutory Auditor The Master's Degree in Management and Governance prepares graduates for the functions of Chartered Accountant and Statutory Auditor.
Additional information.
Course website Specific educational objectives description.
The Master's Degree in Management and Governance (MaGo), integrating and deepening the themes and knowledge already acquired in undergraduate studies, aims to provide advanced training for high-level activities in the field of corporate governance and management.
In this sense, the Course aims to transmit to students a broad and in-depth knowledge of themes related to economics and management. Students are trained in modern economic-management theories, concepts, techniques, and applications. Particular attention is paid to recent developments and major trends of change in the business operational context to transmit to students adequate competencies related to governance, management, organization, and reporting processes in various types of enterprises and organizations operating in different sectors (public and private), both large and medium-small, also considering the now fundamental principles of sustainability, not only economic but also environmental and social. Particular attention is also given to ongoing technological changes, with specific reference to digitalization processes that are modifying the operational dynamics of both private and public entities.
This interdisciplinary training enables them to qualify for access to the profession of Chartered Accountant under Legislative Decree 28 June 2005, No. 139, as well as the performance of statutory audit activities under Legislative Decree 27 January 2010, No. 39.
The Course also aims to foster the development of so-called soft skills (e.g., analysis and synthesis, critical thinking, problem solving, teamwork, leadership, negotiation, collaboration, communication, initiative, proactivity, organization, time and priority management, decision-making, stress tolerance, self-efficacy, autonomy, enterprising spirit, etc.), which are increasingly necessary, if not indispensable, for effective corporate governance. To this end, active teaching methodologies are prioritized - also (but not only) using advanced technological solutions for teaching - which are:
- Learner-centered
- Problem-based
- Experience-based
- Participative and cooperative The training path focuses on courses referring to different profiles of governance and control and business management, in the main disciplinary areas:
1) Business (SECS-P/07, -P/08, -P/09, -P/10, -P/11, -P/13): courses primarily focus on management, control, and performance evaluation themes of both public and private enterprises. These are supplemented by courses aimed at equipping students with knowledge and skills to understand economic phenomena and develop strategies at both business and corporate levels.
2) Economic (SECS-P/01, -P/02, -P/03, -P/06, -P/12): includes courses that deepen the characteristics and specifics of different capitalist systems worldwide, address relevant microeconomic dynamics for business management, and examine the economic implications of sustainable development and industrial organization.
3) Legal (IUS/04, 01, /05, /07, /12, /14): includes courses aimed at deepening legal themes related to: tax law, regulation of labor relations and collective bargaining, regulation of companies using the risk capital market, competition law applicable to businesses and states within the European Union, consumer law, and corporate social responsibility. Within the courses, particular attention is paid to analyzing regulatory systems from a comparative national/international perspective.
4) Statistical-mathematical (SECS-S/03): includes training aimed at preparing students to effectively interpret data bases and use statistical, probability, and sampling concepts in making business decisions.
Given the particular relevance of language training for effective corporate governance - since all companies today operate and compete at a global or at least European level - graduates must also consolidate their language knowledge. In English, in particular, students must acquire competencies at least at level B2 (Common European Framework).

Final Exam Characteristics For admission to the final exam, the student must have passed all exams and completed the training activities specified in the Study Plan.
The final exam consists of a written work of at least 50 pages (or a multimedia work of similar size), written under the guidance of a supervisor in one of the two foreign languages of study, or in Italian based on linguistic and/or cultural areas, also in a comparative key, on issues related to one of the studied disciplines, with the consultation of the supervising teacher. It is possible to collect and analyze empirical data, as well as to conduct an original and critical review and analysis of the current state of literature in a specific area. Alternatively, the student may choose to develop an independent project within one of the more applied disciplines included in their study plan, as well as the internship experience.
Students are required to demonstrate mastery of both foreign languages at an advanced level, as well as advanced disciplinary knowledge, possess current and updated bibliographic, computer, and critical tools, demonstrate independent judgment, original thinking, and the ability to mediate between different linguistic and cultural contexts.
The exam is defended before a specially appointed Commission, which will evaluate the exam on a scale of 110, with the possibility of awarding honors.
Required Knowledge for Admission To access the Master's program in "Languages for Business and Development," it is necessary to hold a three-year university degree or equivalent, or another foreign degree recognized as suitable, along with the required curricular qualifications.
The curricular admission requirements are met by holding a degree in one of the following classes under D.M. 270/04 (or corresponding classes under D.M. 509/99): L-11 and L-12 (under D.M. 270/04), classes 3 and 11 (under D.M. 509/99), or four-year degrees in Foreign Languages and Literatures.
Additionally, graduates from other classes (under the new D.M. 270/04, previous D.M. 509/99, old four-year degrees, or foreign universities) who have obtained their degree with a minimum grade specified in the study program's academic regulations and have earned at least 18 CFU in the first language and 18 CFU in the second language among the following offered in the program:
L-LIN/04 LANGUAGE AND TRANSLATION - FRENCH L-LIN/12 LANGUAGE AND TRANSLATION - ENGLISH L-LIN/21 SLAVIC STUDIES (RUSSIAN LANGUAGE AND TRANSLATION)
L-OR/21 LANGUAGES AND LITERATURES OF CHINA AND SOUTHEAST ASIA For each of the two chosen study languages, a minimum level of B1 (Common European Framework of Reference for Languages) is required for Russian and Chinese; a minimum level of B2 for English and French.
Students without a language certification must take the appropriate level test at the University Language Center in Arezzo.
Additionally, students must have earned:
- at least 21 CFU in literary, cultural, and historical study areas, with particular reference to the following SSDs: L-LIN/03, L-LIN/10, L-LIN/11, L-LIN/21, L-FIL-LET/10, L-FIL-LET/11, L-FIL-LET/14, L-OR/09, L-OR/21, M-STO/01, M-STO/02, M-STO/03, M-STO/04, M-STO/05, M-GGR/01, M-GGR/02;
- at least 18 CFU in linguistic, philological, and language teaching areas, with particular reference to the following SSDs: L-LIN/01, L-LIN/02, L-LIN/12, L-FIL-LET/09, L-FIL-LET/12, L-FIL-LET/15 (including at least 6 CFU in L-LIN/01 and 6 CFU in L-FIL-LET/12).
Candidates lacking these requirements may earn the missing CFU by enrolling in single courses at the University of Siena or other legally recognized universities and passing the relevant exams. The missing CFU for curricular requirements must be earned before the assessment of adequate preparation. The Academic Committee reserves the right to assess each case individually.
For foreign university graduates, the adequacy of curricular requirements is evaluated on a case-by-case basis, considering the coherence between the programs completed in different disciplinary areas, the foundational knowledge deemed necessary for the advanced training offered by the study program, and the linguistic knowledge. Foreign students must have adequate knowledge of Italian and English (at least level B1).
The assessment of personal preparation is mandatory and will be conducted through tests or interviews. Graduates in classes L-11 and L-12 who have obtained their degree with a final grade above a minimum threshold will be recognized as having adequate preparation.
Detailed information will be provided in the study program's academic regulations.
Knowledge and Understanding.
LINGUISTIC AND COMMUNICATION AREA The Master's graduate in LIMS
- will have acquired high-level written and oral interaction skills in at least two foreign languages in addition to Italian (at least level C1 for English and French; level C1 for Russian and Chinese);
- will have in-depth knowledge of the theoretical foundations and mechanisms of interlinguistic and intercultural interaction;
- will possess excellent mastery of theoretical and practical tools for decoding, producing, and translating specialized texts of various types within the context of intercultural, business, or international administrative communication.
These competencies are achieved through i) advanced lectures with updated and innovative bibliographic and didactic materials; ii) seminar courses; iii) translation exercises on documents of particular complexity from the perspective of specialized and sectoral language, intercultural mediation; iv) participation in conferences, seminars, and study days of high scientific value held by national and international experts; v) involvement in regional, national, and international research projects coordinated by faculty members; vi) preparation of original and methodologically rigorous oral and written reports. For foreign language lectures, classroom exercises with CEL staff are also provided.
The general structure of the study program also dedicates sufficient time to guided and independent individual study, enabling the development of the ability to interpret different sociolinguistic and cultural codes in communication contexts in life and work, with particular attention to multilingual and multicultural environments.
ECONOMIC-LEGAL AREA The Master's graduate:
- will have solid foundational knowledge in business economics and international law;
- will understand the contexts and mechanisms of international trade and the process of business internationalization;
- will be able to comprehend the theoretical foundations of argumentation;
- will know the fundamental legal institutions for professional and commercial activities;
- will understand the structures and dynamics of the global economy and a market in constant evolution.
These competencies are achieved through lectures, seminar courses, exercises, in-depth seminars, classroom discussions, case studies, presentation and discussion of quantitative and qualitative analyses, in-depth study of specialized languages, and meetings with experts on specific topics.
The general structure of the study program also dedicates sufficient time to guided and independent individual study, enabling the development of the ability to interpret different sociolinguistic and cultural codes in economic and legal relations between different countries, with particular attention to multilingual and multicultural contexts.
APPLIED AREA Based on the options indicated in the elective courses and the chosen career orientation workshops, the graduate
- will have solid foundational knowledge regarding social, economic, and environmental sustainability;
- will have solid foundational knowledge in European project design;
- will possess transversal skills (soft skills);
- will have statistical and data analysis competencies;
- will have solid competencies to navigate different theoretical and methodological approaches to specialized translation.
These competencies are achieved through workshops, lectures, seminar courses, exercises, in-depth seminars, classroom discussions, case studies, specific training in quantitative and qualitative analysis, in-depth study of specialized and sectoral languages, and meetings with experts on topics consistent with the study program.

Autonomy of Judgment.
The multidisciplinary approach of the Master's program (CdLM) (at the intersection of linguistic, economic, and legal disciplines) enables the student to integrate acquired knowledge and developed skills, formulate and express critical and original reflections, and express judgments related to their field of study, even in new or unfamiliar environments and within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts. If the reference frameworks of such contexts are based on incomplete and/or limited information, as is often the case in multilingual and multicultural settings, the graduate in "Languages for Business and Development" is aware of the social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments. The seminar-based nature of advanced language teaching, sociolinguistics and intercultural pragmatics, and cultural studies, as well as some economic disciplines, aims to strengthen this ability.

The graduate in "Languages for Business and Development" knows how to manage multilingual and multicultural complexity, aware that advanced foreign language learning is also associated with in-depth knowledge of the socio-cultural and pragmatic frameworks in which these languages are embedded. In particular, they will have acquired the ability to:
- collect and interpret linguistic-cultural data useful for forming autonomous judgments within the context of multilingual communication and intercultural dialogue;
- evaluate information sources with a keen critical sense;
- observe and analyze cultural dynamics and phenomena of globalization and 'glocalization';
- detect and manage pragmatic-linguistic ambiguities, using tools of participation and consensus-building.

They will also have acquired the awareness that theoretical knowledge is constitutive of their professionalism and their ability to intervene in specific contexts of multilingual communication, dialogue, and intercultural cooperation, even in conflict situations.

Autonomy of Judgment is achieved by applying the theoretical, methodological, and analytical foundations of the LINGUISTIC AND COMMUNICATION AREA, the ECONOMIC AREA, and the LEGAL AREA integrated within the APPLIED COMPETENCIES AREA (within the fields of data design and analysis, and digital communication through various media):
- by carrying out individual and group work, which involves researching, systematizing, and evaluating data within the proposed training activities;
- by delivering individual and group public presentations aimed at presenting and arguing their work;
- by interacting with professors and peers in various teaching contexts.

The possession of Autonomy of Judgment is verified through:
- final and ongoing written and/or oral exams;
- production and presentation of seminar papers, essays, and individual and group reports;
- laboratory assessment;
- evaluation of internship activities;
- final exam.

Learning Ability.
The attention to multilingualism and multiculturalism, as well as to intercultural themes in the study program requires the student to be able to engage with different environments, methods, and learning styles. This contributes to developing their ability to learn new content dynamically and flexibly, incorporating stimuli from the variety of contexts in which they carry out their study path.

The ability to learn is acquired through seminars, laboratories, and guided written assignments. At the end of the study path, the student will be able to apply the plurality of methods, tools, and techniques acquired to update and deepen the content of the studied disciplines, also in a perspective of self-managed lifelong education, through a path of responsibility and self-assessment.

The verification of learning abilities is carried out during exams, disciplinary seminars (through individual and/or group work), orientation laboratories, and the final exam.

The graduate in "Languages for Business and Development"
- knows the tools for scientific updating in disciplines related to their field of study, having learned the basic notions;
- is able to independently access scientific literature, in Italian and in the study languages;
- is able to use databases, analyze linguistic and economic-legal data, and prepare updated and reasoned bibliographies on specific topics;
- is aware of the richness of the interdisciplinary approach and its necessity in the analysis and management of complex systems;
- has learned to learn and applies this ability in cognitive, operational, and relational dimensions, mostly in an autonomous or self-directed manner.

These abilities are acquired both through participation in taught disciplines (LINGUISTIC AND COMMUNICATION AREA, ECONOMIC AND LEGAL AREA) and through applied activities (APPLIED COMPETENCIES AREA), aimed at integrating general and specific research areas in different disciplinary sectors, while simultaneously considering the need to constantly update methodological knowledge and pay attention to technological innovations.

The learning outcomes indicated are verified through:
- final and ongoing written and/or oral exams;
- preparation of reports and oral presentations in seminar contexts;
- production of individual and group essays and reports;
- laboratory assessment;
- evaluation of internship activities;
- final exam.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
LINGUISTIC AND COMMUNICATION AREA The graduate of the program:
- will be able to confidently use known languages in the context of businesses, organizations, and entities operating in an international setting, also in reference to the specialized terminology of the sector in which they operate;
- will possess excellent mastery of theoretical and practical tools for decoding and producing specialized texts of various types within the scope of cultural, business, or administrative international communication;
- will be able to translate independently various types of texts, including those written in specialized languages, from Italian to the two study languages and vice versa;
- will be able to critically and consciously analyze the dynamics of interaction between subjects from different linguistic and cultural areas, even in conflict situations.

The achievement of the above-mentioned abilities to apply knowledge and understanding occurs through critical reflection on texts, situations, and areas proposed both for classroom activities and for individual study, through critical reflection on linguistic, pragmatic, and socio-cultural competencies, through in-depth bibliographic and field research, and through the execution of individual and/or group research within the common and optional courses.

The methods for assessing the ability to apply knowledge and understanding are exams, written and oral, intermediate assessments, seminar reports, and the final exam. Intermediate assessments, written and oral exams, the preparation of reports, and the drafting of written assignments and oral presentations involve specific tasks in which the student demonstrates mastery of analytical tools, the ability to synthesize, and the use of various methodologies with critical and organizational autonomy.

The habit of active classroom participation, the ability to independently elaborate and communicate the results of work carried out, developed during the biennium training activities, assumes particular relevance at the time of preparing the final exam.

ECONOMIC-LEGAL AREA The graduate:
- will be able to independently select and interpret data and information in the legal and economic fields;
- will be able to cooperate in managing a commercial transaction between parties belonging to different legal systems;
- will be able to apply knowledge and competencies in legal and economic fields in a transversal manner during linguistic mediation activities in different business or institutional contexts.

The achievement of the above-mentioned abilities to apply knowledge and understanding occurs through critical reflection on texts and areas proposed both for classroom activities and for individual study, through critical reflection on economic and legal contexts of different countries, through in-depth bibliographic and field research, and through the execution of individual and/or group research within the common and optional courses.

The methods for assessing the ability to apply knowledge and understanding are exams, written and oral, intermediate assessments, seminar reports, and the final exam. Intermediate assessments, written and oral exams, the preparation of reports, and the drafting of written assignments and oral presentations involve specific tasks in which the student demonstrates mastery of analytical tools, the ability to synthesize, and the use of various methodologies with critical and organizational autonomy.

The habit of active participation, the ability to independently elaborate and communicate the results of work carried out, developed during the biennium training activities, assumes particular relevance at the time of preparing the final exam.

APPLIED AREA Based on the options indicated in the elective courses and the chosen Work Orientation Laboratories, the graduate will be able to:
- work in multilingual and multicultural groups;
- communicate effectively, also on the pragmatic and non-verbal level;
- manage stress situations, especially in multilingual and multicultural contexts;
- adopt negotiation techniques in multilingual and multicultural contexts, even in conflict situations;
- conduct data analysis starting from databases;
- independently use databases and translation software.

The achievement of the above-mentioned abilities to apply knowledge and understanding occurs through critical reflection on texts and areas proposed in classroom activities, especially laboratory-based ones, and in individual study, through critical reflection, through in-depth bibliographic and field research, and through the autonomous and conscious use of databases in different languages.

The methods for assessing the ability to apply knowledge and understanding are exams, written and oral, intermediate assessments, seminar reports, analysis reports, and the final exam. Intermediate assessments, written and oral exams, the preparation of reports, and the drafting of written assignments and oral presentations involve specific tasks in which the student demonstrates mastery of analytical tools, the ability to synthesize, and the use of various analytical methodologies with critical and organizational autonomy.

Communication Skills.

-----

UNIVERSITY: University of Siena
COURSE: [D446] Languages for Business and Development
TYPE: Master's Degree
SECTION: Communication Skills
URL: https://unisi.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/11226

Communication Skills The course aims to develop multilingual and multicultural communication skills for professional purposes, both in business economic contexts and in social economic contexts. The study and in-depth exploration of communication-related themes and the relational aspects they entail are carried out in the courses on foreign languages, cultural studies, sociolinguistics, and intercultural pragmatics throughout the entire study program. At the end of the study program, the graduate possesses the ability to communicate clearly, concisely, and with a focus on the communication objective – even in specialized and sectoral contexts – with interlocutors from very diverse geographical and socio-cultural areas, including conflict zones. They are able to communicate their arguments without ambiguity not only to specialist interlocutors, but also to the non-specialist public. In the course of lectures and seminars, communication skills are reinforced through discussions and interactions in which the student participates, and are evaluated by the instructor. The graduate in "Languages for Business and Development" is able to:
- use the foreign languages of study and Italian to communicate orally and in writing with specialist and non-specialist interlocutors, with linguistic proficiency and using the appropriate registers for each situation, mastering advanced intercultural pragmatics;
- evaluate, select, and use tools to ensure communication effectiveness (traditional, computer-based, multimedia) according to context and purpose;
- adapt communication forms to transmission methods to ensure effective communication;
- actively participate in work groups and contribute to decision-making and the verbal formulation of related arguments.
Communication skills are acquired through:
- participation in frontal lectures, also using modern technologies and major online databases (especially for language learning and linguistic analysis);
- participation in seminar activities with qualified personalities from the scientific community, public institutions, and civil society, also indicated by the Advisory Committee and generally by the Stakeholders, aimed at deepening relevant cultural, economic, and geopolitical dimensions in the current context;
- participation in initiatives related to ongoing research projects at the Department, on topics relevant to the Master's Degree Program;
- participation in initiatives related to the promotion of multilingualism and intercultural themes such as the European Day of Languages, Translation Day, UNESCO Mother Tongue Day, and World Voice Day (some in close collaboration with the University's European Direct Center);
- guided and individual personal study;
- collective interactions with students during course sessions, based on case studies related to national and international contexts;
- preparation and presentation of seminar interventions within the courses and integrated activities;
- individual in-depth studies during instructor office hours.
The possession of communication skills is verified through:
- final and ongoing written and/or oral exams;
- production of individual and group essays, papers, and reports;
- evaluation of laboratory exercises;
- assessment of internship activities;
- final exam.

Public Relations Manager
- multilingual and multicultural communication officer at national and international entities and organizations;

- translator of specialized and scientific texts for national, European, and extra-European companies and organizations.

The knowledge provided by this Master's Degree program can also serve as a foundation for research-oriented careers.

- expert in organizations dealing with the reception, integration, and training of foreign subjects in Italian language and culture;
- linguistic consultant in cultural mediation in detention centers;
- expert in cultural associations, foundations, and cooperatives;
- linguistic consultant in courts and detention centers.

Public Relations Manager
- high proficiency in oral and written communication in Italian and the two foreign languages of study, in interaction with public and private subjects;
- good knowledge of economic, business, and legal aspects involved in communication in multilingual and multicultural contexts, with particular attention to the different cultural sensitivities present in the reference economic and political contexts;
- high capacity to update one's skills based on changing international contexts, with particular attention to conflict situations, including military ones.
Intercultural and Linguistic Mediation Consultant
- ability to apply comprehension and communication strategies of the two main languages studied in an international context;
- cultural competencies for intercultural mediation in multicultural and multilingual contexts;

- ability to sensitize SMEs to cultural differences, whose neglect can compromise the success of negotiations;
- ability to acquire and manage information related to national legal regulations, as well as contractual aspects, whose lack of knowledge can lead to significant time and financial losses.
Role in the workplace.
Public Relations Manager
- organizes and coordinates economic, financial, and legal relations of entities and organizations with foreign counterparts;
- drafts texts and content for multilingual communication;
- monitors and controls the translation of texts, including specialized ones, necessary for the functioning of entities and organizations, both from foreign languages to Italian and from Italian to foreign languages;
- develops projects for international activities;
- plans and manages communication, production, and marketing activities towards foreign countries, as well as the development of promotional and advertising actions.
Intercultural and Linguistic Mediation Consultant
- organizes and coordinates cultural exchanges within initiatives promoted by public administrations, institutions, and other supranational, public, and private bodies;
- arranges linguistic and cultural mediation activities in public and private entities (courts, detention centers, immigrant reception centers, national and international volunteer and assistance centers);
- collaborates on educational projects for linguistic and intercultural mediation within school and training contexts;
- drafts informative and argumentative texts in the two foreign languages on socioeconomic contexts, both local and global;
- conducts consultancy or manages organizations operating in the fields of cooperation and development aid, even in conflict contexts.
Business Internationalization Consultant
- provides support to companies (especially SMEs) seeking to expand into foreign markets;
- organizes and coordinates economic, financial, and legal relations of Italian companies with foreign counterparts;
- provides specialized knowledge to identify business opportunities, foreign commercial practices, export/import procedures and regulations, product standards and specifications, and marketing requirements.
Specific training objectives description.
Training Objectives The Master's Degree Program in 'Languages for Business and Development' (LM-38) aims to provide advanced competence in two modern foreign languages (at least C1 level of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages), as well as Italian, along with solid intercultural and sociolinguistic competencies, and solid knowledge in economic and legal fields, as well as transversal competencies in digital communication, European project design, data management, and sustainable development. It also aims to provide both theoretical and practical knowledge of intercultural processes and the connections between language, culture, society, and communication, enabling graduates to master the typical communication codes of intercultural relations, especially in multilingual contexts.
At the end of their Master's study program, the graduate in "Languages for Business and Development" will have acquired:
• high active and passive competence in two foreign languages and Italian (minimum C1 level of the Common European Framework of Reference);
• solid preparation in the field of linguistic and sociolinguistic analysis applied to written and oral interactions within international organizations, companies, public and private entities interacting with partners and in international contexts;
• solid knowledge in legal and economic fields to confidently navigate international cooperation, trade, and international law, as well as transnational corporate and institutional communication;
• intercultural pragmatics competencies, enabling the conscious use of known languages in international and intercultural communication, even in contexts characterized by complexity or conflict;
• digital competencies and the ability to manage internal and external communication within an organization;
• the ability to apply acquired competencies through internships at companies and public and private entities in the relevant fields.
Description of the training path The training path spans two years and requires the acquisition of 120 CFU following the completion of profit exams evaluated on a 30-point scale, qualifications, internship, career orientation activities, and the final exam. Below, the learning areas in which the training path is structured are described.
Language and Communication Area Advanced foreign language learning is the fundamental training objective of LM-38, hence a significant number of CFU (36) are allocated to it. Upon enrollment, students in "Languages for Business and Development" choose two languages (Language A and Language B) from French, English, Russian, and Chinese (respectively, L-LIN/04, L-LIN/12, L-LIN/21, L-OR/21), subject to verification of the required entry preparation. For each of the two chosen languages, a biennial study is planned, with an annual language and translation course in both the first and second year, conducted throughout both semesters to ensure gradual and consistent learning. Language and translation courses are delivered in a laboratory and interactive format to allow constant monitoring of learning; they are supported by monolingual lectures by native-speaking Linguistic Experts from the University Language Center, which has a section in Arezzo.
To support language learning, a sufficient number of CFU among the core, related, and integrated disciplines are dedicated to acquiring advanced knowledge of the foundations and mechanisms of intercultural communication: within this framework, all students will acquire a minimum of 9 CFU in general or Italian linguistics (L-LIN/01 and L-FIL-LET/12), and may choose from various options for deepening in linguistic and cultural studies disciplines, within the related and integrated subjects, based on their interest in acquiring greater competencies in intercultural or professional communication.
Economic-Legal Area Consistent with the qualifying training objectives of LM-38, the fields of economics and law are allocated an adequate number of core CFU in the SECS and IUS SSD groups. Within the related and integrated activities, students may personalize their study plan by acquiring additional competencies in one or both economic and legal areas to deepen their methodological foundations and cross-cutting themes or acquire skills in specific sectors not included among the core subjects.
Application of Acquired Competencies Area Within the related and integrated activities, internship, and career orientation, future graduates in "Languages for Business and Development" can refine and apply the disciplinary competencies acquired through a series of options that allow them to acquire a richer and more vocationally responsive knowledge and skill set. Among the related and integrated activities, courses are provided to acquire transversal competencies in digital communication, intercultural communication, European project design, territorial marketing, and sustainable development. In addition to specific courses, the consolidation of these competencies can be achieved through internship and career orientation activities.
The activities designated as 'Internship' and 'Career Orientation' are mandatory and scheduled in the second year of the program. 'Internship' refers to a period of work training at a department-contracted entity or company, aimed at allowing students to apply the linguistic and disciplinary competencies acquired during their study program in a professional setting. Students may also identify companies or other organizations of their own knowledge or interest willing to host them, subject to verification of alignment with the study program and the signing of a convention with the University. Internships can also be conducted abroad within the Erasmus for Traineeship program.
The 'Career Orientation' activity is structured into a series of workshops/seminars from which students can choose based on their interests and professional vocations. Some activities in this area may be co-designed with the Advisory Committee and other Stakeholders, as is the case for L-11.

 Degree Awarded. Master's Degree in Modern Letters
 Teaching Delivery Method Conventional
 Knowledge and Understanding. General Area The Master's degree course aims to train Master's graduates with a solid historical-cultural and linguistic preparation, capable of producing texts, including in foreign languages. Graduates will be able to analyze literary, non-literary, and critical texts, considering the context of production, the author's perspective, reception history, and interpretive conflicts. Textbooks are selected based on scientific level, research relevance, content transparency, and methodological effectiveness. The diversity of disciplines allows students to address specific topics in their field of interest with interdisciplinary openness. Critical literature supporting their formation aims to broaden their knowledge and train them in the plurality of methodological and scientific debate. Regarding foundational theoretical and cultural training, Master's graduates will progressively acquire autonomy and awareness of the study method.
 The training focuses on mastering literary history, philology, language history, literary theory, and the history of criticism. Solid historical knowledge, essential for correctly applying knowledge, is accompanied by in-depth study of philological, linguistic, and theoretical-literary analysis methods. The study of foreign literatures, with their related philologies, also aids in comparative analysis.
 In general, knowledge and understanding will be acquired by Master's students through advanced lectures with updated bibliographic and didactic materials; exercises on texts and sources of particular philological, linguistic, and literary relevance; participation in conferences and seminars of high scientific value by national and international experts; preparation of original and methodologically rigorous reports; and the final exam. Knowledge and skills will be verified through examinations, including the final one.
 Area of Philology, Linguistics, and Italian Literature Mastery of the Italian language, spoken and written. Ability to read Italian literary texts from different eras (from the Middle Ages to the present). Good knowledge of the history of the Italian language. Excellent knowledge of Italian literature, both in terms of historical-cultural contexts and individual authors. The main teaching tool is the lecture, optionally accompanied by seminar-style exercises. Evaluation occurs through written and/or oral exams, or through the preparation of essays.
 Area of Comparative Philologies, Languages, and Modern Literatures Ability to understand one or more foreign languages at the highest possible level (except for English, which requires reaching level B2). For this purpose, exercises are provided by the CEL at different levels of linguistic competence. Ability to express oneself in the studied foreign languages at various levels depending on the student's achieved competence. Good knowledge of the history of the foreign country whose language is studied (at least regarding the historical period studied). Ability to navigate within a text, not only literary, in one of the studied foreign languages. Ability to contextualize the text within its production framework.
 Regarding foreign philologies (Romance and Germanic), good knowledge of the earliest phases of the studied literatures and languages, particularly in relation to cultural dynamics of European medieval history. The main teaching tool is the lecture. For language lessons, significant space is given to in-class exercises with the CEL. Knowledge evaluation occurs through written and/or oral exams, exercises, and seminar activities.
 History Area Good knowledge of Western history and the main tools of historical and historiographical analysis; ability to understand the connections between historical contexts and artistic and cultural products (particularly literary). The main teaching tool is the lecture. Evaluation occurs through written and/or oral exams.

Judgment Autonomy.
The Master's degree aims at acquiring mature critical ability, based on knowledge and awareness of tools and methods. The acquisition of judgment autonomy will be achieved through direct confrontation with texts and related issues, and through the didactic formula of exercises and seminars, which allows for in-depth reflection on linguistic and cultural dynamics and activates critical awareness based on systematic comparison of data. The verification of the acquisition of judgment autonomy will take place through written and oral presentations provided for within courses and seminars and at the time of final exams, some of which include both written and oral tests. Particular attention will be devoted to the preparation of the final exam, intended as the final verification moment of the process of acquisition and development of autonomous and conscious critical abilities.

Learning Ability.
With the development of research autonomy, Master's graduates will be provided with the necessary capacity to proceed individually in cultural growth, also in view of possible subsequent studies (PhD, Master's degree Level II). This critical propensity, based on a full understanding of literary, philological, critical, and linguistic facts, will enable Master's graduates to orient themselves, with specialist competence and critical autonomy, in debates within the disciplines studied. This learning ability will allow Master's graduates to undertake individual research paths and apply acquired knowledge for professional purposes.

Through training in the use of bibliographic heritage, syntactic-grammatical, lexicographic tools, and resources such as online tools, databases, text query software, etc., the student will be enabled to deepen and permanently update acquired skills. This ability will be verified during discussion moments and exam tests.

This set of competencies is considered essential for undertaking teaching and accessing selections for the Active Training Internship.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area: In addition to the basic training already acquired, there is a gradual increase in attention to methodological and applied aspects of acquired knowledge. The student will be constantly confronted with the most advanced scientific results. At the end of the course, Master's graduates will be able to apply knowledge and understanding to the analysis of texts in linguistic, comparative, literary-critical, and philological contexts.

These objectives will be achieved through the following tools: frontal lectures and exercises; writing of written papers and research essays; participation in advanced seminars; bibliographic research on specific and complex topics; use of databases, corpora, thesauri, and dictionaries. These advanced tools will enable students to formulate updated and conscious judgments, develop autonomous reflections, and apply acquired knowledge with originality. The independence of judgment will also have positive repercussions on future professional activity. This ability will be systematically verified during discussion moments, written and oral presentations provided for within courses and seminars, exam tests, and the process of conceiving and writing the thesis.

Area of Philology, Linguistics, and Italian Literature: Ability to analyze linguistic, philological, and literary texts from different eras (from the Middle Ages to the present). Ability to place literary texts within reference theoretical frameworks.

Area of Comparative Philologies, Languages, and Modern Literatures: Ability to read, analyze, and place in historical-cultural and linguistic context fundamental texts of studied foreign literatures. Ability to establish connections between the historical-cultural context of the studied foreign language and literature and the Italian context. Ability to apply acquired philological methods and main critical tools to the study of modern literary texts.

Historical Area: Ability to place literary phenomena within their historical context; ability to understand the social and sociological aspects of literary history.

Communication Skills.
Communication skills are an essential part of a Modern Literature course. All disciplines in the course orient towards the production of texts where there is full mastery of specialized languages (philological, theoretical, critical, historical, pedagogical). The development of communication skills will be achieved through constant attention to the modes of written expression (reports and essays) and oral expression (class discussions, seminars, exams), as well as through the teaching in the L-FIL-LET 12 sector (Italian Linguistics), specifically dedicated to reflection on language in its oral and written dimensions. The verification of communication skills will occur through written and oral presentations required within courses and seminars, and during final exams, some of which include both written and oral components. Particular importance will be given to the final thesis, which will specifically attest to the acquisition of communication skills in the context of academic and essay writing.
Expected occupational and professional opportunities for graduates.
Expert in the cultural and editorial industry. Master's graduates in Modern Literature who have sufficient credits in appropriate disciplinary groups may, as provided by current legislation, participate in admission tests for secondary teaching training paths. The Master's degree in Modern Literature also provides an excellent foundation for accessing research doctorate competitions in humanities and philological disciplines. The Master's graduate in Modern Literature is equipped with a comprehensive, versatile, and flexible education, capable of integrating specific in-depth experiences in the fields of classical and modern literature, history, philosophy, and anthropology. Master's graduates in Modern Literature may carry out professional activities at local authorities and specific institutions, such as libraries, archives, and academies, as well as at publishing houses, journalistic editorial offices, foundations, companies, and other professional entities operating in the field of organizing events and cultural activities.
Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIAN Competencies associated with the function.
Expert in the cultural and editorial industry. The expert in the cultural and editorial industry will possess excellent written and oral mastery of the Italian language; good mastery of at least one foreign language; theoretical and practical knowledge of the foundations of linguistics; excellent knowledge of textual analysis methods, their interpretation, and placement in various historical and cultural contexts; advanced ability to produce formal texts in the fields of publishing, journalism, the cultural industry, and library heritage management; preliminary teaching competencies for the teaching-focused path (subject to further training as per current regulations). These competencies will enable the Master's graduate in Modern Literature to competently and precisely fulfill the main functions required by various sectors of the cultural and editorial industry.
Description of admission tests.
The access modalities for the University's degree programs are regulated by Part II of the Guiding Act on the Educational Offer for the 2020/21 academic year - Access to Degree Programs, available at https://www.unisi.it/ateneo/statuto-e-regolamenti/atti-di-indirizzo. Students from the following three-year degree programs under D.M. 270/2005 are admitted to the Master's in Modern Literature: L-10 (Literature), L-11 (Modern Languages and Cultures), L-12 (Linguistic Mediation Sciences), L-20 (Communication Sciences); or from the following degree classes under D.M. 509/99: 5 (Literature), 11 (Modern Languages and Cultures), 3 (Linguistic Mediation Sciences), 14 (Communication Sciences). English language knowledge at least at B1 level is required. Within the 42 CFU, at least one exam (6 CFU) in the following SSD is required: L-FIL-LET/10 Italian Literature, L-FIL-LET/11 Contemporary Italian Literature, or L-FIL-LET/14 Literary Criticism and Comparative Literature, L-FIL-LET/12 Italian Linguistics, L-FIL-LET/09 Romance Philology and Linguistics, or L-FIL-LET/13 Italian Literary Philology. For those coming from a different degree class than those listed above, at least 72 CFU in the following SSD are required: L-FIL-LET/04 Latin Language and Literature, L-FIL-LET/09 Romance Philology and Linguistics, L-FIL-LET/10 Italian Literature, L-FIL-LET/11 Contemporary Italian Literature, L-FIL-LET/12 Italian Linguistics, L-FIL-LET/13 Italian Literary Philology, L-FIL-LET/14 Literary Criticism and Comparative Literature, L-FIL-LET/15 Germanic Philology, L-LIN/01 Glottology and Linguistics, L-LIN/02 Teaching of Modern Languages, L-LIN/03 French Literature, L-LIN/04 French Language, L-LIN/05 Spanish Literature, L-LIN/06 Ibero-American Literatures, L-LIN/07 Spanish Language, L-LIN/08 Portuguese and Brazilian Literature, L-LIN/09 Portuguese Language, L-LIN/10 English Literature, L-LIN/11 Anglo-American Literature, L-LIN/12 English Language, L-LIN/13 German Literature, L-LIN/14 German Language, L-LIN/21 Slavic Studies (Russian Language and Literature), M-GGR Geography, M-DEA Demographic and Anthropological Studies, M-STO/M-FIL. Workplace Function.
Expert in the cultural and editorial industry. The main functions the Master's graduate will perform are: writing scientific texts in Italian and foreign languages; literary translation from ancient and modern languages; editorial activities within publishing houses, newspapers, and press offices; cultural activities at libraries, cultural centers, and Italian cultural institutes abroad. The Master's degree also prepares for humanistic research activities in academic and private settings. The Master's graduate in Modern Literature will be able to operate in the fields of cultural services and production, communication and information, public relations, and productive organizations, as well as in universities and research centers.
Additional Information.
http://www.unisi.it/dipartimenti/dipartimento-filologia-e-critica-delle-letterature-antiche-e-moderne Specific Educational Objectives Description.
The Master's degree in Modern Literature offers a solid humanistic education, integrates and consolidates the knowledge acquired by students in their three-year degrees, provides methods and tools for analysis applicable in research, teaching, and any activities related to humanistic education. It is an interdisciplinary Master's degree. Given the need to train individuals capable of moving confidently in international cultural contexts, the Master's program dedicates ample space to the study of languages, philologies, and foreign literatures as indispensable tools for international communication and critical reflection, also from a comparative perspective. The B1 level in English is required as an entry requirement. To ensure a solid overall cultural preparation, the Master's degree is structured into disciplinary and thematic areas:
1) Area of Philology, Linguistics, and Italian Literature. This area includes courses belonging to the disciplinary sectors L-FIL-LET/9, L-FIL-LET/10, L-FIL-LET/11, L-FIL-LET/12, L-FIL-LET/13. These courses provide a solid preparation on the history of the Italian language and literature from its origins to the present day, according to a diachronic and synchronic perspective. Student training occurs through in-depth philological, linguistic, and stylistic analysis of literary texts. The text is always analyzed in relation to the historical, social, and cultural phenomena of which it is a product, from both an Italian and European perspective. Alongside the analysis of literary texts, the degree program also places great emphasis on the in-depth study of more specifically theoretical issues regarding literary criticism and the sociology of literature.
2) Area of Comparative Philologies, Languages, and Modern Literatures. This area includes courses belonging to the disciplinary sectors: L-FIL-LET/09 (also relevant to Area 1), L-FIL-LET/11 (also relevant to Area 1), L-FIL-LET/14, L-FIL-LET/15, L-LIN/01, L-LIN/03, L-LIN/04, L-LIN/05, L-LIN/06, L-LIN/07, L-LIN/08, L-LIN/10, L-LIN/11, L-LIN/12, L-LIN/13, L-LIN/14, L-LIN/21. Students can choose the focus of their education: they may prefer to deepen Italian literature and linguistics, especially from the modern and contemporary periods, or broaden their interests to philologies (Germanic and Romance), languages, and modern foreign literatures (English, French, German, Spanish, Portuguese, Russian). Both curricula share the centrality of comparative literature as an indispensable tool for training individuals capable of situating specific literary phenomena within broader cultural contexts, from both a textual criticism and literary theory perspective.
3) Historical Area. This area includes courses belonging to the disciplinary sectors M-STO/01, M-STO/02, M-STO/04, M-STO/08. They provide a solid preparation on the history of European culture from classical antiquity to the contemporary era, with a focus on the relationship between historical contexts and literary works. To address the need for a connection between university education and the workplace, a curricular internship is provided for all disciplinary and thematic areas, allowing students to gain training experience through programs proposed by the University or through agreements with entities, companies, and publishing houses. At the end of the educational path, the student must present and discuss a final thesis, demonstrating the achievement of competencies related to their path.

Final Exam Characteristics The final exam will consist of a public discussion before a committee composed according to the modalities indicated in the university's teaching regulations and the course's teaching regulations, of a thesis produced from original research and the result of a personal, organic re-elaboration of knowledge acquired during the training path.

The thesis and its discussion must demonstrate the candidate's ability to autonomously use specific sources of their study area, relevant research tools, and the necessary knowledge resources to develop an original product that constitutes a significant advancement in knowledge in the investigated field. They must also demonstrate the candidate's ability to clearly and effectively present and adequately argue the results of their research.

The thesis work, for which 27 CFU are awarded, will be carried out under the supervision of a course instructor and discussed with the participation of a rapporteur.

The final exam evaluation will be expressed on a scale of 110, with possible honors.

Any deficiencies in academic credits may be remedied, upon recommendation by the competent teaching structures, even during the period between the first-level degree and the closure of enrollment for Master's degree courses, by passing the profit exams of individual courses offered by the university.

Judgment Autonomy.
The Master's degree in Classical Letters will acquire a secure capacity for autonomous judgment, which will be expressed particularly in:
* using the knowledge, skills, abilities, and capacities acquired during the studies to express autonomous, articulated, motivated, and original judgments on specific problems within the disciplines and the area of interest;
* ability to manage in a conscious and critical manner the diversity of interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary approaches possible to build new research topics and new methods of conducting research;
* ability to confidently navigate within the theoretical and methodological reflection related to the area of interest;
* ability to critically treat different source systems in order to preliminarily assess their overall reliability and usability for research purposes, also in reference to the qualitative and quantitative aspects of the statistical sample they represent;
* ability to evaluate and explicitly state the social value of scientific research on human past and antiquity understood in the broadest and most articulated sense of the term.
Teaching methods and tools to achieve the objectives:
Specific courses or specific segments within curricular courses dedicated to theoretical-methodological aspects of different disciplines and issues of interoperability between similar disciplinary fields.
Assessment methods:
Evaluation of judgment maturity regarding these aspects within curricular exams, also through the discussion of independent works.
Learning Capacity.
Graduates in the Master's degree in Classical Letters will have fully developed all learning capacities (linguistic, lexical, dialectical, argumentative, etc.) that enable them to continue their educational path at more advanced levels. In particular:
* ability to use bibliographic tools in traditional form and/or with the support of new technologies in absolute autonomy;
* ability to participate consciously, critically, and actively in advanced training moments within formal courses or on occasions of events of different nature (seminars, conferences, etc.);
* ability to outline their own path for the development of the educational process, selecting the most appropriate training opportunities to achieve the set cognitive, research, and professional goals.
Teaching methods and tools to achieve the objectives:
Specific segments within disciplinary courses dedicated to illustrating the main tools and procedures for individual research, also with the aid of computer resources;
Seminar activities at different levels.
Assessment methods:
Verification of achieved abilities in this area through the evaluation of written works and the degree of active participation in the planned teaching and seminar activities.
Application of Knowledge and Understanding Capacity.
Generic Area Graduates in the Master's degree in Classical Letters will be able to apply the complex set of knowledge and understanding acquired in:
* Construction of an individual cultural identity and a solid professional approach to work in various activity areas (teaching, research, training, etc.);
* Identification of research areas and issues potentially fruitful in the field of philological and linguistic disciplines (but also historical and archaeological) related to antiquity in its broadest sense, to be investigated through the elaboration of independent research projects;
* Creation and management of small work groups aimed at conducting autonomous research in the disciplinary areas of interest;
* Creation and management of innovative research tools related to the application of new technologies to humanities disciplines;
* Design and implementation of diversified forms of public communication (scientific and popularizing publications, new media, events, etc.) in relation to the area of interest.
Literary and Philological Area Construction of an individual cultural identity and a solid professional approach to work in various activity areas (teaching, research, training, etc.).
Identification of research areas and issues potentially fruitful in the field of philological and linguistic disciplines related to antiquity in its broadest sense, to be investigated through the elaboration of independent research projects.

* develop innovative communication tools that fully exploit the potential offered by new technologies in the fields of public communication, training, and the creation of data bases and operational tools aimed at advancing research in their specific field of interest;
* integrate – through the conscious and critical use of a shared specialist language – into an international scientific community.
