ITALIAN Associated competencies for the role.
Expert in ancient sciences, philologist The competencies associated with the role of master's graduate in Classical Literature include knowledge of linguistic (Greek and Latin language and literature), philological (Classical Philology), and historical (Greek and Roman History) disciplines of the classical world, acquired through the two main strands that most characterize the study program within the Siena context: the anthropological study of classical cultures and the study of the classical tradition in medieval, modern, and contemporary culture.
Description of admission tests.
Assessment methods for initial student preparation
1. If the student does not possess the required prerequisites, they may access the Master's degree in Classical Literature after passing an admission test, consisting of an interview with three professors designated annually by the Teaching Committee. The interview will begin with a sight translation and analysis of two short texts (one Greek and one Latin; one prose and one poetry); its objective will be to verify the candidate's knowledge of classical languages and their ability to contextualize major authors of Greek and Roman literature historically and literarily. The test will be considered passed if the candidate demonstrates sufficient mastery of classical languages and the ability to navigate the history of Greek and Latin literature.
2. Graduating students who have passed the verification test will be admitted conditionally and may enroll on the condition that they obtain their degree within the deadlines for closing enrollments.
Direct admission
1. Those exempt from the admission test are graduates who, possessing the required curricular requirements, have obtained a final grade of at least 100/110. Graduates with a final grade below 100/110 may be exempt from the admission test only if the weighted average of the exams contributing to the 48 CFU required in the SSD L-ANT/02 and/or L-ANT/03, L-FIL-LET/02, L-FIL-LET/04, and L-FIL-LET/05 is equal to or above 27/30.
2. Master's graduates possessing the required curricular requirements are also exempt from the admission test.
3. Those exempt from the test, as recognized to possess the required personal preparation, are graduating students who, despite being eligible to participate, have already achieved a weighted average of at least 27/30 in all courses in their study plan in the SSD: L-ANT/02 and/or L-ANT/03, L-FIL-LET/02, L-FIL-LET/04, and L-FIL-LET/05 by the test date. In the absence of this requirement, graduating students planning to graduate by the enrollment closing deadline may choose to take the test, provided that, regardless of the outcome, they will be admitted by right if their graduation grade achieved within the deadline is not below 100/110.
Professional role in the workplace.
Expert in ancient sciences, philologist The professional profile of the master's graduate in Classical Literature is that of an expert in ancient sciences capable of transmitting to society, in diverse forms and intervention sectors, the determining value that this dimension possesses in the construction and protection of our common cultural identity. Therefore, they are able to work in areas such as mass communication (journalism, publishing, public relations, new media), with particular reference to cultural, archaeological, historical, and literary information. Additionally, the master's degree in Classical Literature lays the groundwork for them to pursue a path leading to teaching their disciplines, both at the secondary school level and at the university level.
Additional information.
http://www.unisi.it/dipartimenti/dipartimento-filologia-e-critica-delle-letterature-antiche-e-moderne Specific learning objectives description.
The specific learning objective of the Master's degree in Classical Literature is to train knowledge operators oriented towards the study of the ancient world (in its broadest chronological, spatial, and thematic dimensions) through a multidisciplinary approach, capable of transmitting (in diverse forms and intervention sectors) the determining value of this dimension in the construction and protection of our common cultural identity.
In line with the programmatic approach, the Master's degree in Classical Literature is positioned at a precise stage in the student's educational path, having already acquired with the Bachelor's degree the competencies of a disciplinary area and intending not only to specialize but also to broaden them through knowledge approaches and investigation methods aimed at comprehensively enriching their cultural horizons and individual capabilities to be applied upon entering the workforce.
The specific objectives for master's graduates in Classical Literature can be defined as follows:
* acquisition of advanced disciplinary and methodological competencies in the fields of classical literature, ancient history, and classical philology, referring both to traditional investigation and study tools and to new methodologies and technologies;
* acquisition of a substantial interdisciplinary openness towards the fields of anthropology, medieval and modern history, modern literature, iconography, and medieval and modern art history;
* acquisition of the ability to fluently use, in written and oral expressive forms, the English language and to read scientific texts in the classical field in at least one further European language.
The main learning areas of the study program are three: literary and philological area; anthropological area; historical area.
For the literary and philological area, relevant courses concern the following SSD: L-FIL-LET/02, 04, 05, 06, 08.
For the anthropological area, relevant courses concern the following SSD: L-FIL-LET/02, 04, 05 (particularly the course 'Anthropology of the Ancient World' for this sector).
For the historical area, relevant courses concern the following SSD: L-ANT/02, 03, 05, 07, M-FIL/07, M-STO/09.
The training path is structured as follows: the first year allows master's students to address both fundamental disciplines (classical languages and literatures and ancient history) and a choice of important complementary subjects (papyrology, early Christian literature, medieval Latin literature, classical philology); the second year features courses related to the teaching of classical languages and cultures, offers the opportunity to deepen historical and philological knowledge, and proposes another choice of characteristic subjects (archaeology and history of ancient art, history of ancient philosophy, paleography).
This training path focuses on the study of linguistic disciplines (L-FIL-LET/02 and L-FIL-LET/04), philological disciplines (L-FIL-LET/05, 06, 08, L-ANT/05), and historical disciplines (L-ANT/02 and 03) of the classical world, with the possibility of acquiring additional CFU in disciplines such as classical archaeology and history of ancient art (L-ANT/07) and history of ancient philosophy (M-FIL/07). The main scientific interest strand characterizing the course is the anthropological study of classical cultures, together with the study of the classical tradition in medieval, modern, and contemporary culture. This is a characteristic that distinguishes the Siena context, linked to the Interuniversity Center for Anthropology and the Ancient World, founded in 1986 by Maurizio Bettini.

– Linguistic consultants for companies in the information technology sector (2.5.4.4.1 - Linguists and philologists)
– Translators for specific fields related to advanced research (2.5.4.3 - Interpreters and translators at an advanced level)
– Teachers of foreign languages and Italian as a first or second language (2.6.5.5.5 - Teachers of languages)
Additionally, the two curricula, while not having a qualifying function, provide skills applicable in the following areas:
a) In the field of education services, the Master's graduate will be able to collaborate with support teachers dedicated to the education of young people, adults and children with learning difficulties (2.6.5.1 - Specialists in education and training for people with disabilities), or with language instructors (teaching in schools will comply with current regulations);
b) In the field of health services, at specialized centers for rehabilitation of language disorders;
c) In the field of social services, in public administrations or cooperatives dealing with multilingualism issues in educational contexts (3.4.5.2 - Technicians for reintegration and social integration)
Final Exam Characteristics The Master's thesis must be a personal research work, theoretical and/or experimental. The work is carried out by the student under the guidance of a supervisor chosen by them, a faculty member in one of the disciplines of the Master's program. The thesis must have a certain consistency and be at least 100 pages long. A second faculty member will serve as co-supervisor. The Master's thesis will be defended by the candidate before a committee. The preparation of the Master's thesis will include a mid-term verification with a presentation by the candidate on the progress of their research, within the research seminar dedicated to this purpose during the Master's program schedule. If the presentation at the research seminar is approved by the faculty of the Master's program, the candidate will earn the required CFU. The Master's thesis will be awarded 18 CFU. The score will be assigned based on the average obtained by the student in the exams, calculated out of 110. The score derived from the average may be increased according to the criteria set by the department regulations, for original and high-quality scientific work, which may also be awarded the highest distinction.
Required Knowledge for Admission The knowledge required for admission and curricular requirements are defined in the Didactic Regulations of the Master's program, which also indicate the methods for verifying the student's personal preparation.
Degree Awarded.
Master's Degree in LANGUAGE AND MIND: LINGUISTICS AND COGNITIVE STUDIES Understanding and Knowledge.
Generic Area The Master's program in Language and Mind: Linguistics and Cognitive Studies/Mente e Linguaggio. Linguistica e Studi Cognitivi, besides opening to professions where language and cognition are central, prepares students for more advanced doctoral studies and provides specialized knowledge of research issues in the field. The program emphasizes advanced theoretical and experimental research on language and cognition. Students will be able to address specialized scientific literature and engage with qualified publications and scientific journals, both in print and online. The moment when students demonstrate their level of knowledge is during the preparation and discussion of the Master's thesis, to which the program reserves a significant number of credits. Students will also present their thesis work at a medium-advanced stage within a research seminar included in the Master's program schedule. Two research seminars are organized, one for each curriculum; the program reserves a dedicated number of credits for the seminar, attendance of which is mandatory. For the linguistic curriculum, the seminar consists of sessions throughout the academic year, involving reports on field work and/or material collection and/or methodological discussion for the thesis project, where one or more sessions may include talks by instructors or external speakers. For the philosophical curriculum, the seminar may consist of a Summer School and/or Workshop, requiring participants to write a paper on one of the discussed topics, and/or seminar sessions where a student presents and discusses their thesis work at a medium-advanced stage. The research seminar involves faculty members of the Master's program, classmates in the same curriculum, and new students who have chosen the same curriculum. This facilitates exchange and direct feedback on the attained knowledge, following a practice that has been successfully applied for several years in the Master's program.
ENGLISH The Master's program in Language and Mind: Linguistics and Cognitive Studies, besides opening to professions in which language and cognition are central, prepares students to undertake more advanced doctoral studies and provides them with specialized knowledge of research issues in the field. The program is centered on advanced theoretical and experimental research on language and cognition. Students will become able to address specialized scientific literature and to be in contact with qualified publications and scientific journals, both in print and online. Students will demonstrate the level attained in their overall formation during the preparation and subsequent discussion of their Master's thesis, to which the program reserves a significant number of credits. Students will present the state of their thesis work at a medium-advanced stage within the framework of a research seminar, integrated into the schedule of the Master's program. Two research seminars are arranged, one for each curriculum; the program reserves a dedicated number of credits for the seminar, attendance of which is mandatory. The research seminar for the linguistic curriculum is structured into sessions throughout the academic year, consisting of reports on field work and/or material collection and/or methodological discussion for the thesis project, where one or more sessions may be integrated by talks given by instructors or external speakers. The research seminar for the philosophical curriculum may be structured into a Summer School and/or Workshop, requiring attendees to write a paper on one of the discussed topics, and/or seminar sessions where a student presents and discusses their thesis work at a medium-advanced stage. Faculty members, classmates in the same curriculum, and first-year students who have chosen the same curriculum will participate in the seminar. This facilitates exchange and direct feedback on the attained knowledge, through a practice that has proven highly successful over the years.

Judgment Autonomy.
Once students have chosen the topic of their master's thesis, with the scientific-cultural awareness guaranteed by the training path as described above, they will be able to undertake a personal work that achieves a certain level of originality, which will be evaluated by the thesis supervisor as well as by the teachers present at the presentations and research seminars given by the students. Students will be able to formulate explanatory hypotheses, both at the linguistic-formal level and at the philosophical level, regarding different linguistic and cognitive phenomena, to formulate experimental designs within the field of first and second language acquisition and language pathology, to evaluate the validity and relevance of a scientific and philosophical argument, to choose their cultural interlocutors, also in view of decisions concerning their future, whether in professional contexts or in doctoral programs, at the national or international level.
Learning Capacity.
The Master's degree prepares students for doctoral studies in linguistics, cognitive sciences, philosophy of mind and language, both at the national and international level. In addition to regular frontal lessons, students will be trained in research and in communicating research results through seminar readings, oral presentations during courses, preparation and public discussion of short papers on assigned topics, and active participation in annual research seminars. In this way, they will be enabled to move with adequate autonomy in choosing their subsequent study path and the domains of study and research most suitable to them, typically a natural development of the master's thesis work.
Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
General Area Through theoretical research on the general properties of language, from phonology to morphology, from syntax to semantics and pragmatics, and through experimental work in the field of first and second language acquisition and language pathology, students will be confronted with the most recent results in the fields of linguistics and philosophy of mind and language, as well as natural language logics, and, from an interdisciplinary perspective, with different fields such as neuroscience and neurolinguistics, psycholinguistics, and computational linguistics. This will enable students to become as autonomous and aware as possible in choosing their thesis topic, where their ability to appropriate and apply acquired knowledge in an original manner is expressed, with positive implications for their future professional activity.

Communication Skills.
Within the courses taken during the first year of the Master's program, students will often have the opportunity to give brief oral presentations on topics indicated in the course program, according to methods specific to each course. Students will also frequently be required to prepare a written version of the work presented orally or of other work, again following methods specific to each course. This provides students with the opportunity to systematically exercise their communication skills, both oral and written, to acquire the ability to independently navigate within a defined topic and to construct an adequate bibliography, including both printed works owned by the library and online works researched on qualified national and international websites, journals, and pre-publications. The presence of both the course instructor and classmates at the presentation requires students to adapt their oral presentation so that it can be understood by both specialists and non-specialists. As successfully experimented since the "laurea specialistica in Linguistica," this simple approach guarantees systematic practice of skills that might otherwise remain unexpressed. Therefore, the final assessment of each course will not be based solely on the final exam, but will also take into account, to a degree determined autonomously by each course based on its specific nature, the result of the presentation and/or written work submitted by the student. This constitutes a positive stimulus and challenge for students to achieve the best possible result.

– Linguistic consultants for companies in the field of information technology (2.5.4.4.1 - Linguists and philologists)

b) In the field of health services, at centers specialized in rehabilitation for language disorders;
c) In the field of social services, in public administrations or cooperatives dealing with multilingualism issues in the school environment (3.4.5.2 - Technicians for social reintegration and integration)

Additional information.
http://www.unisi.it http://http://www.dispoc.unisi.it/it Specific educational objectives.
The Master's program in Language and Mind: Linguistics and Cognitive Studies/Mente e Linguaggio. Linguistica e Studi Cognitivi is offered in English within class LM-39/Linguistics, and its structure is a modification of the Master's program in Linguistics and Persuasive Communication; Technologies and Cognitive Studies. The program proposes a highly interdisciplinary training, directly connected with advanced research activities on language conducted at the Interdepartmental Center for Cognitive Studies on Language (www.ciscl.unisi.it). The program is therefore structured into two curricula: Linguistics and Cognition/Linguistica e Cognizione; Philosophy and Cognition/Filosofia e Cognizione.
The fundamental changes are two: i. The teaching is offered in English; ii. The program is structured into two curricula. The first modification aims to emphasize the already strongly international character of the study program and its predecessors, so as to facilitate: access for foreign students to the courses offered; interaction between Italian and foreign students; access to international doctoral programs; the ability to actively participate in international conferences and seminars; opportunities to access job opportunities abroad. The second modification, following the migration of some courses from the previous Master's program in Linguistics and Persuasive Communication; Technologies and Cognitive Studies into another Master's program, aims to build a coherent and diversified training path, featuring a predominant number of common courses in the first year and a second year dedicated to in-depth study in one of the two directions.
The Master's program in Language and Mind: Linguistics and Cognitive Studies /Mente e Linguaggio. Linguistica e Studi Cognitivi focuses in both curricula on the study of languages and language from the perspective of cognitive studies and the philosophy of language and mind. It is primarily addressed to students interested in:
- In-depth description of human languages in their various forms, including dialects;
- Study of language as a cognitive capacity and its implications in the domains of first and second language acquisition and language pathology;
- Study of the philosophical, psychological, biological, and social foundations of language and cognition;
- Study of the relevance of in-depth analysis of human language for philosophical studies.
The main achievements that Master's graduates will attain from the program, which are the primary aims of the program itself, are:
- In-depth knowledge of theoretical models and analytical methods of contemporary linguistics, including experimental methods and field research;
- Ability to apply theories and methods of linguistic research for the description and analysis of different languages, in a comparative perspective;
- Familiarity with different aspects of the interdisciplinary study of language as a cognitive capacity, of first and second language acquisition, and of the relationship between mind, language, and brain;
- Familiarity with philosophical issues underlying the study of language as a cognitive capacity and the relationship between mind and language, as well as the relationship between logic, inference, and meaning in natural languages;
- Ability to apply theories and methods of linguistics in different applied domains, such as language teaching, the study of language pathology, computational applications, and psycholinguistic experimentation.

Access to accounting professions (Chartered Accountant, Company Auditor)
The Master's Degree in International Accounting and Management allows access to the examination for the Chartered Accountant profession under Legislative Decree 28 June 2005, n. 139, as well as the exercise of legal company audit activities under Legislative Decree 27 January 2010, n. 39 (subject to internship and passing the State examination for qualification).
Final examination characteristics The final examination consists of an original thesis prepared under the guidance of a supervisor.
The thesis must be written and defended in English.
Part of the final examination may be carried out within an internship or training activity, which can be conducted either independently by the student or within the practical activities provided by the study programme. To this end, teachers of the Master's programme promote practical training activities related to research and thesis writing within their courses.
The thesis will be evaluated based on the level of theoretical depth, the candidate's ability to use appropriate quantitative methodologies for the research objective, the effectiveness of empirical analyses, the originality of proposed arguments, and the effectiveness of the discussion.
Required knowledge for admission To be admitted to the Master's Degree in IAMA, one must hold a three-year university degree or equivalent foreign qualification recognized as suitable, or a Master's degree, a specialist degree, or a four-year degree under the previous system.
Additionally, proficiency in using main computer tools (text processing and spreadsheet software) and knowledge of English corresponding to at least level B2 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages are required.
Specifically, for admission to IAMA, certain curricular requirements and adequate personal preparation must be met as specified below and verified.
Curricular requirements To be admitted to the Master's Degree in IAMA, one must hold a suitable qualification in business, economic, or management engineering fields (first-level degree classes under DM 270/2004: L-18 - Economics and Business Management Sciences, L-33 - Economic Sciences, L-8 - Information Engineering - Management Engineering, or similar classes under DM 509/1999).
Admission is also permitted with a suitable qualification in a different degree class, provided sufficient university credits have been earned in specific scientific-disciplinary areas of business, economic, mathematical-statistical, and legal fields (minimum 60 CFU, including at least 24 CFU in the business area). Specifically, the essential credits required for enrollment in the study programme are:
• Business area: SECS-P/07 - Business Economics, SECS-P/08 - Economics and Management of Enterprises, SECS-P/09 - Corporate Finance, SECS-P/10 - Business Organization, SECS-P/11 - Economics of Financial Intermediaries;
• Economic area: SECS-P/01 - Political Economy, SECS-P/02 - Economic Policy, SECS-P/03 - Public Finance, SECS-P/04 - History of Economic Thought, SECS-P/05 - Econometrics, SECS-P/06 - Applied Economics, SECS-P/12 - Economic History;
• Mathematical-statistical area: SECS-S/01 - Statistics, SECS-S/03 - Economic Statistics, SECS-S/06 - Mathematical Methods for Economics and Actuarial and Financial Sciences, MAT/02 - Algebra, MAT/03 - Geometry, MAT/05 - Mathematical Analysis, MAT/06 - Probability and Mathematical Statistics, MAT/08 - Numerical Analysis, MAT/09 - Operations Research;
• Legal area: IUS/01 - Private Law, IUS/04 - Commercial Law, IUS/05 - Economics Law, IUS/07 - Labour Law, IUS/09 - Public Law Institutions, IUS/10 - Administrative Law, IUS/12 - Tax Law, IUS/13 - International Law, IUS/14 - European Union Law.
The study programme's teaching regulations further define the curricular requirements in relation to different first-level degree classes, as well as the number of credits to be acquired in specific disciplinary areas and how they are verified.
For graduates holding foreign qualifications, the required knowledge for admission is defined by the study programme's teaching regulations based on the minimum content deemed necessary for the different disciplinary areas, including linguistic knowledge.
Verification of personal preparation For admission to the study programme, students holding the required curricular qualifications must pass a test to verify personal preparation, the modalities of which are defined by the study programme's teaching regulations.
Exemption from the admission test is granted to graduates holding the required curricular qualifications who obtained their degree with a grade exceeding a minimum threshold defined by the study programme's teaching regulations, which also specifies:
• the subjects, modalities, and evaluation criteria of the test;
• the specific modalities for evaluating the initial preparation of foreign university graduates, including necessary linguistic knowledge.

Autonomy of Judgment.
The autonomy of judgment demonstrated in the conduct of teaching activities constitutes one of the evaluation parameters for the student's overall academic performance. It is the responsibility of the course instructor to adequately verify and evaluate this, reflecting the qualitative level expressed by the student in the final grade.
Master's graduates who have successfully completed the course of study must be able to:
a) correctly interpret analyses to adopt the most suitable management approach;
b) find and appropriately utilize professional contributions related to management issues;
c) possess abstract thinking to identify the essence of a problem and apply general principles to specific cases.
These competencies will be acquired and verified through seminars and study groups dedicated to the analysis and interpretation of empirical data relevant to business decisions; for such training activities, collaboration with particularly qualified experts from the economic-business context is also provided. Particular importance will also be given to verifying these competencies during the assessment of the final examination.

Learning Capacity.
Throughout the duration of the Course, students are encouraged to engage with diverse texts including books, scientific articles, manuals, databases, reports, and texts in foreign languages, etc. It is expected that, by operating in this way, at the end of their educational path students will be able to implement different learning strategies according to the context and available materials. In particular:
a) they will be able to tackle subsequent and advanced study programs (Master's, PhD, etc.);
b) they will be able to independently manage their professional life through the continuous education required by today's workplace.
These competencies are primarily acquired and verified within specialized courses, as well as in the training activities for preparing the final examination.

They also have skills in analyzing data and financial documents, processing information, drafting financial information and reports. Particular attention is given to developing problem-solving and leadership abilities, which are highly valued in global recruitment contexts.
Expert in Economic and Business Matters with an International Focus: Master's graduates in International Accounting and Management possess all the necessary competencies to control and manage business processes requiring coordination between different country locations. In particular, they have the competencies to plan and develop the internationalization process of an entrepreneurial activity, the ability to analyze, from a strategic perspective, different country systems at economic, regulatory, social, and cultural levels; the ability to conduct international market and competitive analysis; the ability to manage transnational procurement, production, and distribution processes; and the competencies to harmonize international control and accounting systems.
Access to Accounting Professions (Chartered Accountant, Company Auditor)
The Study Program provides Master's graduates with up-to-date knowledge in tax, economic-business, legal, and administrative matters, enabling them to correctly perform:
- Tax compliance and economic-legal examination of asset management;
- Budget planning;
- Expert assessments for company liquidations;
- Inspections and administrative verifications;
- In general, the processing and adoption of management decisions for private and public entities.
Workplace Function.
Expert in Economic and Business Matters: The Master's Degree in International Accounting and Management prepares graduates to assume directorial responsibility roles within companies, both in staff and line management functions; to undertake autonomous entrepreneurial activities, including consultancy; to assume responsibility roles in institutional bodies at national and international levels (Chambers of Commerce, Industry Associations, Local Authorities, European Union, and International Economic Organizations). In all these cases, the individual can perform decision-making, leadership, coordination, management, and data and information analysis functions.
Expert in Economic and Business Matters with an International Focus: The Master's Degree in International Accounting and Management prepares graduates to assume directorial responsibility roles within companies, organizations, and institutions that operate particularly at the transnational level; to undertake autonomous work with a strong international focus, whether entrepreneurial, professional, or consultancy-oriented; to assume responsibility roles in international institutional bodies.
Access to Accounting Professions (Chartered Accountant, Company Auditor)
The Master's Degree in International Accounting and Management prepares Master's graduates for the functions of Chartered Accountant and Legal Auditor of Accounts.
Additional Information.
Course Website Course Description of Specific Educational Objectives.
The Master's Degree in International Accounting and Management (IAMA) aims to provide advanced training in the field of corporate governance and management, with particular reference to economic-managerial dynamics in the international context. In particular, the course, integrating and deepening the themes and knowledge already acquired in undergraduate studies, aims to equip students with the necessary theoretical-practical competencies to work in business realities and organizations (public or private) operating at both national and international levels. Special attention is given to the tools useful for understanding the specificities and challenges faced by businesses and institutions undergoing or planning internationalization processes: analysis of different economic, cultural, and social contexts, integration of different legal and regulatory frameworks, market expansion, and localization of production, adherence to international accounting principles.
The international character of the course thus provides students with a high qualification essential to respond to the challenges posed by globalization processes to businesses and organizations operating in supranational economic contexts. The interdisciplinary training provided will enable them to qualify for roles typical in different business functions operating at both local and global scales (management, administration, finance and control, marketing, legal areas), affecting both small and medium-sized enterprises and multinational organizations.
The course also aims to foster the development of so-called soft skills (e.g., analysis and synthesis, critical thinking, problem solving, team working, leadership, negotiation, collaboration, communication, initiative, proactivity, organization, time and priority management, decision-making, stress tolerance, self-efficacy, autonomy, entrepreneurship), which are increasingly necessary, if not indispensable, for effective corporate governance. To this end, active teaching methodologies are prioritized—relying also (but not exclusively) on advanced technological solutions for teaching—which are:
- Learner-centered
- Problem-based
- Experience-based
- Participative and cooperative
The educational path is structured into courses referring to the typical disciplinary groupings of corporate governance and management, presented from an international perspective:
1) Business (SECS-P/07, -P/08, -P/09): Courses focus primarily on management, planning, control, and reporting of businesses (public and private) with particular reference to the formulation and implementation of strategies in an international context.
2) Economic (SECS-P/01): Includes courses that deepen the characteristics and specifics of different capitalist systems worldwide, address relevant microeconomic dynamics for business management, and examine the economic implications of sustainable development and industrial organization.
3) Legal (IUS/04, /05, /06, /12, /14): Includes courses aimed at deepening relevant international legal issues. Within the courses, particular attention is given to comparative analysis of national/international regulatory systems, international taxation, and the discipline of competition applicable to businesses and states within the European Union context.
4) Statistical-Mathematical (SECS-S/03): Includes training aimed at preparing students to effectively interpret data bases and use statistical, probability, and sampling concepts in business decision-making.
To provide comprehensive competencies in the study area, student training is integrated with in-depth knowledge and skills in communication and business design, as well as specific economic and legal topics. In this way, students will understand how the acquired knowledge can be applied in different economic, legal, and social contexts.

Final examination characteristics The final examination for the Master's degree in Genetic Counsellors, worth 12 CFU, consists of the preparation of an original thesis by the student under the supervision of a supervisor. The thesis is the result of the studies and research conducted during the final year of the course.
The final examination is orally defended before a dedicated examination committee that assesses the merit score based on the following criteria: originality of the topic, written and oral presentation skills, research methodology. The final degree examination grade is expressed on a scale of 110 with possible honours.

Additionally, possession of an English language certification at B2 level of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR) is required.

Verification methods will be detailed in the teaching regulations of the Master's degree course.
Knowledge and understanding.
Human Genetics - Human Genetics The Master's graduate in Genetic Counselling must possess knowledge of human, medical and laboratory genetics. Therefore, it is necessary to acquire basic knowledge: i) of human genetics, ii) of molecular biology, iii) of the molecular mechanisms responsible for pathology, iv) of the available techniques for their identification, including the latest generation technologies; v) of typical and atypical inheritance patterns, vi) of how to calculate the probabilities of disease occurrence in individuals and offspring. Knowledge and understanding are acquired through lectures and curricular internship activities and are verified through ongoing tests and final exams in each specific sector and during practical activities.
Clinical Genetics - Clinical Genetics The Master's graduate in Genetic Counselling must possess i) in-depth knowledge of major syndromic and non-syndromic pathologies in various medical fields, including fetal pathology, ii) of the technologies available for conducting genetic tests, both traditional and latest-generation, iii) of currently available therapeutic approaches and those in development for the most common and less-well-known pathologies. Knowledge and understanding are acquired through lectures and curricular internship activities and are verified through ongoing tests and final exams in each specific sector and during practical activities.
Genetic Counseling - Genetic Counseling The Master's graduate in Genetic Counselling must know: i) the foundations of human psychology related and unrelated to pathological conditions, ii) the main psychological aspects that may arise from the diagnosis or risk of recurrence of a genetic disease, iii) the necessary approaches to interact with the patient and family, iv) the legal aspects that may be related to genetic counselling. These skills are acquired through theoretical and practical study of all aspects of clinical and medical genetics, psychology, communication, and legislation. Lectures in counselling techniques and curricular practical internships represent the occasion to verify the acquired knowledge and the ability to explain and apply such knowledge.

Judgment Autonomy.
The in-depth knowledge of genetics, medical genetics, and laboratory science enables the Master's degree graduate in Genetic Counsellors to independently judge the appropriate approach in each specific genetic counselling case. The ability to judge specific cases is acquired during front-line teaching activities in each characteristic field and during practical activities conducting genetic counselling. The judgment autonomy of graduates is verified through in-course assessments and final exams for each specific field, as well as during the practical activity of conducting genetic counselling. Judgment autonomy is particularly assessed in the final examination, which verifies the transversal competencies acquired by the graduate.
Learning Ability.
The Master's degree graduate in Genetic Counsellors is able to acquire, understand, and process scientific data, both from literature and gathered in the context of genetic counselling across various possible settings. They know the legislation governing the practice of counselling in European countries and are aware of the recognized ethical principles in countries where they practice. Such knowledge is acquired during the study path through front-line teaching activities and the practical activity.
Learning ability is verified through in-course assessments and final exams for each specific field, as well as during the practical activity of conducting genetic counselling.
Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Human Genetics - Human Genetics The Master's degree graduate in genetic counsellors is able to recognize inheritance patterns in various genetic counselling areas. They can calculate the risks of onset or recurrence of disease in the individual and in the family.
Such knowledge enables the Master's degree graduate in genetic counselling to work alongside the geneticist in the main areas of genetic counselling and to conduct genetic counselling autonomously for cases that do not require a clinical evaluation and/or clinical diagnosis for the patient.
English version:
The Master's degree graduate in genetic counselling is able to recognize inheritance patterns in various genetic counselling areas. They can calculate the risks of onset or recurrence of diseases in the individual and in the family. Such knowledge allows the Master's degree graduate in genetic counselling to work alongside the geneticist in the main areas of genetic counselling and to carry out autonomously genetic counselling for cases that do not require a clinical evaluation and/or clinical diagnosis for the patient.
Clinical Genetics - Clinical Genetics The Master's degree graduate in Genetic Counsellors is able to: i) adopt the correct approach to genetic counselling in various medical fields including the prenatal field; ii) understand and interpret genetic tests performed with both conventional and latest-generation technologies; iii) inform individuals and families with genetic diseases regarding established or experimental therapeutic approaches for an increasing number of genetic pathologies.
English version:
The Master's degree graduate in Genetic Counselling is able to: i) use the correct approach for genetic counselling in various medical fields, including the prenatal field, ii) understand and interpret genetic tests carried out with both conventional and latest-generation technologies, iii) inform individuals and families with genetic diseases about already consolidated or experimental therapeutic approaches for an increasing number of genetic pathologies.
Genetic Counseling - Genetic Counseling The Master's degree graduate in Genetic Counsellors is able to: i) conduct genetic counselling autonomously for cases that do not require a clinical evaluation and/or clinical diagnosis for the patient, in various medical fields such as prenatal, preconceptional, pediatric, and adult fields.
ii) work in teams and particularly support the geneticist in every aspect of genetic counselling, iii) provide necessary support to patients and families, iv) assist patients and families throughout the entire genetic counselling process.
English version:
The Master's degree graduate in Genetic Counselling is able to: i) carry out genetic counselling autonomously for cases that do not require a clinical evaluation and/or clinical diagnosis for the patient, in various medical fields, such as the prenatal, preconceptional, pediatric, and adult fields. ii) work in teams and particularly support the geneticist in every aspect of the counselling, iii) guarantee the necessary support to patients and families, iv) assist patients and family through the whole consultation process.

Communication Skills.
During the study path, the master's graduate in Genetic Counsellors acquires the ability to interact with the patient and family, to communicate with them during the conduct of a genetic counselling session, to mediate the patient/doctor relationship, as well as to manage the counsellor/patient relationship and patient/diagnosis relationship through the acquisition of the fundamental principles of psychology and sociology. These skills are acquired through frontal lessons in specific fields and through the practical activity of conducting and managing genetic counselling sessions. The described skills are verified through ongoing assessments and final exams for each specific sector, as well as during the practical activity of conducting genetic counselling sessions, particularly during the final assessment.
Planned occupational and professional outcomes for graduates.
Genetic Counselling Assistants The master's graduate in Genetic Counsellors has professional opportunities in both private and public entities offering genetic counselling services.
Official teaching and assessment languages.
ENGLISH Associated competencies.
Genetic Counselling Assistants To perform the above-described functions, the master's graduate in Genetic Counsellors must have acquired knowledge of genetics, medical genetics, and laboratory genetics. It is also necessary that they can independently conduct and manage a genetic counselling session by applying the main psychosocial methodologies when interacting with the patient, and therefore have developed empathy towards the patient.
Function in work context.
Genetic Counselling Assistants The master's graduate in Genetic Counsellors has acquired the competencies to support the medical geneticist in the main areas of genetic counselling and to independently conduct genetic counselling sessions for which no clinical assessment of the patient and/or clinical diagnosis is required, such as prenatal, preconception, and infertility genetic counselling, as well as oncological genetic counselling.
Description of specific learning objectives.
The Master's Degree Course in Genetic Counsellors LM-9 aims to develop the knowledge and skills necessary for non-medical health professionals to perform the role of counsellor within clinical genetics structures, where clinical geneticists with a master's degree in medicine and surgery and specialization in medical genetics operate, in both public and private settings.
The training path addresses the principles of genetics and medical genetics, which will be developed primarily in the first year of study. Already from the first year, the basics of legislative aspects impacting new knowledge of the human genome and its interpretation will be introduced. All areas of genetic counselling implementation will be addressed (e.g., prenatal, preconception, pediatric, adult, etc.), covering the most up-to-date diagnostic and therapeutic aspects currently available for genetic diseases. Once the knowledge of human and medical genetics is acquired, during the second year the student will acquire the basics of counselling techniques, especially considering the psychological implications of a genetic disease diagnosis for the individual and family. The entire training path will be structured using the expertise of qualified Italian and foreign experts.
Among the course objectives are: acquisition of the principles and practices of genetics (BIO/18), medical genetics, and laboratory genetics (MED/03); deepening of the psychosocial aspects of genetics (M-PSI/01), relational abilities (being), and competencies in conducting genetic counselling (doing) (MED/03); acquisition of communication techniques useful for conducting genetic counselling (MED/03 and M-PSI/01).
Throughout the Master's Degree training path, theoretical teachings find application and verification in the practical curriculum internship activities, which are fundamental for preparation to practice the profession of genetic counsellor (BIO/18 and MED/03). In particular, practical activity in counselling sessions becomes the primary commitment of the student, with the aim of developing decision-making ability, operational autonomy, management skills, and relationship skills with patients. Special attention is given to teamwork and multidisciplinary work, as well as to the deepening of good clinical practices in Medical Genetics (MED/03, MED/06, MED/26, MED/40).
At the end of the study course, the participant must be able to support the medical geneticist in the main areas of genetic counselling and independently conduct genetic counselling sessions for which no clinical assessment of the patient and/or clinical diagnosis is required. These include prenatal genetic counselling, preconception and infertility genetic counselling, and oncological genetic counselling.
Finally, the thesis elaboration assesses the students' aptitude for conducting bibliographic research and experimental and clinical activities.

Final Exam Characteristics The final exam consists of a discussion, before a designated graduation committee, of a thesis developed in an original manner under the guidance of a supervisor. It must verify that the master's graduate has acquired advanced knowledge of various aspects of finance, relevant both theoretically and professionally, enabling them to develop or apply original ideas through systematic and critically aware understanding; that they have the ability to apply acquired knowledge and solve problems on innovative topics, even within an interdisciplinary context; and that they have the ability to clearly present and argue in written and oral form. The thesis must be written and presented in English.
The merit score attributed to the final exam will take into account, in particular, the level of theoretical depth, the candidate's demonstrated ability to use appropriate quantitative methodologies for the research objective, the effectiveness of the empirical analyses conducted, the originality of the proposed arguments, and the effectiveness of the discussion. The merit score attributed to the final exam contributes to the formation of the final degree grade together with the average of the course exams, according to criteria defined by a specific Regulation. The degree grade is expressed on a scale of 110. If the sum of the merit score attributed to the final exam and the average grade of the course exams exceeds 110/110, upon the supervisor's proposal, the graduation committee may unanimously award the highest distinction.

Course website Study course description Specific educational objectives.
The Master's degree in Finance - Finance is a two-year Master's program dedicated to finance in its various aspects: quantitative, managerial, and economic. The program deepens the main theoretical and technical aspects commonly adopted in financial institutions and markets. It is designed for students who have completed a first-level degree (or equivalent) in economics and subjects capable of providing the necessary initial quantitative and financial competencies.
An additional objective is to activate the process of acquiring English knowledge to eliminate linguistic barriers frequently encountered in finance by graduates. For this reason, an English language course specifically calibrated to deepen technical language has been included among the 'other' training activities.
Students are also offered a course characterized by wide flexibility to adapt the academic path to students' educational needs and to the different professions the course targets.
Specifically, the Master's degree in Finance - Finance aims to:
• Provide quantitative (mathematical-statistical) knowledge that forms the basis of financial process analysis.
• Deepen economic issues most closely related to market functioning (moral hazard, adverse selection, monetary economics, international economics, behavioral economics, sustainable development economics, and emerging markets).
• Deepen market topics, portfolio management, derivative instruments, behavioral finance, market efficiency, corporate finance.
• Develop competencies in using calculation tools and econometric techniques to identify financial market trends and evaluate credits and financial portfolios.
In this sense, the core of the course is substantially equally divided into three study areas:
a) Quantitative area: Courses primarily draw from SSD SECS-S/06 to deepen methodologies applied in finance for the valuation of financial assets and analysis of return volatility.
b) Economic area: Courses from SSD SECS-P/01 and SECS-P/02 are provided to analyze the foundations of financial microeconomics (information asymmetries, game theory, contract theory) and international macroeconomics and monetary policy (central bank behavior and analysis of major economic policy choices). An econometrics course (SSD SECS-P/05) has been added, considered necessary to provide basic knowledge of quantitative modeling applied to the economic context and the function of financial market analysis, enabling correct interpretation of actors' expectations.
c) Business area: Core courses are equally distributed between SSD SECS-P/09 and SECS-P/11 to analyze financial knowledge from both market and fund-seeking enterprise perspectives.
To these areas is added c) Legal area: The core includes the fundamental contribution of analyzing the regulatory and normative context of markets with an international focus, provided by the SSD IUS/05 course.
Among the 'other' training activities, two courses are provided with the aim of delivering fundamental computer methods and knowledge, which are instrumental to other courses.
Additionally, a sufficiently large number of related and complementary courses are offered, from which students must choose three for a total of 18 CFU, to integrate their preparation with in-depth studies in their preferred direction:
- For the quantitative area, SSD SECS-S/06, SECS-S/01, and SECS-S/03 are provided, allowing students to integrate their preparation in advanced financial modeling, statistical methodology, and economic statistics applied to finance.
- For the economic area, SSD SECS-P/01, SECS-P/02, SECS-P/03, and SECS-P/05 are provided, enabling students to integrate their preparation with topics in sustainable development economics, public finance, and advanced financial econometrics.
- For the business area, courses from SSD SECS-P/07, SECS-P/09, and SECS-P/11 are provided, allowing integration with topics in international accounting, corporate treasury management, portfolio management, financial engineering, management of insurance finance instruments, management of alternative assets, and interest rate derivative management.
- For the legal area, SSD IUS/12 is provided to integrate preparation with knowledge of international comparative tax law.
Annually, depending on student interest, the related and complementary courses to be activated will be determined.

Admission requirements There are two possible access methods to the Master's Degree: direct access (based on curriculum) or through an admission test. It is not possible to enroll with academic deficiencies at entry.
Direct access is allowed to students who meet both of the following conditions: 1. Curricular requirements; 2. Minimum quality requirements, consisting of a graduation grade not lower than 95/110, or a weighted average not lower than 26/30 in courses corresponding to at least 40 ECTS in specific Scientific-Disciplinary Areas (SSD).
Curricular requirements. A degree in one of the following classes is required: - L-7 Civil and Environmental Engineering (8) - L-8 Information Engineering (9) - L-9 Industrial Engineering (10) - L-18 Economics and Business Management (17) - L-30 Physics and Technology (25) - L-31 Computer Science and Technology (26) - L-33 Economics (28) - L-35 Mathematics (32) - L-41 Statistics (37 Statistical Sciences) or an equivalent class according to former D.M. 509/99 (the equivalent class number is listed in parentheses, along with the name if different).
Curricular requirements are also satisfied by holders of a specialist degree under former D.M. 509/99 or a degree under the previous D.M. 509/99, in engineering, mathematical, and physical disciplines, subject to evaluation by the Academic Committee regarding the appropriate differentiation of educational objectives of such study paths compared to the Master's Degree in Computer and Automation Engineering.
For students holding a degree from a foreign university, curricular requirements are assessed by the Academic Committee, which particularly verifies: - that the degree is awarded after a study course of at least three years; - that the educational objectives are sufficiently congruent with those of one of the above-mentioned degree classes; - that the grade reported in the study course is adequate.
The knowledge required for access to the Master's Degree course is that of the basic and characteristic SSDs of the Information Engineering (L-8) degree class, concerning the disciplinary fields of mathematics, statistics, physics, and automation, computer, electronic, and telecommunications engineering. Additionally, English language knowledge at least at B1 level of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages is required.
Minimum quality requirements. The 40 ECTS with the best grades related to training activities in the basic and characteristic SSDs for class L-8 are considered, as listed below.
Basic Activities (SSD)
ING-INF/05 Information Processing Systems, MAT/02 Algebra, MAT/03 Geometry, MAT/05 Mathematical Analysis, MAT/09 Operations Research, FIS/01 Experimental Physics, FIS/03 Physics of Matter
Characteristic Activities (SSD)
ING-INF/01 Electronics, ING-INF/03 Telecommunications, ING-INF/04 Automation, ING-INF/05 Information Processing Systems, ING-IND/16 Manufacturing Technologies and Systems, ING-IND/17 Mechanical Industrial Plants, ING-IND/35 Economic and Management Engineering
For students who do not meet the minimum quality requirements, the following cases apply:
- Students who meet curricular requirements but not minimum quality requirements must take the admission test.
- Students who do not meet curricular requirements may take the admission test only if they have achieved a graduation grade of at least 100/110 and their study curriculum includes at least 36 ECTS in basic SSDs and 45 ECTS in characteristic SSDs, as listed above.
- Students who do not fall under the previous cases cannot be admitted to the Master's Degree courses.
For students holding a specialist degree under former D.M. 509/99, a degree under the previous D.M. 509/99, or a degree from a foreign university, the assessment of minimum quality requirements will be evaluated case by case by the Academic Committee.
The admission test is conducted orally. Graduating students who request pre-enrollment in the Master's Degree are also eligible to take the test. Typically, two admission tests are held each year, one in October and one in December.
Professional status conferred by the title.
Responsible for managing complex projects and systems The Master's graduate in Engineering Management naturally finds placement within companies, public bodies, and research centers, at national or international levels, in managerial roles focused on defining overall strategic decisions.
The Study Program also allows for autonomous professional activity as a consultant. The Master's graduate in Engineering Management may take the necessary exams to join the Order of Engineers, in the Information Engineering and Industrial Engineering sections (senior).
Final exam characteristics The final exam requires the preparation and discussion of a thesis (Master's thesis), developed by the student in an original manner under the guidance of a supervisor, possibly assisted by one or more co-supervisors.
The Master's thesis can be compilative or theoretical-experimental. In any case, the final exam aims to highlight the student's acquired abilities for studying, understanding, critically evaluating, and designing advanced and original solutions in the scientific/technological field. Skills in synthesis, scientific rigor, and organization in drafting and presenting the work orally at the end of the study program will also be assessed.
For a theoretical-experimental thesis, the Academic Committee appoints a counter-supervisor, whose task is to evaluate the original contribution of the candidate and the organization of the work.
The Master's thesis can be written in English, Italian, or an official EU language.
It is possible to carry out part of the final exam activities within an internship or traineeship at companies, organizations, or research laboratories.

L-7 Civil and Environmental Engineering (8)

along with having earned a minimum number of ECTS, as defined in the Study Program's Academic Regulations, in each of the following groups of Scientific-Disciplinary Areas:
Group A: MAT/xx, FIS/01, FIS/03, SECS-S/01, SECS-S/02, SECS-S/03, SECS-S/06
Group B: ING-INF/xx, INF/01, ING-IND/09, ING-IND/13, ING-IND/16, ING-IND/17, ING-IND/31, ING-IND/32, ING-IND/35, SECS-P/07, SECS-P/08

Degree conferred.
Master of Science in Engineering Management Teaching delivery method Conventional
Knowledge and understanding.
Area of quantitative methodologies for analysis and decision-making The Master's graduate in Engineering Management knows formal methods to support decision-making in real situations. Starting from the basic modeling culture acquired in the first-level studies, they learn to understand which approach is most appropriate in various decision-making contexts, depending on the strategic level of the decision, as well as the available information, time, and computational resources.
Acquisition of knowledge and understanding is verified through written and/or oral exams.
Technological area The Master's graduate in Engineering Management deepens knowledge of information technology aspects most related to management issues. To this end, ample space is given to methodologies for representing and evaluating complex systems, computer tools for business management, and the development of innovative technologies in various fields.
Acquisition of knowledge and understanding is verified through written and/or oral exams.
Economic-management area The Master's graduate in Engineering Management acquires fundamental knowledge in business management and industrial economics through the study of specific business functions and processes such as marketing, innovation management, and project management.
Acquisition of knowledge and understanding is verified through written and/or oral exams.
Transversal skills Knowledge of business realities in the field of management engineering, with particular reference to their specificities and issues. Advanced English language knowledge.
Verification is represented by the internship, additional activities useful for entering the job market, and the final exam. The final exam allows evaluation of the knowledge and skills acquired by the student, possibly in a business context.

CURRICULUM: Autonomy of judgment
SECTION: Autonomy of judgment
URL: https://unisi.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10892

Autonomy of judgment.
The Master of Engineering Management must develop the ability to form judgments based on limited or incomplete information, anticipating the broad implications of their choices and including reflection on the social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge. Additionally, they must be able to address engineering problems requiring an interdisciplinary approach, such as, in particular, the technical-economic feasibility assessments of projects, the reorganization of processes and departments, and the making of complex decisions regarding research and development programs.
This autonomy of judgment is developed through the application of theoretical and methodological aspects within the various courses. The development of critical awareness is fostered by the completion of projects assigned as partial or final exam assessments and by the preparation of the thesis, in which the student must demonstrate having acquired autonomy and the ability to identify and propose innovative solutions. The verification of the acquisition of an adequate judgment capacity is therefore carried out through the evaluation of the developed projects and the thesis discussion.

Learning ability.
The Master of Engineering Management must develop their own learning ability in order to continue studying and updating themselves, in order to effectively carry out the specific role of liaison and coordination. To this end, they must develop a broad vision of the reference methodological and technical landscape to address new problems of increasing complexity. Many courses, and in particular the thesis work, require personal in-depth study in order to provide the ability to search for and select relevant literature and to study and learn state-of-the-art solutions. The division of the total working hours required for the student places strong emphasis on personal working hours to offer the student the opportunity to verify and improve their learning ability. Other useful tools for achieving this skill are internships, carried out both in Italy and abroad. The verification of achieving an adequate learning ability is conducted in exam assessments requiring personal in-depth study, in the activities carried out during the internship, and in the results achieved in thesis preparation.

Ability to apply knowledge and understanding.
Quantitative methodologies area for analysis and decision-making: The Master of Engineering Management is able to:
Identify crucial variables and parameters for the analysis and management of real problems. Such problems are typically very complex and require multidisciplinary training and a preliminary holistic approach to the effective resolution of problems. Develop and apply mathematical modeling to formulate and propose efficient choices for design, planning, control, and management of individual processes within organizations. Design and use advanced decision support methods, also with the aid of computer tools, for solving complex problems related to product and process development, management of material and information flows, and human resources in companies.
The degree of acquisition of the above-mentioned abilities is verified in passing exams through the resolution of exercises and problems assigned during written, oral and/or practical tests.

Technological area: The Master of Engineering Management is able to:
Adequately map business processes to facilitate the effective implementation of innovative technologies (such as information systems and robotic systems).
Integrate tools from management engineering with innovative technologies typical of the information engineering sector; they are also able to evaluate ex post the effectiveness of such innovative technologies in the business context.
Support the development of new products through appropriate preliminary market analyses, rapid prototyping techniques, and product valorization.
The degree of acquisition of the above-mentioned abilities is verified in passing exams through the resolution of exercises and problems assigned during written, oral and/or practical tests.

Economic-management area: The Master of Engineering Management is able to:
Manage crucial business functions, such as marketing, logistics, and management of innovative processes.
Coordinate work groups and master internal and external communication techniques, enabling the addressing and resolution of coordination and performance evaluation problems within organizations.
Define and analyze the specifications of a business process in its organizational, economic, and technological components.
The degree of acquisition of the above-mentioned abilities is verified in passing exams through the resolution of exercises and problems assigned during written, oral and/or practical tests.

Transversal competencies: Apply the knowledge and methodologies studied to engineering problems in real application contexts. Use of English, with specific reference to the scientific and technological field, to understand and describe engineering problems. Interact with scholars from other fields for the use of research results in application contexts.
Verification is represented by the internship, additional activities useful for entering the job market, and the final exam. The latter, which can also be carried out at business entities, allows for the evaluation, through the presentation and discussion of a theoretical/application-oriented report, of the student's ability to use the knowledge acquired overall.

Communication skills.
The Master's degree in Engineering Management must be able to use their interdisciplinary preparation to dialogue and communicate their ideas to a wide range of professional figures, often very different from each other, using an appropriate and rigorous presentation style. This skill is particularly important for the Management Engineer (compared to more traditional engineering figures) due to the key role they play in managing and coordinating complex projects, processes, and systems.
Communication skills are acquired both through the drafting of technical documents and presentations for specific projects, and through an adequate introduction to the technical language used in the sector's scientific literature. The course being entirely taught in English allows students to directly acquire greater familiarity with the reference technical language at an international level. Additionally, the final exam provides students with an opportunity to deepen and verify their analytical, processing, and communication skills regarding the work performed. It involves discussing, before a committee, a student-produced document on a thematic area covered during their studies. In this case, evaluation is not only on the document's content but also on the candidate's synthesis, communication, and presentation abilities, as well as the justification, even dialectical, of the choices made. The achievement of an adequate level of communication skills is therefore assessed in oral exams, in the evaluation of technical reports for projects completed, and in the writing and presentation of the thesis.
Expected career and professional opportunities for graduates.
Managers of complex projects and systems The Master's graduate in Engineering Management naturally fits within companies, public bodies, and research centers, at national or international levels, in managerial roles directly responsible for defining overall strategic choices.
The Study Course also allows for autonomous professional activities as a consultant. The Master's graduate in Engineering Management can take the necessary exams to join the Order of Engineers, in the Information Engineering and Industrial Engineering (senior) sections.
Official teaching and assessment language(s).
INGLESE Associated competencies.
Managers of complex projects and systems The Master's Degree in Engineering Management aims to train a high-level professional figure with competencies typically related to: innovation and production development; planning and programming; management of complex processes and systems; project coordination; analysis of investment and financing decisions; management and organization of logistics; design and reengineering of business processes; configuration of integrated information and communication systems; development of models, systems, and applications supporting decisions; design of systems and procedures for organizational interaction between companies and between them and buyers of goods and services; reorganization of business processes; strategic planning and management control; operational management of complex projects; industrial marketing and services; management of facilities from an energy-environmental perspective.
Work context role.
Managers of complex projects and systems The Master's graduate in Engineering Management can carry out research and development activities in the management and design of complex systems and processes in business contexts of small, medium, and large size, using advanced techniques for decision support. They may hold coordination roles in research and development projects involving experts from other fields and on an international scale. They can perform activities in various application contexts, dealing with aspects ranging from the analysis and modeling of problems and processes, to the selection and evaluation of solutions to be implemented, to the management, programming, and optimization of resources and assets, up to the search for innovative solutions and the creation of high-technology companies.
Additional information.
http://www.unisi.it/dipartimenti/dipartimento-ingegneria-dell%E2%80%99informazione-e-scienze-matematiche Specific educational objectives description.
The Study Course aims to train engineers capable of combining technical and managerial knowledge to guide specialist groups in contexts such as product and process development, material flow management, and human resource management. Master's graduates in Engineering Management are also required to have communication skills enabling them to interact with colleagues having different competencies and responsibilities. The management engineer must be able to use their competencies also in an international context.
These educational objectives are concretized in a study path characterized by the following main thematic areas.
Quantitative methodologies area for analysis and decisions Mathematical modeling and techniques for formulating and proposing efficient choices for design, planning, control, and management of individual processes are deepened.
Technological area In this area, technological themes most relevant to management engineering are deepened, particularly addressing issues related to the management of productive resources in the energy and environmental context, modeling of complex systems, management information technology, methodological tools and systems for healthcare services, rapid prototyping, and new trends in human-centered robotics.
Economic-management area In the economic-management area, methodologies and tools related to business functions such as marketing, logistics, management of innovative processes and work groups, communication techniques, are deepened, to acquire familiarity with coordination issues within organizations and performance evaluation techniques.
Cross-cutting competencies The student's preparation is completed with technical-practical competencies that can be acquired through internships or traineeships at sector organizations or companies, both in Italy and abroad. The course being taught in English allows students to master the sector's scientific terminology in an international context. Finally, the final exam enables students to apply the acquired knowledge by independently designing an advanced technological solution.
