Program, Texts, and Objectives Professional status conferred by the title.
Research, design, development, production, and management in the field of information processing and transmission systems and in the design of electronic devices and systems. The Master's graduate in Electronics and Communications Engineering naturally fits within industries, companies, organizations, and research centers where research and development, design, production, and management of information processing and transmission systems, fixed and mobile telecommunications networks, and complex electronic systems are present. Graduates also possess the necessary engineering skills to initiate autonomous professional activities and establish high-technology enterprises. The study program offered in Siena is characterized by content aimed at training a Master's graduate with applicable skills in telecommunications, electronics, biomedical, security, automotive, energy, cultural heritage conservation and enjoyment, entertainment, home automation, and industrial automation applications. Master's graduates may access the Order of Engineers, Information Engineering sector, section A.
Final Exam Characteristics The final exam requires the preparation and defense of a thesis (Master's Thesis), prepared by the student in an original manner under the guidance of a supervisor, possibly assisted by one or more co-supervisors.
The Master's Thesis can be compilative or theoretical-experimental. In any case, the final exam aims to highlight the student's acquired abilities for studying, understanding, critically evaluating, and designing advanced and original solutions in the scientific/technological field. The ability to synthesize, scientific rigor, and organization in drafting the thesis and presenting the work orally at the end of the study program will also be assessed. For a theoretical-experimental thesis, the Academic Committee appoints a counter-supervisor, whose task is to evaluate the original contribution of the candidate and the organization of the thesis.
The Master's Thesis can be written in English, Italian, or an official EU language. It is possible to carry out part of the final exam activities within an internship or traineeship at companies, organizations, or research laboratories.
Access Requirements for Entry Entry to the study program is reserved for holders of a three-year university degree or equivalent foreign degree recognized as suitable. Entry requires candidates to meet curricular and personal preparation requirements. No entry with academic debt is permitted.
Curricular Requirements A First Cycle Degree in one of the following classes or an equivalent class according to former D.M. 509/99 (the equivalent class number is indicated in parentheses, along with the name if different):
- L-7 Civil and Environmental Engineering (8)
- L-8 Information Engineering (9)
- L-9 Industrial Engineering (10)
- L-30 Physics and Technology (25)
- L-31 Computer Science and Technology (26)
- L-35 Mathematics (32)
- L-41 Statistics (37 Statistical Sciences)
Holders of a Specialist Degree under former D.M. 509/99 or a degree under the previous D.M. 509/99 system in engineering, mathematics, or physics disciplines also meet the curricular requirements, subject to the Academic Committee's assessment of an appropriate differentiation of the educational objectives of such study paths compared to the Master's program.
For students holding a foreign degree, the Academic Committee assesses whether the degree:
- Is awarded after a study program of at least three years;
- Has educational objectives sufficiently aligned with those of one of the above-mentioned degree classes.
English language proficiency at least B2 level of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages is required. Non-Italian native speakers who do not reach at least A1 level of Italian language proficiency must include activities in their study plan to achieve this level.
Personal Preparation Requirements Admission to the Study Program, for students meeting curricular requirements, is subject to verification of personal preparation, according to the procedures defined in the Study Program Academic Regulations. The verification concerns knowledge in mathematics, statistics, physics, and information engineering fields. For students holding a Specialist Degree under former D.M. 509/99 or a degree under the previous D.M. 509/99 system, the Academic Committee will assess personal preparation on a case-by-case basis.
For students holding a foreign degree, the Academic Committee conducts a selection involving evaluation of personal preparation based on the study curriculum and a written and/or oral admission test.
Knowledge and Understanding.
Scientific and Methodological Deepening.
Deepening of mathematical/scientific tools necessary for comprehensive understanding of the subjects, modeling and solving problems in complex systems, and analysis and design of advanced technological systems. Deepening of analytical tools provided by information theory and digital communications theory. Acquisition of knowledge and understanding is verified through written and/or oral exams.
Information Processing and Transmission Systems.
Knowledge of digital coding and transmission techniques.
Knowledge of the operating mechanisms and analysis methodologies of fixed and mobile telecommunications networks.
Deepening of knowledge on architectures, network protocols, and network management.
Knowledge of technological solutions used in next-generation mobile networks, including the Internet of Things.
Knowledge of advanced image and signal processing techniques.
Knowledge of solutions adopted to ensure data integrity and security in transmission and protection of multimedia information.
Acquisition of knowledge and understanding is verified through written and/or oral exams.
Electromagnetic Fields and Propagation.
Knowledge of operating mechanisms and analysis methodologies of microwave systems in waveguides and planar technology.
Understanding of design techniques for microwave systems and components and their main application scenarios.
Knowledge of operating mechanisms and analysis methodologies of wire, planar, and reflector antennas.
Understanding of antenna design techniques and their main application scenarios (Telecommunications, Space, Radar).
Knowledge of operating mechanisms and analysis methodologies of RFID tags and readers.
Understanding of RFID system design and integration techniques and their main application scenarios.
Knowledge of main electromagnetic field calculation algorithms.
Understanding of electromagnetic simulation methodologies using commercial software for analysis and design of microwave systems, antennas, and RFID systems.
Acquisition of knowledge and understanding is verified through written and/or oral exams.
Electronics and Electronic Measurements.
Knowledge of advanced design techniques for analog and digital electronic systems.
Knowledge of complex "mixed-signal" electronic systems based on programmable logic.
Knowledge of secure design techniques.
Knowledge of methodologies for analysis and evaluation of component and system reliability.
Knowledge of embedded measurement and control systems for industrial applications.
Knowledge of technological solutions for signal measurement: sensor structures, microsensors, microsystems, and interfacing techniques.
Acquisition of knowledge and understanding is verified through written and/or oral exams.
Contextual Knowledge and Final Exam.
Knowledge of business realities in the field of electronic engineering and telecommunications, including applications in energy.
Advanced English language proficiency.
Acquisition of knowledge and understanding is verified through written and/or oral exams. An additional verification is provided by the internship and the final exam, which assesses the knowledge and skills acquired by the student, preferably in a business context.

Judgment Autonomy.
The Master's graduate in Electronics and Communications Engineering must be able to perform quantitative evaluations based on the acquired methodological and technical knowledge. They must also be able to evaluate the possible effects and validity of different solutions from those used to solve known problems, or to new problems imposed by technological development. This ability will be made possible by a perfect mastery of the characteristic technical/scientific tools of the fields of competence and the habit of analyzing complex systems characterized by conflicting requirements and imperfect adherence to reference theoretical models. Fundamental means for developing independence and critical awareness will be the development of projects assigned for more applied courses and the elaboration of the final thesis, in which the student must demonstrate having acquired autonomy in choice and project capability in the most innovative technological fields, using the most advanced tools. The verification of the acquisition of an adequate judgment ability is verified in the evaluation of the developed projects and the discussion of the thesis.
Learning Ability.
The Master's graduate in Electronics and Communications Engineering must develop their own learning ability in order to continue studying and updating, to be able to operate effectively in the most diverse work environments they will encounter, even in the presence of new and previously unaddressed situations. For this reason, the Master's graduate will have a broad view of the methodological, technical, and scientific landscape to refer to for studying and addressing complex and innovative problems. In particular, many courses and especially the thesis work will require personal in-depth studies in order to provide the ability to search for and select relevant literature and to study and learn state-of-the-art solutions. The division of the total working hours planned for the student gives strong emphasis to personal working hours to offer the student the opportunity to verify and improve their learning ability. Other useful tools for achieving this ability are internships carried out both in Italy and abroad. The verification of achieving an adequate learning ability is carried out in examination tests requiring personal in-depth studies, in the activities carried out during the internship, and in the results achieved in the preparation of the thesis.
Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.

The degree of acquisition of the above-described abilities is verified in the examination through the resolution of exercises and problems assigned during written, oral, and/or practical tests.

Communication skills.
The Master's graduate in Electronics and Communications Engineering must be able to use their technical and foundational knowledge to dialogue and communicate their ideas to a wide range of professional figures, with an appropriate and rigorous style. They must also be able to interface with the research world to rigorously present problems requiring innovative solutions and transfer such solutions to the production world. This type of skill is essential for the development and coordination of complex projects. These abilities will be acquired both through the drafting of technical documents for specific projects, as well as through presentations, and through an adequate introduction to the technical language used in the scientific literature of the sector, within the context of the exams for the specific and related courses. The delivery of the course entirely in English will allow the student to directly acquire greater familiarity with the reference technical dictionary. In particular, the final exam offers the student an opportunity for in-depth study and verification of their analysis, processing, and communication skills. It involves the discussion, before a committee, of a work produced by the student on a thematic area covered during their studies. In this case, evaluation is not only on the content of the work, but also on the candidate's synthesis, communication, and presentation skills, as well as the justification, even dialectical, of the choices made. The verification of achieving an adequate level of communication skills is therefore carried out in oral exams, in the evaluation of technical reports for projects completed, and in the writing and presentation of the thesis.
Expected career and professional opportunities for graduates.
Research, design, development, production, and management in the field of information processing and transmission systems and in the sector of design of electronic devices and systems. The Master's graduate in Electronics and Communications Engineering naturally fits within industries, companies, entities, and research centers where research and development, design, production, and management activities of information processing and transmission systems, fixed and mobile telecommunications networks, and complex electronic systems are present. They also possess the necessary engineering skills to start autonomous professional activities and found high-technology enterprises. The study program offered in Siena is characterized by content aimed at training a Master's graduate with skills applicable in fields such as telecommunications, electronics, biomedical, security, automotive, energy, conservation and enjoyment of cultural heritage, entertainment, home automation, and industrial automation. Master's graduates can access the Order of Engineers, Information Engineering sector, section A.
Official language(s) of instruction and assessment.
ENGLISH Associated competencies.
Research, design, development, production, and management in the field of information processing and transmission systems and in the sector of design of electronic devices and systems. The study program allows consolidation of both cross-cutting methodological competencies for analyzing advanced technological solutions, and the aptitude for continuous updating of one's knowledge. Moreover, the study path aims to create competencies for managing innovation and technological research in the field of information processing and transmission systems and in the sector of electronic systems.
Function in work context.
Research, design, development, production, and management in the field of information processing and transmission systems and in the sector of design of electronic devices and systems. The Master's graduate in Electronics and Communications Engineering possesses the necessary engineering competencies to design, develop, produce, and manage electronic and telecommunications systems. They naturally fit within companies, entities, and research centers where design, development, production, and management activities of electronic and telecommunications systems are present, in their broadest sense. They may hold coordination roles in engineering projects involving different professional figures, even from other sectors, in an international context. They may be involved in diverse application areas, dealing with aspects ranging from problem analysis and modeling, to the choice of technologies to be used, to the design of systems based on the development of software, firmware, and hardware solutions for embedded electronics, sensor networks, digital and analog electronics, wireless, mobile, and satellite communications, antennas, digital image processing, and computer networks.
Description of specific learning objectives.
The Master's degree in Electronics and Communications Engineering aims to train a graduate with advanced skills in the field of information processing and transmission systems and in the sector of design of electronic devices and systems. To this end, the necessary competencies and methodological tools are provided to design and develop signal and image processing systems, antenna systems, microwave systems, and electronic systems and circuits.
The study program offers students the possibility to choose dedicated training paths that meet the needs of technological innovation in the workplace in application fields such as security, health, energy, and environment. The course content is structured into the following learning areas.
Information processing and transmission systems Specific competencies in the field of telecommunications engineering are provided through targeted training paths to deepen knowledge in the area of signal and image processing. In relation to this topic, the issue of security, representation, and protection of multimedia information is also addressed.
Specific competencies in the field of telecommunications engineering are provided through targeted training paths to deepen knowledge in the area of digital signal transmission and modulation, analysis, and management of networks and network protocols, even with low energy consumption. In this context, wireless technologies, mobile networks, and sensor networks are covered. In relation to this topic, the issue of security and protection of transmission content is also addressed.
Electromagnetic fields and propagation Integrated knowledge and competencies related to guided propagation and radiation of electromagnetic waves are provided. In particular, modern analysis and design techniques for microwave systems and radiating systems are deepened, with particular emphasis on applications in the field of mobile and fixed telecommunications and electronic subsystems. In the field of RFID systems, specific competencies are provided for the design, integration, and management of modern RF systems for logistics, identification, and data detection.
Electronics and electronic measurements Specific competencies are provided in the field of electronic design, design of systems based on microsensors and sensors, also leveraging technologies suitable for the application of sensor technology and embedded systems in civil and industrial contexts. Knowledge is also provided in the field of secure design and reliability of electronic systems.
Scientific and methodological deepening An adequate integration of mathematical analysis knowledge is provided, with particular reference to functional analysis and complex analysis. Knowledge is also integrated in the field of information theory to provide the necessary tools for formalizing complex problems.
Context knowledge and final exam The student's preparation is completed with technical-practical skills that can be acquired through internships or traineeships at sector entities or companies. Moreover, since advanced English language knowledge is now indispensable for the engineer's role, it is a training objective for all graduates to be able to write and speak English, with particular reference to scientific and technological topics. The final exam allows the student to apply the acquired knowledge by autonomously solving a complex technological problem.

The final exam will consist of a discussion before a graduation committee of an experimental thesis reporting the results of original research on topics consistent with the educational objectives of the proposed Master's Degree, assigned by the CD and under the supervision of one or more tutors (a faculty advisor and optionally one or more co-advisors), carried out at a scientific structure of the University of Siena or another structure (public or private entity) with a formal agreement (internship or traineeship). The Master's Thesis must have the form and structure of a genuine scientific work, with clear indication of the objectives to be achieved, the methodology applied, the results obtained, as well as their relevance within the current scientific knowledge framework. The student must demonstrate having acquired a deep understanding of the modern scientific approach, good ability to process and synthesize acquired data, as well as adequate ability to present the data in written and oral form.
Required Knowledge for Access A basic formation in mathematical, physical and chemical disciplines is required, as well as adequate knowledge in biological and ecological disciplines. The necessary curricular requirements for admission to the Master's Degree Course in Ecotoxicology and Environmental Sustainability, the minimum quantification of the corresponding CFU, as well as the methods for verifying the adequacy of personal preparation, will be specified in the Teaching Regulations of the Study Course.
Degree Awarded.
Master's Degree in ECOTOXICOLOGY AND ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY Mode of Teaching Delivery Conventional Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area The Master's Degree Course is characterized by the coexistence of two knowledge areas: Ecotoxicology and Environmental Sustainability. The two areas are perfectly complementary as they address issues related to the influence of human activity on ecosystems from two different perspectives: the more analytical perspective of Ecotoxicology and the more systemic perspective of Environmental Sustainability.
In the Master's Degree program, the student must be able to manage the information and knowledge offered by both scientific proposals in order to, upon graduation, have a complete understanding of the complexity of human-nature relationships and the skills to professionally manage the problems generated by such relationships.
To meet the specific requirements of each descriptor, the verification of knowledge and understanding capabilities will be carried out at the end of each training activity using teaching tools consistent with the theoretical and experimental issues addressed in the courses, including: critical discussion of data collected during the course, in advanced texts or reported in the most recent international scientific literature; theoretical-practical group activities, whose results will be presented autonomously both during the training activity and at the final individual assessment.
Ecotoxicological Fundamentals The specialized knowledge and understanding capabilities in various sectors of Ecotoxicology will be aimed at describing, explaining and discussing the theoretical and practical foundations of methods for acquiring, analyzing and interpreting ecotoxicological data; starting from the ability to read and understand specialized texts and scientific articles on relevant topics and problems, such knowledge and capabilities will also be useful for acquiring autonomy and originality in formulating and/or applying ideas and solutions in the field of ecotoxicology and communicating results, often in a rapidly evolving research context in line with the emergence of ever new issues related to the interaction between human activity and the natural environment.
Environmental Sustainability Fundamentals The specialized knowledge and understanding capabilities in various sectors of Environmental Sustainability will enable the identification and interpretation of the epistemological bases, bio-physical foundations, and methodologies for analysis and interpretation within the scope of environmental sustainability investigations of different systems. Such knowledge ranges from physical-based environmental accounting methods to the use of specialized instrumentation and software, and will allow acting autonomously in formulating and/or applying ideas and solutions in the field of environmental sustainability, often in a research context. This cultural development, fueled globally by the United Nations 2030 Agenda and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDG), will be supported by the ability to update through international scientific literature, making students capable of contributing to the progressive dissemination of the concept of sustainability in all fields of life.

SECTION: Judgment Autonomy

Judgment Autonomy.
Graduates of the Master's Degree Course in Ecotoxicology and Environmental Sustainability, belonging to Class LM-75, will be able to:
1) discriminate, compare, and validate information obtained through the most current ecotoxicological and environmental sustainability methodologies;
2) validate data produced or produced by third parties through the application of current methodologies;
3) formalize evaluations and opinions on specific and/or transdisciplinary issues, assuming responsibility at any level;
4) be critical based on scientific, social, ethical, and deontological grounds regarding issues of exploitation, alteration, and anthropogenic modification of natural systems;
5) design, plan, organize, manage, and coordinate, in full autonomy, any procedure related to their professional expertise or in which they are professionally involved.
Judgment autonomy is achieved following the educational process and is verified in both examination assessments and in the writing and discussion of the experimental thesis.
Learning Ability.
The Master's Degree Course in Ecotoxicology and Environmental Sustainability, belonging to Class LM-75, is structured and aimed at enabling the student, at the end of the educational path, to independently pursue studies related to Ecotoxicology and Environmental Sustainability, as well as to integrate into national and international PhD programs, where they will be able to carry out research activities in a multidisciplinary and systemic manner. These abilities are acquired through the teaching of both core and integrative courses, the execution and writing of the thesis work, and participation in research groups and seminars.
Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
General Area Graduates of the Master's Degree Course in Ecotoxicology and Environmental Sustainability, belonging to Class LM-75, will be able to professionally integrate into multidisciplinary contexts related to the study and management and maintenance of the integrity of the functional and structural properties of ecosystems and the defense of natural resources affected by anthropogenic pressure, using predictive approaches and at various spatial-temporal scales.
They will be able to independently carry out their professional activities in the field of ecotoxicology and environmental sustainability, assuming responsibility for projects, structures, and personnel coordination in:
a) public and private research institutions;
b) public institutions responsible for environmental quality control and management;
c) private institutions (companies) that view the topics addressed in the Course as an opportunity for development, beyond traditional sectors operating in the control of emissions, effluents, and residues. Among these, for example: a) production units interested in undertaking and communicating environmental performance improvement paths, identifying specific phenomena related to the production process (e.g., pollution and risks) or systemic aspects of production activities (e.g., life cycle and certifications); b) environmental consulting activities that are significantly developing as they are required to support companies in the aforementioned paths.
d) professional studies for environmental impact assessment and environmental risk analysis.
Ecotoxicological Fundamentals The Master's graduate, at advanced qualitative levels, will be able to:
1) use and develop original and innovative observation and analysis methodologies for assessing ecosystem stress;
2) apply their specialized knowledge and acquired data in multidisciplinary contexts, even in highly complex situations, such as biodiversity interventions and management, remediation and restoration of contaminated and polluted areas, remediation plans, environmental impact assessment;
3) predict, analyze, control, and manage the release of contaminants and pollutants into the environment and their effects on biotic components at various complexity scales (individual, population, community, ecosystem) and abiotic components;
4) design, plan, organize, manage, and coordinate evaluation and decision-making procedures, with in-depth analysis of pollutant transport mechanisms, interactions from molecule-organism to molecule-ecosystem, through the application of the most important predictive, analytical, and diagnostic tools;
5) design, plan, organize, analyze, control, and manage environmental hazard and risk assessment studies for natural and xenobiotic substances (risk assessor and manager) according to current regulations (e.g., REACH).
Environmental Sustainability Fundamentals Graduates of the Master's Degree Course in Ecotoxicology and Environmental Sustainability, at advanced qualitative levels, will therefore be able to:
- design, plan, organize, analyze, control, and manage environmental sustainability studies related to the exploitation of natural resources, production systems, and territorial planning;
- apply the most effective and up-to-date environmental accounting methodologies, such as energy and emergy analysis, ecological footprint, and product life cycle assessment (Life Cycle Assessment);
- identify the main factors influencing anthropogenic greenhouse effect and climate change, also through the use of specific monitoring and detection tools for emissions, internationally recognized (e.g., IPCC Guidelines for greenhouse gas inventory preparation), a prerequisite for mitigation activities as required by international agreements;
- predict, identify, analyze, control, and manage issues related to the interactions of environmental and anthropogenic factors responsible for the modification/inhibition of natural processes and ecosystem services.

Communication Skills.
Graduates of the Master's Degree in Ecotoxicology and Environmental Sustainability, belonging to Class LM-75, will be able to:
1) present and communicate with scientific criticality and clarity the data and information produced, both in specialist and transdisciplinary/non-specialist environments, also in English;
2) reasonably respect scientific data, opinions, and viewpoints of any interlocutor in any professional situation;
3) receive and exchange opinions, knowledge, and views in the course of their professional activity in any context.
These skills are acquired through oral and written reports, also using computer support, and verified during individual assessments and the presentation of the experimental Thesis.
Planned occupational and professional opportunities for graduates.
Expert in risk, impact and environmental sustainability assessment. The Master's Degree in Ecotoxicology and Environmental Sustainability is able to train graduates with theoretical and practical preparation to be integrated into various occupational realities, national and international, such as:
1) public and private research institutions;
2) public bodies responsible for environmental quality control and management, biodiversity conservation, nature and territory (e.g. Ministry of the Environment, Regional and Provincial Administrations);
3) specific agencies (e.g. ISPRA, regional and provincial agencies, CPS&Q, ECHA);
4) private companies in the sectors of emission, effluent, and residue control;
5) professional offices for environmental impact assessment, environmental risk analysis, territorial planning;
6) chemical, pharmaceutical, mining-metallurgical, steel industries, for energy production, as ecotoxicologist, LCA expert.
Occupational opportunities are expected to increase in the near future due to the approval of Regulation (EC) No 1907/2006 concerning the registration, evaluation, authorisation and restriction of chemicals (REACH) and the growing need for experts (ecotoxicologists) for managing risks arising from "industrial chemicals", natural resource management, natural systems, territorial planning, traffic management, among other examples, aspects confirmed not only by current national and/or community legislation but also by the increasing need to comply with international protocols and conventions. Master's graduates may also have further professional opportunities in higher education teaching, university level, and scientific communication and dissemination.
Regarding access to professions (DPR 328/01 of 05.06.2001, GU of 17.08.2001), the Master's Degree in Ecotoxicology and Environmental Sustainability, after passing the required state exam, allows registration in the Register of Biologists and the Register of Geologists.

- environmental quality assessment;
- planning of activities oriented towards sustainable development;
- promotion and coordination of initiatives to guide environmental policies and contribute to forming a critical and constructive consensus among citizens for solving problems posed by the territory.
- design and management of remediation, monitoring, and environmental control interventions promoted by public administration, production systems, and private subjects;
- realization and assessment of environmental impact studies, strategic environmental assessment, and environmental risk assessment, as well as safety and related activities;
- analysis and control of pollutants and management of facilities dedicated to their treatment;
- realization and certification of environmental management systems;
- dissemination of environmental culture through education and dissemination activities.

Additional information.
http://www.dsfta.unisi.it/it http://www.unisi.it Specific training objectives description.
The Master's Degree in Ecotoxicology and Environmental Sustainability arises from both cultural and training needs related to themes that are increasingly emerging as determinants for human life in the future. The main objective of the course is to provide students with in-depth knowledge in the fields of ecotoxicology and environmental sustainability and management analysis. The sustainability of human actions can be evaluated from two perspectives: the first aiming to make resources used increasingly renewable, the second aiming to minimize the environmental effects of human actions. Students must therefore follow a path starting from the study of natural cycles to the study of principles and methods for assessing the sustainability level of processes and systems. A significant role in this context is played by all ecotoxicological analyses aimed at studying the fate of various chemicals introduced into the environment and, in general, risk analysis. Students must also acquire knowledge in the direction of international environmental certifications and the REACH system. These innovative aspects find in the Master's Degree ESA a unique educational offer of high scientific value and innovative content at both national and international levels. The Master's Degree in Ecotoxicology and Environmental Sustainability, in addition to the qualifying training objectives of the Master's Degree Class in Environmental and Territorial Sciences and Technologies, which are concretized in 'possessing a systemic environmental culture and good practice of the scientific method for analyzing components and factors of processes, systems, and problems concerning the environment, both natural and modified by humans', aims to train graduates capable of performing professional activities in various sectors related to environmental risk analysis, sustainability assessment, and environmental certifications, including REACH. In particular, the cultural and professional profile of the graduate of the Master's Degree in Ecotoxicology and Environmental Sustainability must:
1) have a solid cultural preparation with a systemic approach, with particular attention to environmental chemistry, ecotoxicology, geochemistry, and contaminant analysis;
2) be able to monitor, analyze, control, and manage complex environmental realities (e.g. heavily polluted areas, remediation) by developing good mastery of various scientific monitoring and management methodologies;
3) develop the ability to evaluate and manage interactions between biotic and abiotic components of ecosystems, identifying the presence and extent of different anthropogenic impacts;
4) be able to carry out analyses of impacts related to specific substances and chemical compounds according to REACH regulations;
5) be able to understand issues related to production systems through life cycle analysis of products (Life Cycle Assessment, LCA); apply methods and techniques for sustainability assessment, such as exergetic, emergy, and ecological footprint analysis;
6) Develop and apply methodologies for environmental data management, acquiring adequate judgment autonomy and communication skills;
7) possess adequate mastery for designing, drafting, and realizing scientific reports and works, combined with written and oral mastery of at least one European Union language in addition to Italian.
The characteristic and related or integrative disciplines identified for the Master's Degree include, within individual programs, not only theoretical aspects but also practical activities in the field and in the laboratory. These activities will be conducted using specific methodologies and equipment; the subsequent analysis of observations and collected data, as well as the final elaborations and considerations, will collectively contribute to meeting the requirements of each descriptor. The didactic regulations of the study course and the educational offer will allow students who wish to follow training paths containing an adequate number of credits in related and integrative fields that are not already characteristic. For the purposes indicated, in relation to specific objectives, activities outside the university may be provided during the training path or for the experimental thesis, including at companies, public administration bodies, and laboratories, as well as study stays at other Italian and European universities, within national and international agreements.

Final exam characteristics The final exam consists of a discussion before a designated graduation committee of an original thesis developed under the guidance of a supervisor. It must verify that the Master's graduate has acquired advanced knowledge on relevant economic themes both theoretically and professionally, enabling them to develop or apply original ideas through systematic and critically aware understanding, to apply acquired knowledge and solve problems on innovative themes even in an interdisciplinary context, and to clearly present and properly argue in written and oral form. The thesis is written in English. The merit score awarded for the final exam takes into account the level of theoretical depth, the candidate's demonstrated ability to use appropriate quantitative methodologies for the research objective, the effectiveness of empirical analyses conducted, the originality of proposed arguments, and the effectiveness of the discussion before the examining committee.
Admission requirements For admission to the Master's degree in Economics, a three-year university degree or equivalent foreign degree recognized as suitable is required. The teaching regulations of the Master's program define the admission requirements for the Economics Master's degree in relation to different first-level degree classes or, for graduates in classes different from those specified, to CFU acquired in specific disciplinary sectors.
In particular, to meet the curricular requirements, a three-year degree in an economic, statistical, mathematical, or political science and international relations field is required. Specifically, referring to classes under D.M. 270/2004: L-33 Economics, L-18 Economics and Business Management, L-41 Statistics, L-35 Mathematics, L-36 Political Science and International Relations, L-37 Social Sciences for Cooperation, Development and Peace. Requirements are also met by having obtained degrees and diplomas from previous regulations considered equivalent to those indicated or foreign study titles equivalent and recognized as suitable.
Admission is also permitted with a suitable title in a different degree class, provided at least 75 CFU are held in specific disciplinary sectors of the following areas:
- Economic (SECS-P/01, SECS-P/02, SECS-P/03, SECS-P/05, SECS-P/06, SECS-P/07, SECS-P/08, SECS-P/09, SECS-P/10, SECS-P/11, SECS-P/12, M-GGR/02, AGR/01, SPS/04)
- Mathematical-Statistical (SECS-S/01, SECS-S/02, SECS-S/03, SECS-S/04, SECS-S/05, SECS-S/06, MAT/01, MAT/02, MAT/03, MAT/04, MAT/05, MAT/06, MAT/09, ING-INF/05, INF/01, CHIM/01, CHIM/12, BIO/07, ICAR/15)
- Legal-Sociological-Political (IUS/01, IUS/04, IUS/05, IUS/06, IUS/07, IUS/09, IUS/10, IUS/12, IUS/13, IUS/14, SPS/01, SPS/02, SPS/04, SPS/05, SPS/07, SPS/10, M-STO/04, M-FIL/01, M-FIL/06)
with at least 40 CFU in the first two areas (economic and mathematical-statistical).
The CFU in the specific disciplinary sectors required as curricular requirements must be held before enrollment (enrollment with academic debts is not permitted).
Admission also requires an adequate level of English language knowledge (B2 level).
For graduates with foreign study titles, the required knowledge for admission is defined by the teaching regulations of the study program based on the minimum content considered necessary for the different disciplinary areas, including those related to Italian and English language.
For admission to the study program, students meeting the required curricular qualifications must pass a selective test to verify personal preparation, the modalities of which are specified annually in the admission notice for the program.
Knowledge and understanding.
FUNDAMENTAL KNOWLEDGE AREA Master's graduates in Economics must master the knowledge necessary for conducting independent economic research. The courses taught in the first year must provide students with basic analytical tools of mathematical-statistical, economic (both microeconomic and macroeconomic), and econometric type, enabling them to navigate comfortably among various themes of economic theory and application, and to continue deepening specific themes to their most recent developments. They must also be able to critically analyze theories and identify appropriate analysis methods for solving policy problems.
SPECIALIZED ECONOMIC KNOWLEDGE AREA Students must acquire advanced knowledge, both theoretical and applied, in a variety of areas of economic discipline, enabling them to achieve as complete an understanding as possible of the functioning of the economic system, the behavior of economic actors, available policy options, and the interpretation of long-term processes.
The available courses cover macroeconomic and microeconomic topics, have both theoretical and applied character, and respond to a variety of theoretical approaches. The focus is on providing a comprehensive yet not restricted overview of a single theoretical approach.
PUBLIC POLICIES AND INSTITUTIONAL CONTEXT AREA As highlighted by consultation with representative organizations, for Master's graduates of this type of study program, it is important to acquire knowledge and skills useful for interpreting and understanding major public policies, also in their institutional and regulatory dimension.
Some of the offered courses, of both economic and legal nature, provide useful knowledge for this purpose, combining economic analysis with an understanding of concrete policy tools and the problems of implementing policy decisions.
MANAGERIAL AND FINANCIAL KNOWLEDGE AREA Master's graduates in the Economics track must have acquired knowledge regarding the functioning of financial markets and business internationalization strategies. These are complementary knowledge to strictly economic fields, aimed at completing preparation, especially for those wishing to enter the business or finance world.

Judgment autonomy.
A Master's graduate in Economics must have acquired the ability to read and analyze existing empirical studies and process data. They must be able to read and interpret empirical evidence presented in scientific articles and institutional reports, while also understanding any potential limitations. Additionally, they must be able to organize data into datasets and perform econometric-statistical analyses using appropriate software.
For these purposes, in addition to specific teachings that develop this direction, the final thesis may allow the graduate to refine their skills through in-depth studies and field experiences.
The verification of these abilities occurs through participation in presentations on assigned topics during individual courses, through passing the profit exams (normally in written form), and particularly through the evaluation of the final thesis and its discussion.

Learning ability.
A graduate of the Master's in Economics must have reached knowledge levels enabling their entry into subsequent training levels, such as Second-Level Master's programs, Italian Doctoral programs, or international PhDs, even at institutions of absolute global prominence.
These knowledge levels also qualify them for entry into the job market in the areas indicated by professional opportunities.
These abilities will primarily be acquired in courses with a higher methodological content in the economic, business-economic, and mathematical-econometric fields.
The verification of acquired abilities will primarily occur through the profit exams of individual courses and through the evaluation of the final thesis.

Ability to apply knowledge and understanding.
CORE KNOWLEDGE AREAS Fundamental knowledge: Master's graduates in Economics must have acquired a solid mathematical-statistical, economic, and econometric methodology. This methodology is the key tool enabling them to subsequently address a wide variety of economic topics from both theoretical and econometric/applied perspectives. Specifically, students must be able to apply the acquired knowledge to deepen the formal structure of economic models, organize statistical data, carry out quantitative econometric analyses, and understand the complex implications of economic decision-makers' choices. Specific attention will be given, particularly within statistical and econometric courses, to the use of specialized software packages for data management and processing (e.g., R), and a dedicated laboratory for programming techniques is also provided.
Thanks to the knowledge acquired through the training path, which alternates frontal classroom teaching with exercises and sessions in didactic laboratories (e.g., computer laboratory), they will be able to use advanced economic and econometric modeling.

SPECIALIZED ECONOMIC KNOWLEDGE: Master's graduates will be able to use theoretical modeling and econometric analysis tools to understand and analyze the micro and macroeconomic context and public policies. Following the knowledge gained in these courses, they will be able to access the understanding of articles and contributions in major specialized journals and independently conduct theoretical and empirical research on specific economic analysis topics.

PUBLIC POLICIES AND INSTITUTIONAL CONTEXT: The described knowledge is applied to the analysis of specific issues related to the implementation of public policies. This involves applying both strictly economic tools (e.g., compatibility in terms of equitable effects, constraints related to public decision-making processes) and legal knowledge. Application also occurs through in-depth study of specific policies, using case studies; methodologies include class exercises and presentations on assigned topics.

MANAGERIAL AND FINANCIAL KNOWLEDGE: The knowledge acquired in management and finance will enable an interdisciplinary understanding of specific issues related to financial markets and enterprise internationalization strategies. Master's graduates will be able to address and provide solutions to typical problems of both financial theory and practice in companies, especially in innovative contexts characterized by high internationalization.

Communication skills.
A graduate of the Master's Degree in Economics must have acquired sufficiently high professional expertise to enable them to communicate economic results to both professional audiences and non-specialist publics, knowing how to extract the insight of certain results while respecting the rigor of the argumentation.
To this end, they must be able to use English, both written and spoken. These skills will be acquired through participation in lectures, presentation of individual or group work within the courses, and writing the final thesis.
Verification of the acquisition of these skills occurs through evaluation of individual or group work presentations, through passing exams, as well as in the evaluation and discussion of the final thesis.
Planned career and professional opportunities for graduates.
Economic analyst The Economics graduate may work in government bodies and organizations, international organizations, public and private enterprises, banks and other financial institutions, sector associations, and trade unions.
Official teaching and assessment languages.
ENGLISH Associated competencies.
Economic analyst A deep understanding of economic phenomena and in particular of market functioning, the ability to coordinate microeconomic analysis with macroeconomic analysis of the economy as a whole, and the use of sophisticated quantitative analysis techniques for economic phenomena constitute the specific knowledge base of the Economics graduate. With these competencies, the Economics graduate may aspire to employment in roles of analyst and research tasks, as well as in more operational roles in complex private and public organizations, in research or strategic economic decision-making functions.
Work context function.
Economic analyst The Master's Degree course in Economics aims to train professional figures of economists capable of assuming responsible roles in multiple fields, within public and private, national and international bodies and organizations. The competencies acquired in interpreting and analyzing economic phenomena will enable Master's graduates in Economics to enter the workforce in positions requiring versatility and analytical skills, understanding the strategic aspects of decisions and their economic repercussions, and the ability to address contexts characterized by complexity and change.
Additional information.
Course website Study program description of specific educational objectives.
The educational objective of the Master's Degree in Economics is to provide advanced preparation in the field of economic disciplines. Students in this program acquire the necessary capacity and knowledge to interpret micro- and macroeconomic phenomena and processes, using both theoretical conceptual tools and advanced techniques for analyzing and interpreting economic data. Based on these knowledge and competencies, they will be able to access the most up-to-date economic scientific production, using its conclusions and results competently and rigorously to guide the strategic choices of economic operators in a context characterized by complexity and change. Their knowledge and competencies can find adequate recognition and value in enterprises, financial institutions, public and economic government institutions, in the field of consulting and research.
The preparation provided by this Master's Degree, similar in approach and level of depth to that offered by the most accredited MSc/MPhil programs in Economics, will also allow those who wish to further deepen their education through international doctoral/PhD programs.
The fact that the program requires the exclusive use of English in both courses and the final thesis writing represents an additional opportunity to familiarize with the working methods of research-oriented institutions and enterprises and organizations operating in a highly internationalized context.
While the specific focus on economic analysis and related quantitative/econometric analysis techniques distinguishes the Master's Degree in Economics from other Master's Degrees in economic fields at the University of Siena, what characterizes this degree compared to similar programs offered by other Italian universities is, on one hand, the high level of internationalization and, on the other, the emphasis on pluralism from a theoretical reference point. These are aspects that have always distinguished the scientific community of economists at the University of Siena, and the Master's Degree in Economics aims to highlight.
The training path specifically includes, during the first year:
- Acquisition of intermediate/advanced mathematical knowledge (with particular attention to linear algebra and constrained optimization techniques - s.s.d. SECS-S/06) and statistical knowledge (with particular attention to statistical inference techniques - s.s.d. SECS-S/01)
- Acquisition of knowledge and techniques for econometric analysis (s.s.d. SECS-P/05)
- Acquisition of intermediate/advanced knowledge of microeconomic and macroeconomic theory (s.s.d. SECS-P/01)
- Acquisition of tools for reading and interpreting economic public policies (s.s.d. SECS-P/03)
The first-year teaching activities are primarily aimed at consolidating the general analytical tools necessary to achieve an advanced level of knowledge in the field of economics.
The teaching activities offer various possibilities for specialization in different fields of economics, both theoretical and applied/empirical, which are completed in the preparation of the final thesis, which in this Master's Degree has primary educational value. Courses offered in the second year also include options that allow individual students to direct their training in their preferred direction. For example, the courses cover fields such as monetary economics, industrial economics, economic policy, economic history, public economics, growth economics, as well as more frontier topics such as experimental economics (s.s.d. SECS-P/01, SECS-P/02, SECS-P/03, SECS-P/12).
Economic preparation is further integrated, over the two years, by:
- Legal knowledge useful for correctly interpreting the regulatory framework within which economic activity takes place (s.s.d. IUS/04 or IUS/05)
- Knowledge in the fields of finance and management, useful for expanding the ability to interpret economic phenomena (s.s.d. SECS-P/08 and SECS-P/11)
Students also have the opportunity to further integrate their preparation, through the options offered by related-integrative activities, with knowledge from other social sciences (s.s.d. SPS/04 and SPS/09) and with knowledge regarding the most recent developments in data analysis (s.s.d. ING-INF/05)

Environmental and Economic Analyst The skills and knowledge acquired during the studies allow the master's graduate in Economics for the Environment and Sustainability to access many types of professions and employment. In particular, the master's graduate in EAS can work at: - international, national, and local entities or agencies conducting applied research and analysis in the field of environmental economics; - private and public companies with managerial, operational, and consulting functions, particularly in the planning and implementation of environmental investments and the management of scarce environmental resources (water, waste, energy); - public administrations and public, private, and non-profit enterprises with executive and advisory functions; - companies operating in the services sector (utilities), consulting, and financial statement review, particularly as social and sustainability accounting experts. Additionally, they may carry out consulting activities for the valorization of a territory's historical, cultural, and environmental heritage. Thanks to the solid economic-quantitative knowledge acquired, they are not excluded from entering the banking and financial sector, particularly in the field of ethical finance, and the research field (eventually following further specialization in a doctoral program) at universities, research centers, and agencies, national and international. Final Exam Characteristics The final exam consists of preparing a work that, in an original manner, addresses theoretical topics or conducts empirical analysis related to the study topics. The preparation work is carried out under the supervision of a supervisor and a co-supervisor and serves to verify that the master's student has acquired in-depth knowledge of relevant economic-environmental topics both theoretically and professionally, enabling them to develop or apply original ideas through systematic and critically aware understanding. The thesis is written in Italian or, at the student's request, in English. The final exam is awarded 21 ECTS credits and a maximum of 8 points, consistently with the significant role the CDS (Course of Study) assigns to the development of the student's independent research and analysis capabilities. Required Knowledge for Admission To access the Master's Degree Course in Economics for the Environment and Sustainability (EAS), it is necessary to hold a degree or a three-year university diploma or another foreign-acquired title recognized as suitable. Curricular requirements are met by holding a degree in one of the following classes of D.M. 270/2004 (or corresponding in the former D.M. 509/99) Economics Sciences L-33 (28) Economics and Business Management Sciences L-18 (17) Statistics L-41 (37) Mathematical Sciences L-35 (32) Political Sciences and International Relations L-36 (15) Social Sciences for Cooperation, Development, and Peace L-37 (35) Alternatively, a four-year degree in economics, statistics, mathematics, or political sciences and international relations from the previous curriculum is required. Additionally, possession of an English language proficiency certificate at the B1 level of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR) is required. For graduates who do not possess these requirements, the following combined curricular requirements are required: a) Hold a three-year degree under D.M. 270/2004 or D.M. 509/1999, or a four-year degree under the previous curriculum. b) Acquire at least 75 ECTS in the following SSD: Group 1 - Economic Area SECS-P/01 SECS-P/02 SECS-P/03 SECS-P/05 SECS-P/06 SECS-P/07 SECS-P/08 SECS-P/09 SECS-P/10 SECS-P/11 SECS-P/12 M-GGR/02 AGR/01 SPS/04 Group 2 - Quantitative Area SECS-S/01 SECS-S/02 SECS-S/03 SECS-S/04 SECS-S/05 SECS-S/06 MAT/01 MAT/02 MAT/03 MAT/04 MAT/05 MAT/06 MAT/09 ING-INF/05 INF/01 CHIM/01 CHIM/12 BIO/07, ICAR/15 Group 3 - Legal/Sociological/Political Area IUS/01 IUS/04 IUS/05 IUS/06 IUS/07 IUS/09 IUS/10 IUS/12 IUS/13 IUS/14 SPS/01 SPS/02 SPS/04 SPS/05 SPS/07 SPS/10 M-STO/04 M-FIL/01 M-FIL/06 of which at least 40 ECTS in Groups 1 (Economic Area) and 2 (Quantitative Area). c) Possess English language proficiency at B1 level, according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages. For graduates who obtained a degree abroad, the suitability of the curricular requirements will be assessed on a case-by-case basis by the Academic Committee, considering the consistency of the programs completed in different disciplinary areas with the foundational knowledge deemed necessary for the advanced training offered by the course of study, as well as the linguistic knowledge. For admission to the course of study, students possessing the required curricular requirements must pass an oral exam to verify personal preparation. The exam covers introductory topics in political economy (microeconomics, macroeconomics) and topics in mathematics, statistics, and econometrics. The verification is conducted by an examining committee appointed by the Department Council, upon proposal from the Academic Committee. The dates of the interviews, the detailed topics of the admission exam, and recommended textbooks for preparation are annually published on the course website. The Academic Committee, or a delegate appointed by it, may consider that graduates have passed the personal preparation verification if, considering the grades obtained and the content acquired in their previous three-year degree, they possess adequate personal preparation to successfully attend the degree course. Knowledge and Understanding. General Area The courses provided in the EAS degree program will provide students with the tools to understand and explain the evolution and functioning mechanisms of the economic system in relation to the environment and the use of environmental resources. The courses are structured to provide knowledge suitable for identifying and evaluating different tools of environmental economic policy and regulation used or to be used to address environmental challenges at the local or supralocal level. At the same time, the EAS graduate will have in-depth knowledge of the main techniques for evaluating and valuing intangible assets. For this purpose, the basic knowledge necessary to frame complex economic-environmental phenomena is provided mainly in the first year of the course, leaving the second-year training activities the task of providing the student with advanced analytical and quantitative knowledge, acquired also through project development, assignment completion, and case study analysis. The combination of courses and activities from different fields, appropriately combined, will allow the EAS student to acquire interdisciplinary knowledge, enabling a more comprehensive understanding of the problems and phenomena under study. Economic Area Students must acquire advanced knowledge in various fields of environmental economics, both theoretical and empirical-applied. Such knowledge must enable them to achieve as complete an understanding as possible of the functioning of the economic system and its interactions with social and environmental phenomena. Mathematical-Statistical Area Students must mandatory acquire adequate statistical knowledge, which, in a synergistic manner with other acquired knowledge, allows the formation of the environmental economist figure. Business Area Students must also acquire economic-business knowledge to understand environmental aspects more directly related to business management and the associated environmental and social sustainability. Legal Area To complete the knowledge framework necessary for a fruitful analysis of economic-environmental phenomena, the graduate in Economics for the Environment and Sustainability may acquire adequate knowledge of environmental law or sustainable development law.

Judgment autonomy.
A graduate of the LM in Economics for Environment and Sustainability (EAS) must have acquired the ability to read and analyze existing empirical studies and process data. They must be able to read and interpret empirical evidence presented in scientific articles and institutional reports. In particular, they must be able to correctly evaluate data relevant to the use of natural resources and the impact of such use on the environment and economy; they must be able to evaluate alternative strategies and formulate policy proposals regarding the use of environmental resources, both at the economic system level and at the enterprise level; they must be able to use qualitative information necessary to identify the determinants of sustainable development.
After acquiring a correct conceptual framework (applied analysis of urban, local, and regional economies, development economics, policies for well-being) and adequate analytical techniques (econometrics, methods for environmental valuation), the EAS graduate must be able to evaluate the local impact of economic policies. They must also be able to assess, in terms of costs and benefits, the validity of investments for improving business processes.
These abilities, in addition to being acquired within specific courses designed in this direction and through didactic laboratories, will be acquired through comparison activities and group work carried out in the various courses of the CdS, and can be enhanced through the acquisition of soft skills via attendance at dedicated modules and laboratories. Judgment autonomy can also be refined through field experiences (e.g., internships) and through work done for the preparation of the final thesis, with the supervision of an internal or external professor assisted by the collaboration of a CdS professor.
The verification of these abilities occurs through participation in presentations on assigned topics during individual courses, through passing the exams (normally in written form), and particularly through the evaluation and discussion of the final thesis.
Learning capacity.
A graduate of the LM in Economics for Environment and Sustainability (EAS) must have reached knowledge levels enabling their entry into subsequent training levels, such as II-level Master's programs, Italian doctoral programs, or international PhD programs, even at institutions of absolute global prominence. Such knowledge will also qualify them for entry into the job market in the areas indicated by professional opportunities.
These abilities will be acquired and verified primarily through courses with a higher methodological content in the economic, business economics, and mathematical-statistical areas.
Ability to apply knowledge and understanding.
General Area Graduates of the LM in Economics for Environment and Sustainability (EAS) must have acquired a solid analytical ability and mastery of the studied methodologies. Mastery of methodologies and their correct application constitute the key tool for addressing and proposing solutions to a wide range of economic issues and problems. EAS graduates must be able to critically analyze theoretical aspects and identify appropriate analytical methods for solving policy problems.
Thanks to the knowledge acquired through the training path, both through frontal teaching and seminar interventions in the classroom, as well as through didactic laboratories and exercises, EAS graduates will be able to understand economic and economic-environmental phenomena and propose suitable policy solutions, both of a standard type (regulation and taxation) and non-standard (nudging). The interdisciplinary approach of the course will also enable them to develop solutions where the natural environment represents a strategic competitive advantage variable rather than a cost factor.
Economic Area Master's graduates will be able to use theoretical modeling and tools and methods for quantitative analysis useful for understanding and analyzing the micro and macroeconomic context of the problems examined.
Mathematical-Statistical Area Statistical knowledge enables EAS graduates to understand and manage issues related to risk analysis and insurance, particularly concerning environmental disasters, sampling, and estimation of animal and plant populations or the study of social phenomena.
Business Area The knowledge acquired in the economic-business field will allow an adequate understanding of aspects related to the enterprise and those more directly connected to social and environmental management and market ethics.
Legal Area Master's graduates in EAS will be able to use and apply their legal-normative knowledge in the field of environmental damage and sustainable development, particularly to provide technical-cultural support for the analysis of practical problems, evaluation processes, and the development or analysis of policy tools.

ITALIAN Associated competencies for the role.
Environmental and Economic Analyst A master's graduate in Economy for the Environment and Sustainability possesses in-depth knowledge of economic-environmental phenomena and, in particular, of the interrelationships between economic activities and socio-environmental aspects. To these knowledge, they add analytical and technical competencies useful for understanding phenomena of interest, both micro and macro. They master sophisticated qualitative-quantitative analysis techniques and some statistical and econometric software.
The master's graduate also possesses competencies useful for managing and controlling the environmental and social performance of complex systems such as those of companies.
Through appropriate management packages, they are able to simulate scenarios and conduct data and document analysis aimed at preparing reports and projects.
They are able to conduct cost-benefit analyses and estimate the value of so-called non-market goods.
Role in work context.
Environmental and Economic Analyst Master's graduates in Economy for the Environment and Sustainability operate in professional positions requiring mastery of solid interpretative tools in the economic field, while simultaneously demanding versatility and analytical and decision-making abilities in contexts characterized by complexity and change. In particular, they can perform the following functions:
- analysis and processing useful for developing environmental policies, sustainable development projects, and the management and valorization of environmental and historical-cultural resources;
- assessment of environmental damages and, in general, of so-called non-market goods;
- company-level consulting, particularly in the utilities sector;
- control and management of corporate environmental risks, costs, and performance;
- preparation of summary reports and sustainability reports;
- development of projects for corporate environmental and social efficiency.
Additional information.
Course website Specific training objectives description.
The Master's Degree Course in Economy for the Environment and Sustainability (EAS) aims to provide master's graduates with a high level of preparation in the fields of economic and economic-quantitative disciplines, integrated with appropriate knowledge in business and legal areas.
A master's graduate EAS must have acquired the ability to interpret and address complex economic and social problems, with particular regard to those concerning the interaction between the economic system and the environment. Students will acquire theoretical-applicable knowledge and competencies for the empirical analysis of economic-environmental phenomena. Graduates will be able to master methodologies and tools for the evaluation and valorization of environmental resources necessary for the design and development of sustainable local and supra-local development programs. They will also be able to develop and/or collaborate on projects and processes for corporate efficiency and certification.
To this end, the training path is structured into courses and activities aimed at providing students with broad and technically advanced preparation on topics of economics and applied economics, as well as adequate training in economic-business and legal fields focused on the analysis of environmental issues and sustainability. This preparation is primarily acquired through courses activated in the SSD SECS-P/01 and SECS-P/02, SECS-P/07 and IUS/13 respectively. The training path also includes economic-quantitative courses (primarily in the SSD SECS-P/01, SECS-S/01 and SECS-S/03) capable of providing students with the appropriate knowledge for the empirical analysis of study phenomena, cost-benefit analysis, and the valuation of intangible goods (non-market goods).
The training path concludes with the preparation of a thesis, which on one hand serves to verify that the student has acquired advanced knowledge on economic or economic-environmental topics, also with an interdisciplinary approach, and on the other hand contributes to ensuring the student advanced knowledge and competencies on specific aspects concerning economic-environmental phenomena and sustainability. The final thesis is highly significant for training, with 21 credit points allocated to it.
