Final exam characteristics The final exam consists of a discussion, before the graduation committee, of a thesis developed in an original manner under the guidance of a supervisor. It must verify that the master's graduate has acquired advanced knowledge on financial intermediation topics, relevant both theoretically and professionally, enabling them to develop or apply original ideas through systematic and critically aware understanding; that they have the ability to apply acquired knowledge and solve problems on innovative topics, even within an interdisciplinary context; that they have the ability to present clearly and argue in written and oral form. The thesis can be written and presented in Italian or English. The ECTS credits attributed to the final exam are 18. For each master's thesis, a co-supervisor is appointed, proposed by the supervisor, and a counter-supervisor, proposed by the competent academic body. The merit score attributed to the final exam will take into account, in particular, the level of theoretical depth, the candidate's ability demonstrated in using appropriate quantitative methodologies for the research objective, the effectiveness of the empirical analyses conducted, the originality of the proposed arguments, and the effectiveness of the discussion. The merit score attributed to the final exam contributes to the formation of the final degree grade together with the average of the course exams, according to the criteria defined by a specific Faculty Regulation. The degree grade is expressed in hundredths. If the sum of the merit score attributed to the final exam and the average grade of the course exams exceeds 110/110, upon the supervisor's proposal, the graduation committee may unanimously award the highest distinction.
Required knowledge for admission The knowledge required for admission to the master's course in Economics and Management of Financial Intermediaries relates to the economic, business, mathematical-statistical, and legal fields. Knowledge in the business field must also include basic knowledge of the economics of financial and credit intermediation. Knowledge in the mathematical field must also include basic knowledge of financial mathematics. Additionally, basic computer skills at least at the ECDL core level (particularly regarding spreadsheet use) and knowledge of the English language corresponding to at least level B1 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages are required. The course's academic regulation defines the curricular requirements in relation to the different first-level degree classes as well as the number of credits to be acquired in specific disciplinary sectors. For graduates holding a foreign degree, the required knowledge for admission will be defined by the course's academic regulation based on the minimum content deemed necessary for the different disciplinary areas, including linguistic ones. For admission to the course, students possessing the required curricular qualifications must pass a selective test to verify personal preparation, the modalities of which are defined by the course's academic regulation. The admission test for verifying personal preparation is selective in nature and conducted in written form, through the solution of multiple-choice questions. The subjects, composition of the examination committee, and evaluation criteria of the test will be defined by the course's academic regulation. Graduates possessing the required curricular qualifications who have obtained their degree with a grade above a minimum threshold defined by the course's academic regulation will be exempt from the admission test. The course's academic regulation may also define specific modalities for evaluating the initial preparation of graduates from foreign universities, also with regard to the necessary linguistic knowledge.
Degree awarded Master's Degree (second-level degree) in Economics and Management of Financial Intermediaries Teaching delivery mode Conventional
Knowledge and understanding. Generic Area Master's graduates who have successfully completed the course must have acquired the following knowledge and understanding abilities: a) Ability to understand and explain the policies and operational strategies of the main categories of financial intermediaries. b) Knowledge of the theoretical evolution underlying different portfolio management models and their implications in terms of risk and development capacity of intermediaries. c) Ability to understand and explain the interrelationships between the different components of financial systems, both domestically and internationally. d) Knowledge of current approaches to financial regulation and their implications both at the macroeconomic level and for the operations of intermediaries. e) Knowledge of the regulatory and institutional framework of financial systems, with particular reference to the European Union. These knowledge and understanding abilities will be acquired and verified primarily through the curricular courses and their respective passing exams in the different areas.
Business Area Operational policies and strategies of the main categories of financial intermediaries. Theories, tools, and markets for risk management. Organizational models of intermediaries.
Economic Area Structural and institutional characteristics of financial systems. Evolution of the theoretical debate on the relationship between financial systems, growth, and instability.
Legal Area Institutional architecture of the EU Regulation of banks and other financial intermediaries Corporate governance of regulated companies Liability of directors and other corporate bodies
Quantitative Area Tools and models for managing financial and insurance risks Econometric methods relevant for financial applications
Judgment autonomy. Master's graduates who have successfully completed the course must: a) Be able to use relevant data for analyzing the main risk profiles of financial intermediaries, for evaluating their management choices, and for the implications on performance. b) Be able to use micro- and macro-economic data and qualitative information necessary to conduct scenario and stress analyses. c) Be able to evaluate alternative strategies and formulate policy proposals, taking into account the constraints that may arise during implementation. To consolidate these competencies, collaboration with particularly qualified experts from the banking and financial world is provided. Particular emphasis will also be placed on verifying these competencies during the evaluation of the final exam.
Learning ability. The methodological training, specialized knowledge, and required critical abilities allow for addressing subsequent study programs at the level of second-level university master's and research doctorate. The same competencies and abilities allow for autonomous learning, and thus to continue growing professionally and developing new or more advanced skills. These competencies are acquired and verified predominantly through specialized content courses in both business and economic areas, as well as in the training activities for preparing the final exam.
Ability to apply knowledge and understanding. Generic Area Master's graduates who have successfully completed the course must: a) Be able to use the most suitable theoretical approaches and quantitative methods to address management problems related to financial intermediation, even in a changing context. b) Be able to critically analyze theoretical contributions and studies developed by the professional world to assess their operational implications. c) Ability to apply acquired competencies for analyzing and identifying problems in the general debate areas related to economic and financial disciplines. d) Ability to abstract to identify the essence of a problem and apply general principles to specific cases. These competencies will be acquired and verified using, as study material, articles with both theoretical and empirical content, central bank reports, strategic plans of financial institutions, as well as proposing in-class and exam exercises on current and concrete cases and problems. Particular emphasis will also be placed on verifying these competencies during the evaluation of the final exam.
Business Area Evaluation of the impact of prudential rules and accounting standards and their changes. Comparative analysis of risk-adjusted performance across different business areas. Compliance risk and effectiveness of governance and internal control processes. Competencies in implementing methods and models for managing and covering financial and operational risks. Analysis and measurement of credit risk using different models proposed by theory and professional practice.
Economic Area Evaluation of macro-prudential policies. Scenario analysis. Econometric tools for financial data analysis.
Legal Area Analysis of the regulatory convergence process in different jurisdictions Specificity of financial contracts and their risk implications Analysis of mechanisms for managing and resolving financial crises.
Quantitative Area Application of quantitative tools to the analysis of micro- and macro-economic data Scenario analysis Volatility and correlation analysis for risk measurement and coverage calculation.

Course website Specific educational objectives description.
The Master's degree in Economics and Management of Financial Intermediaries aims to:
- Provide in-depth knowledge and advanced understanding of the structure, operation, and regulation of financial systems, particularly the role of banks, financial and insurance companies, and central banks.
- Develop the ability to frame financial systems in an international dimension and acquire skills in using appropriate risk assessment techniques.
- Develop the ability to critically understand and evaluate management strategies, portfolio decisions, and the performance of financial intermediaries through appropriate risk measurement models.
- Develop skills in using computational tools and econometric/statistical techniques to identify trends in financial markets and assess credits and financial portfolios.
The training path focuses on courses related to different profiles of banking and insurance intermediation, across four main disciplinary areas:
1) Business, which includes courses in relevant SSDs for specific training (SECS-P/11, SECS-P/09, SECS-P/07). These courses primarily address two major thematic areas: on one hand, the evaluation and management of financial risks from both management and prudential supervision and accounting standards perspectives; on the other hand, the operations of main business units typical of different categories of intermediaries.
2) Economic, which includes a series of courses aimed at framing the macroeconomic, policy, and public regulatory context, both internal and international, in which financial intermediaries operate (SECS-P/01, P/02, and P/03). Additionally, courses for quantitative analysis of financial phenomena are offered in the disciplinary sectors SECS-P/01 and/or SECS-P/05.
3) Legal, which includes courses in three disciplinary sectors: one focused on providing a framework of regulatory aspects of financial intermediation within the EU context (SSD IUS/05); one in corporate law (IUS/04), supporting training in investment banking; and one in tax law (IUS/12).
4) Mathematical-Statistical, which includes courses in financial mathematics, dedicated to main market models and derivative contract valuation (SECS-S/06). Other quantitative courses are statistical in orientation (SECS-S/01 and S/03), equally relevant for risk management in credit, finance, and insurance areas.
Graduates must also consolidate information technology knowledge for data management and use of financial and econometric functions. Alternatively, credits are provided for training activities such as internships and placements at financial institutions.
Particular importance is given to linguistic training. Students must acquire English skills at least at level B2; they must also know at least an intermediate level of a second EU language (French or Spanish).

Program, Texts, and Objectives Professional title conferred by the degree.
Chemist (Senior)
The main employment sectors are:
- Self-employment, subject to registration with the professional register,
- Private analysis laboratories: specialized facilities for environmental analyses, where chemical analyses are conducted,
- Public research laboratories and centers: university laboratories and centers that conduct, promote, and disseminate research activities and transfer them to private companies,
- Private companies: industries in various industrial sectors (chemical, pharmaceutical, cosmetic, dye, new materials, agri-food, etc.) in the fields of research and development, production, and quality control,
- Institutes, Research Centers, Public or Private Entities, Central or Local Public Administration, which deal with territorial planning, issuance of production authorizations, ...
The Master's Degree in Chemistry allows students to take the state exam for admission to the profession of Chemist, subject to registration with the Order of Chemists (Section A).
Master's graduates in Chemistry can also access the Research Doctorate, in Italy or at other international institutions.
Final Exam Characteristics The Master's thesis in Chemistry must contain the experimental and/or theoretical work developed by the student during an internship at a research laboratory of the department, or at companies or other public and private research institutions (in Italy or abroad).
The student must demonstrate having acquired autonomy and ability in research work, in the design and execution of experimental measurements, their interpretation, as well as the ability to apply mathematical, statistical, and computer algorithms for data rationalization and the development of interpretation models.
The final degree examination will consist of a student dissertation, the elaborated and presented experimental thesis, and will be in English.
The grade will be expressed on a scale of 110 with possible honors.
Required Knowledge for Admission To access the Master's Degree Course in Chemistry (LM-54), it is necessary to hold a degree or a three-year university diploma or another foreign-acquired title recognized as suitable.
To be admitted to the Master's degree course, it is necessary to possess certain curricular requirements (as listed below) and an adequate personal preparation in the fundamental subjects for the preparation of a chemist, such as mathematics, physics, chemistry, and computer science.
The required curricular requirements are met by holding a degree in one of the following classes:
Chemical Sciences and Technologies ─ L-27 (D.M. 270/2004) or 21 (D.M. 509/1999)
Graduates from different degree classes may also be admitted, provided they have acquired at least 90 ECTS in the Scientific Disciplinary Sectors (SSD) from CHIM/01 to CHIM/12 during their academic path.
Additionally, knowledge of the English language at a level of at least B2/2, as defined by the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages, is required.
The verification of personal preparation is mandatory, and only students possessing the curricular requirements may access this verification.
For international students, admission will be decided by a representative appointed by the Unique Academic Committee through the analysis of the curriculum, possibly supplemented by an interview conducted via teleconference and/or an online entrance test.
For foreign students, verification of adequate knowledge of the Italian language is required. Students who do not possess these linguistic skills may attend specific courses to reach the required level within the additional training activities (Article 10, paragraph 5, letter d).
Knowledge and Understanding. Molecular and Biomolecular Area Master's graduates in Chemistry will acquire in-depth knowledge of investigation techniques regarding organic, inorganic, and organometallic compounds useful in the pharmaceutical, nutraceutical, environmental, biomaterials, and industrial biotechnology sectors.
Particular attention will be given to knowledge in the field of bio-organic and bio-inorganic chemistry to understand the mechanism of action of biologically active molecules and biomaterials through the use of synthesis, analytical, spectroscopic, and microscopy techniques.
Additionally, extensive emphasis will be placed on theoretical-computational studies for investigating complex reaction mechanisms of biological interest.
These knowledge will be acquired through fundamental teaching tools, such as frontal lectures and laboratory exercises (to be carried out through both individual and group activities under the guidance of a teacher and direct tutoring) and the preparation of a final experimental and original thesis, under the guidance of a supervisor.
The achievement of these objectives will be verified through written and/or oral exams at the end of the training activity, and the discussion of the final elaboration (experimental thesis).
Environmental Monitoring and Sustainable Development Area Master's graduates in Chemistry will acquire in-depth knowledge of the themes related to the analytical characterization of quality, especially in the environmental, nutraceutical, and agri-food sectors.
Particular attention will be dedicated to cutting-edge methodologies (NMR, mass spectrometry, EPR, etc.) that form the basis for modifying the standards required at the European level for product quality certification.
Additionally, the Master's student will deepen the study of environmental issues related to the correct thermodynamic use of energy, minimization of pollution, and analysis of production cycles to be developed sustainably within the environmental context, according to the need to progress towards a society that can balance environmental protection, social and economic development of local communities.
Great attention will be devoted to knowledge in the field of environmental remediation and the control of quality of surface water bodies.
These knowledge will be acquired through fundamental teaching tools, such as frontal lectures and laboratory exercises (to be carried out through both individual and group activities under the guidance of a teacher and direct tutoring) and the preparation of a final experimental and original thesis, under the guidance of a supervisor.
The achievement of these objectives will be verified through written and/or oral exams at the end of the training activity, and the discussion of the final elaboration (experimental thesis).

Judgment Autonomy.
Master's degree graduates in Chemistry will have acquired advanced critical reasoning skills and consequent judgment autonomy, in carrying out scientific research activities, developing competencies in evaluating, interpreting and synthesizing information derived from experimental data and theoretical results and models.
This will enable the Master's degree graduate in Chemistry to evaluate and interpret laboratory safety conditions, aspects of teaching evaluation, principles of professional ethics, and scientific approach to molecular and environmental chemical issues.
The Master's degree graduate in Chemistry will also be able to use, process and critically synthesize data with full intellectual and judgment autonomy, and integrate knowledge for the analysis and management of even complex systems.
These judgment autonomy skills will be acquired through laboratory and exercise activities, which will be reinforced through direct interaction opportunities with the business world and professions (through seminar activities and internships) offering students many opportunities for constructive discussion.
The achievement of these objectives in judgment autonomy will be verified mainly through written and/or oral exams at the end of the training activity, and the discussion of the final thesis (experimental thesis).
Additionally, for some courses, students will be required to prepare written reports (scientific reports) and oral presentations, as individual or group work, to be discussed and defended in front of peers and the course instructor.

Learning Capacity.
Master's degree graduates in Chemistry will have acquired qualities suitable for continuing studies in post-graduate academic paths, and in particular for entering Research Doctorate programs, and/or occupying professional roles as independent professionals or in laboratories, structures, public and private companies, even at managerial and Senior Chemist levels.
The Master's degree graduate in Chemistry possesses the basic knowledge tools for continuous knowledge updating.
These learning capacities will be acquired mainly through laboratory exercises, individual study, and preparation of the final thesis.
The achievement of these objectives in learning capacities will be verified mainly through written and oral exams at the end of each course and laboratory exercises, which will allow instructors to assess individual study skills and the ability to approach topics autonomously.
The thesis supervisor will also evaluate the learning capacities and research aptitude of the graduate during the preparation of the final thesis (experimental thesis).

Application of Knowledge and Understanding.
Molecular and Biomolecular Area Master's degree graduates in Chemistry must have acquired the ability to apply knowledge and understanding to solve qualitative and quantitative problems in molecular and biomolecular fields, through calculation and chemical data processing skills.
Master's degree graduates will be able to:
- Independently retrieve all necessary bibliographic information to plan and carry out the synthesis of organic, inorganic and organometallic molecules, and proceed to optimize new analytical protocols;
- Process scientific data obtained through appropriately designed experiments;
- Set up and conduct experiments in synthetic chemistry and perform computational simulation and prediction calculations;
- Understand a professional issue, conduct a critical evaluation, and propose specific solutions (problem posing & problem solving);
- Utilize computer methods for processing experimental data.

Environmental Monitoring and Sustainable Development Area Master's degree graduates in Chemistry must have acquired the ability to apply knowledge and understanding to solve qualitative and quantitative problems in environmental monitoring and sustainable development, and will be able to:
- Evaluate practical problems that may arise during scientific research in environmental, nutraceutical, and rational energy use fields;
- Use advanced instrumental techniques and critically evaluate quality parameters related to the issue under examination;
- Handle the qualitative-quantitative characterization of complex matrices (industrial, food, biological, and environmental) with the most modern experimental diagnostic techniques;
- Use software for database management and data processing;
- Know the procedures for product Life Cycle Assessment (LCA).

Communication Skills.
Master's graduates in Chemistry will have acquired skills in presenting scientific material and topics to both specialized and non-specialized audiences, both in writing and orally, clearly and without ambiguity. They will have a solid knowledge of written and spoken English in the scientific context and will be able to present a scientific report with linguistic propriety and terminological rigor, both orally and in written form.
Additionally, the communication skills of the Master's graduate in Chemistry will also encompass information technology and instrumental skills for managing scientific information, processing experimental data, and conducting accurate bibliographic research.
These communication skills will be acquired through laboratory activities, individual study, and preparation of the final thesis.
The achievement of these communication skills objectives will be verified primarily through the preparation of written reports (scientific reports) at the end of laboratory activities, and the preparation of oral presentations, either individually or in groups, to be discussed and defended in front of peers and the course instructor, but especially through the discussion of the final thesis (experimental thesis).
Planned occupational and professional outcomes for graduates.
Senior Chemist
The main employment sectors are:
- Self-employment, following registration with the professional register,

- Public research laboratories and centers: university laboratories and centers that carry out, promote, and disseminate research activities and transfer them to private companies,

- Institutes, Research Centers, Public or Private Entities, Public Administration at central or local level, dealing with territorial planning, authorization for production, ...

Senior Chemist
Graduates in Chemistry will be involved in activities promoting scientific and technological innovation, design, synthesis, and characterization of products and materials meeting efficiency and environmental sustainability criteria set by stringent European regulations effective since 2007; using the most modern technologies for structural determination of new molecules and their interactions with macro-biomolecules; being familiar with the use of spectroscopic and computational techniques to solve structural and dynamic problems, or to correlate microscopic molecular properties with macroscopic properties of substances.
Role in work context.
Senior Chemist
In summary, the Master's Degree in Chemistry aims to provide professional preparation applicable as a self-employed professional or in laboratories, structures, and public and private companies, also at managerial and Senior Chemist levels, in sectors such as industry, design, synthesis, and characterization of new materials, health, food, environment, energy, security, cultural heritage, and public administration, applying disciplinary investigation methods independently.
With the acquired competencies, the Master's graduate in Chemistry has a cultural, technical-scientific, and professional preparation enabling them to:
- Hold roles of high responsibility (coordination and management) in work contexts requiring the design of synthesis and characterization processes (in various application sectors: pharmaceutical, cosmetic, new materials, nutraceutical), management of energy and environmental resources, management of the most modern chemical technologies (e.g., green chemistry processes), and use of theoretical computational approaches for studying complex processes
- Coordinate and manage research groups at the corporate level in production and research and development departments
- Hold positions in education, promote and disseminate scientific and technological innovation and the diffusion of scientific culture
Specific training objectives description.
The Master's Degree in Chemistry aims to train graduates with a solid chemical scientific culture at the molecular level, as well as broad knowledge of major applications in numerous research and service production sectors, corresponding to possible training paths. These paths are characterized by in-depth study of specific aspects that chemical sciences can provide to different issues, while always requiring knowledge of cutting-edge technological approaches and methodologies in chemical sciences, the ability to critically interpret experimental parameters, and good mastery of the most recent computer tools.
Therefore, the degree program aims to:
- Ensure a solid cultural and operational preparation in disciplines characterizing the class, with particular attention to theoretical principles and the construction of theoretical models suitable for interpreting chemical phenomena,
- Ensure good mastery of the scientific method of investigation, from planning and conducting laboratory experiments, to data collection with evaluation of experimental errors, up to interpretation with an appropriate theoretical model and dissemination of scientific data,
- Ensure appropriate knowledge of the most important experimental investigation techniques and fundamental and cutting-edge analytical instrumentation for obtaining and interpreting chemical data, including statistical treatment of experimental data,
- Ensure good written and oral knowledge of the English language,
- Ensure a high degree of autonomy in the workplace through individual responsibility for conducting research within themes of significant scientific relevance,
- Provide adequate preparation for conducting independent research activities in scientific laboratories in public and private research structures.
TRAINING PATH The complete training path is structured in 120 CFU.
Common courses aim to introduce theoretical knowledge in themes characteristic of chemical sciences (biochemistry, computational chemistry, EPR and NMR spectroscopy, materials chemistry, electrochemistry, chemometrics, ...) not covered or only briefly covered in the undergraduate degree, as well as to enable appropriate experimental verification in practical and laboratory courses coordinated with the respective theoretical courses.
Elective courses aim to further deepen themes related to the applications of chemical sciences in specific sectors.
In detail:
- In the first year of the course, courses in chemical fields are offered, mostly activated in characteristic activities and in SSD CHIM/01, CHIM/02, CHIM/03, CHIM/06.
Elective courses in related and integrative activities are also provided in SSD CHIM/01, CHIM/02, CHIM/03, CHIM/06 and BIO/10, allowing students to integrate and deepen knowledge in the application sectors of chemical sciences by choosing from courses in different curricula.
- In the second year of the course, related and integrative activities and student-selected courses are provided to consolidate and personalize the training path. The student's academic workload is primarily dedicated to seminar activities, useful for entering the workplace, internships, and preparation for the final exam.
Seminar activities will be organized in collaboration with representatives of companies and, more generally, organizations representing the world of work (e.g., Order of Chemists and Physicists, sector associations, ...) and aim to increasingly introduce graduates into the production and research and development world at the corporate level. This is also the objective of the internship activity, which can be carried out in companies (Italian and foreign) or in public and private research institutions (Italian and foreign), representing an important opportunity for contact and exchange between academia and productive activities, constituting a preferred channel for cooperation between teachers/students and entrepreneurs/representatives of organizations for the quality improvement of training processes, where research plays a fundamental role.
The main themes of seminar activities will focus on regulatory aspects related to certain production and analytical sectors, quality management systems (validation of analytical methods, calculation of measurement uncertainty, accreditation of methods and protocols, ...).
Seminar activities will also be directed towards acquiring transversal competencies (soft skills), additional and complementary to technical and specialized knowledge, and the study of new interpretative models of production (e.g., Industry 4.0).

Final exam characteristics The final exam for the Master's Degree in Biotechnologies of Human Reproduction LM-9 consists of an original experimental thesis written in English under the guidance of a supervisor. This document represents the results of studies and research conducted in the final year of the course. The results required for the final exam may also be achieved through research periods carried out in Italy or abroad, in the form of internships or traineeships at public and private structures affiliated with the University. The final exam is defended before a judging committee that awards a merit score based on the originality of the topic, written and oral presentation skills, and research methodologies. The final exam grade is expressed on a scale of 110 with possible honors.
Required knowledge for admission To access the Master's Degree Course in Biotechnologies of Human Reproduction LM-9, it is necessary to hold a degree or Master's degree, a three-year university diploma, a four-year old system degree in biological, biotechnological, medical-sanitary fields obtained at any national university or other equivalent title, deemed suitable, obtained abroad. It is necessary to possess adequate basic preparation in cytology, biochemistry, biology, molecular biology, genetics, microbiology, general physiology.
Curricular requirements are met by holding a degree or Master's degree in one of the following classes of D.M. 270/2004 (or corresponding in the old D.M. 509/99):
L-2 Biotechnology L-13 Biological Sciences LM-6 Biology LM-9 Medical, Veterinary and Pharmaceutical Biotechnology LM-41 Medicine and Surgery LM-13 Pharmacy and Pharmaceutical Industry Other degree classes may be admitted, provided that they have acquired at least 75 CFU in the following specific disciplinary sectors and obtained the degree with a minimum grade specified in the study course didactic regulations:
- BIO/10; BIO/11, BIO/13; BIO/14 BIO/18; BIO/19; BIO/06; BIO/16; BIO/17, MED/03; MED/07, MED/46
For students meeting the curricular requirements, personal preparation will be verified according to the modalities indicated in the study course didactic regulations.
Additionally, possession of an English language certification at B2 level of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR) is required. Knowledge and understanding.
General area The Master's graduate in Biotechnologies of Human Reproduction LM9 possesses advanced knowledge related to the anatomy, histology, physiology and pathology of male and female reproductive systems, the structure and functions of biological systems involved in the reproductive process such as male and female gamete biology, assisted reproduction techniques, embryology principles and infertility genetics. The Master's graduate possesses skills on the epidemiological aspects of infertility and the management of infertile couples from a gynecological, andrological and psychological perspective. The Master's graduate knows the active principles and mechanisms of action of drugs used in medical assisted reproduction practices and in the management of couple pathologies. The Master's graduate possesses skills on the ethical-legal aspects related to the field of medical assisted reproduction. They must also develop the ability to keep such knowledge updated and connected to the most innovative and advanced aspects in the context of their professional practice.
Scientific methodology and behavioral sciences The Master's graduate in Biotechnologies of Human Reproduction LM 9 deeply understands epidemiology as a tool of the scientific method, as well as the current regulations in the field of medical assisted reproduction. The Master's graduate also acquires the general principles of psychology, which are fundamental for interacting with infertile couples.
General medical-biological disciplines The Master's graduate in Biotechnologies of Human Reproduction LM 9 must possess knowledge of the pathophysiology and histology of male and female reproductive systems. They must acquire in-depth knowledge of human infertility genetics, as well as possess skills related to the active principles and mechanisms of action of drugs used in medical assisted reproduction practices and in the management of couple pathologies. They must finally acquire knowledge on the study of microorganisms involved in common infections of the male and female genital tract.
Disciplines characterizing the field of medical assisted reproduction The Master's graduate in Biotechnologies of Human Reproduction LM 9 must have in-depth knowledge of oocyte, sperm and embryo biology, possess knowledge related to the management of gametes and embryos in the laboratory and their cryopreservation. Working closely with gynecologists and andrologists, the Master's graduate must possess adequate knowledge of gynecology and andrology to follow a complete diagnostic and therapeutic path for infertile couples.

Judgment autonomy.
In the Master's Degree course in Biotechnologies of Human Reproduction LM-9, teaching tools are used to promote judgment autonomy:
-the teaching provided in small groups aims to encourage and strengthen the teacher-student relationship
-the collegial discussion of scientific articles and clinical cases enhances the student's individual interest and contribution
-the independent execution of practical activities and exercises, although under the supervision of the teacher responsible for the course or their collaborators
-internship activities that will lead to the preparation of a final experimental thesis written in English, in which the student uses the acquired methodologies, independently plans and manages their activity, and processes laboratory activities related to the assigned experimental project.
Master's graduates in Biotechnologies of Human Reproduction LM-9 are therefore able to formulate hypotheses, critically and independently collect and evaluate results. They are able to develop personal solutions in solving analytical and complex problems by applying a rigorous scientific methodology.
The Master's graduate is aware of the importance of decisions made during the practice of gamete manipulation in respect of ethical-legal standards and patients.
Master's graduates in Biotechnologies of Human Reproduction LM-9 are able to evaluate the commercial and therapeutic impact of applied procedures in the scientific context and in health and social fields.
The Master's graduate must also identify commercial and patent aspects, optimizing protocols, developing new technologies, identifying molecular markers useful for diagnosing infertility causes or for interactions between gametes, or between embryo and endometrium for the implantation process.
Student judgment autonomy is assessed during the study course through interactive frontal teaching, examination tests, discussing therapeutic treatment options, protocols and clinical cases.
Learning ability.
The Master's graduate in Biotechnologies of Human Reproduction LM-9 knows how to consult scientific databases, read, interpret and critically review scientific literature, knowing how to select the best opportunities and methods for updating.
Qualified and updated information is provided by teachers during frontal lessons.
Continuous development and deepening of skills, particularly regarding consultation of specialized databases, occurs through learning innovative technologies, updating specific knowledge through reading and critical analysis of scientific publications, and participating in conferences.
Learning ability is assessed throughout the course through various verification methods, especially during the writing of the thesis, which is controlled by the supervisor and evaluated by the graduation committee.
Ability to apply knowledge and understanding.
General area The Master's graduate possesses problem-solving abilities, applies acquired knowledge and practical skills to the field of human reproduction biotechnology.
They are able to solve operational questions requiring complex skills, such as managing laboratory equipment, developing methodologies and protocols for cell cultures and cryopreservation of sperm, oocytes and embryos. They are able to apply basic and advanced diagnostic protocols and interpret laboratory test results, also in collaboration with other healthcare professionals in a multidisciplinary approach. They are capable of using procedures in compliance with current legislation. The Master's graduate in Biotechnologies of Human Reproduction LM-9 is therefore able to reproduce biological processes related to fertilization and also to use and act upon them with appropriate interventions and scientific and technological tools to obtain useful, controllable, repeatable and certified goods and services. To achieve these goals, they must be able to address problems that may arise in the work context, intervene on the management and control procedures of the technologies used, plan and independently carry out technical, research, and laboratory coordination work in the sector.
The Master's graduate in Biotechnologies of Human Reproduction LM-9, leveraging their English language skills, can utilize high-quality scientific production disseminated internationally through specialized journals and electronic databases, and attend training events featuring internationally renowned speakers.
Teaching methods and tools for achievement and verification Knowledge and understanding abilities, as well as the ability to apply knowledge and understanding, are achieved and verified through the following training activities provided in the Master's course:
-frontal lessons, which provide basic and specialized updated knowledge necessary for students to critically approach laboratory practical work;
-individual study, necessary for any type of knowledge to be understood, consolidated and elaborated;
-laboratory practical activities aimed at acquiring procedures related to reproductive medicine, carried out under the supervision of the teacher and laboratory staff. Students gradually acquire their own autonomy, working individually with appropriate technical support in equipped laboratories. In this way, students apply the theoretical knowledge acquired to consolidate their practical skills necessary for operating in the field of assisted medical reproduction;
-specific curricular internships or internship activities, organized during the training path at qualified public and private centers, Italian and foreign, operating in the field of reproduction and contracted with the University;
-internship activity required for preparing an experimental thesis written in English, which can be carried out within the University laboratories or at external contracted structures operating in areas related to the training path;
-participation in seminars and conferences related to the training path, organized on-site by the University and scientific societies/organizations/centers operating in the field of reproductive medicine.
The assessment of learning level and specific methodological skills occurs through intermediate evaluation tests with multiple-choice and true/false questions, written tests on topics related to various courses, and especially through active student participation in frontal lessons by discussing scientific articles assigned by the teacher.
At the end of each course, the level of knowledge and understanding of the topics covered is assessed through written or oral exams. The acquired theoretical knowledge must have a practical experimental counterpart related to the laboratory procedures required for PMA.
A crucial moment for verifying expected outcomes is the presentation and discussion of the final exam carried out by the student under the guidance of a supervising teacher. During the preparation of the experimental thesis, the supervising teacher has the opportunity to assess the student's ability to apply acquired knowledge to critically solve operational problems of the proposed methodologies, manage laboratory equipment, and test the student's knowledge regarding methodologies and protocols applied in the PMA field.
Scientific methodology and behavioral sciences Master's graduates are able to use scientific methodology knowledge to understand the most recent scientific articles published internationally. The application of ethical-legal aspects is fundamental to ensure procedure correctness and patient respect. The application of psychology knowledge is helpful for establishing a correct relationship with patients.
General medical-biological disciplines The Master's graduate is able to apply their general medical-biological knowledge to frame infertile couples, set up and refine new protocols in the field of semen diagnostics and in the management of male and female gametes in the laboratory.
Disciplines characterizing the assisted reproduction sector The knowledge acquired by the Master's graduate in the field of biology and management of gametes and embryos is fundamental and necessary to run a PMA laboratory and increase the success rate of PMA itself. Knowledge acquired regarding gynecological and andrological issues contributes to building the professional profile of a biotechnologist operating in the PMA field and possessing an overall view necessary to achieve success in the field of assisted reproduction.

Communication Skills.
The Master's graduate in Biotechnologies of Human Reproduction LM-9 has acquired through the training path the ability to express oneself with scientific rigor, to draft technical-scientific reports, and to disseminate clinical and research results. At the same time, they have acquired communication skills directed towards a broader audience, using clear, rigorous, and effective language to disseminate research results and offered services. The Master's graduate has developed effective communication with patients, who must understand their clinical condition, the procedures to be performed, and the therapies that may be indicated. At the end of the course, they demonstrate the ability to interact and collaborate with other professional figures they encounter, such as gynecologists, andrologists, psychologists, pharmaceutical informants, and nurses. By using computer tools and software, they are able to manage rapid, efficient, and effective communication.

Communication skills are acquired through discussion and teacher-student interaction sessions during frontal and laboratory teaching activities, through the presentation of technical-scientific topics, the presentation of literature data related to the delivered courses, and the discussion of research results obtained during the training internship and thesis preparation.

The verification of communication skills is carried out through written or oral in-course assessments, discussion of scientific papers presented within journal clubs, and final exams for each training activity. An additional verification tool for acquired communication skills includes the presentation of the experimental thesis work to the Degree Committee using multimedia tools.

English language training and in-depth knowledge of scientific literature facilitate the Master's graduate's integration into the international scientific community and professional networks to communicate and share achieved results.

Expected occupational and professional opportunities for graduates.

Operator, supervisor, and coordinator in Assisted Medical Reproduction (PMA) laboratories.
The Master's graduate in Biotechnologies of Human Reproduction LM-9 can practice freely in public and private PMA laboratories after registration with the Professional Register following the passing of the state exam. The Master's degree allows access to non-medical specialization schools, whose title permits performing activities as a first-level manager in National Health Service structures.

Operator, supervisor, and coordinator in semenology centers.
The Master's graduate in Biotechnologies of Human Reproduction LM-9 can work in public structures within the framework of free practice in independent or PMA-attached semenology laboratories after registration with the Professional Register following the passing of the state exam. The Master's degree allows access to non-medical specialization schools, whose title permits performing activities as a first-level manager in National Health Service structures.

Operator, supervisor, and coordinator of biological banks for the preservation of reproductive cells and tissues.
The Master's graduate in Biotechnologies of Human Reproduction LM-9 can work within free practice in public and private centers for the preservation of reproductive cells and tissues, independent or within PMA centers, after registration with the Professional Register following the passing of the state exam. The Master's degree allows access to non-medical specialization schools, whose title permits performing activities as a first-level manager in National Health Service structures.

Biotechnology researcher in private research centers operating in the field of human reproduction pathophysiology nationally and internationally.
The Master's graduate in Biotechnologies of Human Reproduction LM-9 can serve as a biotechnology researcher in private, national, and international research centers operating in the field of human reproduction pathophysiology. They may also participate in clinical trials as an expert in reproduction pathophysiology and in national and international research projects.

Biotechnology and pharmacological laboratory manager and operator.
The Master's graduate in Biotechnologies of Human Reproduction LM-9 can serve as a manager and operator of biotechnology and pharmacological laboratories in public settings such as universities and research institutions, and in private companies active in the pharmaceutical and biomaterials sectors, both nationally and internationally.

Skills associated with the role.

Operator, supervisor, and coordinator in Assisted Medical Reproduction (PMA) laboratories.
To perform the above-described functions, the Master's graduate in Biotechnologies of Human Reproduction LM-9 must have acquired knowledge of the anatomy and physiology of the male and female reproductive apparatus, gamete biology, knowledge of assisted fertilization techniques, skills in embryology, and knowledge of the diagnostic process for infertile couples. Additionally, the operator, supervisor, and coordinator in PMA laboratories must develop communication and relational skills essential in patient interactions and be familiar with the national and international regulatory framework governing human reproductive biotechnology.

Operator, supervisor, and coordinator in semenology centers.
The Master's graduate in Biotechnologies of Human Reproduction LM-9 who undertakes the role of operator, supervisor, and coordinator in semenology centers has acquired knowledge of male gamete biology and the techniques related to semen analysis and functional sperm selection following the guidelines of the World Health Organization (WHO, 2010).

Operator, supervisor, and coordinator of biological banks for the preservation of reproductive cells and tissues.
The Master's graduate in Biotechnologies of Human Reproduction LM-9 who undertakes the role of operator, supervisor, and coordinator of biological banks for the preservation of reproductive cells and tissues knows gamete biology, tissue histology, and cryobiological techniques. They are familiar with the regulations governing these procedures at national and international levels.

Biotechnology researcher in private research centers operating in the field of human reproduction pathophysiology nationally and internationally.
The Master's graduate in Biotechnologies of Human Reproduction LM-9 who undertakes the role of biotechnology researcher in the field of human reproduction pathophysiology has skills in human reproduction biology and genetics, pathophysiology of male and female reproductive systems, and the use of drugs in in vitro and in vivo animal models.

Biotechnology and pharmacological laboratory manager and operator.
The Master's graduate in Biotechnologies of Human Reproduction LM-9 who undertakes the role of biotechnology and pharmacological laboratory manager and operator has skills in molecular analysis, biomedical technologies in human fields, and the development and testing of innovative pharmaceutical products, with potential development of patents in the healthcare sector.

Role in the workplace context.

Operator, supervisor, and coordinator in Assisted Medical Reproduction (PMA) laboratories.
The Master's graduate in Biotechnologies of Human Reproduction LM-9 has acquired the skills to manage, treat in vitro, culture, and cryopreserve human gametes and embryos. They are able to manage gametes in the laboratory from collection through in vitro fertilization to the early stages of embryonic development, and have acquired the skills to reproduce in vitro the physiological processes of egg maturation and fertilization. They have also acquired the skills to perform first, second, and third-level PMA techniques.

Operator, supervisor, and coordinator in semenology centers.
The Master's graduate in Biotechnologies of Human Reproduction LM-9 has acquired the skills to analyze and treat semen and sperm in vitro. They are able to manage semen from collection to use and possible cryopreservation. They are able to perform standardized tests for morpho-functional parameters (semen analysis) important in sperm selection and to conduct biochemical tests in semen.

Operator, supervisor, and coordinator of biological banks for the preservation of reproductive cells and tissues.
The Master's graduate in Biotechnologies of Human Reproduction LM-9 has the skills to serve as an operator, supervisor, and coordinator of biological banks for the preservation of reproductive cells and tissues. They can manage cryopreservation procedures for gametes and tissues and the equipment according to current national and international regulations.

Biotechnology researcher in private research centers operating in the field of human reproduction pathophysiology nationally and internationally.
The Master's graduate in Biotechnologies of Human Reproduction LM-9 has the skills to serve as a biotechnology researcher in private, national, and international research centers operating in the field of human reproduction pathophysiology.

Biotechnology and pharmacological laboratory manager and operator.
The Master's graduate in Biotechnologies of Human Reproduction LM-9 has the skills to serve as a manager and operator of biotechnology and pharmacological laboratories in private, national, and international settings.

Specific training objectives description.
The Master's Degree course in Biotechnologies of Human Reproduction LM-9 aims to acquire the knowledge and develop the skills necessary in the field of human reproduction.
The training path addresses reproduction themes through a multidisciplinary approach, leveraging the expertise of qualified Italian and foreign experts.
During the first year, the Master's graduate acquires knowledge of anatomy-histology (BIO/17), physiology (BIO/09), and pathology of the male and female reproductive systems (MED/04; MED/05), gamete biology and interaction (BIO/13), embryonic development mechanisms (BIO/13), the genetic basis of human fertility (MED/03, BIO/18), and infertility epidemiology (MED/42). The Master's graduate also gains theoretical-practical experience in basic and advanced techniques in human reproductive biotechnology (BIO/13).
Specific skills related to the management of infertile couples from a gynecological (MED/40), andrological, and psychological (MPSI/01; MPSI/05) perspective are introduced at the beginning of the second year. Concurrently, the study of applied toxicology in reproduction, including animal model investigations (BIO/13), and knowledge of the mechanisms of action of drugs used in treating infertility-causing pathologies (BIO/14) are included. The training is completed by knowledge of the national and international regulatory framework within which reproductive biotechnology operates in research and assisted reproduction, and a critical study of the bioethical aspects related to these themes (IUS/01).
The training internship and thesis preparation activities contribute to developing the soft skills that will help the Master's graduate in Biotechnologies of Human Reproduction LM-9 integrate into the workforce; the graduate acquires practical skills in the specific activities carried out in assisted reproduction laboratories, such as gamete analysis and selection, in vitro fertilization techniques, gamete and embryo culture, and their cryopreservation.
At the end of the training path, the Master's graduate, integrating theoretical and practical knowledge, possesses the tools to design experimental deepening on human reproductive biotechnology and to produce, independently, an experimental thesis.
In this regard, Master's graduates are also evaluated on their aptitude for team development, time management, critical thinking, and problem solving.
The choice of English as the official language of the course responds to the need to prepare the Master's graduate for easier consultation of international scientific databases, integration into a workforce increasingly based on internationalization, and participation in international scientific conferences to compare research results, forming the basis for continuous updating.

Judgment Autonomy.
Master's graduates in Sanitary Biology will have the ability to choose the most suitable investigation methodologies in the fields of biomedical research, biosanitary, toxicological, and hygienic-environmental areas. They will possess the necessary knowledge regarding current legislation in each field, as well as the ability to draft reports, update records, and interact with authorities responsible for monitoring the activities described above. Furthermore, Master's graduates will be aware of the risks associated with the use of equipment and chemical products, as well as the behavioral norms in biological, biochemistry-clinical, pharmacological, and microbiological laboratories, and the aspects related to safety and environmental issues. Master's graduates will also acquire the ethical elements related to the profession of Biologist, considering the possibility of registration with Section A of the professional register of the Order of Biologists following a state exam. These competencies are guaranteed by the presence of permanent faculty members with extensive teaching experience, involved in scientific research activities.
Judgment Autonomy will be achieved through formal teaching activities, which will not only involve the presentation of specific course content but will also include critical reading of scientific literature. Additionally, the planned laboratory activities will involve not only the execution of experiments but also their detailed planning, critical analysis of the results obtained, and the drafting of reports where students can demonstrate their ability to critically reprocess data.
The achievement of the objective specified by this descriptor will be verified through written or oral examinations for each course. An additional moment, both for the student to apply Judgment Autonomy and for the verification of objective achievement, will be constituted by the preparation of the Master's thesis.
Learning Ability.
The study program is designed to develop learning abilities that enable Master's graduates of the class to continue their studies independently in the biomedical field.
This objective is achieved through formal teaching and other training activities provided both within individual courses and during the internship period.
In particular, the Master's graduate develops the professional abilities required for entry into the workforce and therefore the necessary abilities to select and use tools for applying analytical methodologies in the field of basic and applied biomedical sciences. Additionally, they acquire the ability to process the analytical data obtained and to present their results, also using computer tools.
Learning Ability will be assessed through specific written and/or oral tests for each teaching unit, as well as in the final examination.
Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area Referring to the European system of study title descriptors (Dublin descriptors), graduates of the Master's Degree in Sanitary Biology belonging to class LM 6 are able to apply their knowledge and understanding by demonstrating a professional approach to work in the biosanitary field, enabling them to:
a) work with considerable autonomy in developing, managing, and performing biochemical-clinical, biomolecular, microbiological, and toxicological analyses as required by current national, community, and, more generally, international regulations in laboratories of research institutions, public and private companies contracted with the National Health Service.
b) carry out their professional research activities in the biomedical field with considerable autonomy, also assuming responsibility for projects and structures in both public and private sectors.
c) carry out monitoring and manage specific laboratory activities for pharmacological, toxicological, microbiological, and methodological control in various stages of production of drugs, medications, diagnostics, dietary products, and generally products requiring authorization from the Ministry of Health;
d) prepare monitoring protocols for pollutants and contaminants present in the environment (water, air, soil), microenvironment, and food, according to certification and quality standards;
e) plan prevention and health education interventions for the population in relation to toxicological aspects arising from chemical and biological environmental pollution;
f) carry out their professional activities in various application areas of applied toxicology, in public and private structures, in dependent or freelance capacity.
The Master's graduate's ability to apply knowledge and understanding is achieved through highly professionalizing courses and seminar activities in collaboration with experienced professionals from the workplace, internship activities, and the final thesis, which together provide an interdisciplinary perspective for applying knowledge. Additionally, a significant proportion of individual teaching units will include practical exercises designed to stimulate application abilities, during which students will independently carry out the proposed activities.
The Master's graduate will develop the professional abilities required for entry into the workforce, namely the necessary abilities to select and use tools for applying analytical methodologies aimed at biomedical research and laboratory diagnostics. Additionally, they will have the ability to process the analytical data obtained and to present their results, also using widely used computer tools such as Word, PowerPoint, and Excel.
The achievement of the specific educational objectives of each teaching activity will be verified through laboratory activity reports and pass exams. An additional moment, both for the student to apply knowledge and understanding and for the faculty to verify the achievement of the objectives of this descriptor, will be constituted by the final examination.

AREA BIOMEDICAL Ability to work with considerable autonomy in developing, managing, and performing biochemical-clinical, biomolecular, microbiological, and toxicological analyses as required by current national, community, and, more generally, international regulations in laboratories of research institutions, public and private companies contracted with the National Health Service.
Ability to carry out their professional research activities in the biomedical field with considerable autonomy, also assuming responsibility for projects and structures in both public and private sectors.
Ability to carry out monitoring and manage specific laboratory activities for pharmacological, toxicological, microbiological, and methodological control in various stages of production of drugs, medications, diagnostics, dietary products, and generally products requiring authorization from the Ministry of Health;
Ability to carry out their professional activities in various application areas of applied toxicology, in public and private structures, in dependent or freelance capacity.
CONTEXTUAL KNOWLEDGE AND FINAL EXAM Ability to write technical reports on results obtained using appropriate calculation software or a series of measurements.
Ability to deliver an oral presentation.
Ability to apply acquired knowledge in the workplace context of bio-sanitary laboratories of research institutions, public and private companies contracted.
Ability to read and understand scientific documents, European regulations, and documents in English.

Communication Skills.
Master's degree graduates in Health Biology acquire through the training path the ability to interact with scientific and professional figures of different or similar cultural background during practical training or during curricular extramural training.
These communication skills will be achieved through training activities that include the presentation of technical-scientific topics, such as the presentation of literature data as an integral part of each course and the presentation of research data obtained during the internship within journal clubs organized by the respective university and/or company supervisors.
Verification of achieving the objective of this descriptor will occur within in-course assessments, journal clubs, and the examination assessments scheduled at the end of the training activities.
The final exam with discussion of the results obtained during the internship will further evaluate the level of communication skills achieved. The planned training activities will also enable the health biologist, through adequate theoretical-practical preparation on the methods of investigation used in the biosanitary field, to have a good command of the scientific method of investigation and a good level of knowledge of the English language and scientific literature to communicate and present the results achieved, in national and international contexts.
Expected employment and professional opportunities for graduates.
Senior Biologist, Researcher. The Master's Degree in Health Biology allows the graduate to be employed in public or private structures, in dependent or freelance capacity, such as:
-universities and other public and private biomedical research bodies (IRCCS)
-pharmaceutical and diagnostic products industries;
-applied biotechnology laboratories;
-dietetic and food industries;
-National Health Service structures;
-conventioned diagnostic laboratories with the SSN;
-public and private structures dealing with medically assisted procreation;
-toxicological and environmental study and monitoring centers;
-bodies responsible for drafting technical regulations or quality certification;
-industries interested in developing biological and biochemical applications in the healthcare field.
Master's degree graduates possessing the requirements set by current regulations may participate in entrance exams for teacher training programs for primary and secondary schools.
Official teaching and assessment language(s).
ITALIAN Associated competencies for the role.
Senior Biologist, Researcher. The Master's degree graduate in Health Biology has in-depth knowledge of the interconnections between the structure and function of organs and systems, the pathogenic mechanisms underlying diseases, as well as the instrumental methodologies, analytical tools, and data analysis techniques in the field of Biomedical and Health Sciences.
Therefore, they possess the necessary competencies to work with broad autonomy in the sectors of basic and applied research in industry, healthcare, and public administration, to integrate into the development processes of new innovative technologies, and to carry out responsible tasks, particularly in biological and microbiological analysis laboratories, biological control, and quality control of products relevant to human health.
Description of admission tests.
The admission test procedures are indicated in the Didactic Regulations of the Master's Degree Course, available at: http://www.unisi.it Role in work context.
Senior Biologist, Researcher. Possession of the Master's degree in Health Biology, following successful completion of the State Exam for authorization to practice the profession of Biologist, allows operation within the public and private healthcare services and also in the professional fields of Health Biology as defined by the law establishing Section A of the professional register of the Order of Biologists (G.U. August 17, 2001, No. 190, General Series, Chapter VI, Articles 31-34). It also enables conducting biomedical research in universities and other public and private research bodies.
Additional information.
http://www.unisi.it/dipartimenti/dipartimento-scienze-della-vita Description of specific training objectives.
The Master's Degree Course in Health Biology aims to train a Biologist with specific competencies in the field of Biomedical and Health Sciences who will work in the Public and private healthcare sector (food, genetic, histological, and clinical biochemistry laboratories, public and private structures dealing with Medically Assisted Procreation) and in structures conducting research in the field of Applied Biomedical Sciences (e.g., Pharmaceutical Industries, small and medium enterprises in the diagnostic and biotechnology sectors, etc.).
The learning areas of the Health Biology degree course provide a suitable cultural foundation for accessing recognized Biosanitary Specialization Schools by the Ministry of Health, necessary for entering the managerial career of Biologist in both public and private healthcare sectors, as well as for Doctoral Programs in Biomedical Fields and Second-Level Master's Degrees.
The training path is structured into the following thematic blocks, including basic and applied disciplines: 1) Biodiversity and Environment Area, 2) Biomedical Area, 3) Contextual Knowledge and Final Project.
1. BIODIVERSITY AND ENVIRONMENT AREA Includes courses in relevant SSD for acquiring knowledge and skills in basic disciplines such as 'Zoology' (BIO/05) and 'Comparative Anatomy and Cytology' (BIO/06) and applied discipline such as 'Ecology' (BIO/07). The courses activated in these areas aim to acquire adequate and in-depth knowledge of pathogenic noxae and factors that may affect human health and environmental quality.
2. BIOMEDICAL AREA Includes courses in relevant SSD for acquiring knowledge and skills in basic disciplines such as Molecular Biology (BIO/11), Pharmacology (BIO/14), Human Anatomy (BIO/16), Histology (BIO/17), and Physiology (BIO/09) and applied disciplines such as Hygiene (MED/42), General Pathology (MED/04), Clinical Pathology (MED/05), Clinical Biochemistry (BIO/12), Clinical Microbiology (MED/07), Legal Medicine (MED/43). The courses activated in these areas aim to acquire adequate and in-depth knowledge of the normal and altered functioning of the human body, drugs, and other therapeutic means relevant to safeguarding human health and well-being, modern techniques for analyzing chemical-biochemical, cellular, genetic, immunological, and microbiological parameters relevant to human health, the scientific method of investigation, and current regulations for biosanitary laboratories.
3. CONTEXTUAL KNOWLEDGE AND FINAL PROJECT Contextual knowledge and primarily the final project, scheduled at the end of the training path, contribute to generating the comprehensive vision required for the specific training of the Health Biologist, mainly achieved through the integration of knowledge and skills in basic and applied disciplines.
These knowledge areas are attained through 1) laboratory activities aimed at acquiring adequate and in-depth knowledge of scientific instrumentation, organization, and management of biomedical laboratories, practical tools (acquisition, processing, and transmission of data and information using electronic tools) to apply acquired knowledge in a biosanitary laboratory; 2) opportunities for curricular extramural internships, to be carried out at research bodies, public and private companies, aimed at understanding the dynamics of the working world and applying knowledge; 3) English language knowledge at B2 level, for understanding scientific documents, European regulations, and communication.
The conclusion of the training path includes a final exam based on the work carried out by the student during the internship period, concerning various aspects of Health Biology, presented in a written report organized according to internationally accepted scientific standards.
