Professional Status Conferred by the Degree.
Cultural Anthropologist Career opportunities are certainly within a highly specialized area that, at present, appears to be constantly growing, albeit in forms of flexibility and transferability of skills that make the overall profile of these professionals difficult to measure quantitatively. The follow-up of graduates from previous specialized degrees and the interclass degree from which the current course originated allows for a broad occupational recognition over the medium term, from which the following career paths can be inferred.
Master's graduates, according to the individual in-depth path pursued, may propose for high-level professional roles in public bodies and private institutions operating in the fields of cultural heritage, artistic heritage, museum and archival management, protection of demo-ethnoanthropological heritage, and valorization of traditional expressive knowledge and skills. Master's graduates who have deepened the anthropology of image and performance may alternatively access occupational areas related to expressive design, artistic production, and various creative and performance activities.
Master's graduates may also assume high-level professional roles in public bodies, voluntary organizations, and governmental and non-governmental development support organizations, contributing with the knowledge methods and critical toolkit of their multidisciplinary training.
The Master's degree naturally opens to the research sector, encompassing both public university research and research supported by foundations and private bodies.
For graduates in the Master's degree class LM-1, the sector of volunteering and public intervention in society is also open, particularly concerning bodies interested in phenomena such as migration flows, reception policies, and control of exclusion processes (racism, gender discrimination), and dependency (access to work, political representation). Institutions overseeing positive processes of hybridization (school and neighborhood integration), affirmation of new social subjectivities, new forms of family and collective experience, and valorization of popular and basic cultural traditions' communicative and expressive heritage will also find these competencies relevant.
Career opportunities can, in summary, be identified in cultural and research institutions (foundations, private institutes, and universities), as well as in cooperation bodies (governmental and non-governmental), social and cultural voluntary associations, scientific journalism, publishing, cultural tourism, territorial promotion bodies, expressive design in both social and cultural industry contexts. The flexibility of the offered training is only partially represented in the professional career coding as specified by Istat codes. The following summary should be considered a general and incomplete overview of a specialized professional field that spans multiple areas, from information to cultural markets, from cooperation to development and local bodies. The Master's training offered enables access to specific research doctorates in the anthropological field and interdisciplinary areas (semiotics, performance, cognitive psychology), thus aspiring to future roles in University Teaching within the humanities, as well as, based on previous experience, positions as Manager of Cultural Organizations or Manager of Humanitarian Organizations.
Final Exam Characteristics The final exam consists of writing a written work (thesis) based on a research experience or, alternatively, a thorough bibliographic and documentary review. For those who have specialized in other expressive/communication modalities, the written work serves as support for the audiovisual, hypertextual, or multimedia product, which will be considered the main work for final assessment.
The Master's thesis may involve various documentation procedures (audiovisual, hypertextual, digital, etc.) and must result from an independent and original research; in cases where the research initiative develops within a broader project, the personal contribution must be clearly identifiable. The process of defining the subject, methodological options, bibliographic updates, and analytical deepening constitutes an integral part of the final product, which will be submitted for evaluation by the Master's Committee. Therefore, the final exam must demonstrate that the student has acquired autonomous capabilities in designing and conducting original research; analytical and theoretical-methodological synthesis; completeness of the investigation; originality of conclusions. The Master's thesis must also demonstrate proficiency in accessing and utilizing international bibliographies, including extensive use of foreign language materials.
These elements—solid theoretical foundation, comprehensiveness of comparison with existing scientific literature, methodological rigor in both ethnographic and editorial phases, originality of approach, and innovation of contribution—along with the oral presentation and discussion of the work with the committee members, contribute to the final grade.
The final exam is conducted through the presentation of the research, with the support of the thesis tutor and supervisor, followed by a discussion initiated by the correlating professor's report and open to interventions from other committee members. The projection/exhibition of final audiovisual, multimedia, hypertextual, or other expressive/communication products is permitted, provided they are unequivocally attributable to the candidate.
The evaluation of the thesis (and exam) is added to the admission grade, calculated as the weighted average of the grades, rounded to the thousandth and converted to the traditional centesimal scale. The Master's Committee has additional grades available, as previously defined by the Faculty of Letters and Philosophy and now under review by the Department of Social Sciences, Politics, and Cognitive Sciences. Of the five available grades, one is awarded automatically if there is an international study experience within the university's internationalization programs.
The Master's thesis is awarded a total of 27 credits.
Required Knowledge for Admission The knowledge required for admission to the Master's degree consists of a solid general humanistic foundation (anthropological, sociological, historical, philosophical, literary), certified by possession of a relevant degree (corresponding to one of the following degree classes: L-1, L-3, L-5, L-6, L-10, L-11, L-12, L-15, L-19, L-20, L-24, L-36, L-37, L-39, L-40, L-42, L-43 under D.M. 270/2004); a core of at least 42 ECTS, within the disciplinary groups characterizing the training project (courses in artistic, philosophical, psycho-pedagogical, oriental, historical, geographical, demographic, economic, and sociological disciplines, as well as anthropological courses); knowledge of English as a basic resource for addressing international bibliographies and studies, and in preparation for achieving the B2 level as a graduation requirement; and basic computer skills documentation. Other more technical measures are detailed in the course's didactic regulation, including criteria for evaluating curricular credits from master's degrees or other master's qualifications, and verification procedures for competencies when the average grade is below the required threshold of 27/30.
The personal preparation verification test is conducted orally through an interview with a committee composed of three professors from the Master's program, appointed annually by the Teaching Committee, aimed at assessing the candidate's knowledge within the chosen study area and the coherence of their training project with the offered curriculum. The test is considered passed if the candidate demonstrates good ability in navigating theoretical-methodological themes and key developments in the history of studies, as well as sufficient ability to identify and frame, theoretically and methodologically, a research area within which they have initiated or intend to develop a personal specialization.
Degree Awarded.
Master's Degree in Anthropology and Languages of Imagery Teaching Delivery Method Conventional Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area Having acquired higher-level competencies beyond the first-cycle university education and tested them through a personal research project culminating in the Master's thesis, Master's graduates will be able to act responsibly in theoretical and methodological terms within anthropological/ethnographic, semiotic, and language theory, as well as theory and history of performance and visual/audiovisual representation.
In particular, Master's graduates must be able to design and conduct original research, grounded in solid methodological competencies in ethnographic/semiotic/sociological and historical fields, to study in the following areas:
. Cultural representation;
. Anthropology of the contemporary world;
. Languages of performance and visual representation.
Graduates of the Master's program must master the fundamental tools related to the intersection of disciplinary areas converging on the anthropological theoretical/methodological axis (semiotics, performance disciplines, cognitive psychology), having also gained research and in-depth experience to produce original research, with full critical and scientific autonomy, and to navigate professional contexts in the technical and specialized needs of the labor market regarding knowledge of cultural systems, their representative practices, cultural mediation, and cultural heritage management.
This goal is achievable through personal study and a teaching approach that alternates traditional frontal lectures with active seminar and laboratory practice, particularly designed to intertwine diverse knowledge and methodologies, thereby concretely demonstrating to students in the training phase the integration of competencies and perspectives that constitute the core of this project.
Learning assessments will be conducted in written and oral form, as well as through the development of personal research and application projects, preparatory to the demanding final thesis work, which synthesizes the multiple methodologies acquired.
The Master's degree, in connection with doctoral schools, local public institutions, and cultural enterprise subjects, aims to become a hub for promoting study meetings and communication of the most advanced scientific and teaching methodologies, with particular emphasis on international student experiences through specific collaboration protocols with other universities and entities engaged in scientific training, such as the École de Hautes Études en Sciences Sociales (EHESS), the London School of Economics, the University of Toronto, the International School of Theatre Anthropology (LISTA) in Holstebro, DK, The University of Eurasian Theatre, the Italian Institute of Human Sciences (SUM), the Interdisciplinary Center for the Study of Arts (CISA) in Bucharest, the University of Arts and Design of Taik (Finland), the Center for Semiotics of Visual Arts in Puebla, the University of Paris VIII – S. Denis, and the Complutense University of Madrid.

Judgment Autonomy.
It is a foundational objective of the course to promote critical thinking and judgment autonomy among its students, actively stimulating the focus on personal study and research paths, individualized even when developed within collective projects and more enduring than the biennium, activating seminars for discussion and debate that may be suggested from multiple directions: from the students' own needs, from formalized relationships with social, political/institutional, and/or professional subjects of interest, from the research, experimentation, and international connection experiences that the teachers themselves will bring.
In addition to traditional complementary activities to teaching (archival and bibliographic documentation, through the databases to which the University is entitled), it is intended to continue proposing field research exercises, internships at institutions and subjects of artistic and/or spectacular production, as synthesis experiences and confrontation with scientific research, which enhance the critical and personalized data of the educational path. Constant reference to external realities will also ensure necessary reflection on research ethics and the ethical and social role of the researcher in contemporary society, with particular attention to issues connected to the position of the anthropological gaze and its relationships with other disciplinary positions represented in the course (semiotician, sociologist, historian, etc.).
Verification of such abilities will be entrusted to examination tests (which for this reason will never be entirely delegated to tests, written exercises, or other mediated forms) as well as to specific seminar moments of discussion on texts or exercises.
Learning Abilities.
The educational process aims to consolidate students' learning abilities by constantly intertwining acquired and consolidated disciplinary competencies with models of scientific operation in action, drawn from the research heritage that will be constantly made available by the teaching staff in their respective scientific fields. The open educational offer that shares ongoing research experience constitutes the main path to trigger that virtuous process of acquiring theoretical-methodological tools that includes verifying their heuristic potential, which can lead to the formation of an autonomous scientific profile, methodologically responsible, and firmly rooted in the state of the art of the various disciplines that compose the overall educational framework. Such learning ability will be subject to various verification opportunities throughout the educational process; with the same purpose, it is planned that the path concludes with the elaboration of an autonomous research work (final exam) that highlights the Master's graduates' ability to apply in a personal and original way the knowledge and methodological tools acquired during the course. This final synthesis must be the culmination of the entire educational process and thus involve in the most organic way the different disciplines present in the course.
The personal contribution of students and their active contribution to the organization and conduct of lectures and seminars will also be valued. The primary objective is to stimulate as much as possible a critical and active attitude, indispensable prerequisite for entering the job market or further training and research paths. Learning abilities will be verified during normal teaching activities and examination tests.
Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area The educational offer aims to form critical, interpretative, and analytical abilities that students can autonomously apply to themes related to cultural representation and anthropology of the contemporary world, in a markedly interdisciplinary perspective, as befits those who engage in understanding cultural representation in the image civilization and the representational practices of cultural otherness. Students will be invited to a theoretical and practical confrontation with themes related to the representation of self and other; to meeting the different in here and elsewhere; to expressive practices that characterize cultural and identity reactions to ongoing transformations. In particular, the application of competencies will occur in relation to the needs of entities and administrations responsible for managing cultural and educational policies, with attention to migration issues, and with organizations working and producing international policies for growth and development. The acquisition of such abilities, through study and personal application under the direction of the course teachers, will be verified in specific in-course assessments (also composed of practical exercises) and in the final examination tests for each course.

Communication Skills.
The professional opportunities of the course require, in addition to precise methodological imperatives inherent to the basic anthropological field, to prioritize the consolidation or acquisition of communication skills that can connect the student—and subsequently the Master's graduate—with individuals, institutions, and various environments, both for documentary purposes and for potential applications in intervention projects or scientific communication. The educational path therefore recognizes a clear priority for acquiring communication skills, placing at the center of the teaching experience the direct and multi-oriented communication of competencies and/or formative experiences being developed, encouraging the use of seminar and dialogic teaching models, and valuing both oral presentations and the preparation of critical reports, reviews, research reports, and readings, to be spread throughout the entire educational path. The acquisition of communication skills will be monitored starting from the gradient of appropriateness, breadth, and critical control of scientific language, both in the phase of verifying acquired knowledge and in communicating the research experiences conducted. The technological spectrum within which acquired or consolidated communication skills must be verified ranges from simple direct oral communication to mediated and hypermedia communication techniques, aiming for maximum integration between textual languages and image and performance languages.
Expected occupational and professional opportunities for graduates.
Cultural Anthropologist: The occupational opportunities are certainly within a highly specialized area that, at present, appears to be constantly growing, even though the flexibility and transferability of skills make these profiles difficult to measure quantitatively. Master's graduates may also assume high-level professional roles at public bodies, voluntary and development support organizations, governmental and non-governmental, where they can contribute with the cognitive methods and critical arsenal of the multidisciplinary training that will constitute their professional baggage. The Master's degree, of course, opens to the research sector, consisting of both public university research and research supported by foundations and private entities. For graduates in the Master's class LM-1, the sector of volunteering and public social intervention is also open, concerning entities interested in phenomena such as migration flows and reception policies and control of exclusion processes (racism, gender discrimination) and dependency (forms of access to work, political representation). Institutions overseeing positive processes of valorization of hybridization phenomena (school and neighborhood integration), affirmation of new social subjectivities and new forms of family and collective experience, and valorization of communicative and expressive heritage of popular and basic cultural traditions will also be interested in these competencies. Professional opportunities can, in summary, be identified in cultural and research institutions (foundations, private institutes, and universities), as well as in cooperative bodies (governmental and non-governmental), social and cultural volunteer associations, scientific journalism, publishing, cultural tourism, territorial promotion entities, and expressive design in both the social and cultural industry sectors. The flexibility of the proposed training is only partially represented in the codification of professional opportunities as prescribed by Istat codes. The offered Master's training allows access to specific research doctorates for the anthropological area and interdisciplinary intersection areas (semiotics, performance, cognitive psychology), and therefore to aspire to future access to University Teaching roles within the humanities, as well as, based on previous experience, to positions of Cultural Organization Director or Humanitarian Organization Director.
Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIANO Associated competencies for the role.
Cultural Anthropologist: Capable, due to the empirical and experiential component of their training, to interact with the constituted reality, to the point of assuming its management and orientation, on one hand, and led to analytical reflection, in a markedly self-reflective key, on the other, the anthropologist, in practice and where organizational framework and job division allow, exercises a guiding function and a guide for action. The LM1 training path therefore leaves students maximum freedom to choose, among the specializations the department can offer, the one that best aligns with individual vocations and talents, thus proposing even very diverse figures to a similarly varied labor market. For the local culture operator, capable of designing and/or managing cultural promotion policies, revitalizing local knowledge and/or production chains, the orientation towards heritage and performance anthropology overlaps with the competencies of performance operators, event organizers, and cultural program directors. In this case, the anthropologist will apply their knowledge and know-how in the production of images, cultural representations, and communicative and artistic installations. For the operator in development processes or policies for recovering marginality, anthropological knowledge overlaps with social services professions, development economists, family consultants, and participatory practice scientists; in this case, medical/health knowledge, on one hand, and psychological/psychiatric specializations, define the poles of a professional continuum that theoretical training renders "concrete" without disabling its self-corrective and self-formative potentialities.
Description of admission tests.
The verification of personal preparation is conducted orally, through an interview with a commission composed of three professors from the Master's program (assigned annually by the Teaching Committee), focusing on the candidate's knowledge of the chosen study area and the congruence of their training project with the offered educational path. The test will be considered passed if the candidate demonstrates good ability to navigate theoretical-methodological themes and key points in the history of studies, as well as sufficient ability to identify and frame, theoretically and methodologically, a research area within which they have initiated or intend to develop a personal specialization. The test may be held in one or more sessions. If multiple sessions are scheduled, those not admitted in the first session may reapply for the next session. The test may be attended by graduates meeting the curricular requirements and students enrolled in courses who have acquired, by the test date, at least 120 CFU in total. Students who have passed the verification test will be admitted conditionally and may enroll provided they obtain their degree within the deadlines for enrollment closure.
Direct Admission
1. Graduates who are exempt from the verification test, as they are recognized to already possess the required personal preparation, are:
a) those who have acquired at least 20 CFU in the sectors M-DEA-01, L-ART/04-08, M-STO/04-07, SPS/07-08, M-FIL/05 with a weighted average grade not lower than 27/30;
b) those who have obtained their degree with a grade not lower than 100/110, or, even if they have a lower degree grade, have acquired with a weighted average grade not lower than 27/30 the CFU required in their study plan for the following SSD: M-DEA-01, L-ART/04-08, M-STO/04-07, SPS/07-08, M-FIL/05.
Graduates with the required curricular qualifications are also exempt from the admission test. Graduates who, despite having the right to participate, have already passed all required courses in their study plan with a weighted average grade not lower than 27/30 in the SSD: M-DEA-01, L-ART/04-08, M-STO/04-07, SPS/07-08, M-FIL/05 by the test date will also be exempt from the test. In the absence of this requirement, students who plan to graduate by the enrollment closure deadline may choose to take the test, with the understanding that, regardless of the outcome, they will be admitted if their degree grade by the deadline is not lower than 100/110.
Role in the workplace context.
Cultural Anthropologist: The strong theoretical and analytical inclination of the cultural anthropologist's training path makes, from a professional perspective, a figure capable of addressing a relatively wide range of responsibilities, both in terms of intervention fields or grounds and in terms of operational level, which can range from study to planning/implementation of an intervention in the concrete reality. The analytical imprint of the predominantly theoretical training reflects in a high transferability of competencies—within social, geographical, and cultural contexts that are even highly differentiated—and a pronounced aptitude for complementarity with other knowledge, both theoretical and managerial and/or technical/operational. The breadth of occupational possibilities varies according to the specialization chosen by the graduate within the overall educational proposal, ranging from the operator in the field of cultural representations—artistic productions and cultural performances—to the operator in international cooperation and social policies. If we simplify by identifying these two areas—the cultural work on one hand, and social intervention on the other—as the main directions of anthropological employment, the function that emerges is that of an expert in decoding the practices, logics, and policies of the action in question, capable of acting reflectively (participant observation, research/action) as well as documenting/analyzing the actions or processes that need to be guided or understood (participant observation, comparative attitude, holistic approach, and connective skills of micro-analysis with macro contexts). The cultural anthropologist who has professionally translated their scientific competencies is a valuable resource for entities and institutions that aim for creative and innovative yet concrete goals, such as a local culture museum, a service for caring for socially weak or disadvantaged subjects, or an economic revitalization intervention in a marginal area. Professions that often converge at various stages—from ideation, to feasibility study, to implementation, to follow-up—can find in the presence of a duly specialized anthropologist an effective professional medium between fields and knowledge, between needs and representations of reality that are not always reconcilable.

Description of specific educational objectives.
The course aims to train Master's graduates who:
a) possess advanced, in-depth, and up-to-date general knowledge of demo-ethnoanthropological disciplines and international debates on cultural representation practices, with particular reference to performance disciplines, multiculturalism, and its connection with performative and visual languages;
b) possess methodological knowledge and skills to design and implement anthropological research on social and socio-cultural dynamics, cultural representations, visual, audiovisual, and performance; to competently position themselves in the labor market interested in these areas, up to the experimentation of cognitive technologies and communication;
c) have developed awareness of specific themes of social structures, cultural dynamics, expressive languages, and artistic communication processes, identity construction processes, patrimonialization processes, the circularity of exchange between different cultural systems, the plurality of self-representation and self-definition paths, in a context of globalization and rediscovery of local identities and global cultural heritage.
d) possess good oral and written knowledge of at least one European language.
The educational path includes a first year dedicated to acquiring part of the characteristic knowledge tools, both disciplinary (12 CFU out of 24 in M-DEA/01) and interdisciplinary (SPS/08, M-STO/04, M-FIL/05), and the initiation of acquiring the critical and methodological tools characteristic of the professional profile pursued by the student (drawing also from the Affine sectors), according to a differentiated and personalized approach within the limits allowed by the regulations, continuing into the second year and refining in the experience of direct ethnographic research for the thesis. Along the biennial path, students are given the opportunity to acquire skills that may be useful for potential specialization paths in teaching. The educational process will also benefit from student tutoring, the availability of laboratories for experimenting with documentary and analytical practices, and will encourage all possible forms of research practice experience, from ethnography to the documentation of artistic practices and cultural representations. A successful completion of this path places particular emphasis on the final thesis, based on research experiences or experimental applications promoted by the reference professors in close connection with questions emerging from institutions, territory, and other ethnographic interest areas, including live intersections with more reflective artistic and performance practices, capable of certifying the acquisition of tested scientific methods, languages, and critical autonomy.
At the end of the study path, Master's graduates, in relation to the options exercised, are expected to have acquired:
I) knowledge of specific topics, such as migration movements, gender relations, family forms, economic action strategies and political confrontation, religious and symbolic systems, dynamics of cultural heritage production, artistic and communicative performances.
II) the theoretical foundations of anthropology, declinable in its various basic competencies, but especially open to experimentation and innovation regarding themes, languages, investigation methods, and sharing and communication of acquisitions.
III) the ability to adapt knowledge to at least one regional area, which can be defined at various scales, and placed within the tradition of classical regional ethnographies, including European ethnology and the broader European-Western cultural area.
IV) the aptitude to actively interact with other disciplines such as demography, cultural and communication processes sociology, cultural semiotics, as well as theories and practices of creation and production in the artistic, media, and performance fields.
V) the ability to use anthropological, semiotic, and sociological tools to describe the relationships between expressive practices and cultural identities, along with solid knowledge of theory and history of image, visual representation, and performance, and analytical methodologies such as anthropology, semiotics, and sociology;
VI) critical and interpretative dramaturgical, sociological, and aesthetic skills regarding cinema, theater, and music, and a comprehensive knowledge of the various media characterizing contemporary communication;
VII) the ability to recognize and interpret expressive languages characterizing cultural production, with particular attention to visual representation and performance;
VIII) organizational, critical, and creative abilities for cultural and performance events and products.

Secondary School Diploma Fees and Contributions For information on tuition and contribution amounts, visit the University website www.unisi.it/tasse Dates and Deadlines For information on dates and deadlines, visit the University website "Study Plan" www.unisi.it/didattica/immatricolazioni-e-iscrizioni/immatricolazioni Roles Student Mobility Responsibilities LEONARDO DISPERATI Program, Texts and Objectives Professional title conferred by the degree.
Graduate Surveyor The graduate in Technologies for Environment, Construction and Territory L-P01, qualified for the profession of Graduate Surveyor, will be able to practice the profession in both public and private sectors. In particular, the main employment opportunities include:
- construction and maintenance companies for works, plants and civil infrastructure;
- professional offices and design companies for works, plants and civil infrastructure;
- public offices for design, planning, management and control of urban and territorial systems;
- companies, bodies, consortia and agencies for management and control of works and service systems;
- companies, public and private bodies, professional offices dealing with the design, planning, implementation and management of works and systems for environmental and territorial control and monitoring, soil protection, management of waste and environmental and energy resources;
- companies, laboratories, public and private bodies, professional offices dealing with measurements and surveys for territory control and protection.
Final Exam Characteristics The final exam consists of a Practical Assessment Test (PPV) and the presentation of a written thesis, prepared under the guidance of one or more supervisors. The PPV aims to verify knowledge, skills, abilities and operational autonomy necessary for the exercise of the profession and focuses on topics consistent with professional activities and the specificities of the study course. It is assessed with an "adequate" judgment by a committee composed equally of teachers and representatives of relevant professional realities. The "adequate" judgment does not contribute to determining the graduation grade.
The written thesis (or dissertation) addresses theoretical or practical-applied themes covered during the training path.
Passing the final exam with a grade expressed in hundredths enables the exercise of the profession of Graduate Surveyor.
Required Knowledge for Access To be admitted to the Professional Orientation Bachelor's Degree in Technologies for Environment, Construction and Territory L-P01, it is necessary to hold a secondary school diploma, or another foreign qualification recognized as suitable.
The Bachelor's Degree is a locally programmed course and the number of places will be defined annually based on available resources. Access modalities will be specified in the annual course call and published on the University of Siena website.
Initial preparation verification will be conducted according to the modalities provided by the Didactic Regulations of the Professional Orientation Bachelor's Degree in Technologies for Environment, Construction and Territory L-P01. In case of any deficiencies in initial preparation, Additional Educational Requirements (OFA) will be assigned to be remedied within the first year of the course.
Knowledge and Understanding.
Basic Training The basic learning area courses ensure students achieve an adequate level of knowledge and understanding of the fundamentals of mathematics, physics and chemistry.
In particular, the course on Fundamentals of Mathematics aims to cover basic knowledge of linear algebra, set theory concepts, functions of a single variable, differential and integral calculus concepts, and elementary methods for solving differential equations.
The course on Fundamentals of Physics aims to introduce basic concepts regarding physical quantities, their measurement, mechanics of point masses, rigid bodies, fluids, and thermodynamics.
The course on Materials Chemistry will provide knowledge of general inorganic and organic chemistry, atomic structure and periodic table, chemical bonds, states of matter (solid, liquid, gaseous), acid-base equilibria, electrochemistry, and materials for innovative technologies.
In the training path, students also acquire fundamental concepts of computer science and its practical application through the use of spreadsheets to solve real problems, perform data analysis, create graphs and visual representations to facilitate communication and interpretation of results.
These courses are complemented by knowledge and understanding, in written and oral form, of the English language at QCER B1 level or higher, also referring to disciplinary vocabulary.
Interdisciplinary Technical-Professional Training The courses in the interdisciplinary technical-professional area include:
● drawing and digital representation disciplines, where students deepen traditional and modern representation techniques and tools. In particular, students acquire knowledge of representation techniques for buildings and territory, through surveying, drawing and three-dimensional modeling;
● technical legislation disciplines for public and private works, which allow students to acquire knowledge of law and procedures for managing the administrative process necessary for drafting building permits.
Construction The courses in the Construction learning area aim to provide students with the theoretical and practical knowledge necessary for professional activity.
In particular, they cover:
● the course on Science and Technology of Structures, which enables students to acquire knowledge and understanding of basic theoretical aspects, always introduced starting from concrete elementary problems, regarding structural design for the main construction types and their structural behavior under different possible loads. The course on Soil and Rock Mechanics aims to provide students with the fundamentals of the physical-mechanical properties of these natural materials in relation to the resistance and stability of soils and slopes;
● the course on Architecture, Urban Planning and Territory Protection, where students develop knowledge and understanding of construction themes related to historical, contemporary and future built environments, in their architectural individuality and integration into the urban context.
● the course on Energy Certification provides the fundamentals of building energy efficiency, illustrating methodologies and techniques for design and investigation, both for new construction and renovation, and methods for evaluating building energy consumption.
Territory The courses in the Territory area cover:
● the study of methods and techniques for evaluating soils and properties, through which students acquire knowledge and understanding of principles and estimation methods for analyzing costs in construction production, analyzing real estate markets, and verifying the financial feasibility of projects;
● the study of modern geomatic technologies (GIS, remote sensing, digital photogrammetry, laser scanning, satellite positioning, etc.), through which students acquire competence for cadastral, topographic and environmental studies, also applying advanced measurement and surveying techniques;
● the study of basic geological processes necessary for understanding the nature and characteristics of the rocky substrate on which various types of constructions and structures are based; basic knowledge of geological map reading and geomorphological processes influencing landscape and territory development and stability will also be provided.
● the study of geological materials and their industrial equivalents, their chemical, physical and mechanical properties, crystalline structure, mineral phases, and their importance for use in construction (ceramic and brick materials; binders and cements; glass; metallurgy and alloys).

SECTION: JUDGMENT AUTONOMY
URL: https://unisi.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/11295

Judgment autonomy.
The ability for autonomous judgment will be acquired particularly in laboratories and internship activities. The student will examine real case studies, acquire the ability to frame a single problem and independently identify appropriate solutions.
In summary, graduates will be able to:
- identify the most appropriate mathematical, physical, and statistical models for the contextual situation;
- interpret available information in civil and building projects, topographic surveys, and landscape and environmental context analyses of the territory;
- identify and collect additional information to better understand civil and building project and execution activities and the issues of the analyzed context, also at territorial scale.
The acquisition of judgment autonomy will be verified during the Degree Course through the evaluation of the effectiveness and quality of the produced work, as well as any classroom presentations. The final level of autonomy achieved by the student will be verified in the final exam through the evaluation of specifically prepared work.

Learning capacity.
The ability for autonomous learning is acquired within the training activities of individual courses, laboratories, and internships, and is further strengthened in activities related to the final exam.
In summary, graduates will have the ability to:
- autonomously learn updates regarding territory management and monitoring, civil and building works design and execution, including the evolution of regulations;
- draw from various bibliographic sources, both in Italian and English, to acquire new skills.
The verification of these abilities will be carried out through the evaluation of intermediate tests, individual and/or group work, and the judgment of the final exam.

Ability to apply knowledge and understanding.
Basic Training The student will be able to know and understand:
- basic concepts of mathematics;
- basic concepts of elementary physics;
- fundamentals of materials chemistry;
- basic concepts of computer science.
Finally, the student will be able to read, write, and sustain a conversation in English at a level equivalent to B1 of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR).
The teaching tools used to achieve these goals include frontal lessons, exercise activities, and the use of software dedicated to various disciplines.
The ability to apply the received knowledge is verified through written and/or oral profit tests that involve solving specific problems to verify that the student has developed interdisciplinary problem-solving skills.

Interdisciplinary Technical-Professional Training The student will be able to:
● consciously apply the rules of descriptive geometry;
● develop a design process and employ different representation techniques;
● manage building, valuation, and urban planning procedures and disputes;
● know the technical legislation for public and private works;
● apply notions of law and procedures to manage the administrative process necessary for drafting building procedures.
The knowledge and understanding abilities listed above are acquired by students through attendance at theoretical and practical courses, study of the teaching material indicated or provided by instructors, discussion and dialogue with instructors, performance of laboratory activities, and completion of a training internship and/or placement.
Verification of the acquisition of such knowledge involves the discussion of a design work and/or a technical report developed during the lecture period. The preparation of such works is consistent with the highly technical and professional nature of the Study Program.

Construction The student will develop the ability to apply knowledge and understanding regarding:
● basic topics of Structural Engineering;
● basic topics of Construction Engineering;
● basic topics of Rock Mechanics and geotechnics;
● drawing and design, at appropriate levels of depth, of a small building characterized by sustainability and innovative technologies;
● Energy Certification and methodologies and techniques for design and investigation, both for new construction and renovation.
The knowledge and understanding abilities listed above are acquired by students through attendance at theoretical and practical courses, study of the teaching material indicated or provided by instructors, discussion and dialogue with instructors, performance of laboratory activities, and completion of a training internship and/or placement.
Verification of the acquisition of such knowledge involves the discussion of a design work and/or a technical report developed during the lecture period. The preparation of such works is consistent with the highly technical and professional nature of the Study Program.

Territory The student will have acquired the ability to apply knowledge and understanding for:
● describing and interpreting cities, territory, and landscape and their interactions with geological and geomorphological environments and processes using geological analysis and urban planning design techniques;
● studying territory and environment through knowledge and use of various geomatic tools using advanced measurement, survey, and representation methods;
● analyzing costs in building production, being able to analyze real estate markets and verify the financial feasibility of projects.
The knowledge and understanding abilities listed above are acquired by students through attendance at theoretical and practical courses, study of the teaching material indicated or provided by instructors, discussion and dialogue with instructors, performance of laboratory activities, and completion of a training internship and/or placement.
Verifications involve the discussion of a design work and/or a technical report developed during the lecture period. The preparation of such works is consistent with the highly technical and professional nature of the Study Program.

SECTION: Communication Skills

Communication Skills.
The fundamental ability in the practice of the profession of Construction and Territory Technician is constituted by communication skills, which are expressed through clear exposition and the ability to synthesize necessary to communicate within a public and/or private organization, as well as with the various interlocutors involved in work processes.
Communication skills will be acquired in all training activities where students, individually or divided into small work groups, will need to communicate and interact effectively with each other. The verification of English language knowledge, level B1, will allow interaction with people from different countries. Written and oral communication skills will be regularly assessed during exam sessions and will constitute a criterion in the final evaluation.
In summary, graduates will be able to:
- effectively communicate information and discuss problems and solutions appropriate to the interlocutor, even in English;
- use appropriate technical language for the reference work context, even in English.
Expected occupational and professional opportunities for graduates.
Graduate Surveyor The graduate in Technologies for the Environment, Construction, and Territory L-P01, qualified for the profession of Graduate Surveyor, will be able to practice the profession in both public and private sectors. In particular, the main occupational opportunities include:
- construction and maintenance companies for works, facilities, and civil infrastructure;
- professional studios and design companies for works, facilities, and civil infrastructure;
- public offices for design, planning, management, and control of urban and territorial systems;
- companies, bodies, consortia, and agencies for management and control of works and service systems;
- companies, public and private bodies, professional studios involved in the design, planning, implementation, and management of works and monitoring systems for the environment and territory, soil protection, waste management, and environmental and energy resources;
- companies, laboratories, public and private bodies, professional studios involved in measurements and surveys for the control and protection of the territory.
Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIAN Competencies associated with the function.
Graduate Surveyor The competencies acquired by the graduate in the Professional Orientation Bachelor's Degree in Technologies for the Environment, Construction, and Territory concern adequate preparation in the relevant applied disciplines and a sufficient body of operational knowledge indispensable for working independently in areas such as:
- topographic, cartographic, and architectural surveying, including the subsequent creation of georeferenced geographic databases, using advanced digital technologies for surveying and restitution;
- activities based on the use of digital methodologies supporting urban and architectural planning and design;
- support activities for monitoring and diagnostics of structures, infrastructure, territory, and auxiliary facilities;
- activities related to the management and updating of cadastral, demarcation, and local authority databases;
- estimation evaluations;
- safety in site management and workplace management with the drafting of procedures for design and execution;
- analysis and monitoring activities aimed at energy efficiency, energy certification, and certification of environmental sustainability and healthiness;
- drafting of building procedures, technical specifications, maintenance plans, technical drawings, and forensic technical consulting activities;
- design, work management, and supervision of structural, distribution, and plant aspects related to modest constructions.
The graduate will also be adequately familiar with aspects concerning technical and economic feasibility, cost calculation, as well as the production and realization process of building works, auxiliary facilities, and territorial transformations.
Workplace Function.
Graduate Surveyor The Professional Orientation Bachelor's Degree in Technologies for the Environment, Construction, and Territory L-P01 is designed so that the graduate is configured as a qualified technician in the construction and civil infrastructure sector, and in territorial and environmental monitoring using new geomatic technologies.
The main tasks that this professional figure will routinely perform are:
- support functions for design and consulting activities carried out by more specialized professional figures in the field of monitoring and diagnostics of structures, infrastructure, and territory;
- autonomous activities in the estimation, topographic, cadastral, building, and territorial sectors;
- topographic and cartographic surveys and restitution, also in digital format, of territory-related data;
- autonomous or support activities in the field of technical and estimation appraisals;
- verification of the correct application of regulations and safety procedures in site management, with the drafting of procedures for design and execution;
- drafting of building procedures, technical specifications, maintenance plans, technical drawings, and forensic consulting activities;
- design, work management, and supervision of structural, distribution, and plant aspects related to modest constructions.
Description of specific educational objectives.
The Professional Orientation Bachelor's Degree in Technologies for the Environment, Construction, and Territory L-P01 aims to train a qualified technical-professional figure capable of responding to the demands expressed by the construction sector, within both organizations such as companies, engineering firms, and public administrations, as well as the practice of free profession. The graduate will be able to interpret the complexity of projects for building, infrastructure, and territory monitoring and development, also promoting the transition from traditional monitoring, design, and construction systems to digital ones, based on the implementation of various geomatic technologies (GIS, remote sensing, digital photogrammetry, etc.).
Based on the anticipated profile and delineated functions, in addition to the qualifying educational objectives of class L-P01, the following specific educational objectives are identified:
- know the methods of technical representation and computer-aided design (CAD) techniques;
- know the methods of creating and maintaining geographic databases (cadastral, demarcation, local authority, etc.);
- know the use of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) for managing and representing territorial and environmental data;
- know the methods for topographic and cartographic surveying using the most modern tools and software for remote sensing, digital photogrammetry, laser scanning, satellite positioning, etc.;
- know the methods for optimizing planning, implementation, and management of constructions through the use of codes (Building Information Modelling, BIM);
- know the building process and the organization of work in the construction sector, with particular reference to the implementation of planning and safety management systems;
- know the basic geological concepts useful for understanding the evolution and monitoring of territorial and environmental parameters;
- know the various types of geomatic materials for construction, from synthetic to natural stone materials and their acquisition according to sustainability models, and application possibilities;
- know the basic elements of private law and administrative law;
- know the main criteria and procedures for estimating costs, prices, and yield rates of real estate and land;
- know the procedures and methods for submitting cadastral procedures;
- know the procedures and methods for submitting basic building procedures;
- know the legislative framework regarding environmental, construction, and territorial governance and the main planning/evaluation/implementation tools provided by current regulations;
- know the techniques for managing and organizing a construction site and construction processes.
- acquire linguistic competencies (English language – level B1)
These objectives are achieved over the three years in which the Bachelor's Degree is structured.
During the training path, scientific disciplines that form the theoretical basis are deepened, with particular reference to areas such as chemistry (CHIM/01 – CHIM/03), physics (FIS/01 – FIS/03), and mathematics (MAT/01 – MAT/09).
The path also includes specific and professionalizing courses in the field of CAD design (ICAR/17), topographic surveying, representation, and monitoring of building and territorial heritage (with courses on modern geomatic techniques – ICAR/06), architecture, urban planning (ICAR/14), construction science and technology (ICAR/08 – ICAR/09), valuation (ICAR/22), and private and administrative law (IUS/01 and IUS/10).
The training extends to disciplinary areas such as telecommunications and remote sensing systems and basic geological aspects necessary for a correct understanding of territorial and environmental parameters. Activities are provided to offer knowledge on industrial geomatic materials and natural stone materials for construction and the determination of their physical-mechanical characteristics. These are considered strategic for monitoring lands and associated criticalities (flooded areas, landslide areas, etc.).
Over the three years, theoretical-practical laboratory activities are also provided, whose function is to integrate the disciplinary knowledge imparted through the courses.
Finally, the Practical Assessment Internship (TPV) and the final exam are provided. The TPV represents a crucial part of the training path both in terms of CFU (minimum 48 CFU) and educational relevance: it allows the student to receive direct training from companies, professional studios, and public administrations through the development of shared project topics, with constant support and supervision from an academic tutor and an industry tutor. The aim is to create strong integration with the business and public administration network, which will be available to support the students' project path, also in relation to the final exam.
The final exam consists of a Practical Assessment Test (PPV) and the presentation of the Thesis.
The student is qualified for the profession of Graduate Surveyor following the successful completion of the PPV, which assesses knowledge, competencies, skills, and operational autonomy necessary for practicing the aforementioned profession.
At the end of the training path, graduates in Technologies for the Environment, Construction, and Territory will have also acquired basic linguistic competencies, required in any professional field, corresponding to level B1 of the English language.

Admission Requirements Students with a High School Diploma or equivalent foreign degree may be admitted.
Required knowledge will include: general culture and logical reasoning, mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology.
Additionally, knowledge of English at least at level A2/2 (CEFR) is required.
Professional status conferred by the degree. Expected employment and professional opportunities for graduates (DM 19 February 2009, Article 4, Paragraph 6)
Graduates in Medical Radiology Techniques for Imaging and Radiotherapy are health professionals who perform their activities in departments and services of Diagnostic Imaging, Radiotherapy, or Nuclear Medicine within hospital and non-hospital structures of the National Health Service (SSN) and similar private structures, as well as in Scientific Research and Care Institutes. They may also be employed in industries producing, sales agencies operating in the specific sector of diagnostic and therapeutic equipment, in general. Technicians may also find employment in university and non-university biomedical research centers and may carry out freelance activities.
Final Exam Characteristics The final exam has the value of a state exam qualifying for professional practice (D.Lgs 502/1992, Article 6, Paragraph 3) and consists of:
a) a practical test during which the student must demonstrate having acquired the theoretical-practical and technical-operative knowledge and skills specific to the professional profile;
b) preparation of a thesis and its defense. See DM 19 February 2009, Article 7.
5 CFU will be awarded for the final exam.
The final exam cannot be repeated more than once.
Criteria for awarding the merit score will include: evaluation of the abilities demonstrated during the presentation and discussion of the thesis; judgment on the technical skills demonstrated during the practical test.
The final score is expressed out of 110.
If a total score of 110/110 is achieved, the president of the final exam committee will put forward the award of honors, which can only be granted unanimously by those present.
Required knowledge for access Students with a High School Diploma or equivalent foreign degree may be admitted.
Required knowledge will include: general culture and logical reasoning, mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology.
Additionally, knowledge of English at least at level A2/2 (CEFR) is required.
Degree Awarded. DEGREE IN MEDICAL RADIOLOGY TECHNIQUES FOR IMAGING AND RADIOTHERAPY
Teaching Delivery Method Conventional
Knowledge and Understanding. Generic Area Graduates in Medical Radiology Techniques for Imaging and Radiotherapy will have acquired the scientific foundations and theoretical-practical preparation, thus the necessary competencies to correctly manage and use various radiological techniques and methodologies for diagnosis and radiotherapy treatments according to the standards and guidelines currently adopted by the medical and scientific community.
They will have knowledge related to clinical risk management and research methodology, but above all the right mindset that drives towards continuous training and updating.
Area of Foundational, Biomedical and First Aid Sciences Knowledge of basic disciplines such as human anatomy, biology, physiology, and other biomedical disciplines for understanding basic pathophysiological events that characterize situations requiring appropriate assistive behavior, even in emergency and first aid cases.
Knowledge of basic computer and statistical notions fundamental in the field of medical statistics, computer science, electrical and electronic measurements used in biomedical and computerized equipment, as well as understanding the use and management of such data and measurements used or recorded.
Area of Prevention Sciences and Health Services Knowledge and understanding of the concept of health and disease. Knowledge of health determinants and situations, risk factors, behaviors, and activities that can compromise health, as well as prevention strategies, collective and individual protection systems, including targeted interventions for the protection of workers' and users' health and safety.
Basic knowledge of the main health systems adopted by various countries and the evolution and organization of the Italian health system.
Area of Diagnostic and Therapeutic Technical Sciences Knowledge of technologies, techniques, and methodologies of radiology and radiotherapy for correct application, aimed at the optimal diagnostic question or radiotherapy treatment, applying necessary radioprotection and safety measures.
Knowledge to manage and improve technical-diagnostic procedures for image acquisition and processing and radiotherapy treatment according to scientific evidence and diagnostic-therapeutic guidelines. Ability to continuously update in line with technological evolution.
Area of Psychosocial, Ethical, Legal and Health Management Sciences Knowledge and understanding of the importance and organizational complexity of a health system, the necessity and utility of acting in accordance with regulations and ethics, with the aim of maintaining or improving the health conditions of the population.
Understanding the need for optimization and good management of human and economic resources necessary for this purpose.
Understanding the importance of correct work relationships, the interdependence of health activities, team work while maintaining and improving professional autonomy without losing sight of it.
Area of Informatic and Linguistic Disciplines Knowledge and understanding of the English language to access international scientific literature, understand equipment user manuals and maintenance, and exchange information with foreign users and colleagues.
Basic knowledge of computer science for understanding the processes of management, analysis, processing, and computerized storage of clinical-radiological data and images.

Judgment autonomy.
The graduate in Medical Radiology Techniques, for Imaging and Radiotherapy must demonstrate the ability to: collect and interpret data and situations characterizing their professional activity in order to develop independent thinking and judgment, including reflection on relevant practices, social, scientific or ethical issues;
- use critical thinking skills to provide effective technical-diagnostic and therapeutic services;
- assume responsibility for their actions in relation to the goals and priorities of the work activity;
- identify criticalities within organizational contexts or diagnostic/therapeutic techniques, proposing solutions through the application of best evidence while fully respecting ethical and professional norms.
These results can be achieved through the following teaching tools, methodologies and training activities:
- Case discussions in small groups with presentations in plenary sessions
- Internship with supervised experiences by tutors in various contexts and with progressive acquisition of autonomy and responsibility
- Debriefing sessions to reflect and reprocess professional practice experiences The achieved results will be assessed through the following tools:
- Written and oral exams, staged case tests
- Evaluation feedback during the internship (through structured evaluation forms and clinical reports on professional practice)
- Structured objective station exam Learning abilities.
The graduate in Medical Radiology Techniques, for Imaging and Radiotherapy must develop abilities, strategies, learning methods or practical skills necessary to undertake, if any, further studies with a high degree of autonomy. In particular, they must demonstrate the ability to self-assess their competencies and development needs and to update themselves. They must also demonstrate independent study ability, autonomy in searching for information and the ability to promote their knowledge in academic and professional contexts.
These results can be achieved through the following teaching tools, methodologies and training activities:
- Problem-Based Learning (PBL)
- Use of contracts and self-learning plans to empower the student in planning their internship path and self-assessment
- Research methodology laboratories for bibliographic research (paper and online)
- Guided reading for critical evaluation of scientific and professional literature in both Italian and English The achieved results will be assessed through the following tools:
- Project work, reports on specific research assignments
- Tutor supervision on the internship path
- Active participation in work and debriefing sessions
- Punctuality and quality in the presentation of assignments Application of knowledge and understanding.
Generic Area The graduate in Medical Radiology Techniques, for Imaging and Radiotherapy must apply acquired knowledge, demonstrating an appropriate professional approach to work, the ability to identify, analyze and solve problems and issues, even interdisciplinary, related to their field of study. They must also demonstrate the ability to ensure the use of appropriate methods and technologies, guaranteeing necessary radioprotection and safety measures, and integrate their knowledge and skills while maintaining high quality standards in various fields of Medical Imaging, interventional radiology, Nuclear Medicine and Radiation Therapy. These abilities can be achieved through the following teaching tools, methodologies and training activities:
- Frontal lessons;
- Professional laboratories;
- Demonstrations, schemes and graphic materials;
- Case discussions, project work, problem solving;
- Internship, which, based on the course year and theoretical knowledge, is carried out in increasingly complex sectors, with experiences supervised by expert tutors in various contexts and with progressive autonomy.
The acquired abilities will be assessed through the following tools:
- Oral exams
- Evaluation feedback throughout the internship (through portfolio, structured evaluation forms and reports on professional practice)
- Annual practical internship exam including verification of the ability to connect theoretical-practical understanding and problem-solving in non-routine situations that may occur during professional activity.
Propaedeutic, Biomedical and First Aid Sciences Area Apply the scientific and experimental method to the study of relevant anatomical-physiological and technological phenomena for the profession, demonstrating the ability to use knowledge of physics, biology, and anatomical and physiological knowledge for the correct use of equipment and techniques in medical imaging and radiation therapy. The assessment of knowledge and understanding abilities will be carried out through oral and written exams, simulated practical tests, written reports.
Prevention and Health Services Sciences Area Ability to apply knowledge regarding prevention and health in the work context and daily life.
The assessment of knowledge and understanding abilities will be carried out through oral and written exams, simulated practical tests, written reports.
Diagnostic and Therapeutic Technical Sciences Area Ability to apply procedures and techniques of medical imaging in all radiological sectors, including mammographic, angiographic and interventional, computed tomography, magnetic resonance, as well as in health physics, nuclear medicine and radiation therapy.
The assessment of knowledge and understanding abilities will be carried out through oral and written exams, professional internship evaluation, simulated practical tests, written reports.
Psychosocial, Ethical, Legal and Health Management Sciences Area Ability to apply knowledge and understanding to ensure comfort, safety and privacy for users; to adopt professional behaviors in line with ethical and professional principles; to act by identifying criticalities within organizational contexts or diagnostic/therapeutic techniques, proposing solutions through the application of best evidence while fully respecting ethical and professional norms.
The assessment of knowledge and understanding abilities will be carried out through oral and written exams, internship evaluation, simulated practical tests, written reports.
Informatics and Languages Sciences Area Ability to apply knowledge of the English language (and others) to enhance the quality of communication and understanding of international scientific literature. Ability to use information systems for the collection, analysis and management of demographic, clinical-radiological and statistical data in general.
The assessment of knowledge and understanding abilities will be carried out through oral and written exams, internship evaluation, simulated practical tests, written reports.

- Communicate with users while respecting cultural or ethnic differences;
- Adapt language as needed, using English when necessary, and verify understanding of provided information;
- Utilize various specific information and computer technologies in their professional field.

- Discussion of cases and paradigmatic relational situations in subgroups with presentations in plenary sessions
- Group and individual computer lab exercises on specific applications
- Internship with supervised experiences by tutors in various contexts with debriefing sessions to reflect and reprocess relational experiences with users and the team.

- Evaluation feedback during internship (through portfolios, structured evaluation sheets and clinical reports)

Description of admission tests.
The number of students admitted to the degree program is planned annually based on regional needs.

The test consists of a multiple-choice quiz on the following subjects: general culture, logical reasoning, mathematics, physics, chemistry and biology.

Medical Radiology Technician for Imaging and Radiotherapy Graduates in Medical Radiology Techniques, Imaging and Radiotherapy must acquire the necessary scientific foundations and theoretical-practical preparation to obtain professional licensing. They must also learn the methodology and culture required for continuous training, reaching a level of professional, decision-making and operational autonomy to ensure full mastery of all necessary competencies, knowledge, skills and attitudes, resulting in immediate employability in the workplace.
To achieve these goals, the graduate in Medical Radiology Techniques, Imaging and Radiotherapy must demonstrate the ability to:
- Manage technical-diagnostic procedures for acquisition and processing of imaging according to scientific evidence and guidelines, both in diagnostic and therapeutic contexts;
- Evaluate the technical quality of the produced image document and whether it meets the proposed investigation requirements, both in diagnostic and therapeutic contexts;
- Manage technical-diagnostic procedures for transmission and archiving of imaging, both in diagnostic and therapeutic contexts;
- Prepare and implement all necessary procedures for planning and practical implementation of radiotherapy treatments according to received clinical indications;
- Utilize technologies and tools for control, evaluation and quality review;
- Implement radioprotection and safety regulations and use personal protection devices;
- Establish communication of adequate professional level with users, other professionals and colleagues;
- Ensure comfort, safety and privacy of users during diagnostic investigations and radiotherapy treatments;
- Act responsibly towards users and the service, adopting professional behaviors in line with ethical and deontological principles;
- Receive and manage patient preparation for diagnostic investigations and radiotherapy treatment, obtaining informed consent within their competence;
- Collaborate with doctors, colleagues and all staff to ensure optimal service functioning and contribute to solving organizational problems;
- Utilize information systems for data collection, analysis and information management;
- Seek the best scientific evidence to deepen areas of uncertainty and improve professional practice;
- Know English for exchanging instructions and information within their specific field of competence.
Additional knowledge must be acquired in the following areas:
- Management in the Healthcare Sector;
- Regulations and state laws governing the technical profession and public health medical-surgical equipment;
- The most modern biotechnological methodologies and their applications;
- Value of automation, informatization and communication;
- Control, verification and quality assurance, also in relation to technological progress;
- Ability to identify, prevent and address critical events related to various types of risks connected to activities in different professional operational areas;
- Knowledge and ability to handle emergency situations within first aid;
- Knowledge of research methodology basics and their application to improve both efficiency and effectiveness of work contexts;
- Knowledge of regulations for protecting workers' and patients'/clients'/users' health;
- Ability to act consistently with professional disciplinary, ethical and deontological principles in technical-diagnostic and production contexts as defined in the training program and the deontological code;
- Ability to interact and actively collaborate in interprofessional teams;
- Teaching skills oriented towards continuous training of staff and tutoring of students during internship;
- Ability to identify risk factors, evaluate effects and intervene to protect work environments;
- Knowledge of the method for independent study and continuous training through systematic bibliographic research and critical reading of scientific articles.

Graduates in Medical Radiology Techniques, Imaging and Radiotherapy must acquire the necessary scientific foundations and theoretical-practical preparation to obtain professional licensing. They must also learn the methodology and culture required for continuous training, reaching a level of professional, decision-making and operational autonomy to ensure full mastery of all necessary competencies, knowledge, skills and attitudes, resulting in immediate employability in the workplace.
Learning areas of the Study Program:
PREPARATORY, BIOMEDICAL AND FIRST AID SCIENCES include basic disciplines such as Applied Physics, Medical Statistics, Electrical and Electronic Measurements, Computer Science, General Psychology necessary for their subsequent application in the professional field. This learning area also includes Human Anatomy, Physiology, Applied Biology, General Pathology and first aid courses such as Basic Surgery, Anesthesiology and Pharmacology.
PREVENTION AND HEALTH SERVICES SCIENCES aim to develop the ability to analyze health problems, dangers and risk factors, as well as prevention strategies, protection systems, both collective and individual, including interventions for the protection of workers' and users' health and safety.
DIAGNOSTIC AND THERAPEUTIC TECHNICAL SCIENCES include the disciplines characteristic of the profession such as Imaging and Radiotherapy, Applied Medical Technical Sciences, Neuroradiology, Applied Physics, with the objective of ensuring the correct use of appropriate methods and technologies according to received clinical indications for optimal diagnostic or therapeutic results, applying necessary radioprotection and safety measures. This learning area also includes Basic Radiobiology and Radioprotection and Integrated Diagnostics.
PSYCHOSOCIAL, ETHICAL, LEGAL AND HEALTH MANAGEMENT SCIENCES include knowledge of the complexity of the National Health Service organization, the importance and utility of acting in compliance with regulations and guidelines to improve professional autonomy and work relationships, interdependently with other healthcare operators;
INFORMATICS AND LANGUAGE DISCIPLINES include English language and informatics disciplines such as statistics for experimental and technological research and information processing systems.
A fundamental part of the degree program is the internship activity, which will allow students to acquire the skills necessary for professional practice. In this context, students will be able to apply the knowledge, methodologies and techniques learned in theoretical settings. The importance assigned to internship experiences in terms of both quality and quantity is emphasized, allowing students to gradually assume autonomy and responsibility under expert supervision.
