Required knowledge will include: general culture and logical reasoning, mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology.
Additionally, knowledge of English at least at level A2/2 (CEFR) is required. The number of students admitted to the C.d.L. is programmed each year based on regional needs.
The access test is common to all C.d.L. in the health area and is conducted on the same day at all Italian universities.
Professional status conferred by the title.
The main professional opportunities for the Biomedical Laboratory Technician are employment in biomedical and biotechnological analysis laboratories at all public health structures of the SSN and at accredited and non-accredited private biomedical and biotechnological structures, both for clinical diagnostics and research. It is estimated that among approximately 30,000 employees, there is a need for a 5-6% turnover.
Additional professional opportunities are employment in veterinary health, in zooprophylactic laboratories, and in industries producing laboratory reagents and equipment, as well as in the pharmaceutical, food, and cosmetic industries.
Final Exam Characteristics The final exam has the value of a state-licensed professional exam (D.Lgs 502/1992, art. 6, comma 3) and consists of:
a) a practical test during which the student must demonstrate having acquired the theoretical-practical and technical-operative knowledge and skills specific to the professional profile;
b) preparation of a thesis and its defense. See DM February 19, 2009, art.7
5 CFU will be awarded for the final exam.
The final exam cannot be repeated more than once.
Criteria for awarding merit score will include: evaluation of the abilities demonstrated during the presentation and discussion of the thesis; judgment on the technical skill demonstrated during the practical test.
The final score is expressed out of 110.
If a total score of 110/110 is achieved, the president of the final exam committee will put the awarding of honors to a vote, which can only be granted unanimously by those present.
Required knowledge for access Students with a High School Diploma or equivalent foreign degree may be admitted. Required knowledge will include: general culture and logical reasoning, mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology. Additionally, knowledge of English at least at level A2/2 (CEFR) is required.
Specific Educational Objectives.
The course objective is to provide students with the necessary scientific foundations and theoretical-practical preparation to be licensed to practice the profession of Biomedical Laboratory Health Technician, as well as the methodology and culture necessary for continuous training, and a level of professional, decision-making, and operational autonomy to ensure, at the end of the training path, full mastery of all necessary skills and their immediate applicability in the workplace.
Specific educational objectives consist of acquiring essential theoretical knowledge derived from basic sciences, with a view to their subsequent professional application and as a prerequisite for understanding the subjects characterizing the profession,
theoretical and practical knowledge of professionalizing sectors, with particular emphasis on innovative methodologies and the ability to plan, implement, and evaluate technical-diagnostic activities related to biochemical, molecular biology, hematology, and immunohematology investigations, toxicology, pharmacology (including galenic and magistral preparations), radioimmunology, immunological and immunometric, microbiological and virological, genetic, cytological, histological, and pathological anatomy (including diagnostic autopsy techniques);
knowledge of the most modern biotechnological methodologies and their applications; knowledge and evaluation of automation, informatization, and communication;
knowledge of management in the health sector; knowledge of state regulations and laws governing the technical profession, laboratory activities, medical-surgical facilities, and public health;
the ability to implement and verify Quality Control and Assurance, also in the context of continuous quality improvement in care;
the ability to collaborate with different professional figures in group health activities; the ability to identify, prevent, and address critical events related to various types of risks connected with activities in different laboratory areas;
knowledge and ability to resolve emergency situations within first aid; knowledge of the basics of research methodology and the ability to apply it to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of analysis and production processes;
knowledge of norms for worker health protection (particularly radioprotection); the ability to act in accordance with the disciplinary, ethical, and deontological principles of the profession in technical-diagnostic and productive situations as outlined in the training project;
the ability to interact and actively collaborate with interprofessional teams to plan and manage analysis and production activities, even in decentralized settings;
teaching skills oriented towards staff training and student internship tutoring; the ability to identify environmental risk factors, assess their effects on health, and plan protective interventions in the workplace;
the method for independent study and continuous training, also through systematic bibliographic research and critical reading of scientific articles, with a good level of written and spoken English knowledge.
Degree Awarded.
BIOMEDICAL LABORATORY TECHNIQUES DEGREE Teaching Delivery Method Conventional Knowledge and Understanding.
Scientific Fundamentals Area During the first year of the C.d.L., students acquire knowledge of the scientific foundations of professional disciplines.
The disciplines learned in this area, being preparatory, are indispensable for the subsequent learning of theoretical-applicative knowledge within the Biomedical Laboratory, applicable also in biomedical research laboratories and in the fields of veterinary medicine, pharmaceuticals, and biotechnology.
The lessons cover basic subjects such as physics and mathematics, chemistry and biochemistry, human anatomy and histology, physiology, and general pathology.
Professionalizing Area The teaching path naturally continues with the in-depth study of professionalizing disciplines that, in different fields but strictly interdependent and complementary, lead the student to complete their academic journey.
These teachings are aimed at understanding and deepening subjects such as clinical chemistry, microbiology, pathological anatomy and autopsy techniques with direct experience in sector rooms, immunohematology, medical genetics, pharmacology, and toxicology.
Particular attention will be given to acquiring specific knowledge and skills in the field of laboratory techniques, classical and biomolecular, through courses taught by personnel from the specific scientific discipline of the professional profile.
A fundamental part of the course is dedicated to internships and laboratory activities, where students attend both university laboratories and the A.O.U.S. affiliated laboratories.
This preparation allows them, in addition to acquiring work experience and competence, to understand and implement innovative methodologies they will encounter throughout their profession.
Additionally, knowledge of specific topics in first aid and the ability to perform basic resuscitation maneuvers are required, in the field of risk prevention in the places where they operate by implementing all necessary measures for their own and others' safety, in the field of storage, use, and disposal of radioactive isotopes necessary for laboratory diagnostics, in the field of health management to understand the management of healthcare companies and implement cost analysis with the aim of containment and/or optimization, in the field of informatics and acquiring the necessary skills to conduct diagnostic research projects adequately documented and supported by the necessary statistical tests.

UNIVERSITY: University of Siena
COURSE: [ME011] BIOMEDICAL LABORATORY TECHNIQUES (QUALIFYING FOR THE HEALTH PROFESSION OF BIOMEDICAL LABORATORY TECHNICIAN)
SECTION: Autonomy of judgment
URL: https://unisi.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10366

Autonomy of judgment.
The autonomy of judgment of graduates will be expressed through the ability to independently evaluate critical issues related to chemical-clinical and experimental analyses performed and to choose methodologies, strategies, and equipment optimal for the expected results, also through critical review of information obtained from bibliographic research.
The development of such abilities will occur and be verified during internships, where interaction with people, professional profiles, structures, and different methodologies will facilitate the development of independent critical thinking. Equally important will be active participation in lectures, preparation for exams and the final test, further moments of development and verification.

Learning ability.
Graduates will acquire learning abilities and competencies enabling them to continue studies in specialized degree courses or in updating and deepening courses, with a high degree of autonomy. They will be able to independently update their competencies regarding technological and scientific innovations in the context of professional activity.
This ability will be developed and verified through exam preparation, internship attendance, where theory is combined with laboratory practice, and through critical use of bibliographies also for the preparation of the final test.

Ability to apply knowledge and understanding.
Scientific Fundamentals Area Students must be able to know and understand human anatomical structure, the structure and ultrastructure of tissues, organs, and human systems; must be able to know and understand the fundamental mechanisms of different metabolisms, physiology, and pathophysiology; must be able to know and understand the nature and biochemical structure, and replication mechanisms of pathogenic microorganisms and viruses; must be able to know, understand, and apply the epistemological foundations in the future perspective of scientific research activity within their professional field.

Professional Area The student and graduate in Biomedical Laboratory Techniques will use the acquired basic knowledge and be supported by them in every laboratory procedure involving the application of consolidated techniques or the development of new methodologies.
Knowledge of the etiology of pathological processes, the related pathogenetic mechanism, reactions to pathogenic agents, and consequences for the organism constitute a fundamental prerequisite for understanding the diagnostic methods used in various areas of Laboratory Medicine.
At the end of the course, the graduate will be able to independently choose and use laboratory methodologies and equipment suitable for producing clinical and experimental data characteristic of various specialized branches, and to carry out their analytical validation, particularly being able to:
• analyze instrumental procedures and understand errors in relation to biological interest operational descriptions;
• apply techniques to understand cellular and tissue alterations, specific mechanisms of immune response in neoplastic transformation;
• apply techniques related to the main mechanisms of hormonal regulation;
• apply specific and essential competencies for the appropriate use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) as required by current regulations, both regarding the handling of organic material and its correct disposal, as well as the safe use of laboratory reagents.
• use basic computer principles in the laboratory area, particularly regarding the storage of clinical and health-related data and reports;
• apply knowledge to understand and apply processes for searching information on the Web;
• represent the principles of psychology related to emotions, motivational states, and their influence on behavior in the workplace.
• be able to discuss obtained results, propose solutions for optimizing methodologies, and document used procedures with appropriate technical-scientific language.
• be capable of performing specific professional activities of various specialized branches of diagnostic laboratories while fully respecting safety regulations for the use of reagents of various nature, biological agents, and complex analytical equipment, even automated.

The fundamental tool for achieving these objectives is the professional internship in different analytical specialties and in different disciplinary fields.
The closed-number nature of the Degree Course allows students to be continuously and consistently guided by Professional Tutors throughout their three-year internship path.
This enables equally consistent and specific monitoring of the educational path, with particular attention to achieved progress and/or potential difficulties encountered, also with the aim of creating specific educational paths to overcome such difficulties.
At the same time, other practical laboratory activities are carried out in the computer field, also for bibliographic research aimed at acquiring autonomous continuous training capabilities, rational use of scientific publications, and preparation for the final test, which is strictly experimental in nature.

Planned occupational and professional opportunities for graduates.
Biomedical laboratory techniques (enabling the profession of Biomedical Laboratory Technician)
The main professional opportunities for the Biomedical Laboratory Technician are employment in biomedical and biotechnological analysis laboratories within all public healthcare structures of the SSN and within accredited and non-accredited private biomedical and biotechnological structures, for both clinical diagnostics and research. It is estimated that among approximately 30,000 employees, there is an annual turnover need of 5-6%.

Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIAN Associated competencies for the role.
Biomedical laboratory techniques (enabling the profession of Biomedical Laboratory Technician)
The biomedical laboratory technician is a healthcare professional, holding an enabling degree, responsible for their own actions, who performs laboratory activities related to biomedical and biotechnological analyses, particularly in biochemistry, microbiology and virology, pharmacotoxicology, immunology, clinical pathology, hematology, cytology and histopathology.
Description of admission tests.
The number of students admitted to the Degree Program is planned annually based on regional needs.
The access test is common to all Degree Programs in the health area and is conducted on the same day at all Italian universities.
The test consists of a multiple-choice quiz on the following subjects: general culture, logical reasoning, mathematics, physics, chemistry and biology.
Ranking is based on merit. Role in work context.
Biomedical laboratory techniques (enabling the profession of Biomedical Laboratory Technician)
The biomedical laboratory technician:
a) performs their professional work autonomously in direct collaboration with the laboratory-qualified staff responsible for various operational duties;
b) is responsible, in laboratory settings, for the correct implementation of analytical procedures and their own work, within their functions in accordance with the protocols defined by the responsible managers;
c) verifies that the services provided correspond to the predefined indicators and standards set by the facility manager;
d) checks and verifies the correct functioning of equipment used, performs routine maintenance and addresses minor issues;
e) participates in the planning and organization of work within the facility where they operate;
f) performs their activities in public and private authorized laboratories, in accordance with current regulations, either as an employee or as a self-employed professional.
3. The biomedical laboratory technician contributes to the training of support staff and directly participates in the updating of their professional profile and research.

Professional status conferred by the degree.
Expected employment opportunities and professional prospects for graduates Graduates have been in insufficient numbers for many years to meet demand. Employment opportunities in relation to ISTAT classification include specialized hospitals and care facilities, and Institutes, clinics and university polyclinics equipped with cardiothoracic surgery, cardiology or oncology centers where hyperthermic antiblastic perfusion is practiced.
Characteristics of final exam The final exam has the value of a state exam enabling professional practice (D.Lgs 502/1992, art. 6, comma 3) and consists of:
a) a practical exam during which the student must demonstrate having acquired the theoretical-practical and technical-operative knowledge and skills specific to the professional profile;
b) preparation and defense of a thesis. See DM 19 February 2009, art.7
The final exam will be worth 5 CFU.
The final exam cannot be repeated more than once.
Criteria for awarding merit score will include: evaluation of abilities demonstrated during the presentation and discussion of the thesis; judgment on technical ability demonstrated during the practical exam.
The final score is expressed on a scale of 110.
If a total score of 110/110 is achieved, the chair of the final exam committee will put the award of honors to a vote, which can only be granted unanimously.
Required knowledge for access Students holding a Secondary School Diploma or equivalent foreign qualification may be admitted. Required knowledge will include: general culture and logical reasoning, mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology. Additionally, English language knowledge at least at A2/2 level (CEFR) is required.
Degree awarded.
DEGREE IN TECHNIQUES OF CARDIOVASCULAR PHYSIOPATHOLOGY AND PERFUSION Delivery mode Conventional Knowledge and understanding.
Cardiopulmonary physiopathology The graduate must have demonstrated a broad range of knowledge and critical understanding of the physiopathological response of adult and pediatric patients affected by congenital and acquired heart diseases. Basic techniques of extracorporeal circulation The graduate must demonstrate extensive knowledge of current clinical technologies, which must at least include:
a. Cardiopulmonary bypass b. Pumps, hemofiltration, gas exchange, oxygenators, hemodilution, myocardial protection and preservation, temperature regulation, perfusion circuits, pharmacological interventions, blood conservation techniques including autotransfusion, platelet gel production, acute normovolemic hemodilution and phlebotomy, monitoring, analysis and management of anticoagulation and hemostasis.
Advanced techniques of cardiopulmonary support The graduate must demonstrate good knowledge of advanced extracorporeal and intracorporeal vital support technologies. Knowledge must concern different types of support systems and their respective indications for use.

Judgment autonomy.
The graduate must demonstrate:
1. assumption of responsibility, in a varied and specific range of contexts, for the quality and quantity of the result;
2. initiative and independence in carrying out defined activities;
3. quality and capacity necessary for employment that requires the exercise of personal responsibility and decision-making ability.
Judgment autonomy will be acquired during frontal lessons and during internships and professional laboratories. Verification will occur through evaluations by tutors and through internship and professional laboratories examinations in Applied Medical Sciences, which must demonstrate the achievement of the objectives.
Learning ability.
The graduate must have demonstrated the ability to:
1. undertake additional training, expand existing capabilities, and acquire new competencies;
2. undertake and successfully complete a research project, even if the result may not be publishable.
Learning abilities will be acquired throughout the course and during the conception, planning, and development of the theoretical-applicative thesis for the final exam. They will be verified by tutors, through internship examinations and during the final exam.
Ability to apply knowledge and understanding.
Cardiopulmonary physiopathology The graduate must have demonstrated the ability to apply acquired knowledge to extracorporeal circulatory support in cardiac, pulmonary, renal, hepatic, vascular, and neurosurgery. Basic extracorporeal circulation techniques The graduate must have demonstrated the ability to apply acquired knowledge to the management of patients undergoing cardiac surgery for acquired and congenital heart diseases, heart and lung transplantation. Advanced cardiopulmonary support techniques The graduate must have demonstrated the ability to apply acquired knowledge to the management of patients supported with various left and/or right ventricular assist systems, ECMO in its different applications, artificial heart. Communication skills.
The graduate must have demonstrated the ability to:
1. communicate information, topics, and analyses effectively in many modes;
2. explain the fundamental techniques of the discipline effectively;
3. integrate and operate in multiple, complex, and heterogeneous groups.
Communication skills will be acquired during exercises, internships, and professional laboratories in Applied Medical Sciences and verified by tutors.
Expected occupational and professional opportunities for graduates.
The graduate is the expert, qualified through university and clinical education, who manages the extracorporeal circulation system in pathologies requiring support or replacement of cardiorespiratory functions.
Graduates have been insufficient in number for many years to meet demands. Professional opportunities in relation to ISTAT classification include specialized hospitals and care facilities, and Institutes, clinics, and university polyclinics equipped with cardiac surgery, cardiology, or oncology centers where hyperthermic antiblastic perfusion is practiced.
Official teaching and assessment language(s).

Graduates will plan and manage the proper functioning of equipment they are responsible for; ensure correct application of support techniques; carry out their professional activities in healthcare facilities, public or private, in dependent or self-employed status; contribute to the training of support staff and participate in updating and research.

RESEARCH DOCTORATE PROGRAMS (RDP), SPECIALIST DEGREE PROGRAMS/MASTER'S DEGREE PROGRAMS - CLS/CLM, UNIVERSITY MASTER'S PROGRAMS 1ST LEVEL Admission requirements Students possessing a High School Diploma or equivalent foreign qualification may be admitted.
Required knowledge will include: general culture and logical reasoning, mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology.
Additionally, English language knowledge at least at level A2/2 (CEFR) is required. The number of students admitted to the degree program is planned annually based on regional needs.
The entrance exam is common to all health area degree programs and is conducted on the same day at all Italian universities.
Professional status conferred by the degree.
The Prevention Technician in the Environment and Workplaces is the health operator responsible, within their competencies, for all prevention, verification and control activities regarding environmental and workplace hygiene and safety, food and beverage hygiene, public and veterinary hygiene. The Prevention Technician in the Environment and Workplaces, operating in services with inspection and monitoring duties, is, within the limits of their attributions, a judicial police officer: carries out investigative activities aimed at issuing technical health authorizations or approvals for activities subject to control.
The degree obtained is enabling for the profession and allows the practice of professional activity, in dependent or self-employed status, within the National Health Service (85.1 Health Services Activities) in all prevention, control and monitoring services provided for by current regulations. (85.14.2 Independent paramedical professional activities; 85.2 veterinary services; 90.0 disposal of solid waste, wastewater and similar).
Final exam characteristics The final exam has the value of a state-licensing exam for professional practice (D.Lgs 502/1992, art. 6, comma 3) and consists of:
a) a practical test during which the student must demonstrate acquisition of theoretical-practical and technical-operational knowledge and skills specific to the professional profile;
b) preparation and defense of a thesis. See DM 19 February 2009, art.7
The final exam will be awarded 5 CFU.
The final exam cannot be repeated more than once.
Criteria for awarding merit score will include: evaluation of abilities demonstrated during the presentation and discussion of the thesis; judgment on technical ability demonstrated during the practical test.
The final score is expressed on a scale of 110.
If a total score of 110/110 is achieved, the chair of the final exam committee will put the award of honors to a vote, which can only be granted unanimously.
Required knowledge for access Students possessing a High School Diploma or equivalent foreign qualification may be admitted. Required knowledge will include: general culture and logical reasoning, mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology. Additionally, English language knowledge at least at level A2/2 (CEFR) is required.
Degree awarded.
DEGREE IN TECHNIQUES OF PREVENTION IN THE ENVIRONMENT AND WORKPLACES Teaching method Conventional Knowledge and understanding.
Research area
- Acquire basic statistical and epidemiological knowledge necessary to understand and address issues related to organization, research and teaching in the field of prevention health sciences;
- Use research methods and tools in the area of organization of health services and evaluation of their quality;
- Acquire elements for social research based on information collection through questionnaires;
- Evaluate results of interventions in research and health promotion;
- Deepen understanding of organization and content of scientific publications including main statistical and epidemiological analyses;
- Know basic aspects of research;
- Use a widely used spreadsheet (Excel, Microsoft) for synthetic and graphical representation of data.
Professional area Acquire basic knowledge of technical, operational and managerial aspects typical of prevention health professions (class 4) and use this knowledge for organization and management of health services:
- Know main models of economic, social and health development and environmental protection in industrialized countries;
- Know organization of health services at national and international level and understand dynamics of their development;
- Know basic aspects of vaccinations in a preventive perspective;
- Know chemical and ergonomic risk factors and some tools for risk assessment in occupational health and public health;
- Know basic aspects of medical parasitology in a preventive perspective;
- Know fundamental principles of infectious diseases, their transmission methods and control, reporting procedures and principles of screening and individual protection;
- Know principles of infectious disease risk management in health settings by the Risk Manager figure;
- Know tools for improving quality of health services in the prevention area;
- Know classification of occupational diseases, their active research in different exposure and risk scenarios, with particular reference to agriculture;
- Know programming and optimization of resources for management of territorial health services with preventive purposes.
Management area
- Acquire basic concepts of economic-business analysis applied to health systems (public, private and accredited private);
- Understand and evaluate functioning of organization and role of managerial functions in a health company;
- Acquire and be able to use skills aimed at promoting and supporting innovation, creativity and organizational change;
- Understand psychological aspects of work behavior, both individual and in group and organizational contexts;
- Know and evaluate structural characteristics of communication and its content, examining communication peculiarities within a professional team;
- Manage and solve organizational problems based on integrated evaluation of technical, social, individual and institutional components, and in relation to objectives to be achieved in terms of user service and role of the health structure;
- Know regulatory references regarding prevention and protection of health and safety in workplaces;
- Understand relationships between planning and control systems and concepts of effectiveness, efficiency and economy of the health company;
- Learn basic notions of labor law, professional responsibility in health, main tools for health protection and role of main international organizations.
Biomedical sciences The graduate is able to:
- Possess knowledge and ability to understand: composition and fundamental biochemical processes of living matter, morphological-functional characteristics of the cell, principles and mechanisms of gene expression and inheritance transmission.
- Possess basic knowledge necessary to understand macro and microscopic structure of organs and organization of the human body (systems) as well as main models of body district functioning and pathogenic mechanisms underlying common pathologies.
- Possess basic knowledge to distinguish different microorganisms and their modes of diffusion and transmission and to understand main analytical techniques for recognizing microorganisms in biological and environmental matrices.

COURSE: [ME004] TECHNIQUES OF PREVENTION IN THE ENVIRONMENT AND WORKPLACES (ENABLING THE HEALTH PROFESSION OF PREVENTION TECHNICIAN IN THE ENVIRONMENT AND WORKPLACES)
SECTION: Judgment autonomy
URL: https://unisi.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10329

Judgment autonomy.
Graduates will have the ability to collect and interpret data in relation to scientific evidence present in literature, particularly in the field of Evidence prevention. They will be able to independently assess the impact of environmental and working conditions not only on health, but also in terms of psychological and socioeconomic well-being. Furthermore, graduates will be aware of risks present in living and working environments, as well as of behavioral norms and aspects related to safety and environmental issues.
Judgment autonomy is achieved through frontal lectures and training internships and is verified in exam assessments for each course, in internships, and in the final exam.

Learning ability.
The study course, through frontal lectures, specific internships, and the professional laboratory, aims to develop the learning ability that enables graduates to independently continue subsequent studies in the field and update themselves.
Learning ability will be assessed through specific written and/or oral tests, in internships, in the laboratory, and in the final exam.

Ability to apply knowledge and understanding.
Research Area
- Apply theoretical elements learned during lectures in the research area, in the execution of specific internship and thesis projects where the student must take an active/propositional/critical role;
- Develop skills in research through reading and interpreting scientific articles;
- Develop transversal skills in presenting work orally;
- Develop the ability to interact constructively and correctly with other prevention professionals.

Professional Area
- Apply theoretical elements learned during lectures in the advanced professional area, in the execution of specific internship and thesis projects where the student must take an active/propositional/critical role;
- Develop transversal skills in preparing a technical-scientific document;
- Develop transversal skills in presenting work orally;
- Develop the ability to interact constructively and correctly with prevention professionals who act as internship tutors.

Management Area
- Apply theoretical elements learned during lectures in the management area, in the execution of specific internship and thesis projects where the student must take an active/propositional/critical role;
- Use skills in health economics and business organization necessary for organizing health services and managing available human and technological resources, evaluating cost/benefit ratios;
- Interpret the economic-financial balances of health companies through reading financial statements and management control data;
- Apply and evaluate the impact of different theoretical models on the operation and management of health services;
- Plan the optimization of all human, technological, informational, and financial resources;
- Communicate clearly on organizational and health issues with colleagues and users;
- Know the classification of health personnel, plan and optimize their management, including shift scheduling and absence monitoring, understand how to apply service orders and aspects of planning and control;
- Be able to apply the main methods and tools for iconographic representation of organizations to represent a service delivery system in the health and/or social-health sector;
- Plan prevention service activities and verify their effectiveness;
- Know the regulatory references related to prevention and health and safety protection in workplaces and understand their implementation in health companies;
- Critically analyze ethical and deontological aspects of health professions;
- Effectively coordinate and communicate within the health operator team;
- Apply knowledge of psychology to the workplace to enhance individual and group capabilities and effectively manage work-related stress;
- Know the main rights and duties between employers and workers, both individually and collectively, and the legal responsibilities of health professionals.

Biomedical Sciences Graduates are able to:
- Know the structure and functions of cells, have judgment autonomy and communication skills regarding basic biochemical and biological issues, specific aspects of the functioning (normal and pathological) of various organ systems and their interactions; they are also able to evaluate the role and action of risk factors on the human body
- Know the characteristics of microorganisms and their transmission modes, and be able to apply analytical techniques to study microbial contamination of biological and environmental matrices.

Communication skills.
Through specific frontal lessons and internships, graduates will be able to establish and maintain positive communication relationships both for general communications and technical communications. The ability to interact is fundamental in this type of work. Additionally, they will be able to process and present acquired data and disseminate scientific information on current topics.
The achieved communication skills will be assessed through specific oral or written tests for each course and internship, as well as in the final exam.
Expected occupational and professional outcomes for graduates.
The Technician of Prevention in the Environment and Workplaces is the health operator responsible, within their own competencies, for all prevention, verification and control activities regarding environmental and workplace hygiene and safety, food and beverage hygiene, public health and veterinary hygiene. The obtained title enables for the profession and allows the performance of professional activities, in dependent or freelance capacity, within the national health service (85.1 Health service activities) at all prevention, control and surveillance services provided for by current regulations. (85.14.2 Independent paramedical professional activities; 85.2 veterinary services; 90.0 disposal of solid waste, wastewater and similar).

Additional information.
http://www.unisi.it/dipartimenti/dipartimento-medicina-molecolare-e-dello-sviluppo Specific educational objectives description.
Graduates must achieve the following specific cultural and professional competencies:
-knowledge of the principles of chemistry and physics necessary for interpreting environmental monitoring data in living and working environments;
-knowledge of the principles of anatomy, physiology, histology, and general pathology necessary for understanding common pathologies, particularly occupational ones;
-ability to correctly apply environmental sampling methodologies for chemical pollutants;
-ability to correctly perform measurements of physical agents as required by current regulations;
-ability to control the quality of food and beverages intended for consumption;
-adequate knowledge of occupational and environmental toxicology;
-knowledge of medical-surgical sciences enabling understanding of the etiopathogenesis of diseases, particularly occupational ones;
-knowledge of microbiological techniques;
-knowledge of the principles underlying labor law;
-knowledge of the principles underlying criminal law concerning environmental property crimes and violations of hygiene and safety regulations in living and working environments and food;
-ability to assess the need for investigations and inquiries for occupational accidents and diseases;
-ability and sensitivity to evaluate psychological issues within communities and work organizations;
-knowledge of the fundamental concepts of health organization;
-knowledge, from a preventive perspective, of the most common disease patterns, particularly occupational ones;
-knowledge, from a preventive perspective, of accident phenomena;
-knowledge, from a preventive perspective, of infectious diseases;
-knowledge of the fundamental methodological elements of epidemiology;
-knowledge of issues related to ergonomics with particular regard to the relationship between work and vision;
-knowledge of the most common industrial technologies;
-ability to use statistics to evaluate biological and environmental monitoring data;
-ability to propose sufficiently validated and recognized evaluation methods in the fields of ergonomics, hygiene, and toxicology;
-learning the basics of research methodology and the ability to apply results in public health prevention;
-ability to identify, prevent, and address occupational risks in various work situations and evaluate their effects on health;
-knowledge of the essential elements of business organization with particular reference to health services;
-ability to act consistently with the legal, ethical, and deontological principles of the profession during surveillance and control activities as outlined in the training program;
-knowledge of fundamental regulations regarding hygiene and safety in living and working environments;
-proficient computer skills for managing service information systems and for self-education.
The degree program in techniques of prevention in the environment and workplaces requires 180 credit points over three years of study, with at least 60 CFU to be acquired through training activities aimed at developing specific professional skills (internship).
Internship:
Regarding internship experiences focused on Hygiene and Safety in Workplaces (both public and private sectors), specific technical competencies will be emphasized for organizing and evaluating analytical risk assessment processes for work activities, implementing the necessary preventive and protective measures to safeguard safety; this implies, beyond knowledge of current safety regulations, specific training in business organization, management, and quality assurance. Practical experiences will be specifically designed to achieve the following objectives:
-Application of current regulations on Hygiene and Safety in Workplaces aimed at exercising surveillance and control activities and collaborating on occupational accidents and diseases.
-Ability to prepare a plan for assessing risks within a work environment.
-Evaluation of the significance of environmental and biological monitoring investigations in workplaces.
-Ability to identify preventive and protective measures to contain risks.
-Use of tools to evaluate the effectiveness of adopted measures.
-Knowledge of quality and safety management systems at the business level (ISO series) and the environmental impact of activities, products, and services (ISO series).
Regarding internship experiences focused on Environmental Hygiene, Food and Beverage Hygiene, Public Health, and Veterinary Hygiene:
-Application of current regulations on environmental protection aimed at exercising surveillance and control activities, also through the use of monitoring tools for air, water, and soil quality.
-Ability to identify, based on obtained results, appropriate preventive measures for environmental protection and verify their effectiveness.
-Application of current regulations on food and beverage quality and cosmetic products.
-Ability to analyze food production cycles, identify critical control points, and prepare measures to safeguard hygiene and quality of beverages and foods, including those of veterinary origin.
-Knowledge of quality and safety management systems at the business level (ISO series) and the environmental impact of activities, products, and services (ISO series).
-Acquire the ability to analyze and solve problems related to issuing opinions for authorizations in the fields of environmental hygiene in living and working environments, food and beverage hygiene, and public and veterinary health;
-Acquire the ability to assess the need for investigations and detect irregularities during surveillance activities in living and working environments; possession of teaching skills for informing and training staff.
-Acquire the ability to conduct site visits, inspections, and sampling at various production units.
-Ability to draft main administrative and judicial police documents.
The training path, based on the specific objectives described above, is implemented through learning basic disciplines such as physics (FIS/07), biology (BIO/13), biochemistry (BIO/10), anatomy (BIO/16), histology (BIO/17), physiology (BIO/09), general pathology (MED/04), microbiology (MED/07), and subsequently through learning more specific disciplines such as electromagnetic fields (ING-INF/02), chemical plants (ING-IND/25), ecology (BIO/07), medical statistics (MED/01), General and Applied Hygiene (MED/42), and sociology of environment and territory (SPS/10).
Particular attention is given, within the core courses and internship, to evidence-based prevention, providing theoretical and practical means to ensure professional autonomy and the capacity for continuous scientific updating.
A significant space is reserved for statistical-computer preparation of students through basic modules, computer statistics (Medical Statistics MED/01 - Bioengineering and Electronics ING-INF/06), to enable them to evaluate the results of investigations in the health field. The cultural training is enriched by courses in human sciences and psychopedagogy (General Sociology SPS/07 – General Psychology M-PSI/01 - History of Medicine MED/02), to ensure the acquisition of behavioral, relational, and communication competencies necessary for operating in a complex work environment.
Particular attention is paid to prevention sciences in health services (General and Applied Hygiene MED/42 – Legal Medicine MED/43 – Occupational Medicine MED/44 – Radioprotection MED/36) and first aid (Internal Medicine MED/09 – Anesthesiology MED/41 – General Surgery MED/18). Health management sciences are developed particularly regarding public law (IUS/09) and labor law (IUS/07), as well as economics (SEC-P/07) and business organization (SECS-P/10) for understanding the basic mechanisms of health company management and in the perspective of deeper study in specialized degree programs. Students are provided with an English language course (Medical English) also aimed at understanding scientific literature, with the possibility offered by the University to acquire additional certifications such as PET or FCE.
Courses are structured into modules and are delivered through frontal lessons, classroom exercises, or laboratory sessions. Learning outcomes are assessed through possible in-course tests, which also serve as self-assessment for the student, and through a final oral or written exam, which serves to verify the achievement of the set objectives, unique and simultaneous for each course, necessary for acquiring credit points. Learning outcomes of laboratory courses, English, and some internships result in a pass. Students have access to 5 credits dedicated to preparing for the final exam of the course at facilities designated for training; this activity can also be carried out at non-university facilities, such as hospitals, health services, or private entities.
The degree program in Techniques of Prevention in the Environment and Workplaces requires a total of 180 credit points, structured over three years of study, with at least 60 to be acquired through training activities aimed at developing specific professional skills (internship).

Roles Chairman/Chairman of the Teaching Committee LORENZO SALERNI
Program, Texts and Objectives Professional status conferred by the title.
Audioprosthetic Technician The Audioprosthetic Technician works under dependency or as a self-employed consultant at public or private entities that deal with audiologic rehabilitation for both children and adults.
Final Exam Characteristics In accordance with Article 6, paragraph 3, of Legislative Decree No. 502/1992 and subsequent amendments, and Article 6 of the Interministerial Decree of February 19, 2009 (Determination of university degree classes for health professions), the final exam of the Degree Course has the value of a state-recognized exam enabling professional practice.
The final exam consists of a practical test, through which the student must demonstrate having acquired theoretical-practical and technical-operative knowledge and skills, as well as the preparation of a thesis report assigned under the guidance of a supervisor and discussed with the committee and the co-supervisor.
The final exam is worth 5 CFU.
Required Knowledge for Admission To be admitted to the Audioprosthetic Techniques Degree Course, one must hold a secondary school diploma or another foreign degree recognized as suitable.
Admission to the Degree Course is annually planned on a national basis, as stipulated by Article 1 of Law No. 264 of August 2, 1999 (Regulations on Access to University Courses), also based on the availability of teaching staff, teaching facilities, and assistive structures for practical activities.
Admission is based on a national multiple-choice test.
The number of students admitted to the first year of the course is defined by a ministerial decree in accordance with Article 3 of the same Law 264/1999.
Among the necessary knowledge for entry, English language knowledge at least at level A2/2 (CEFR) is required.
The student's initial preparation will, however, be assessed through the analysis of errors found in logic, chemistry, biology, mathematics, and physics quizzes (multiple-choice questions) administered in the entrance exam.
If the assessment is not positive or falls below the established minimum, additional mandatory training obligations will be assigned to be fulfilled in the first year of the course. In this regard, the instructors of the relevant modules will conduct a brief recovery course for the main knowledge gaps, which must still be addressed in the first year.
Knowledge and Understanding. PREPARATORY AND CLINICAL AREA
1. Understand the basic concepts of Biochemistry, Biology, Genetics, Physiology, Histology, and Anatomy that form the basis of physiological and pathological processes developing in childhood, adulthood, and old age.
2. Understand the basic concepts of Applied Physics (with emphasis on Acoustic Physics), Informatics (applied to the Biomedical environment), and Medical Statistics.
3. Understand concepts of electronics and materials technology.
4. Understand the Psychological and Pedagogical aspects of hearing-impaired patients and/or those with language issues in both pediatric and adult age.
5. Study of the English language with particular focus on the scientific aspects of the Medical field.
6. Know the basics of business economics and labor law.
7. Know the basics of healthcare management.
The evaluation of these knowledge and understanding abilities, acquired through frontal lessons and the professional clinical internship, as well as through seminars and laboratory activities over the three years of the course, will be verified and consolidated through the following assessment methods: oral exams, written exams, simulated practical tests, practical tests on patients, written reports, case reports.
Teaching Tools: classroom activities, practical lessons in clinics and/or equipped classrooms, clinical internship, reading and interpretation of international literature, study hours, and self-training.
APPLIED AND PROFESSIONAL AREA In the area of characteristic activities, the student in Audioprosthetic Techniques must acquire:
- knowledge regarding the most relevant diseases of the otological, rhinological, and laryngological districts
- ability to integrate audiologic data with pathology indicators
- knowledge regarding public health activities (surveillance, prevention, and health education)
- knowledge of legislative and economic principles
Additionally, the main issues concerning occupational medicine must be known, and basic principles of legal medicine must be acquired.
- knowledge that constitutes the communication process and all elements that compose it
- daily work themes of accredited audiometrists, who guide the acquisition of audiologic techniques for investigating the auditory and vestibular apparatus
- knowledge of general pediatrics and neonatology.
The specific aspects of various diseases in childhood and the related issues with audiologic pathologies will be considered; pediatric neuropsychiatric and rehabilitative aspects will be further explored.
- knowledge in interdisciplinary and medical-surgical sciences for understanding physio-pathological elements applicable to various clinical situations.
- knowledge in prevention sciences and healthcare services
- knowledge in statistical sciences, quantitative methods, and scientific updates, for developing knowledge of statistical tools useful for planning the research process, selecting and using analytical methods in professional practice, using the best available scientific evidence in the literature in the field of audiological sciences, as well as the ability to evaluate epidemiological data.
- knowledge in hygiene-preventive sciences for understanding health determinants, risk factors, individual and collective prevention strategies, and interventions aimed at promoting the safety of healthcare operators and users.
Judgment Autonomy.
The graduate in Audioprosthetic Techniques, at the end of the study path, will be able to know and apply, autonomously, the audioprosthetic rehabilitation intervention using clinical reasoning as a guiding tool in the selection criteria, within the possible options that compose the various phases of the process itself.
This autonomy will be achieved through the acquisition, consolidation, and experimentation of competencies and abilities to effectively respond to individual and/or collective health needs, as a single operator or in a team, opting for the best therapeutic strategies, identifying appropriate approaches and tools, conducting data collection (including social context analysis), patient evaluation, suitable audiologic assessments, defining short, medium, and long-term prognoses and therapeutic goals, contributing to formulating a rehabilitation project, developing the therapeutic program, selecting and applying rehabilitation methodologies and techniques to the clinical case (including intensity, time, and type of technical-professional approach) according to possible and available scientific evidence, following international guidelines and Evidence-Based practices; ethically, it will manifest through respect for reference regulations, professional, legal, healthcare, and deontological standards.
The graduate's judgment autonomy in Audioprosthetic Techniques will be fully realized through the habitual and judicious use of communication, knowledge, technical skills, clinical reasoning (diagnostic and evaluation process), emotions, values, and reflection in daily practice for the benefit of the individual or the community, especially through the professional clinical internship and small group laboratories.
Judgment autonomy is achieved through the following teaching tools: classroom activities, practical lessons in the laboratory and/or equipped classrooms, clinical internship, reading and interpretation of international scientific literature, and verified through written reports on in-depth technical/professional topics, discussion of clinical cases, definition of the Rehabilitation Project/Program and real clinical cases. Annual clinical internship exam.
Learning Ability.
The graduate in Audioprosthetic Techniques will be able to conduct a self-assessment of their educational level to maintain their knowledge at the highest level required for professional practice and design self-training paths to enhance their competencies, with particular reference to Evidence-Based Practice in the audiological and audioprosthetic rehabilitation field.
Over the three years, they will acquire learning abilities and competencies that allow, at the end of the course, the continuation of studies, including a master's degree in Class LM/SNT/02, scientific specialization courses, and permanent and recurring advanced training (1st and 2nd level master's, specialization courses), update and in-depth courses (Continuing Medical Education), with a high degree of autonomy.
Teaching tools through which learning abilities are achieved: hospital and company internships, professionalizing seminars, frontal lessons, self-learning hours, theoretical and practical exercises, professionalizing laboratory.
Learning verification is carried out through in-progress tests aimed at assessing the effectiveness of the content of different teaching modules. Profit exams may be conducted in multiple phases, including practical tests, but will conclude with an oral test to verify the candidate's preparation on all subjects included in the Integrated Course.
Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
PREPARATORY AND CLINICAL AREA Graduates at the end of the training path will be able to apply the work process within the rehabilitation setting, both in simulated form and on patients, adopting the problem-solving methodology (clinical reasoning) and implementing the correlated procedures that allow the realization of care and rehabilitation interventions for hearing disorders in various ages and various physiological and pathological alterations of the auditory system.
Knowledge application will develop considering fundamental aspects such as interaction with the real-life context of individuals, interpersonal and inter-professional relationships, and organizational management of aspects directly related to the type of work performed.
This ability will be fully achieved through the mandatory attendance of the professional internship and didactic laboratory activities (60 ECTS credits of internship distributed over 3 years gradually; 3 ECTS credits of didactic laboratory as a technical and relational learning gymnasium), where each student has access to specially designated clinical tutors.
Professional skills acquisition is systematically verified through a logbook certifying presence and a "Core Values" evaluation sheet measuring attitudes, behaviors, and general abilities, compiled by the clinical tutor at the end of each internship experience; the combination of knowledge and skills is assessed through a structured test at the end of each academic year (in the 1st year it results in a "pass," while at the end of the 2nd and 3rd years it results in an exam graded out of 30).
The aforementioned activities are planned, monitored, and verified by the Coordinator of theoretical/practical activities and internships, who promotes meetings with tutors and students, proposes training activities, facilitates the student's development of self-training, access to bibliographic sources, etc.
Teaching Tools: classroom activities, practical lessons in audiology, otology, and acoustics laboratories, reading rooms, and interpretation of international literature.
The evaluation of such knowledge and understanding abilities will be carried out through the following assessment methods: theoretical/practical exams, written reports on technical aspects, oral and written presentation of acoustic rehabilitation projects, simulated and/or patient-based practical tests.
APPLIED AND PROFESSIONAL AREA In the area of characteristic activities, the student in Audioprosthetic Techniques must acquire:
The knowledge acquired through training activities and appropriate internship will allow optimal adaptation to assigned work tasks through the use of acquired specialized knowledge;
The ability to apply learned techniques to critically analyze given information and propose suitable solutions;
To employ learned diagnostic techniques to critically analyze results and propose appropriate audioprosthetic solutions, evaluating results over time and possible solutions for failures.
Communication Skills.
The graduate in Audioprosthetic Techniques will be able to: establish professional relationships and collaborate with other healthcare professionals, aware of the specificities of different professional roles; demonstrate effective communication skills with users and in relationships with other professionals; communicate effectively using verbal, non-verbal, and written methods for technical and assistive evaluations and decisions in interdisciplinary healthcare teams; collaborate with the care team to implement and develop protocols and guidelines; communicate effectively with patients, families, and other professionals to provide optimal healthcare.
Communication skills are acquired through classroom activities and internship and verified through written reports on communication aspects of the rehabilitation setting; briefings with tutors and the coordinator; oral and written presentation of projects; internship.
Expected Occupational and Professional Opportunities for Graduates.
Audioprosthetic Technician The Audioprosthetic Technician works under dependency or as a self-employed consultant at public or private entities that deal with audiologic rehabilitation for both children and adults.
Official Teaching and Assessment Languages.
ITALIAN
Skills Associated with the Function.
Audioprosthetic Technician The activity of the Audioprosthetic Technician is aimed at applying prosthetic devices through the measurement of the external auditory canal impression, the construction and application of shells or other acoustic coupling systems, and the administration of prosthetic evaluation tests.
The Audioprosthetic Technician has teaching and scientific competencies in Prosthetic Audiology and can be integrated into multidisciplinary teams for clinical and research activities.
Function in Work Context.
Audioprosthetic Technician The Audioprosthetic Technician is responsible for the selection, supply, adaptation, and control of prosthetic devices for the prevention and correction of hearing deficits; conducts counseling for the use of hearing aids and operates under medical prescription through professional acts that imply full responsibility and consequent autonomy.
Additionally, collaborates with other professional figures in prevention and rehabilitation programs for hearing loss through the provision of prosthetic devices and training in their use.
Description of Specific Educational Objectives.
The Audioprosthetic Techniques Degree Course aims to train graduates with high scientific and technological competence in management, training, and research processes in the field of application, programming, and evaluation of Audioprosthetics.
The training path has specific educational objectives, defined for its Professional Profile according to the Ministry of Health Decree No. 668 of September 14, 1994.
In particular, the graduate in Audioprosthetic Techniques must achieve the following educational objectives:
- Possession of adequate basic preparation in the fields of physics, statistics, informatics, and chemistry oriented towards practical aspects;
- Learning the basics of anatomy, physiology, and pathophysiology of the auditory apparatus;
- Acquisition of adequate theoretical foundations in technical, medical (general and specialized), and social disciplines suitable for professional practice;
- Knowledge of instrumental methodologies for performing an otoscopic evaluation;
- Acquisition of methodologies for threshold and suprathreshold audiometry, impedance testing, and behavioral audiometry;
- Learning the basics of recording bioelectric phenomena;
- Knowledge of rehabilitation methodologies for hearing loss;
- Acquisition of theoretical, technical, technological, and methodological principles in the realization and operation of hearing aids;
- Knowledge of principles and methodologies suitable for the selection, coupling, fitting, adaptation, control, and technical assistance for prosthetic aids, in theoretical and practical aspects;
- Development of appropriate practical experience, preparatory for transferring theoretical knowledge to professional applications;
- Ability to work in multidisciplinary teams, interact with colleagues and other healthcare and non-healthcare professionals, operate with defined degrees of autonomy, and integrate appropriately into work environments;
- Ability to communicate and relate with the assisted person, caregivers, social context, and other healthcare and non-healthcare professionals, respecting cultural and behavioral differences;
- Development of cultural and methodological competencies and aptitude for continuous training, to maintain a level of technical-professional, decisional, operational, and managerial autonomy;
- Acquisition of aptitudes for training, teaching, and research activities in the field of Prosthetic Audiology;
- Acquisition of adequate knowledge of management and healthcare economics.
The degree course has a duration of three years with the acquisition of 180 ECTS credits in total (of which 60 through professionalizing internship training activities), sufficient to achieve full and autonomous professional competence.
Training Path The first year of the course is aimed at providing biomedical knowledge as well as the foundations of the professional discipline as prerequisites for facing the first internship experience aimed at orienting the student to the reference professional fields and acquiring basic competencies, through courses activated in the following scientific disciplines: FIS/07, INF/01, ING-INF/07, ING-IND/22, ING-INF/06, BIO/09, BIO/10, BIO/13, BIO/16, BIO/17, MED/03, MED/04, MED/09, MED/18, MED/31, MED/32, MED/43, MED/50, M-PSI/01, M-PSI/04, IUS/07, SPS/07, SECS-P/07, SECS-P/10, ENGLISH LANGUAGE
The second year of the course is aimed at deepening audiologic and audioprosthetic knowledge in adulthood and childhood. Multiple internship experiences are planned in both SSN clinics and private accredited audioprosthetic centers, where students can apply and deepen the knowledge and techniques learned in courses activated in the following scientific disciplines: MED/10, MED/25, MED/26, MED/31, MED/32, MED/36, MED/39, MED/50, ING-INF/05, SECS-S/02, ENGLISH LANGUAGE
The third year of the course is aimed at expanding specialized and interdisciplinary knowledge, as well as acquiring methodologies related to professional practice and the ability to work in teams and complex organizational contexts. Additionally, the professional internship experiences conducted by the student under supervision and with gradual assumption of autonomy and responsibility will be of significant importance. The third-year training activities are activated in the following scientific disciplines: MED/8, MED/17, MED/31, MED/32, MED/50, ING-INF/04, ING-INF/06
The set of knowledge acquired by the graduate, totaling 180 ECTS credits, will constitute the necessary cultural, scientific, and relational background to acquire full professional competence and to understand, address, and manage pathological events requiring rehabilitation and/or therapeutic intervention in all age groups. These knowledge will be acquired through participation in frontal lessons, practical lessons in equipped classrooms with rehabilitation devices, guided by teachers and tutors belonging to the specific professional profile, as well as through personal study (library, databases) of the subjects offered by the Degree Course.

High School Diploma Tuition and Fees For information on tuition and fees, visit the University website www.unisi.it/tasse Dates and Deadlines For information on dates and deadlines, visit the University website "Study Plan" www.unisi.it/didattica/immatricolazioni-e-iscrizioni/immatricolazioni Roles Chair/Chair of Teaching Committee ALESSANDRO LINGUITI Program, texts, and objectives Professional title conferred by the degree.
Expert in promoting and managing cultural and communication activities Graduates of the degree class can carry out professional activities at local authorities and specific institutions, such as libraries, archives, and academies, as well as at publishing houses, journalistic editorial offices, foundations, companies, and other professional entities operating in the field of organizing events and cultural activities. However, it should be noted that for many professional roles, the basic skills and abilities acquired during the three-year course must be complemented by specific training offered in Master's courses, first and second level Master's programs, doctoral courses (starting from those activated at the Siena University), and subsequent training levels provided for by the regulations for access to teaching. Graduates who have sufficient credits in appropriate subject groups may, as provided by current legislation, participate in admission tests for secondary teaching training paths.
Final Exam Characteristics The final exam may be conducted in two different ways:
a) It may consist of a written exposition whose topic falls within one of the SSDs present in the Curriculum of the SLF Degree Course. This written work must demonstrate possession of specific knowledge and the ability to set up a basic research project, using appropriate methodologies and updated bibliographic tools;
or b) It may consist of an oral exam, during which the graduate must demonstrate in-depth knowledge of fundamental texts (primary and secondary bibliography, according to modalities to be specified in the Study Course Teaching Regulations) of one of the SSDs present in the Curriculum of the SLF Degree Course; additionally, they must demonstrate the ability to set up a basic research project, using appropriate methodologies and updated bibliographic tools, referring to at least two written reports prepared within the context of the passed exams.
The choice between the two final exam modalities will be agreed upon by the graduate with the supervising professor, taking into account the specificities of the SSD in which the student is graduating.
The final exam is worth 6 CFU. The graduation grade is expressed on a scale of 110, with possible honors. The final grade is calculated by adding the grade assigned to the final exam to the average of the exam scores.
Required Knowledge for Admission To be admitted to the Bachelor's Degree Course, one must possess a secondary school diploma or another foreign qualification recognized as equivalent.
Students enrolling in the course are required to have a basic preparation consisting of linguistic skills and cultural knowledge typically acquired in high schools and upper secondary education institutions.
In particular, a good command of the Italian language, basic knowledge of Latin, and knowledge of English at least at the A2/2 level of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR) are required.
To verify personal preparation regarding these knowledge areas, entrance tests in Italian and English will be activated. For Latin, an entrance test is not provided, but a Preliminary Linguistic Knowledge Verification will be conducted, which is a prerequisite for the first exam in Latin Language and Literature (SSD L-FIL-LET/04).
Students who do not pass these tests can still enroll in the Bachelor's Degree Course, but they will be required to fulfill additional training obligations in the first year of the course. Students with additional training obligations regarding Italian language expression must attend an intensive Italian language workshop; students with additional training obligations regarding English language knowledge must attend a recovery course, which will be organized by the University Language Center.
Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area Graduates of the Bachelor's Degree Course will have integrated and developed the preparation acquired at secondary school through the acquisition of competencies and understanding abilities in the fields of philological-linguistic and classical literary, philological-linguistic and modern literary, and philosophical areas, within a solid foundational framework. Verification occurs throughout the entire educational path through written and oral exams (with possible seminar and/or laboratory activities, internships, and traineeships), and through the final exam.
Students must have demonstrated, for the purpose of obtaining the degree, theoretical and methodological knowledge in the various fields, competencies in reading and analyzing texts, knowledge of critical methods, and the ability to use fundamental bibliographic research tools and consult the most recent developments in research.
Area of Classical Philologies, Languages, and Literatures:
Good command of Greek and Latin, knowledge of the historical development and main authors and texts of Greek and Latin literature, main methods of philological study of classical texts, and main cultural and anthropological issues related to the ancient world (for students who do not choose a training path oriented towards the classical world, such knowledge is considered more general and limited to the Latin context). The main teaching tool is the frontal lecture, optionally accompanied by seminar exercises. Knowledge assessment typically occurs through oral and/or written exams.
Area of Philology, Linguistics, and Italian Literature:
Good knowledge of the historical development and main authors and texts of Italian literature (including theatrical), mastery of main methods of philological study of modern texts, awareness of main cultural issues related to the study of Italian literary production; good knowledge of the diachronic development of the Italian language (for students who choose a training path not oriented towards Italian studies, such knowledge is considered more general). The main teaching tool is the frontal lecture, optionally accompanied by seminar exercises. Knowledge assessment typically occurs through oral and/or written exams.
Area of Modern and Comparative Philologies, Languages, and Literatures:
General knowledge of the historical development and main authors and texts of one or more modern foreign literatures; knowledge of one or more modern languages, in addition to English; awareness of philological, theoretical, and historical-critical issues in the study of modern literatures (for students who choose a training path not oriented towards modern and comparative languages and literatures, such knowledge is considered more general). The main teaching tool is the frontal lecture, optionally accompanied by seminar exercises. Knowledge assessment typically occurs through oral and/or written exams.
Historical Area:
Good knowledge of Western history from classical antiquity to the present; awareness of main historiographical issues related to sources and their interpretation; mastery of the connections between historical development and cultural events. The main teaching tool is the frontal lecture, optionally accompanied by seminar exercises. Knowledge assessment typically occurs through oral and/or written exams.
Philosophical Area:
Good knowledge of the development of philosophical thought from classical antiquity to the present; awareness of main theoretical, logical, moral, and aesthetic issues, and main methods of philosophical text analysis (for students who choose a training path not oriented towards philosophy, such knowledge is considered more general). The main teaching tool is the frontal lecture, optionally accompanied by seminar exercises. Knowledge assessment typically occurs through oral and/or written exams.
Demographic-Ethno-Anthropological Area:
Knowledge of main methods and contents of demographic-ethno-anthropological research, capable of placing literary and philosophical texts within a broader reflection on human cultures (for students who choose a training path oriented towards demographic-ethno-anthropological sciences).

Judgment Autonomy.
Graduates will be able to address themes within the literary and linguistic fields (relating to both classical and modern worlds) and the philosophical field, identifying and critically evaluating the various accredited positions on the scientific plane; and to form their own judgment based on available documentation and the critical analysis tools provided, developing an autonomous and mature judgment. They must have demonstrated the ability to independently set up and conduct bibliographic research using new technologies, to establish the necessary data bases for their studies, and to process and interpret such data critically, paying attention to scientific, social, and ethical implications (an ability that, among other things, may be fostered and verified through the assignment of in-depth topics to students, who will report on them during lectures, meetings, or seminars). The achievement of these objectives will occur through attendance at training activities (basic, characteristic, and related) and the performance of in-depth activities. To verify the achievement of the planned objectives, the oral examination will be primarily used, referring where appropriate to written works or other materials resulting from the aforementioned activities.
Learning Ability.
The Bachelor's degree in Literary and Philosophical Studies, by virtue of its own specificity and vocation, aims to provide students with a high degree of autonomy for further studies beyond the degree, both in terms of acquiring the necessary tools and in developing a particular ability and sensitivity for the analysis and reading of literary texts and texts specific to the linguistic, literary, historical, and philosophical fields. Teachers will therefore guide students in acquiring the practical knowledge necessary for individual study, prioritizing direct student contact with bibliographic catalogs, libraries, and archives. From the basic courses, particular attention will be paid to learning the methods of reading textbooks, the ability to rework orally and in writing these and the content presented by the teacher in lectures. The presence of written intermediate assessments and the encouragement of producing essays and oral and/or written seminar reports will allow students to develop a good ability to individually process acquired knowledge; it will also enable teachers to monitor these abilities, intensifying educational efforts precisely where further study is anticipated. Direct contact with disciplinary tools and the encouragement of independently identifying content, linguistic, and formal data, correlated with their contextualization and historical and geographical tradition, will constitute an analytical and reading competence (verified and ratified during written and oral examinations, during seminar presentations and discussions, and also during the preparation of the final work) that constitutes the foundational specificity for the further learning of the graduate in Literary and Philosophical Studies.
Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area Graduates in Literary and Philosophical Studies must also have demonstrated the ability, with professional aptitude, to apply and extend such knowledge and skills in order to develop and support personal and coherent arguments on the themes addressed during their studies, identifying difficulties and problematic aspects and proceeding towards their resolution. A sufficient number of hours of guided study within each discipline will be dedicated to achieving this objective. To verify the attainment of such a result, the final examination outcome will be primarily considered, expressly designed in its two different aspects to apply acquired knowledge to convincingly support one's arguments.
Areas of Philologies, Languages, and Classical Literatures:
Ability to read, analyze, and situate classical texts within their linguistic, historical-cultural, and anthropological context; ability to apply the main philological methodologies and critical methods to the study of ancient texts; ability to argue logically and with appropriate historical references when interpreting a classical text.
Area of Philology, Linguistics, and Italian Literature Ability to read, analyze, and situate within their linguistic, historical-cultural, and anthropological context the texts of the Italian literary tradition, from origins to the present; ability to apply the main philological methodologies and critical methods to the study of Italian texts; ability to argue logically and with appropriate historical references when interpreting an Italian literary text.
Area of Philologies, Languages, and Modern and Comparative Literatures Ability to read, analyze, and situate within their linguistic, historical-cultural, and anthropological context important texts from modern foreign literatures studied; ability to apply the main philological methodologies and critical methods to the study of modern foreign texts; ability to argue logically and with appropriate historical references when interpreting a modern foreign literary text.
Historical Area Ability to analyze and use various types of historical sources; ability to connect historical events and cultural phenomena.
Philosophical Area Ability to read, understand, historically situate, and analyze philosophical texts of the Western tradition; ability to connect the articulations of philosophical thought to historical development and other cultural phenomena; logical argumentation ability.
Demo-Ethno-Anthropological Area Ability to understand cultural phenomena with reference to the ethnological and anthropological study of different societies.
