Communication skills.
Graduates in Literary and Philosophical Studies must have demonstrated in-depth linguistic and argumentative skills enabling them to communicate information, ideas, problems and solutions to both specialist and non-specialist audiences, using various types of written language, including computer-based languages appropriately. These skills will be acquired through exercises, written and oral reports during seminars aimed at improving linguistic precision and expository clarity. Teaching activities during study abroad stays will further refine these skills in languages other than Italian. The achievement of these communication skills will primarily be assessed through exam outcomes (written and oral), designed specifically to communicate acquired knowledge.
Employment and professional prospects for graduates.
Expert in promotion and management of cultural and communication activities Graduates of this class may perform professional activities at local authorities and specific institutions such as libraries, archives and academies, as well as at publishing houses, journalistic editorial offices, foundations, companies and other professional entities operating in the field of organizing events and cultural activities. However, it should be noted that for many professional roles, the basic competences and skills acquired during the three-year degree must be complemented by specific training offered in master's courses, first and second level master's programs, doctoral courses (starting from those activated at the Siena University), and subsequent training levels provided for by regulations for access to teaching. Graduates with sufficient credits in appropriate sector groups may, as provided by current legislation, participate in admission tests for secondary teaching training paths.
Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIAN Associated competences.
Expert in promotion and management of cultural and communication activities Good written and oral command of the Italian language; theoretical and practical knowledge of linguistic fundamentals; good knowledge of text analysis methods, their interpretation and placement in various historical-cultural contexts.
Function in work context.
Expert in promotion and management of cultural and communication activities The main functions the graduate will perform are: writing of scientific texts in Italian and foreign languages; literary translation from ancient and modern languages; support for editorial activities. Graduates will thus be able to operate in the fields of cultural services and production, communication and information, public relations and productive organizations.
Description of specific learning objectives.
The Bachelor's degree in Literary and Philosophical Studies offers a detailed and coherent possibility of training paths based on the common foundation of Basic and Characteristic Activities of class L-10, with a wide range of credits to be acquired in classical and modern literary disciplines, philological-linguistic disciplines, and philosophical disciplines, as well as historical disciplines and geography. Starting from this basis, students may choose to acquire greater competences in the field of classical culture (Greek and Latin language and literature, classical philology, ancient history), in that of philologies, literatures, languages and modern cultures (Romance philology and Italian, Italian literature, modern foreign languages and literatures), or in that of philosophical and demo-etno-anthropological disciplines, giving more weight to one or the other area according to the specific training choice.
Moreover, students must be able to confidently master critical writing appropriate for the analysis and interpretation of specific cultural products under investigation: for this purpose, exam verification, in a significant number of courses, will also proceed through written tests; a minimum of 6 cfu will be dedicated to the study of Italian linguistics and grammar; other specific analytical and critical writing skills may be acquired in the preparation of the final exam (see Characteristics of the final exam). Upon graduation, students will have acquired both the ability to read, interpret and place a wide variety of texts in an appropriate historical-cultural context, and the ability to navigate the places of preservation of these texts and more generally within their reference cultural context, in order to be able to expand, deepen and appropriately use, also independently, their knowledge and competences.
Among the training objectives of the degree course is also the acquisition by students of knowledge and skills that constitute not only a basic preparation regarding the literary (classical and modern) and philosophical area, but also a key to accessing the organizational and relational modalities necessary to perform a professional role in this area.
Fundamental are, in this regard, the basic skills related to theoretical reflection and critical interpretation, acquired not only in specific theoretical-methodological teachings, but also through the learning and practice of philological and philosophical knowledge.
All graduates of the course will also be able to use the main computer tools, with particular reference to software dedicated, in specific sectors, to text composition and analysis, bibliographic research, management of multimedia languages and archival-book assets (computer lab: 3 cfu). Each graduate will also have adequate mastery of at least one EU language (English language proficiency: 3 cfu; Foreign Language exam: 6 cfu).
While maintaining the common base, the course allows for an articulation into specific training paths, oriented towards the valorization of the different potentials present within class L-10, on the different sides of classical philological-literary, modern philological-literary (Italianist and comparative), historical-philosophical, philosophical, and social sciences. In this sense, both the number of different sectors present within the characteristic disciplines, and the appropriate possibility of choice and the breadth of the credit range assigned to the sector of related and integrated activities, offer students the possibility to orient their study plan according to a more specific study perspective and future employment opportunities. In this way, even within the chosen training path, each student has the possibility to partially personalize their study plan.
While maintaining on one hand the possibility of foreseeing differentiated training paths and on the other the need to consider the entire training offer from a unitary and interdisciplinary perspective, the teachings provided in the study course can be aggregated into six main disciplinary learning areas:
1) Area of Philologies, Languages and Classical Literatures: teachings belonging to scientific-disciplinary sectors L-FIL-LET/02, L-FIL-LET/04, L-FIL-LET/05, L-FIL-LET/08 offer solid preparation on languages, cultures and literatures of the ancient world and medieval Latin, through both philological text analysis and anthropological study of classical cultures.
2) Area of Philology, Linguistics and Italian Literature: teachings belonging to scientific-disciplinary sectors L-FIL-LET/09, L-FIL-LET/10, L-FIL-LET/11, L-FIL-LET/12, L-FIL-LET/13 offer solid preparation on the history of literature, language and culture in Italy from the Middle Ages to the present, through both philological and linguistic text analysis, and through the study of relationships between literary phenomena and other cultural phenomena characterizing different historical periods (with particular reference to the history of theater and performance: in this context, sector L-ART/05 may also be included).
3) Area of Philologies, Languages and Modern and Comparative Literatures: teachings belonging to scientific-disciplinary sectors L-FIL-LET/14, L-FIL-LET/15, L-LIN/01, L-LIN/03, L-LIN/04, L-LIN/05, L-LIN/06, L-LIN/07, L-LIN/08, L-LIN/09, L-LIN/10, L-LIN/11, L-LIN/12, L-LIN/13, L-LIN/14, L-LIN/21 (as well as sector L-FIL-LET/09, 'Romance Philology and Linguistics', relevant to both the Italianist and other Romance languages and literatures context) offer solid preparation on modern European and American languages and cultures, through both philological study of texts (Romance and German philology), historical, theoretical and comparative analysis of literary production (modern literatures, comparative literatures), and acquisition of theoretical and practical skills in languages (general linguistics, modern languages).
4) Historical area: teachings belonging to scientific-disciplinary sectors L-ANT/02, L-ANT/03, L-ANT/07, M-STO/01, M-STO/02, M-STO/04, M-STO/07 offer solid preparation on Western history from classical antiquity to the present, through the study of different types of sources (from archaeological to archival) and with constant attention to the relationship between historical context and cultural production (literary and artistic: in this context, scientific-disciplinary sectors L-ART/01, L-ART/02, L-ART/03 also fall).
5) Philosophical area: teachings belonging to scientific-disciplinary sectors M-FIL/01, M-FIL/02, M-FIL/03, M-FIL/04, M-FIL/05, M-FIL/06, M-FIL/07, M-FIL/08 offer solid preparation on Western philosophical thought from classical antiquity to the present, investigating both its historical development and theoretical, logical and moral implications, also with particular reference to reflection on language and beauty (philosophy of language, semiotics, aesthetics) which makes philosophical knowledge indispensable in the training path of class L-10.
6) Demo-etno-anthropological area: teachings belonging to scientific-disciplinary sector M-DEA/01 offer solid training on methods and contents of demo-etno-anthropological research, capable of placing literary and philosophical texts within a broader horizon of reflection on human cultures.

LABOR CONSULTANT For the practice of the labor consultant profession, the graduate must complete a mandatory internship period of eighteen months at the office of an authorized labor consultant, six of which may be completed in advance during the third year of the degree course, in accordance with the agreement signed between the University of Siena and the Provincial Council of Labor Consultants of Siena.
Once the certification of completed internship is obtained, the individual may participate in the qualification exam, held annually, organized regionally following the official announcement made by the Ministry of Labor.
Once the qualification exam is successfully passed, the new labor consultant may register with the Provincial Order Council where they intend to practice the profession.
Labor consultants may operate in a free profession regime, with their own office, or at companies, public or private, trade unions, associations representing professional interests typical of the labor and business world.
Other employment opportunities relate to the professional profiles of Judicial Services Technician, Occupational Safety Technician, and Employment Services Technician.
Legal Operator in Companies and Public Entities The training path is aimed at immediate employment in central and peripheral state administrations, excluding only senior management, in territorial administrations, publicly owned companies, in the organizational structures of administrations operating in the sectors of the environment, cultural heritage, and immigration; in public and private companies, especially those that frequently interact with public administrations.
Final Exam Characteristics The degree is obtained by passing a final exam, which consists of the evaluation by the graduation committee of the final work written by the student under the supervision and responsibility of the thesis advisor.
The final work consists of a written document accompanied by the necessary bibliographic references on a topic agreed upon between the student and the thesis advisor according to the procedures defined by the course's academic regulations.
To pass the final exam, the student must demonstrate adequate knowledge and understanding of the assigned topic, autonomous learning and research skills, ability to correctly use the consulted literature and necessary sources, and ability to present and support scientific arguments in a logical and coherent manner.
The final work may also be written in English.
3 ECTS credits are awarded for the final degree exam.
Required Knowledge for Admission To be admitted to the Bachelor's Degree Course, one must possess: - a secondary school diploma or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent; - English language proficiency at level A2/2, which may be obtained through language courses offered by the University Language Center. The verification of titles attesting level A2/2 is conducted by the University Language Center according to standard procedures.
For those enrolling in the Bachelor's Degree in Legal Services, initial knowledge verification tests are provided, requiring basic knowledge of General Culture, political current affairs, Civic Education with particular reference to constitutional principles, and Modern and Contemporary History.
Participation in these tests is mandatory, but does not affect admission or enrollment in the Bachelor's Degree Course. The procedures for conducting the verification test will be further defined in the course's academic regulations.
Students who do not pass the verification will be assigned additional mandatory courses to complete during the first year of study through the recovery courses organized by the Department of Jurisprudence; the acquired preparation will be verified after the recovery courses. In case of persistent gaps, supplementary readings will be recommended, and the student's entire training path will be periodically monitored by tutor professors.
Degree Awarded. First Level Degree in Legal Services
Knowledge and Understanding. Public Law Area The graduate:
- possesses adequate knowledge of constitutional law, with particular reference to norms on state organization and law production.
- has knowledge of current administrative law issues and doctrinal and jurisprudential interpretations;
- knows the substantive and procedural discipline of general taxation;
- possesses good knowledge of the fundamentals of European Union law and international law;
- has knowledge of general principles of criminal law and some specific criminal offenses related to business and labor organization, crimes against public administration, as well as criminal procedural law.
- has knowledge of some of the most modern branches of the legal system, such as law of new technologies and data privacy and protection law.
- possesses adequate knowledge to address legal issues related to the organization of the labor world, public administration, local authorities, and specific areas such as cultural heritage, tourism, food consumption, and trade.
Private Law Area The graduate:
- acquires knowledge of general theory (system, sources, constitution, code, interpretation);
- possesses excellent knowledge of fundamental private law institutions, with particular regard to aspects relevant to labor consultants and industrial relations experts;
- has in-depth knowledge of the fundamental principles of commercial law and civil procedural law, with particular reference to judicial and extrajudicial dispute resolution procedures in labor matters.
- has deep knowledge of data privacy and new technologies legislation;
- possesses excellent legal knowledge to address issues related to the tourism sector, as well as production, consumption, and trade of food products, with particular reference to agricultural production, labeling, and valorization of regional typical products.
Historical-Philosophical Area The graduate:
- possesses adequate knowledge of the historical evolution of legal models of business and labor, also within the context of local and national public organization, both regarding the origin of fundamental institutions and the development of protection systems.
- knows the fundamental notions of legal theory.
Labor Law Area The graduate:
- has in-depth knowledge of labor and union regulations, discipline regarding worker health and safety in the workplace, social security legislation, and conciliation procedures;
- has adequate knowledge of European labor legislation;
- has solid mastery of labor law in public administration;
- is fully aware of the interaction mechanisms between different social parties present in the labor market.

Judgment autonomy.
The graduate is able to:
- identify the best solution for a concrete case;
- solve problems in the most effective and efficient way, through weighing the interests at stake;
- identify the most appropriate measures and actions in a specific organizational context, also through investigation of legal norms, collective contracts, study of scholarly contributions, and judicial pronouncements.
These abilities are acquired through classroom lectures, individual study of textbooks recommended by the instructor, targeted research on specific topics of particular relevance, possibly in student groups; as well as through the preparation of the thesis; the experience of training internships; and any study stays abroad.
Judgment autonomy will be verified in practical exercises and in-course assessments conducted during the lectures of individual courses, in final examination tests, and in the preparation of the thesis.

Learning capacity.
The graduate has:
- the ability to autonomously implement the knowledge and skills acquired during the degree course;
- the ability to conduct in-depth studies and update knowledge, also critically re-elaborating the acquired content in light of changes in regulations, jurisprudence, and scholarship.
These abilities are acquired through classroom lectures, attendance at seminars and practical exercises where specific research is conducted on topics of particular current relevance in light of subsequent regulatory and/or jurisprudential changes.
The adequacy of acquiring these abilities will be verified in-course through practical exercises and intermediate tests, as well as through final examination tests of individual courses, and through the preparation of the thesis.

Ability to apply knowledge and understanding.
Public law area The graduate:
- has excellent knowledge of the system of sources of national law, with particular reference to constitutional norms and the characteristics of the state legal system;
- has mastery of tax law in both substantive and procedural dimensions;
- is able to correctly apply administrative law norms in resolving concrete cases and problems, also taking into account jurisprudential and scholarly guidelines;
- has the ability to interpret the norms of the European Union legal system and possesses a global view of the European integration process.
- has high knowledge of public administration organization in the structures of central and local government.
- is able to recognize penal aspects of non-compliance with certain rules concerning labor organization and the status of public administration.
The acquisition of the above requirements will be verified through the following methods:
- practical exercises on jurisprudential cases;
- intermediate tests and final exams of individual courses;
- internships and other training experiences organized within the study program.

Private law area The graduate:
- has the ability to navigate between normative sources of various origins;
- is fully capable of interpreting legal norms and applying them to concrete situations;
- has in-depth knowledge of the normative and organizational reality of business, commerce, and labor.
The acquisition of the above requirements will be verified through the following methods:
- practical exercises on jurisprudential cases;
- intermediate tests and final exams of individual courses;
- internships and other training experiences organized within the study program.

Historical-philosophical area The graduate:
- is able to interpret positive law, also in light of its historical and philosophical evolution;
- has full awareness of the typical methods of legal science and their application modalities in judicial practice.
The acquisition of the above requirements will be verified through the following methods:
- intermediate tests and final exams of individual courses;
- internships and other training experiences organized within the study program.

Labor law area The graduate:
- has solid theoretical-practical preparation in the field of labor consulting and personnel management;
- is able to interpret and apply remuneration, pension, and social security norms related to employment relationships and apply them to concrete cases, also thanks to professional internships;
- is able to identify obligations and measures that can be implemented in a specific organizational context.
The acquisition of the above requirements will be verified through the following methods:
- practical exercises on jurisprudential cases;
- intermediate tests and final exams of individual courses;
- internships and other training experiences organized within the study program.

Expected occupational and professional opportunities for graduates.
LABOR CONSULTANT For the practice of the profession of labor consultant, the graduate must complete a mandatory internship period of eighteen months at the office of an authorized labor consultant, six of which may be completed in advance during the third year of the degree course, in accordance with the agreement signed between the University of Siena and the Provincial Council of Labor Consultants of Siena.

Legal Professional in Companies and Public Bodies The training path is aimed at immediate employment in central and peripheral state administrations, excluding only senior management, in territorial administrations, publicly owned companies, in the organizational structures of administrations operating in the sectors of the environment, cultural heritage, and immigration; in public and private companies, especially those that frequently interact with public administrations.
Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIAN Associated competencies for the role.
LABOR CONSULTANT The labor law expert must have excellent knowledge of labor law regulations, commercial law, and in particular the functioning of business organizations. In particular, the ability to interpret regulations, especially those related to employment relationships as well as remuneration, tax, pension, and social assistance regulations; knowledge of all legal obligations is also required.
Other competencies associated with the role, in addition to good mastery of the English language, relate to effective written and verbal communication, the ability to work in a group, and the ability to pose and solve problems.
Legal Professional in Companies and Public Bodies The competencies associated with the professional profiles relate to: knowledge of reference national and European regulatory systems; knowledge of interpretative and application methods and techniques of normative sources; the ability to contextualize legally relevant issues within the reference socio-economic and institutional system; the ability to draft legal documents.
Function in the workplace.
LABOR CONSULTANT The degree course aims to train experts in labor law capable of performing a qualified professional activity dedicated to personnel administration and management, labor relations, collective bargaining, and social security. The main functions relate to the establishment and evolution of employment relationships; maintaining related accounting, economic, legal, insurance, pension, and social positions; informing about obligations in labor, pension, and social assistance matters for workers; maintaining the payroll and calculating pension contributions; interpreting and applying collective agreements.
Legal Professional in Companies and Public Bodies The study path aims to train a professional with a solid basic legal competence, especially in administrative law. The graduate will be able to exercise the following functions in their workplace: identification of reference normative sources; critical understanding of legal texts; identification of interpretative and application issues; broad knowledge of organizational dynamics of businesses and public administration, central and peripheral, as well as penal profiles closely related to public administration activities. The graduate will also be able to perform consulting activities and prepare legal documents.
Description of specific training objectives.
The Bachelor's degree course in Legal Services aims to provide students not only with an adequate institutional knowledge of the various disciplines in the legal field, but also with a pronounced professional knowledge in line with the prescribed curricula. This is to train professionals of different types, particularly, on one hand, labor law experts with high competence in personnel administration and management as well as industrial relations and social security; on the other hand, corporate lawyers and legal consultants for companies, public bodies, and territorial administrations.
The training offer proposed in the first two years of the course is common to all prescribed curricula, while it differs in the final year of study, where the offer is more tailored to the different possible occupational opportunities.
In the two-year period of the Legal Services degree course, all basic training activities (IUS/01, IUS/08) and a significant portion of characteristic activities (IUS/04, IUS/07, IUS/10) are included, providing students with solid legal knowledge as well as adequate historical-philosophical (IUS/18, IUS/19, IUS/20), linguistic, and economic knowledge (SECS-P/01; SECS-P/07).
More specifically, the courses included in the common two-year period are aimed at providing students with essential knowledge to navigate different areas of law and also the ability to use legal terminology and reasoning, both generally and with regard to specific issues of individual subjects (for example, those falling under the disciplinary sector IUS/12-tax law).
The subjects taught in the third year differ according to the configured curricula. Alongside other characteristic and related-integrative courses of the degree class, the final year also includes student-selected courses and additional training activities, with particular attention to training and orientation internships, in order to provide students with specific sectoral competencies useful for developing the different professional profiles the degree course aims to cultivate, such as labor consultant (after passing the relevant qualification exam); corporate lawyer and legal expert for public bodies; judicial operator; etc. For this purpose, the final year will particularly focus on deepening legal knowledge and reasoning and applying the acquired knowledge.

High School Diploma University fees and contributions For information on university fees and contributions, visit the following page on the university website www.unisi.it/tasse Dates and deadlines For information on dates and deadlines, visit the following page on the university website "Study Plan" www.unisi.it/didattica/immatricolazioni-e-iscrizioni/immatricolazioni Roles Chair/Chair of the Teaching Committee FRANCO CAMBI Program, textbooks, and objectives Professional title conferred by the degree.
CULTURAL HERITAGE OPERATOR Given the continuous and rapid evolution of the job market, which requires new skills for numerous professional profiles capable of collaborating in operational interventions for the protection, conservation, and enhancement of cultural heritage, as well as those related to its valorization and accessibility (ex art. 1, law 110/2014), the knowledge and skills acquired by graduates will enable them to access various employment opportunities related to study, cataloging, documentation, assistance, teaching, and archaeological excavations at public and private entities operating in the management, protection, enhancement, and accessibility of cultural heritage, including:
- State, regional, and local museums;
- Central and peripheral bodies of MiBACT;
- Local authorities;
- Archives and libraries;
- Phototeques, cinecites, media libraries;
- Theaters; professional companies and organizations;
- Publishing houses and record labels.
Final exam characteristics The final exam consists of the discussion of a written work prepared by the candidate on a topic agreed upon with one of the course lecturers. Candidates must demonstrate the ability to conduct basic scientific research, using appropriate methodologies and updated bibliographic tools, or to complete technical-operational procedures applied to the knowledge, protection, and enhancement of cultural heritage, while accompanying the work with a written text justifying methodology, foundation, and update.
In both cases, candidates must demonstrate having acquired the necessary competencies to design and support arguments and to solve specific problems in their field of study.
The final exam may be prepared in the following ways: a) essay-style written work; b) computer-based work configured as a system or product (website, CD, etc.); c) multimedia work. For types a) and b), the work must be accompanied by a few pages of text illustrating theoretical and/or scientific motivations, structure, execution methods, produced results, and contribution to the relevant discipline.
Typically, the final exam work is written in Italian. The Teaching Committee may authorize the final exam and its discussion to be conducted in one of the other languages of the European Community.
9 ECTS are attributed to the final exam. The merit score is expressed in 110 (centodecimi), with possible honors, and is assigned according to precise parameters: the commission adds the grade assigned to the written work and discussion to the weighted average of the grades obtained by the student in the exams, evaluating completeness, correctness, foundation, and potential original contribution.
Required knowledge for access Admission to the Bachelor's Degree course is conditional on possessing a secondary school diploma or another title obtained abroad, recognized as suitable.
Students enrolling in the Bachelor's Degree course must have adequate basic preparation consisting of linguistic skills and cultural knowledge typically acquired in high schools and upper secondary education institutions.
In particular, good skills in various forms of the Italian language are required, as well as knowledge of English at least at level A2/2 of the Council of Europe Language Reference Framework.
The evaluation of skills in various forms of the Italian language is conducted through a written test (Tolc-SU Test on line - Humanistic Studies offered by CISIA Interuniversity Consortium for Integrated Systems for Access).
In case of negative test result, admission to the Bachelor's Degree course is permitted, but additional educational obligations (OFA) will be assigned to address the identified educational gaps and meet requirements in the first year of study.
In particular, students with OFA will be required to attend an intensive Italian recovery course with a final assessment.
Regarding English language knowledge, students enrolling must take a test to evaluate individual linguistic skills, which will direct them to the most suitable preparatory course to reach the level required by the study plan (B1).
Degree awarded.
Bachelor's Degree in Historical Sciences and Cultural Heritage Knowledge and understanding.
Generic Area The training path for students in the three-year Bachelor's Degree in Historical Sciences and Cultural Heritage aims to form graduates with significant historical-cultural knowledge in a broad sense and the ability to understand and deepen specific themes in the fields of archaeology, history, and the sciences of the book and document, visual arts and architecture, cinema, music, and theater. Textbooks for each learning phase will be selected based on high scientific and cultural standards, research updates, content transparency, and methodological effectiveness. The acquisition of solid historical foundations, essential for the correct application of knowledge in the cultural field, will be accompanied by the development of appropriate analytical methods (typological, phenomenological, stylistic, paleographic, diplomatic) for the study object (documentation, codes and books, landscapes, constructions, archaeological finds, artworks, musical compositions, theatrical pieces, films) and by an analytical reading of critical texts, considering the context in which they were developed, the author's perspective, and generally the history of reception and interpretation of the data collected. The achievement of these objectives is substantially supported by seminars, exercises, and laboratory activities, alongside frontal lessons, and for the Archaeology curriculum, by field missions in territorial areas and significant archaeological sites. The interactive nature of these activities will allow teachers to progressively verify the growth of knowledge and acquisition of analytical methods by students, without relying solely on final exams. The multiplicity of disciplines characterizing the study course will enable graduates to identify connections between different aspects of cultural heritage and to address specific issues in their field of interest with openness and awareness of interaction possibilities with other fields of knowledge.
Archaeological Area At the end of studies, graduates will have acquired general knowledge of different archaeological phases (from prehistory to post-medieval archaeology) and the transformations affecting landscapes, constructions, artistic objects, and material culture of the past. Basic knowledge also includes principles, methodologies, and approaches of contemporary archaeology, useful for understanding different historical and cultural contexts. A third knowledge vector involves themes of organization, conservation, protection, and enhancement of cultural heritage.
Acquisition of such knowledge and skills will be verified throughout the training path through seminars, written and oral exams, and reports.
Cinema, Music, and Theater Area At the end of studies, graduates will have acquired general knowledge of the history of cinema, music, and theater. They will know the fundamental aspects of the theoretical frameworks of these disciplines and possess the necessary knowledge to produce critical analyses of texts and sources.
They will have research skills in historiography, archival investigation, cataloging, inventory compilation, description of phenomena, and data interpretation, also aimed at the conservation and enhancement of material culture of cinematic, musical, and theatrical practices as cultural heritage.
Basic knowledge will also allow reconstructions and identification of styles, languages, and genres, according to multiple competence areas, open to considering formal, organizational, productive, communicative, and public consumption aspects.
Acquisition of such knowledge and skills will be verified throughout the training path through seminars, written and oral exams, and reports.
Historical-Artistic Area At the end of the three-year program, graduates will have acquired solid basic knowledge of the development of art history from the ancient world to the contemporary era. The discipline is understood within its broad methodological criteria: study of artistic and architectural artifacts in their dual material and cultural nature, dynamics of realization and reception, physical and conservation history, and critical and collecting history.
The path aims to stimulate critical analysis skills, develop competencies in stylistic and iconographic reading of artworks, and understand artifacts in relation to their context of origin or belonging, often altered or irretrievably lost. The goal is to form figures capable of understanding, navigating, and operating in the field of historical-artistic heritage.
Historical-Documentary Area At the end of studies, graduates will have acquired general knowledge of different historical periods and corresponding economic, social, political, and cultural transformations, with full awareness of historiographical traditions and periodization issues, as well as good ability to synthesize historical literature texts.
They will have acquired solid basic knowledge of principles, methods, and technical aspects of archival science for understanding documentary materials from the medieval, modern, and contemporary eras, enabling them to place them in their historical and cultural context and subject them to necessary critical analysis, as well as to know and address issues related to their organization, conservation, protection, and enhancement as cultural heritage.
They will possess paleographic and codicological knowledge enabling critical investigation of the evolution of writing in all its manifestations and, by reconstructing the history of graphic forms, derive elements and data for cultural history.
Acquisition of such knowledge and skills will be verified throughout the training path through seminars, written and oral exams, and reports.

COURSE: [D002] HISTORICAL SCIENCES AND CULTURAL HERITAGE
SECTION: Autonomy of Judgment
URL: https://unisi.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10697

Autonomy of Judgment.
The common courses of the degree program provide a solid foundation of historical and cultural knowledge to develop intellectual and moral sensitivity towards essential themes of history, memory, culture, and the conservation of the 'products' of diverse cultures. The progressive focus of learning on more specific themes in different disciplinary fields prevents an overly specialized approach at this stage of university education and ensures the integration of each field's issues within a broad framework of social, economic, and ethical considerations that characterize today's most advanced trends in the conception and management of cultural heritage. Critical and analytical reflection, and thus autonomy of judgment, will be stimulated through lectures, but more specifically through participation in workshops, exercises, and seminars: direct participation in excavations and field surveys; seminars and lectures by external professors; archaeological survey seminars and classification and conservation of archaeological artifacts; seminars on analysis and reading of various documentary types; paleographic and codicological exercises; iconographic and stylistic analysis exercises of artworks; seminars on artistic techniques; guided visits to museums and monuments; guided viewings of films, videos, and theatrical performances. The goal of these activities is to allow students to engage in a thorough and monitored manner with specific questions, as well as to develop their ability to formulate autonomous judgments grounded in objectively verifiable contexts, for example: the reconstruction of an ancient landscape, the history of a monument, an urban neighborhood, a rural settlement, the analysis of an archaeological artifact; the analysis of a documentary type and the methods of memory conservation; the reconstruction of the development of a book type and the methods of knowledge transmission; the iconographic reading, historical contextualization, and dating of an artwork; the analytical reading of a film sequence; the scenic reconstruction of a theatrical text; the comparison of two interpretations of the same musical piece. Autonomy of judgment will be assessed at every level of the learning evaluation tests to which students will be subjected: oral presentations of individual and group work, essays and written reports, outcomes of internship and training activities, oral and written exams (where applicable also in progress). Finally, the judgment capacity must be fully expressed in the final thesis presented as the final assessment.

Learning Ability.
To ensure a solid degree of autonomy in any subsequent studies after the degree, particular attention will be given from the basic courses to learning methods of reading textbooks, the ability to process content presented by the instructor in lectures, as well as the methods of acquiring practical knowledge (exercises, laboratory experiences, and later field training and internship activities). The bibliographies of individual courses will be accompanied by usage instructions; students will also be guided in selecting and structuring direct experiences in various sectors of cultural heritage (excavation experiences, visits to archaeological sites, artistic monuments and museums, archives and libraries, viewing films and theatrical performances, listening to live music). A specific space will be dedicated to bibliographic research methodologies and the compilation of inventories and catalogs in each field of investigation. The assessment of individual courses must allow the instructor to monitor the student's ability to organize individual study, and to invest further educational efforts in cases where further studies are anticipated. The wide range of common courses and the progressive definition of the characteristic path will allow motivated students to verify and solidify their choices and to conclude the degree course with a wealth of knowledge and study and research methods, culminating in the writing of the final thesis, a valuable opportunity for the graduate and the reference instructor to establish the groundwork for a relationship of exchange and increasing student autonomy, suitable for the more advanced stages of study.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area The three-year Bachelor's program in Historical Sciences and Cultural Heritage aims to combine foundational training with a critical-analytical approach to study objects. As the training activities progress from year to year, there is a gradual increase in attention to the methodological and practical aspects of the acquired knowledge. For this purpose, contract professors, including professionals in the protection and conservation of cultural heritage, are also provided. The assessment of the application ability may take the form of a written paper and/or an oral presentation on a specific concrete problem, followed by an interactive classroom discussion. Student interaction with representatives from the professional world and the guided sharing of results achieved throughout the learning process are both useful and effective elements for enhancing awareness of the inseparable connection that exists in various fields of cultural heritage between history, theory, and practice, and between individual knowledge and interaction with the context. This awareness is the first step towards a professional and creative approach to the specific requirements and tasks of the different areas of the degree program. Particularly significant in this regard are the laboratory activities, differentiated according to the different curricula. Graduates will be able to apply the comprehensive set of knowledge and understanding acquired in various sectors: building a solid professional approach to work in various activity areas (research, protection, valorization, training, communication); identifying areas and innovative research themes in the cultural heritage sector; participation in working groups aimed at conducting research in the fields of interest; participation in the construction and experimentation of innovative tools and technologies in the cultural heritage sector; design and implementation of diverse forms of public communication. The pursuit of these goals is made possible by the very structure of the individual curricular courses, seminar activities, and internships. Assessment Methods: Curricular exams. Evaluation of participation in seminar activities and field and laboratory research.

Archaeological Area.
At the end of the course, the graduate will be able to: apply basic knowledge and understanding regarding the reconstruction of past landscape transformation phenomena, the evolution of urbanization phenomena, residential field experiments, the production, circulation, and consumption of material culture, the mobility of people, animals, and goods, and the dissemination of ideal forms conveyed by archaeological artifacts; critically use archaeological sources in their various forms; decipher and analyze material evidence from the past, of any type and era, dating and locating them through classification; analyze archaeological artifacts from different perspectives: typological, functional, archaeological; reconstruct from various perspectives the economic and ecological profiles of human communities over time; deepen their knowledge in various training areas through the main documentary and bibliographic sources.

Cinema, Music, and Theater Area.
At the end of the course, the graduate will be able to: apply basic knowledge to conduct historical and theoretical research and compilations; use fundamental skills to work on works and their circulation; analyze the technical, formal, linguistic, and stylistic aspects of an expressive practice; produce a reconstruction of the critical profile of the most important authors of the past and present; identify the most significant phenomena from both an aesthetic and a communicative perspective; describe the construction processes and the formation methods of texts, their representations, and performances; refer to traditional critical literature and reconstruct contemporary debate; address the issues of organization, preservation, and valorization of cultural heritage, with specific reference to cinematic, musical, and theatrical heritage; deepen their knowledge in various areas through the visitation of libraries, cinemateques, conservatories, and academies.

Historical-Artistic Area.
At the end of the training course, graduates will be able to: analyze and understand historical-artistic and architectural testimonies from ancient to contemporary times; know and reconstruct the technical and historical-cultural events of artistic and architectural artifacts, also in relation to protection and conservation themes.

Historical-Documentary Area.
At the end of the course, the graduate will be able to: apply knowledge and understanding regarding the reconstruction of the economic, social, and political dimensions of historical events, identifying their interconnections, evolution, and transformations; use, subjecting them to critical analysis, historical sources and documents; decipher and analyze written testimonies from the past, of any type and era, dating and locating them through the study and comparison of execution techniques; describe documents and documentary complexes, having learned the formation lines of archival collections and the main techniques of their management; know and address issues related to the organization, preservation, and valorization of archival heritage; deepen their knowledge in various training areas through the main documentary and bibliographic sources.

Communication Skills.
The characteristic teachings of the degree course involve active student participation not only in frontal lectures but also during exercises and seminar activities. Historical disciplines and cultural heritage require a communication skill that has a particularly intricate relationship with the subject of study. Describing an archaeological artifact, a document, a code, or a figurative or performative work of art, as well as presenting a historical-critical evaluation, implies – in addition to studying textbooks and their analytical objects – precise linguistic and ecphrastic skills, which vary according to the nature of the audience. The monitoring of the student's communication skills will cover both the oral and written aspects. These competencies and skills will be acquired gradually throughout the educational path, and in particular, students will be involved in individual or group written and oral presentations on specific study topics. This will stimulate general and dissemination-oriented communication and presentation skills, progressing to a reasonable level of scientific specificity in the final examination.
Expected occupational and professional opportunities for graduates.
CULTURAL HERITAGE OPERATOR. In light of a continuously evolving and rapidly changing labor market, which requires new skills for numerous professional profiles capable of collaborating in operational interventions for the protection, preservation, and conservation of cultural assets, as well as those related to their valorization and accessibility (ex art. 1, Law 110/2014), the knowledge and skills acquired by graduates will enable them to access various occupational opportunities related to activities such as research, cataloging, classification, assistance, teaching, and archaeological excavations at public and private institutions operating in the field of management, protection, valorization, and accessibility of cultural assets, including:
- State, regional, and local museums;
- Central and peripheral bodies of MiBACT;
- Local authorities;
- Archives and libraries;
- Photo archives, film archives, media archives;
- Theaters; companies and professional organizations;
- Publishing houses and record companies.
Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIANO Associated competencies for the role.
CULTURAL HERITAGE OPERATOR
- Ability to interpret, historically situate, and compare archaeological artifacts, works of art, architectural monuments, and multimedia works;
- Ability to conduct historical, paleographic, and diplomatic analysis of texts and documentation;
- Ability to interpret and direct social relationship structures;
- Ability to design and manage textual and visual communication channels;
Role in the workplace.
CULTURAL HERITAGE OPERATOR
- Participates in the management of routine activities within institutions and public bodies and private companies engaged in the cultural heritage sector;
- Contributes to documentation, bibliographic research and cataloging activities, and conservation;
- Collaborates in the planning of initiatives, activities, and events for the knowledge and promotion of cultural heritage;
- Collaborates in the dissemination and education within the cultural heritage sector, designing and implementing specific interventions for distinct target groups;
- Drafts informational and promotional materials.
Description of specific educational objectives.
The course aims to train graduates with significant historical and cultural competencies, supported by foundational educational activities that constitute a substantial part of the educational path (especially the first and second years of the course): historical disciplines (L-ANT/02, L-ANT/03, M-STO/01, M-STO/02, M-STO/04), Latin language and literature (L-FIL-LET/04), classical philology (L-FIL-LET/05), Italian literature (L-FIL-LET/10), geography (M-GGR/01), and demo-ethno-anthropological disciplines (M-DEA/01).
In addition to the activities that form the common and foundational educational axis, the degree course provides, from the first year, a more specific and characteristic education. In particular, the characteristic educational offer includes historical, critical, and methodological courses that, choosing among the archaeological, historical-archival-paleographic, historical-artistic, and performing arts fields, students differentiate according to disciplinary perspective. For the archaeological field, acquisition of the fundamentals and methodologies of the discipline (excavation, survey, context documentation, L-ANT/10), as well as for the prehistoric, Etruscan, Greek, Roman, late-antique, and medieval periods, analysis and interpretation of material and figurative culture, as well as architecture, settlements, landscapes, and productions that characterize the societies and economies of Europe and the Mediterranean (L-ANT/01, L-ANT/06, L-ANT/07, L-ANT/08); for the historical-documentary field, methodological and critical preparation in the disciplinary fields of ancient, medieval, modern, and contemporary history (L-ANT/02, L-ANT/03, M-STO/01, M-STO/02, M-STO/04) and geography (M-GGR/01), with an emphasis on the analysis and interpretation of written library and documentary sources from antiquity to the contemporary era, considered both in technical and material aspects and in relation to their formation and tradition, through the specific approaches of paleography, codicology, and archival science (M-STO/08, M-STO/09); for the historical-artistic field, preparation in the disciplinary fields of medieval, modern, and contemporary art history (L-ART/01, L-ART/02, L-ART/03), as well as in the fields of iconography and iconology, minor arts, and the history of architecture (ICAR/18), then in the protection and conservation of artistic heritage, referring to aspects of the history, theory, and practice of restoration and their practical verification in the laboratory (L-ART/04), in a strong and cohesive overall vision across various disciplinary fields, with a rigorous philological approach, both on works of art and architecture in their production and reception contexts (from the artist's workshop and studio to private collecting, from religious buildings to public spaces and museums) and thus on their documentation and historical-critical analysis (from art literature to historiography, to militant criticism); for the performing arts curriculum, preparation in the disciplinary fields of theater, performance, and acting history (L-ART/05), the history, theory, criticism of cinema and the cinematic and audiovisual language (L-ART/06), musical language and music history (L-ART/07), in a common perspective across the three fields that requires the rigorous integration of historical and critical analysis of theatrical, cinematic, and musical events and their related discursive practices with a multiplanar theoretical and analytical approach, with particular attention to the technical, formal, expressive, and compositional analysis of theatrical, cinematic, and musical texts.
A common characteristic activity for all is cultural heritage legislation (IUS/10).
Students' specific training can be enhanced through choices made within the related and integrative activities, aimed at creating further knowledge and skills in the fields of protection, valorization, management, and accessibility of cultural assets. Related courses may also vary depending on the curricula and include, for example, archaeological methodologies (L-ANT/10), technological developments and scientific methods (GEO/09), and some demo-ethno-anthropological disciplines (M-DEA/01).
The characteristic historical, critical, and methodological courses are structured over three years according to degrees of progressive depth. Completing the students' educational profile are the acquisition of linguistic knowledge (English language, level B1) and computer skills (Applied Informatics), as well as the opportunity to undertake internships and traineeships at public and private institutions active in various sectors of cultural heritage. Students can rely on a series of agreements with various institutions operating not only in Siena and Tuscany but also across the national territory, established for this specific purpose by the University of Siena. Recent agreements will allow students to gain training experience at foreign museums within the Erasmus Placement project. It is the intention of the degree course to strengthen these agreements to encourage international student mobility.

Final exam characteristics The final exam completes the individual study course and consists of a written report (thesis) prepared individually by the student on a topic that deepens themes related to disciplines already taught in the study course. It is prepared under the supervision of a course instructor, possibly in collaboration with other instructors or experts. It aims to assess the student's acquired abilities and competencies, particularly their ability to apply them in analyzing a specific theme or issue and in independently developing an illustrative and interpretative reconstruction, accompanied by their own evaluation and judgment. During the public discussion of the report, the candidate is required to confirm their knowledge of the topic and in particular to demonstrate their independent communication and discussion skills regarding the analytical and interpretative results achieved.
The final grade, expressed out of 110, and any honors, is determined also taking into account the weighted average of the grades obtained in the exams taken. The minimum overall grade required to pass the final exam is 66/110. The Commission may award up to a maximum of 6 additional points based on the work and the outcome of the discussion. The final exam is worth 7 CFU.
Entry knowledge requirements To be admitted to the Degree Course, one must hold a secondary school diploma of the second level or another foreign qualification recognized as equivalent. The knowledge required for entry to the Degree Course in Political Sciences is as follows: 1) basic knowledge of contemporary history, including national, European, and international experience; 2) knowledge of the evolution of the Italian and European political-institutional system; 3) knowledge of English at least at A2 level; 4) basic knowledge of mathematics, computer science, and logic. The verification of the above-mentioned knowledge occurs according to the criteria described in Framework A3.b, and the modalities will be further specified in the teaching regulations of the Degree Course. Participation in the entrance test is mandatory for all first-year students of the L-36 curriculum, on the dates set each year by the Teaching Committee, and no later than the beginning of the second curriculum year, otherwise the academic career will be suspended until the next agreed test. Students who fail the verification will be assigned additional educational obligations (OFA) to be fulfilled in the first year of study through the recovery courses activated by the Department, or, for those who could not attend, by obtaining the material of these courses for an oral verification to be agreed with the instructor responsible for the training/recovery course. The Department has also activated a personalized tutoring system, assigning each instructor a specific number of enrolled students, and if requested individually by students, the result of the admission test is discussed with the tutor, who will provide appropriate guidance.
Participation in these tests is mandatory, but does not affect access or enrollment in the Degree Course. The modalities for conducting the verification test will be further specified in the teaching regulations of the Degree Course. Students who fail the verification will be assigned additional educational obligations to be fulfilled in the first year of study through the recovery courses organized by the Department of Jurisprudence; the acquired preparation will be verified after the recovery courses. In case of persistent gaps, additional readings will be recommended, and the student's entire educational path will be periodically monitored by the tutor instructors.

Degree title.
Bachelor's degree in Political Sciences Teaching delivery method Conventional Knowledge and understanding.
Generic Area Graduates acquire a versatile and multidisciplinary basic education, characterized by diverse but closely integrated knowledge in historical-political, economic, legal, political science, sociological, and linguistic fields. They are therefore able to understand and interpret the structural arrangements, change dynamics, and main phenomena of contemporary society, particularly:
- National, European, and international social and political-institutional transformations, contextualized within a historical perspective and the global context;
- Main issues related to political and socio-economic development processes in different territorial contexts, European and extra-European; principles, provisions, and applications of international law; dynamics of international relations and foreign policy;
- Legal, organizational, and management issues of public and private administration systems and operational procedures;
- Socio-economic development processes within the national territory, with particular attention to the third sector (cooperation and social utility).

Historical-Political Area Comparative study of contemporary political, social, and economic history and the context of the present time, with in-depth focus on political, economic, and social changes, political doctrines and institutions, governance and territory, and political, diplomatic, and legal issues related to international relations and foreign policy.

Economic Area Study of macro and microeconomics, determination of economic equilibrium, economic policy issues, behavior of the state and private operators in the economy; functioning of markets, third sector economy, knowledge of territorial policies and sustainable development; socio-economic phenomena geographical analysis; statistical surveys; demographic studies and demographic trends in developing countries; history of policies and socio-economic transformations.

Legal Area Study of fundamental principles of the Italian Constitution and sources of law; comparative methodology in constitutional law; administrative organization and activities; individual and collective labor relations; labor market regulation; tax law; fundamental elements of Italian private law; history of international and European law; origins, development, and content of international law and the international community; comprehensive system of international organization and European Union law.

Political Science Area Study of the nature of the state, political doctrines and philosophies; study of political regimes and transition processes, the Italian political system, and the party system in Italy and Europe; history, dynamics, and structures of European institutions; social research and methodology of political science.

Sociological Area Study of classical and contemporary sociological thought and criticism; social transformation and integration processes; transformation of societies; international development and cooperation; migration phenomena and multiculturalism.

Linguistic Area Written and oral knowledge of English and a second European Union language, chosen between French or Spanish.

Autonomy of judgment.
Graduates have the ability to apply their cultural background to the analysis of problems emerging in various professional fields, thanks to the habit of contextualizing events. They are able to carry out research activities on specific topics related to their field of study, organize and interpret collected documentation and data, and develop summaries demonstrating autonomy of judgment and a propensity for reflection from a multidisciplinary perspective. They are also able to formulate independent judgments regarding the functioning logic of Italian and foreign institutional and administrative apparatuses. These abilities are acquired and developed through participation in seminars and classroom discussions, preparation of reports, reading specialized publications, individual and guided study. The autonomy of judgment of students is verified by instructors during exams, seminars, final exam, and case or problem discussions by students with the instructor present.

Learning capacity.
Graduates demonstrate flexibility and aptitude for learning. The foundational training and study methods acquired enable them to access higher education paths with a high degree of autonomy: they possess the cultural and organizational capacity to integrate their competencies with content typical of higher education. They demonstrate the ability to consult databases and other available online information sources, as well as to manage such information using statistical tools and economic models.

Learning capacity is developed through individual and guided study, reading specialized publications, preparation of reports, and the final exam. Learning capacity is assessed by instructors throughout the educational process, particularly during the final exam.

Ability to apply knowledge and understanding.
Generic Area Graduates, thanks to the basic knowledge and skills acquired, are able to reach professional positions requiring analytical, organizational, and project capabilities. Their training in various curricular areas enables them to:
- Draft analyses of social, political, and economic realities according to a plurality of methodological and conceptual perspectives, to highlight criticalities and potentials.
- Collaborate in the realization of intervention projects with development and resource valorization objectives, addressing institutional, legal, and organizational dimensions.
- Interact with experts from different disciplines and work in teams in contexts (institutions, bodies, agencies, non-governmental organizations, associations, etc.) at national and international levels, as well as in public and private administration sectors.

Historical-Political Area Comparative study of contemporary political, social, and economic history and the context of the present time, with in-depth focus on political, economic, and social changes, doctrines and political institutions, governance and territory, and political, diplomatic, and legal issues related to international relations and foreign policy.

Economic Area Evaluation and analysis of economic policies, socio-economic phenomena, and statistical data related to the national and international market. Ability to support arguments and solve problems specifically within their field of study.

Legal Area Ability to present the Italian constitutional apparatus also through a comparative perspective; support arguments in the field of public law disciplines and evaluate national, international, and European legal specifics.

Political Science Area Ability to assess political regimes and their changes through scenario analysis, as well as the dynamics of Italian and European political theory and practice through a comparative approach.

Sociological Area Evaluation and ability to analyze social dynamics; scenario analysis through a plurality of perspectives.

Linguistic Area Possession of adequate mastery in linguistic disciplines and skills to support arguments and discussions in the languages learned.

Communication, public relations, and press officers The linguistic and multidisciplinary preparation offers the necessary competencies to interpret the complexity of phenomena typical of contemporary age, where it is decisive to distinguish the relationship and difference between legal, economic, sociological issues, to elaborate and interpret statistical data, to grasp the logic of a development increasingly supranational. Knowledge of two languages complements the methodological competencies necessary to operate in the knowledge society.

The in-depth study of at least two foreign languages (within the EU) ensures the ability to communicate internationally, maximizing the acquired knowledge.

They also participate, with responsible functions, in planning and organizing meetings and conferences, and following up on them.
Human resources management staff The professions examined evaluate individuals' abilities and inclinations, inform them about the structure and dynamics of the labor market and educational and training offers. They assist individuals in identifying the most suitable paths for personal, social, educational, and professional development. Additionally, they inform job seekers about available job opportunities; collect information on abilities, training, interests, and work experience; help formulate resumes and use available job search tools; propose candidates to employers; handle mandatory placement according to legal provisions. Therefore, they deal with all issues related to human resources management in the private and public sectors, starting from internal needs assessment, personnel selection processes, work organization analysis, conflict management, talent promotion, career planning, and training programs.
Communication, public relations, and press officers The professional figures included here are able to create information, distinguishing between descriptive and critical-interpretative levels, entering the communication world, both within print, television, or web media (after completing the necessary training internship), and within the internal and external communication of medium-large companies, associations, parties, or public institutions.
Information collection, management, and transfer staff Professional profile dealing with the acquisition, archiving, and management of information, both qualitative and quantitative. It is primarily engaged in reorganizing and packaging information according to client needs and requests; conducting surveys and sampling investigations through online, telephone, or face-to-face interviews. The professional profile is able to organize the information necessary for planning strategies of organization of public and private institutions of different nature and purpose. In the context where it operates, it performs a predominantly auxiliary role, supporting professions more involved in research and development, ensuring data quality and integrity, and the possibility of analyzing it.
Cooperation officers The development cooperation officer works on implementing projects in various sectors within aid and solidarity processes for developing countries (LDCs). Ability to design, coordinate, and manage humanitarian projects within the programming choices of international organizations and national institutions. In-depth knowledge in specific intervention areas: environmental protection, crime prevention, human rights protection, local entrepreneurship development, conflict prevention strategies, strategies supporting democratization processes.
Public service staff for issuing certifications and documentation They examine applications and verify conditions for granting licenses for business and commercial activities; examine applications and verify conditions for issuing passports, identity documents, and other personal certifications by public administration. The staff member must have the ability to organize and manage an electronic archive of documentation; to process administrative procedures related to application management, verifying requirement consistency; and to draft resolutions and administrative acts coordinating the different phases of the process.

http://www.unisi.it/dipartimenti/dipartimento-scienze-politiche-e-internazionali Specific educational objectives description.
The Bachelor's Degree aims to provide knowledge and methodological, cultural, and practical competencies in the areas of historical-political, economic, legal, political science, sociological, and linguistic learning. The project choice on which the course's teaching organization is based is aimed at managing the problems of contemporary society, in an interdisciplinary and comparative perspective.
Historical-political area: with particular reference to the study and in-depth of contemporary political, social, and economic history; history of territory, social doctrines, political institutions, and international relations (M-STO/04 and SPS/06)
Economic area: with particular reference to the study of political economy, economic policy, market functioning; geographical analysis of socio-economic phenomena, statistical surveys, and demographic studies (SECS P/01, SECS P/02, SECS P/03, SECS S/03, and SECS S/04).
Legal area: with particular reference to the study of constitutional law disciplines (also in a comparative perspective), private law, administrative, tax, and labor law, as well as international law and the overall system of international organization and EU law (IUS/01, IUS/07, IUS/08, IUS/10, IUS/12, IUS/13, IUS/18, IUS/19, and IUS/21).
Political science area: with particular reference to the study of philosophical and political theories, comparative analysis of political systems and parties, and the study of political science methodology (SPS/04).
Sociological area: with particular reference to the study of classical and contemporary sociological thought, including the study of foundations, assumptions, and implications from a philosophical perspective of social sciences, as well as analysis of social transformations and globalization dynamics (MFIL/02, SPS/01, and SPS/07).
Linguistic area: with particular reference to acquiring the ability to use English and another EU language proficiently, in written and oral form, to be found in the Department or University training offer (L-LIN/04, L-LIN/07, and L-LIN/12).
The training path includes acquiring fundamental knowledge for analyzing and interpreting issues related to international relations and foreign policy; knowledge of the international order and the European Union; basic knowledge of legal sources and the Italian and comparative institutional framework; knowledge related to political-institutional and economic-social history, with specific attention to both the Italian and European context and the extra-European context; political science knowledge on the organization of political systems, dynamics of democratic participation and representation, electoral observation, and public decision-making processes; sociological knowledge regarding the perception of social dynamics and collective action logic; acquisition of basic concepts of public administration sciences, national and international economic policy, analyzing constraints and opportunities arising from integration and globalization phenomena; analysis of cooperative economy and the third sector; analysis of global demographic developments and their geopolitical and geo-economic impact; written and oral knowledge of English and a second EU language. The training path is completed with English B1 proficiency, computer proficiency, and internship activities. The training path concludes with the final exam: elaboration and discussion of the thesis.
Graduates will be able to reach professional positions requiring analytical, organizational, and project skills; they will also be able to conduct research on specific topics related to their field of study, organize and process collected documentation and data, prepare syntheses or final documents based on in-depth analysis and reflection, and independent judgment in a multidisciplinary perspective. The graduate can access, with high-level functions, diplomatic structures, bodies, and international organizations, public administration offices, public and private national and international companies, consulting and cooperation companies, third-sector enterprises, and non-governmental organizations.
