Professional status conferred by the degree.
Educator in early childhood services The graduate in Education Sciences who has followed the "Educator in Early Childhood Services" curriculum can perform the role of educator and facilitator of development in early childhood services; in particular, can work as an educator in nurseries, micro-nurseries, early childhood centers, family nurseries, company nurseries; social-educational animator in early childhood services; educator in public and private services for families with children.
Social Educator The graduate in Education Sciences who has followed the "Social Educator" curriculum can perform the role of educator in non-profit sector associations, companies or re-educative communities; can carry out the professions of educator and technician in state and non-state recreational and cultural services, territorial services for individuals, social assistance, mediation and integration services, orientation and educational assistance services for people with disabilities.
Final exam characteristics To be admitted to the final exam, the student must have passed all exams and completed the training activities specified in the Study Plan. The final exam consists of writing and discussing a written thesis (possibly supplemented by visual or multimedia support) on a topic chosen from those relevant to the study path, possibly related to activities carried out during the internship, or work experiences or study abroad stays, etc., aimed at demonstrating the acquisition of specific knowledge, skills and abilities as well as the ability to critically reflect on them.
The exam, deepened by the student under the guidance of a faculty tutor, is discussed before a specifically appointed committee, which will evaluate the exam on a scale of 110 with possible distinction. The final grade will also take into account the student's academic record and participation in particularly formative activities.
Required knowledge for admission The student holding a secondary school diploma or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent (Article 6, paragraph 1 of D.M. 270/2004) may access the Bachelor's Degree in Education and Training Sciences.
Access to the Bachelor's Degree requires: basic preparation to approach the content of the disciplines to be studied, good analytical and synthetic skills for texts of medium complexity.
At the beginning of the academic year, the Entry Orientation Test will be held as provided by D.M. 270/2004. Seminars on university study methodologies and scientific writing will be organized.
If the Entry Orientation Test result is negative, the Bachelor's Degree establishes specific mandatory training obligations that each student must fulfill within the first year of the course.
The Department, in consultation with the University Language Center, ensures the assessment of English language knowledge (at least A2/2 level is required).
Awarded degree.
Bachelor's Degree in Education and Training Sciences Teaching delivery method Conventional Knowledge and understanding.
Generic Area The graduate in Education and Training Sciences:
- has acquired theoretical, epistemological and methodological knowledge related to the analysis of educational emergencies in their various manifestations, specificities and differences;
- knows the development, learning and social integration processes related to different life stages, also considering individual differences, gender, race, ability and culture;
- is able to read and interpret the educational and training needs of individuals, groups and communities present in educational, social and work contexts through the use of specific theoretical and methodological tools;
- is able to recognize the cultural, social and organizational specificity of the professional contexts in which they are called to operate;
- is able to adapt system interventions and actions in response to specific educational needs;
- is able to interpret relational dynamics and use group management techniques;
- knows the communication methodologies and main topics of the debate on educational technologies, digital artifact creation, and the use of Artificial Intelligence technologies in education;
- is able to relate their professionalism to contemporary scientific debate.
Pedagogical, sociological, psychological and historical-philosophical knowledge The graduate in Education and Training Sciences:
- knows the main pedagogical theories on education in early childhood, adult education and training in organizational contexts;
- knows sociological and psychological theories on individual, group and social learning processes;
- is able to analyze the main sociomaterial events in daily life and community contexts;
- is able to correctly frame the main social phenomena from a historical perspective and the evolution of philosophical and anthropological paradigms.
Connection with the labor market The graduate in Education and Training Sciences:
- has developed the necessary transversal skills to work independently or within organizations;
- knows the changes in the labor market;
- is able to anticipate future occupational scenarios for educational and training professions;
- knows the main types of educational services present in the local, regional and national territory;
- knows the importance and necessity of continuous specific professional updating.
Educational and training design The graduate in Education and Training Sciences:
- knows the theoretical models and methodologies of educational and training design;
- knows the individual and contextual issues that can generate an educational or training need;
- masters a repertoire of methodologies and tools for designing activities in educational and training contexts;
- is able to differentiate between the main educational and training design models in formal, informal and non-formal contexts;
- understands the need for careful monitoring of implemented activities;
- knows the main evaluation tools for the results and effects of designed and implemented educational and training activities.
Research and educational and training interventions The graduate in Education and Training Sciences:
- knows the emerging issues in socio-educational and training research;
- knows the main approaches to empirical research in education;
- possesses the basic knowledge to collect, analyze, validate and communicate data;
- knows the different logics of educational and training design;
- knows the main tools for evaluating educational research and can apply them to projects in specific contexts.

SECTION: AUTONOMY OF JUDGMENT

Autonomy of judgment.
The graduate in Education and Training Sciences:
- is able to critically analyze data and information collected through systematic observations and the use of specific research methodologies;
- is able to critically utilize pedagogical, psychological, sociological, and organizational literature (and other sources of scientific knowledge) to address professional situations;
- is able to use new technologies to expand their competencies and critically evaluate already acquired ones;
- is capable of applying appropriate methodologies to verify the efficiency and effectiveness of designed educational and/or training interventions;
- recognizes and values the different 'points of view' expressed by subjects involved in educational and training relationships and contexts;
- assumes an autonomous, critical, and reflective professional attitude.
Through the courses offered, it is considered that students acquire an autonomous perspective of judgment on educational and training issues. Furthermore, to strengthen this area, within the degree course, exercises are organized that aim to make students more active and participatory, and thus also more autonomous in their ability to evaluate and judge.
The indicated abilities will be verified through various assessment methods: a) oral or written exams with quantitative or qualitative structure; b) reports, papers, or documents created individually or collaboratively; c) case analyses; d) final internship reports.
Learning ability.
The graduate in Education and Training Sciences:
- is aware that continuous learning and self-learning are conditions for the development and qualification of their professional skills;
- possesses the tools that allow them to constantly expand and revise their professional knowledge (discriminating and selecting sources from which to draw theories, knowledge, and skills, navigating the broad research landscape and adopting interdisciplinary research perspectives);
- knows how to use experience as a source of knowledge and critically examine it;
- is capable of using personal experience to promote self-assessment actions oriented towards professional development.
The aim is to make students active subjects in learning processes. The acquisition of this ability is realized through the use of classrooms and multifunctional spaces of the Department. In spaces adjacent to classrooms, students are invited to independently and in groups (among peers) carry out projects and research that involve consulting various available documents and materials (printed and online bibliographic texts). Teachers are particularly encouraged to use these spaces to enhance participatory learning. Additionally, this ability is assessed through in-course assessments and the final exam.
Ability to apply knowledge and understanding.
Generic Area The graduate in Education and Training Sciences is able to:
- use basic operational skills in the fields of pedagogy and education sciences for analyzing social, cultural, and territorial realities;
- apply acquired knowledge to develop, implement, manage, and evaluate educational interventions and projects;
- use methodological-didactic competencies related to education and training fields to facilitate learning processes for individuals and groups from childhood to adulthood;
- organize educational and/or training environments according to the training needs of individuals;
- cooperate in defining training strategies in high-multiplicity social contexts;
- cooperate in planning and managing educational services in the territory;
- collaborate in implementing integrated systems for managing and valuing human resources and developing competencies.
Pedagogical, sociological, psychological, and historical-philosophical knowledge The graduate in Education and Training Sciences:
- is able to interpret pedagogical, psychological, and sociological dynamics connected to educational and training work;
- is able to develop interpretive frameworks for contemporary social phenomena;
- is able to apply general knowledge to analyze specific and personalized educational problems.
In particular, the graduate of the "Educator in Early Childhood Services" curriculum knows the main pedagogical, psychological, and sociological theories related to the development of children in early childhood, the specific reality and historical evolution of the main types of early childhood services at both national and local levels, and is able to differentiate service types and interventions for families. Applies differentiated methodological-didactic competencies within different types of early childhood services and the ability to design educational interventions for children, parents, educational staff, and operators.
The graduate of the "Social Educator" curriculum knows the main pedagogical, psychological, and sociological theories related to socioeducational contexts with particular reference to groups and communities, and the pedagogical, psychological, and social aspects concerning situations of disadvantage and marginality in different groups (disabled, elderly, adolescents, asylum seekers, adults and minors involved in the judicial system). Applies methodological-didactic knowledge to socioeducational support and assistance contexts and is able to develop interpretive frameworks for contemporary social phenomena. Masters the methodological coordinates of educational planning in services for individuals and groups in prison contexts, home education, and public and private socioeducational services.
Connection with the world of work The graduate in Education and Training Sciences:
- has developed complex transversal skills to successfully enter the world of work;
- is able to integrate their knowledge and understanding with transversal skills developed to analyze organizations;
- knows how to use networking strategies and tools;
- knows how to use teamwork and multiprofessional team working strategies.
In particular, the graduate of the "Educator in Early Childhood Services" curriculum is able to apply the competencies acquired during studies within early childhood educational services, school and extracurricular services, and services for families.
The graduate of the "Social Educator" curriculum is able to apply the competencies acquired during studies within educational services for personal and community development. It is also capable of envisioning occupational trajectories in prison contexts, educational communities, public administrations, and home education services.
Educational and training planning The graduate in Education and Training Sciences:
- is able to plan an analysis of educational and training needs;
- is able to use educational and training planning tools in a wide range of contexts;
- is able to prepare an educational and training project in various phases;
- is able to evaluate the effectiveness and outcomes of implemented educational and training processes.
In particular, the graduate of the "Educator in Early Childhood Services" curriculum knows the issues related to early childhood education and knows the theoretical models, methodologies, and tools of educational planning for the reference context. Plans educational pathways in relation to reference pedagogical models and uses acquired knowledge to build educational projects in continuity with early childhood services, territorial agencies, and families.
The graduate of the "Social Educator" curriculum is able to identify, document, and record situations of social disadvantage, marginality, and vulnerability, applies specific knowledge and methodologies in the design, planning, and evaluation of educational projects related to anti-racist, anti-sexist, and anti-ableist education, and the educational care of groups exposed to marginality. Uses techniques for evaluating educational projects.
Research and educational and training interventions The graduate in Education and Training Sciences:
- is able to translate a theory into an empirical research protocol in educational and training contexts;
- is able to position research and educational interventions within the organizational context in which they operate;
- is able to retrieve, prepare, and manage basic tools for conducting empirical research, particularly using a qualitative approach;
- is able to analyze and interpret data collected during the research process;
- is able to draft a research report.
In particular, the graduate of the "Educator in Early Childhood Services" curriculum conducts research and interventions by applying observation, data collection, and analysis tools and procedures in specific educational contexts for early childhood.
The graduate of the "Social Educator" curriculum conducts educational research and interventions for people with disabilities and in marginal situations, cultural and environmental education interventions, and community, social, and work inclusion interventions for people with disabilities or in situations of potential disadvantage.

Communication skills.
The graduate in Education and Training Sciences:
- can clearly and unambiguously convey useful information to individuals, groups, and organizations;
- can establish appropriate and effective relationships with subjects and services with which they interact;
- can communicate collected information to other professionals to improve organizational practices;
- can develop projects according to participatory logic and activate processes for sharing goals and strategies;
- can participate in discussions, conduct user interviews, and collaborate with the structures in which they operate, as well as with other professionals;
- can use discursive and conversational practices to stimulate and guide knowledge construction processes;
- can use multimedia technologies and distance learning systems for communication purposes.
The teachings provided, particularly in psychological and sociological fields, contribute to acquiring communication skills. Furthermore, to strengthen these skills, teachers are invited by the Teaching Committee to adopt teaching approaches where students are involved in classroom exercises and where public presentation of group work is required. Communication skills are finally assessed through the final exam presentation.
Planned occupational and professional outcomes for graduates.
Educator in early childhood services The graduate in Education and Training Sciences who has followed the "Educator in early childhood services" curriculum can perform the role of educator and facilitator of development in early childhood services; in particular, they can work as an educator in nurseries, micro-nurseries, early childhood centers, family nurseries, corporate nurseries; social-educational animator in early childhood services; educator in public and private services for families with children.
Social educator The graduate in Education and Training Sciences who has followed the "Social educator" curriculum can perform the role of educator in non-profit sector associations, companies, or re-educative communities; they can carry out the professions of educator and technician in state and non-state recreational and cultural services, territorial services for individuals, social assistance services, mediation and integration services, orientation and educational assistance services for people with disabilities.

Initial preparation assessment occurs through a mandatory but non-binding written test (aimed at verifying the student's basic preparation), to be taken before the start of the academic year, according to modalities defined by the Faculty. If the outcome of this test is negative, the degree course establishes specific educational obligations that each student must fulfill within the first year of the course. Role in work context.
Educator in early childhood services Recent surveys on the state of welfare in Italy and ongoing socio-economic and migratory global changes highlight the need for socio-educational professionals with increasingly broad and qualified competencies, also in the field of early childhood. To this end, the "Educator in early childhood services" curriculum aims to train professionals capable of accompanying children's development in a multicultural context and knowing, promoting, and valuing specific educational interventions aimed at the "full development" of their personalities, considering their social and cultural backgrounds.
The study path focuses on disciplines such as Pedagogy and Didactics, Special Pedagogy, Child Psychology, Management of educational services.
Social educator Recent surveys on the state of welfare in Italy and ongoing socio-economic and migratory global changes highlight the need for socio-educational professionals with increasingly broad and qualified competencies, also in the social sector and in mediation contexts with high multicultural density.
To this end, the "Social educator" curriculum aims to train specialized professionals in the elaboration, planning, and monitoring/evaluation of educational interventions in institutions and social environments aimed at promoting the person and managing complex personal and social situations (following migration flows, encounters with "other" cultures, etc.). For this purpose, in-depth cultural insights in Social Pedagogy, Pedagogy of Differences and Care, Family and Migration Sociology, and Intercultural Psychology will be provided.
Additional information.
https://scienze-educazione-formazione.unisi.it/
www.unisi.it Specific educational objectives description.
The Bachelor's degree course is structured into two curricula within which students can orient and specialize their cultural and professional training in two directions:
a) out-of-school services for early childhood, where they can exercise educational functions of first and second level aimed at supporting children's development, promoting the establishment of support networks for parenting, and integrating educational, health, and social services of the reference territory. Students will acquire basic knowledge to manage inclusion processes and phenomena related to changing living contexts from a technological and multicultural perspective;
b) social, socio-health, organizational, and associative contexts for young people, adults, and elderly. Students can exercise educational and training functions aimed at promoting autonomy and social integration of individuals, groups, or communities, as well as supporting processes of labor inclusion, management of cultural diversity, and prevention of radicalization processes. Graduates will acquire knowledge and competencies to work with subjects and groups expressing needs for social or professional development, integration, and reintegration, or guidance in rewriting personal growth trajectories.
The general objective of the Bachelor's degree in Education and Training Sciences is to train professionals who intend to carry out educational and training professions (early childhood educators, social educators, socio-cultural animators, trainers, adult educators, training activity tutors) in complex and rapidly changing contexts. Graduates, after acquiring disciplinary competencies primarily in the psycho-socio-pedagogical area, will develop, depending on the chosen curriculum, competencies in the field of educational and training planning, needs research and analysis, while mastering a wide repertoire of technical-operational tools necessary to identify and detect the presence of changing educational and training needs and to plan, implement, and evaluate interventions in these areas.
The learning areas characterizing the course are as follows:
1. Psycho-socio-pedagogical (M-PED/01, M-PED/02, M-PSI/01 and SPS/07) which allows students to know the historical evolution of educational institutions and educational and training systems and methods, and to learn elements of the sector's regulations and professional ethics;
2. Educational and training planning to use appropriate methodologies (e.g., media education, Fad, cooperative learning) in continuously changing educational contexts, manage projects/interventions in organizational contexts, and master methods and techniques for evaluating educational and training processes (M-PED/03, SPS/08).
3. Educational and training research and interventions to identify the nature, tasks, and organizational structure of educational services related to individuals, families, and social groups with specific needs, as well as to follow their evolving and complex developments (M-PSI/04);
4. Educational and social needs analysis (M-PSI/05) to interpret educational and training needs present in different contexts (families, educational institutions, assistance bodies, reception centers and/or gathering centers, children's communities and minors living in socially marginal situations, recreational and cultural animation structures, agencies and centers dealing with orientation, personnel selection and management, initial and continuous professional training).
The learning outcomes are achieved by students through participation in highly participatory lectures characterized by discussion moments, reflection, exchange of arguments, use of concepts and theories in reference to student projects and research projects, exercises, and seminar activities involving active participation, as well as through personal, guided, and autonomous study, lectures. These outcomes are verified through interviews, questionnaires, written and oral tests, as well as through critical text analysis, practical educational and training intervention planning, simulations, and reflections on completed or referenced experiences, etc.

Specialist or Master's Degree Courses University Master's Courses Admission requirements To be admitted to the degree course, it is necessary to hold a five-year Secondary School Diploma or another foreign qualification recognized as equivalent, as well as a four-year Secondary School Diploma with the corresponding supplementary year or, if no longer active, the assigned educational debt.
It is also necessary to possess the knowledge specified by the educational framework of the study course.
Professional status conferred by the degree.
Social Service Operator or, after passing the state exam, Social Assistant Social Assistants can work in both public and private sectors, with activities ranging from social assistant roles to more organizational and coordination tasks. In particular, employment can be found in Ministries, hospitals, ASLs, private clinics, family homes, prisons, reception centers, Juvenile Courts, addiction centers, as well as in research activities (thus Universities and research institutions).
Typical work areas are healthcare and hospital enterprises, Municipalities and their Consortia, the External Penitentiary Execution Office and the Juvenile Social Service Office of the Ministry of Justice, as well as all Entities and Institutions that utilize the expertise of the Social Assistant; additionally, Social Assistants are increasingly required by the non-profit sector (for example in social cooperatives) in managing Health and Social Care Residences, Day Centers, Family Homes, etc.
Final exam characteristics The degree is obtained after passing a final exam consisting of a written report, possibly in a foreign language, accompanied by the necessary bibliographic references, on topics previously agreed with the instructor responsible for one of the courses in the candidate's curriculum, and subsequently evaluated by a Committee composed according to current regulations.
Required knowledge for access Access to the Bachelor's Degree is permitted to all who hold a five-year Secondary School Diploma or another foreign qualification recognized as equivalent under current laws.
The required knowledge for access to the Social Service Sciences degree is as follows: 1) basic knowledge of contemporary history not limited to national and European experience, but extended to extra-European events; 2) knowledge of the evolution of the Italian and European political-institutional system; 3) knowledge of English at least at A2/2 level.
Regarding the assessment of the student's initial preparation, the Department of Social, Political and Cognitive Sciences organizes, concurrently with other Italian universities and using nationally shared methodologies, an entrance test, the outcome of which does not prevent enrollment in any of the activated study courses.
The test is structured in multiple-choice questions divided into four verification areas:
1. Italian language
2. English language (for those without a B1 level certification)
3. Elements of civic education
4. History of the 19th and 20th centuries Additionally, during the test, students' computer skills at ECDL core module basic level are assessed. Any additional educational obligations will be fulfilled through integrated training activities within the first year of the course.
Since the Department has long activated a personalized tutoring system assigning each instructor a specific number of enrolled students, the test result will be discussed with the tutor, also to plan an individualized training program aimed at addressing any identified gaps.
Degree awarded.
Bachelor's Degree in Social Service Sciences Teaching delivery method Conventional Knowledge and understanding.
Generic Area The graduate in Social Service Sciences must possess basic interdisciplinary knowledge to understand the individual in their social actions, as well as knowledge of institutions (local, national, and international) in their competencies and functions. For this purpose, the curriculum's course list is structured following a gradual criterion, from broad and general areas (sociology, anthropology, psychology, law, economics) to more specific areas (characteristic professional courses), up to specific disciplinary fields (such as migration sociology or criminal law).
Sociological and social history knowledge is aimed at interpreting social structure and macro phenomena, as well as the change events that have characterized contemporary society, in light of the most recent literature, both Italian and international. Knowledge of constitutional principles and administrative regulations, including European directives, enables understanding of laws and the organization of collective social life and public and private institutions. Knowledge of private law matters is fundamental to act not only for the protection of individual rights but particularly for family law and the protection of minors; it is equally important to know social security law in the context of the labor world. Psychological knowledge, both general and social, provides students with the ability to understand individuals and groups in their characteristics and dynamics, thus forming the basis for interacting not only with service users but also with colleagues and superiors. Other indispensable knowledge, to be further developed, relates particularly to social policies (local, regional, national, EU) and all professional methodologies and techniques. Finally, B1 level English knowledge represents a necessary overall mastery.
Due to the interdisciplinary and professional nature of the Bachelor's Degree, all types of activities contribute to the educational goals: frontal lectures, evenly distributed across two annual semesters and over the three years of the course, along with related exercises and thematic seminars for in-depth study, together with students' individual study of recommended texts. Assessment of results occurs, depending on the nature and total CFU of each course, both through intermediate written tests, usually conducted in the classroom, and especially through final written and oral exams.

Judgment Autonomy.
Judgment autonomy is transversal to academic training and professional practice. In training, it is mainly experienced through internships and interdisciplinary seminars; the social assistant graduate must demonstrate judgment autonomy in "case responsibility," as provided by Regional Law Tuscany No. 41/2005. Respecting professional conduct that values the self-determination of the citizen user of services, the graduate operator formulates their diagnostic evaluation within their area of competence, referring to the role held in the Institution or organization. Consequently, they make operational choices consistent with the problem assessment, and their operational project must account for respecting hierarchies (e.g., supervision of activities) and other functions, with interdisciplinary collaboration where required. For the social assistant graduate, implementing autonomous professionalism implies conscious and adequate use of resources and their promotion, in accordance with public administration frameworks and non-profit sector regulations. All this while respecting the profession's principles and values such as equity, appropriateness, and priority assessment.
For this objective, the teaching and verification annotations already made for previous descriptors apply, but the internship experience is emphasized as the preferred method, as it is essentially individual and often involves different institutions and territorial contexts. The internship requires the elaboration of a written work project plan discussed with the academic tutor and professional tutor, systematic verifications, production of administrative and professional documentation up to the final verification, conducted through the student's descriptive and evaluative report alongside the academic and professional tutor's evaluation.

Learning Abilities.
Regarding learning abilities, the graduate in this program must safely and immediately apply acquired knowledge and skills, demonstrating the ability to interact with a wide range of professional fields. The course also serves as an ideal stepping stone for further specialized professional learning experiences (e.g., master's degrees in administrative sciences or social services management, or first-level master's programs in the sector), but the foundational learning guaranteed by the three-year degree should naturally motivate the graduate to orient towards already specific study and work sectors. Indeed, a high number of graduates from this program immediately aim to pass the State exam and competitions or selections in the social services field.
For achieving this objective, the fundamental importance of internship experiences is emphasized, as well as the elaboration of the final thesis as an individual, autonomous, in-depth experience, often experimental in professional matters, with continuous evaluation by supervisors up to the final judgment by the graduation committee.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area The abilities and skills primarily concern technical-professional competencies, which must translate knowledge into action. In particular, the graduate operator must have the ability to develop a diagnostic framework for individual and group problems, conduct needs analysis for communities, and evaluate resources. A characteristic ability is organizing and managing structures and services, from simpler ones (such as home help or educational services) to more complex ones (like residential facilities for non-autonomous elderly, severe disability, or at-risk minors). Another applicable ability concerns implementing consulting and mediation interventions, using not only available resources but also innovative tools aimed at effectiveness and cost-efficiency.
Moreover, interdisciplinary work and collaboration with other social professionals is considered essential, from various medical specialists to psychologists, pedagogists, judges, lawyers (e.g., new forms of protection such as support administrators), up to all operators in the socio-health sector. The course's interdisciplinarity thus enables sharing of languages and codes essential for practicing as a social assistant.
Other indispensable abilities include using correct administrative procedures, including computerized registration and reading systems, as well as the ability to use information systems for service quality evaluation.
Regarding the ability to apply knowledge, particular relevance is placed on professional courses, which include role-playing simulations and problem-solving exercises or the presentation of videos of experiences to be discussed in groups. In such cases, verification is conducted through individual reports discussed during the exam, alongside the teaching program. Furthermore, interdisciplinary deepening on professionally relevant thematic areas with lectures by various experts is highly relevant for achieving practical competence.

Communication Skills.
Communication skills have already been highlighted as a characteristic ability of the professional profile of a graduate in Social Service Sciences, as this professional must carry out a social profession that is quintessentially "allocentric." The relational habitus concerns the use of knowledge and competencies to inform citizen users of services, interact and collaborate with colleagues, and relate in the management of interdisciplinary work for both diagnosis and intervention, expressing judgments and proposals with clear and competent language. This refers to the need to communicate in a bidirectional and even expanded interaction, in meetings or small specialist groups (e.g., evaluations and projects for non-self-sufficiency, disability, mental health).
For this objective, all didactic and verification notes made to previous descriptors apply; it is emphasized that the preferred didactic method for communication is the experience of group work, both as interaction between students and in the execution of relationships to be presented in class. Additionally, during the internship experience, individual supervision represents an excellent didactic method to foster communication and student professional growth, which is then verified in the various aspects of the final assessment (knowledge, skills, behaviors, ethics, etc.).
Expected occupational and professional outcomes for graduates.
Social Service Operator or, after passing the state exam, Social Assistant. Social Assistants can work in both the public and private sectors with activities that may range from social assistant functions to more organizational and coordination tasks. In particular, employment can be found in Ministries, hospitals, ASLs, private clinics, family homes, prisons, reception centers, Juvenile Courts, drug addiction centers, as well as in research activities (thus Universities and research bodies).
Typical work areas are healthcare companies and hospitals, municipalities and their consortia, the External Penitentiary Execution Office and the Juvenile Social Service Office of the Ministry of Justice, and all Entities and Institutions that rely on the professionalism of the Social Assistant; furthermore, Social Assistants are increasingly required by the non-profit sector (e.g., in social cooperatives) for managing Health and Social Care Residences, Day Centers, Family Homes, etc.
Official teaching and assessment language(s).
ITALIAN Associated competencies for the role.
Social Service Operator or, after passing the state exam, Social Assistant. After passing a state exam, a three-year graduate in Social Service Sciences may register with the Professional Register, category B, and thus practice the profession of Social Assistant. Registration with the Register also involves performing freelance activities. This professional figure must: possess basic and specialized knowledge in sociology, psychology, and law; hold competencies regarding social policies, health, and safety; understand service organization and analysis of social and cultural phenomena; be able to prevent and find solutions to situations of distress for individuals or groups; be capable of planning interventions; be able to organize and coordinate service structures; know at least one European Union language for professional updating.
Description of admission tests.
No admission test is required for the study program.
Professional function in work context.
Social Service Operator or, after passing the state exam, Social Assistant. The Bachelor's degree in Social Service Sciences is aimed at training graduates destined for the Social Assistant profession. The Social Assistant works closely with people or families in serious situations of distress and/or social vulnerability, carrying out also preventive activities. The categories that typically benefit from this professionalism are minors, the elderly, drug addicts, people with disabilities, and immigrants.
This figure performs not only socio-assistential tasks but also administrative and organizational tasks; specifically:
- Identifies and registers situations of marginalization based on reports from teachers, doctors, law enforcement, etc.;
- Contacts people in distress and analyzes their needs;
- Identifies the most suitable tools for the individual case and available locally;
- Creates a connection between local competent services and the subject;
- Reports cases requiring judicial intervention to the authorities (abandonment, abuse, etc.);
- Coordinates activities carried out by competent structures;
- Defines the paths to follow with people in need, developing them also within multidisciplinary teams.
Additionally, the Social Assistant performs advisory tasks at courts and collaborates with judicial authorities in matters of child custody and adoption, in social service placements as an alternative to prison sentences.
Additional information.
http://www.unisi.it/dipartimenti/dipartimento-scienze-sociali-politiche-e-cognitive
Description of specific educational objectives.
A distinctive objective of the course is the interdisciplinary training as a foundational culture, with integrated operational capacity. Reference is made to the professional figure of the Social Assistant outlined in national laws, Law 84 of March 23, 1993 "regulating the profession of Social Assistant and establishing the Professional Register," and particularly Law 328/2000, where professional social service is indicated, in minimum assistance levels, as a social secretariat and advisory function, that is, with functions of reception, analysis, and evaluation of problems and needs of individuals and groups, and subsequent planning of appropriate and effective interventions.
Furthermore, reference is made to the Ministry of Justice regulations, where professional figures are indispensable for "probation" functions regarding alternative penalties for adults, civil code reform, and laws on child custody and adoption. All these regulations are implemented primarily by Social Assistants of basic social services and Juvenile Courts.
Additionally, important reference points are Law 84/1993, which established the Professional Order of Social Assistants, and the Social Assistant's Code of Ethics, which defines appropriate professional attitudes and behaviors. Further references are the Tuscany Region laws No. 40 and 41 of 2005, which define a model for integrating social and health services.
In particular, the specific educational objectives of the Bachelor's degree in Social Service aim to create a professional profile capable of addressing new challenges faced by those working in the field of social services. The Bachelor's degree guides student training based on recent definitions of social policies and the most recent national and regional legislation. Through preventive actions, the Social Service graduate can work in favor of promoting citizenship rights, social cohesion and inclusion, and reducing and eliminating individual and family distress and need. Given the broad scope of tasks and the numerous work contexts characterizing the professional figure being developed, learning objectives are characterized by interdisciplinarity and methodological rigor. For this reason, the Bachelor's degree operates on two educational levels: 1. The first includes training activities related to the study of basic, characteristic, and related disciplines, indispensable for cultural and academic formation; 2. The second refers to the specific professional training necessary to practice the profession of Social Assistant.
The first level is oriented towards developing the following competencies: - a good interdisciplinary basic culture in sociological (SPS/07), anthropological (M-DEA/01), juridical-economic (IUS/09, IUS/17, IUS/07, IUS/01), psychological (M-PSI/05), and historical (M-STO/04) fields, suitable for understanding the characteristics of modern societies and participating in the construction of individual and social intervention projects; - adequate mastery of methodologies and techniques typical of social research (SPS/04); - adequate ability to evaluate and analyze social policies (SPS/04); - adequate knowledge of socio-health topics (MED/25; MED/42). The second level of training is oriented towards acquiring the following competencies: - knowledge of the principles and foundations of social service (SPS/07); - knowledge of methods and techniques of social service; knowledge of social service organization (SPS/07); - knowledge related to social and territorial planning (SPS/10); - basic knowledge of at least one European Union language, in addition to Italian (L-FIL-LET/12); - field experience under the guidance of Social Service professionals as supervisors in public and private entities where Professional Social Service is present.

Awarded degree.
Bachelor's degree in Chemical Sciences Teaching delivery method Conventional Knowledge and understanding.
GENERAL AREA Graduates in Chemical Sciences will have acquired the necessary principles for understanding basic chemistry. In particular, the foundations of inorganic chemistry, organic chemistry, physical chemistry, analytical chemistry, and elements of biological chemistry. These notions will be sufficient for understanding and contextualizing a chemical problem.
Additionally, students must be able to address, also in English, the reading of sector texts and articles. English language certification will be managed by the University Language Center (CLA) and will reach B2 level by the end of the study program.
Finally, students must be able to design and conduct a chemical experiment, taking into account current regulations regarding "Health and Safety at Work".
These knowledge and skills will be acquired through participation in lectures, guided personal study, and independent study, as provided by the activated training activities.
Verification of achieved knowledge and understanding will occur at the end of the relevant training activities, through written and/or oral exams.
CORE AREA PHYSICAL-MATHEMATICAL AND INFORMATICS Graduates in Chemical Sciences will have acquired:
- Solid theoretical knowledge of basic exact sciences, mathematics, and physics, which are prerequisites for teaching chemistry. In particular, for mathematics, graduates must know the tools of mathematical analysis and the basics of numerical calculation, and for physics, basic knowledge of classical mechanics and elements of electromagnetism.
- Theoretical and applied computer science knowledge; knowledge of logical foundations of programming, knowledge of a programming language, knowledge of operating systems and most common applications.
CORE AREA CHEMISTRY Graduates in Chemical Sciences will have acquired:
- In-depth theoretical knowledge of the main disciplinary fields of Chemistry: Analytical Chemistry, Physical Chemistry, General and Inorganic Chemistry, Organic Chemistry.
- Theoretical-practical skills in performing numerical exercises and laboratory activities in various scientific disciplines.
- Knowledge and ability to use methodologies for preparing and characterizing chemical systems and studying the relationship between structure and properties.
- Knowledge of scientific instrumentation for analytical and structural investigations of matter.
Regarding the last three points, in this study program, practical activities (laboratory) are considered highly important, as the ability to work in the laboratory, design an experiment, and coordinate an experiment with other operators are fundamental characteristics of graduates in Chemical Sciences.
CORE AREA BIOLOGICAL Graduates in Chemical Sciences will acquire basic knowledge of cell and molecular biology, with particular attention to the structure of bio-macromolecules: nucleic acids, proteins, polysaccharides.

Judgment autonomy.
The three-year graduate in Chemical Sciences will have acquired the ability to evaluate the quality and accuracy of laboratory results and will be able to critically interpret the experimental data obtained by developing a possible interpretative model. They will also be able to evaluate the safety, costs, yields, and, if applicable, the environmental impact of performing standard chemical reactions.
These judgment autonomy skills will be acquired through laboratory and exercise activities, which will be reinforced through direct interaction with the business world and professions through seminar activities, offering students many opportunities for constructive discussion.
The achievement of these objectives in judgment autonomy will be verified mainly through written and/or oral exams at the end of the training activity, and the discussion of the final thesis (experimental thesis).
Additionally, for some courses, students will be required to prepare written reports (scientific reports) and oral presentations, as individual or group work, to be discussed and defended in front of peers and the course instructor.
Learning capacity.
The three-year graduate in Chemical Sciences will be able to continue studies in a master's degree in chemistry or other related disciplines, having developed a good degree of autonomy and a solid, yet flexible, preparation in fundamental disciplines. In particular, the flexible content preparation will allow them to adapt to different work environments.
These learning capacities will be acquired mainly through laboratory exercises, individual study, and preparation of the final thesis.
The achievement of these objectives in learning capacities will be verified mainly through written and oral exams at the end of each course and laboratory exercises, which will allow instructors to assess individual study abilities and the approach to topics in an autonomous manner.
The thesis supervisor will also evaluate the learning capacities and research aptitude of the graduate during the preparation of the final thesis (experimental thesis).
Ability to apply knowledge and understanding.
GENERAL AREA Graduates in Chemical Sciences will have achieved the ability to apply information acquired during studies, or obtained from literature, to solve elementary or routine problems in the sector.
In particular, they will be able to:
- use online bibliographic research tools and access databases,
- ability to design and carry out chemical reactions and characterize products, under the safety conditions required in a chemical laboratory,
- ability to work with international scientific literature (in English).
The verification of the acquisition of these abilities will be carried out through the evaluation of the training activities activated during and at the end of the lessons, and through the preparation and discussion of the final project (experimental thesis).
BASIC PHYSICAL-MATHEMATICAL AND INFORMATICS AREA Graduates in Chemical Sciences will be able to apply knowledge acquired in physics, mathematics, and informatics to understand disciplines to be acquired subsequently in the training path.
They will also be able to apply knowledge acquired in informatics to design and use specific applications useful in the chemical field.
These results will be acquired through classroom exercises, individual study, laboratory activities, and group work experiences.
Verification of the results will be carried out through written and/or oral exams at the end of the respective training activities.
BASIC CHEMISTRY AREA Graduates in Chemical Sciences will be able to apply knowledge acquired in various chemical disciplines for the correct execution of their professional activities in different fields: industrial, environmental, university, and professional. They will be able to address and, where possible, solve independently the issues related to these fields.
In particular, within a laboratory, they will have the ability to operate and/or manage the chemical laboratory, demonstrating complete autonomy and aptitude to coordinate a work group. These results will be acquired through classroom exercises, individual study, laboratory activities, and group work experiences.
Verification of the results will be carried out through written and/or oral exams at the end of the respective training activities.
Three-year graduates in Chemical Sciences will also have opportunities for direct contact with the world of work, introducing an important interface in the 'exit orientation' process for new graduates. Knowledge and skills useful for entering the workforce will be provided through seminar activities organized with the collaboration of representatives from companies and, more generally, organizations representing the world of work (e.g., National Federation of the Order of Chemists and Physicists, sector associations, FederChimica, ...), and additional and complementary transversal skills (soft skills) will be acquired, in addition to technical and specialized knowledge.
These knowledge will be acquired through traditional teaching tools (monothematic frontal seminars) or webinars, guided group work by expert instructors, flipped classroom experiences, cooperative learning, and other innovative teaching methodologies.
The achievement of these objectives will be verified through interaction with students during the development of the teaching and training activity itself.
BASIC BIOLOGICAL AREA Three-year graduates in Chemical Sciences will be able to apply knowledge of biology and molecular biology, as an indispensable prerequisite for correctly understanding the functioning and regulation of vital processes. They will be able to apply knowledge of biochemistry, applied biochemistry, and molecular biology to understand and study the molecular mechanisms underlying drug action.
These results will be acquired through classroom exercises, individual study, and group work experiences.
Verification of the results will be carried out through written and/or oral exams at the end of the respective training activity.

Finally, the graduate in Chemical Sciences must be able to conduct study and research activities in collaboration.

Self-assessment test Role in work context.

- manage a chemical laboratory in accordance with safety regulations,
- communicate scientific information to specialists and non-specialists in the field;
- collaborate in the testing of new protocols and new technologies (synthesis, characterization, qualitative/quantitative analysis);
- hold organizational and process control roles under the guidance of a Senior Chemist.
Additional information.
https://scienze-chimiche.unisi.it Specific educational objectives description.
The Chemical Sciences Bachelor's Degree (L-27) has the main educational objective of training a graduate with solid basic skills and knowledge in the main areas of theoretical and experimental chemistry and in the prerequisite mathematical, physical, and computer science disciplines.
This objective aims to train a versatile and dynamic graduate, properly prepared both to continue studies in any second-level Chemistry degree course or related disciplines or in a first-level master's program, and to find employment in the public or private sector, in research and development, production, quality control, and commercial support fields.
More specifically, the Chemical Sciences Bachelor's Degree (L-27) aims to train graduates who have acquired:
- solid basic knowledge in the different disciplines characterizing Class L-27, both theoretically and experimentally;
- mastery of the scientific method of investigation in relation to applied problems;
- good knowledge of mathematical and computer tools, and physical disciplines, particularly those related to electromagnetism and optics;
- use of complex equipment in the chemical field,
- ability to apply innovative methods and techniques,
- technological competencies both theoretical and experimental, also of a multi- and interdisciplinary nature.
- adequate competencies and tools to communicate and manage information, synthesis procedures, characterization and analysis procedures, and experimental and theoretical data;
- good knowledge of the English language in oral and written form, within the specific competencies and for sharing technical-scientific information;
- ability to work both independently and in groups, both at the level of study and research investigation, and in a professional context;
- manual skills in chemical laboratory practice and use of common instrumental methods;
- ability to interpret and apply knowledge regarding the environmental impact of chemical practice and how to operate correctly in safety.
EDUCATIONAL PATH:
The educational path is structured in 180 CFU.
In the first year of the course, all teaching activities are in the basic area. Based on physical-mathematical and computer knowledge, in the scientific-disciplinary sectors (SSD) FIS/01 (experimental physics), MAT/05 (mathematical analysis), MAT/07 (mathematical physics) and INF/01 (computer science), which are prerequisites for chemistry teaching. Basic chemistry teaching is also provided in the SSD CHIM/01 (analytical chemistry) and CHIM/03 (general and inorganic chemistry).
In the second year and most of the third year, the study plan develops a balanced knowledge of fundamental chemical disciplines, with all teaching activities in the basic chemistry area, in the scientific-disciplinary sectors CHIM/01 (analytical chemistry), CHIM/02 (physical chemistry), CHIM/03 (general and inorganic chemistry) and CHIM/06 (organic chemistry). For each of these sectors, a significant amount of practical and laboratory activities organized in modules connected to the relevant theoretical lessons is provided. Basic competencies in biological chemistry (BIO/10, biochemistry) are also provided.
To complete the educational path, seminar activities are provided, useful for entering the job market, organized in collaboration with representatives of companies and, more generally, organizations representing the world of work (e.g., Chemists' and Physicists' Orders, sector associations, ...) and aimed at increasingly introducing graduates into the production and research and development world at the company level.
The main themes of the seminar activities will focus on regulatory aspects related to some production and analytical sectors, quality system management (validation of analytical methods, calculation of measurement uncertainty, accreditation of methods and protocols, ...). The seminar activities will also be directed towards acquiring transversal competencies (soft skills), additional and complementary to technical knowledge and the study of new interpretative models of production (e.g., Industry 4.0).
The educational path concludes in the third year with an activity dedicated to preparing an experimental thesis, with the aim of integrating the various disciplinary knowledge acquired throughout the course.

High School Diploma or equivalent qualification obtained abroad recognized as suitable Tuition and Fees For information on tuition and fees, visit the University website www.unisi.it/tasse Deadlines and Dates For information on deadlines and dates, visit the University website "Study Plan" www.unisi.it/didattica/immatricolazioni-e-iscrizioni/immatricolazioni Roles Responsibilities Mobility Coordinator for Students MARIA FROSINI Chair/Chair of Teaching Committee SANDRA DONNINI Program, texts, and objectives Admission Requirements Secondary school diploma or other foreign qualification recognized as suitable Final Exam Characteristics The final exam consists of the discussion of a written thesis prepared independently by the student under the guidance of a faculty member during the internship period, which can be carried out at the university or an external company. The final exam aims to verify that the graduate has acquired knowledge and understanding in the biological field, is able to process them individually, and apply such knowledge in a professional context.
The final exam consists of a concise presentation of the thesis and a discussion of its contents before a Degree Committee.
After the presentation and discussion of the thesis, the supervisor proposes a grade, up to a maximum of four points, based on the student's effort and preparation demonstrated during the internship, while the Degree Committee proposes a grade, up to a maximum of four points, regarding the student's written composition, oral presentation, and discussion skills.
The Degree Committee, based on the evaluations obtained throughout the educational path and the final exam score, expresses the candidate's evaluation in thirtieths, with possible Honors. The score achieved by each candidate will be made public at the graduation ceremony held two business days after the presentation and discussion of the thesis before the Degree Committee.
The final exam may be conducted in English upon request.
Required Knowledge for Admission The required knowledge for admission and their mandatory verification methods are defined in the Course Teaching Regulations, which also indicate any additional educational obligations if the verification of the required knowledge is not successful.
Awarded Degree
Bachelor's Degree in Biological Sciences Teaching Method Conventional Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area The graduate will have acquired, through the courses provided by the program, the ability to understand microbiology, animal and plant biology, and the ability to evaluate morphological-functional, cellular-molecular, and chemical-biochemical aspects of each organism. These abilities will include an evolutionary perspective of various kingdoms, general mechanisms of inheritance, and mechanisms of reproduction and development of various organisms. Graduates will also have acquired elements for evaluating ecological-environmental aspects of ecosystems and the ability to analyze various fields using elements of mathematics, physics, statistics, and informatics. Knowledge and understanding will be assessed through written and/or oral exams for each course.
Molecular-Cellular Learning Area The molecular-cellular learning area will provide further in-depth knowledge on molecular, functional, and cellular aspects underlying the functioning of living systems, genes, their expression, and alterations. These in-depth studies will also enable the acquisition of knowledge on new technologies useful for entering the workforce or as a basis for continuing the educational path in Master's Degrees in molecular/cellular fields.
Knowledge and understanding will be assessed through written and/or oral exams for each course.
Biological-Health Learning Area The biological-health learning area will provide further in-depth theoretical-practical knowledge on aspects related to human pathophysiology. Knowledge will be acquired on anatomy, general etiology, immunology, pharmacology, neuroscience, stem cell biology, as well as bioimaging and bioinformatics. Such knowledge will enable graduates to enter the workforce and provide a solid foundation for continuing the educational path in Master's Degrees in bio-health fields.
Knowledge and understanding will be assessed through written and/or oral exams for each course.
Biodiversity, Ecology, and Evolution Learning Area The biodiversity, ecology, and evolution learning area will provide further in-depth knowledge on aspects related to biodiversity, its evolution, and various adaptations. Specific knowledge will be acquired on various environmental ecological contexts and advanced techniques for analyzing them. Topics such as environmental botany, animal and plant diversity, biological evolution, wildlife management and conservation, and bioinformatics will be explored in depth. These in-depth studies will enable graduates to enter the workforce and provide a solid foundation for continuing the educational path in Master's Degrees in biodiversity, ecology, and evolution.
Knowledge and understanding will be assessed through written and/or oral exams for each Teaching Unit.

Judgment Autonomy.
Graduates will have the ability to independently analyze and interpret laboratory experimental data, critically evaluate results, and express reflections related to both scientific and social and ethical aspects. They will also be able to assess the parameters determining safety in workplaces, independently judge teaching methods, and express their opinions on principles of professional ethics and scientific approaches to bioethical issues. The achieved judgment autonomy will be assessed through specific written and/or oral tests for each Learning Unit, as well as in the final exam.

Learning Ability.
Graduates will be autonomous in consulting bibliographic material and databases to update their knowledge, even in preparation for further studies. The learning ability will be assessed through specific written and/or oral tests for each Learning Unit, as well as in the final exam.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area Through knowledge acquired in various disciplinary fields and individually re-elaborated, also through the use of advanced texts, graduates will be able to apply statistical, bioinformatic, biochemical, biomolecular, biotechnological, microbiological, and toxicological methodologies to the analysis of biodiversity, environmental and food quality and hygiene. Graduates will also be able to use biological and biomedical methodologies and broad-spectrum instrumentation for analysis and research in biological and biomedical fields. The ability to apply knowledge and understanding of the various Learning Units of the educational process will be assessed through written tests, scientific reports and/or oral presentations on laboratory activities carried out. The final moment of verification of this ability to apply knowledge and understanding by the student will be constituted by the final exam.

Molecular-Cellular Learning Area The knowledge acquired in this learning area will provide students with the ability to correctly apply various biomolecular and cellular methodologies in the analysis of complex biological systems. These capabilities will concern bioinformatic, biochemical, genetic-molecular, pharmacological, and cellular knowledge. Graduates will also be able to use broad-spectrum instrumentation for analysis and research in the biomolecular field. The ability to apply knowledge and understanding of the various courses will be assessed through scientific reports, written tests and/or oral presentations on laboratory activities carried out. The final moment of verification of this ability to apply knowledge and understanding by the student will be constituted by the final exam.

Biological-Health Learning Area Through knowledge acquired in various disciplinary fields, graduates will have the ability to apply methodologies and instrumentation in the fields of human anatomy, etiology and immunological processes, pharmacology, neuroscience, bioimaging, and bioinformatics. Such capabilities will primarily be directed towards the analysis of human health. The ability to apply knowledge and understanding of the various courses will be assessed through written tests, scientific reports, and/or oral presentations on laboratory activities carried out. The final moment of verification of this ability to apply knowledge and understanding by the student will be constituted by the final exam.

Biodiversity, Ecology and Evolution Learning Area Through knowledge acquired in this area and individually re-elaborated, also through the use of advanced texts, graduates will be able to apply statistical and bioinformatic methodologies, as well as detection, analysis, and monitoring techniques for biodiversity at the species, population, community, and ecosystem levels. They will be able to estimate levels of exploitation of wild species populations compatible with biodiversity conservation and the recovery of natural ecosystems.
The ability to apply knowledge and understanding of the various courses will be assessed through written tests, scientific reports, and/or oral presentations on laboratory activities carried out. The final moment of verification of this ability to apply knowledge and understanding by the student will be constituted by the final exam.

Communication skills.
Graduates will be able to communicate to specialists and non-specialists, orally and in writing, in Italian and English and with computer support, the acquired information and ideas and issues independently developed in various fields of biology, to work in groups both in theoretical and experimental fields, to process and present acquired data and to disseminate scientific information on current topics. The achieved communication skills will be assessed through specific written and/or oral tests for each teaching unit, as well as in the final exam.
Expected career and professional opportunities for graduates.
The course prepares for professions in life sciences such as biologists, zoologists, botanists, biochemists, microbiologists and similar.
The main expected career and professional opportunities for graduates of the course are professional and technical activities in:
1) biochemical, biosanitary, industrial, veterinary, food and biotechnology laboratories.
2) public and private research and service bodies where living organisms and their constituents are classified and used.
3) Environmental impact assessment, biodiversity studies and biological safety.
Official teaching and assessment language(s).
ITALIAN Associated competencies for the role.
The course prepares for professions in life sciences such as biologists, zoologists, botanists, biochemists, microbiologists and similar.
The competencies associated with the role of a three-year biologist are related to professional activities carried out in biochemical, agri-food, environmental, pharmaceutical industry research and quality control laboratories. Additionally, it may carry out professional activities in clinical analysis laboratories where the role of a three-year biologist is required.
Role in the work context.
The course prepares for professions in life sciences such as biologists, zoologists, botanists, biochemists, microbiologists and similar.
The main roles attributed to a three-year biologist are those involving the use of standardized methodologies, such as independently performing: a) analytical-instrumental procedures related to biological investigations; b) technical-analytical procedures in biotechnology, biomolecular, biomedical fields, also aimed at research activities; c) technical-analytical procedures and control in environmental and water, air, soil and food hygiene; d) technical-analytical procedures in chemical-physical, biochemical, microbiological, toxicological, pharmacological and genetic fields; e) quality control procedures.
Additional information.
http://www.unisi.it/dipartimenti/dipartimento-scienze-della-vita Specific educational objectives description.
The two main objectives of the study course are: 1) to provide a solid knowledge of various fields of Biology to enable access to all Master's degrees consistent with the indicated training path and 2) to ensure the possibility of accessing application fields related to the role of a biologist. To achieve this result, a single-branch - methodological-cultural training path has been adopted.
Training Path.
The achievement of educational objectives is carried out through the following teaching path aimed at providing a broad and in-depth basic preparation in various areas of Biology through an integrated multidisciplinary approach that particularly considers the evolution of knowledge at both functional and molecular levels. The path will allow the acquisition of 180 CFU as described in the table and is structured as follows:
1) Non-biological basic disciplines such as mathematics, computer science, physics and chemistry to understand the complexity of biology and master scientific methodologies and related techniques.
2) Basic and characteristic activities in the fields of botanical, cytological, zoological, ecological and microbiological disciplines to provide a solid knowledge of the animal, plant and microbial world, the functional morphology of the organisms that compose them, their evolution and interrelationships within the ecosystem, and knowledge of cellular systems, tissue formation and differentiation.
3) Basic and characteristic activities in the fields of biochemistry, molecular biology, genetics, physiology, bioinformatics and developmental biology to provide an integrated system of knowledge for understanding the cellular world at the molecular level.
4) Related and integrative activities indispensable for specific in-depth studies consistent with the objectives of the teaching path.
5) Related and integrative activities aimed at acquiring competencies in the field of safety, hygiene and quality control, indispensable for a modern biologist.
The training path is structured in lectures, classroom and/or laboratory exercises and seminar activities. At least 20 CFU in laboratory activities will be guaranteed in the main teaching areas. The training path includes 20 exams, one of which is reserved for student-selected activities.

High School Diploma University Fees and Contributions For information on university fees and contributions, visit the following page on the University website www.unisi.it/tasse Dates and Deadlines For information on dates and deadlines, visit the following page on the University website "Study Plan" www.unisi.it/didattica/immatricolazioni-e-iscrizioni/immatricolazioni Roles Responsibilities for Student Mobility LEONARDO DISPERATI President/Chair of Teaching Committee FEDERICO MARIA PULSELLI Program, Texts and Objectives Admission Requirements Secondary school diploma or other foreign qualification recognized as equivalent Characteristics of Final Exam The final exam consists of discussing a thesis related to an individual project. The discussion will take place in a public session before a committee of at least 5 professors, who will assign a final grade out of 110, possibly with honors. The conversion of grades obtained in various teaching activities (which result in grades out of 30) to a scale out of 110 will involve a weighted average based on the credits acquired.
The final assessment aims to verify whether the graduate has achieved the expected learning outcomes and whether the exam itself is consistent with the specific objectives of the degree program. The criteria for assigning the merit score consist of evaluating the student's previous academic record, mastery demonstrated in discussing the thesis topic, and the time taken to graduate.
For details on admission to the final exam and preparation of the thesis, refer to the Course of Study Teaching Regulations.
Required Knowledge for Access Basic scientific knowledge obtainable at secondary school level, certified by possession of a secondary school diploma or equivalent foreign qualification. Additionally, knowledge of English at least at level A2/2, as defined by the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages, is required. For students not possessing the required English skills, the University Language Center organizes recovery courses to be held preferably before the start of official courses.
In compliance with Article 6, paragraphs 1 and 2 of D.M. 270/04, students must possess adequate initial preparation. To this end, students must take an entrance knowledge assessment test to identify their level of preparation relative to the chosen degree program and encourage them to deepen their study subjects, ensuring performance aligned with a university curriculum. The test results will determine necessary adjustments and any additional requirements to be fulfilled during the first year of study. The test is normally held in October, before the start of lectures, and repeated in December/January. The verification and integration procedures will be supervised by the Unique Committee for Teaching of the Courses of Study in Environmental and Natural Sciences, as well as by the tutor professors.
The required knowledge for access to the Environmental and Natural Sciences Degree Program will be specified in the relevant Teaching Regulations, which will also indicate any additional mandatory training obligations if the verification is not positive.
Degree Awarded.
BACHELOR'S DEGREE IN ENVIRONMENTAL AND NATURAL SCIENCES Teaching Methodology Conventional Knowledge and Understanding.
General Area Knowledge of the fundamentals of Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Computer Science, and Statistics to acquire the basic languages of individual disciplines and the scientific method.
Understanding of the processes and mechanisms by which organisms and the physical landscape function, form, and interact.
Understanding of the interdisciplinary aspects of environmental and natural studies.
Knowledge and ability to recognize and classify biotic components (animals and plants) and abiotic components (minerals and rocks) of the landscape, and to analyze the ecosystem as a whole.
These knowledge areas are acquired through attendance at teaching courses, use of advanced textbooks, audiovisual and hypertextual materials. Individual study may also benefit from tutors. The quality and level of knowledge achieved will be verified through oral and/or written tests during the course and through the final exam for each teaching activity.
Scientific and Methodological Foundations This learning area, primarily located in the first year, includes basic knowledge in Mathematics, Environmental Statistics, Chemistry, Physics, and Computer Science, as these disciplines are essential for natural and environmental studies. The relevant courses are placed in the early years as they are considered preparatory for optimal academic progression.
Natural and Environmental Foundations This learning area, located between the first and second year, includes basic common knowledge for naturalists and environmentalists, particularly Biology, General Zoology, General Botany, Physiology, Ecology, and Geology. They provide general knowledge functional for adequate understanding of the content of natural and environmental ecological subjects.
Advanced Natural Studies This learning area includes both mandatory and elective courses aimed at acquiring knowledge for recognizing and classifying biotic components (Systematic Zoology of Vertebrates and Invertebrates, Systematic Botany, Mycology, Soil Biocenosis, Urban Biodiversity, Comparative Anatomy, Paleontology, Biogeography), interpreting the abiotic landscape (Mineralogy, Physical Geography, Identification, Ecology and Management of Habitats of Community Interest, etc.), and understanding the prehistoric environment (Deepening of Prehistoric Ecology and Anthropology).
Advanced Environmental Ecology This learning area includes both mandatory and elective courses aimed at acquiring knowledge for analyzing, monitoring, and sustainably managing the environment through the acquisition of chemical-analytical, chemical-physical, toxicological (Environmental Chemistry, Applied Ecology, Biological Effects of Pollutants, Pharmaceutical Botany), and ecological data (Nature Conservation, Ecodynamics, Identification and Management of Habitats of Community Interest, Community Ecology, Agroecology, and Marine Ecology), as well as through the study of possible utilization of production waste as secondary raw materials for medical, pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and food integration fields.
