Judgment Autonomy.
Judgment autonomy and decision-making capacity are not secondary aspects of applying the knowledge acquired by the student in relation to: evaluation, processing, and interpretation of experimental data, collected independently or within the context of internships and field activities, bioethics, and professional ethics. These can be concretized in:
- ability to evaluate the social and ethical implications in planning interventions on the environment and nature;
- ability to choose appropriate techniques for analyzing the components of the environment and nature;
- ability to frame one's scientific knowledge and technological skills within the historical development of key ideas in contemporary science.
Judgment autonomy is stimulated and encouraged, and possibly achieved, during the teaching and training process through the examination methods provided for each course, and in particular with some courses of the fourth area related to characteristic disciplines (Agricultural, chemical, physical, legal, economic, and contextual disciplines), which allow the acquisition of correct ethical behavior in one's professional field and the framing of one's knowledge within a historical-evolutionary context. The acquisition of such abilities and behaviors will be assessed both in the exams of these specific courses and in the preparation and discussion of the final thesis.
Learning Ability.
The ability to learn involves a phase of development and deepening in relation to the continuous updating of knowledge through consultation of bibliographic material, internet research, comparison and verification of sources, use of databases, etc. Therefore, knowledge of scientific update tools for the disciplines of the sector and the ability to access scientific literature produced in at least one other European language, besides one's own, will be essential.
This objective is developed in the work of the final exam, in the preparation of reports from various laboratories (including interdisciplinary ones) and internship activities, and in consulting scientific bibliography also in English.
The verification of these competencies is consequently carried out during the final exam, as well as in the work related to the preparation of the final thesis carried out under the guidance of a tutor professor.
Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area Multidisciplinary Competences and ability to identify and recognize the value of natural heritage through the description of biodiversity (intraspecific, specific, and ecosystem), environmental monitoring, understanding of the physical component and its modification processes, also in order to acquire a better understanding of the impact of climate change on animal, plant, and ecosystem biodiversity. Ability to contribute and collaborate in territorial planning and sustainable development projects. Application of methodological procedures to verify the quality of easily accessible plant-based products (phytotherapeutic or dietary supplements) on the market. Ability to design, implement, and coordinate environmental education projects and museum activities. Acquisition of experimental skills in the field and in the laboratory, including the computer laboratory. Problem-solving ability. Ability to plan experimental protocols and procedures, apply them, and draft reports on them. Such competencies are acquired in the courses of the characteristic areas with their respective laboratories and excursions, and specific internship activities, which are integral parts of the training path, and in particular interdisciplinary ones. These activities constitute at least 33 cfu, excluding the 9 cfu dedicated to internship and/or training.
Verification is carried out through reports or in-course tests, written or oral, and with the final profit exam provided for each course, but also during the preparation of the final thesis.
Scientific and Methodological Foundations Application of mathematical methods to model and analyze naturalistic and environmental issues.
Interpretation of physical and chemical phenomena and utilization of the laws governing them within the Natural and Environmental Sciences Natural and Environmental Foundations Recognition of prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.
Recognition of the most common mega and mesostructures of the Earth's crust and the main magmatic, sedimentary, and metamorphic rock types. Description of primary and secondary structures of roots, stems, and leaves of plants.
Recognition of the main groups of terrestrial and marine invertebrates.
Recognition of ecosystems and the most common ecological phenomena and cycles. Deepening of Natural Sciences Such foundations form the natural science competence of the graduate, who is able to read and interpret the present and past biotic and abiotic landscape, as well as to evaluate, using animal and plant species as bioindicators, the health status and/or conservation value of habitats and ecosystems.
Deepening of Environmental Ecology Such foundations constitute the environmental ecology competence of the graduate, who will be able to analyze and monitor marine and terrestrial ecosystems from an ecological, toxicological, and chemical perspective for their sustainable management.

Planned occupational and professional opportunities for graduates.
University-level technician for the study of the environment and nature. As professional opportunities, in the public sector, environmental management and service companies, Ministries (Environment and Territorial Protection, Agriculture and Forestry, Health, Cultural Heritage and Activities, Infrastructure and Transport, Education, University and Research), and national and international bodies (Experimental Institute for Environmental Prevention and Research - ISPRA, ARPA, all its Regional Agencies, the Land Transport and Infrastructure Agency, and the ISS - National Institute of Health) require graduates with professional skills in the analysis, monitoring, protection, valorization, and conservation of environmental and cultural assets (e.g., protected areas, archaeological sites, prehistoric, protohistoric, and historical sites and materials).
Additionally, graduates' skills may support Regional, Provincial, Municipal, Mountain Communities, and other Public Bodies in collecting, organizing, and disseminating environmental and natural data.
Skills also enable employment opportunities in the scientific research sector at institutions such as the University, CNR - National Research Council, ENEA - National Agency for New Technologies, Energy, and Environment, ENEL - National Electricity Agency, and CCR - Joint Research Centre.
In the private sector, graduates in Environmental and Natural Sciences may find employment in companies producing goods and services, with tasks of data analysis and collection for all issues involving interaction between production activities and environmental systems.

Additional information.
http://www.unisi.it/dipartimenti/dipartimento-scienze-fisiche-della-terra-e-dell%E2%80%99ambiente Specific educational objectives description.
The specific educational objectives of the University of Siena's Environmental and Natural Sciences degree program are defined as follows:
1) Acquire both cultural and professional knowledge and skills to perform:
- Environmental analysis and monitoring, achieved through the acquisition of abiotic and biotic parameters, such as the detection and description of geosites, censuses of faunal and floral heritage (biomonitoring), and subsequent processing using methodologies based on floristic and faunistic indicators, synthetic indices, and thematic mapping;
- Organization and execution of projects for the conservation and management of biotic (animals and plants) and abiotic components of landscapes and natural and anthropized habitats;
- Analysis and monitoring of chemical-analytical, chemical-physical, toxicological, and ecological data;
- Analysis of prehistoric environments with in-depth ecology and anthropology;
- Analysis and simulation aimed at managing local operational activities related to pollution control and environmental restoration;
- Programs for the rational use of natural resources from a sustainability perspective, based on acquired protocols.
2) Acquire a body of knowledge enabling one to provide, as a first-level expert, education, dissemination, and communication of natural and environmental topics in pre-university schools, information centers in protected areas, and structures offering tourism related to the territory.
3) Obtain a solid naturalist/environmental culture allowing continuation of the educational path through various types of second-level (master's and specialized degrees, etc.) and third-level (PhD, etc.) qualifications.
The educational path enabling the acquisition of knowledge, skills, and competencies to achieve the specific educational objectives of the study program is briefly as follows:
- Foundational knowledge in mathematics, environmental statistics, computer science, chemistry, and physics, and at least one foreign language;
- Knowledge, both aimed at acquiring professional methodologies and cultural, of the fundamentals of biology (biology, zoology, botany, physiology), chemistry (general chemistry, organic chemistry), Earth sciences (geology and mineralogy), and ecology and their phenomenology;
- Ability to recognize and classify biotic components (animals and plants) and read abiotic landscapes (systematic zoology, botany, physical geography);
- Ability to perform environmental analysis and monitoring through the acquisition of chemical-analytical, chemical-physical, toxicological, ecological data, and simulation (geochemistry, environmental chemistry, applied ecology);
- Correct behaviors, particularly regarding sensitivity to environmental issues, as well as environmental safety and professional ethics.
The study path is integrated and personalized by the student, who has access to a wide range of courses in related or complementary subjects to choose from for a total of 18 CFU and elective courses for a total of 12 CFU.

Final exam characteristics The final exam for the Bachelor's Degree in Midwifery, worth 5 CFU, has the value of a State exam enabling the exercise of the profession (D.Lgs 502/1992, art. 6, comma 3), and consists of:
a) a practical exam during which the student must demonstrate having acquired the theoretical-practical and technical-operative knowledge and skills specific to the professional profile (discussion of a clinical case, evaluation of an ultrasound tracing, demonstration of surgical instrument use, obstetric maneuvers on a manikin);
b) preparation and defense of a thesis.
The grade is expressed on a scale of 110, with possible honors Required knowledge for admission Students possessing a High School Diploma or another foreign qualification recognized as equivalent may be admitted to the Bachelor's Degree in Midwifery.
Among the mandatory knowledge for the course, English language knowledge at least at A2/2 level (CEFR), as defined by the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages, is required.
Information regarding linguistic qualifications is available on the University Language Center-CLA website https://www.cla.unisi.it/it For other basic knowledge (biology, chemistry, mathematics, and physics at high school level), refer to the course's didactic regulations.
The Bachelor's Degree provides the Syllabus of Minimum Knowledge, drafted in agreement between the biology, chemistry, mathematics, and physics teachers of the University's scientific faculties and some teachers of these subjects from the high schools in the University of Siena's territorial area, to define the essential minimum knowledge required for admission to scientific faculties and therefore valid for the Midwifery Degree Course.
The didactic organization of the Midwifery Degree Course requires that students admitted to the first year possess adequate initial preparation, achieved through previous studies. The student's initial preparation is assessed through the administration of an entrance quiz, common to all health area Degree Courses of the Medical Departments, consisting of multiple-choice questions on logic, chemistry, biology, physics-mathematics.
Any gaps in initial preparation that determine additional educational obligations must be remedied within the first year of the course Degree awarded.
BACHELOR'S DEGREE IN MIDWIFERY Teaching method Conventional Knowledge and understanding.
Area Biomedical Sciences Graduates in Midwifery who have successfully completed the course must have acquired the following knowledge and understanding abilities:
1. Qualitative and quantitative foundations of biological and pathophysiological phenomena;
2. Fundamental principles of human anatomy and essential elements of histology with particular reference to the female genital apparatus;
Such knowledge and understanding abilities will be acquired through the training activities provided in the study plan, which include not only curricular courses but also seminars and didactic laboratories. Student preparation will be verified through the respective passing exams in the different areas.
Area Obstetric-Gynecological and Neonatal Sciences Graduates in Midwifery who have successfully completed the course must have acquired the following knowledge and understanding abilities:
1. Ability to understand the conceptual and theoretical principles of gynecology and the obstetric discipline in general, and in particular in relation to the birth process.
2. Ability to understand the conceptual and theoretical principles of the obstetric-gynecological discipline and to use the technical-practical methods to evaluate obstetric care in general;
3. Ability to understand the conceptual and theoretical principles of the obstetric discipline and to use the technical-practical methods to evaluate neonatal care.
Such knowledge and understanding abilities will be acquired through curricular courses, clinical seminars, and didactic laboratories. Student preparation will be verified through the respective passing exams in the different areas.
Area Hygienic-Preventive Sciences Graduates in Midwifery who have successfully completed the course must have acquired the following knowledge and understanding abilities:
1. Knowledge of the fundamental principles of hygiene and preventive medicine essential for correctly interpreting the hygiene and prophylaxis norms related to the midwife's activities;
2. Knowledge of the fundamental principles of hygiene and preventive medicine essential for evaluating the risk factors related to the midwife's activities;
Area Ethical, Legal, and Organizational Sciences Graduates in Midwifery who have successfully completed the course must have acquired the following knowledge and understanding abilities:
1. Knowledge and compliance with bioethics regulations, professional deontology, and legal and medical-legal principles.
2. Ability to understand and apply the conceptual and theoretical principles of the obstetric-gynecological discipline to plan, organize, and evaluate general obstetric care;
General Area Graduates in Midwifery who have successfully completed the course must have acquired the following knowledge and understanding abilities:
1. Ability to understand the various phases of physiological pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum;
2. Ability to understand potential complications related to the previous aspects;
3. Knowledge of appropriate psychological approaches according to the cultural and economic level, nationality of origin, and religious beliefs of the woman being assisted Judgment autonomy.
The Midwifery graduate, thanks to the theoretical and practical knowledge acquired during the course, must be able to assume responsibility for their professional practice.
The Midwifery graduate must be able to recognize the main reactions and responses of the woman to pregnancy, illness, suffering, hospitalization, vaginal birth, and cesarean section, respecting behavioral differences related to cultural belonging.
The Midwifery graduate must be able to assess the physiological progression of pregnancy, childbirth, postpartum, and breastfeeding. They must also assess situations of pathology and emergency-urgency in the woman (during pregnancy, childbirth, and postpartum) and the newborn requiring medical intervention.
The Midwifery graduate must also be able to evaluate the clinical, psychological, and socio-cultural manifestations related to the progression of pregnancy and the main diseases associated with it, treatment, monitoring of pregnancy, reactions to illness, and postpartum, hospitalization, and assistance interventions.
The acquisition of judgment autonomy regarding the various circumstances the Midwifery graduate will face will result from the degree of scientific knowledge and cultural level acquired during the didactic activities (frontal lessons, internship, and clinical case discussions) and will be verified through the passing of exams (grade expressed in thirtieths for frontal lessons and the second semester internship) or suitability (only for the first trimester internship).
Learning ability.
The Midwifery graduate must be able to independently organize their continuous professional development, according to correct meta-cognitive strategies, conducting bibliographic research on major biomedical databases and critically reading scientific articles. Finally, the graduate will constantly rely on teachers for guidance in selecting criteria for the scientificity of the main "learning facilities."
The Midwifery graduate must plan, organize, and develop their professional work in response to the continuous changes in knowledge and the health and social needs of women.
The learning ability of the Midwifery graduate will be acquired during the three-year study period through their participation in frontal lessons and verified through the passing of the exam held at the end of each course (grade expressed in thirtieths).
Ability to apply knowledge and understanding.
Area Biomedical Sciences Graduates in Midwifery who have successfully completed the course must:
1. Use the basic knowledge acquired as a foundation for the more specific training of their profession and apply it to interpret clinical issues based on the topics addressed during the course, essential for the practice of midwifery.
These competencies will be acquired using scientific texts as study material and proposing practical exercises in class and during exams. Particular emphasis will be placed on verifying these competencies during the final exam.
Area Obstetric-Gynecological and Neonatal Sciences Graduates in Midwifery who have successfully completed the course must:
1. Use the acquired obstetric-gynecological knowledge to identify the needs of women in various stages of reproductive life;
2. Be able to use the most appropriate theoretical-practical approaches to address the physiological progression of pregnancy, childbirth, postpartum, and breastfeeding;
3. Correctly and critically apply diagnostic-therapeutic prescriptions.
Such knowledge and understanding abilities will be acquired through the training activities provided in the study plan, which include not only curricular courses but also seminars and didactic laboratories. Student preparation will be verified through the respective passing exams in the different areas.
Area Hygienic-Preventive Sciences Graduates in Midwifery who have successfully completed the course must:
1. Apply appropriate prevention strategies to promote and support the health of women, pregnant women, parturient women, postpartum women, and newborns;
2. Apply hygiene norms for newborn care and for the prophylaxis of risk factors and neonatal diseases;
3. Perform interventions aimed at promoting safety in the work environment benefiting both healthcare workers and users.
Area Ethical, Legal, and Organizational Sciences Graduates in Midwifery who have successfully completed the course must:
1. Adapt their conduct during professional practice to the profile and code of ethics;
2. Apply the conceptual and theoretical principles of the obstetric-gynecological discipline and use the technical-practical methods acquired during the course to plan, organize, implement, and evaluate general obstetric care within the specific areas of professional competence of the midwife;
Such knowledge and understanding abilities will be acquired through the training activities provided in the study plan, which include not only curricular courses but also seminars. Student preparation will be verified through the respective passing exams in the different areas.
General Area Graduates in Midwifery who have successfully completed the course must:
1. Be able to use the acquired theoretical knowledge to address both physiological and pathologically complicated pregnancy;
2. Be able to analyze and recognize the psychological needs of the woman during pregnancy.

Communication skills.
Graduates in Midwifery must be able to establish and maintain helping relationships with the assisted woman and intervene in the educational process of new families, applying the fundamentals of relational dynamics aimed at promoting appropriate coping methods and developing assistance skills. A Midwife graduate must also be able to plan and implement health education interventions for healthy women and groups, as well as therapeutic education interventions aimed at self-management of illness, treatment, and rehabilitation. Communication skills will be acquired primarily during internship activities, which become increasingly demanding and carry greater weight as the study course progresses: following the ward's daily life and having daily contact with patients will allow the Midwife graduate to develop the ability to engage in constructive dialogue with pregnant women. This will also enable them to develop a trusting relationship with the patient and represent a reference point to which the woman can turn to express and be reassured about the issues that arise. The acquisition of these skills will be verified daily by ward staff and through passing the exam (or qualification) held at the end of each internship.
Planned occupational and professional outcomes for graduates.
Midwife For occupational outcomes, we refer to the "economic activity classifications Ateco 2007" indicated by the following titles: institutions, university hospitals and polyclinics; National Health Service outpatient clinics and polyclinics; other specialist medical offices and polyclinics; other independent paramedical activities; university and post-university education; training courses and professional update courses.
Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIAN Associated competencies for the role.
Midwife Graduates in Midwifery perform their professional activities in healthcare facilities, public or private, in dependent or self-employed status.
Description of admission tests.
The number of students admitted to the degree program is planned annually based on regional needs.
The entrance test is common to all healthcare degree programs and is conducted on the same day at all Italian universities.
The test consists of a multiple-choice quiz on the following subjects: general culture, logical reasoning, mathematics, physics, chemistry, and biology.
Ranking is based on merit Work context function.
Midwife The Midwife is a qualified professional who intervenes in the care of women during pregnancy, childbirth, and the postpartum period, conducts and completes normal births with personal responsibility, and provides care to the newborn. The Midwife, within their competence, participates in:
a. health and sexual education interventions both within the family and in the community;
b. psychological preparation for childbirth;
c. preparation and assistance for gynecological interventions;
d. prevention and detection of tumors in the female genital area;
e. maternal and neonatal care programs.
The Midwife manages, respecting professional ethics, as a member of the healthcare team, the assistance interventions within their competence.
The Midwife contributes to the training of support staff and directly participates in updating related to their professional profile and research.
The Midwife is able to identify potentially pathological situations requiring medical intervention and to carry out, if necessary, appropriate emergency measures.
Additional information.
http://www.unisi.it/dipartimenti/dipartimento-medicina-molecolare-e-dello-sviluppo Specific educational objectives description.
The Midwifery degree program aims to:
- Develop knowledge of the pathophysiological processes of pregnancy evolution, utilizing clinical and instrumental diagnostic methods and tools.
- Provide adequate knowledge to perform assistance functions for pregnant women and the fetus, and for the couple throughout the birth process.
- Develop competencies to assist women during physiological childbirth, acquire the ability to promptly identify maternal and fetal clinical situations requiring operative or cesarean delivery, and prepare the operating room for cesarean section.
- Develop competencies to perform functions specified by ethical-deontological and medical-legal regulations and evaluate their compliance in gynecological-obstetric-neonatal settings.
The training path focuses on courses related to the following thematic areas:
1. Biomedical Sciences, which include courses in disciplines relevant for acquiring basic knowledge for the specific professional profile.
2. Obstetric-Gynecological and Neonatal Sciences, which include courses of more specific disciplines for the Midwifery degree program.
3. Hygienic-Preventive Sciences, which include courses in essential subjects for understanding risk factors and prevention strategies related to obstetric assistance activities.
4. Ethical, Legal, and Organizational Sciences, which include courses aimed at forming professionals aware of the essential principles of professional deontology and experts in the main regulations governing activities in the obstetric field.
Students receive specific training in healthcare management through courses offered in related and integrated activities.
Students must also consolidate their computer knowledge for managing clinical data related to obstetric activities and organizing specific healthcare activities. During the study course, students are required to attend a targeted English course (Medical English) aimed at understanding scientific literature, improving interactions with foreign users, and collaborating with professionals operating in the obstetric field at European and international levels.

Professional status conferred by the degree.
Orthoptists and ophthalmic assistants find placement within the National and Regional Health Service (see National Health Service Agreement), and can independently exercise activities as defined by the Professional Profile (14/09/1994 no. 743) in various fields: in orthoptic centers and Hospital Departments; in accredited University facilities and private practices; in Child Neuropsychiatry, Rehabilitation, and Pediatric Departments; in Legal Medicine and Occupational Health services; in schools and low-vision centers.
They work in collaboration with doctors and other health professionals, personally responsible for planning and quality of professional activities. The generational turnover requires necessary staff renewal and expansion within the orthoptic personnel dependent on the National Health Service. Increased incidence of central vascular accidents; increased degenerative retinal phenomena related to aging; road and work injuries; increased congenital refractive defects requiring good visual function, determine a forecast of growth for the Orthoptist role. Final exam characteristics The final exam has the value of a state licensing exam for professional practice (D.Lgs 502/1992, art. 6, comma 3) and consists of:
a) a practical test during which the student must demonstrate acquisition of theoretical, practical, and technical skills specific to the professional profile;
b) preparation and defense of a thesis. See DM 19 February 2009, art.7
The final exam will be awarded 5 CFU.
The final exam cannot be repeated more than once.
Criteria for awarding merit score will include: evaluation of abilities demonstrated during the presentation and discussion of the thesis; judgment on technical skills demonstrated during the practical test.
The final score is expressed on a scale of 110.
If a total score of 110/110 is achieved, the chair of the final exam committee will put the award of honors to a vote, which can only be granted unanimously.
Required knowledge for access Students holding a High School Diploma or an equivalent foreign qualification may be admitted. Required knowledge will include: general culture and logical reasoning, mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology. Additionally, English language knowledge at least at A2/2 level (CEFR) is required.
Degree awarded.
DEGREE IN ORTHOPTICS AND OPHTHALMOLOGIC ASSISTANCE Teaching delivery method Conventional Knowledge and understanding.
Generic Area At the end of the training path, graduates in Orthoptics and Ophthalmic Assistance will have acquired a wide range of knowledge, both in basic sciences and in characteristic disciplines, as well as in communication and professional management.
In particular, they must achieve solid cultural and scientific foundations in the fields of:
- Preliminary, basic, biomedical and psychological sciences, for understanding biological phenomena, mechanisms of ocular apparatus functioning, motor and psychomotor development, physiological phenomena, also in correlation with psychological, social, and environmental dimensions of disease.
- Orthoptic sciences, necessary to identify preventive and rehabilitative needs of the subject through evaluation of clinical data in ophthalmological, orthoptic, psychomotor, cognitive, and functional fields, for the extent and significance of symptoms.
- Understand the constituents underlying pathological processes focused on by rehabilitation and/or therapeutic intervention, in pediatric, adult, or geriatric age.
- Develop the best therapeutic, technical, and methodological approaches for resolving patient health issues.
- Design and verify orthoptic interventions using objective evaluation and effective therapeutic methods, and all appropriate diagnostic tools for case resolution, proposing possible therapeutic treatments such as occlusion, use of conventional or prismatic lenses and/or low-vision aids, also in relation to ophthalmologist's indications and prescriptions.
- Interdisciplinary and surgical-medical sciences for understanding pathophysiological elements applicable to different clinical situations, also in relation to diagnostic parameters.
- Prevention Sciences and Health Services sciences, to acquire the ability to analyze health problems of individuals and/or communities and the responses of health and social services to citizens' main needs.
- Statistical Sciences, quantitative methods, and scientific updating, for developing knowledge of statistical tools useful for planning research processes, some analytical methods to choose and use in professional practice, using the best available scientific evidence in the field of Orthoptic Sciences.
- Health Management Sciences aimed at organizing rehabilitation activities through definition of priorities, appropriateness, and use of available resources, both by delegating to collaborators activities within their competence, and working in teams, ensuring continuity and quality of care.
- Knowledge of at least one European Union language, besides Italian, within the specific field of competence and for exchanging general information and understanding international scientific literature.
Tools and teaching activities available for acquiring knowledge include: classroom activities, teaching laboratories, practical lessons in laboratories and/or equipped classrooms, internships, reading and interpretation of international literature.
Evaluation of such knowledge and understanding abilities will be carried out through the following verification methods: oral and written exams, practical tests on patients or simulations, clinical case discussions, written reports, completion of orthoptic sheets.

SECTION: Autonomy of judgment
URL: https://unisi.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10364

Autonomy of judgment.
The graduate at the end of the study path will be able to know and apply, autonomously, orthoptic science using clinical reasoning as a guiding tool for the criterion of choice among the possible options composing the various phases of orthoptic treatment. This autonomy will be achieved through the ability to effectively respond to the health needs of the patient, as an individual operator or in a team, opting for the best therapeutic strategies, identifying appropriate approaches and tools, conducting data collection (including social context analysis), patient examination, orthoptic evaluation/diagnosis, defining prognosis and therapeutic goals, short, medium and long term, developing the therapeutic program, selecting and applying suitable orthoptic methodologies and techniques for the clinical case (including intensity, time, type of professional technical approach) according to the best possible and available scientific evidence, according to international guidelines and Evidence Based; ethically, it will manifest through respect for the reference regulations, professional, legal, health and deontological standards. The autonomy of judgment of the graduate in Orthoptics and ophthalmic assistance will be fully realized through the habitual and judicious use of communication, knowledge, technical skills, clinical reasoning (diagnostic and evaluative process), emotions, values, and reflection in daily practice for the benefit of the individual or the community.
Teaching tools: classroom activities, Teaching laboratories, practical lessons in laboratories and/or equipped classrooms, Internship, reading and interpretation of international literature.
Verification methods: written and oral reports on technical/professional aspects, clinical case discussions, definition of the Rehabilitation Project/Program and compilation of the orthoptic file on real clinical cases; practical demonstration of the design and execution of specific techniques.

Learning capacity.
The graduate will be able to conduct an self-assessment of their educational level in order to maintain their knowledge at the highest level required for professional practice and to plan self-formation paths to enhance their skills, with particular reference to Evidence Based Practice in the field of orthoptics and ophthalmic assistance.
Over the three years, they will acquire learning abilities and competencies enabling, at the end of the path, the continuation of studies, including a master's degree in Class LM/SNT/02, scientific specialization courses and advanced permanent and recurring training (1st and 2nd level master's, specialization courses), update and in-depth courses (Continuing Medical Education), with a high degree of autonomy.
This ability will be developed and verified through exam preparation, attendance and evaluation of the internship, which combines theory with practice, through critical use of scientific literature and bibliography also for final exam preparation.
Teaching tools: classroom activities, seminars, laboratories, internship. The assessment of learning abilities will be carried out through the following verification methods: theoretical-practical exams, written and oral reports on technical/professional aspects, clinical case discussions, definition of the Rehabilitation Project/Program and compilation of the orthoptic and/or rehabilitation file on simulated and real clinical cases; research and production of teaching materials.

Ability to apply knowledge and understanding.
Generic Area Graduates at the end of the training path will be able to use orthoptic competencies within the orthoptic rehabilitation context, adopting the problem-solving methodology (clinical reasoning) by implementing all interconnected procedures that enable the realization of visual functional recovery.
The application of knowledge will develop considering fundamental aspects such as interaction with the real-life context of individuals, interpersonal and inter-professional relationships, and organizational management of aspects directly related to the type of work performed.
This ability will be fully achieved through mandatory attendance of the Professional Internship and teaching laboratory activities, both in quantitative terms (65 CFU of Internship distributed over 3 years in a gradual manner) and qualitative terms (3 CFU of teaching laboratory as a technical and relational learning gymnasium), where each student has access to a clinical tutor with a 1:1 ratio, maximum 1:2. The acquisition of professional skills is systematically verified through a logbook certifying presence and a "Core Values" evaluation sheet measuring attitudes, behaviors and general skills, compiled by the clinical tutor at the end of each internship experience; the combination of knowledge and skills is assessed through a structured test (station exam) held at the end of each academic year (in the 1st year it results in "eligibility," while at the end of the 2nd and 3rd years it results in an exam evaluated on a scale of thirty). All the above activities are planned, monitored and verified by the Professional Teaching and Internship Coordinator, who promotes meetings with tutors and students themselves. This figure also proposes training activities and facilitates the student in developing self-formation, accessing bibliographic sources, etc.
Teaching tools: classroom activities, teaching laboratories, practical lessons in laboratories and/or equipped classrooms, internship, reading and interpretation of international literature.
The assessment of such knowledge and understanding abilities will be carried out through the following verification methods: theoretical-practical exams, written reports on technical aspects, oral and written presentation of projects, practical tests on patients.

Communication skills.
The graduate must be able to manage communication effectively as the ability to establish a meaningful therapeutic relationship with the person and to establish an effective relationship with all other professionals from the same or other disciplines; they must also be capable of using communication tools in the healthcare context, demonstrating the ability to complete the orthoptic record, draft a therapeutic report, design an orthoptic intervention, etc., communicating clearly, concisely, and professionally in both verbal and written form, technically and grammatically accurate, and able to translate technical language into understandable terms for non-specialists; they must be able to communicate appropriately in international scientific contexts to convey ideas, problems, and related solutions.
Teaching tools: classroom activities, Laboratories and Internship. Assessment methods: written reports on the communication aspects of the rehabilitation setting; briefings with tutors and the coordinator; oral and written presentation of projects; Internship.
Expected occupational and professional outcomes for graduates.
Orthoptist and Ophthalmological Assistant The graduate can perform their activities in public or private structures, or as a self-employed professional. Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIAN. Competencies associated with the role.
Orthoptist and Ophthalmological Assistant Graduates are responsible for organizing, planning, and ensuring the quality of professional acts performed within their scope; they carry out their professional activities in healthcare structures, public or private, in an employed or self-employed capacity.
Description of admission tests.
The number of students admitted to the degree program is planned annually based on regional needs.
The entrance test is common to all health area degree programs and is conducted on the same day at all Italian universities.
The test consists of a multiple-choice quiz on the following subjects: general culture, logical reasoning, mathematics, physics, chemistry, and biology.
The ranking is based on merit. Role in the work context.
Orthoptist and Ophthalmological Assistant The graduate deals with and treats, on medical prescription, motor and sensory vision disorders and performs instrumental ophthalmological semiotics techniques. Additional information.
http://www.unisi.it/dipartimenti/dipartimento-scienze-mediche-chirurgiche-e-neuroscienze Description of specific educational objectives.
For the degree of responsibility, autonomy, and training (D.L.42/99, D.L. 251/00, D.L. 43/06), orthoptists and ophthalmological assistants acquire the foundations for understanding the qualitative and quantitative aspects of biological and pathological phenomena, the physiological and sensory principles of systemic and ocular apparatus, necessary to perform orthoptic rehabilitation treatment for disorders of ocular motility and binocular vision aimed at preventing and rehabilitating visual impairment in various biological ages.
During the Bachelor's degree, the student must acquire specific competencies for using sophisticated ophthalmological semiotics techniques that allow for precise and certain diagnoses, such as perimetry, ocular electrophysiology, tonometry, corneal topography, pachymetry, OCT, HRT, biometry, color sense examination, light sense examination, and contactology, developing professional skills defined by their professional profile (14/09/1994 n°743). They implement health education interventions for the prevention and rehabilitation of amblyopia and actively interact and collaborate with interdisciplinary teams to plan and share evaluative and rehabilitative interventions for multiple disabilities.
They acquire skills in ophthalmological assistance in the operating room, as modern ophthalmology increasingly requires personnel with specific competencies in this area to assist the ophthalmologist during interventions on ocular motility (strabismus) and laser interventions for correcting refractive defects.
The graduate in Orthoptics and Ophthalmological Assistance may also be included in research groups and may find professional opportunities by independently performing activities as defined by the Professional Profile (14/09/1994 n°743) in various fields: in orthoptic centers and Hospital Departments; in university clinics and private practices; in child neuropsychiatry and rehabilitation services; in legal medicine and occupational health services; in schools and low-vision centers. They work in collaboration with doctors and other health professionals and are personally responsible for planning and ensuring the quality of professional acts performed. The specific educational objectives of this Bachelor's degree are aimed at training technically-professional graduates, qualified to practice the profession of Orthoptist and Ophthalmological Assistant, and their achievement is realized through theoretical and practical learning focused on the specificity of the profession, including disciplines foundational to international cultural areas:
• Bio-molecular and bio-technological sciences,
• Integrated biological functions of human organs and systems,
• Etiopathogenetic bases of visual apparatus diseases,
• Orthoptic sciences,
• Diagnostic methodologies and techniques, medicine, and public health,
• Emergency medicine, emergency, and first aid,
• Human sciences and human behavior sciences,
• Clinical methodology,
• Elements of ocular surgery,
• Integrated systemic pathology, clinical medicine,
• Surgery and primary care, person-centered treatment,
• Neurological diseases and sense organs,
• Elements of pediatrics and multi-malformation syndromes,
• Elements of genetics. Particular emphasis has been placed on achieving specific learning objectives in the field of research methodology, through the development of statistical, computer, applied research, and scientific updating sciences at two levels. Students are provided with an English course (Medical English) also aimed at understanding scientific literature, with the possibility offered by the University language services to obtain B1 and B2 level certifications.
In the formulation of the Project, priority is given to the theoretical/practical study of Orthoptic Sciences, implemented through frontal lectures, especially exercises, teaching laboratories, and professional Internship in sectors qualifying orthoptics, such as visual apparatus rehabilitation, across all age groups.
The Bachelor's degree in Orthoptics and Ophthalmological Assistance is structured over three years and is established within the Faculty of Medicine and Surgery. The Course proposes the achievement of educational objectives. Graduates in the Bachelor's degree, pursuant to Law 10 August 2000 n. 251, art.2 comma I, are operators of Health Professions in the rehabilitation area and must possess scientific foundations and theoretical-practical preparation necessary to be qualified to practice the profession of Orthoptist and Ophthalmological Assistant and the methodology and culture necessary for practice and continuous training, as well as a level of professional, decisional, and operational autonomy derived from theoretical and practical training that also includes the acquisition of behavioral competencies and is achieved in the specific work context, thus guaranteeing, at the end of the training path, full mastery of all necessary competencies and their immediate applicability in the work environment.
To this end, the Bachelor's degree course for Orthoptist and Ophthalmological Assistant provides a total of 180 CFU, structured over three years of study, of which at least 48 must be acquired through training activities aimed at developing specific professional internship capabilities, primarily:
• Knowledge of the physiopathological aspects of refractive defects, ocular motility, and low vision, including specific rehabilitative treatments, as well as specific use of ophthalmological diagnostic equipment
• Essential theoretical knowledge of basic sciences, in the perspective of their subsequent professional application.
• Ability to collaborate with different professional figures in group healthcare activities.
• Ability to apply, in professional decisions, also the principles of healthcare economics
• Ability to recognize community health problems and intervene competently.
Graduates must specifically be able to:
* Know the physiopathological aspects of refractive defects and ocular motility.
* Perform instrumental ophthalmological semiotics, orthoptic techniques, functional rehabilitation methodology, and orthoptic rehabilitation treatment, along with specific clinical correlations.
* Know the needs for ophthalmological and orthoptic prevention in children, applying the most modern diagnostic and rehabilitation methods.
* Know and apply the principles governing ophthalmological surgical assistance, both outpatient and traditional.
* Learn and perform methods, techniques, and the use of rehabilitation orthoptic aids in disorders of ocular motility and mono-binocular vision in developmental age,
* Know the characteristics of the hospital structure hosting the internship of operators, the structure and services with their relative connections.
* Identify, prevent, and address critical events related to risks of various nature and type connected with the activities of different rehabilitation ophthalmology areas;
* Know the state regulations and laws governing the profession, medical-surgical equipment, and Public Health.
* Evaluate the reliability of education and rehabilitation processes by applying knowledge of biological, physiological, and pathological phenomena.
* Know and evaluate dynamic concepts of automation, informatization, and communication.
* Apply knowledge of the scientific process to improve the efficiency and effectiveness of rehabilitation processes.
* Realize and verify Quality Control and Assurance and identify appropriate interventions in case of unacceptable results.
* Act consistently with the disciplinary, ethical, and deontological principles of the profession in educational, rehabilitative, and productive situations as defined in the training project.
* Recognize and respect one's own role and competencies and those of other operators, establishing collaborative relationships, actively interacting and collaborating with interdisciplinary teams.
* Demonstrate teaching skills oriented towards staff training and student internship tutoring.
* Learn the basics of research methodology and apply research results in the technical-methodological field to improve the quality of specific rehabilitation methodologies.
* Know the essential elements of human resource management, with particular reference to issues in the healthcare field.
* Achieve an adequate level of written and spoken knowledge of at least one European Union language, in addition to Italian.
* Provide correct and effective technical services in application and respect of fundamental scientific principles, adapting such services to the assisted person in relation to different pathologies, operational sectors, and ages.
* Organize their activities using correctly the material and structural resources available in internship sites.
* Identify the demand for assistance and prevention and participate with the multi-professional team in identifying needs in ophthalmological and orthoptic fields across different social groups and ages.
* Contribute to the diagnostic-rehabilitative organization through the optimal use of available resources, thus ensuring progressive improvement in the quality of assistance.
* Know the themes of radioprotection through theoretical-practical courses.
During the TRAINING PATH, the graduate must acquire and deepen that set of knowledge (knowing), competencies (knowing how to do), and relationship capabilities (knowing how to be) equal to 180 CFU, of which 91 from frontal teaching, 65 from clinical professional Internship, and 24 from other teaching activities ("optional, language, thesis preparation, etc.") that will constitute the necessary cultural, scientific, and relational background to acquire full professional competence and to understand, address, and manage pathological events requiring orthoptic/rehabilitative intervention across all age groups. All this will be achieved through participation in frontal lectures, laboratory exercises, practical lessons in equipped classrooms with rehabilitation aids, guided by teachers and tutors, as well as personal study (library, databases) of the subjects offered by the degree program. In particular, through the disciplines represented by the SSD: FIS/07, M-DEA/01, M-PED/01, MED/01, SECS-S/02, BIO/09, BIO/10, BIO/13, BIO/17, MED/03, MED/04, MED/07, BIO/14, MED/41, MED/09, MED/718, the student will acquire a solid foundation of knowledge of the aspects and integrated functions of human organs and systems, statistical methodology for detecting phenomena regulating individual and social human life, and concepts of emergency and first aid in preparation for the disciplines characterizing the degree program. They will realize the professional construct through the characterizing SSD: MED/09, MED/08, MED/17, MED/30, MED/38, MED/50, M-PSI/08, MED/02, MED/36, MED/37, MED/42, MED/43, MED/44, MED/13, MED/27, MED/26, MED/28, MED/29, MED/32, MED/39, ING-INF/06, which will allow learning the fundamental concepts of human sciences and behavior, ethics and professional deontology, physiopathology of visual apparatus diseases, rehabilitation methodologies and techniques, etiology and pathogenesis of diseases, pathology and clinical practice, person-centered treatment, neurological diseases and sense organs, and reproductive and maternal-child medicine; furthermore, through the SSD: IUS/07, IUS/09, SECS-P/10, they will acquire elements of management and administration, useful for professional development in work sectors. In the formulation of the Project, priority is given to the theoretical/practical study of Orthoptic Sciences, implemented through frontal lectures, exercises, teaching laboratories, and professional Internship in sectors qualifying orthoptics, such as visual apparatus rehabilitation, across all age groups. The necessary competence and relational capacity to interact with the patient, caregivers, and the professional system is developed through the teaching of human sciences and psychopedagogical disciplines aimed at acquiring those behaviors and attitudes necessary and fundamental for relating to the patient. The teaching is structured into modules and is carried out through frontal lectures, classroom or laboratory exercises. Learning outcomes are assessed through possible in-course tests, also serving as self-assessment for the student, and with a final oral or written exam, an opportunity to verify the achievement of the set objectives, unique and simultaneous for each teaching unit, necessary for acquiring training credits. The learning outcomes of laboratory, English, and first-year Internship teaching result in eligibility. Regarding professional and internship activities, the reference is the Internship Manual v.2009 and subsequent modifications and integrations available at the Bachelor's degree program. The student has access to 5 credits for preparing the final exam of the Course at structures dedicated to training; this activity is defined as 'thesis internship' and can be carried out in non-university structures, such as hospital or private research facilities, subject to authorization by the Didactic Committee and the signing of a stage convention. In every phase of the mandatory Internship, the Student must operate under the direct supervision of a Tutor. The didactic functions of the Tutor, to whom students performing mandatory Internship activities are assigned, are the same as those provided for tutorial teaching within the teaching courses.

Master's Degree Courses University Master's Programs of 1st Level Admission Requirements High School Diploma or other foreign degree recognized as equivalent Professional status conferred by the degree. In general, Mathematics graduates can perform professional activities: (a) in companies and industry; (b) in laboratories and research centers; (c) in the field of scientific culture dissemination; (d) in the service sector; (e) in public administration. The Mathematics degree from the University of Siena provides competencies (to be completed with studies in a Master's degree) for career prospects in both teaching mathematics and sciences and scientific research in the same fields (in particular, consider the presence at the University of the Research Doctorate in Mathematical Logic, Computer Science, and Bioinformatics). These prospects are "definitely interesting" for - respectively - over 30% and over 50% of graduates in the class (Source: Alma Laurea, Graduate Profile 2006 and 2007). Moreover, the Mathematics degree provides more immediate professional competencies in the field of modeling phenomena in natural, biological, health, engineering, social, and humanistic sciences through the use of acquired information and computational tools. It should also be noted that an appropriate choice of the path, which includes acquiring additional statistical and computer science competencies, provides graduates with specific career prospects beyond those already mentioned: • in the economic and financial world, • in the field of managing and interpreting data related to human activities (financial, banking, insurance, and generally economic on one hand, socio-health and socio-political on the other) as well as data from natural and biological sciences. Final Exam Characteristics The final exam consists of the presentation, with discussion before a Degree Committee in a public session, of an individual written dissertation on topics of mathematical interest. The dissertation and presentation are in Italian, unless a motivated request is made by the student to the Academic Committee for another language. The dissertation must be prepared under the supervision of a supervisor, chosen among the University's faculty. The choice of the supervisor is made by the candidate and subject to approval by the Academic Committee, after consulting the chosen faculty member. For the preparation of the dissertation, the student may – upon approval by the Academic Committee – undertake internships at a company or external organization, or study periods at institutions other than the University of Siena. With the dissertation and its public discussion, the student must demonstrate – through the presentation of the specific topic discussed – that they have achieved the specific educational objectives of the degree course. The final exam grade is expressed on a scale of 110, with possible honors, and 6 ECTS credits are awarded for it. The merit score is primarily awarded based on the quality of the student's entire study path, and also based on the demonstration of maturity and mastery achieved in acquiring the learning objectives indicated through the presentation of the specific topic discussed in the dissertation. Required Knowledge for Admission For admission to the Mathematics degree course, the following elementary mathematics knowledge is required: Operations and inequalities between fractions; operations and inequalities between real numbers; familiarity with manipulating simple algebraic expressions and solving first and second-degree algebraic equations and inequalities; elements of Euclidean geometry and analytic geometry; familiarity with the definitions and basic properties of elementary functions (polynomials, exponential, logarithmic, and trigonometric functions). Such knowledge is typically acquired during high school studies (or equivalent for foreign students); in any case, verification of possession of such knowledge is a prerequisite for admission. Additionally, knowledge of the English language at least at level A2/2 is required. The following additional requirements are also considered important: • Appropriate motivation and good ability to adopt a correct methodological approach to study • Good logical reasoning and symbolic manipulation skills • Attitude towards the scientific method. Method of evaluating the student's initial preparation: Faculty of Mathematical, Physical, and Natural Sciences entrance/orientation test. In accordance with Faculty initiatives, recovery courses for academic deficits assigned following the entrance test evaluation are provided. Degree Awarded: Mathematics Degree Teaching Delivery Method: Conventional Knowledge and Understanding. Basic Training Area Mathematics graduates: Know and are able to use calculus in one and multiple variables, linear algebra, and the basics of algebra and geometry. They also possess the following knowledge and competencies: - Basic knowledge of physics and computer science. - Knowledge and understanding of basic applications of mathematics to physics. - Computational and computer science competencies including knowledge of programming languages and specific software. These objectives are achieved through activities related to some fundamental mandatory courses for all students, concentrated in the first year of the Study Course, and verified through the respective intermediate assessments (where provided by the Academic Regulations) and final exams (always mandatory). These fundamental courses are structured with lectures and exercises. Additionally, the Computer Science and Physics courses include appropriate laboratory activities. Theoretical Training Area Mathematics graduates also possess the following knowledge: • Mathematical logic • Analytic and differential geometry • Algebraic structures • Metric spaces, function sequences and series, and differential equations These objectives are achieved through activities related to some courses - mostly mandatory for all students - and verified through the respective intermediate assessments (where provided by the Academic Regulations) and final exams (always mandatory). Additionally, Mathematics graduates are able to • read and understand Mathematics texts and consult research articles in Mathematics. This objective is achieved partly through the systematic use of reference texts to be adopted for all courses, and partly – regarding more advanced texts and research articles in mathematics – through the writing of the dissertation for the final exam, which will be the main verification of the achievement of the result. Modeling and Application Training Area Mathematics graduates also possess the following knowledge: • Probability and statistics • Some numerical methods • Mathematical physics • Operations research This objective is achieved through a group of fundamental mandatory courses for all students and the related training activities (lectures, exercises, attendance at numerical analysis laboratories, individual study, intermediate assessments), and verified through the written, practical, and/or oral exams provided for the respective courses. Cross-Cutting Training Area Depending on the chosen path, Mathematics graduates acquire some of the following knowledge: • Additional and more advanced knowledge in physics, both theoretically and experimentally; • Additional and more advanced knowledge in computer science, both logically-theoretically and computationally; • Historical-critical knowledge of the development of mathematics; • Knowledge of dynamic systems modeling; • Knowledge of Artificial Intelligence; • Appropriate statistical competencies, both in methods and applications to economics, life sciences, and social sciences. This objective is achieved through a significant number of courses, organized into "packages" consistent with the desired educational objective, which the student will follow once the path is chosen. Verification of the achievement of the objective occurs through the respective intermediate assessments (where provided by the Academic Regulations) and final exams (always mandatory).

Critical Thinking.
Mathematics graduates:
• Are able to construct and develop logical arguments with a clear identification of assumptions and conclusions;
• Are able to recognize correct proofs and identify fallacious reasoning;
• Are able to propose and analyze mathematical models associated with concrete situations derived from other disciplines, and use such models to facilitate the study of the original situation;
• Have experience working in groups, but are also able to work well independently.
The first two objectives will be achieved through activities (lectures, exercises, individual study) provided for all courses. The third objective will be attained using specific characteristic courses (particularly in probability and statistics and mathematical physics) mandatory for all students, in addition to those of the related and integrated activities of the degree program (which are mandatory and do not belong to the mathematical scientific/disciplinary sectors). Verification of achieving the objectives occurs through the relevant intermediate assessments (where provided by the Didactic Regulations) and the corresponding final exams (which are mandatory). These methods and verifications also apply to the ability to work well independently. For the last objective, the main tool is attendance at computer science and numerical analysis laboratories, and verification occurs through the ability to complete the assigned programs, both in groups and individually.
Learning Capacity.
Mathematics graduates:
• Are able to continue their studies, both in Mathematics and other disciplines, with a high degree of autonomy.
In particular, they are able to address advanced topics and those close to scientific research in the following fields of study, specific to Mathematics or closely related to it:
Mathematical Logic and Foundations;
Algebra and Geometry;
Mathematical Analysis;
Mathematical Physics;
Numerical Analysis;
Computer Science.
Additionally, they are able to learn and process information and research regarding natural and social phenomena within the fields of Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Economics, and Statistics, with the aim of placing them in a rational framework and formulating mathematical models for the phenomena in question.
Furthermore, Mathematics graduates:
• Have a flexible mindset and are able to quickly integrate into study and work environments, easily adapting to new issues.
All the training activities of the Mathematics Degree Course will be used to verify the achievement of these objectives.
Basic Training Area Mathematics graduates are able to:
- Mathematically formalize moderately difficult problems stated in natural language, and benefit from this formalization to clarify or solve them.
- Extract qualitative information from quantitative data.
- Use computer and computational tools as support for mathematical processes, and to acquire additional information.
The degree of acquisition of the above-mentioned skills is verified in passing exams through the resolution of exercises and problems assigned during written, oral, and/or practical tests.
Theoretical Training Area Mathematics graduates are able to:
• Produce rigorous proofs of mathematical results not identical to those already known but clearly related to them;
• Solve moderately difficult problems in various fields of mathematics;
• Mathematically formalize moderately difficult problems stated in natural language, and benefit from this formalization to clarify or solve them;
• Extract qualitative information from quantitative data.
The degree of acquisition of the above-mentioned skills is verified in passing exams through the resolution of exercises and problems assigned during written and/or oral tests.
Modeling and Application Training Area Mathematics graduates are able to:
• Solve moderately difficult problems in various fields of mathematics, with particular reference to optimization problems;
• Mathematically formalize problems in moderately difficult physical systems stated in natural language, and benefit from this formalization to clarify or solve them;
• Extract qualitative information from quantitative data, considering probabilistic and statistical models;
• Use computer and computational tools as support for mathematical processes, and to acquire additional information, with particular reference to numerical methods.
The degree of acquisition of the above-mentioned skills is verified in passing exams through the resolution of exercises and problems assigned during written, oral, and/or practical tests.
Cross-disciplinary Training Area Mathematics graduates are able to:
• Produce rigorous proofs of mathematical results not identical to those already known but clearly related to them;
• Solve moderately difficult problems in various fields of mathematics;
• Mathematically formalize moderately difficult problems stated in natural language, and benefit from this formalization to clarify or solve them;
• Extract qualitative information from quantitative data;
• Use computer and computational tools as support for mathematical processes, and to acquire additional information.
The degree of acquisition of the above-mentioned skills is verified in passing exams through the resolution of exercises and problems assigned during written, oral, and/or practical tests.

Additional information.
http://www.unisi.it/dipartimenti/dipartimento-ingegneria-dell%E2%80%99informazione-e-scienze-matematiche Specific learning objectives description.
The Mathematics Degree at the University of Siena aims to train graduates who have acquired:
Understanding of methods specific to Mathematics, appreciation of the abstraction procedures it uses, strong awareness of the logical rigor inherent to it Basic knowledge in physics and computer science Knowledge of statistical and computational aspects of mathematical methods used in describing phenomena Knowledge of mathematical models for describing and studying natural, social, and economic phenomena Knowledge of developments in modern mathematical theories and the problems they address Ability to continuously update their knowledge.
The proposed training path to achieve the described objective is based on a predominant part of courses and related formative activities (lectures, exercises, individual study, intermediate tests, laboratory, written and oral exams), common to all students, organized to provide them with a detailed and in-depth mathematical preparation – with an accentuated presence of content in the theoretical training field – accompanied by the necessary basic competencies in subjects closely related to Mathematics, such as Physics and Computer Science. This common part is substantiated in the Ordinamento through the sharing of a minimum of 48 CFU in Basic Formative Activities and a minimum of 57 CFU in Characterizing Formative Activities, for a total of at least 105 CFU – of which 87 in MAT/ sectors, characterizing the Class – shared by all students.
The common part is then completed with differentiated paths, aimed at better characterizing the graduate profile, while providing the possibility to either continue studies in a Master's Degree (in Mathematics or other disciplines, e.g., Physics, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Statistics) or to enter the job market. To this end, the Degree Course may – where conditions are met, particularly regarding the number of Teachers and Students – activate an adequate number of Curricula.
The differentiation between paths (or Curricula where activated) is achieved by flexibly using the available credits for Affine and Integrative Formative Activities, for which the proposed Ordinamento provides a minimum of 18 CFU to a maximum of 36 CFU, all not belonging to the MAT/ scientific/disciplinary sectors characterizing the Class.
Specifically, two different training Orientations are currently well-defined and available to students (but not mandatory): the first ('General') is realized through the Data Bases path (2nd year) + Physics 2 (3rd year), the second ('Mathematics and Statistics') is obtained by choosing Statistics II (2nd year) + Statistics for Economics and Business (3rd year). The second path benefits from current scientific/teaching competencies present in the Department of Economics, Politics, and Statistics (DEPS), and, as already indicated in the Presentation (see 'The Study Program in Brief'), allows the graduate to enroll without academic debts in the Master's Degree in Statistical Sciences for Survey Sampling (SSIC) offered by the aforementioned Department.
