Program, Texts, and Objectives Admission Requirements Students possessing a High School Diploma or an equivalent foreign degree may be admitted.
Required knowledge will include: elements of general culture and logical reasoning, mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology.
Additionally, knowledge of English at least at level A2/2 (CEFR) is required. The number of students admitted to the degree program is planned annually based on regional needs.
The entrance exam is common to all health-related degree programs and is conducted on the same day at all Italian universities.
Professional status conferred by the title.
L/SNT2 LOGOPEDIST According to a recent survey by Unioncamere (www.unioncamere.it), the profession of Logopedist is ranked among the most sought-after in the job market and most difficult to find among highly specialized professionals.
Final Exam Characteristics The final exam, which serves as the State Exam for the Logopedist profession (D.Lgs 502/1992, art. 6, comma 3), consists of:
a) a practical test in which the student must demonstrate acquisition of theoretical, practical, and technical skills specific to the professional profile;
b) preparation of a thesis and its defense. See DM 19 February 2009, art. 7.
The final score is expressed on a scale of 110.
If a total score of 110/110 is achieved, the President of the Final Exam Commission will propose the award of honors, which can only be granted unanimously by the members present.
The final exam is worth 5 CFU.
Required knowledge for admission Students possessing a High School Diploma or an equivalent foreign degree may be admitted to the Bachelor's Degree in Logopedics. The number of students admitted is determined based on national and regional planning, availability of teaching staff, teaching facilities (classrooms), and clinical facilities for practical activities.
English language knowledge at least at level A2/2 (CEFR) is required. Basic knowledge of biology, chemistry, mathematics, and physics at the high school level, as well as general culture, are required as defined in the Study Program's didactic regulations.
Student preparation will be assessed through analysis of errors in logic, chemistry, biology, physics-mathematics quizzes (multiple-choice questions) administered during the entrance exam, common to all health-related degree programs.
In line with verification of any educational deficits related to biology, chemistry, and physics-mathematics, verified through analysis of errors in the quizzes administered during the entrance exam, the instructors of the relevant modules will conduct a brief recovery course of the main knowledge in deficit during the first semester before the modules begin.
Any educational obligations must be fulfilled by the first day of the course.
Degree awarded.
BACHELOR'S DEGREE IN LOGOPEDICS Teaching Methodology Conventional Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area At the end of the training path, graduates in Logopedics must have acquired a wide range of knowledge in basic sciences, characteristic disciplines, and communication and professional management fields.
In particular, students must achieve solid cultural and scientific foundations in the following areas:
Preparatory, basic, biomedical, and psychological sciences, for understanding biological phenomena, organ and system functioning mechanisms, cognitive and psychomotor development, physiological phenomena, and their correlation with psychological, social, and environmental dimensions of disease;
Logopedics Sciences, necessary to identify preventive and rehabilitative needs through clinical data evaluation in cognitive and functional fields, to understand the components underlying pathological processes targeted by rehabilitation and/or therapeutic interventions in pediatric, adult, or geriatric age, to know and apply effective and current therapeutic approaches, technical and methodological for resolving patient/client health issues, to acquire the scientific basis of functional alterations and general and specific rehabilitation methodologies in various specialized fields (neurology, pediatrics, child neuropsychiatry, geriatrics, critical care, otorhinolaryngology, phoniatrics, audiology, etc.), to design, implement, and verify logopedic rehabilitation interventions using objective assessment tools, such as standardized tests and effective instruments, and all appropriate tools for case resolution (instrumental therapies, approaches and methodologies, communication aids).
Interdisciplinary and medical-surgical sciences for understanding physio-pathological elements applicable to various clinical situations, also in relation to diagnostic parameters;
Prevention and Health Services Sciences, to acquire the ability to analyze health problems of individuals and/or communities and the responses of health and social services to citizens' main needs;
Statistical Sciences, quantitative methods, and scientific updating, to ensure constant scientific updating, knowledge, and correct interpretation of statistical tools useful for research, knowledge of main analytical methods to be used in professional practice (scientific evidence available in literature);
Health Management Sciences, focused on organizing rehabilitation activities through defining priorities, appropriateness, and use of available resources for activities within competence, in individual and team work, ensuring continuity and quality of care;
Knowledge of at least one European Union language, preferably English, in addition to Italian, within the specific area of competence, for exchanging general and specific information, for accessing and producing international scientific literature.
The evaluation of such knowledge and understanding abilities, acquired through frontal lectures and professional clinical internship, as well as through seminars and laboratory activities over three years, will be verified and consolidated through the following assessment methods: oral and written exams, practical tests in simulation, practical tests on patients, written reports, case reports.
Teaching tools: classroom activities, practical lessons in clinics and/or equipped classrooms, clinical internship, reading and interpretation of international scientific literature, study hours, and self-training.
Area of Preparatory Basic Biomedical and Psychological Sciences Knowledge and understanding of organs and systems; knowledge of physical, cognitive, and psychomotor development and physiological phenomena. Knowledge of psychological, social, and environmental dimensions of disease.
Area of Logopedics Sciences Knowledge and understanding of preventive and rehabilitative needs of the subject in different life stages through instrumental and functional evaluation of clinical data in communication, cognitive, and functional fields. Knowledge of physiological and pathological processes underlying rehabilitation interventions.
Area of Medical-Surgical Sciences Knowledge and understanding of physio-pathology in various clinical situations.
Area of Prevention and Health Services Sciences Knowledge and understanding of health problems of an individual and community and the responses of health and social services to citizens' main needs.
Area of Statistical Sciences Knowledge and understanding of statistical tools useful for planning research processes and correct consultation and interpretation of reference scientific literature.
Area of Health Management Sciences Knowledge and understanding of the organization of the National Health Service (SSN) and care priorities and patient management, appropriateness, and use of available resources within a work system. Knowledge of care priorities and patient management, appropriateness of one's intervention in private, contracted, and non-contracted work contexts.
Area of English Language Knowledge of English at a level not lower than A2/2 upon entry.
Critical Thinking.
Graduates in Logopedics, at the end of their studies, will be able to know and independently apply logopedic interventions using clinical reasoning as a guiding tool in decision-making, within the possible options composing the various phases of the process. This autonomy will be achieved through acquisition, consolidation, and experimentation of competencies and abilities to effectively respond to individual and/or collective health needs, as a single operator or in a team, choosing the best therapeutic strategies, identifying appropriate approaches and tools, collecting data (including social context analysis), patient evaluation, appropriate logopedic assessments, defining short, medium, and long-term prognoses and therapeutic goals, contributing to formulating a rehabilitation project, elaborating the therapeutic program, selecting and applying rehabilitation methodologies and techniques to the clinical case (including intensity, time, type of technical-professional approach) according to possible scientific evidence and international guidelines and Evidence-Based practice; ethically, it will manifest through respect for relevant regulations, professional, legal, health, and deontological standards.
Graduates' critical thinking will be fully realized through habitual and judicious use of communication, knowledge, technical skills, clinical reasoning (diagnostic and evaluative process), emotions, values, and reflection in daily practice for the benefit of the individual or community, especially through the professional clinical internship and small group laboratories.
Teaching tools: classroom activities, practical lessons in laboratories and/or equipped classrooms, clinical internship, reading and interpretation of international scientific literature.
Assessment methods: written reports on technical/professional topics, discussion of clinical cases, definition of Rehabilitation Project/Program and completion of logopedic and/or rehabilitation records for real clinical cases. Annual clinical internship assessment.
Learning Ability.
Logopedics graduates will be able to conduct self-assessment of their educational level to maintain their knowledge at the highest level required for professional practice and plan self-training paths to enhance their competencies, particularly in Evidence-Based Practice in rehabilitation.
Over three years, they will acquire learning abilities and competencies enabling them, at the end of the program, to pursue further studies, including a Master's degree in Class LM/SNT/02, scientific specialization courses, and permanent and recurring advanced training (1st and 2nd level master's, specialization courses), continuing medical education courses, with a high degree of autonomy.
This ability will be developed and assessed through exam preparation, attendance and evaluation of the internship, which combines theory with practice, critical use of scientific literature and bibliography for final exam preparation.
Teaching tools: classroom activities, seminars, internship.
Assessment of learning abilities will be conducted through the following methods: theoretical/practical exams, written and oral reports on technical/professional aspects, discussion of clinical cases, definition of Rehabilitation Project/Program and completion of logopedic and/or rehabilitation records for simulated and real clinical cases; research and production of teaching materials; journal club.
Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area Graduates at the end of the training path will be able to apply the logopedic process within the rehabilitation setting, both in simulated and patient scenarios, adopting problem-solving methodology (clinical reasoning) and implementing correlated procedures to realize care and rehabilitation interventions in language, articulation, phonation, and hearing areas following various congenital or acquired pathological events.
Application of knowledge will be developed considering fundamental aspects such as interaction with the real-life context of people, interpersonal and inter-professional relationships, and organizational management of aspects directly related to the type of work performed.
This ability will be fully achieved through mandatory clinical internship attendance and didactic laboratory activities, both quantitatively (60 CFU of internship distributed over 3 years gradually) and qualitatively (3 CFU of didactic laboratory as a technical, gestural, and relational learning environment), where each student has access to designated clinical tutors. Professional skills acquisition will be systematically verified through a logbook certifying presence and a "Core Values" evaluation sheet measuring attitudes, behaviors, and general skills, completed by the clinical tutor at the end of each internship experience; the combination of knowledge and skills will be assessed through a structured exam at the end of each academic year (in the 1st year it results in "adequacy," while at the end of the 2nd and 3rd years it results in an exam scored out of 30). All these activities are planned, monitored, and verified by the Coordinator of theoretical/practical activities and internships, who promotes meetings with tutors and students, proposes training activities, facilitates student self-training, access to bibliographic sources, etc.
Teaching tools: classroom activities, practical lessons in clinics and/or equipped classrooms, clinical internship, reading and interpretation of international scientific literature.
Assessment of knowledge and understanding abilities will be conducted through the following methods: theoretical/practical exams, written reports on technical aspects (completion of Rehabilitation Project/Program), oral and written presentation of rehabilitation projects, simulated and/or patient-based practical tests.
Area of Preparatory Basic Biomedical and Psychological Sciences Ability to apply acquired knowledge in areas requiring anatomical, physiological, psychological, chemical, and biochemical competencies.
Knowledge and understanding acquisition will occur through curricular courses with frontal lectures and corresponding assessment via oral and written exams, at the discretion of the instructor. These knowledge areas will be deepened and consolidated through didactic laboratories and professional clinical internships over the three years of the program.
Area of Logopedics Sciences Ability to design and initiate the evaluation-rehabilitation process using all appropriate tools for resolving clinical questions.
Acquisition of these competencies and knowledge will occur through curricular courses and professional clinical internships in various logopedic intervention areas. Assessment of knowledge and understanding abilities will be conducted through oral and written exams for frontal lectures, and through simulated practical tests, patient-based practical tests, written reports, and case reports, simulation, and practice of diagnostic-rehabilitative tools during and at the end of each year's professional clinical internship.
Teamwork in small groups and discussion of clinical cases in various logopedic intervention areas.
Area of Medical-Surgical Sciences Ability to understand, discuss, and evaluate a clinical case requiring medical or surgical intervention.
These knowledge areas will be acquired through frontal lectures of relevant curricular courses and assessed via oral and written exams.
Area of Prevention and Health Services Sciences Ability to apply knowledge regarding health in the context of real life and interpersonal relationships.
Acquisition of these competencies will occur through frontal lectures of relevant curricular courses, followed by assessment of knowledge and understanding abilities via oral and written exams.
Area of Statistical Sciences The student must know and develop the ability to apply analytical methods in consulting scientific literature to utilize scientific evidence available in literature within the field of Logopedics and rehabilitation.
These competencies will be learned through curricular courses and corresponding learning assessments (written and oral exams), then tested and consolidated during professional clinical internships and laboratories.
Area of Health Management Sciences Ability to operate while ensuring patient continuity and quality of care. These competencies are provided to students through frontal lectures of relevant curricular courses.
Assessment of knowledge and understanding abilities will be conducted through oral and written exams, at the discretion of the instructor.
Area of English Language Knowledge of English, particularly in the scientific field. Ability to read, interpret, and understand international scientific literature, as well as communication and information exchange capabilities.
These competencies are refined through frontal English language instruction (oral or written proficiency exam) and continuously consolidated by the student through self-training via consultation of scientific literature.

Communication skills.
The graduate must be able to manage communication effectively as the ability to establish a meaningful therapeutic relationship with the person and to establish an effective relationship with all other professionals in the same or other disciplines; they must also be capable of using communication tools in the healthcare setting, demonstrating the ability to complete the speech therapy record, draft a therapeutic report, design a speech therapy intervention, etc., communicating clearly, concisely, and professionally in both verbal and written form, technically and grammatically accurate, and also knowing how to translate technical language into understandable terms for non-specialists; they must be able to communicate appropriately in international scientific contexts to convey ideas, problems, and related solutions.
Teaching tools: classroom activities, internship.
Assessment methods: written reports on communication aspects of the rehabilitation setting; briefings with tutors and coordinators; oral and written presentation of projects; internship.
Planned occupational and professional outcomes for graduates.
L/SNT2 SPEECH THERAPIST According to a recent survey by Unioncamere (www.unioncamere.it), the profession of Speech Therapist is ranked among the most sought-after in the job market and most difficult to find among highly specialized operators.
Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIAN Associated competencies for the role.
L/SNT2 SPEECH THERAPIST The Speech Therapist can perform their profession in public and private healthcare settings, schools, rehabilitation and recovery centers, service cooperatives, non-governmental organizations, and public and private prevention services.
Description of admission tests.
The number of students admitted to the degree program is planned annually based on regional needs.
The entrance test is common to all healthcare degree programs and is conducted on the same day at all Italian universities.
The test consists of a multiple-choice quiz on the following subjects: general culture, logical reasoning, mathematics, physics, chemistry, and biology.
The ranking is based on merit. Role in work context.
L/SNT2 SPEECH THERAPIST At the end of the training program, the Speech Therapist will be able to implement all procedures that allow for the realization of care and rehabilitation interventions in the areas of language, phonatory articulation, and hearing following acquired or congenital pathologies. The Speech Therapist will also be able to establish an effective therapeutic relationship with the patient and all professional figures useful for the rehabilitation intervention. They will autonomously use all communication tools in healthcare and non-healthcare settings, demonstrating the ability to manage and design any type of speech therapy intervention.
Additional information.
http://www.unisi.it/dipartimenti/dipartimento-scienze-mediche-chirurgiche-e-neuroscienze Specific educational objectives description.
The specific educational objectives of this degree program are aimed at the technical-professional training of graduates, qualified to practice the profession of Speech Therapist, and their achievement is realized through theoretical and practical learning focused on the specificity of the profession, including disciplines forming the international cultural fields (Core Curriculum of the Speech Therapist, v. 2008 and subsequent modifications and additions) such as:
• Molecular foundations of life;
• Morphological foundations;
• Psychological and anthropological sciences;
• Principles of rehabilitation and introduction to Logopedics;
• Sciences of phonation;
• Theoretical and applied language sciences;
• Theoretical and practical sciences of logopedics;
• Pharmacology and general pathology;
• Quantitative methods;
• Pathology of the phonatory-articulatory apparatus;
• Logopedics in neurorehabilitation and neuropsychology;
• Logopedics in respiratory and swallowing contexts;
• First aid elements;
• Prevention sciences;
• Logopedics in pediatric contexts;
• Logopedics in audiological contexts;
• Logopedics and rehabilitation in geriatric and disability contexts;
• Evidence-based logopedics and scientific update;
• Healthcare management.
Learning areas of the degree program:
FOUNDATIONAL BASIC, BIOMEDICAL, AND PSYCHOLOGICAL SCIENCES: for understanding biological phenomena, mechanisms of organ and apparatus functioning, cognitive and psychomotor development, physiological phenomena also in correlation with psychological, social, and environmental dimensions of disease.
LOGOPEDIC SCIENCES: necessary to identify preventive and rehabilitative needs of the subject through the evaluation of clinical data in cognitive and functional fields for the entity and significance of symptoms; understanding the constituents underlying pathological processes focused on by therapeutic rehabilitation interventions in developmental, adult, and geriatric age; designing, implementing, and verifying speech therapy interventions using objective evaluation methods, such as tests, and standardized tools, and effective therapeutic methods and all appropriate tools for case resolution.
INTERDISCIPLINARY AND MEDICAL SURGICAL SCIENCES: for understanding physio-pathological elements applicable to different clinical situations, also in relation to diagnostic parameters.
PREVENTION AND HEALTH SERVICES SCIENCES: to achieve the ability to analyze health problems of the individual and/or community and the responses of health and social services to the main needs of citizens.
STATISTICAL SCIENCES: knowledge of quantitative methods and necessary content to realize scientific update, to promote understanding of statistical tools useful for planning the research process, some analytical methods to choose and use in professional practice, using the best scientific evidence in the field of logopedics.
HEALTHCARE MANAGEMENT SCIENCES: aimed at organizing rehabilitation activities through the definition of priorities, appropriateness, and use of available resources, both by delegating to collaborators activities of their competence and working in teams ensuring continuity and quality of care.
ENGLISH LANGUAGE: for exchanging general information and understanding international scientific literature. Particular emphasis has been placed on achieving specific learning objectives in the field of research methodology, through the development at two levels of statistical, computer, applied research, and scientific update sciences. Students are provided with an English language course (Medical English) also aimed at understanding scientific literature, with the possibility, provided by the University language services, to obtain B1 and B2 level certifications.
In the formulation of the Project, priority is given to the theoretical/practical study of Logopedic Sciences, which is carried out through frontal lectures, exercises, and professional internship in sectors qualifying Logopedics, such as rehabilitation in pediatric, neurological, neuropsychological, phoniatric, and audiological contexts.
The necessary relational competence and capacity to interact with the patient, caregivers, and the professional system is developed through the teaching of human sciences and psychopedagogical sciences aimed at acquiring the necessary behaviors and attitudes for relating to the patient/client, which are then tested in professional clinical internships.
The teaching is structured in modules and is delivered through frontal lectures, classroom exercises, and when appropriate, theoretical-practical laboratories. Learning outcomes are assessed through possible in-course tests, which also serve as self-assessment for the student, and are refined through a final oral or written exam at the discretion of the instructor; this serves as an opportunity to verify the achievement of the set objectives, unique and simultaneous for each teaching unit, necessary for acquiring training credits. The learning outcomes of laboratory, English, and first-year internship teaching result in eligibility.
Regarding professional and internship activities, reference is made to the Internship Manual v.2009 and subsequent modifications and integrations available at the Degree Program.
Students have access to 5 credits for preparing the final exam at facilities dedicated to training; this activity is defined as 'thesis internship' and can be carried out in non-university facilities, such as hospital or private research facilities, subject to authorization by the Teaching Committee and the signing of a stage agreement.
Graduates in this class, pursuant to Article 6, paragraph 3, of Legislative Decree 30 December 1992, No. 502 and subsequent modifications and additions, pursuant to Law 26 February 1999, No. 42, and pursuant to Law 10 August 2000, No. 251, are healthcare professionals whose specific field of activity and responsibility is determined by the contents of the ministerial decrees establishing the professional profiles and the educational frameworks of the respective university courses and post-basic training courses as well as the specific professional codes of ethics.
The Speech Therapist, at the end of the training program, must acquire knowledge (knowing), skills (knowing how to do), and relational capacity (knowing how to be) with particular reference to the following fields: rehabilitation interventions in pathologies of children and adults, both regarding the linguistic sphere from the phonetic-articulatory point of view, and from the point of view of fluency, comprehension, and linguistic organization, taking responsibility for their own training and reflecting on their professional practice with the aim of learning.
TRAINING PATH:
The set of knowledge to be acquired by the graduate, totaling 180 CFU (of which 96 from frontal teaching, 60 from professional clinical internship, and 24 from other teaching activities 'optional, English language, thesis preparation, etc.'), will constitute the necessary cultural, scientific, and relational background to acquire full professional competence and to understand, address, and manage pathological events requiring rehabilitation and/or therapeutic intervention in all age groups, achieved through participation in frontal lectures, practical lessons in equipped classrooms with rehabilitation aids, guided by teachers and tutors belonging to the specific professional profile, as well as through personal study (library, databases) of the subjects offered by the degree program.
In particular, through the disciplines represented by the SSD: BIO/10, BIO/13, MED/03, BIO/17, BIO/16, BIO/09, M-PSI 08, M-PED/01, M-DEA/01, MED/02, BIO/14, MED/04, MED/09, MED/07, MED/01, ING/INF 06, MED/41, MED/18, MED/39, MED/38, MED/31, MED/32, MED/26, MED/27, MED/01, a solid foundation of knowledge of biological aspects and functions of human organs and apparatuses, statistical methodology for detecting phenomena regulating individual and social human life, and concepts of emergency and first aid will be acquired, preparing for the characteristic disciplines of the degree program.
Starting from the 2019-20 academic year, in compliance with Legislative Decree of 31 January 2018, the degree program modifies the educational framework and programming by increasing the CFU of the Linguistics SSD L-LIN/01 teaching and introducing the teaching of Philosophy and Theory of Languages SSD M-FIL/05, considering that these disciplines constitute the fundamental theoretical basis for future specialists of language pathologies.
The graduate in Logopedics will realize the professional construct through the characteristic SSD: MED/50, MED/31, L-LIN/01, M-FIL/05, BIO/16, MED/32, FIS/07, MED/08, BIO/09, MED/28, MED/26, MED/25, MED/10, MED/44, MED/43, MED/42, which will allow the learning of fundamental concepts of human sciences and behavior, ethics and professional deontology, respiratory and swallowing physiopathology and respiratory apparatus diseases, logopedic methodologies and techniques, etiology and pathogenesis of diseases, pathology and clinical practice, treatment of the person, neurological diseases and sense organs; furthermore, through the SSD: IUS/07, IUS/09, SECS-P/10, elements of management and business administration will be acquired, useful for professional development in work contexts.

Admission Requirements High School Diploma or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent Professional status conferred by the title.
Language Operator and Mediator in social, tourist, cultural, and international cooperation contexts. In the cultural-tourism sector, career opportunities fall within various fields related to cultural services and cultural mediation between countries. Main occupational roles include: media operator; translator and language mediation expert in literary, artistic, and performance fields; tourist operator.
Socio-cultural career opportunities are primarily linked, in Italy, to the need for linguistic and cultural mediation connected to migration phenomena and the planning of cultural tourism development in multilingual contexts, tangible and intangible; abroad, to activities of non-profit organizations engaged in socio-economic and cultural development initiatives, as well as embassies, consulates, and representative offices maintaining exchanges with European and extra-European countries.
Career opportunities in language mediation, dissemination, and promotion of Italian language and culture for foreign audiences are linked, in Italy, to the cultural tourism sector and needs connected to migration phenomena; abroad, graduates of the Course may work in organizations and companies focused on disseminating Italian culture, as well as public and private institutions and organizations dedicated to teaching Italian as a foreign language.
Language Operator and Mediator in business and commercial contexts. In business and commercial settings, graduates in Languages for Intercultural and Business Communication are sought by companies of various sizes for marketing, intercultural mediation, commercial exchanges, and professional offices offering legal and administrative services to entities operating nationally and internationally. Main occupational roles include: foreign correspondent, international business operator, foreign relations officer, customer service officer, foreign trade officer.
Final Project Characteristics To be admitted to the final project, the student must have passed all exams and completed the training activities specified in the Study Plan.
The final project consists of a written thesis of at least 30 pages and no more than 50 (or a multimedia project of similar size). Respecting the student's interests and professional vocation, works may include translation, contrastive analysis, linguistic and/or philological analysis, critical literary, sociological, or cultural research on social, linguistic, and cultural phenomena related to one or more studied languages and cultures; alternatively, the student may choose to develop an independent project within one of the professionalizing disciplines included in their Study Plan, as well as the internship experience.
Students are required to demonstrate mastery of the languages, cultures, and disciplinary knowledge under analysis, possess current bibliographic, computational, and critical tools, understand the necessary scientific criteria for preparing the thesis, and demonstrate independent judgment and the ability to mediate between different linguistic and cultural fields.
The project, prepared under the guidance of a faculty tutor, is defended before a specially appointed Committee, which evaluates the project on a scale of 110, with possible summa cum laude. The final thesis defense also includes verification of competencies acquired in one of the foreign languages studied. The score will consider the base average, quality of the final thesis, language competence achieved, external certifications obtained, university curriculum (in course/out of course), and possible participation in international exchange projects.
4 CFU are assigned to the final project.
Required Knowledge for Admission Admission to the Degree Course is open to students holding a high school diploma or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent (Article 6, paragraph 1 of D.M. 270/2004).
Admission requires: a basic preparation enabling engagement with the disciplines studied, good analytical and synthetic skills for texts of medium complexity.
An entrance verification will be conducted at the start of the academic year as per D.M. 270/2004. University study methodologies and scientific writing workshops will be organized.
If the entrance verification result is negative, the Degree Course will establish specific compulsory educational obligations that each student must fulfill within the first year.
For the study languages, the required entry-level competence is defined as follows: i) for English, not below B1 level of the Common European Framework of Reference; ii) for French, Spanish, or German as study languages, not below A1 level; iii) entry to the study of Russian and Chinese does not require prior knowledge.
Knowledge of previously studied languages will be verified through written tests (classroom collective and/or individual in the language laboratory) to assess grammatical knowledge and receptive skills (reading, listening), determining each student's pre-existing competence relative to the Common European Framework levels. If deemed necessary by the instructors or upon request, tests may be supplemented with an in-depth interview to evaluate oral comprehension and expression skills.
Course instructors will conduct orientation and tutoring activities during enrollment, according to a pre-established and public schedule, to identify and assess potential educational gaps and guide students toward recovery paths.
Degree Awarded.
Degree in LANGUAGES FOR INTERCULTURAL AND BUSINESS COMMUNICATION Teaching Delivery Method Conventional
Knowledge and Understanding.
LINGUISTIC AREA Graduates of the Course will have acquired:
- full mastery of spoken and written Italian;
- excellent mastery of English and another language offered in the curriculum, in all four skills described in the Common European Framework of Reference (C1 level for English; at least B2 level for French, Spanish, and German; at least B1 level for Russian and Chinese);
- good knowledge in philology and general linguistics;
- basic knowledge in language teaching, Italian and foreign.
LITERARY AREA Graduates of the Intercultural Communication Languages curriculum will have acquired:
- advanced knowledge of English literature and culture, and literature and culture related to the second foreign language studied;
- good knowledge of Italian literature history;
- good competence in using the main tools of textual analysis and literary criticism (genre, rhetoric, metrics, stylistics, narratology).
Graduates of the Business Languages curriculum will have acquired:
- basic knowledge of English literature and culture, and literature and culture related to the second foreign language studied;
- good knowledge of Italian literature history;
- good competence in using the main tools of textual analysis and literary criticism (genre, rhetoric, metrics, stylistics, narratology).
SOCIOECONOMIC, HISTORICAL-PHILOSOPHICAL, ARTISTIC AREA Graduates of the Course will have acquired:
- basic knowledge of Italian, European, and extra-European history and geography;
- basic knowledge in at least one of the following fields: history and management of artistic-cultural heritage; economic sociology and labor; aesthetics.
FORMATION, ECONOMICS, LAW, INFORMATICS AREA Graduates of the Intercultural Communication Languages curriculum will have acquired:
- basic knowledge in computer science;
- knowledge in one or more of the following fields: cultural heritage law, law and literature, business economics, territorial marketing.
Graduates of the Business Languages curriculum will have acquired:
- basic knowledge in computer science;
- basic knowledge in economics and business management;
- knowledge in one or more of the following fields: administrative law, international law, accounting and finance, territorial marketing.

Judgment Autonomy.
The richness and variety of the fields of application of linguistic learning, the awareness of the genesis and development of languages, attention to the knowledge of updated computer, bibliographic, and critical tools, and the habit of comparing traditions and cultures will develop in the graduate the flexibility and critical spirit adequate to allow them to integrate into different professional contexts; to overcome, with awareness regarding methodology and with thinking autonomy, issues related to acquired competencies, and to develop updating and adaptation capabilities according to the needs of the professional activity. Moreover, it is considered that the study of some disciplines in geographical and historical, sociological, philosophical, and pedagogical areas will favor reflection on social, scientific, or ethical issues connected to the specific profile. The subjects in economic and legal areas will contribute to forming the student in areas particularly susceptible to application and deepening. The ability to express critical judgments will be verified not only in the exam setting, but also and especially in the preparation work and during the discussion of the final exam.

Learning Ability.
The graduate will be able to use Italian and the studied foreign languages by applying critical, bibliographic, and cultural tools with confidence; to move within different linguistic and cultural contexts with competence, effectiveness, and critical autonomy; to acquire operational skills in public, business, mediation, and teaching contexts. Furthermore, they will develop an aptitude and preparation for research, a habit of deepening practical and theoretical issues, and competencies potentially usable both for continuing studies within a two-year program and for entering the workforce. The teaching methods, as well as the use of laboratories and internships at Italian and foreign institutions and companies, guarantee the development of autonomy in learning. The final exam will be structured to verify and confirm the specific competencies acquired, thinking autonomy, and the ability to organize research according to rigorous parameters and with clarity in techniques and objectives. Together with exam and in-course assessments, the final exam will allow the verification of learning abilities.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
LANGUAGE AREA I/Graduates of the Course will be able to:
- use Italian with precision, sectoral languages, and available registers for producing texts tailored to different needs (regulatory, expository, argumentative, descriptive, narrative);
- apply the linguistic skills acquired in the two main study languages in different communication contexts and in producing texts with different linguistic registers;
- translate texts, including those written in sectoral languages, from Italian to the two main study languages and vice versa.

LITERARY AREA I/Graduates of the Course will be able to:
- analyze, critically comment on, and evaluate texts written in Italian and the two study languages;
- discuss orally or argue in written reports on cultural issues and related to the history, meaning, function, and reception of literary texts;
- compare literary texts at the thematic or formal level.

SOCIOECONOMIC, HISTORICAL-PHILOSOPHICAL, ARTISTIC AREA I/Graduates of the Course will be able to:
- analyze, deepen (even autonomously), and discuss issues of a historical, political, social, or philosophical nature;
- independently retrieve, consult, and organize a critical bibliography on a specific topic.

TRAINING, ECONOMICS, LAW, INFORMATICS AREA I/Graduates of the Course will be able to apply the acquired knowledge in a work context and address and solve specific complex problems using appropriate methodological approaches. In particular, depending on the professionalizing disciplines included in the study plan, they will be able to:
- manage the accounting of a company;
- work in contexts characterized by complex intercultural and social dynamics;
- possess management and organizational skills in cultural, training, and business environments.

Additionally, based on the chosen Career Orientation Laboratories, graduates will be able to:
- conduct data analysis;
- navigate between different theoretical and methodological approaches to specialized translation;
- use databases and translation software.

Communication Skills.

These objectives are guaranteed by the study of specific linguistic subjects and the communicative teaching and learning methodologies provided by the Course.
Systematic practical training related to the learning of modern foreign languages (facilitated by the presence of CEL staff at the university), extensive use of seminar activities, group work for project realization or report writing (also in dedicated spaces such as the department's Campus Lab), familiarize the student with secure and well-structured presentation and exercise them in constructive comparison between ideas, competencies, and goals. - Carry out mediation activities between people of different languages and cultures in migration and multilingual contexts.
- Plan, coordinate, and implement initiatives and activities aimed at valorizing and disseminating Italian artistic and cultural heritage.
- Carry out Italian language teaching for non-native speakers in private entities and institutions in Italy and in public and private institutions abroad.
Linguistic and cultural mediator in economic and commercial contexts
- Establish and manage commercial contacts at national and international levels.
- Provide qualified linguistic and cultural support to companies operating internationally.
- Mediate between languages, both in written and oral form, in relation to texts and speeches of various types and different communication registers.
Additional information.
https://lingue-comunicazione.unisi.it/
www.unisi.it Specific educational objectives description.
The Course is oriented towards insertion in the fields of cultural services, cultural tourism, journalism, and publishing, as well as responding to the needs of industry, business, the tertiary sector, and linguistic and cultural mediation in multietnic and multicultural contexts. Consistent with the qualifying educational objectives of the L-11 degree class, the Course has a structure where the common core of all linguistic teachings aims to provide knowledge and competencies, theories, interpretive models, research and action methodologies capable of integrating with those offered by other humanities (literature, history, philosophy, socio-economic disciplines) concerned with the study of linguistic phenomena and promoting competencies useful for scientifically legitimate interventions in this field.
The objectives are:
1) to foster communication between nations, cultures, and ethnicities through the training of graduates with excellent linguistic-communicative abilities and a critical understanding of Italian history and culture and modern civilizations;
2) to enable those who, after graduation, intend to pursue professions requiring the application of linguistic and glottodidactic competencies, to possess interdisciplinary general knowledge and specific sectoral knowledge related to the different contexts in which they are exercised (institutions, social services, companies, cooperatives, businesses, public administration, mediation and Italian language teaching contexts, etc.), as well as to master a wide repertoire of technical-operational tools necessary for designing and implementing projects and interventions in these areas, establishing relationships with the reference context, and creating synergies between the different structures and professional profiles involved.
To achieve these objectives, the course is structured into two curricula:
- the first curriculum is primarily oriented towards acquiring linguistic and disciplinary competencies in the field of intercultural mediation;
- the second curriculum aims to provide competencies useful for immediate entry into the job market, particularly within the fabric of small and medium-sized enterprises.
To facilitate a conscious choice of the study path and consequently promote regular academic progress, the two curricula share the same educational offer in the first year of the course; students will therefore choose the curriculum at the time of enrollment in the second year.
Graduates of both curricula will possess solid and articulated linguistic-pragmatic competencies in two foreign languages (one of which is English, considered the international lingua franca); basic theoretical competencies in the study of Glottology and general linguistics and Philology and historical linguistics, which will provide the necessary theoretical, historical, and methodological support for mastering the study languages; as well as excellent knowledge of the structures and parallel competencies in spoken and written Italian (LINGUISTIC AREA, scientific-disciplinary sectors L-LIN/01, L-LIN/04, L-LIN/07, L-LIN/12, L-LIN/14, L-LIN/21, L-OR/21, L-FIL-LET/09, L-FIL-LET/12, L-FIL-LET/15).
Linguistic disciplines are associated with foreign, Italian, and comparative literature (LITERARY AREA, scientific-disciplinary sectors L-FIL-LET/11, L-FIL-LET/14, L-LIN/05, L-LIN/06, L-LIN/10, L-LIN/13, L-LIN/21, L-OR/21), considered essential for the student to develop a detailed critical view of Italian literary-cultural heritage and the main modern and contemporary civilizations, with particular but not exclusive reference to the two chosen foreign languages; and to be able to move and mediate between different socio-cultural contexts: Italian, European, extra-European. Foreign literature and cultures are allocated a larger number of CFU in the intercultural mediation curriculum, and a more limited space in the business-oriented curriculum.
In both curricula, to allow each student sufficient autonomy in designing their educational path, the structure of basic and characteristic disciplines has been limited to mandatory subjects (or with rigid choice options, such as the second language of study), leaving ample space for related and integrative subjects, which are organized into coherent choice groups by educational areas (LINGUISTIC-PHILOLOGICAL; SOCIOECONOMIC; CULTURAL AND ARTISTIC; LEGAL; PSYCHOPEDAGOGICAL) and functional to the specific educational objectives and planned professional outcomes for each curriculum. In this context, the general mastery of linguistic and cultural competencies is reinforced by specific professionalizing or cultural and linguistic deepening teachings, also on specific areas (such as extra-European countries): in one curriculum, more space is given to disciplines of the first group (with a central role reserved for economic and business organization sectors), while the other offers a wider choice in disciplines of the second group.
The students' professional preparation is also supported by activities carried out in language, computer, professional writing laboratories, and other career orientation activities. Additionally, the seminar format of some teachings enables graduates to possess a consolidated method of autonomous learning, encouraged also through continuous in-course tutoring. Finally, contact with the world of work is guaranteed through the mandatory professional internship (which can be carried out both in Italy and abroad). In this way, Course graduates achieve excellent capabilities in linguistic reception, production, and interaction.
The endpoint of the educational path is the final project, which must provide a concrete demonstration of the acquired competencies and, at the same time, fully express the individual educational project of each student. Depending on the chosen curriculum, competencies acquired in curricular disciplines and in the internship, and especially the student's individual inclination towards a specific professional field or further studies, the final project may consist of a translation work, linguistic and/or philological analysis, research (even limited) and/or planning within the critical-literary, sociological, historical-philosophical, cultural and environmental heritage fields.

Final exam characteristics The final exam consists of writing a report on a topic assigned by a Department lecturer (supervisor) or describing activities carried out during the training internship. The objective is to verify the student's analytical and synthesis abilities regarding the technical description of work done independently. In particular, for students completing the internship at a company or external organization, the final exam consists of writing a technical report on the activities performed. In this case, the supervisor is typically the university internship tutor.
Required knowledge for access To be admitted to the Bachelor's program, one must hold a secondary school diploma or another foreign degree recognized as equivalent. English language knowledge at least at A2/2 level is also required.
Basic knowledge of mathematics and physics is also required, typically acquired by the end of secondary school. More specifically, for mathematics, reference can be made to the official document approved in 2006 by the joint Commission of the Italian Mathematical Union and the Conference of Engineering Deans, which identifies the following main prerequisites:
Algebra; operations, powers, approximation; numerical calculation Progressions, exponentials, logarithms Elements of Trigonometry Elements of Euclidean Geometry, spatial geometry Elements of Analytical Geometry Elementary Logic For physics, in addition to the prerequisites already indicated for mathematics, the prerequisites, approximately, are:
Concept of physical quantity, measurements and errors Vectors Uniform linear motion, uniformly accelerated motion, uniform circular motion Mass and density Basic logical reasoning and verbal comprehension skills are also required.
Access knowledge is verified through an entrance test, which aims to assess the student's personal preparation in mathematics, physics, and logical reasoning and verbal comprehension abilities. If the verification is not positive, additional mandatory educational obligations must be fulfilled during the first year of the program.
Awarded degree.
Bachelor's degree in Computer Engineering and Information Engineering Teaching method Conventional Knowledge and understanding.
Fundamental scientific and methodological aspects At the end of studies, the graduate has acquired knowledge and understanding of the fundamental methodological aspects that characterize physical-mathematical sciences and computer science.
Acquisition of knowledge and understanding is verified through written and/or oral exams.
Information engineering At the end of studies, the graduate has acquired knowledge and understanding of the fundamental methodological aspects of the main disciplines of information engineering, electrical engineering, electronics, electrical communications, dynamic systems, software programming and design.
Acquisition of knowledge and understanding is verified through written and/or oral exams.
Electronics At the end of studies, the graduate has acquired knowledge and understanding of reference models, methods, and technologies for the design of electronic and measurement systems.
Acquisition of knowledge and understanding is verified through written and/or oral exams.
Systems and automation At the end of studies, the graduate has acquired knowledge and understanding of reference models, methods, and technologies for the design of automation and robotic systems.
Acquisition of knowledge and understanding is verified through written and/or oral exams.
Computer systems At the end of studies, the graduate has acquired knowledge and understanding of the methodologies and technologies specific to information processing systems. In particular, they know and are able to understand the design criteria for computer architectures, operating systems, databases, and computer networks.
Acquisition of knowledge and understanding is verified through written and/or oral exams.
Telecommunications At the end of studies, the graduate has acquired knowledge and understanding of methodologies and technologies for the design of telecommunications systems, electromagnetic fields, propagation, and signal processing.
Acquisition of knowledge and understanding is verified through written and/or oral exams.
Context knowledge and final exam At the end of studies, the graduate has acquired knowledge and understanding of key aspects of business organization, in relation to their application to solving engineering problems; knowledge of business realities in the information engineering sector and their specific characteristics and issues; knowledge of the English language.
Verification is primarily represented by the internship and the final exam, which allows evaluation of the knowledge and skills acquired by the student, preferably in a business context.

Judgment Autonomy.
The graduate in Computer Engineering and Information Engineering must be able to make quantitative assessments based on acquired methodological and technical knowledge: they must be able to critically analyze data and measurements; they must be able to evaluate the approximation errors with which engineering problems are modeled, and therefore must be able to critically analyze the results derived from simulations and specific implementations.
In detail, the graduate is able to identify, formulate, and solve problems related to the design, management, and adaptation of functionalities of systems and applications in the field of information engineering;
is able to carry out testing, conduct experimental trials, evaluate the performance of automatic, computer, electronic, and telecommunications systems, and determine their compliance with design specifications by interpreting the results obtained;
is able to focus on the essential contributions of technical relations presented or prepared by interlocutors, and to extract from them the qualifying and innovative aspects; is able to consult technical/scientific literature and proceed to formulate an independent judgment on the relevance and implications of the described technological solutions;
is able to locate and consult, also via web, the main bibliographic sources, emerging national or international standardization proposals, and regulations concerning the certification of products and systems of industrial interest.
Judgment autonomy is developed through the continuous application of theoretical aspects provided in all courses, especially during the internship period when the student faces problems to be addressed autonomously in a real context and during project development and examination report activities. The degree of achieved judgment autonomy will be assessed based on results obtained in such tests, particularly within the final examination.
Learning Ability.
The graduate in Computer Engineering and Information Engineering is able to stay updated on methods, techniques, and tools oriented towards requirements analysis, modeling and design, testing and fine-tuning, and performance optimization of systems and applications in the field of Information Engineering;
is able to follow the evolution of technologies and choose paths for updating their own skills;
is able to undertake advanced studies in any sector of Information Engineering with a high degree of autonomy.
Learning abilities are achieved through the inclusion in the study plan of basic methodological and broad-spectrum engineering courses.
The level of learning ability will be verified primarily in the project activities provided in exams and during the internship and final examination.
Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Scientific and Methodological Foundations At the end of studies, the graduate is able to formalize engineering problems using the languages of mathematics and physics; design and implement algorithms using major programming languages.
The degree of acquisition of the above abilities is verified in passing exams through the resolution of exercises and problems assigned during written, oral, and/or practical tests.
Information Engineering At the end of studies, the graduate is able to analyze and design specific systems and subsystems of information engineering; use the main technologies of information engineering.
The degree of acquisition of the above abilities is verified in passing exams through the resolution of exercises and problems assigned during written, oral, and/or practical tests.
Electronics At the end of studies, the graduate is able to analyze and design electrical, electronic, and measurement systems; analyze and design systems for efficient energy conversion.
The degree of acquisition of the above abilities is verified in passing exams through the resolution of exercises and problems assigned during written, oral, and/or practical tests.
Systems and Automation At the end of studies, the graduate is able to analyze and design digital control systems, automation systems, and robotic systems.
The degree of acquisition of the above abilities is verified in passing exams through the resolution of exercises and problems assigned during written, oral, and/or practical tests.
Computer Systems At the end of studies, the graduate is able to analyze and design computer architectures; design and manage databases, web applications, computer networks, and operating systems.
The degree of acquisition of the above abilities is verified in passing exams through the resolution of exercises and problems assigned during written, oral, and/or practical tests.
Telecommunications At the end of studies, the graduate is able to analyze and design systems for multimedia signal processing and Internet of Things systems; understand issues related to the design of next-generation telecommunications systems; model electromagnetic wave propagation; apply high-frequency circuit design techniques.
The degree of acquisition of the above abilities is verified in passing exams through the resolution of exercises and problems assigned during written, oral, and/or practical tests.
Contextual Knowledge and Final Examination At the end of studies, the graduate is able to address engineering problems in real application contexts; use English, with specific reference to the scientific and technological field, to understand and describe engineering problems.
Verification is primarily represented by the internship and final examination, conducted also at company sites, which allow evaluating, through the presentation and discussion of a theoretical/application-oriented report, the ability to apply the knowledge acquired by the student.

Communication skills.
The graduate in Computer Engineering and Information Engineering is able to communicate efficiently and effectively in English, both in written and oral form, regarding technical issues, ideas, solutions, and information to both specialist and non-specialist interlocutors;
is able to draft technical reports on activities carried out and to present the key results concisely in collegial discussions;
is able to successfully integrate into teams managing, designing, testing, and verifying the performance of systems and processes related to the chosen application field.
The achievement of the above results is particularly supported by:
for point 1, the activity related to foreign language knowledge, verified by a specific test;
for point 2, the internship activity and preparation for the final exam, and all training activities that require, during evaluation, the presentation of a report by the student to pass credit-bearing exams;
for point 3, all engineering-oriented courses that require group projects to pass credit-bearing exams, and, within additional training activities, the internship activity.
The verification of achieved communication skills will be conducted during oral exams, in project reports, and in the preparation of the final thesis.
Employment and professional prospects for graduates.
Computer Engineer in the field of information engineering. The main professional prospects consist, besides the exercise of free profession, in medium-high level positions in technical fields within companies and organizations requiring cross-functional skills in the field of information engineering.
Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIAN Associated competencies for the role.
Computer Engineer in the field of information engineering The study program allows the acquisition of basic and methodological competencies characterizing the various sectors of information engineering. In particular, the graduate in Computer Engineering and Information Engineering possesses competencies related to electronics, telecommunications, and signal processing, modeling and control of dynamic systems, and programming and management of software projects. Moreover, depending on the chosen areas of specialization, possesses specific competencies in the fields of information systems, electronic systems, robotics and industrial automation, telecommunications systems, electromagnetic fields, and signal propagation.
Description of admission tests.
The Faculty of Engineering requires new enrollees to take an entrance test that has only orientation purposes and is non-selective, to verify if the initial preparation level is adequate to undertake the chosen path. The Faculty uses the test prepared by the Interuniversity Center for Access to Engineering and Architecture Schools (CISIA, www.cisiaonline.it), which is used by almost all Italian engineering faculties and is held everywhere on the same day and with the same procedures.
The results of the entrance test are used to verify the existence of educational deficits in the student's preparation. In case of unsatisfactory test results, the Faculty may assign additional educational obligations (OFA) to the student, while simultaneously establishing the modalities for their fulfillment. Even in the case of OFA assignment, the student may still enroll and attend classes regularly.
Workplace function.
Computer Engineer in the field of information engineering The graduate in Computer Engineering and Information Engineering naturally finds placement within companies and public and private organizations where methodologies and technologies for information processing play a key role. In particular, their tasks may involve the analysis, development, and management of information and information systems; communication systems; electronic systems at both software and hardware levels; robotic and industrial automation systems.
Additional information.
http://www.unisi.it/dipartimenti/dipartimento-ingegneria-dell%E2%80%99informazione-e-scienze-matematiche Specific educational objectives description.
The bachelor's degree program in Computer Engineering and Information Engineering aims to provide broad methodological and technical competencies in the field of information engineering, with a predominant focus on computer engineering, to create a professional figure with a high degree of flexibility and adaptability to market demands. Alongside a solid basic preparation in mathematics and physics, necessary to provide the scientific tools and methodologies for analyzing and formalizing engineering problems, there is an in-depth study of cross-cutting themes in the field of information engineering, such as automation, electronics, computer science, and telecommunications. The offer is completed by specialized courses, according to differentiated paths, which allow for characterizing the acquired competencies by deepening technical and application solutions in specific areas of information engineering.
The training path is structured in the following learning areas.
Scientific and methodological foundations The training path includes an in-depth study of the foundations of mathematics, physics, numerical calculus, and probability theory. Additionally, cross-cutting computer science competencies are provided in the fields of algorithm analysis, information representation, and programming.
Information engineering The training path provides a common base of knowledge in the field of Information Engineering regarding electrical engineering and electronics, electrical communications, modeling and control of dynamic systems, advanced programming, and software design.
Electronics In this area, specific knowledge is provided regarding methodologies and instrumentation for analysis and design of electrical and electronic systems and systems for energy conversion.
Systems and automation This learning area allows the student to deepen techniques for designing digital control systems, measurement technologies typical of automation systems, modeling and implementation of robotic systems.
Information systems This learning area allows the student to deepen aspects specific to information processing systems with reference to theoretical and practical problems of operating systems, computer architectures, database design and management, and computer networks.
Telecommunications In this learning area, competencies are acquired regarding the design of systems for transmitting and processing multimedia signals, remote sensing, electromagnetic fields and signal propagation, and electromagnetic compatibility.
Context knowledge and final thesis The student's preparation is completed by knowledge of economics and business organization, and technical-practical competencies that can be acquired through internships or traineeships at sector organizations or companies. Additionally, since knowledge of English is now indispensable for the engineer's role, it is a training objective for all graduates to be able to write and speak in English, with particular reference to scientific and technological topics.

Judgment autonomy.
The graduate in Management Engineering must be able to make quantitative assessments based on the acquired methodological and technical knowledge, integrating them with subjective and relational aspects. The graduate must have developed critical and analytical skills to formulate and support their viewpoint based on analytical/quantitative elements. A Management Engineering graduate who achieves good judgment maturity will be able to address an engineering problem not only from a purely technical perspective, but also from an economic, financial, ethical, cultural, and relational standpoint.
This judgment autonomy will be developed through the application of theoretical and methodological aspects in individual courses and will be assessed within the written, oral and/or practical examinations of the planned educational activities.

Learning capacity.
The graduate in Management Engineering must be able to update their knowledge and integrate it with knowledge from different and sometimes heterogeneous methodological and scientific fields. Facing a complex problem, such as optimizing/re-engineering a production process, analyzing a financial situation, or evaluating a company's performance from an economic or production perspective, the management engineer must know which methodologies to draw upon and how to correctly integrate information, taking into account, among other things, data imperfections, modeling limitations, and the characteristics of available computer tools. More generally, the management engineer must have acquired the ability to critically evaluate the relevance and appropriateness of a solution in the current situation. The learning capacities necessary for continuing studies in higher-level courses are provided through the inclusion in the study plan of basic methodological courses in mathematics, physics, and engineering.

The level of learning capacity will be verified particularly in the project activities provided in exams and during the internship and final thesis.

Ability to apply knowledge and understanding.
Scientific and methodological foundations At the end of studies, the graduate is able to analyze, model, and formalize engineering-management problems using mathematical language, applying and adapting specific methods and algorithms.
The level of acquisition of the above abilities is verified in passing exams through the resolution of exercises and problems assigned during written, oral and/or practical examinations.

Economic and management engineering At the end of studies, the graduate has acquired specific competencies that enable them to analyze and apply solutions in business contexts, particularly regarding business organization and management, and management control.
The level of acquisition of the above abilities is verified in passing exams through the resolution of exercises and problems assigned during written, oral and/or practical examinations.

Information engineering At the end of studies, the graduate is able to analyze and manage specific systems and subsystems of information engineering and use some technologies specific to this area. The level of acquisition of the above abilities is verified in passing exams through the resolution of exercises and problems assigned during written, oral and/or practical examinations.

Context knowledge and final thesis At the end of studies, the graduate is able to address engineering-management problems and tackle them in real application contexts; use English, with specific reference to the scientific and technological field, to work on specific problems in an international work environment.
Verification is represented by the internship and final thesis, carried out also at business realities, which allow evaluating, through the presentation and discussion of a theoretical/application elaboration, the ability to apply the knowledge acquired by the student.

Information technology management At the end of studies, the graduate is able to analyze and manage specific systems and subsystems of information engineering within the context of industrial control, electronic technologies, and computer networks. They are also able to use the main technologies specific to this area. The level of acquisition of the above abilities is verified in passing exams through the resolution of exercises and problems assigned during written, oral and/or practical examinations.

Business process management At the end of studies, the graduate is able to apply methodologies specific to the analysis and modeling of business processes in real contexts that involve the management of plants or services; they are able to understand operational and management organizational processes in real contexts. The level of acquisition of the above abilities is verified in passing exams through the resolution of exercises and problems assigned during written, oral and/or practical examinations.
