UNIVERSITY: University of Siena
COURSE: [IE002] MANAGEMENT ENGINEERING
SECTION: Communication skills
URL: https://unisi.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10235

Communication skills.
The graduate in Management Engineering must be able to communicate their results to a wide range of people and professional figures, generally not strictly related to their professional area. Indeed, one of the defining characteristics of the management engineer is the ability to manage and coordinate various actors and functions, both technical and managerial. The communication style of the management engineer must balance rigor, clarity, and relevance for the interlocutor in every circumstance. The management engineer must be able to read a technical article and write a report rigorously, even in English, but must also be able to explain and argue their positions to professionals very different from their own, as occurs in project coordination. Communication skills are acquired gradually as all teachings include an oral exam and often require group work. The ability to communicate in English is provided at B1 level and stimulated by the use of technical texts in English.
The verification of achieved communication skills will be carried out during oral exams, in project reports, and in the preparation of the final thesis.
Expected career and professional opportunities for graduates.
Management engineer The main career opportunities are in companies and organizations operating in various sectors, particularly service companies (such as banks and financial institutions), utilities (energy operators), manufacturing (for example, the fashion industry), process industries (for example, pharmaceutical companies), providers of solutions and services related to information technology, and public administration bodies. These areas are of particular interest to the local business territory, predominantly service-oriented and composed of many medium and small enterprises, for which a rational management of production and information processes is critically important for achieving business objectives.
Official language(s) of teaching and assessment.
ITALIAN Associated competencies for the role.
Management engineer The Study Course allows the acquisition of basic and methodological competencies for the implementation and management of systems and services using information technologies and for the optimal management of operational and decision-making processes. To this end, the management engineer relies on distinctive knowledge and the use of tools to analyze, model, and formulate management problems, and to understand and address the main issues related to information technologies, management, and the improvement of management, organizational, and process models. The organization of the study course also provides specific competencies, such as strategic planning for manufacturing and service companies, business organization and management, cost analysis, industrial accounting and analytical accounting, management control, management of companies in regulated sectors, project planning and management, optimization and simulation of production factors and processes, organizational and productivity improvement through "lean production," introduction, management, and implementation of digital information and communication technologies, management of energy and environmental technologies and systems, and corporate sustainability.
Description of admission tests.
The Faculty of Engineering requires new enrollees to take an entrance test that has only orientation purposes and is non-selective, to verify if the initial preparation level is adequate to undertake the chosen path. The Faculty uses the test prepared by the Interuniversity Center for Access to Engineering and Architecture Schools (CISIA, www.cisiaonline.it), which is used by almost all Italian engineering faculties and is held everywhere on the same day and with the same procedures.
The results of the entrance test are used to verify the existence of educational deficits in the student's preparation. In case of unsatisfactory test results, the Faculty may assign additional educational obligations (OFA) to the student, while simultaneously establishing the modalities for their fulfillment. Even in the case of OFA assignment, the student can still enroll and attend classes regularly.
Work context function.
Management engineer The graduate in Management Engineering finds their placement in production and service companies and in public administration where analysis and strategic planning of technical-operational activities and coordination characterized by extensive use of information technologies are required. In such contexts, the management engineer can cover a wide range of functions related to business management, such as: management of ICT technologies, tools, and digital technologies; management and support of industrial automation; introduction and management of information systems; analysis and mapping of main organizational, operational, and management processes; development and use of appropriate models and tools for collecting and analyzing data to support decisions and solve organizational and management problems; configuration of planning and control systems for technical-operational and financial activities; evaluation and design of company investments, including economic, financial, organizational, and technical aspects; strategic planning and management control; production and logistics planning and management; project management; environmental services management; regulatory management, technical, and tariff management of local public services.
Additional information.
http://www.unisi.it/dipartimenti/dipartimento-ingegneria-dell%E2%80%99informazione-e-scienze-matematiche Specific learning objectives description.
The Management Engineering degree course aims to provide solid methodological, modeling, and technological knowledge. The management engineer must be an engineer of change and innovation, capable of addressing management and organizational problems of business systems with an interdisciplinary approach and vision. The learning objectives are pursued through a teaching offer where, alongside a wide range of basic courses in disciplines common to all engineering bachelor's degrees (oriented to provide methodological preparation for analyzing, modeling, and formulating problems), there is ample space for disciplines in the area of management engineering and those of other engineering fields of information engineering. The training path is then completed in one of the following domains: a) management of information technologies; b) management of business processes.
The training path is structured in the following learning areas.
Basic and methodological sciences The training path includes the study of the fundamentals of mathematical analysis, linear algebra, physics, computer science, statistics, and main topics of operations research. These fundamentals provide the tools and competencies necessary for other learning areas.
Information engineering The training path includes acquiring a common base of knowledge in the field of Information Engineering regarding electrical engineering, computer science, data processing and management, dynamic systems, and automation.
Economic-management engineering This learning area is designed to provide fundamental knowledge of organizational systems, economic analysis, and operational and decision-making processes. In particular, the proposed training path aims at acquiring specific competencies of the management engineer, such as business organization and management, management control, project planning and management.
Additionally, the student will choose to acquire specific preparation in the following domains:
a) management of information technologies: disciplines characterizing information engineering (electronics, telecommunications, automation, computer science) are introduced and consolidated.
b) management of business processes: disciplines of industrial engineering (applied mechanics, industrial plants, and sustainable technologies for energy and environment) are introduced and the area of management engineering is consolidated (lean management and business management).
Context knowledge and final exam The student's preparation is completed by courses reflecting the peculiarities of competencies most required by the local territory, combining technical-scientific skills with critical thinking, relational, and expressive abilities. The training project is complemented by the acquisition of technical-practical skills through internships or traineeships at local entities or companies. Moreover, since knowledge of English is now indispensable for the engineer's role, it is a learning objective for all graduates to write and speak English, with particular reference to the language used in scientific and technological contexts.
To achieve the stated objectives, the course provides a training path characterized as follows:
In the first year of the course, basic teachings in the areas of mathematical sciences, physics, computer science, and economics are provided. The second and third years of the course include the study of engineering disciplines with fundamental content of information engineering disciplines (computer science, automation, electrical engineering), and essential elements of economic and organizational analysis (financial statements and management control) and decision models (operations research, optimization, simulation, and statistics). In characterizing their training plan, the student can choose to complete their preparation in the following domains:
a) management of information technologies: disciplines characterizing information engineering are introduced and consolidated. In particular, the basics of electronic systems and telecommunications are acquired, and knowledge of control systems and computer networks is deepened.
b) management of business processes: disciplines of industrial engineering are introduced and the area of management engineering is consolidated. In industrial engineering, principles of industrial plants, mechanical systems, and technologies for energy and environment are introduced, with references to principles of corporate sustainability and circular economy. In the management area, aspects related to business management through processes and via "lean management" (lean management) are addressed.

BACHELOR'S DEGREE IN NURSING Delivery mode Conventional Knowledge and understanding.
Basic disciplines area Graduates in Nursing who have successfully completed the program will be able to:
1. describe, interpret and infer implications regarding the qualitative and quantitative bases of biological, pathophysiological and pathological phenomena.
2. describe and interpret the molecular, morphological and functional bases of vital, physiological and pathological processes.
3. describe, interpret and discuss the fundamental principles of hygiene, health promotion and disease prevention.
4. describe, interpret and infer implications and meanings regarding the basic concepts of human sciences applied to professional contexts.
Learning objectives will be achieved through ex-cathedra, seminar and interactive teaching tools. Assessment will be conducted through in-course tests, suitability evaluations and final exams.
Professional disciplines area Graduates in Nursing who have successfully completed the program must have acquired the following knowledge and understanding abilities:
1. Define, describe, interpret, distinguish and infer implications, relationships and meanings regarding the main conceptual models and theories of nursing care.
2. Describe, interpret and infer implications, relevance, relationships and meanings regarding technical-practical methodologies for diagnosing, planning, organizing, implementing and evaluating general nursing care.
3. Describe and discuss current knowledge in pharmacology, medicine and surgery, general and specialized, maternal-child health, mental health, and emergency-urgent areas.
4. Describe, interpret and infer implications, relevance, relationships and meanings regarding nursing disciplines applied to general and specialized medical and surgical areas, chronicity and disability both in hospital and community settings.
5. Describe, interpret and infer implications, relevance, relationships and meanings regarding nursing disciplines applied to maternal-child health, mental health, and emergency-urgent areas.
6. Define, describe, interpret, distinguish and infer implications, relationships and meanings regarding relational principles and supportive methodologies applied to individual professional contexts.
7. Describe and discuss operational methodologies related to continuity of care in both hospital and territorial contexts.
8. Define, describe, interpret, distinguish and infer implications, relationships and meanings regarding bioethical, deontological, care safety, legal and medical-legal principles applied to professional contexts.
Learning objectives will be achieved through ex-cathedra, seminar and interactive teaching tools, as well as through demonstrations and laboratory simulations. Assessment will be conducted through in-course tests, suitability evaluations and final exams.
Integrated disciplines area Graduates in Nursing who have successfully completed the program must have acquired the following knowledge and understanding abilities:
1. Describe, interpret and infer implications regarding the fundamental principles of management, organization and health economics.
2. Describe and discuss knowledge related to biomedical and nursing research, as well as the use of information systems useful for managing health information systems, with particular reference to methodologies for acquiring scientific information for one's own training and updating.
Learning objectives will be achieved through ex-cathedra, seminar and interactive teaching tools. Assessment will be conducted through in-course tests, suitability evaluations and final exams.
General area At the end of studies, the graduate will have acquired knowledge and understanding abilities related to preventive, curative, palliative and rehabilitative nursing care, in technical, relational and educational aspects:
- disease prevention
- care for sick and disabled people of all ages
- health education Critical judgment.
Nursing graduates will develop critical analysis abilities enabling them to act autonomously, assuming responsibility for choices and judgments in relation to different situations and priorities. In this sense:
1. recognize the main human reactions and responses to illness and suffering, as well as behavioral differences related to cultural belonging
2. evaluate clinical, psychological and socio-cultural manifestations connected to the progression of major diseases, treatment, lifestyle habits, reactions to illness, hospitalization, home care, and care interventions
3. monitor critical situations related to clinical, even psychological, worsening of the person being cared for, promptly activating other professionals
4. based on the evaluation of the person being cared for and in accordance with the profile of supporting staff, assign appropriate care activities to them and evaluate results
5. regarding the management function:
5a. identify critical elements in the care setting regarding safety conditions for the person being cared for and healthcare workers
5b. be able to identify and promote elements of quality, efficiency and effectiveness of care services in the care setting
6. based on the identification of training needs, be able to design and deliver training programs, evaluating results
7. regarding the research function:
7a. be able to conduct bibliographic research on major biomedical databases and critically read scientific articles, applying results based on the best available evidence to improve care quality
7b. carry out research projects independently or in collaboration with other professionals.
8. regarding the consulting function, provide technical/professional advice.
Learning objectives will be achieved through interactive teaching tools and clinical internships at Faculty and Convened Healthcare Companies facilities. Assessment will be conducted through in-course tests, suitability evaluations and final exams in theoretical and practical teaching contexts, as well as clinical internships.
Learning abilities.
Graduates in Nursing:
1. will develop critical thinking abilities enabling them to select training opportunities congruent with their own training needs
2. will identify training and self-training strategies for their professional growth
3. will independently organize their continuous training, according to correct metacognitive strategies.
Learning objectives will be achieved through ex-cathedra, seminar, interactive teaching tools and clinical internships at Faculty and Convened Healthcare Companies facilities. Acquired learning abilities will be assessed through in-course evaluations based on structured observation methods during clinical and tutorial activities.

4. identify, distinguish and recognize the main reactions of the person to illness, suffering, hospitalization, respecting behavioral differences related to cultural belonging
5. plan, design, manage and evaluate health promotion and education interventions for healthy individuals and groups

8. critically apply general bioethical, deontological, legal and medical-legal principles, as well as principles related to clinical safety, to individual clinical cases in the context of professional activities.
9. independently perform consulting functions providing technical/professional advice.
Learning objectives will be achieved through ex-cathedra, seminar, interactive and laboratory teaching tools, as well as clinical internships. Assessment will be conducted through in-course tests, suitability evaluations and final exams, particularly the final internship exam is designed to measure the achievement of expected competencies through specific tests for each learning area: cognitive, psychomotor and affective.

3. design and implement nursing research protocols aimed at producing new knowledge
4. use and manage information systems of hospital and territorial healthcare services
5. guide the training of supporting staff; independently plan and organize student internships
6. apply principles of health organization to the delivery of nursing care
Learning objectives will be achieved through ex-cathedra, seminar, interactive and laboratory teaching tools, as well as clinical internships. Assessment will be conducted through in-course tests, suitability evaluations and final exams, particularly the final internship exam is designed to measure the achievement of expected competencies through specific tests for each learning area: cognitive, psychomotor and affective.

http://www.unisi.it/dipartimenti/dipartimento-scienze-mediche-chirurgiche-e-neuroscienze Specific training objectives description.
Graduates in Nursing are the health professionals to whom the attributions provided for by the Ministerial Decree of the Ministry of Health n. 739 of 14/9/94, and subsequent modifications and additions, as well as the specific Code of Ethics, apply. Graduates will be responsible for general preventive, curative, palliative and rehabilitative nursing care of a technical, relational and educational nature; their functions will relate to prevention and health education, care, therapeutic education, management, training, research and consultation. Nursing graduates will promote health culture in the community, design and implement, in collaboration with other professional figures, training and educational interventions for the person and family, independently carry out activities directed at prevention, care and safeguarding of individual and collective health using goal-oriented planning methodologies for care in the developmental, adult and geriatric age groups.
Regarding the specific training objectives of the course, nursing graduates will be able to: participate in identifying health needs of the person and community; identify nursing care needs of the person and community and formulate related objectives; plan, manage and evaluate nursing care interventions, utilizing supporting staff where necessary; ensure correct application of diagnostic-therapeutic prescriptions. They will carry out self-training activities and training for students, supporting staff and new hires; develop research activities aimed at producing new knowledge for continuous improvement of care; participate in interdisciplinary work groups for citizen care; provide consultation for the development of care services.
Based on the described specific training objectives, the training path is structured over 3 years of study comprising 6 semesters, totaling 180 CFU, of which 65 must be acquired through training activities aimed at developing specific professional abilities (internship). To achieve the specific course objectives, Nursing graduates will be equipped with adequate theoretical and theoretical/practical preparation in three disciplinary areas focused on the profession's specificity:
1. Basic disciplines area, oriented towards understanding the most relevant elements underlying physiological and pathological processes to which preventive, therapeutic, rehabilitative and palliative interventions are directed, as well as maximum integration with other professions. Training activities include basic biomedical disciplines (BIO/10 Biochemistry, BIO/13 Biology and Fundamentals of Genetics, BIO/16 Anatomy and Elements of Histology, BIO/09 Physiology and Food Sciences, MED/04 General Pathology and Pathophysiology, MED/07 General and Clinical Microbiology and MED/08 Pathological Anatomy) and basic humanistic disciplines (M-DEA/01 Demography and Ethnoanthropology, M-PSI/01 General Psychology, SPS/07 Health Sociology). Particular attention is given to Preventive Sciences and Health Services (MED/44 Occupational Medicine and MED/42 Health Promotion and Hygiene).
2. Professional disciplines area, oriented towards acquiring specific knowledge in disciplines characterizing professional training. Includes disciplines in the strict sense (MED/45 General Nursing and Nursing Theory, Clinical Nursing and Applied Nursing, Relational and Community Nursing, Pediatric Nursing, MED/47 Obstetric Care), clinical disciplines (BIO/14 Pharmacology, MED/09 Internal Medicine and Medical Therapy, MED/18 General Surgery, MED/17 Infectious Diseases, MED/09 Geriatrics, MED/26 Neurology, MED/33 Orthopedics, MED/38 Neonatology and Pediatrics, MED/40 Gynecology and Obstetrics, MED/25 Psychiatry, M-PSI/08 Clinical Psychology), basic disciplines in emergency care (MED/09 Emergency Medicine, MED/18 Emergency Surgery, MED/41 Anesthesia and Intensive Care, MED/45 Emergency Nursing and Critical Care). Particular attention is given to ethics and professional deontology (MED/43 Legal Medicine and MED/45 Professional Deontology). The internship (65 CFU) and Nursing laboratories (3 CFU), fundamental parts of the Degree Program, receive special attention regarding site selection and timing relative to the advancement of the study program.
3. Integrated disciplines area, including health management disciplines (IUS/07 Labor Law, SECS-P/10 Business Organization, MED/45 Nursing Management) developed for understanding the basic mechanisms of healthcare companies and from the perspective of deeper study in specialist degree programs, as well as disciplines aimed at statistical-computational preparation through basic statistics modules (MED/01 Medical Statistics) and applied computer science (ING-INF/05 Information Processing Systems) which, through the performance of statistical and computer laboratory activities as well as the basics of scientific research (MED/45 Nursing Research Methodology and MED/42 Epidemiology), provide theoretical/practical means for adequate and independent technical-scientific updating.
Students are also provided with an English language course (Medical English) aimed at understanding scientific literature, with the possibility, provided by the university language services, to obtain certifications such as PET and/or FCE.

High School Diploma University Fees and Contributions For information on university fees and contributions, visit the following page on the University website www.unisi.it/tasse Dates and Deadlines For information on dates and deadlines, visit the following page on the University website "Study Plan" www.unisi.it/didattica/immatricolazioni-e-iscrizioni/immatricolazioni Roles Responsibilities for Student Mobility ALESSANDRA VIVIANI Student Mobility Coordinator MARCO FERRARI Chair/Chair of Teaching Committee MARCO FERRARI Program, Texts, and Objectives Admission Requirements Students possessing a High School Diploma or an equivalent foreign qualification may be admitted.
Required knowledge will include: general culture and logical reasoning, mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology.

The entrance exam is common to all Health Area Degree Programs and is conducted on the same day at all Italian Universities.
Professional status conferred by the degree.
DENTAL HYGIENIST According to the latest official estimates, there are approximately 7,000 dental hygienists working in Italy. In public facilities, the demand for these professionals is still too limited, especially for assisting long-term patients, the elderly, and immobilized individuals requiring daily care. In the private sector, however, demand for this professional figure is very high, particularly in central-northern regions and large cities. No significant changes are expected in the future. Any potential increase is included in the overall national assessment of the need for graduates in health professions expressed by the Regions.
Characteristics of Final Exam The final exam, which has the value of a State Exam for professional qualification in the profession of Dental Hygienist (D. Lgs 502/1992, art. 6, comma 3), is worth 5 CFU and consists of:
a) Practical exam during which the student must demonstrate having acquired the theoretical, practical, and technical skills specific to the professional profile of Dental Hygienist; passing this exam has sufficiency value and allows access to the thesis discussion.
b) Preparation and defense of a thesis, in compliance with D.I 19 February 2009, art. 7.
The final score is expressed out of 110.
The merit score is calculated starting from the arithmetic mean of the grades obtained during the training path, scaled to 110 (rounded to the nearest integer), which forms the basis of the calculation.
To this value, the score related to the thesis discussion (obligatorily experimental) will be added, up to a maximum of 10 points, awarded by the Commission evaluating:
1) Quality of the thesis presentation and discussion in relation to:
- clarity of exposition, conciseness of presentation;
- richness and updating of scientific information;
- ability to provide concise and comprehensive answers to questions from Commission members;
- completeness of the topic development within the assigned time (15 minutes);
- ability to appropriately use audiovisual systems.
2) Quality of the work performed by the candidate in relation to:
- originality and importance of the research;
- complexity of the experimental work;
- autonomy and actual role played by the candidate.
If a total score of 110/110 is achieved, the Chair of the Final Exam Commission will put the award of honors to a vote, which can only be granted unanimously by those present.
Required Knowledge for Access Students possessing a High School Diploma or another foreign qualification recognized by the University as suitable may be admitted to the Dental Hygiene Degree Program.
An adequate initial preparation, obtained through previous studies, in mathematics, physics, chemistry, and biology is required.
Admission to the program is granted upon passing an entrance test prepared by the Ministry.
The modalities for accessing the Degree Program and the content of the entrance exam are established by Law 264/1999 "Regulations on Access to University Courses" (GU n. 183 of 6-8-1999), as well as by annual ministerial decrees concerning both the modalities and content of entrance exams for nationally programmed courses, and the definition of available places for admission to the Degree Program.
Enrollment in the Degree Program must be completed within the deadlines set annually by the competent teaching body.
Students admitted to the program with a score below a predetermined minimum threshold will be assigned additional academic obligations to be fulfilled within the first year of the program.
The adequacy of the student's preparation will be verified according to the modalities indicated in the Study Program Didactic Regulations.
Degree Awarded.
DEGREE IN DENTAL HYGIENE Teaching Delivery Method Conventional Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area Graduates in Dental Hygiene will have acquired theoretical and practical knowledge in the field of dental hygiene, applicable in both public and private sectors, regarding assistance and biomedical research in the numerous fields of oral and dental hygiene (prevention, maintenance of good health, therapy for dental and/or systemic pathologies and for incorrect oral hygiene).
They will possess knowledge in dentistry, genetics, pathological anatomy, pharmacology, microbiology, and nutrition sciences, reached through basic knowledge of physics, biochemistry, anatomy and histology, physiology, and general pathology.
In particular, they will have acquired knowledge and skills regarding technical topics and practical abilities related to dental hygiene and dental health education, thanks to courses taught by staff from the specific scientific discipline of the professional profile, professional training activities to be carried out directly in the clinic and/or ward, interaction with defined groups of people (school population, patients in protected and assistive facilities, etc.) under the guidance of qualified and experienced personnel including professional profile tutors, attendance in dental and dental hygiene facilities, laboratories, and completion of professional internships. All this will enable the graduate to acquire knowledge sufficient to recognize specific situations and apply, case by case, what is established and recognized by the scientific community as "best practice" for that particular problem.
Acquisition of such knowledge and understanding will be facilitated by the overall teaching activities (frontal lectures, seminars, teaching laboratories, internships, preparation of the final exam, etc.) and will be verified through exams, whose modalities depend on the type of teaching activity provided (sufficiency for internships (1st semester), English language and various laboratories, grades expressed in thirtieths for frontal lectures, self-learning activities, and 2nd semester internships of years I, II, and III, grades expressed out of 110 for the final exam).

COURSE: [ME014] DENTAL HYGIENE (ELIGIBLE FOR THE HEALTHCARE PROFESSION OF DENTAL HYGIENIST)
SECTION: Autonomy of Judgment
URL: https://unisi.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10377

Autonomy of Judgment.
The autonomy of judgment of graduates will be expressed through the recognition and ability to autonomously evaluate critical issues related to the patient's condition, in relation to oral hygiene aspects and prevention of dental pathologies, and in developing practical and/or experimental prevention schemes, and in choosing methodologies, strategies, and the optimal use of equipment to achieve the expected results, also through the critical review of information obtained through bibliographic and/or computer research.
The development of these skills will occur and be verified during internships, where interaction with people, professionals, structures, and different methodologies will facilitate the development of independent critical thinking. Equally important will be active participation in lectures, preparation for exams and the final project, further moments of development and verification.
Knowledge of the relevant regulations, professional, legal, and health regulations, and their application, will be aimed at achieving specific professional competencies, i.e., the ability to master and manage independently and/or in teams, acts, technologies, and procedures.
Acquiring a behavior consistent with the foundational ethical principles will be one of the objectives that completes the educational path.
Autonomy of Judgment will be verified through evaluations by assigned tutors, through internship exams, and through the verification related to the final exam: in its practical part and in the evaluation of the thesis content.

Learning Ability.
Graduates will acquire learning abilities and competencies enabling, with a high degree of autonomy, the continuation of studies, including the master's degree (LM/SNT3), scientific specialization courses, and advanced permanent and recurring training (1st and 2nd level master's programs), as well as update and in-depth courses (Continuing Medical Education).
They will be able to autonomously update their competencies regarding scientific and technological innovations within their professional activities.
This ability will be developed through the overall teaching activities and exam preparation, through internship attendance, where theory is combined with practice, and through critical use of bibliography for the preparation of the final project.
This ability will be verified through the conduct of exams (oral, written, simulated practical tests), which assess student preparation, as well as through tutor evaluations of the internship, and finally through the preparation and conduct of the final exam.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
General Area
At the end of the study course, graduates will be able to choose and use appropriate methodologies and equipment in various specialized fields for the acquisition of clinical and experimental data and to analyze and interpret them (anamnesis of habits related to oral hygiene, objective examination).
By interpreting the obtained data, they will be able to identify the correct oral hygiene education, applied tartar ablation therapy, and modification of any incorrect habits to resolve the proposed problem, and, collaborating with the physician and dentist, participate in the diagnostic and rehabilitative process, proposing solutions that may contribute to resolving the subject's issues.
They will be able to develop ideas and proposals for optimizing the adopted educational methodologies and document the procedures used with appropriate scientific language. They will be capable of performing activities in full compliance with safety regulations for the use of equipment and procedures.
The internship will be a fundamental tool for achieving these objectives, along with the overall teaching activities (frontal lectures, self-learning, etc.), as well as activities carried out at the department/clinic level (seminars, teaching laboratories).
Other fundamental tools will include the use of computer tools, consultation and/or construction and updating of databases, bibliographic research, use of textbooks, and preparation of the thesis for the final project, strictly of an experimental nature.
The evaluation of these skills will occur through internship verifications, aptitude and exams (depending on the type of teaching activity administered), and through the final project itself.

SECTION: Communication skills
URL: https://unisi.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/10377

Communication skills.
The graduate must establish and maintain a relationship with the user, starting from prevention, taking into account the various levels of complexity related to it. This constitutes the foundation of professional practice, which must be centered on the subject, respecting individual differences and taking into account their influence on eating habits related to oral cavity health, lifestyle, and the individual's own habits.
The Dental Hygienist graduate:
- will work in accordance with the principles of patient/user-centered professional practice;
- will build a relationship/partnership as the foundation of oral hygiene intervention;
- will employ a variety of personalized strategies based on the patient's needs.
Graduates must be particularly skilled in interpersonal communication, including oral and written communication with professionals and service users, in group work, and within interdisciplinary work groups with health and social professionals.
To achieve this, the Dental Hygienist graduate must:
- select appropriate communication methods;
- identify and recognize communication barriers (problems reading or writing, misunderstanding, cultural issues, fear, etc.);
- adapt to a communication style suitable to meet the needs and learning abilities of individual persons and/or groups;
- employ effective verbal communication skills;
- write clearly, concisely, and professionally, technically and grammatically accurate;
- develop educational material taking into account the comprehension capacity of the target group and/or individuals;
- facilitate two-way communication;
- employ active listening techniques;
- interpret and respond to non-verbal communication;
- apply principles of collaboration and negotiation in group work;
- incorporate the knowledge, experiences, and skills of other members of the work group during their activities;
- collaborate with other members of the work group to define objectives;
- adapt their personal approach to the members and situations involving the work group;
- work with other members of the work group to identify and resolve conflicts;
- contribute to decisions made within the work group;
- take responsibility for completing the assigned task.
Communication skills will be acquired through the teachings of human sciences, psychopedagogical, and sociological sciences to ensure the learning of necessary behavioral and relational competencies to operate in a complex work environment. Furthermore, the internship involves close contact between the student and patients, under the supervision of tutors whose task will be to modulate the approach methodology from the initial phase to the completion of professional training.
Communication skills will be verified by tutors during the related teaching activities, during the internship, and through the evaluation of teaching activities, up to the final exam.
Expected occupational and professional opportunities for graduates.
DENTAL HYGIENIST According to the latest official estimates, there are approximately 7,000 dental hygienists operating in Italy. In public structures, the demand for these professionals is still too limited, especially for the care of long-term patients, the elderly, and immobilized individuals requiring daily care. In the private sector, however, the demand for this professional figure is very high, particularly in the center-north and large cities. No significant changes are expected in the future. An estimated increase is included in the overall assessment of the national need for graduates in health professions expressed by the Regions.
Official teaching and assessment language(s).
ITALIAN Associated competencies for the role.
DENTAL HYGIENIST It is estimated that among approximately 30,000 personnel in the health sector, there is a need for a turnover of 5% - 6%. At the level of the National Health Service (S.S.N.), an increase in the need for this figure is also expected in relation to the priority health issues highlighted by the WHO, such as periodontal diseases, oral cavity diseases related to soft tissues, gingivitis, caries, etc., for which the Dental Hygienist role is central in the prevention and rehabilitation process.
Current regulations allow the performance of free professional activities, in individual or associated professional offices, service cooperatives, etc.
The profession of dental hygienists is included in item 85.14.2 (Independent paramedical professional activities) of the Ateco Economic Activities Classification: health activities not performed by hospitals or doctors, but by legally recognized paramedical staff.
Description of admission tests.
The number of students admitted to the degree program is planned annually based on regional needs.
The entrance test is common to all health area degree programs and is conducted on the same day at all Italian universities.
The test consists of a multiple-choice quiz on the following subjects: general culture, logical reasoning, mathematics, physics, chemistry, and biology.
The ranking is based on merit Function in work context.
DENTAL HYGIENIST The Dental Hygienist can perform their activities, both for diagnosis and research, in public or private health structures (privately contracted structures with the S.S.N., accredited and non-accredited structures, such as clinics and rehabilitation centers, Sanitary Assistance Residences, wellness centers, medical and/or specialist clinics, etc.), as an employee or as a self-employed professional; however, as this is a relatively new profession at the legislative level, this figure has so far found employment mainly in the private sector, that is, in medical and dental offices. It is likely that in the future, thanks to the activation of the degree program and the establishment of the appropriate professional register, even greater occupational opportunities will open up also within the S.S.N.
Additional information.
http://www.unisi.it/dipartimenti/dipartimento-biotecnologie-mediche Specific training objectives description.
The objective of the Dental Hygiene degree program (licensed for the health profession of Dental Hygienist) is to provide students with the necessary scientific foundations and theoretical-practical preparation to be licensed to practice the profession of Dental Hygienist, as well as the methodology and culture necessary for lifelong training, and a level of professional, decision-making, and operational autonomy sufficient to guarantee, at the end of the training path, full mastery of all necessary competencies and their immediate applicability in the work environment.
The specific training objectives will enable Dental Hygiene graduates (licensed for the health profession of Dental Hygienist) to:
- acquire essential theoretical knowledge derived from basic sciences, in the perspective of their subsequent professional application and as a prerequisite for understanding the disciplines characteristic of the profession;
- acquire knowledge related to health recovery, providing adequate support for the patient's oral hygiene necessary for the prevention and protection of numerous systemic diseases, and for maintaining health in healthy individuals, through the indication of correct oral hygiene practices;
- intervene in prevention, suggesting "good practices" of toothbrushing and use of other aids (interdental brush, floss, etc.);
- be able to use appropriate diagnostic tools to identify bacterial plaque and dental calculus, motivating the need for periodic clinical checks;
- be able to indicate the norms of rational nutrition for the protection of dental health;
- be able to perform tartar removal and root planing as well as the topical application of various preventive means;
- possess adequate basic knowledge of anatomical-biological systems, interpreted from an anatomical and physiological-pathological perspective, enabling the development of operational professionalism;
- possess the cultural and experimental bases of multidisciplinary techniques characterizing the operational field of dental hygiene and preventive dentistry for the production of services through the modification of personal and collective habits;
- possess disciplinary methodologies and be able to apply them in concrete situations with appropriate knowledge of regulations and deontological and bioethical issues;
- be able to effectively use English, in written and oral form, within their specific area of competence and for the exchange of general information;
- possess adequate competencies and tools for communication and information management;
- be capable of working in groups, but also of operating autonomously and integrating quickly into work environments;
- be capable of collaborating in the compilation of the dental-stomatological clinical record and in the collection of technical-statistical data;
- know and evaluate automation and informatization;
- know health management;
- be able to collaborate with different professional figures in group health activities;
- be able to carry out their professional activities in public or private health structures, in an employee or self-employed capacity, on the recommendation of dentists and medical surgeons legally authorized to practice dentistry;
- know the main regulations regarding radioprotection.
Based on the specific training objectives described, the training path requires the acquisition of a total of one hundred and eighty (180) CFU, divided over three years of study, of which sixty (60) to be acquired through training activities aimed at developing specific professional skills (internship). This path is implemented first through theoretical and theoretical-practical learning, focused on the specificity of the profession, of basic disciplines: FIS/07, MED/03, MED/04, MED/07, MED/09, BIO/09, BIO/10, BIO/13, BIO/16, BIO/17, such as physics, biology, biochemistry, anatomy, histology, general pathology, microbiology, psychology, and subsequently through the learning of disciplines more strictly characteristic, such as prevention sciences and health services sciences, sciences and techniques of dental hygiene, medical-surgical sciences: MED/28, MED/42, MED/50, BIO/14, MED/08, MED/36, MED/43, MED/44. Each of these disciplines corresponds to at least one module regarding the relevant topics, collected in specific teachings by topic, to facilitate the acquisition of essential knowledge for the profession and to support the internship in the corresponding sectors.
In particular, considerable space is reserved for the statistical-informatic preparation of students through basic statistics modules (MED/01) and computer science (ING-INF/05) and subsequent specific teachings of applied statistics for experimental and technological research (SECS-S/02) and the performance of laboratory activities in statistics and computer science, so that they acquire the ability to manage data related to various aspects of nutrition (production, availability, processing of health statistics on computerized clinical records) and to benefit from such results, evaluating their usefulness in relation to normal and/or clinical oral hygiene situations and research.
Theoretical and practical means are also provided for adequate and autonomous future technical-scientific updating (MED/50).
Cultural training is enriched by teachings of human sciences and psychopedagogical and sociological sciences: M-PSI/01, M-PED/01, M-DEA/01, MED/02 and SPS/07, to ensure the acquisition of necessary behavioral and relational competencies to operate in a complex work environment; to know the distribution of pathologies related to an incorrect relationship with oral hygiene, taking into account, towards users/patients, the psychological motivations linked to behavior, which give rise to serious pathologies such as dental and systemic diseases.
Particular attention is paid to Prevention Sciences and Health Services (MED/36, MED/42, MED/43, MED/44, MED/45, MED/50) and also to First Aid (MED/09, MED/18, MED/41).
Health Management Sciences (IUS/07, SECS-P/07) are developed in particular regarding labor law, as well as business economics, for the basic understanding of management mechanisms of health companies and in the perspective of further development in specialized degree programs.
Students are provided with an English course (Medical English) also aimed at understanding scientific literature, with the possibility, provided by the University language services, to obtain B1 and B2 level certifications.
The internship (60 CFU), which is a fundamental part of the study program to enable students to acquire the necessary skills for the practice of Dental Hygienist, will receive particular attention regarding both the choice of locations and the timing of implementation in relation to the advancement of the study program itself.
Teaching is organized into modules and is carried out through frontal lectures, classroom exercises, or in specific "laboratories" for the Degree Program.
The learning outcomes of laboratory activities, English language, and some internships will result in a qualification.
Students will have 5 CFU available for the preparation of the final exam of the Course at facilities dedicated to training; this activity, defined as 'degree internship', can also be carried out in non-university facilities, such as hospital or public and/or private accredited structures, subject to authorization by the Teaching Committee.

Final Exam Characteristics The final exam consists of (D.I. February 19, 2009, art. 7): a) a practical test during which the student must demonstrate having acquired the theoretical-practical and technical-operative knowledge and skills specific to the professional profile. b) preparation of a thesis and its defense. The final exam is evaluated by a Commission. It consists of at least seven and no more than eleven members, including at least two members designated by the Professional Order in accordance with current regulations. During this exam, the student must demonstrate having acquired a scientific and theoretical-practical preparation, methodology, and skills enabling professional, decision-making, and operational autonomy for the exercise of the profession. The final exam contributes 5 ECTS credits to the total credit load, and the grade is expressed as 110/110 with possible honors. Required Knowledge for Admission The course is nationally programmed under Article 1 of Law 264/1999; the annual national programming regulations issued by the Ministry of University and Research (MIUR) and published in the competition notices apply. Candidates possessing a Secondary School Diploma or another foreign title recognized as equivalent may be admitted to the Physiotherapy Degree Course. The number of eligible students (training potential) is proposed based on the availability of teaching staff, teaching facilities (classrooms, laboratories), and, in particular, clinical-assistive facilities usable for practical activities, applying the standards defined by the competent teaching structure. The number of students admitted to the course is subsequently determined based on national and regional programming. Among the necessary entry knowledge, English language knowledge at least at level A2/2 (CEFR) is required. Additionally, basic knowledge of biology, chemistry, mathematics, physics, and general culture characterizing the entrance exam for Health Professions study courses is required. Normally, given the high number of admission applications to the Physiotherapy course and the consequent high required score, passing the entrance exam ensures an adequate level of basic knowledge. The student's initial preparation will, however, be assessed through the analysis of errors found in the logic, chemistry, biology, mathematics, and physics quizzes (multiple-choice questions) administered during the entrance exam. In case the verification is not positive or falls below the established minimum, additional mandatory training obligations will be assigned to be fulfilled in the first year of the course. In this regard, the instructors of the relevant modules will conduct a brief recovery course for the main deficient knowledge, which must still be completed in the first year. Degree Awarded. PHYSIOTHERAPY DEGREE Teaching Delivery Mode Conventional Knowledge and Understanding. Basic Sciences Area Physiotherapy graduates must have acquired the following knowledge and comprehension abilities: a) knowledge of biochemical and genetic mechanisms underlying human life, including biological phenomena occurring in cells and tissues; b) ability to understand the structure of the human body and its physiological mechanisms of operation, with particular reference to the somatic and autonomic nervous systems, the musculoskeletal and cardiovascular systems; c) knowledge of psychological elements underlying interpersonal relationships, especially in the healthcare context, and pedagogical principles for correct communication and interpersonal relations; d) knowledge of the organism's response mechanisms to major pathogenic factors and the etiology and pathogenesis of major acute and chronic pathologies of interest to physiotherapy, including the general effects of their treatment. Physiotherapy Sciences Area Physiotherapy graduates must have acquired the following knowledge and comprehension abilities: a) knowledge of the fundamental principles and their historical evolution of rehabilitation methodology and physiotherapy in all age groups; b) knowledge of the etiopathogenesis and clinical presentation of disorders of the musculoskeletal, neurological, cardiovascular, and visceral systems in all age groups; c) knowledge of physiotherapy and rehabilitation techniques and methods applied to specific clinical conditions of the musculoskeletal and cardiovascular systems, the central, peripheral, and autonomic nervous systems in all age groups; d) knowledge of research methodology, scientific update methods, and statistical and computer sciences applied to the specific field; e) ability to understand the complexity of communication and relational aspects in the context and for the type of patients requiring rehabilitation at every stage of life. Management Area Physiotherapy graduates must have acquired the following knowledge and comprehension abilities: a) knowledge of the principles for maintaining well-being, health, and disease prevention through an appropriate lifestyle and correct physical exercise practice; b) knowledge of individual health issues, including disabilities, and/or community health issues, even within the context of health emergencies; c) knowledge of current professional regulations and the principles of legal medicine and the code of ethics applied to physiotherapy.

SECTION: Judgment Autonomy

Judgment Autonomy.
The graduate, at the end of the study path, will be able to know and apply autonomously the physiotherapy process using clinical reasoning as a guiding tool for decision-making. This autonomy will be achieved through the ability to effectively respond to individual and/or collective health needs, either as a single operator or in a team, by choosing the best therapeutic strategies, identifying appropriate approaches and tools, through the collection of necessary data, including analysis of the social context, i.e., according to the biopsychosocial model. In an ethical context, it will manifest through respect for relevant regulations, professional, legal, health, and deontological standards. The physiotherapist's judgment autonomy will be fully realized through the habitual and judicious use of communication, knowledge, professional skills, clinical reasoning (diagnostic and evaluative process), emotions, values, and reflection in daily practice for the benefit of the individual or the community.
These competencies are primarily acquired 'on the field', i.e., within laboratory and clinical-practical internship activities.
Judgment autonomy is verified through the results of Internship and Laboratory activities, in the fields of prevention, care and rehabilitation, therapeutic education, evidence-based practice, professional responsibility, management and administration.
Verification of these skills is mainly entrusted to internship tutors and instructors of professional activities, who rely on specific items drafted in the core competencies of the physiotherapist and reported in the evaluation grid of the internship notebook, completed by the tutor at the end of each shift, and in that related to the second and third year internship exam.
The final assessment of this competency is also verified collegially by the Thesis Commission during the final practical exam, which, following the guidelines of the Ministry of Health/MIUR Circular of 30/09/2016 point 1, includes a practical simulation on a structured clinical case.

Learning Ability.
The graduate physiotherapist must be able to conduct a self-assessment of their knowledge in order to maintain their expertise at the highest level required for professional practice and to plan self-education paths to enhance their skills, with particular reference to Evidence-Based Medicine in rehabilitation and physiotherapy. To this end, students annually take the Ministry's test on transversal and disciplinary competencies (TECO) to annually verify the implementation and acquisition of competencies and any gaps.
The graduate must also be able to pursue further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
These competencies are acquired through frontal lectures, specific laboratories, and clinical internship, and are assessed during profit exams (written or oral) and the TECO verification.
In this regard, during the studies, the student must prepare at least seven real clinical cases on a specific form, which will subsequently be assessed by a commission chaired by the Head of Professional Teaching. Furthermore, two of the prepared clinical cases must be presented in plenary to a commission and all other students. The subsequent discussion must focus particularly on the scientific evidence supporting the rehabilitation path, treatment methods, and prognosis.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Basic Sciences Area Graduates in physiotherapy who have successfully completed the course must be able to:
a) integrate knowledge of the biological mechanisms underlying human life;
b) clearly describe, also to the patient, the structure of the human body, particularly the somatic and autonomic nervous system, musculoskeletal and cardiovascular apparatus;
c) interpret clinical signs after adequate assessment; set up a treatment based on evidence of efficacy and prognosis, and carry it out correctly in compliance with the patient;
d) build effective interprofessional collaboration and negotiate and manage interpersonal conflicts;
e) understand the etiopathogenetic differences between acute and chronic pathologies of interest to physiotherapy and the possible side effects of drugs and other therapies in relation to the rehabilitation treatment.

Physiotherapy Sciences Area Graduates in physiotherapy who have successfully completed the course must be able to:
a) apply the physiotherapy process as a whole, using the collection, analysis, and interpretation of significant data for the patient's needs, in various pathologies and across all age groups;
b) integrate valid and relevant scientific evidence with clinical experience and the patient's condition;
c) correctly perform functional assessment and formulate physiotherapy diagnosis (functional diagnosis);
d) define therapeutic goals, considering not only the extent of damage but also recovery factors;
e) plan and implement care and rehabilitation interventions aimed at specific functional outcomes through a person-centered approach;
f) implement the intervention safely and effectively, making necessary adjustments to the treatment plan as needed;
g) demonstrate the ability to evaluate the outcome of the treatment plan, verifying overall effectiveness based on results from the specific intervention;
h) demonstrate empathetic and relational skills towards the person assisted, those caring for the patient, and the professional environment.

These knowledge and understanding abilities will be acquired through frontal lectures, teaching laboratories, exercises, and professional internship, using study materials such as textbooks recommended by instructors, multimedia aids, and scientific articles. A significant part of the learning process is constituted by practical activities in the sectors defining physiotherapy, verified both during the process and at the end, through theoretical-practical, simulated, and patient-based tests. Regarding professional and internship activities, the reference is the Internship Manual available at the Degree Course.

Management Area Graduates in physiotherapy who have successfully completed the course must be able to:
a) organize prevention and rehabilitation activities by defining priorities in relation to available resources, ensuring continuity and quality of care;
b) promote necessary actions to maintain health, motivating individuals and groups to adopt ergonomic principles and lifestyles suitable for promoting their physical and social well-being;
c) analyze the effectiveness of health and social services in responding to citizens' main needs;
d) operate fully respecting current regulations as well as patient needs.

These knowledge and understanding abilities will be acquired and verified primarily through curricular teaching and respective profit exams in different fields.

Communication skills.
The graduate, at the end of the study path, must be able to manage communication as the ability to establish a meaningful therapeutic relationship with the person and to establish an effective relationship with all other professionals of the same or other disciplines. They must also be capable of using communication tools in the healthcare context, demonstrating the ability to complete the physiotherapy record, participate in the compilation of a rehabilitation project in a multidisciplinary team, draft a physiotherapy report, design a physiotherapy program, in a clear, concise, and professional manner, technically and grammatically accurate. The graduate must be able to communicate appropriately in clinical-organizational and scientific contexts, national and international. They must finally be capable of translating technical language in a way that is understandable even to people outside the healthcare world.
These competencies are acquired mainly 'on the field', that is within laboratory and clinical-practical internship activities, and verified through the results achieved in these activities.
The verification of these skills is primarily entrusted to internship tutors and the teachers of professionalizing activities, who make use of the specific items drawn up in the core competence of the physiotherapist and reported in the evaluation grid of the internship notebook, completed by the tutor at the end of each shift, and in that related to the internship exam of the second and third year. In particular, regarding communication skills, the evaluated competencies concern the areas of the relationship with the patient. Additionally, the third-year internship exam is primarily focused on functional and prognostic evaluation, discussion of rehabilitation goals, treatment execution, and the ability to interact with real patients with whom the student must be promptly capable of structuring an adequate therapeutic and communicative relationship.

Expected occupational and professional outcomes for graduates.
Physiotherapist The Physiotherapist finds placement within the National Health Service, in private structures accredited and contracted with the N.H.S., professional studios and rehabilitation centers, Sanitary Assistance Residences, thermal establishments, medical and/or multi-specialty outpatient clinics, sports associations and societies in various types, service cooperatives, non-governmental organizations, public or private prevention services.
The preparation provided by the Physiotherapy Degree Course allows for rapid integration into the workforce, as well as access to the Master's Degree in Rehabilitation Sciences of Health Professions, or University Level Master's Programs.
Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIAN Associated competencies for the role.
Physiotherapist Graduates in Physiotherapy develop, also in a multidisciplinary team, the identification of rehabilitation programs aimed at identifying and overcoming the health needs of the disabled; they independently perform therapeutic activities for the functional rehabilitation of motor, psychomotor, and cognitive disabilities using instrumental, manual, therapeutic exercise, and occupational therapies; propose the adoption of prostheses and aids, train in their use, and verify their effectiveness; verify the correspondence of the rehabilitation methodology implemented to the functional recovery goals; carry out activities of study, teaching, and professional consultancy in healthcare services and in those requiring their professional competencies.

Description of admission tests.
The number of students admitted to the Degree Course is programmed annually based on regional needs.
The entrance test is common to all Degree Courses in the health area and is conducted on the same day at all Italian universities.
The test consists of a multiple-choice quiz on the following subjects: general culture, logical reasoning, mathematics, physics, chemistry, and biology.
The ranking is formulated based on merit.

Function in the work context.
Physiotherapist Graduates in Physiotherapy carry out, with professional autonomy and independence, towards individuals and the community, activities directed at prevention, treatment, rehabilitation, and functional evaluation procedures. They are healthcare operators to whom the attributions provided for by Ministerial Decree of the Ministry of Health of September 14, 1994, no. 741 and subsequent amendments and integrations apply, who independently or in collaboration with other healthcare figures, in reference to the diagnosis and prescriptions of the physician, within their areas of competence, carry out their activities in the areas of motricity, higher cortical functions, and visceral functions following pathological events.

Additional information.
http://www.unisi.it/dipartimenti/dipartimento-scienze-mediche-chirurgiche-e-neuroscienze

Description of specific educational objectives.
The Physiotherapy Degree aims to:
- Provide in-depth knowledge and advanced understanding of the morphology and functioning of the human body with particular reference to the nervous, musculoskeletal, cardiorespiratory, and pelvic floor systems.
- Develop the ability to frame the main pathologies within the scope of physiotherapy, as well as the knowledge for applying concepts, methods, and techniques for preventive, therapeutic, and rehabilitative purposes, as well as professional management.
- Develop competencies for correct interaction with the patient, the use of evaluation and analysis tools, interpretation of scientific research, respecting current regulations.
- Develop abilities for interaction and organization with all other healthcare operators to create the basis for a multidisciplinary methodological and operational approach.

The main learning areas of the Course are:
1) Basic Sciences area, related to Integrated Courses of the first year, includes teachings relevant to three major thematic areas: the first aimed at understanding biological phenomena (BIO/10, BIO/13 and MED/03) and the integrated structure and functioning of organs and systems (BIO/09, BIO/16 and BIO/17); the second for knowledge of psychological and anthropological (M-PSI/08, BIO/08), social and environmental (M-DEA/01, M-PED/01 and MED/02) dimensions of diseases; and the third related to understanding their etiology and pathogenesis (BIO/14, MED/04, MED/07 and MED/08).
2) Physiotherapy Sciences area, related to Integrated Courses of the second and third years, includes on one hand a series of theoretical-practical teachings aimed at learning the fundamental concepts of functional assessment, physiotherapy methods, and techniques (FIS/07, MED/34, MED/48 and M-EDF/01); on the other hand, it includes specific theoretical-practical teachings related to the framing of pathologies of the locomotor system (MED/16, MED/33 and MED/36), neurological and neuropsychiatric (MED/26, MED/27 and MED/39), cardiorespiratory (MED/10 and MED/11), visceral (MED/24 and MED/40), and plastic-reconstructive (MED/19) systems, both in pediatric (MED/38) and adult and geriatric (MED/09, MED/26) contexts. The main subject of the teachings is the treatment of disabling pathologies in acute, post-acute, and chronic phases (MED/48 and MED/50). Particular attention is paid to issues related to pain syndromes (MED/41). Some teachings are aimed at research and critical interpretation of Evidence Based Medicine (ING-INF/06, MED/01 and SECS-S/02), also for the purpose of drafting the thesis.
Additionally, a minimum of 60 CFU of internship (MED/48) is required over the three years of the course.
3) Management area, related to Integrated Courses mainly of the third year, includes the basic elements for knowledge of three additional thematic areas that can be considered supportive of the physiotherapist's professional activity as a healthcare operator. They concern: concepts of emergency and first aid (MED/09, MED/18 and MED/41), legal elements of management and administration (MED/43, IUS/07, IUS/09 and SECS-P/10), and those of prevention, hygiene, and occupational medicine (MED/36, MED/42, and MED/44) necessary for professional practice.
Exams can be taken in written, oral, and/or practical form, according to the teacher's indication and the teaching type.
Students must also attend an English language course (Medical English), aimed at understanding scientific literature, acquiring competencies equivalent to the B1 level of the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages.

Final Exam Characteristics The candidate must demonstrate sufficient scientific maturity to undertake and complete a short thesis. This activity is normally facilitated by the experience gained during the internship, during which the candidate's activity may already be directed towards the thesis.
The final exam consists of a written dissertation discussed publicly by the candidate before the committee on the graduation day, with a presentation lasting approximately 30 minutes total. The dissertation concerns a scientific topic that verifies whether the general educational objectives of the study program have been achieved; in particular, the content may relate to one of the research activities present in the department.
The thesis may be written and defended, at the candidate's discretion, in a foreign language; for this work, the prescribed credits and a merit score calculated according to the criteria indicated in the Study Program Regulations are awarded.
Required Knowledge for Access Basic scientific knowledge acquired in secondary school, certified by possession of a High School Diploma or other foreign qualification recognized as equivalent, and basic knowledge of English (at least A2/2 level).
In compliance with Article 6, paragraph 1 of D.M. 270/04, students must possess adequate initial preparation. To this end, students must take an entrance knowledge assessment test to identify their level of preparation relative to the chosen degree program and encourage them to deepen their study subjects, ensuring their performance matches a university curriculum. The test results are used to establish necessary corrections and any required integrations to be fulfilled during the first year of study. The test is normally held in October, before the start of lectures. The verification and integration procedures mentioned above will be carried out under the supervision of the Study Program Teaching Committee for Physics and Advanced Technologies, as well as the tutor teachers.
Awarded Degree
Bachelor's Degree in Physics and Advanced Technologies Teaching Methodology Conventional Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area Graduates in Physics and Advanced Technologies have acquired knowledge and understanding regarding:
- Appropriate mathematical tools for "quantitative" analysis of physical systems and for studying theoretical models describing physical phenomena, and as a guide to problem solving.
- Physical principles with in-depth knowledge and understanding of Classical Physics and solid introductory bases for concepts of Modern Physics and Non-relativistic Quantum Mechanics.
- Physical phenomena from an experimental perspective: realization of direct experiences with physical phenomena, design of experiments and their development at every stage, critical analysis capabilities of collected data.
- Applications of physical sciences both in research and technological fields, physical mechanisms underlying the operation of specific applications of current interest.
Fundamental Scientific and Methodological Knowledge At the end of studies, the graduate has acquired knowledge and understanding:
Fundamental scientific and methodological aspects of basic disciplines (mathematics, chemistry, computer science): differential and integral calculus for functions of one or more real or complex variables, linear algebra and analytic geometry, linear systems and differential equations, computer system architecture and related languages, elements of inorganic and organic chemistry
Basic Physical Sciences At the end of studies, the graduate has acquired knowledge and understanding:
Advanced physical foundations, theoretical and formal aspects regarding dynamics of material points and systems, conservation laws of momentum, energy and angular momentum, Fluid Dynamics, Thermodynamics, Electromagnetism, Generation and Propagation of Electromagnetic Waves, Physical and Geometric Optics.
Mathematical Physics and Theoretical Physics At the end of studies, the graduate has acquired knowledge and understanding:
Models and methods for analyzing the mechanical behavior of systems with a finite number of degrees of freedom, free and constrained, Lagrangian and Hamiltonian formulation of mechanical systems, Laplace and Fourier transforms; advanced mathematical knowledge related to algebras of observables, Hilbert spaces and linear operators in Hilbert spaces, fundamentals of quantum mechanics and first elements of solid-state physics.
Physics Laboratory and Experimental Physics Activities At the end of studies, the graduate has acquired knowledge and understanding:
General methodologies for designing and conducting measurements of physical quantities in mechanical, thermodynamic, electrical, electronic, and optical contexts; semiconductor technology, transistors, amplifiers and related circuit models in optical devices, microprocessors and microcontrollers; data acquisition and analysis systems, their statistical treatment, analog and digital signals; operation of various types of detectors, electronic instrumentation, and modern experimental techniques used in Nuclear and Subnuclear Physics, Atomic Spectroscopy, Laser Physics.
Modern Physics At the end of studies, the graduate has acquired knowledge and understanding:
Relevant aspects for specific training in modern research, advanced technology, and the most advanced theories in this area, such as elements of Special Relativity, Astrophysics, experiments leading to the crisis of Classical Mechanics, elements of Atomic and Molecular Physics, introduction to Solid-State Physics, Elements of Nuclear and Elementary Particle Physics, radioactive phenomena, Medical Physics.
Applications in Related Fields At the end of studies, the graduate has acquired knowledge and understanding in complementary scientific fields, aimed at forming a general university-level cultural heritage in areas not strictly related to the specific learning project.
They have acquired knowledge and skills enabling them to enter the regional register of Competent Technicians in Acoustics, a registration required by law for graduates of the L-30 three-year degree who have earned the credits prescribed by the Acoustics course (offered as elective credits).
They have acquired knowledge in the field of Physics Education, useful for subsequent qualification paths for teaching.
