Autonomy of judgment.
Students must develop the ability to gather (through databases and dedicated literature) the information necessary to formulate an independent judgment and critical analysis, not only to compare experimental data with theoretical models, but also regarding scientific and ethical issues connected with research. Students must realize that falsifying, misrepresenting data, or committing plagiarism constitutes unethical scientific behavior and should achieve a level of maturity allowing them to be objective and rigorous in all aspects of their scientific work.
These abilities are primarily acquired in teaching and laboratory courses; they are verified through practical tests, discussions, and written work presentations.
Learning ability.
A degree in Physics and Advanced Technologies should foster certain learning abilities, including:
* problem-solving ability. Graduates must develop the ability to formulate problems and identify their key points; they must also become accustomed to trying different approaches to the same problem.
* research ability – Graduates must develop individual research ability. They must also be able to use advanced texts, search for information in databases and on the internet, and interact with colleagues, exchanging useful information;
* analytical ability – A basic education in physical disciplines helps the graduate to pay attention to details and develop the aptitude for rigorous reasoning, logical deduction construction, and correct use of scientific and technological language.
* computational ability – During their studies, graduates must develop the ability to use computer tools and the skill to use software and programming languages.
* personal abilities – Graduates must develop the ability to work independently, use their initiative, and organize in groups, interacting constructively in team work.
* learning ability – Verified in individual courses through written, oral tests, and discussions.
Ability to apply knowledge and understanding.
Generic Area At the end of the training path, the graduate is able to:
- formulate and solve physics problems, identify relevant physical principles and conservation laws, extrapolate parameters in limiting cases and calculate order of magnitude estimates, frame complex problems and propose efficient solutions, present results making explicit the assumptions and approximations used.
- use mathematical models to describe physical reality and understand their limits and approximations.
- plan, carry out, and present the results of an experiment, use appropriate data analysis methods and evaluate experimental uncertainty, critically compare theoretical model results with data from experimental observation.
Scientific and Methodological Foundations At the end of studies, the graduate is able to:
study functions of one variable (limits, derivatives, integrals), solve problems of analytical geometry in the plane and space concerning lines, planes, spheres, circles, conics, and quadrics, solve problems of differential calculus for functions of multiple variables, and related to differential equations and systems, use programming languages.
Basic Physical Sciences At the end of studies, the graduate is able to:
apply mathematical models and/or concepts to scientific problems in the fields of Mechanics, Thermodynamics, Electromagnetism, and Optics, correctly evaluate the order of magnitude of phenomena within Classical Physics, formalize and solve problems in this area.
Mathematical Physics and Theoretical Physics At the end of studies, the graduate is able to:
apply Laplace and Fourier transforms to differential systems, transform a physical problem into a mathematical one and, after solving it, interpret the physical result, systematically and rigorously translate a mechanical system into equations, solve it, and discuss the results; use Lagrangian and Hamiltonian formalisms to solve mechanics problems, determine the motion paths of system components; solve elementary problems in quantum mechanics.
Physics and Experimental Physics Laboratory Activities At the end of studies, the graduate is able to:
solve problems of discrete and continuous probability, design and carry out the measurement of a physical quantity and critically analyze experimental results, analyze electrical circuits, develop codes in C language and design data acquisition systems, use operational amplifiers and digital oscilloscopes for studying complex waveforms, design digital circuits and carry out experiments, including data acquisition, with advanced instrumentation: for example, spectroscopic measurements or cosmic ray rate measurements. They also have the ability to work in groups and write scientific reports on the experiments performed.
Modern Physics At the end of studies, the graduate is able to:
solve quantum mechanics problems related to Atomic Physics and Nuclear and Subnuclear Physics, formalize and solve problems concerning Matter Physics.
Applications in Related Fields At the end of studies, the graduate is able to:
integrate the knowledge provided by Physics courses from standard program teachings with in-depth studies related to disciplines focused on the best professional expertise expressed by DSFTA; frame an advanced physics topic within a broad scientific context that considers possible multidisciplinary applications where techniques and models characteristic of physical systems can offer innovative solutions.

Communication Skills.
Both Physics and the Mathematics used in Physics are based on concepts of a certain complexity; therefore, it is essential that graduates have acquired good communication skills. To obtain the degree, students are required to develop skills in carefully listening, reading advanced texts (also in English), and presenting information of a certain complexity clearly and concisely.
Presentation skills are stimulated in all courses and verified through oral examinations. Particular attention is paid to and developed in activities associated with laboratory courses. Some laboratory courses are expected to require the preparation and discussion of a written report presenting the problems addressed and the results achieved; this will allow verification of the ability to communicate both in written and oral form.

Additional information.
http://www.unisi.it http://www.dsfta.unisi.it Specific educational objectives description.
The Physics and Advanced Technologies Study Course aims to provide preparation equivalent to that of similar European degrees (e.g.: BSc English). The objective is to train graduates with:
- solid basic knowledge of classical and modern Physics;
- familiarity with the scientific method;
- good knowledge of mathematical and computer tools;
- operational and laboratory skills;
- ability to work independently and in groups;
- adequate professionalism for entry into the workforce.
The educational path that allows the acquisition of knowledge, skills, and competencies to achieve the specific educational objectives of the study course is, briefly:
- basic prerequisite knowledge in mathematics, computer science, chemistry, and at least one foreign language;
- basic prerequisite knowledge in Physics regarding classical mechanics, including Lagrangian and Hamiltonian formulation, thermodynamics, classical electromagnetism;
The overall set of basic disciplines receives a number of credits well above the minimum required by the DM, providing students with a solid basic preparation.
The educational path continues with characteristic training activities:
- strongly experimental and applied in nature, with a laboratory offering in every academic year capable of providing knowledge of statistical data processing, reinforcing problem-solving skills using experiences related to mechanics, acoustics, and thermodynamics, the basics of electrical circuit theory, as well as electricity and magnetism, and allowing familiarity with technologically advanced experiments to develop knowledge and skills related to electronics and photonics;
- introducing ideas and techniques of modern Physics and their applications in fields such as medicine, cultural heritage, energy production, materials study, environment;
- introducing concepts that historically led to the crisis of classical Physics and providing a basic preparation in Quantum Mechanics, suitable for an introduction to fundamental interactions physics, nuclear and elementary particle models, as well as topics in Solid State Physics, Atomic and Molecular Physics, and Molecular Physics.
The study path is integrated and personalized by the student, who now has a wide range of courses in related or complementary subjects to choose from, allowing students to tailor their curriculum in the fields of spectroscopy, materials science, medical physics, environment, geophysics, based on important scientific skills developed at the University of Siena's Department of Physics, Earth and Environment (DSFTA).
The educational path can therefore be structured into modules/courses referring to the following learning areas (thematic blocks):
Scientific and Methodological Fundamentals Includes basic non-physical scientific and technological disciplines (mathematics, chemistry, computer science), providing the necessary tools for adequate preparation in using languages and formalization in the physical context; these courses are preferably placed in the first year and refer to the SSDs required by the class for basic activities.
Basic Physics Sciences Includes a series of modules/courses common to frame the foundations of Physical Sciences within FIS/01, regarding theoretical and formal aspects. They are preferably distributed between the first and second year and cover: kinematics of translations and rotations, inertial and non-inertial reference systems, dynamics of material points, dynamics of systems, conservation laws of momentum, energy, and angular momentum, fluid dynamics, thermodynamics, electromagnetism, generation and propagation of electromagnetic waves, physical and geometric optics.
Mathematical and Theoretical Physics Includes a series of courses/modules in SSD FIS/02 covering: formalization of dynamics of material points and systems in Lagrangian-Hamiltonian formulation, spectral analysis according to Fourier and Laplace developments, introduction to the formalism of non-relativistic quantum mechanics in Dirac and Heisenberg versions.
Physics and Experimental Physics Laboratory Activities Includes a series of common modules/courses in SSD FIS/01 and FIS/07 covering: statistical data processing, measurements in mechanics, acoustics, and thermodynamics, measurements in electromagnetism, electrical circuits in direct and alternating current, measurements in analog and digital electronics, microelectronics measurements, data acquisition and analysis techniques, experimental measurements and techniques commonly used in physics research laboratories, such as cosmic ray measurements, laser spectroscopy measurements, and applied optics.
Modern Physics Includes a series of common modules/courses in relevant SSDs for specific training (FIS/01, FIS/03, FIS/04) covering: elements of special relativity, crisis of classical mechanics, key experiments in the transition to quantum mechanics, atomic physics, elements of molecular physics, elements of spectroscopy, introduction to solid state physics, nuclear physics, elementary particle physics, radioactive phenomena.
Applications in Related Fields Includes courses in complementary scientific fields capable of providing a more comprehensive view and more versatile preparation, leveraging internal departmental skills in the Department of Physics, Earth and Environment. These courses belong to SSDs FIS/01, FIS/07, FIS/08, MAT/04, MAT/07, MAT/08, CHIM/05, CHIM/12, GEO/06, GEO/10, GEO/11, ING-INF/01, ING-IND/22, and cover: applied physics to medicine, numerical calculus, applications of spectroscopy to environmental study and protection, theoretical study and experimental investigation techniques of crystals, elements of materials science, advanced electronic circuits, geophysics, sustainability.
The educational path is completed by language knowledge (English skills at least at B1 level), training internships and orientation that allow students to interact with work environments both outside the Academy and at public research institutions, and a final examination.

Accounting Expert and Business Analyst Graduates of the course, with reference to the business environment, will be able to hold managerial and operational functions already mentioned in the context of: private companies of any size operating in any economic sector; business consulting firms; non-profit organizations; public companies; business, sector, and trade union associations. Banking Operator and Financial Consultant Graduates of the course, with reference to the banking and financial sector, will be able to hold operational functions already mentioned in banks, insurance companies, and financial intermediaries, or front and back office roles. Economic Analyst Graduates of the course, with reference to the economic-social sector, will be able to leverage their skills to hold the functions already mentioned in the context of: private companies operating in any economic sector; research offices of national and international organizations and entities; economic consulting firms; non-profit organizations and third-sector organizations; public companies; business, sector, and trade union associations. Graduates may also perform operational activities in professional consulting contexts, with particular regard to aspects related to economic activities.
Final Exam Characteristics The degree is obtained by passing a final exam consisting of the evaluation by the graduation committee of the final work written by the student under the supervision of a thesis advisor.
The final work consists of a brief document, accompanied by the necessary bibliographic references, on a theoretical or empirical topic.
To pass the final exam, the student must demonstrate having acquired, in addition to adequate knowledge and understanding of the chosen topic, autonomous learning and research abilities; the ability to correctly use the consulted literature and necessary data sources; the ability to present and defend scientific arguments in a logical and coherent manner.
The final exam is worth 3 CFU.
Required Knowledge for Admission To be admitted to the Bachelor's Degree Course, one must possess a secondary school diploma or another foreign degree recognized as suitable. The knowledge required for admission to the Bachelor's Degree Course is that acquired at the secondary school level, with particular reference to the mathematical field, in addition to a basic general culture. The specific content of the required mathematical knowledge for admission will be indicated in the course's teaching regulations. Additionally, knowledge of the English language at least at level B2 (CEFR) is required.
The evaluation of the student's initial preparation will be conducted according to the criteria and methods detailed in the course's teaching regulations. It will be based on a test, developed and conducted nationally, aimed at verifying the aptitude and minimum preparation required to undertake economic studies, through verbal comprehension tests, basic mathematical knowledge, and simple elementary logic problems. The evaluation of English language knowledge will be conducted through tests carried out in collaboration with the Siena University Language Center. The course's teaching regulations establish the additional educational obligations in case of a negative evaluation of the access test and the English language test; these obligations must be fulfilled in the first year of the course, possibly through specific recovery courses in mathematics and English organized by the relevant departments.
Knowledge and Understanding.
General Area With reference to the business environment, the graduate in Economics and Management possesses the basic knowledge to critically address management planning and control issues, and to prepare and analyze measurement and financial reporting documents. Additionally, they know and understand the role and functioning of capital markets in the allocation of financial resources.
With reference to the banking and financial sector, the graduate possesses adequate knowledge of different financial intermediaries, with particular regard to the risks assumed in the intermediation processes. They know and understand the functioning of financial markets and instruments, the processes of portfolio construction and analysis. They know and understand the role of technological innovation and the importance of its applications in the financial sector (Fintech).
With reference to the economic sector, the graduate possesses a good knowledge of the main economic models, both microeconomic and macroeconomic, and of the determinants, also from a historical perspective, of the main economic variables (GDP, inflation rate, exchange rate). They know and understand the economic and social context of consumer and business behavior, the market conditions influencing their behavior both from an individual and social perspective, and the social impact of economic policy measures aimed at countering market failures.
With reference to the legal sector, the graduate knows and understands legal terminology, even in an international context; masters the main institutions of private law and public law and the principles regarding the legal regulation of individual and collective business, also with reference to EU law.
With reference to the quantitative sector, the graduate in Economics and Management knows the mathematical tools useful for making economic decisions; masters the basic statistical tools, understanding their use in both descriptive and inferential contexts. They know the mathematical tools for micro and macroeconomic choices, for the analysis of interest rates, annuities, and amortization. They know the main tools for data analysis.
The graduate in Economics and Management has excellent knowledge of the English language and high ability to understand written and spoken English. These knowledge and comprehension abilities must be acquired and verified primarily through the curricular courses and their respective passing exams in the various fields.
Business Area The graduate in Economics and Management possesses a good mastery of the theory and technique of business management, and the theory and technique of preparing a business balance sheet, whether for a private or public company. They have a good knowledge of national accounting principles (OIC) and international ones (IFRS); know analytical accounting and are able to understand its results in terms of costs, revenues, and operational margins related to specific business segments.
The graduate will acquire basic knowledge of Financial Intermediaries, Financial Markets, Corporate Finance, and tools to analyze and understand investment decisions.
The graduate knows and understands the role and functioning of capital markets in the allocation of financial resources. In this context, they know and understand the structure and functioning of financial markets, financial intermediaries, and the essential characteristics of financial instruments and products. They know and understand the main differences between credit intermediaries, insurance intermediaries, securities intermediaries, with particular regard to the types of risks assumed. They know and understand the functions and characteristics of bond, equity, and derivative instruments from a portfolio perspective.
The graduate in Economics and Management knows and understands the specifics of banking and insurance and the new role they have assumed in the financial system and in the allocation and management of savings as a result of the implementation of technological innovations that are modifying traditional business models. They know banking operations and have a good knowledge of bank management balances, with particular reference to risk management and capital and economic balances, as well as the determinants of bank performance. They know the evolutionary processes present in the banking and financial world related to Fintech.
Economic Area The graduate in Economics and Management possesses a good knowledge of the historical evolution of the economy and is able to understand how economic variables have influenced the decisions of economic operators over time.
The graduate possesses a good knowledge of the main economic models, both microeconomic and macroeconomic, and of the determinants of the main economic variables (GDP, inflation rate, exchange rate), and is able to understand and interpret the economic and social context, conduct an analysis of the market conditions in which the company operates, and develop a consequent business strategy, also regarding international markets.
Depending on the curriculum and chosen courses, the graduate possesses:
a) a rigorous basic knowledge of the main quantitative methods and data analysis, enabling the use of tools to set up, process, and evaluate a basic empirical project, also through learning the functionalities and use of econometric packages for social sciences;
b) knowledge of topics related to international markets, globalization, and policies to control the effects on inequality, based on the latest theories and models;
c) knowledge of topics concerning social and economic aspects highlighted by behavioral theories and the application of analysis tools specific to experimental economics;
d) knowledge of the theoretical and empirical foundations of imperfect markets (monopoly, oligopoly, monopolistic competition), including the analysis of competition/collusion levels with reference to variables such as market power, price discrimination, vertical relationships, product differentiation, advertising, research and development.
Legal Area The graduate in Economics and Management knows and understands legal terminology; knows the main institutions of private law (rights of persons, property rights, obligations and their sources) and public law (the Italian Constitution and the Italian political system with references to the European system).
The graduate knows principles regarding the legal regulation of individual and collective business, with particular attention to the practical and applied aspects of the studied institutions, and, depending on the chosen curriculum, a complete knowledge of harmonized European legislation regarding business and company law.
Also depending on the optional courses chosen in the third year, the graduate knows and understands the basics of domestic and community special legislation regarding banking, financial, and insurance companies, and, in particular, has a full understanding of the institutional mechanisms underlying the formation of the banking system, the specificities of banks (and the products offered), and the supervision methods (national and community) applicable to them. Finally, the graduate, through the analysis of the main institutions characterizing administration from the perspective of its organization, activities, and relations with other subjects of the system, acquires the necessary tools to understand the framework of principles and rules that public subjects and private subjects (under certain profiles) equated to them must adhere to.
Mathematical-Statistical Area The graduate in Economics and Management has a good knowledge and understanding of the basic tools of mathematical analysis and linear algebra necessary for statistical, economic, financial, and social analyses. Additionally, they know the tools of probability calculus and the main methods of descriptive and inferential statistics; in particular, the graduate has knowledge focused on the collection, analysis, synthesis, and interpretation of economic, business, and financial data.
The graduate knows and understands mathematical techniques for analyzing interest rates, annuities, and amortization. They have a good mastery of the fundamental elements for the quantitative study of profiles related to financial instruments.
Finally, depending on the curriculum and chosen courses, they possess a rigorous basic training in econometric theory, with particular reference to the multiple regression model, and a good knowledge of statistical methods for multivariate data analysis.

UNIVERSITY: University of Siena
COURSE: [D339] ECONOMICS AND MANAGEMENT English
SECTION: Autonomy of Judgment

Autonomy of Judgment.
The autonomy of judgment represents an essential quality of the Economics and Management graduate, as they will commonly operate in dynamic and complex contexts, both micro and macro, where they must make decisions or express evaluations.
In particular, at the end of the course, the Economics and Management graduate:
- is able to express autonomous and rigorous assessments on the management profiles of a company, using data derived from the annual financial statement and the main economic and financial reports, as well as obtained through the application of mathematical-statistical processing methodologies;
- thanks to the ability to retrieve, process, and analyze quantitative and qualitative data, is able to express themselves correctly, comprehensively, and rationally regarding the analysis of the trends of the main economic variables and their effects in micro and macroeconomic terms;
- thanks to their knowledge and skills acquired in the legal field, is able to provide well-founded judgments on the relationships and formal legal relationships that companies and economic institutions establish with various stakeholders, such as employees, suppliers, and customers;
- is able to rationally evaluate financing, communication, reporting, and strategic planning options at the corporate level;
- will demonstrate full awareness in addressing and resolving problems related to choosing between different financing and investment opportunities, identifying the consequences of each decision not only in economic and financial terms, but also social and political terms.
The Economics and Management graduate is able to apply these analytical, judgmental, and evaluative skills in various contexts and in relation to very diverse realities, both at the micro and macroeconomic level.
These skills are developed through continuous critical discussion with professors and through a range of participatory student activities, such as project works, case studies, and presentations.
The autonomy and flexibility of judgment of the Economics and Management graduate are further ensured and tested through seminars and study groups dedicated to the analysis and interpretation of empirical data relevant to micro and macroeconomic decision-making. For some of these training activities, collaboration with particularly qualified experts from the professional world is provided.
The work related to the final thesis is another important opportunity for Economics and Management students to develop, from a theoretical and/or practical perspective, their autonomy of judgment, for example through methodologies such as case study analysis or field research.
Finally, the development of an autonomous and creative judgment capacity is guaranteed and verified through active participation in seminars aimed at acquiring soft skills (such as complex problem solving, teamwork, organizational and leadership abilities) in collaboration with other university structures.
Learning Ability.
The Economics and Management graduate, thanks to the teaching activities and techniques provided in this program and the study method acquired, is able to learn, apply, and adapt operational techniques for collecting, measuring, analyzing, reporting, and communicating available data and information.
Furthermore, at the end of their studies, the Economics and Management graduate will demonstrate:
- a substantial improvement in the ability to leverage available information to analyze and solve problems at both micro and macroeconomic levels, and in relation to the legal sphere of the analyzed contexts;
- a better inclination to actively integrate into work environments where their skills and knowledge must be applied;
- an improved ability to manage and effectively use their soft skills (such as complex problem solving, teamwork, and leadership).
These abilities are progressively acquired, developed, and reinforced throughout the degree program, not only through a study method suited to the purpose, but also thanks to teaching activities and techniques that support students in preparing for intermediate and final assessments, as well as for the final thesis.
The aforementioned assessments will be useful for continuously evaluating these learning abilities. The final thesis will also contribute to assessing the self-learning ability of the Economics and Management student. It should be noted that learning abilities are achieved both through individual study and collectively through participation in activities such as seminars and group work.
Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
General Area. Thanks to knowledge of accounting techniques and financial statement preparation, the Economics and Management graduate is able to manage corporate accounting, critically analyzing the flow of data on costs and revenues and identifying potential critical issues. They are also able to calculate the product cost for the company and organize and manage internal auditing processes. The graduate is able to prepare and analyze the corporate financial statement of a national company and analyze a financial statement prepared according to international standards. They will be able to monitor the economic, financial, and equity balance of the company, with particular attention to companies operating in an international context.
Thanks to knowledge of markets, financial instruments, and intermediaries, the Economics and Management graduate is able to analyze and manage a basic portfolio in terms of performance and risk measurement. They are also capable of evaluating the equity and economic balances of banks and insurance companies, with particular attention to credit risk. They can also assess the impact of technological innovations by applying bancassurance solutions and alternative financing techniques such as crowdfunding.
Thanks to knowledge of the functioning mechanisms of the macroeconomic and microeconomic markets and other acquired economic knowledge, the Economics and Management graduate is able to conduct a critical analysis of the economic cycle and its effects on consumer and firm decisions; they are capable of analyzing the behavior of consumers and firms in relevant markets and developing decision-making processes of economic agents and optimal strategies for firms, both in the short and long term; they understand the basic dynamics of major international markets, also from a historical perspective and their social impact.
Thanks to legal knowledge, the Economics and Management graduate is able to critically manage the legal constraints of the company, with particular attention to contracts the company must establish, and analyze the effects that changes in national, community, and international regulations may have on the company's short and long-term decisions.
Thanks to acquired quantitative knowledge, the Economics and Management graduate is able to apply mathematical-statistical models to the analysis of micro and macroeconomic data, having the ability to use these tools to obtain statistically robust indicators of the company's situation and to make reliable forecasts of the future trends of relevant variables for the company. They are able to creatively use the most important computer programs for business and economic analysis.
The Economics and Management graduate is able to communicate fluently in English and write correctly economic texts in English, thus integrating effectively into an international work team.
The ability to apply knowledge and understanding is acquired through curricular courses, seminar activities involving professionals from the workplace, and participation in training experiences aimed at acquiring soft skills.
The preparation of the thesis represents an important opportunity for students to apply the knowledge acquired.
The ability to apply knowledge and understanding is primarily verified through profit exams and thesis evaluation.
Business Area. Thanks to knowledge of accounting techniques and financial statement preparation, the Economics and Management graduate is able to manage corporate accounting, critically analyzing the flow of data on costs and revenues and identifying potential critical issues. They are also able to calculate the product cost for the company and organize and manage internal auditing processes. The graduate is able to prepare and analyze the corporate financial statement of a national company and analyze a financial statement prepared according to international standards. They will be able to monitor the economic, financial, and equity balance of the company.
Depending on the curriculum and chosen courses, the Economics and Management graduate is able to, at a basic level, assess the impact of corporate financial decisions on value creation for shareholders. The graduate is capable of critically analyzing the differences between capital markets with varying degrees of orientation toward intermediaries and markets, interpreting the consequences on the development model of different geographical areas and the trends of international capital markets. They are able to recognize different business models of financial companies, evaluating their risks and performance, also in relation to the economic and regulatory context. They are able to critically interpret the innovation of financial instruments, recognizing the role each instrument plays in meeting the needs of issuers and investors. They are able to manage a portfolio of financial instruments, measuring expected risks and performance, and using financial databases.
The graduate is able to compare and evaluate different banking business models, interpret the lending and collection policies implemented by banking companies. They are able to, at a basic level, conduct a credit risk analysis of fund borrowers. They are capable of understanding the contractual structures of collection and investment operations, evaluating the risks and costs for the involved parties. They are able to critically analyze the equity and economic balances of banks. They are able to interpret the evolution of the banking industry in the face of increasing technological development. They are able to, at a basic level, assess the impact of international regulation, its expected costs and benefits.
Economic Area. Thanks to acquired knowledge, the Economics and Management graduate is able to conduct a critical analysis of major historical-economic phenomena as a guide to understanding current economic evolution, also from a social impact perspective.
Thanks to knowledge of the functioning mechanisms of the macroeconomic market, the Economics and Management graduate is capable of conducting a critical analysis of the economic cycle and its effects on consumer and firm decisions.
In light of knowledge of microeconomic market functioning and the analysis of firm decisions in various market forms, the Economics and Management graduate is able to analyze the relevant market for the company and develop the optimal strategy for the company, both in the short and long term, also with reference to sustainability.
Depending on the curriculum and chosen courses, the Economics and Management graduate is able to organize their own data set, specify estimation equations, and statistically test hypotheses suggested by economic theory, understand the different constraints imposed by market forms and strategic interdependence with other firms operating in the same sector, address the issue of efficient and sustainable resource use, participate in debates on related policies by acquiring some of the specific competencies of a socio-economic impact analyst of macro policy choices, a market trend analyst, and more generally of socio-economic impacts of competition and regulation.
Legal Area. The Economics and Management graduate is able to critically manage the legal constraints of the company, with particular attention to contracts the company must establish with suppliers and customers.
The graduate is able to analyze the effects that national, community, and international regulations, both common and special law (banking, financial, and insurance), may have on the company's short and long-term decisions.
Also depending on optional courses chosen in the third year, the Economics and Management graduate is able to apply national and community banking, insurance, and financial regulations to concrete cases, recognizing their specific aspects compared to common law for companies. They are also able to manage the framework of principles and rules to which public subjects and private subjects (under certain aspects) equated must adhere. Finally, they are able to manage legal relationships with employed staff and the legal constraints arising from the company's international expansion.
Mathematical-Statistical Area. The Economics and Management graduate is able to apply mathematical tools and statistical techniques to the analysis of microeconomic and macroeconomic data and the study of company data flows. In particular, from company data, the graduate is able to evaluate firm performance, identify costs and benefits based on possible choices, analyze consumer demand structure, and critically assess strategic growth or consolidation hypotheses.
The graduate is able to perform the main quantitative assessments of financial and credit instruments, critically compare the market prices of bonds, and clearly articulate a financial valuation or decision problem.
Finally, depending on optional courses chosen in the third year, the Economics and Management graduate is able to estimate a multivariate regression model and apply the most important multivariate techniques to complex data systems, interpreting the results.

Communication Skills.
The graduate in Economics and Management possesses lexical and terminological knowledge, as well as full mastery of technical language in the fields of political economy, business economics, corporate finance, law (private and public), quantitative analysis, mathematics, and statistics. The graduate in Economics and Management is able to communicate clearly, comprehensively, and correctly the results of their work, knowing how to highlight the sources, applied methodologies, and techniques for interpreting the data and information used.
The graduate in Economics and Management is able to clearly highlight and communicate the relevance of the topics addressed, the nature of the issues faced, the value, originality, and implications of the results obtained and the proposed solutions.
In their communication actions, the graduate in Economics and Management is able to use a wide range of languages, not only verbal and textual, but also accounting and mathematical-statistical. In this sense, the graduate is able to adapt and modify their communication format according to the reference context, their interlocutors, and the specific situation faced, always maintaining a high level of expressive and communicative effectiveness.
At the end of an English-language program, the graduate in Economics and Management has valid communication skills in English, both written and oral, enabling effective and full interaction within the work context they will face. The course also includes credits aimed at further deepening English language knowledge, and ensuring knowledge of the Italian language for students whose native language is different from Italian. Communication skills are acquired and assessed through ongoing and final written and/or oral evaluations, through the preparation and presentation in class of business cases and reports, as well as through the final exam.
The development of good communication skills is enhanced and tested through active participation in seminars and other initiatives aimed at acquiring and/or reinforcing soft skills (such as complex problem solving, teamwork, organizational ability, and leadership) in collaboration with other structures of the University of Siena.
Expected occupational and professional opportunities for graduates.
Accounting Expert and Business Analyst. Graduates of the course, with reference to the business environment, can hold managerial and operational roles within: private companies of any size operating in any economic sector; business consulting firms; non-profit organizations; public companies; business, sector, and trade union associations. Graduates may also perform professional consulting activities related to administrative matters and management control in all the aforementioned contexts. Graduates may also practice as independent professionals (following the successful completion of the necessary state exams to register with professional bodies, registers, etc.).
Banking Operator and Financial Consultant. Graduates of the course, with reference to the banking and financial sector, can hold the operational roles already mentioned in banks, insurance companies, and financial intermediary firms, or front and back office positions. They may also practice as financial promoters and/or independent financial consultants following the successful completion of the necessary exams to register with professional bodies.
Economic Analyst. Graduates of the course, with reference to the economic-social sector, can leverage their competencies to hold the roles already mentioned within: private companies operating in any economic sector; research offices of national and international organizations and institutions; economic consulting firms; non-profit organizations and third-sector entities; public companies; business, sector, and trade union associations. Graduates may also perform operational activities in professional consulting contexts, particularly regarding economic aspects.
Official teaching and assessment languages.
ENGLISH Associated competencies.
Accounting Expert and Business Analyst. Graduates of the course, with reference to the business environment, will be able to effectively apply the acquired skills and competencies in the areas of administration and management control to carry out, within reference organizations, activities related to the measurement and reporting of financial and non-financial performance, accounting analysis, cost analysis, and the use of business data (including digital data), sustainability control, and corporate social responsibility. Graduates will also possess legal and mathematical-statistical skills that will complement their profile.
Banking Operator and Financial Consultant. Ability to monitor banking lending processes and analyze and manage risks related to financial intermediary activities. Portfolio analysis and support for the decision-making activities of managers. Financial consulting within public or private institutions.
Economic Analyst. Graduates of the course, with reference to the economic-social sector, will have a good understanding of economic phenomena and, in particular, the functioning of markets, the ability to connect and develop micro and macroeconomic analyses, and good competence in using the main quantitative analysis techniques for investigating economic phenomena. Graduates will also possess legal skills and basic tools of the business area, which will complement their profile and enable them to aspire to roles requiring both analytical and more operational functions.
Role in the workplace context.
Accounting Expert and Business Analyst. Graduates of the course, with reference to the business environment, will be able to carry out a wide range of activities in managerial and management control areas for companies of any size operating in various economic sectors. Regarding employment areas, graduates may hold leadership roles, employee or self-employed positions, including in the form of independent practice, leveraging competencies drawn from various foundational areas (business, economic, mathematical-statistical, and legal), with a focus on management and corporate control.
Banking Operator and Financial Consultant. Graduates of the course, with reference to the banking and financial sector, will be able to assume operational responsibilities in banking and insurance intermediaries, particularly in the financial services and commercial sectors, in the processing and monitoring of lending procedures, risk management, internal control activities, and client-facing consulting services. The distinctive feature of the proposed program allows operation in asset management companies and new financial entities based on technological financialization processes (Fintech).
Economic Analyst. The course, with reference to the economic-social sector, aims to train professional economists capable of carrying out a wide range of activities in multiple contexts within public and private, national and international organizations and entities. The acquired competencies in interpreting and analyzing economic phenomena will enable graduates to enter the workforce in positions requiring versatility and analytical skills, understanding the economic aspects of decisions and their economic repercussions, as well as the ability to address contexts characterized by dynamism and high complexity.
Description of specific educational objectives.
The Bachelor's degree in Economics and Management adopts a multidisciplinary approach to studying the processes of business management, banking and insurance intermediary models, and financial markets and disciplines in the economic and statistical-quantitative areas.
Overall, the training path of the Economics and Management degree aims to form students by imparting knowledge and competencies related to four main disciplinary areas:
1) Economic, which includes microeconomic and macroeconomic courses (SECS-P0/1), economic policy (SECS-P/01), and economic history (SECS-P/12).
2) Business, which includes courses in relevant disciplinary areas for the training path (SECS-P/07, SECS-P/08, SECS-P/09, and SECS-P/11).
3) Legal, which includes courses providing the foundations of private, commercial, economic, community, and international law, as well as public law (IUS/01, IUS/04, IUS/05, IUS/14, and IUS/09).
4) Mathematical-Statistical, with courses ranging from general and financial mathematics (SECS-S/06) to statistics (SECS-S/01).
In line with the diverse training needs and professional profiles required by the labor market and relevant stakeholders, after a broad common path, the Economics and Management course is structured into three curricula aimed at developing more specific competencies in the managerial, banking-financial, or economic-social areas.
All training paths within the course satisfy the requirements of both classes, allowing students to choose until the final year of the course in which class to obtain their degree.
The course, with reference to the management area, aims to train graduates with knowledge and competencies across the four foundational areas (business, economic, mathematical-statistical, and legal), with a primary focus on the topics of administration and management control. Through the characteristic courses of this path, the course provides, in particular, the basic knowledge necessary to critically address problems of planning and management control, and to prepare and analyze corporate performance measurement and reporting documents (SECS-P/07). In particular, in the final part of the study path, students will acquire specific competencies in the economic-business area and management, including innovative and highly current topics such as digital management (SECS-P/08) and corporate social responsibility (SECS-P/07).
The course, with reference to the banking and financial area, aims to train graduates with a good knowledge of capital markets and financial intermediary processes (SECS-P/09 and SECS-P/11). The training will be completed with legal, economic, and technical-financial competencies aimed at evaluating investment choices and the possibilities of providing loans to natural and legal persons. In the final year, to align the training path with new needs arising from the evolution of the work environment, Fintech and Digital Banking topics (SECS-P/11) and their implications in the operational world are also examined.
The course, with reference to the economic-social area, provides the basic knowledge necessary to critically address interdisciplinary problems where economic analysis techniques are combined with tools for reading economic-social phenomena in a broader sense. In particular, in the final part of the study path, students acquire specific competencies in the micro and macroeconomic areas with reference to innovative and highly current topics such as inequality (SECS-P/02), behavioral economics (SECS-P/01), the functioning of economic and social organizations, always within a perspective that allows capturing evolution over time (SECS-P/12), with attention to data analysis supporting decision-making (SECS-S/01).
Additional linguistic knowledge is allocated a sufficient number of credits for the study of economic English and the Italian language for foreign students. Parallelly, Italian students are provided with further deepening of English language knowledge.
The course also allows the acquisition of soft skills (such as complex problem solving, teamwork, organizational ability, and leadership), planned and developed in collaboration with other university structures.
Finally, graduates can acquire competencies through internship and training experiences.

- in business, sector and trade union associations Characteristics of final exam The Economics and Commerce degree is obtained by passing a final exam consisting of the evaluation by the graduation committee of the final work written by the student under the supervision of a faculty advisor. The final work consists of a short paper, accompanied by the necessary bibliographic references, on a theoretical or empirical topic chosen by the student according to the procedures defined by a regulation on the final exam prepared by the competent teaching structure.
To pass the final exam, the student must demonstrate having acquired, in addition to adequate knowledge and understanding of the chosen topic, autonomous ability to learn and research; the ability to correctly use the consulted literature and necessary data sources; the ability to present and defend scientific arguments in a logical and coherent manner.
The final work can be written in English; it must be written in English if students graduate in a study path conducted in English.
The final exam is worth 3 CFU. The score of the final exam is expressed in hundredths. The graduation committee assigns a score for the final exam that takes into account the average expressed in hundredths of the grades obtained in the profit exams, increased by any additional points provided for in the regulation for the final exam for specific academic merits, and the quality of the written work. If the overall evaluation is above 110/110, the committee unanimously may award honors.

For the English language curriculum, English language knowledge at least at level B2 (CEFR) is required.

English language knowledge will be assessed through tests conducted in collaboration with the University of Siena Language Center. The study program's teaching regulation establishes the additional training obligations in case of negative assessment of the access test and the English language knowledge test, possibly in the form of specific recovery courses in mathematics and English organized by the Departments.
For foreign students, the study program's teaching regulation determines the procedures through which the presence of the basic knowledge necessary to successfully attend the bachelor's degree program can be verified.

The graduate knows and understands the legal language and the fundamentals of public and private law. Possesses a good knowledge of basic mathematical and statistical tools.

Economic Area The graduate in Economics and Commerce possesses a good knowledge of the historical evolution of economics and is able to understand how economic variables have influenced the decisions of economic operators over time.
The graduate in Economics and Commerce possesses a good knowledge of the main economic models, both microeconomic and macroeconomic, and of the determinants of the main economic variables (GDP, inflation rate, exchange rate), and is able to understand and interpret the reference economic framework, conduct a market analysis in which the company operates, and develop a consequent business strategy.
Depending on the chosen curriculum, the graduate in Economics and Commerce possesses a) a deep knowledge of the interpretative models of the state's role in the economy and is able to understand the mechanisms through which the tax system and public expenditure influence the decisions of consumers and companies;
b) a knowledge of the behavioral model of the enterprise in various market forms in which it operates, with particular attention to pricing and production strategies in situations of strategic interdependence and to technological innovation strategies.
Business Area The graduate in Economics and Commerce possesses a good mastery of the theory and technique of business management, and of the theory and technique of preparing a business balance sheet, whether for a private or public company. Has a good knowledge of national accounting principles (OIC) and (depending on the chosen courses) a good knowledge of international accounting principles (IFRS); knows analytical accounting and is able to understand its results in terms of costs, revenues, and operating margins for specific business segments.

Legal Area The graduate in Economics and Commerce knows and understands legal terminology; knows the main institutions of private law (rights of persons, property rights, obligations and their sources) and public law (the Italian Constitution and the Italian political system with references to the European system).
The graduate in Economics and Commerce knows the principles relating to the legal regulation of individual and collective enterprises, with particular attention to the practical and applied aspects of the studied institutions.
Depending on the curriculum and chosen courses, the graduate knows and understands the basics of labor market legislation and the relationships between employees and companies, tax legislation with particular attention to the fiscal obligations of the company, international trade and transnational investment legislation, administrative law, and legal relationships between private individuals and State bodies.
Quantitative Area The graduate in Economics and Commerce must know the mathematical analysis tools, with particular attention to mathematical tools useful for making economic decisions (basic tools for maximization and optimization).
The graduate in Economics and Commerce must know the main statistical tools, understanding their use both in descriptive and inferential contexts; must know the main institutions of descriptive statistics and probability, understanding their relevance and effectiveness within the business management process.
The graduate in Economics and Commerce knows and understands the mathematical tools for analyzing interest rates, annuities, and amortization. Knows the mathematical tools for analyzing and pricing bonds and for analyzing the structure of the bond and financial market.

Judgment Autonomy.
Judgment autonomy constitutes a fundamental characteristic of the graduate in Economics and Commerce, who frequently operates in contexts where information is incomplete and uncertain and must make decisions or express reasoned evaluations in complex situations involving strategic interaction among multiple actors.
In particular, the graduate:
- is able to express autonomous and rigorous evaluations on the health status of a company, both regarding the income statement and the balance sheet, thanks to the ability to select, collect, and process quantitative and qualitative data, and knowledge of management and reporting techniques;
- is able to express informed opinions on the trends of major economic variables and the impact that the micro and macroeconomic framework may have on corporate performance, thanks to knowledge and skills acquired in the economic field and statistical knowledge;
- is capable of expressing well-founded opinions and judgments on relationships and formal legal matters that the company establishes with employees, suppliers, and customers, thanks to knowledge and skills acquired in the legal field;
- is able to critically evaluate corporate consolidation plans and development strategies, including long-term ones, as well as market expansion strategies, thanks to skills and knowledge acquired in the field of corporate strategy and marketing.
The graduate is able to apply this analytical capacity to very diverse business realities, regardless of the company's size and ownership structure.
The graduate's judgment autonomy and flexibility are acquired and verified through seminars and study groups dedicated to the analysis and interpretation of empirical data relevant to business decisions: for such training activities, collaboration with particularly qualified experts from the business world is also provided. The preparatory work for the final exam is another important opportunity for Economics and Commerce students to practice preparing a reasoned and scientifically rigorous report on a topic of particular interest that demonstrates their autonomous evaluation capability.
The development of an autonomous and creative judgment capacity is enhanced through participation in seminars aimed at acquiring soft skills (such as planning and organization, communication skills, problem solving, teamwork, leadership capacity) in collaboration with other university structures.
Learning Ability.
The graduate in Economics and Commerce, thanks to the study method acquired, is able to independently update and deepen the studied content; is able to learn, master, and modify techniques that may spread subsequently in all professional contexts consistent with the training objective of the degree course; is able to participate critically and creatively in organizational learning processes within innovative companies.
The solid theoretical preparation in economic, business, quantitative, and legal fields enables the graduate to undertake subsequent studies with a high level of autonomy and excellent prospects for success.
Learning abilities are acquired throughout the entire study path, both through individual study, and through participation in seminars and group work, as well as in the activities carried out for the preparation of the final exam.
The ability to learn is assessed through final and ongoing verification of training activities and through the evaluation of self-learning capabilities developed during the final exam activity.
Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area Thanks to the solid foundational preparation acquired, the graduate in Economics and Commerce:
- has the possibility to critically address the most important economic-business problems;
- is able to use the acquired theoretical knowledge to conduct critical analysis processes of the investigated business realities;
- is capable of preparing and analyzing business planning and reporting documents;
- is able to use the acquired theoretical knowledge to perform managerial or consulting functions in companies, whether private or public, and whether small, medium, or large in size.
These competencies are acquired and verified using as study material both theoretical and empirical articles, business cases, strategic plans, and corporate reporting documents, as well as proposing in-class and exam exercises on current and concrete cases and problems.
Economic Area Thanks to the acquired knowledge, the graduate in Economics and Commerce is able to conduct a critical analysis of major historical-economic phenomena as a guide to understanding current economic evolution.
Thanks to knowledge of the functioning mechanisms of the macroeconomic market, the graduate in Economics and Commerce is capable of conducting a critical analysis of the economic cycle and its effects on consumer and business choices.
Due to knowledge of the functioning of microeconomic markets and the analysis of business decisions in various market forms, the graduate in Economics and Commerce is able to analyze the company's reference market and develop the optimal corporate strategy in both the short and long term.
As a result of knowledge of public and industrial economics models (depending on the curriculum and chosen courses), the graduate in Economics and Commerce is able to evaluate the impact that changes in taxation and public spending may have on businesses, consumer choices, as well as the different constraints imposed by market forms and strategic interdependence with other companies operating in the same sector.
Additionally, the graduate in Economics and Commerce is able to apply the acquired knowledge to analyze corporate innovation strategies and policies.
Business Area Thanks to knowledge of accounting techniques and financial reporting, the graduate is able to manage corporate accounting, critically analyzing the flow of cost and revenue data and identifying potential issues. Additionally, they are able to calculate the product cost for the company and organize and manage internal audit processes.
The graduate in Economics and Commerce is able to prepare and analyze the corporate balance sheet of a national company and analyze a balance sheet prepared according to international standards. They will be able to monitor the economic, financial, and equity conditions of the company.
The graduate in Economics and Commerce is capable, through the analysis of various synthetic indices studied, of highlighting critical areas in corporate performance and purchasing and sales decisions, and to correctly plan appropriate strategies aimed at improving corporate results.
The graduate in Economics and Commerce is able to develop and plan corporate strategy, analyze sales markets for products and growth and consolidation prospects, and develop marketing strategies and study the best policies for the company's market penetration (especially in one of the two curricula in which the degree course is structured).
Legal Area The graduate in Economics and Commerce is able to critically manage the legal constraints of the company, with particular attention to contracts the company must establish with suppliers and customers.
The graduate in Economics and Commerce is able to analyze the effects that national legislation and, depending on the curriculum, EU and international legislation may have on the company's short and long-term choices, on relations with employees, and with public administrations.
Depending on the curriculum and chosen courses, the graduate is able to manage the tax legislation affecting the company and organize and comply with its obligations. They are also able to evaluate the effect that such legislation may have on the company's short and long-term choices. They are able to manage legal relations with employed personnel and legal issues arising from the company's international expansion.
Quantitative Area The graduate in Economics and Commerce is able to apply the studied mathematical-statistical models to the analysis of micro and macroeconomic data, having the ability to use these tools both to obtain statistically robust indicators of the microeconomic and macroeconomic situation in which the company operates and to make reliable forecasts of the future trends of relevant variables for business decisions.
The graduate is able to apply mathematical-statistical methods to the analysis of business data flows to evaluate corporate performance, analyze the costs and benefits of different possible choices, analyze consumer demand structure, and critically assess strategic growth or consolidation hypotheses.
The graduate is able to perform the main quantitative evaluations of financial and credit instruments relevant to the company, critically compare market prices of bonds, and clearly articulate a financial evaluation or decision problem.

The graduate is able to adopt a variety of registers that allow adapting and modifying the communication format according to the specialization level of their interlocutors, thus always maintaining a high level of communicative effectiveness.
The graduate in Economics and Commerce has good written (in the English-language curriculum) and oral communication skills in English.

Description of admission tests.
It will be based on a test, developed and conducted nationally, aimed at verifying the necessary aptitude and minimum preparation required to undertake economic studies, through verbal comprehension tests, basic mathematical knowledge, and simple logical reasoning problems. The assessment of English language knowledge will be carried out through tests conducted in collaboration with the University of Siena Language Center. The test is orienting and establishes any additional educational obligations in case of negative evaluation of the access test and the English language knowledge test, possibly in the form of specific recovery courses in mathematics and English.

Role in the workplace context.
Expert in company administration and control The graduate in Economics and Commerce is able to carry out activities related to the administration and management control of both public and private companies of any size operating in any economic sector, and the role of legal auditor of accounts; activities related to administration and control can be carried out either as an employee within a company or other economic organization, or as an autonomous worker in the form of free practice (after completing necessary internships and passing the qualifying exam to join Registers, Lists, etc.).
In particular, this professional figure:
- prepares and drafts summary accounting reports, annual financial statements, and budgets;
- maintains accounting, tax, and labor books;
- verifies the reliability of financial statements and accounting entries and conducts administrative inspections and audits;
- performs balance sheet analysis, production cost analysis, financial and profitability dynamics;
- analyzes sales, purchases, and market outlets;
- contributes to defining and implementing short- and medium-term business projects aimed at improving/consolidating performance.

Business, administrative, and financial manager The graduate in Economics and Commerce can perform junior manager functions by creatively and autonomously inserting into the company's management structure and actively participating in defining company policy and implementing the economic goals of a company, whether public or private, profit or non-profit.
The junior manager participates in defining company policy, acquires direct management responsibility for areas and/or segments of the company, and autonomously makes decisions on the use of available economic resources.
In particular:
- develops business projects within assigned strategic lines;
- carries out administrative, commercial, marketing, and organizational activities;
- performs macroeconomic framework analysis and its impact on the company;
- analyzes the reference market for the company considering the dynamics and choices of competing companies, suppliers of raw materials and semi-finished products;
- controls and manages cost flows and implements policies to minimize them;
- studies the company's market outlet, consumer demand, implements optimal sales and marketing strategies, and optimizes advertising investments.

Expert in the process of company internationalization In the global world, even small and medium-sized companies cannot remain confined exclusively to a national dimension. The graduate in Economics and Commerce can support the internationalization process of a company by facilitating its entry into the international market or developing and consolidating its presence.
In particular:
- studies the international macroeconomic framework and its impact on the company;
- conducts critical analysis of international markets, both regarding the purchase of raw materials and semi-finished products, and regarding the market outlet for the company's products;
- performs liaison functions with national, community, and international government offices;
- studies economic feasibility and, if necessary, prepares procedures for participation in international tenders;
- oversees contract negotiation and drafting of joint venture agreements with foreign companies.

Additional information.
Additional information Specific educational objectives description.
The Bachelor's degree in Economics and Commerce allows the acquisition of multidisciplinary knowledge (in the business, economic, legal, and quantitative areas) that enables understanding how companies function and operate within the increasingly complex social and economic environment in which they operate.
In particular, the Bachelor's degree in Economics and Commerce aims to train graduates who possess:
- a solid preparation enabling them to critically address economic-business problems and prepare and analyze corporate control, planning, and reporting documents;
- theoretical knowledge to conduct critical analysis processes of investigated business realities, both in the private and public sectors;
- skills in using quantitative statistical, management, and economic-business analysis tools necessary to understand the trends of key economic-financial variables;
- ability to correctly frame business phenomena within the micro and macroeconomic context, both domestic and international;
- knowledge of regulatory and normative profiles (both national and community) relevant in the business context, with reference to the private and public sectors;
- ability to express themselves correctly in English;
- knowledge of widely used computer tools.

The Bachelor's degree also allows the acquisition of soft skills (such as planning and organizing, communication skills, problem solving, teamwork, leadership capacity) in collaboration with other structures of the University of Siena.
The degree program is structured into three curricula: two taught in Italian and one entirely taught in English.
The Italian-language curricula share almost entirely the initial two-year period and differ mainly in the third year. The English-language curriculum emphasizes enterprise internationalization processes.
The training path of the Bachelor's degree in Economics and Commerce is structured into four disciplinary areas:
1) Economic which includes microeconomic (consumer and enterprise analysis) and macroeconomic (macroeconomic equilibrium) courses (SECS-P0/1), and depending on the chosen curriculum, public economics (SECS P0/3), industrial and applied economics (SECS-P0/1 and SECS-P/06).
2) Business which includes courses in the two relevant disciplinary areas for specific training (SECS-P0/7 and SECS-P0/8). These courses focus on three major thematic areas: techniques for detecting business phenomena and the formal and substantive logic for preparing economic-financial summary documents; analysis of business management and strategic and operational planning activities; analysis of business functions with particular emphasis on marketing.
3) Legal which includes courses providing the foundations of public and private law (IUS/01 and IUS0/09), subsequently offering elements relevant for the specific training of the course, such as commercial law (IUS/04), and depending on the curriculum chosen, administrative law (IUS/10), labor law (IUS/07), tax law (IUS/12), and community and international law (IUS/14).
4) Mathematical-statistical which includes courses aimed at providing the basis for statistical-quantitative analysis of economic-business problems, ranging from general and financial mathematical analysis (SECS-S/06) to general statistics and applied statistics to the economic-business reality (SECS-S/01 and SEC-S/03).

Program, Texts and Objectives Admission Requirements Students with a High School Diploma or an equivalent foreign degree may be admitted.
Required knowledge will include: elements of general culture and logical reasoning, mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology.
Additionally, English language knowledge at least at A2/2 (CEFR) level is required. The number of students admitted to the C.d.L. is programmed each year based on regional needs.
The entrance exam is common to all C.d.L. in the health area and is conducted on the same day at all Italian universities.
Professional status conferred by the title. Dietist The dietist, in addition to the S.S.N., finds placement in private structures contracted with the S.S.N. for both diagnosis and research, accredited and non-accredited structures such as clinics and rehabilitation centers, Sanitary Assistance Residences, thermal establishments and wellness centers, medical and/or specialist clinics, school and company cafeterias, etc.
At the level of the S.S.N., an increase in the need for this figure is expected in relation to the priority health issues highlighted by the WHO, such as cardiovascular accidents, diet-related pathologies, overweight and obesity, etc., for which the Dietist figure is central in the prevention and rehabilitation process.
Current regulations allow the performance of freelance activities in individual or associated professional offices, sports companies of various types, service cooperatives, etc.
The dietist profession is included in code 85.14.2 (Independent Professional Activities) of the Ateco Economic Activity Classification: health activities not performed by hospitals or doctors, but by legally recognized personnel.
Final Exam Characteristics The Bachelor's Degree course is qualifying for the Dietist profession. The final exam is worth 5 ECTS and consists of: a) Practical exam during which the student must demonstrate having acquired the theoretical-practical and technical-operative knowledge and skills specific to the Dietist professional profile, the successful completion of which is qualifying and allows access to the thesis discussion.
b) Preparation of a thesis and its defense The grade is expressed on a scale of 110 with possible honors.
Required Knowledge for Admission Students with a Secondary School Diploma or another foreign degree recognized by the University may be admitted to the Dietetics Bachelor's Degree. The student must possess an adequate initial preparation, obtained from previous studies, in biology, chemistry, mathematics, and computer science. Additionally, English language knowledge at least at A2/2 (CEFR) level is required.
The student's initial preparation will be assessed through the analysis of errors found in the logic, chemistry, biology, physics-mathematics (multiple-choice questions) quizzes administered in the entrance exam, common to all health area C.d.L.
If the verification of the required knowledge for admission is not positive, additional mandatory training obligations will be assigned to be fulfilled in the first year of the course, as specified in the Course's Teaching Regulations.
Degree Awarded. BACHELOR'S DEGREE IN DIETETICS
Teaching Delivery Mode Conventional
Knowledge and Understanding. Basic Disciplines Area Graduates in Dietetics who have successfully completed the course will possess basic knowledge of physics, chemistry, biochemistry, anatomy and histology, physiology, general pathology, medical genetics, microbiology, medical statistics, and will also acquire fundamental knowledge regarding, among others, pathological anatomy, pharmacology, internal medicine, general surgery, anesthesiology, psychology, demoetnoantropology, and general sociology.
Therefore, they will be able to: a) describe and interpret biological, pathophysiological, and pathological phenomena; b) describe and interpret the molecular, morphological, and functional bases of vital processes.
Learning objectives will be achieved through ex-cathedra, seminarial, and interactive teaching tools.
Learning assessment will be conducted through in-course tests, suitability evaluations, and final exams.
Professional Disciplines Area During the course of study, Dietetics graduates will acquire theoretical and practical knowledge in various fields of competence, both for the public and private sectors, regarding biomedical research and assistance directed towards numerous health fields involved with proper nutrition.
In particular, the Dietist will be able to: a) Evaluate the nutritional status of individuals to implement appropriate dietary prescriptions; b) collaborate with bodies responsible for safeguarding the hygienic-sanitary aspect of the food service; c) develop, formulate, and implement diets prescribed by the doctor and monitor patient acceptability; d) collaborate with other figures in the multidisciplinary treatment of eating behavior disorders; e) study and develop the composition of food rations to meet the nutritional needs of population groups and plan the organization of community food services for healthy and sick individuals; f) conduct educational and informative activities aimed at disseminating correct nutrition principles to allow recovery and maintenance of good health for individuals, communities, and population groups; g) organize and coordinate specific activities related to nutrition in general and dietetics in particular;
Learning objectives will be achieved through teaching tools of the following types: a) ex-cathedra lectures; b) professional activities carried out at clinics and/or wards; c) attendance at facilities where food is prepared (school and hospital cafeterias); d) facilities that produce and/or modify food; e) attendance at laboratories and completion of professional internships; f) seminarial and interactive activities.
Learning assessment will be conducted through in-course tests, suitability evaluations, and final exams.
Related and Integrative Disciplines Area Dietitians must know and understand English; information management processes; acquire adequate statistical and computer science skills; ability to understand international scientific literature and ability to exchange information;
Learning objectives will be achieved through ex-cathedra, seminarial, and interactive teaching tools. Learning assessment will be conducted through in-course tests, suitability evaluations, and final exams.
