Judgment Autonomy.
The graduate, at the end of the study path, will be able to recognize and evaluate critical issues related to the patient's condition in relation to nutritional and dietary aspects, and to develop practical and/or experimental dietary schemes, and to choose methodologies, strategies, and the possible use of equipment, optimal for achieving the expected results, also through the critical review of information obtained through bibliographic and/or computer research. Knowledge of the relevant regulations, professional, legal, and health regulations and their subsequent application will be aimed at achieving specific professional competencies, i.e., the ability to master and manage autonomously and/or in teams acts, technologies, and procedures. The acquisition of a behavior consistent with ethical foundations will be one of the objectives that completes the training path.
These abilities will be achieved by attending internships, where encounters with people, professionals, visits to facilities, and knowledge of different methodologies will facilitate the development of independent critical thinking. Equally important will be active participation in lectures, practical laboratory and/or equipped classroom sessions, clinical internship, reading and interpretation of national and international scientific literature.
Judgment autonomy will be assessed during the course through oral and/or written examination tests, from which the assigned tutors can evaluate the ability to analyze and process clinical cases; internship periods will be followed by tests during which students must verify the acquisition of the proposed topics; finally, the verification related to the final exam: in its practical part and in the evaluation of the thesis content. Equally important will be written reports on in-depth topics and technical-professional aspects and discussion of clinical cases.

Learning Capacity.
Graduates will acquire and must demonstrate the ability to learn and competencies that allow, with a high degree of autonomy, the continuation of studies, including the Master's Degree (LM/SNT3), scientific specialization courses, and advanced permanent and recurring training (1st and 2nd level master's), and update and in-depth courses (Continuing Medical Education).
They will be able to independently update their skills regarding scientific and technological innovations within the scope of their professional activity.
This capacity will be acquired through the overall teaching activity and exam preparation, through internship attendance, where theory is combined with practice, and through critical use of bibliography also for final exam preparation.
This capacity will be verified through examinations (oral, written, simulated practical tests), which identify student preparation and by tutors through internship assessment, and finally through the preparation and conduct of the final exam.

Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Area of Basic Disciplines: Dietitians who successfully complete the study course will be able to:
a) identify health needs related to the individual or the community;
b) use the bases of pathophysiology to analyze medical acts in their practical applications;
c) identify, analyze, distinguish, and recognize various psychological and socio-cultural manifestations related to various situations (pathological or not) to which appropriate nutritional interventions can be applied.
Learning objectives will be achieved through ex-cathedra, seminarial, and interactive teaching tools.
Learning assessment will be conducted through in-course tests, suitability evaluations, and final exams, particularly the final internship exam is aimed at verifying the achievement of expected competencies.

Area of Professionalizing Disciplines: Dietitians who successfully complete the study course will be able to:
a) choose and use appropriate methodologies and equipment in various specialized fields for the acquisition of clinical and experimental data and to carry out their analysis and interpretation (nutritional status assessment, dietary history, physical examination);
b) be able to calculate the parameters of a specific diet for resolving the proposed problem and, collaborating with the physician, psychologist, psychiatrist, participate in the diagnostic and rehabilitative process, proposing solutions that can contribute to resolving the subject's issues;
c) be able to develop ideas and proposals for optimizing nutritional methodologies adopted and document the procedures used, with an appropriate scientific language, fully respecting safety regulations for the use of equipment and procedures.
Learning objectives will be achieved through ex-cathedra, seminarial, and interactive teaching tools.
Learning assessment will be conducted through in-course tests, suitability evaluations, and final exams, particularly the final internship exam is aimed at verifying the achievement of expected competencies.

Area of Related and Integrated Disciplines: Dietitians who successfully complete the study course will be able to: use information systems for data collection, analysis, and management; consult and evaluate international scientific literature.
Learning assessment will be conducted through in-course tests, suitability evaluations, and final exams, particularly the final internship exam is aimed at verifying the achievement of expected competencies.

Communication skills.
The graduate must establish and maintain a relationship with the user, starting from prevention, taking into account the various levels of complexity related to it. This constitutes the foundation of professional practice, which must be centered on the individual, respecting individual differences and considering their influence on eating habits, lifestyle, and the individual's own habits.
The dietist graduate:
- will interview clients to assess needs
- will work in accordance with the principles of patient/user-centered professional practice
- will build a relationship/partnership as the foundation of dietary intervention
- will employ a variety of personalized strategies based on the client's needs
- will develop education programs and educational materials to meet the learning needs of individuals and groups. Graduates must be particularly skilled in interpersonal communication, including oral and written communication with professionals and service users, in group work, and within interdisciplinary work groups with health and social professionals.
To achieve this, the dietist graduate must:
- select appropriate communication methods
- identify and recognize communication barriers (problems reading or writing, misunderstanding, cultural issues, fear, etc.)
- adapt to a communication style suitable to meet the needs and learning abilities of individual persons and/or groups
- employ effective verbal communication skills
- write clearly, concisely, and professionally, technically and grammatically accurately
- develop educational materials considering the comprehension capacity of the target group and/or individuals
- facilitate two-way communication
- employ active listening techniques
- interpret and respond to non-verbal communication
- apply principles of collaboration and negotiation in group work
- incorporate the knowledge, experiences, and skills of other group members during their activities
- collaborate with other group members to define goals
- adapt their personal approach to group members and situations involving the work group
- work with other group members to identify and resolve conflicts
- contribute to decisions made within the work group
- take responsibility for completing assigned tasks.
Communication skills will be acquired through the teachings of human sciences, psychopedagogical, and sociological sciences to ensure the learning of necessary behavioral and relational competencies to operate in a complex work environment. Additionally, the internship requires close contact between the student and patients under the supervision of tutors whose task will be to modulate the approach methodology from the initial phase to the completion of professional training.
Communication skills will be verified by tutors during related teaching activities, during the internship, and through evaluations of teaching activities, up to the final exam.

Dietist The dietist, in addition to the National Health Service (S.S.N.), finds placement in private structures contracted with the S.S.N. for both diagnosis and research, accredited and non-accredited structures such as clinics and rehabilitation centers, Sanitary Assistance Residences, thermal establishments and wellness centers, medical and/or specialist outpatient clinics, school and company canteens, etc.
At the level of the S.S.N., an increase in the need for this figure is expected in relation to the priority health issues highlighted by the WHO, such as cardiovascular accidents, nutrition-related pathologies, overweight and obesity, etc., for which the dietist figure is central in the prevention and rehabilitation process.
Current regulations allow the performance of freelance activities in individual or associated professional offices, sports societies of various types, service cooperatives, etc.

health activities not performed by hospitals or doctors, but by legally recognized personnel.

The ranking is based on merit. Job context function.
Dietist The dietist professional profile is identified as follows: The dietist is the health operator, competent for all activities aimed at the correct application of nutrition and diet, including educational aspects and collaboration in implementing food policies, in compliance with current regulations.
Additional information.
http://www.unisi.it/dipartimenti/dipartimento-scienze-mediche-chirurgiche-e-neuroscienze Specific educational objectives description.
Graduates in Dietetics perform, with professional autonomy, all procedures necessary for the execution of technical-assistive activities on individuals, in accordance with regulations concerning the identification of figures and their professional profiles defined by the Minister of Health's decree.
The professions included in this class collectively contribute to a diagnostic and assistive process that identifies characteristic signs of disease states in numerous areas (skeletal system, sensory organs, functional systems), participates in formulating therapy and monitoring it over time, providing the doctor with a series of tools to formulate diagnosis and prescribe appropriate therapy, provides necessary assistive support during illness, and has preventive value for the social context.
Dietetics graduates are operators in the health professions of the technical-assistive area and occupy an irreplaceable position in ensuring individual well-being and good quality of life, because:
- Collaborates in the recovery of health by providing appropriate nutritional support to both internal and surgical therapy;
- Contributes to maintaining health in healthy individuals through the indication of a correct diet;
- Intervenes in prevention by suggesting 'good practices' of nutrition.
They must therefore possess:
- adequate basic knowledge of biological system physiology to develop operational professionalism;
- possess the cultural and experimental foundations of multidisciplinary techniques characterizing operations in the field of nutrition for the production of goods and services through food modification and the development of dietary schemes and personalized diets;
- possess disciplinary methodologies and be able to apply them in concrete situations with appropriate knowledge of regulations and deontological and bioethical issues;
- be able to effectively use English, or at least another European Union language, in addition to Italian, both in written and oral form, within their specific area of competence and for general information exchange;
- possess adequate competencies and tools for communication and information management;
- be able to draft technical-scientific reports;
- be capable of working in groups, performing autonomous operational activities, and quickly integrating into work environments.
The primary objectives of this degree course, which includes a total of 180 CFU over three years (with 60 CFU to be acquired through training activities aimed at developing specific professional abilities (internship)), aim to train dietist graduates qualified to practice the dietist profession. These are achieved through theoretical and theoretical/practical learning, focused on the specificity of the profession, divided into three disciplinary areas:
1) Basic training activities: FIS/07 Physics, MED/01 Medical Statistics, MED/03 Medical Genetics, MED/04 General Pathology, MED/07 Microbiology, MED/09 Internal Medicine, BIO/09 Physiology, MED/18 General Surgery, MED/41 Anesthesiology, BIO/10 Chemistry and Biochemistry, BIO/13 Biology, BIO/16 Human Anatomy, BIO/17 Histology, M-PSI/01 Psychology, M-DEA/01 Demoetnoanthropology, SPS/07 General Sociology;
2) Professional training activities: AGR/15 Food Sciences and Technologies, BIO/12 Clinical Biochemistry, BIO/14 Pharmacology, CHIM/10 Food Chemistry, ING-INF/06 Information Processing Systems, IUS/07 Labour Law, IUS/09 Public Law Institutions, MED/02 History of Medicine, MED/06 Medical Oncology, MED/08 Pathological Anatomy, MED/09 Internal Medicine and Geriatrics, MED/11 Cardiovascular Diseases, MED/12 Gastroenterology, MED/13 Endocrinology and Diabetology, MED/16 Rheumatology, MED/25 Psychiatry, MED/26 Neurology, MED/36 Radioprotection, MED/38 Pediatrics, MED/39 Child Neuropsychiatry, MED/40 Gynecology and Obstetrics, MED/42 General and Applied Hygiene, MED/43 Medical and Professional Ethics, MED/44 Occupational Medicine, MED/49 Applied Dietetic Sciences, M-PED/01 General Pedagogy, SECS-P/07 BUSINESS ECONOMICS, SECS-P/10 ORGANIZATIONAL MANAGEMENT, SECS-P/13 MERCHANDISING SCIENCES, SECS-S/02 STATISTICS FOR EXPERIMENTAL AND TECHNOLOGICAL RESEARCH.
3) Related and complementary disciplines training activities: BIO/15 Pharmaceutical Biology.
Students are provided with an English language course (Medical English) also aimed at understanding scientific literature.
The internship (60 CFU), which is a fundamental part of the C.d.L. for students to acquire the necessary skills for dietist practice, will receive particular attention regarding the choice of sites and the timing of implementation relative to the advancement of the study course.
Teaching is organized into modules and is delivered through frontal lectures, classroom exercises, or in specific 'laboratories' for the CdL.
The learning outcomes of laboratory, English, and some internship courses will result in a qualification.
Students will have 5 CFU available for preparing the final exam of the Course at facilities dedicated to training; this activity, defined as 'degree internship', can also be carried out in non-university facilities, such as hospital or public and/or private accredited facilities, subject to authorization by the Teaching Committee.

Knowledge: mathematics (level: scientific high school); computer science (knowledge of main applications and PC programs); English language (level A2/2); general culture (more specifically history at high school level, civic education with specific reference to the Italian Constitution).
Professional status conferred by the degree. Biotechnologist
The course allows obtaining preparation for the profession of junior biologist (after passing the state exam and registration with the order) and finding employment opportunities in the role of:
Technician laboratory, in public or private structure, able to apply the most appropriate analytical and diagnostic techniques in biotechnological production of health products (drugs, vaccines, medical devices).
Technician laboratory, in public or private structure, able to correctly apply analytical and diagnostic techniques for quality control, safety, and efficacy in the production processes of biotechnological health products (drugs, vaccines, medical devices), in compliance with good preparation, quality, and safety regulations.

Final Exam Characteristics The final exam will consist of a written paper discussion in front of a faculty committee, in Italian or English.
The experimental thesis will be the result of studies and research conducted during the last year of the course, also through internships or research periods that may be carried out in Italy or abroad.
The final exam grade is expressed on a scale of 110 with possible honors.
The criteria for calculating the merit score are defined by the Course Regulations.
Required Knowledge for Admission Students enrolling in the Biotecnologie Study Course must possess a secondary school diploma obtained in Italy or a foreign study title after at least 12 years of schooling, recognized as suitable according to current regulations, with adequate knowledge of basic scientific disciplines - biology (level: scientific high school); English language (level A2/2); mathematics, physics, chemistry - and understanding of elementary logic and general culture basics.
To ensure teaching quality, admission to the Study Course may be quota-based locally, in relation to the sustainability of the facilities.
The methods for evaluating the student's initial preparation will be indicated in the Course's Teaching Regulations, where additional educational obligations will also be specified if the verification is not positive.
At the start of training, basic discipline teachers verify the minimum knowledge requirements in the areas of biology, chemistry, and physics, which could result in the student having educational debts (OFA) in the specific area.
The verification of the aforementioned knowledge will be conducted according to the methods, criteria, and procedures determined by the Course's Teaching Regulations.
Students found lacking in one or more areas, with the support of reference teachers and the teaching committee, must fulfill the identified OFA within the first year of the course.
Degree Awarded. BACHELOR'S DEGREE IN BIOTECHNOLOGY
Teaching Delivery Mode Conventional
Knowledge and Understanding. Generic Area Referring to the European system of study title descriptors (Dublin descriptors), the Biotecnologie Bachelor's Degree Course is designed so that its graduates, at the end of their studies, achieve knowledge and understanding in the field of biotechnology.
Transversal Learning Objectives are: a) ability to understand phenomena and simple and complex models related to chemical, physical, mathematical, and statistical disciplines; b) knowledge of biological foundations and physiological mechanisms underlying biological phenomena at the molecular, cellular level, and their integration at the organ system and whole organism level; c) knowledge of the main techniques used in biotechnology and their theoretical foundations; d) knowledge of national and international legislation of interest to biotechnology, with particular regard to patenting rules and bioethics.
To clearly and concisely illustrate how the expected learning outcomes above connect to the courses in the training path, please refer to the course link https://biotecnologie.unisi.it/it where programs and evaluation methods for individual courses can be found.
Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry Area Knowledge and Understanding The student acquires knowledge of the basic methods and tools of mathematics and computer science, physics, and chemistry for understanding and interpreting biological systems.
In detail, Biotecnologie graduates are able to: 1) critically understand a mathematical-statistical reasoning 2) understand the statistical foundations associated with life sciences 3) understand physical phenomena in various fields of Biotechnology. 4) understand chemical phenomena in various fields of Biotechnology.
These abilities will be developed primarily through traditional teaching tools, by participating in lectures, exercises, laboratory activities, and through personal study of texts and scientific publications.
Molecular, Cellular, and Organismal Area Knowledge and Understanding The student acquires knowledge of biological systems, particularly at the cellular and molecular level, providing cognitive tools related to the structure and function of eukaryotic cells and multicellular organisms with reference to functional, biochemical, molecular, and genetic aspects.
Specifically, they acquire: 1) knowledge necessary to understand mechanisms regulating the transmission of inherited traits, gene expression regulation, and biochemical processes underlying cellular communication, cellular physiology, and organism physiology 2) knowledge related to structure-function relationships of macromolecules, cells, and tissues 4) knowledge necessary to understand the structure of the human genome and the principles of methods used for its analysis. 6) knowledge necessary to understand molecular mechanisms underlying diseases and the definition and classification of pharmacological targets, and understanding the different aspects of pharmacodynamics underlying drug action. 7) knowledge necessary to understand molecular mechanisms underlying bacterial and viral infections, molecular phenomena of microorganism-host interaction and their treatment, and the immune response of organisms.
Knowledge and abilities are acquired and verified in the following training activities, which, in addition to lectures, may include classroom and laboratory exercises involving the use of optical microscopes for observing and recognizing stained histological and anatomical preparations using conventional methods, to distinguish morphological characteristics corresponding to different tissues and organs.
Biotechnology Area Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding. Students in Biotechnology acquire knowledge and understanding of the main diagnostic and biotechnological techniques and the basic principles of pharmacology - experiment and acquire knowledge of the most recent applications of biotechnology in the fields of medicine, public health, and diagnostics - acquire knowledge of synthesis and biosynthesis techniques for therapeutic peptides and recombinant antibodies, integrating biotechnological and chemical knowledge essential for developing new therapeutic devices - acquire knowledge of biological databases using bioinformatics tools automatically, and read/write shell scripts and PYTHON programs. Acquire basic knowledge of patent law regarding ethical and economic aspects of scientific research and biotechnological applications in the medical field.
Knowledge and abilities are acquired and verified in the following training activities, which, in addition to lectures, include classroom and laboratory exercises.
The verification of acquired knowledge and understanding abilities in the different areas will be assessed during the respective passing exams, which will be conducted primarily through oral examinations or written final and in-course tests in the form of closed or open-ended questions.

Judgment Autonomy.
Referring to the European framework of study title descriptors (Dublin descriptors), the Biotechnology Degree course is designed so that its graduates achieve judgment autonomy, which will be encouraged and promoted throughout the entire course of study, both during lectures and laboratory activities. To this end, their ability to independently collect and interpret data will be stimulated, developing their capacity to conduct bibliographic research on scientific sources, particularly but not exclusively, in preparation for the final exam;
-they have the capacity to design and conduct experiments, interpret data, as they receive the necessary computer and statistical foundations in specific courses and are required to apply them in laboratory experimental activities;
-they have the capacity to consult databases related to, but not limited to, the biotechnology sector.
Judgment autonomy is developed through activities requiring personal effort from the student, such as producing an independent work in individual courses or for the final exam, but is also implemented in group activities, such as laboratories. To consolidate these skills, collaboration with particularly qualified experts from the private research and industry world is provided. The achievement of this objective will be verified during laboratory activities, during the preparation of works, and especially through the writing and discussion of the thesis.
Learning Ability.
Referring to the European framework of study title descriptors (Dublin descriptors), the Biotechnology Degree course is designed so that its graduates develop the necessary learning abilities to independently pursue subsequent studies throughout their educational path. The teaching activities of the Biotechnology Degree are oriented towards stimulating and enhancing the student's learning abilities, making graduates autonomous in facing subsequent study paths or different work realities in the biotechnology field. Methodological training, specialized knowledge, and critical abilities enable graduates to tackle subsequent master's level study programs. The same skills and abilities allow for independent learning, thus enabling continued professional growth and the development of new or more advanced competencies. The field of Biotechnology/life sciences represents disciplines that are constantly evolving, requiring autonomous learning capacity throughout life; laboratory activities represent a significant initial stage where the student must demonstrate initiative autonomy and implementation of their knowledge when faced with real problems not pre-prepared for didactic purposes.
The ability to learn primarily in a guided manner is developed in the preparation for oral exams, in the writing of works and/or reports. However, it is in the writing of the final report and in practical and laboratory activities that the student develops and demonstrates autonomous learning ability.
The verification of achieving the objective is linked to academic performance results in traditional teaching, the evaluation by the graduation committee, and the specific reports of tutors provided for practical and laboratory activities.
All this to enable the student to develop the necessary competencies to pursue subsequent studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Ability to Apply Knowledge and Understanding.
Generic Area Graduates in Biotechnology who have successfully completed the course of study must:
a) be able to use chemical, physical, mathematical, and statistical knowledge to interpret and evaluate observed biological phenomena;
b) have acquired sufficient knowledge to analyze potential perturbations of biological system homeostasis and the capacity to intervene to restore homeostatic balance;
c) have acquired the ability to apply biotechnology techniques to common research or production processes;
d) have acquired the necessary methodological judgment capacities to evaluate procedures from both a bioethical and legislative perspective;
e) demonstrate the ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify and formulate approaches in the biotechnology sector, combining theory and practice to solve problems in various application fields;
Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry Area The Biotechnology graduate acquires the ability to apply the basic methods and tools of mathematics and computer science, physics, and chemistry for understanding and interpreting biological systems.
In detail, Biotechnology graduates are able to:
1) critically analyze a mathematical-statistical reasoning and apply the same processes to other biotechnology disciplines.
2) apply the statistical foundations associated with life sciences, particularly in the analysis of data from animal and cellular models.
3) critically analyze physical phenomena in various areas of Biotechnology.
4) critically analyze chemical phenomena in various areas of Biotechnology.
Knowledge and skills are acquired and verified in the following training activities, which may include both lectures and classroom or laboratory exercises:
Molecular, Cellular, and Organismal Area Biotechnology graduates are able to use knowledge of biological systems through the application of methodologies for analyzing cellular macromolecules and studying complex systems. Graduates are also able to apply microbiology techniques for identifying pharmacological targets that can modulate cell communication and the physiology of cells and tissues. Graduates are also able to apply knowledge of genome structure and gene regulation for identifying new therapies for treating genetic and metabolic diseases.
Biotechnology Area The Biotechnology graduate is able to apply the main diagnostic and biotechnology techniques and the basic principles of pharmacology in the fields of medicine, public health, and diagnostics.
They are able to apply techniques for the synthesis and biosynthesis of therapeutic peptides and recombinant antibodies for the development of new therapeutic devices.
- They apply the fundamental principles of statistics to understand the basic concepts of experimental research and applied biotechnology in medicine.
They can query biological databases automatically using bioinformatics tools, and read/write shell scripts and PYTHON programs.
They know the main aspects of patent law, scientific research ethics, and biotechnology applications in the medical field.

Communication Skills.
Referring to the European framework of study title descriptors (Dublin descriptors), the Biotechnology Degree Course is designed so that its graduates are able to communicate information, ideas, problems and solutions to both specialist and non-specialist audiences, in Italian and in a foreign language (generally English, at least at B1 level).
In particular, students must acquire:
a) communication skills necessary to clearly and effectively convey the results of experimental activities to both experts and laypersons;
b) ability to write and present scientific reports;
c) communication skills, also in English, ability to communicate scientific reports in English, both in written and oral form.
The ability to communicate information, ideas, problems and their solutions will be assessed in oral or written exams for each course. Relational skills are acquired during internships and practical and laboratory activities and will be highlighted in the evaluations prepared by teachers/tutors. In particular, the thesis discussion is structured to verify this skill, through the presentation and exposition of the final work with PowerPoint presentations.
Expected occupational and professional opportunities for graduates.
Biotechnologist The course enables preparation for the profession of junior biologist (subject to passing the state exam and registration with the professional order) and finding employment opportunities in the role of:
Laboratory Technician, in public or private structures, capable of applying the most appropriate analytical and diagnostic techniques in the biotechnological production of health products (drugs, vaccines, medical devices).
Laboratory Technician, in public or private structures, capable of correctly applying analytical and diagnostic techniques for quality control, safety and efficacy in the production processes of biotechnological health products (drugs, vaccines, medical devices), in compliance with good manufacturing, quality and safety regulations.
Laboratory Technician in diagnostic structures (public or private), capable of operating in health-related diagnostics (laboratories of public or contracted structures).
Laboratory Technician in public or private structures (company) authorized for certification and quality control of biotechnological-derived drugs, vaccines, medical devices.
- Entrepreneur of biotechnology companies in the health field (red biotech).
Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIAN Associated competencies for the role.
Biotechnologist The graduate will have acquired conceptual and methodological tools enabling them to work in laboratories characterized by the use of biotechnology for:
- environmental improvement and monitoring, and
- the ability to operate for the promotion and development of scientific and technological innovation in biotechnological contexts related to human health in all its aspects, from diagnostics to vaccine production to the management of services connected to industrial pharmaceutical biotechnology. They may work in analysis, certification and biological control laboratories, and in health monitoring services. Thanks to the ability to analyze and use, even modifying them, cells or their components both in the laboratory and on the production plant, the Biotechnologist can work in companies operating in biotechnological research and production where, leveraging the acquired skills, including bioinformatics, they will be able to analyze problems to choose the most effective methodological approaches for the production and research process. The acquired preparation also enables the valorization of intellectual property, based on current national and community regulations.
Description of admission tests.
The admission test and the limited enrollment are decided annually by the Teaching Committee and made public on the website of the Degree Course and the University of Siena. If applicable, it consists of multiple-choice quizzes prepared by the Teaching Committee. Subjects: Mathematics (level: scientific high school); computer science (knowledge of main PC applications and programs); English language (level A2/2); general culture (more specifically history at high school level, civic education with specific reference to the Italian Constitution). There is no minimum score required to pass the admission test: a ranking will be drawn up based on the score achieved in the test (70%) and the score achieved in the high school graduation exam (30%).
Role in the work context.
Biotechnologist The graduate of the Biotechnology Degree Course corresponds to a professional figure capable of operating preferably in the field of technological innovation to support control and improvement, particularly in the health sector, through the analysis and use of cells or their components, even modified through advanced molecular techniques, both in research laboratories and on production plants. Alongside technical skills, they also possess analytical and evaluative abilities regarding compliance with current national and community regulations.
Additional information.
http://www.unisi.it/dipartimenti/dipartimento-medicina-molecolare-e-dello-sviluppo Specific training objectives description.
The Biotechnology Degree Course aims to prepare graduates with adequate basic knowledge of chemical-physical-computer-biological type, interpreted from a molecular and cellular perspective, enabling them to develop interdisciplinary operational professionalism in the application of technological methodologies to various fields of biotechnology in the biomedical and environmental context.
The proposed training project is primarily aimed at training graduates with a dedicated focus on biotechnology applied in the field of human health (red biotechnology), but who also possess the cultural and experimental foundations of multidisciplinary techniques characterizing biotechnological operations for the production of goods and services through the analysis and use of biological systems; who are able to know disciplinary methodologies and apply them in concrete situations with appropriate knowledge of national and international law concerning bioethical aspects, protection of inventions and safety in the biotechnology sector; who are able to effectively use English, in addition to Italian, both in written and oral form within their specific field of competence and for general information exchange; who are able to draft technical-scientific reports and are capable of working in teams, operating autonomously and quickly integrating into work environments.
The Biotechnology Degree Course includes integrated courses and single courses in the first year, providing graduates with sufficient basic knowledge in mathematics, statistics, computer science, physics, chemistry and biology related to the scientific disciplines INF/01, FIS/01, CHIM/03, CHIM/06, BIO/13.
In the second and third years, activities will be differentiated to deepen more specific application areas, such as agri-food, pharmaceutical (BIO/01, BIO/14) and biomedical, including integrated courses, single courses, student-selected activities, practical and laboratory activities useful for entering the job market and a final exam aimed at acquiring essential knowledge on the structure and function of biological systems under physiological, pathological and simulated pathological conditions, understanding their molecular, informational and integrative logic (BIO/09, BIO/16, BIO/17, BIO/10, MED/04, MED/07, MED/08).
In the training path, students will deepen knowledge of biological systems at both cellular and molecular levels (BIO/13, BIO/11, MED/08) and acquire the conceptual, technical-practical and computer tools necessary to develop experimental skills on which biotechnology is based (INF/01). They will also be provided with tools to understand the principles of bioethics related to research and animal and clinical experimentation (IUS/14). The teaching project is embedded in a scientific context capable of providing highly qualified teaching staff, cutting-edge infrastructure, and industrial realities not only participating in teaching objectives but also available to host students both in training activities and in terms of job placement.

High School Diploma Tuition and Fees For information on tuition and fees, visit the University website www.unisi.it/tasse Dates and Deadlines For information on dates and deadlines, visit the University website "Course Plan" www.unisi.it/didattica/immatricolazioni-e-iscrizioni/immatricolazioni Roles Chair/Chair of Teaching Committee MASSIMO NEPI Program, texts and objectives Professional title conferred by the degree.
Qualified agricultural technician The Agribusiness Degree Programme (L-P02) is a professional-oriented degree with immediate job market entry, therefore enrolling in a master's degree does not constitute a natural progression for graduates. The programme aims to train the professional figure of a qualified agricultural technician. This professional will find employment opportunities in the diverse agricultural production sector where they may be employed in the following areas:
- Independent profession;
- Agricultural sector consultancy for Public and private bodies;
- Public administration with non-managerial roles;
- Agricultural companies;
- Cooperatives and consortia;
- Professional associations;
- Large retail;
- Laboratories for agricultural and environmental analysis;
- National and international institutions;
- Service companies for the primary sector.
The professional-oriented Agribusiness Degree may qualify for the professions of licensed agricultural engineer, qualified agrotechnician, and licensed industrial engineer (food technology section) following a practical evaluation test assessing the necessary knowledge, skills, abilities, and operational autonomy for practicing the aforementioned professions, to be conducted prior to the final exam.
Final exam characteristics The final exam for the professional Agribusiness Degree qualifies for the practice of the professions of qualified agrotechnician and/or licensed agricultural engineer and/or licensed industrial engineer registered in the "food technology section".
The final exam includes the completion of an evaluative practical test (EPT) preceding the final exam. The EPT aims to verify the knowledge, skills, abilities, and operational autonomy necessary for professional practice, focusing on topics consistent with professional activities and the specificities of the study programme.
The final exam represents an important opportunity for individual training and consists of the discussion of a written report deepening practical, applied/project-oriented themes addressed during the evaluative practical internship activities. This report is prepared independently by the student under the guidance of one or more faculty supervisors, possibly supported by external professional or company figures.
The final exam aims to verify that the graduate has acquired knowledge, understanding, and independent judgment in the field of Agribusiness.
The final exam may be conducted in English.
The final exam grade is expressed on a scale of 110 with the possibility of honors.
Required knowledge for admission To be admitted to the Degree Programme, one must hold a secondary school diploma or another foreign qualification recognized as equivalent, and possess basic knowledge in mathematics, chemistry, and biology. The required knowledge for admission and their mandatory verification methods are defined in the Teaching Regulations of the Study Programme, which also indicate any additional training obligations if the verification of required knowledge is not successful. These additional training obligations must be fulfilled within the first year of study.
The programme is quota-controlled, and the number of admitted students will be adjusted based on internship availability, laboratory capacity, and labor market needs.
For admission to the Degree Programme, English language proficiency at least at A2/2 level, as defined by the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages, is required.

Knowledge and understanding.
Generic Area The expected learning outcomes in the basic disciplines are adequate knowledge and understanding of disciplines in statistics, chemistry, biology, and ecology oriented towards practical applications in the agricultural sector.
These outcomes may be achieved through attending lectures during the study programme, participating in in-depth seminars, specific laboratory activities, and evaluative practical internships. Learning outcomes are verified through in-course assessments, non-final evaluation tests, written and/or oral exams.
The final student assessment is based on both the evaluation of knowledge of the programme content and the evaluation of the ability to critically reprocess content for potential application in various professional challenges.
Technical-Agricultural Area The expected learning outcomes in the disciplines of plant and animal production and agricultural machinery are adequate knowledge and understanding in the areas of agricultural product production, quality, and safety, and machinery and equipment for the agricultural sector.
These outcomes may be achieved through attending lectures during the study programme, participating in in-depth seminars, specific laboratory activities, and evaluative practical internships. Learning outcomes are verified through in-course assessments, non-final evaluation tests, written and/or oral exams.
The final student assessment is based on both the evaluation of knowledge of the programme content and the evaluation of the ability to critically reprocess content for potential application in various professional challenges.
Economic-Legal Area The expected learning outcomes in the economic and legal disciplines are adequate knowledge and understanding in the areas of business management, food economy and marketing, and agricultural legislation.
These outcomes may be achieved through attending lectures during the study programme, participating in in-depth seminars, laboratory activities, and evaluative practical internships. Learning outcomes are verified through in-course assessments, non-final evaluation tests, written and/or oral exams.
The final student assessment is based on both the evaluation of knowledge of the programme content and the evaluation of the ability to critically reprocess content for potential application in various professional challenges.

COURSE: [D341] AGRIBUSINESS Inter-university
SECTION: Communication skills
URL: https://unisi.coursecatalogue.cineca.it/corsi/2024/11095

Communication skills.
Graduates in Agribusiness will be able to communicate to specialists and non-specialists, using computer-based tools, the information acquired and the ideas and issues they have independently developed in various sectors of biology, agricultural production, economics, marketing, and legislation. They will also be able to work in groups both in theoretical and experimental fields. Graduates will have developed the ability to interact with the market. They will also be able to promote their initiatives using digital technologies such as social media, online marketing, e-commerce sites, and web platforms.
Communication skills are acquired during frontal lectures, internships, seminar activities and individual study, as well as through non-disciplinary laboratory activities. The verification of communication skills is carried out through in-course assessments, passing exams, group work, and the final exam.
Expected occupational and professional opportunities for graduates.
Qualified Agricultural Technician. The Agribusiness Study Course (L-P02) is a professional-oriented degree with immediate entry into the job market, therefore enrolling in a master's degree does not constitute a natural progression for graduates. The Study Course aims to train the professional figure of a qualified Agricultural Technician. This figure will find employment opportunities in the diversified agricultural production sector, where they can be employed in the following areas:
- Independent profession;
- Consulting in the agricultural sector for Public and Private Entities;
- Public administration with non-managerial roles;
- Agricultural companies;
- Cooperatives and consortia;
- Professional associations;
- Large distribution;
- Analysis laboratories for agriculture and the environment;
- National and international institutions;
- Service companies for the primary sector.
The professional-oriented Agribusiness degree can qualify graduates for the professions of Licensed Agricultural Technician, Licensed Agrotechnician, and Licensed Industrial Technician (Food Technology Section) following a practical assessment aimed at evaluating the necessary knowledge, skills, abilities, and operational autonomy for practicing the aforementioned professions, to be conducted prior to the final exam.
Official teaching and assessment languages.
ITALIANO Associated competencies to the function.
Qualified Agricultural Technician. The competencies associated with the functions of an Agribusiness graduate (L-P02) are characterized by a significant multidisciplinary nature, necessary for performing operational tasks and resolving problems in a particularly dynamic and innovative production context. The Agribusiness graduate also possesses tools for managing information in the field of agricultural technologies. Overall, the Agribusiness graduate possesses competencies related to production in the agricultural and animal husbandry sector, sustainable management of agro-ecosystems, promotion, valorization, and marketing of products, economic and financial management, as well as the tools of agricultural policy aimed at managing businesses and rural development.
Function in the workplace.
Qualified Agricultural Technician. Based on the competencies acquired and developed in the Study Course, the Agribusiness graduate (L-P02) can independently perform technical activities in the following work areas:
- Organization and control of production processes in the agricultural and animal husbandry sector, with particular reference to the design and application of simple technologies for production control;
- Economic management of production companies;
- Marketing and distribution of agricultural products;
- Marketing activities in the primary sector;
- Participation in the management processes of eco-sustainable production and the protection of plant and animal biodiversity.
Description of specific educational objectives.
Agribusiness L-P02 is a professional-oriented inter-university course between the University of Siena and the University of Pisa, directly related to the needs of the labor market in the agri-food sector. The course's objective is to train new professional figures capable of operating, even not at a managerial level, in the management of agricultural productions, from primary activities to product marketing and commercialization, as well as using acquired knowledge to solve multiple practical problems in a complex and dynamic context such as the agricultural and agri-food sector.
For this purpose, the course is structured to:
1) Provide knowledge in mathematical/statistical, biological, chemical, economic, legal, and marketing disciplines within the agricultural and agribusiness sector, disciplines related to plant and animal production, product quality, as well as mechanization and plant engineering in the agricultural context.
2) Provide competencies related to production in the agricultural and animal husbandry sector, sustainable management of agro-ecosystems, promotion, valorization, and marketing of products, economic and financial management, as well as the tools of agricultural policy aimed at managing businesses and rural development.
The educational objectives are therefore oriented towards the following learning areas:
- 1) Basic scientific knowledge area, characterized by courses necessary for acquiring foundational knowledge in mathematics and statistics, ecology, chemistry, and biology;
- 2) Plant and animal production area, identified by courses necessary for acquiring knowledge in the field of agronomy, herbaceous and tree crop cultivation, plant protection, animal breeding technologies, and animal nutrition;
- 3) Food technology area: Basic knowledge on business transformation of products, hygiene, and safety;
- 4) Agricultural engineering area: Identified by courses necessary to acquire knowledge on the use of agricultural machinery and equipment;
- 5) Economic, managerial, and legal disciplines area: Identified by courses aimed at providing knowledge of the fundamentals of economics, agricultural business management, legislation, and marketing;
- 6) Area of non-disciplinary transversal competencies useful for entering the workforce.
The achievement of these objectives is carried out through a training path that ensures broad transversality of the knowledge necessary to form a versatile professional figure that possesses both mastery of scientific methods and content, as well as management and marketing capabilities in the primary sector.
The planned training activities are structured as follows:
- In the first year of the course, to provide students with a foundation useful for more effective learning in subsequent years, the following are provided:
1) Basic discipline activities, i.e., biological disciplines in SSD BIO/01 and BIO/05, chemical disciplines (SSD CHIM/03, AGR/13), statistical disciplines in SSD SECS-S/01, aimed at providing knowledge on the complexity of living systems, management of agroecosystems including their interactions with natural components such as wildlife, as well as scientific methodologies and techniques for data processing;
2) Characterizing discipline activities in SSD AGR/02 aimed at knowledge of agricultural systems and the main foundations of plant production;
3) Affine and integrative activities indispensable for specific in-depth studies in areas consistent with the training path objectives. In particular, these activities are necessary to provide specific knowledge related to biochemistry, animal and plant physiology, safety of agri-food products, hygiene and safety in the workplace, biodiversity, and environmental quality. These activities are mostly included as student-selected courses and are functional to compose a flexible path, depending on individual interests and inclinations, in areas still considered relevant to the training of a professional operating in a complex and dynamic field such as agricultural and agri-food productions;
4) Laboratories useful for entering the workforce to provide non-disciplinary transversal competencies, such as digital skills, team working abilities, problem-solving, skills for continuous updating of knowledge using modern technologies, communication skills, etc.
5) Adequate knowledge of the English language (B1 level)
- In the second year, activities in the more specifically technical-agricultural field are provided:
1) Characterizing activities in the field of plant engineering and mechanization (AGR/09), the field of Animal Production, particularly product quality (AGR/19), production defense (AGR/11 and AGR/12), as well as the field of Economic, Valuation, and Legal Disciplines (AGR/01). These activities are oriented to provide knowledge on primary agricultural and animal production, as well as machines and equipment for the agricultural sector, plant production defense, and marketing strategies to compete in the agri-food products market.
2) Affine and integrative activities indispensable for specific in-depth studies in areas consistent with the training path objectives. In particular, the interaction of the soil-plant system, plant genetics and genetic improvement, horticultural and tree crop production, principles of food transformation, as well as disciplines for managing the quality of productions and products, production sustainability, and rural development.
3) Laboratories useful for entering the workforce to provide non-disciplinary transversal competencies, such as the ability to use data management platforms, knowledge of tools for collaborating in information management and communication, project planning, knowledge of the principles and areas of professional activities and their relevant regulations and ethics, etc.
4) One student-selected course consistent with the training path.
- In the third year of the course, the following activities are provided:
1) Characterizing activities in the field of Economic, Valuation, and Legal Disciplines, particularly SSD SECS-P/08 and IUS/03, necessary to provide competencies for managing agricultural production, considering communication and marketing strategies, economics, economic policies, and law in the agricultural context;
2) Practical assessment internship (TPV) to be carried out at private companies, public entities, or professional orders and colleges, or professional offices. The TPV represents a fundamental element in developing professional competencies in a work context, as well as an opportunity to establish future professional relationships.
For the adequate implementation of the Agribusiness L-P02 Study Course training path, especially in the context of internship and laboratory activities, conventions have been established between the University of Siena and professional colleges.
These conventions provide for collaboration between the parties regarding both the identification of sites for conducting internships (professional offices, companies) and the organization of laboratory activities useful for entering the workforce.
Laboratory activities useful for entering the workforce are differentiated between the first and second years. Those of the first year aim at acquiring common soft skills while providing direct knowledge of the workforce and professions. Laboratory activities of the second year, however, are more specifically related to the course topics and partly (for a minimum of 12 cfu) dedicated to topics related to the area "Foundations of Plant Production". Laboratory activities, mostly conducted by non-academic professionals, are fundamental to complement the knowledge and competencies imparted through disciplinary courses and apply them in work contexts.
The TPV is fundamental for the training of the Agribusiness graduate as it represents a significant portion of the training path (minimum 48 cfu out of a total of 180 for the entire Study Course). Interaction with the professional world and the business network is also indispensable for the internship activities scheduled in the third year, which students can carry out at private companies or at professional orders and colleges or professional offices that have signed specific conventions.
The TPVs are conducted under the supervision of an academic tutor and an industry tutor who, in synergy with the student, define and plan the activities.
The business network is continuously expanding and is appropriately scaled to ensure adequate internship experiences for the maximum number of enrolled students.
At the end of the training path, the student can qualify for the professions of Licensed Agricultural Technician, Licensed Agrotechnician, and Licensed Industrial Technician (Food Technology Section) following a practical assessment (PPV) aimed at evaluating the necessary knowledge, skills, abilities, and operational autonomy for practicing the aforementioned professions, to be conducted prior to the final exam.
